declarations.docstring: Exact Möbius recovery: `μ * f_A = 1_A` as arithmetic functions.

declarations.name: mobius_supportCoeff_eq_one_iff
declarations.signature: theorem mobius_supportCoeff_eq_one_iff (A : Set ℕ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * supportCoeffAF A) n = 1 ↔ n ∈ A
declarations.docstring: Pointwise positive-index form of Möbius recovery.

declarations.name: mobius_supportCoeff_boolean
declarations.signature: theorem mobius_supportCoeff_boolean (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * supportCoeffAF A) n = 0 ∨ (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * supportCoeffAF A) n = 1
declarations.docstring: The Möbius transform of every support coefficient is Boolean.

declarations.name: mobius_supportCoeff_recovers_support
declarations.signature: theorem mobius_supportCoeff_recovers_support (A : Set ℕ) (hzero : 0 ∉ A) : {n : ℕ | (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * supportCoeffAF A) n = 1} = A
declarations.docstring: Under the honest zero normalization, the Boolean Möbius transform recovers the entire support set, not merely its positive part.

declarations.name: booleanMobiusSupport
declarations.signature: noncomputable def booleanMobiusSupport (f : ArithmeticFunction ℤ) : Set ℕ
declarations.docstring: The positive support selected by the Boolean Möbius transform of `f`.

declarations.name: zero_not_mem_booleanMobiusSupport
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem zero_not_mem_booleanMobiusSupport (f : ArithmeticFunction ℤ) : 0 ∉ booleanMobiusSupport f

declarations.name: moebius_mul_eq_positiveSupportBitAF_of_boolean
declarations.signature: theorem moebius_mul_eq_positiveSupportBitAF_of_boolean (f : ArithmeticFunction ℤ) (hbool : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * f) n = 0 ∨ (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * f) n = 1) : ArithmeticFunction.moebius * f = positiveSupportBitAF (booleanMobiusSupport f)
declarations.docstring: A Boolean Möbius transform is exactly the normalized indicator of the support that it selects.

declarations.name: eq_supportCoeffAF_booleanMobiusSupport_of_boolean
declarations.signature: theorem eq_supportCoeffAF_booleanMobiusSupport_of_boolean (f : ArithmeticFunction ℤ) (hbool : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * f) n = 0 ∨ (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * f) n = 1) : f = supportCoeffAF (booleanMobiusSupport f)
declarations.docstring: **Boolean Möbius inversion, converse direction.** Every integer-valued arithmetic function with Boolean Möbius transform is the support coefficient of the positive set selected by that transform. No search or finiteness hypothesis appears.

declarations.name: card_divisors_le_two_mul_sqrt
declarations.signature: theorem card_divisors_le_two_mul_sqrt (n : ℕ) : n.divisors.card ≤ 2 * Nat.sqrt n
declarations.docstring: Elementary divisor-pair estimate `τ(n) ≤ 2⌊√n⌋`. Mathlib currently supplies only the coarser `τ(n) ≤ n`; the partition below pairs every divisor above the square root with its complementary divisor below it.

declarations.name: supportCoeff_le_two_mul_sqrt
declarations.signature: theorem supportCoeff_le_two_mul_sqrt (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : supportCoeff A n ≤ 2 * Nat.sqrt n
declarations.docstring: The support coefficient inherits the sharp divisor-pair envelope.

declarations.name: sqrt_shift_le_sqrt_add_index
declarations.signature: theorem sqrt_shift_le_sqrt_add_index (N j : ℕ) : Nat.sqrt (N + j + 1) ≤ Nat.sqrt N + j + 1
declarations.docstring: The floor-square-root of a shifted index is controlled by the fixed root plus the shift.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_le_two_sqrt_add_four
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_le_two_sqrt_add_four (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 4
declarations.docstring: **Sharp support-tail strip.** The scaled binary support-coefficient tail grows at most like `2√N + 4`, exactly the envelope used by the T8 Boolean-carry formulation.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_pos_of_exists_pos_mem
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_pos_of_exists_pos_mem (A : Set ℕ) (hA : ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ a ∈ A) (N : ℕ) : 0 < binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N
declarations.docstring: A single positive support element forces every scaled coefficient tail to be strictly positive.

declarations.name: erdosSupportSeries_two_eq_binaryCoeffSeries
declarations.signature: theorem erdosSupportSeries_two_eq_binaryCoeffSeries (A : Set ℕ) : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = binaryCoeffSeries (supportCoeff A)
declarations.docstring: At base two, the support Lambert series is literally the generic binary coefficient series of `supportCoeff A`.

declarations.name: erdosSupportSeries_rational_iff_exists_temperedCarry
declarations.signature: theorem erdosSupportSeries_rational_iff_exists_temperedCarry (A : Set ℕ) : HasRationalValue (erdosSupportSeries 2 A) ↔ ∃ q : ℕ, 0 < q ∧ ∃ U : ℕ → ℤ, IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U
declarations.docstring: Rationality of the support series is exactly existence of a tempered integer carry orbit for its support coefficient.

declarations.name: exists_temperedCarry_of_support_fraction
declarations.signature: theorem exists_temperedCarry_of_support_fraction (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : ∃ U : ℕ → ℤ, U 0 = p ∧ IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U
declarations.docstring: A displayed fraction produces an orbit with that exact denominator. The proof constructs the integer prefix orbit and identifies it with the scaled analytic tail.

declarations.name: support_fraction_of_temperedCarry
declarations.signature: theorem support_fraction_of_temperedCarry (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (hU0 : U 0 = p) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Every tempered carry orbit with initial numerator `p` certifies the displayed fraction `p/q`.

declarations.name: support_fraction_iff_exists_temperedCarry
declarations.signature: theorem support_fraction_iff_exists_temperedCarry (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) ↔ ∃ U : ℕ → ℤ, U 0 = p ∧ IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U
declarations.docstring: Fixed-fraction equivalence form of the Boolean carry trunk.

declarations.name: correctionCarry_add_one_recurrence_iff
declarations.signature: theorem correctionCarry_add_one_recurrence_iff (A : Set ℕ) (K : ℕ → ℤ) (N : ℕ) : K (N + 1) = 2 * K N + 1 - (supportCoeff A (N + 1) : ℤ) ↔ K (N + 1) + 1 = 2 * (K N + 1) - (supportCoeff A (N + 1) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Adding one to the correction recurrence turns its affine input `1 - f_A` into the existing unit support-carry input `f_A`.

declarations.name: correctionCarry_two_mul_add_one_recurrence_iff
declarations.signature: theorem correctionCarry_two_mul_add_one_recurrence_iff (A : Set ℕ) (K : ℕ → ℤ) (N : ℕ) : K (N + 1) = 2 * K N + 1 - (supportCoeff A (N + 1) : ℤ) ↔ 2 * (K (N + 1) + 1) = 2 * (2 * (K N + 1)) - ((2 * supportCoeff A (N + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Doubling the add-one correction state gives exactly the denominator-two support-carry recurrence.

declarations.name: halfCarry_eq_affineBinaryOrbit
declarations.signature: theorem halfCarry_eq_affineBinaryOrbit (A : Set ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (hU0 : U 0 = 1) (hrec : ∀ N : ℕ, U (N + 1) = 2 * U N - ((2 * supportCoeff A (N + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)) : ∀ N : ℕ, U N = affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((2 * supportCoeff A n : ℕ) : ℤ)) 1 N
declarations.docstring: The initial value and recurrence determine the denominator-two support carry uniquely, and identify it with the existing affine orbit.

declarations.name: support_half_iff_affineBinaryOrbit_tempered
declarations.signature: theorem support_half_iff_affineBinaryOrbit_tempered (A : Set ℕ) : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (1 : ℝ) / 2 ↔ IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) 2 (affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((2 * supportCoeff A n : ℕ) : ℤ)) 1)
declarations.docstring: A support has displayed value `1/2` exactly when its canonical affine denominator-two carry is tempered. This is the fixed-fraction carry theorem with the existential orbit removed by recurrence uniqueness.

declarations.name: halfSupportSeries_residual_scaled_eq_affineCarry_sub_tail
declarations.signature: theorem halfSupportSeries_residual_scaled_eq_affineCarry_sub_tail (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : (2 : ℝ) ^ N * ((1 : ℝ) / 2 - erdosSupportSeries 2 A) = (affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((2 * supportCoeff A n : ℕ) : ℤ)) 1 N : ℤ) / 2 - binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N
declarations.docstring: Exact residual identity for the canonical half carry. It is the prefix-plus-scaled-tail decomposition expressed directly in the existing affine-orbit coordinate.

declarations.name: supportCoeff_inter_Iic_eq_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem supportCoeff_inter_Iic_eq_of_le (A : Set ℕ) {n M : ℕ} (hnM : n ≤ M) : supportCoeff (A ∩ Set.Iic M) n = supportCoeff A n
declarations.docstring: Truncating a support above `M` does not change its divisor-count coefficient through level `M`.

declarations.name: affineHalfCarry_inter_Iic_eq
declarations.signature: theorem affineHalfCarry_inter_Iic_eq (A : Set ℕ) (M : ℕ) : affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((2 * supportCoeff (A ∩ Set.Iic M) n : ℕ) : ℤ)) 1 M = affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((2 * supportCoeff A n : ℕ) : ℤ)) 1 M
declarations.docstring: Consequently, the canonical half carry at depth `M` can be computed from the full support or from its finite prefix through `M`.

declarations.name: halfDenominatorCarry_eq_two_mul_integerCarry
declarations.signature: theorem halfDenominatorCarry_eq_two_mul_integerCarry (A : Set ℕ) (hone : 1 ∉ A) (N : ℕ) : affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((2 * supportCoeff A n : ℕ) : ℤ)) 1 (N + 1) = 2 * affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ ↦ (supportCoeff A (n + 1) : ℤ)) 1 N
declarations.docstring: If exponent one is absent, the denominator-two carry factors after its first step as twice an integer affine carry with unit coefficient input. This is the precise `U = 2V` identification from the corrected development.

declarations.name: halfFinitePrefix_residual_eq_pow_mul_integerCarry_sub_finiteTail
declarations.signature: theorem halfFinitePrefix_residual_eq_pow_mul_integerCarry_sub_finiteTail (A : Set ℕ) (hone : 1 ∉ A) (N : ℕ) : (1 : ℝ) / 2 - erdosSupportSeries 2 (A ∩ Set.Iic (N + 1)) = ((affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ ↦ (supportCoeff A (n + 1) : ℤ)) 1 N : ℤ) - binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff (A ∩ Set.Iic (N + 1))) (N + 1)) / (2 : ℝ) ^ (N + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Finite-prefix carry-tail residual formula (the formal development.s equation (18)).** The integer term is the existing affine support carry, while the analytic term is the future-multiple tail generated only by the finite support `A ∩ Iic (N+1)`.

declarations.name: temperedCarry_difference
declarations.signature: theorem temperedCarry_difference (A : Set ℕ) (q : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) (N : ℕ) : 2 * U N - U (N + 1) = (q : ℤ) * (supportCoeff A (N + 1) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The exact carry difference in a support orbit.

declarations.name: denominator_dvd_temperedCarry_difference
declarations.signature: theorem denominator_dvd_temperedCarry_difference (A : Set ℕ) (q : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) (N : ℕ) : (q : ℤ) ∣ 2 * U N - U (N + 1)
declarations.docstring: Divisibility of every carry difference by the displayed denominator.

declarations.name: temperedCarry_quotient_eq_supportCoeff
declarations.signature: theorem temperedCarry_quotient_eq_supportCoeff (A : Set ℕ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) (N : ℕ) : (2 * U N - U (N + 1)) / (q : ℤ) = (supportCoeff A (N + 1) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: After exact division, the carry quotient is precisely `f_A(N+1)`.

declarations.name: temperedCarry_pos_of_exists_pos_mem
declarations.signature: theorem temperedCarry_pos_of_exists_pos_mem (A : Set ℕ) (hA : ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ a ∈ A) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) (N : ℕ) : 0 < U N
declarations.docstring: A positive support and positive multiplier force every state of a tempered support carry to be a positive integer.

declarations.name: temperedCarry_le_denominator_mul_two_sqrt_add_four
declarations.signature: theorem temperedCarry_le_denominator_mul_two_sqrt_add_four (A : Set ℕ) (q : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) (N : ℕ) : (U N : ℝ) ≤ (q : ℝ) * (2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 4)
declarations.docstring: Every tempered support carry lies in the formal development.s sharp square-root strip.

declarations.name: tendsto_div_pow_zero_of_nonnegative_sqrt_bound
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_div_pow_zero_of_nonnegative_sqrt_bound (q : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (hnonneg : ∀ N : ℕ, 0 ≤ U N) (hbound : ∀ N : ℕ, (U N : ℝ) ≤ (q : ℝ) * (2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 4)) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ ↦ (U N : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ N) atTop (nhds 0)
declarations.docstring: The square-root strip is strong enough to enforce the tempered boundary; the proof deliberately relaxes `√N` to `N+1` and uses the already checked linear-over-exponential limit.

declarations.name: carryQuotient
declarations.signature: def carryQuotient (q : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The normalized integer carry quotient. Index zero is forced to zero; at positive index `n` this is `(2U(n-1)-U(n))/q`.

declarations.name: carryQuotientAF
declarations.signature: def carryQuotientAF (q : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℤ) : ArithmeticFunction ℤ
declarations.docstring: The carry quotient packaged as an arithmetic function.

declarations.name: BooleanMobiusCarryCertificate
declarations.signature: structure BooleanMobiusCarryCertificate (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The quotient-only T8 certificate. It mentions no support set: Boolean Möbius inversion reconstructs the unique normalized support afterwards.

declarations.name: carryQuotient_zero
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem carryQuotient_zero (q : ℕ) (U : ℕ → ℤ) : carryQuotient q U 0 = 0

declarations.name: carryQuotientAF_eq_supportCoeffAF
declarations.signature: theorem carryQuotientAF_eq_supportCoeffAF (A : Set ℕ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) : carryQuotientAF q U = supportCoeffAF A
declarations.docstring: A tempered support carry recovers the whole divisor-count coefficient through exact quotient extraction.

declarations.name: moebius_mul_carryQuotientAF
declarations.signature: theorem moebius_mul_carryQuotientAF (A : Set ℕ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) : ArithmeticFunction.moebius * carryQuotientAF q U = positiveSupportBitAF A
declarations.docstring: The Möbius transform of the carry quotient is the normalized support bit. This is the inversion formula `μ * f_U = 1_A`.

declarations.name: mobius_carryQuotient_boolean
declarations.signature: theorem mobius_carryQuotient_boolean (A : Set ℕ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) (n : ℕ) : (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * carryQuotientAF q U) n = 0 ∨ (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * carryQuotientAF q U) n = 1
declarations.docstring: Hence the Möbius transform of every exact carry quotient is Boolean.

declarations.name: mobius_carryQuotient_recovers_support
declarations.signature: theorem mobius_carryQuotient_recovers_support (A : Set ℕ) (hzero : 0 ∉ A) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (horbit : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit (supportCoeff A) q U) : {n : ℕ | (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * carryQuotientAF q U) n = 1} = A
declarations.docstring: With `0 ∉ A`, the carry quotient's Boolean Möbius transform recovers the support literally as a set.

declarations.name: exists_booleanMobiusCarry_of_support_fraction
declarations.signature: theorem exists_booleanMobiusCarry_of_support_fraction (A : Set ℕ) (hzero : 0 ∉ A) (hpos : ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ a ∈ A) (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : ∃ U : ℕ → ℤ, BooleanMobiusCarryCertificate p q U ∧ {n : ℕ | (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * carryQuotientAF q U) n = 1} = A
declarations.docstring: **Forward T8 direction.** A normalized nonempty support with value `p/q` produces a positive square-root-bounded integer orbit whose differences are divisible by `q`, whose carry quotient has Boolean Möbius transform, and whose selected support is exactly the original `A`.

declarations.name: support_fraction_of_booleanMobiusCarry
declarations.signature: theorem support_fraction_of_booleanMobiusCarry (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (U : ℕ → ℤ) (cert : BooleanMobiusCarryCertificate p q U) : let A
declarations.docstring: **Converse T8 direction.** A quotient-only Boolean carry certificate reconstructs a normalized support `A`, becomes a tempered support orbit for that `A`, and certifies the exact value `p/q`.

declarations.name: BooleanMobiusCarryCertificate.reconstructsSupport
declarations.signature: theorem BooleanMobiusCarryCertificate.reconstructsSupport {p : ℤ} {q : ℕ} {U : ℕ → ℤ} (hq : 0 < q) (cert : BooleanMobiusCarryCertificate p q U) : let A
declarations.docstring: A quotient-only Boolean carry certificate exposes every reconstructed object used by the converse, not only the final scalar identity.

declarations.name: exists_normalized_support_fraction_iff_exists_booleanMobiusCarry
declarations.signature: theorem exists_normalized_support_fraction_iff_exists_booleanMobiusCarry (p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) : (∃ A : Set ℕ, 0 ∉ A ∧ (∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ a ∈ A) ∧ erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) ↔ ∃ U : ℕ → ℤ, BooleanMobiusCarryCertificate p q U
declarations.docstring: **Certificate T8 equivalence.** Positive normalized supports with value `p/q` are in exact correspondence at the existence level with quotient-only Boolean Möbius carry certificates. The converse support is not guessed: it is reconstructed as `booleanMobiusSupport` of the carry quotient.

declarations.name: support23
declarations.docstring: The two-point support used in the formal development.s explicit orbit check.

declarations.name: supportCoeff23Residue
declarations.docstring: The positive-index coefficient `f_{\{2,3\}}`, represented by its six residue values. Its value at zero is a table convenience and is never used as an arithmetic-function value.

declarations.name: carryOrbit23
declarations.docstring: The formal development.s pure period-six numerator orbit.

declarations.name: mod_six_cases
declarations.signature: private theorem mod_six_cases (n : ℕ) : n % 6 = 0 ∨ n % 6 = 1 ∨ n % 6 = 2 ∨ n % 6 = 3 ∨ n % 6 = 4 ∨ n % 6 = 5

declarations.name: supportCoeff23Residue_eq_divisibility
declarations.signature: theorem supportCoeff23Residue_eq_divisibility (n : ℕ) : supportCoeff23Residue n = (if 2 ∣ n then 1 else 0) + (if 3 ∣ n then 1 else 0)
declarations.docstring: Residue form equals the expected pair of divisibility indicators.

declarations.name: supportCoeff_support23_eq_residue
declarations.signature: theorem supportCoeff_support23_eq_residue {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : supportCoeff support23 n = supportCoeff23Residue n
declarations.docstring: The residue table is not an auxiliary model: on positive integers it is exactly the kernel's `supportCoeff` for `{2,3}`.

declarations.name: erdosSupportSeries_support23_eq_ten_div_twenty_one
declarations.docstring: Exact value of the support series: `1/3 + 1/7 = 10/21`.

declarations.name: carryOrbit23_initial_cycle
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit23_initial_cycle : carryOrbit23 0 = 10 ∧ carryOrbit23 1 = 20 ∧ carryOrbit23 2 = 19 ∧ carryOrbit23 3 = 17 ∧ carryOrbit23 4 = 13 ∧ carryOrbit23 5 = 26
declarations.docstring: The six listed orbit values, in their unambiguous order `U₀,...,U₅`.

declarations.name: carryOrbit23_periodic
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit23_periodic (N : ℕ) : carryOrbit23 (N + 6) = carryOrbit23 N
declarations.docstring: The orbit is purely periodic with period six.

declarations.name: carryOrbit23_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit23_bounds (N : ℕ) : 10 ≤ carryOrbit23 N ∧ carryOrbit23 N ≤ 26
declarations.docstring: Uniform positive bounds for the explicit orbit.

declarations.name: carryOrbit23_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit23_recurrence (N : ℕ) : carryOrbit23 (N + 1) = 2 * carryOrbit23 N - ((21 * supportCoeff support23 (N + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Exact carry recurrence for the explicit orbit.

declarations.name: carryOrbit23_isTempered
declarations.docstring: The explicit six-cycle is a genuine tempered integer carry orbit, not merely a finite recurrence check.

declarations.name: ten_coprime_twenty_one
declarations.docstring: The displayed fraction is reduced.

declarations.name: twenty_one_dvd_carryOrbit23_difference
declarations.signature: theorem twenty_one_dvd_carryOrbit23_difference (N : ℕ) : (21 : ℤ) ∣ 2 * carryOrbit23 N - carryOrbit23 (N + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact divisibility of every difference in the explicit six-cycle.

declarations.name: carryOrbit23_quotient_eq_supportCoeff
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit23_quotient_eq_supportCoeff (N : ℕ) : (2 * carryOrbit23 N - carryOrbit23 (N + 1)) / (21 : ℤ) = (supportCoeff support23 (N + 1) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Exact quotient recovery in the explicit six-cycle.

declarations.name: mobius_carryOrbit23_recovers_support
declarations.signature: theorem mobius_carryOrbit23_recovers_support : {n : ℕ | (ArithmeticFunction.moebius * carryQuotientAF 21 carryOrbit23) n = 1} = support23
declarations.docstring: The explicit quotient's Möbius transform recovers exactly `{2,3}`.

declarations.name: carryOrbit23_eq_twenty_one_mul_tail
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit23_eq_twenty_one_mul_tail (N : ℕ) : (carryOrbit23 N : ℝ) = 21 * binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff support23) N
declarations.docstring: The analytic scaled-tail identity behind the six-cycle.

declarations.name: carryOrbit23_positive_and_sqrt_bounded
declarations.signature: theorem carryOrbit23_positive_and_sqrt_bounded (N : ℕ) : 0 < carryOrbit23 N ∧ (carryOrbit23 N : ℝ) ≤ 21 * (2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 4)
declarations.docstring: The explicit orbit satisfies the sharp positive square-root strip.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffPrefix
declarations.signature: noncomputable def binaryCoeffPrefix (c : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ → ℝ | 0 => 0 | N + 1 => binaryCoeffPrefix c N + (c (N + 1) : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ (N + 1) /-- Integer numerator of the same dyadic prefix at denominator `2^N`. -/ def binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator (c : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ | 0 => 0 | N + 1 => 2 * binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator c N + c (N + 1) /-- Natural-valued membership bit of a support. Unlike `supportCoeff`, this is the actual binary word used
declarations.docstring: The first `N` binary Lambert coefficients, before carrying.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator
declarations.signature: def binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator (c : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ | 0 => 0 | N + 1 => 2 * binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator c N + c (N + 1) /-- Natural-valued membership bit of a support. Unlike `supportCoeff`, this is the actual binary word used
declarations.docstring: Integer numerator of the same dyadic prefix at denominator `2^N`.

declarations.name: supportMembershipBit
declarations.signature: noncomputable def supportMembershipBit (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Natural-valued membership bit of a support. Unlike `supportCoeff`, this is the actual binary word used by the dyadic-correction fixed point.

declarations.name: supportMembershipBit_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem supportMembershipBit_le_one (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : supportMembershipBit A n ≤ 1

declarations.name: supportMembershipBit_eq_zero_iff
declarations.signature: theorem supportMembershipBit_eq_zero_iff (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : supportMembershipBit A n = 0 ↔ n ∉ A

declarations.name: supportMembershipBit_eq_one_iff
declarations.signature: theorem supportMembershipBit_eq_one_iff (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : supportMembershipBit A n = 1 ↔ n ∈ A

declarations.name: supportDyadicPrefixNumerator
declarations.signature: noncomputable def supportDyadicPrefixNumerator (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Dyadic numerator of the actual support word through depth `N`.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator_div_pow
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator_div_pow (c : ℕ → ℕ) : ∀ N : ℕ, (binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator c N : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ N = binaryCoeffPrefix c N
declarations.docstring: The recursive numerator really represents `binaryCoeffPrefix` at the common dyadic denominator.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator_terminal_zero_of_pow_two_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator_terminal_zero_of_pow_two_dvd (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hbit : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ 1) : ∀ {N r : ℕ}, r ≤ N → 2 ^ r ∣ binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator c N → ∀ n : ℕ, N - r < n → n ≤ N → c n = 0
declarations.docstring: If a binary prefix numerator has `r` trailing zero bits, then its final `r` coefficients vanish. This is the exact arithmetic bridge from a large two-adic boundary valuation in the correction iteration to a long skipped block in the underlying support word.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator_terminal_one_of_pow_two_dvd_succ
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator_terminal_one_of_pow_two_dvd_succ (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hbit : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ 1) : ∀ {N r : ℕ}, r ≤ N → 2 ^ r ∣ binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator c N + 1 → ∀ n : ℕ, N - r < n → n ≤ N → c n = 1
declarations.docstring: If `2^r` divides one plus a binary prefix numerator, its final `r` coefficients are all one. This is the right-boundary companion to `binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator_terminal_zero_of_pow_two_dvd`.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator_pow_two_dvd_of_terminal_zero
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator_pow_two_dvd_of_terminal_zero (c : ℕ → ℕ) : ∀ {N r : ℕ}, r ≤ N → (∀ n : ℕ, N - r < n → n ≤ N → c n = 0) → 2 ^ r ∣ binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator c N
declarations.docstring: Conversely, a zero terminal block contributes an explicit power of two to the binary prefix numerator.

declarations.name: supportDyadicPrefixNumerator_terminal_gap_of_pow_two_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem supportDyadicPrefixNumerator_terminal_gap_of_pow_two_dvd (A : Set ℕ) {N r : ℕ} (hr : r ≤ N) (hdiv : 2 ^ r ∣ supportDyadicPrefixNumerator A N) : ∀ n : ℕ, N - r < n → n ≤ N → n ∉ A
declarations.docstring: Divisibility of a support-word numerator by `2^r` means that the final `r` membership bits are all zero.

declarations.name: supportDyadicPrefixNumerator_terminal_full_of_pow_two_dvd_succ
declarations.signature: theorem supportDyadicPrefixNumerator_terminal_full_of_pow_two_dvd_succ (A : Set ℕ) {N r : ℕ} (hr : r ≤ N) (hdiv : 2 ^ r ∣ supportDyadicPrefixNumerator A N + 1) : ∀ n : ℕ, N - r < n → n ≤ N → n ∈ A
declarations.docstring: Divisibility of one plus a support-word numerator by `2^r` means that the final `r` membership bits are all selected.

declarations.name: supportDyadicPrefixNumerator_empty_doublingBlock_iff
declarations.signature: theorem supportDyadicPrefixNumerator_empty_doublingBlock_iff (A : Set ℕ) (K : ℕ) : (∀ n : ℕ, K < n → n ≤ 2 * K → n ∉ A) ↔ 2 ^ K ∣ supportDyadicPrefixNumerator A (2 * K)
declarations.docstring: Exact support-word form: an empty doubling block is equivalent to `K` trailing zero bits in the depth-`2*K` dyadic numerator.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffSeries_eq_prefix_add_tail
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffSeries_eq_prefix_add_tail (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) : ∀ N : ℕ, binaryCoeffSeries c = binaryCoeffPrefix c N + binaryCoeffTail c N / (2 : ℝ) ^ N
declarations.docstring: Exact prefix/tail decomposition of the binary Lambert series.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffPrefix_supportCoeff_inter_Iic_eq
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffPrefix_supportCoeff_inter_Iic_eq (A : Set ℕ) {N M : ℕ} (hNM : N ≤ M) : binaryCoeffPrefix (supportCoeff (A ∩ Set.Iic M)) N = binaryCoeffPrefix (supportCoeff A) N
declarations.docstring: Restricting a support above `M` leaves its binary prefix through `N ≤ M` unchanged.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportValue_inter_Iic_eq_prefix
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportValue_inter_Iic_eq_prefix (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportValue (A ∩ Set.Iic N) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, Set.indicator A mersenneWeight (k + 1)
declarations.docstring: The support value cut off at exponent `N` is exactly its displayed finite prefix.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffPrefix_greedySupport_le
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffPrefix_greedySupport_le {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (N : ℕ) : binaryCoeffPrefix (supportCoeff (greedyMersenneSupport x)) N ≤ x
declarations.docstring: The binary Lambert prefix generated by the first `N` greedy choices is bounded by the target. This is the analytic source of the unconditional one-sided carry estimate.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyFinitePrefixTail
declarations.docstring: The scaled future-multiple tail generated by the first `N` choices of the denominator-`21` greedy support. Truncating the support is essential: this quantity is determined at depth `N`, without assuming any future greedy decisions or achievement-set membership.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyCarry
declarations.docstring: The canonical denominator-`21` carry driven by the greedy support of `1/21`.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyCarry_succ
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyCarry_succ (N : ℕ) : twentyOneGreedyCarry (N + 1) = 2 * twentyOneGreedyCarry N - ((21 * supportCoeff (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)) (N + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Exact carry recurrence.

declarations.name: scaled_twentyOneGreedyCarry_antitone
declarations.signature: theorem scaled_twentyOneGreedyCarry_antitone : Antitone (fun N : ℕ => (twentyOneGreedyCarry N : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ N)
declarations.docstring: The denominator-`21` carry divided by its binary place value is antitone. This is the mechanism which turns cofinally many small returns into a global limit theorem.

declarations.name: affineSupportCarry_eq_pow_mul_prefixResidual
declarations.signature: theorem affineSupportCarry_eq_pow_mul_prefixResidual (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℤ) (q N : ℕ) : (affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ => ((q * supportCoeff A n : ℕ) : ℤ)) p N : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ) ^ N * ((p : ℝ) - (q : ℝ) * binaryCoeffPrefix (supportCoeff A) N)
declarations.docstring: Closed finite-prefix formula for an affine support carry.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyCarry_eq_scaled_remainder_add_finitePrefixTail
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyCarry_eq_scaled_remainder_add_finitePrefixTail (N : ℕ) : (twentyOneGreedyCarry N : ℝ) = 21 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ N * greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) N + twentyOneGreedyFinitePrefixTail N)
declarations.docstring: **Exact defect/remainder bridge before taking a limit.** The denominator-`21` carry is the sum of two nonnegative depth-`N` quantities: the actual greedy remainder scaled by `2^N`, and the future-multiple tail generated by the already selected finite prefix. No survival, tempering, or future-support hypothesis is used.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyFinitePrefixTail_nonneg
declarations.docstring: The finite-prefix divisor tail is nonnegative at every depth.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyFinitePrefixTail_le_two_sqrt_add_four
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyFinitePrefixTail_le_two_sqrt_add_four (N : ℕ) : twentyOneGreedyFinitePrefixTail N ≤ 2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 4
declarations.docstring: The universal divisor-pair estimate applies to the finite-prefix tail without any information about future greedy choices.

declarations.name: affineSupportCarry_eq_pow_sub_prefixNumerator
declarations.signature: theorem affineSupportCarry_eq_pow_sub_prefixNumerator (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℤ) (q N : ℕ) : affineBinaryOrbit (fun n : ℕ => ((q * supportCoeff A n : ℕ) : ℤ)) p N = (2 : ℤ) ^ N * p - (q : ℤ) * (binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator (supportCoeff A) N : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Exact integer form of the affine-prefix identity.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyCarry_nonneg
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional all-depth estimate.** The denominator-`21` greedy carry is nonnegative at every depth. Equivalently, the signed periodic-bit carry used in the Booleanisation search is nonpositive at every depth.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyPrefixNumerator_le_div
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyPrefixNumerator_le_div (N : ℕ) : binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator (supportCoeff (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ))) N ≤ 2 ^ N / 21
declarations.docstring: The displayed greedy Lambert numerator lies below the integral quotient `⌊2^N / 21⌋`. This isolates the exact natural-number subtraction hidden in the denominator-`21` carry.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect
declarations.docstring: The genuinely dynamical part of the denominator-`21` carry, after removing the six-periodic residue of `2^N mod 21`. Unlike the raw carry, this coordinate starts at zero and is an ordinary natural number.

declarations.name: twentyOneFloorBit
declarations.docstring: The next binary digit of the periodic rational baseline `⌊2^N / 21⌋`, represented in an integer form that makes the defect recurrence division-free.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_cast_eq
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_cast_eq (N : ℕ) : (twentyOneGreedyDefect N : ℤ) = ((2 ^ N / 21 : ℕ) : ℤ) - (binaryCoeffPrefixNumerator (supportCoeff (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ))) N : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Cast form of the defect definition, with the natural subtraction certified by the greedy prefix bound.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_succ
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_succ (N : ℕ) : (twentyOneGreedyDefect (N + 1) : ℤ) = 2 * (twentyOneGreedyDefect N : ℤ) + twentyOneFloorBit N - (supportCoeff (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)) (N + 1) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The exact one-dimensional recurrence behind the certified computation. The only nonperiodic input is the actual greedy divisor-count coefficient.

declarations.name: twentyOneFloorBit_eq_two_mul_mod_div
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneFloorBit_eq_two_mul_mod_div (N : ℕ) : twentyOneFloorBit N = ((2 * (2 ^ N % 21) / 21 : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The next denominator-`21` floor bit is the quotient of twice the current period residue. In particular it is a genuine binary digit.

declarations.name: twentyOneFloorBit_le_one
declarations.docstring: The periodic denominator-`21` baseline contributes at most one unit in each one-step defect transition.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_succ_le
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_succ_le (N : ℕ) : twentyOneGreedyDefect (N + 1) ≤ 2 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 1
declarations.docstring: Dropping the nonnegative divisor load from the exact recurrence gives the universal one-step growth envelope for the natural defect.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_one_le_pow_mul
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_one_le_pow_mul (N L : ℕ) : twentyOneGreedyDefect (N + L) + 1 ≤ 2 ^ L * (twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 1)
declarations.docstring: Iterated one-step growth in a subtraction-free form. The added unit turns `Q ↦ 2Q+1` into pure dyadic multiplication.

declarations.name: twentyOneSixStepRepairLoad
declarations.docstring: The divisor load removed from the defect during the six ranks after `N`. The weights are the exact binary propagation weights in the iterated defect recurrence.

declarations.name: twentyOneFloorBit_six_weighted
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneFloorBit_six_weighted (N : ℕ) : 32 * twentyOneFloorBit N + 16 * twentyOneFloorBit (N + 1) + 8 * twentyOneFloorBit (N + 2) + 4 * twentyOneFloorBit (N + 3) + 2 * twentyOneFloorBit (N + 4) + twentyOneFloorBit (N + 5) = 3 * ((2 ^ N % 21 : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Six periodic baseline bits telescope to three times the current remainder modulo `21`. This is the arithmetic reason that blocks of six are the natural scale for the denominator-`21` defect.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_six
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_six (N : ℕ) : (twentyOneGreedyDefect (N + 6) : ℤ) = 64 * (twentyOneGreedyDefect N : ℤ) + 3 * ((2 ^ N % 21 : ℕ) : ℤ) - (twentyOneSixStepRepairLoad N : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Exact six-step defect dynamics. The exponentially magnified old defect is opposed by the actual weighted divisor load accumulated over the next six greedy ranks.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_six_le_iff_repairLoad
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_six_le_iff_repairLoad (N : ℕ) : twentyOneGreedyDefect (N + 6) ≤ twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 1 ↔ 63 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 3 * (2 ^ N % 21) ≤ twentyOneSixStepRepairLoad N + 1
declarations.docstring: A six-rank block contracts the defect to `Q_N + 1` exactly when its weighted divisor load pays the full `63 Q_N` amplification plus the periodic residue charge. This is an iff, so the remaining frontier is a finite-window load inequality rather than an opaque real approximation.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_six_le_div_six_iff_repairLoad
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_six_le_div_six_iff_repairLoad (N : ℕ) : twentyOneGreedyDefect (N + 6) ≤ (N + 6) / 6 ↔ 64 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 3 * (2 ^ N % 21) ≤ twentyOneSixStepRepairLoad N + N / 6 + 1
declarations.docstring: The exact slope-aware form of the six-step recurrence. Unlike the translation-invariant contraction above, this spends all slack already accumulated below `⌊N/6⌋`; exact computation shows that this distinction is essential, since the translation-invariant contraction first fails at `N = 73` while the slope envelope survives.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyDefectSlopeDanger
declarations.docstring: A rank is slope-dangerous precisely when the old defect and periodic charge already exceed the next `⌊N/6⌋` allowance before any of the six new divisor loads are credited. At every other rank the desired slope step is automatic.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_six_le_div_six_of_not_slopeDanger
declarations.docstring: Outside the slope-danger region, nonnegativity of the repair load alone closes the next six-rank slope step.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefectSlopeDanger_rank_lt
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefectSlopeDanger_rank_lt (N : ℕ) (hdanger : TwentyOneGreedyDefectSlopeDanger N) : N < 384 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 354
declarations.docstring: Every slope-dangerous rank is genuinely a high-defect rank. Thus the repair-load frontier is confined to `N < 384 Q_N + 354`; the vast low-defect region needs no divisor arithmetic at all.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_le_div_six_of_dangerRepairLoad
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_le_div_six_of_dangerRepairLoad (hbase : ∀ N : ℕ, N < 6 → twentyOneGreedyDefect N = 0) (hdanger : ∀ N : ℕ, TwentyOneGreedyDefectSlopeDanger N → 64 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 3 * (2 ^ N % 21) ≤ twentyOneSixStepRepairLoad N + N / 6 + 1) : ∀ N : ℕ, twentyOneGreedyDefect N ≤ N / 6
declarations.docstring: The sharp slope envelope now asks for repair load only at exact slope-danger ranks. This is strictly weaker than a false uniform block contraction: safe ranks close from accumulated slack, while dangerous ranks pay only the load actually needed to remain below `⌊(N+6)/6⌋`.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_le_div_six_of_highDefectRepairLoad
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_le_div_six_of_highDefectRepairLoad (hbase : ∀ N : ℕ, N < 6 → twentyOneGreedyDefect N = 0) (hload : ∀ N : ℕ, N < 384 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 354 → 64 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 3 * (2 ^ N % 21) ≤ twentyOneSixStepRepairLoad N + N / 6 + 1) : ∀ N : ℕ, twentyOneGreedyDefect N ≤ N / 6
declarations.docstring: A slightly coarser but simpler producer may discharge the load inequality only under the explicit high-defect condition `N < 384 Q_N + 354`.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_le_div_six_of_blockContraction
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_le_div_six_of_blockContraction (hbase : ∀ N : ℕ, N < 6 → twentyOneGreedyDefect N = 0) (hblock : ∀ N : ℕ, twentyOneGreedyDefect (N + 6) ≤ twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 1) : ∀ N : ℕ, twentyOneGreedyDefect N ≤ N / 6
declarations.docstring: The block contraction plus the six initial rows implies the observed global bound `Q_N ≤ ⌊N/6⌋`. This separates the finite base certificate from the repeating arithmetic obligation.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyDefectFloorSlopeBlockContraction
declarations.docstring: A floor-slope contraction over a configurable block. Exact falsification shows that the smallest surviving block grows with the tested horizon, so the block length is deliberately not hardcoded.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_le_div_six_of_floorSlopeBlockContraction
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_le_div_six_of_floorSlopeBlockContraction {B : ℕ} (hBpos : 0 < B) (hBdiv : 6 ∣ B) (hbase : ∀ N : ℕ, N < B → twentyOneGreedyDefect N ≤ N / 6) (hblock : TwentyOneGreedyDefectFloorSlopeBlockContraction B) : ∀ N : ℕ, twentyOneGreedyDefect N ≤ N / 6
declarations.docstring: Any positive block divisible by six gives a valid induction scheme. The finite base strip and the translation-invariant block contraction imply the sharp all-depth `⌊N/6⌋` envelope.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyCarry_ge_pow_mod
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyCarry_ge_pow_mod (N : ℕ) : ((2 ^ N % 21 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ twentyOneGreedyCarry N
declarations.docstring: The carry is at least the ordinary period-six remainder `2^N mod 21`. This is the precise all-depth form of nonnegativity for the signed periodic Lambert defect.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyCarry_eq_mod_add_defect
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyCarry_eq_mod_add_defect (N : ℕ) : twentyOneGreedyCarry N = ((2 ^ N % 21 : ℕ) : ℤ) + 21 * (twentyOneGreedyDefect N : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Exact periodic-baseline decomposition. All unboundedness questions are therefore concentrated in the natural-valued defect `Q_N`; the residue term is uniformly below `21`.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_mod_div_eq_scaled_remainder_add_tail
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_mod_div_eq_scaled_remainder_add_tail (N : ℕ) : (twentyOneGreedyDefect N : ℝ) + ((2 ^ N % 21 : ℕ) : ℝ) / 21 = (2 : ℝ) ^ N * greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) N + twentyOneGreedyFinitePrefixTail N
declarations.docstring: Exact real decomposition of the defect coordinate. The periodic remainder fraction, the scaled actual greedy remainder, and the finite-prefix divisor tail are now separated with no limiting argument.

declarations.name: two_pow_mul_mersenneWeight_le_two
declarations.signature: theorem two_pow_mul_mersenneWeight_le_two {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) : (2 : ℝ) ^ N * mersenneWeight N ≤ 2
declarations.docstring: A positive-index Mersenne weight occupies at most two units after dyadic rescaling. This deliberately keeps the sharp endpoint at rank one: `2^N / (2^N - 1) ≤ 2`.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_lt_two_sqrt_add_six_of_skip
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_lt_two_sqrt_add_six_of_skip {N : ℕ} (hskip : N ∈ greedyMersenneSkippedSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)) : (twentyOneGreedyDefect N : ℝ) < 2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 6
declarations.docstring: At every omitted greedy exponent, the denominator-`21` defect is only square-root sized. A skip leaves the remainder unchanged and strictly below the omitted Mersenne weight; after dyadic rescaling this costs fewer than two units. The remaining defect is therefore confined to the universal finite-prefix divisor tail.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_one_lt_pow_mul_sqrt_of_skip
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_one_lt_pow_mul_sqrt_of_skip {N : ℕ} (L : ℕ) (hskip : N ∈ greedyMersenneSkippedSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)) : (twentyOneGreedyDefect (N + L) : ℝ) + 1 < (2 : ℝ) ^ L * (2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 7)
declarations.docstring: A skip at rank `N` constrains the defect at every later rank `N+L`. Consequently, a violation of this explicit dyadic-square-root envelope is a certificate that the earlier rank was selected.

declarations.name: mem_greedyMersenneSupport_of_defect_growth_threshold
declarations.signature: theorem mem_greedyMersenneSupport_of_defect_growth_threshold {N L : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) (hlarge : (2 : ℝ) ^ L * (2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 7) ≤ (twentyOneGreedyDefect (N + L) : ℝ) + 1) : N ∈ greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Large later defect forces selection at the earlier rank. This is the contrapositive interface used to turn defect growth into a certified long selected run.

declarations.name: twentyOne_scaled_greedyRemainder_le_defect_add_one
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_scaled_greedyRemainder_le_defect_add_one (N : ℕ) : (2 : ℝ) ^ N * greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) N ≤ (twentyOneGreedyDefect N : ℝ) + 1
declarations.docstring: The scaled actual remainder is at most `Q_N + 1`. This is the non-circular direction of the defect bridge: the finite divisor tail is nonnegative and the periodic residue is strictly below the denominator.

declarations.name: twentyOne_defect_sub_two_sqrt_sub_four_le_scaled_greedyRemainder
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_defect_sub_two_sqrt_sub_four_le_scaled_greedyRemainder (N : ℕ) : (twentyOneGreedyDefect N : ℝ) - (2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 4) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ N * greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) N
declarations.docstring: Conversely, after subtracting the universal `O(√N)` finite-tail allowance, every remaining unit of defect is forced into the actual scaled greedy remainder. Thus a linearly large danger defect cannot be hidden in old divisor corrections.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyCarryCofinalLinearReturn
declarations.docstring: Beyond every requested depth, the carry returns below a linear envelope. This is strictly weaker than a uniform all-depth square-root estimate.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyCarry_scaled_tendsto_zero_of_cofinalLinearReturn
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyCarry_scaled_tendsto_zero_of_cofinalLinearReturn (hreturn : TwentyOneGreedyCarryCofinalLinearReturn) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (twentyOneGreedyCarry N : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ N) atTop (nhds 0)
declarations.docstring: Cofinal linear returns force the whole scaled carry to zero. The antitone scaled orbit propagates each late return to every later depth.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_carry_tendsto
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_carry_tendsto (hcarry : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (twentyOneGreedyCarry N : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ N) atTop (nhds 0)) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Any subexponential upper bound implies the prescribed-point membership. The lower squeeze bound is supplied by `twentyOneGreedyCarry_nonneg`, so the only remaining mathematical burden is an upper estimate, and that estimate remains unproved.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_cofinalLinearReturn
declarations.docstring: A cofinal sequence of merely linear returns already implies the prescribed-point membership. The return condition remains unproved.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyDefectSlopeStepCofinally
declarations.docstring: It is enough for the sharp floor-slope estimate to hold after one six-step block at cofinally many starting ranks. No estimate is required between those ranks.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_slopeStepCofinally
declarations.docstring: Cofinal floor-slope steps already give the cofinal linear carry returns needed for membership. This discards both a global defect bound and any bound on the gaps between successful steps.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyDefectSlopeSafeCofinally
declarations.docstring: The experimentally dominant route: it suffices that slope-safe ranks occur cofinally. At each such rank the six-step floor bound is automatic, so no repair-load estimate is needed there.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyDefectCofinalLinearSeparation
declarations.docstring: A concrete cofinal sublinear-return target. It asks only for arbitrarily late ranks at which the defect lies below the very weak affine threshold `(N - 354) / 384`; neither boundedness nor an all-depth estimate is required.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_eventually_slopeDanger_of_not_mem
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_eventually_slopeDanger_of_not_mem (hnot : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∉ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, K ≤ N → TwentyOneGreedyDefectSlopeDanger N
declarations.docstring: Contrapositive classification: non-membership cannot merely produce occasional large defects. It forces every sufficiently late rank to be slope-dangerous.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_eventually_linearLower_of_not_mem
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_eventually_linearLower_of_not_mem (hnot : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∉ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, K ≤ N → N < 384 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 354
declarations.docstring: Hence the sole non-membership branch has an eventual explicit linear lower bound on the defect. One arbitrarily late violation of this bound already proves membership.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainder_sub_tail_eq_of_fatalAt_add
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneRemainder_sub_tail_eq_of_fatalAt_add {x : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hfatal : GreedyMersenneFatalAt x n) (k : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainder x (n + k) - mersenneTail (n + k) = greedyMersenneRemainder x n - mersenneTail n
declarations.docstring: Once a greedy state is fatal, its excess over the complete remaining Mersenne tail is conserved exactly. Both quantities lose the same selected weight at every later step.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_one_ge_geometric_fatalExcess
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_add_one_ge_geometric_fatalExcess {n : ℕ} (hfatal : GreedyMersenneFatalAt (1 / 21 : ℝ) n) (k : ℕ) : (2 : ℝ) ^ (n + k) * (greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) n - mersenneTail n) ≤ (twentyOneGreedyDefect (n + k) : ℝ) + 1
declarations.docstring: A fatal denominator-`21` state forces a geometric lower bound on the defect. The fixed positive tail excess is multiplied by `2^(n+k)`; the exact defect/remainder bridge loses only the harmless additive unit.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefect_geometricLower_of_not_mem
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyDefect_geometricLower_of_not_mem (hnot : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∉ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, (2 : ℝ) ^ (n + k) * δ ≤ (twentyOneGreedyDefect (n + k) : ℝ) + 1
declarations.docstring: Non-membership is therefore exponentially rigid: it supplies one positive constant `δ` such that `2^(n+k) δ ≤ Q_(n+k)+1` at every later rank. The earlier eventual linear lower bound is only a coarse shadow of this fatal-tail alternative.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyDefectSubexponential
declarations.docstring: Direct defect-coordinate version of subexponentiality. Unlike a global polynomial bound, it asks only that `Q_N+1` eventually lie below every fixed positive multiple of `2^N`.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_defectSubexponential
declarations.docstring: Any subexponential estimate in the natural-valued defect coordinate rules out the geometrically growing fatal branch and proves membership.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyCarry_scaled_tendsto_zero_of_mem
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyCarry_scaled_tendsto_zero_of_mem (hmem : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (twentyOneGreedyCarry N : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ N) atTop (nhds 0)
declarations.docstring: Membership supplies the missing tempered boundary for the *canonical* denominator-`21` greedy carry. The support code witnessing membership is necessarily the greedy code; the displayed-fraction carry it produces has the same initial state and recurrence as `twentyOneGreedyCarry`, hence is that carry by induction.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyDefectSubexponential_of_mem
declarations.docstring: Conversely, actual membership forces the natural defect to be subexponential. The periodic-baseline decomposition bounds `Q_N + 1` by the nonnegative carry plus one, so the tempered carry limit transfers directly to the defect coordinate.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_iff_greedyDefectSubexponential
declarations.docstring: **Exact normalized-defect characterization.** The prescribed point is represented if and only if the canonical denominator-`21` defect is subexponential relative to `2^N`. Thus the subexponential producer is not an arbitrary sufficient bound: it is precisely the remaining asymptotic content of the problem in this coordinate.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyDefectNormalizedSmallCofinally
declarations.docstring: Weakest normalized-return producer exposed by the fatal/subexponential dichotomy: after every cutoff, `Q_N + 1` falls below any prescribed positive multiple of `2^N` at some later rank. Unlike subexponentiality, this imposes no eventual bound at all; a single sufficiently small normalized return beyond each cutoff is enough.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_iff_defectNormalizedSmallCofinally
declarations.docstring: **Exact cofinal normalized-return characterization.** Membership at `1/21` is equivalent to arbitrarily small normalized defect returns occurring cofinally. The reverse implication uses only the fatal geometric lower bound: a single cofinal return below its fixed positive excess contradicts non-membership.

declarations.name: TwentyOneScaledGreedyRemainderCofinallyBounded
declarations.docstring: Weakest bounded-return formulation in the native greedy coordinate: there is one fixed ceiling hit by the scaled remainder beyond every cutoff. No convergence, return frequency, or prescribed ceiling is required.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_iff_scaledGreedyRemainderCofinallyBounded
declarations.docstring: **Exact cofinal scaled-remainder characterization.** Membership at `1/21` is equivalent to the scaled greedy remainder returning cofinally to one fixed bounded interval. On the surviving branch the scaled remainder is bounded by the scaled complete tail, which tends to `1`. On the fatal branch one fixed positive tail excess is conserved, so multiplication by `2^N` eventually exceeds every proposed ceiling.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyDangerRepairSucceedsCofinally
declarations.docstring: Most generally, at cofinally many ranks either floor slack closes the block automatically or the exact repair-load inequality pays for it.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyDefectCofinallyBounded
declarations.docstring: The denominator-`21` defect need not obey a uniform slope bound. It suffices that some fixed bounded defect band is visited beyond every cutoff. This concrete interface matches the certified repeated returns to `Q_N ≤ 1`; the slope-safe cofinal interface above is weaker still and also allows the defect to grow sublinearly.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_defectCofinallyBounded
declarations.docstring: Cofinal returns to any fixed defect band force cofinal linear carry returns and hence membership of the prescribed rational point.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_defect_le_one_cofinally
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_defect_le_one_cofinally (hreturn : ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ M : ℕ, N ≤ M ∧ twentyOneGreedyDefect M ≤ 1) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: The concrete band seen by exact computation is `Q_N ≤ 1`. Proving that it recurs cofinally is already enough; no global bound on the defect or on the gaps between returns is required.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_defect_le_div_six
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_defect_le_div_six (hdefect : ∀ N : ℕ, twentyOneGreedyDefect N ≤ N / 6) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Exact one-dimensional arithmetic target suggested by the certified greedy computation. Proving `Q_N ≤ ⌊N/6⌋` at every depth would solve the prescribed-point problem outright.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_sixStepRepairLoad
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_sixStepRepairLoad (hbase : ∀ N : ℕ, N < 6 → twentyOneGreedyDefect N = 0) (hload : ∀ N : ℕ, 63 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 3 * (2 ^ N % 21) ≤ twentyOneSixStepRepairLoad N + 1) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: A finite six-row base check and the exact repair-load inequality solve the prescribed point `1/21`. No asymptotic estimate remains in this interface.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_dangerRepairLoad
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_dangerRepairLoad (hbase : ∀ N : ℕ, N < 6 → twentyOneGreedyDefect N = 0) (hdanger : ∀ N : ℕ, TwentyOneGreedyDefectSlopeDanger N → 64 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 3 * (2 ^ N % 21) ≤ twentyOneSixStepRepairLoad N + N / 6 + 1) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Slope-aware repair-load endpoint. It is enough to pay the exact six-step load only when accumulated floor slack cannot close the block automatically.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_highDefectRepairLoad
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_highDefectRepairLoad (hbase : ∀ N : ℕ, N < 6 → twentyOneGreedyDefect N = 0) (hload : ∀ N : ℕ, N < 384 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 354 → 64 * twentyOneGreedyDefect N + 3 * (2 ^ N % 21) ≤ twentyOneSixStepRepairLoad N + N / 6 + 1) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Explicit high-defect version of the slope-aware endpoint. Repair-load arithmetic is required only while `N < 384 Q_N + 354`; low-defect ranks are closed for free by the floor slack.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_floorSlopeBlock
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_floorSlopeBlock {B : ℕ} (hBpos : 0 < B) (hBdiv : 6 ∣ B) (hbase : ∀ N : ℕ, N < B → twentyOneGreedyDefect N ≤ N / 6) (hblock : TwentyOneGreedyDefectFloorSlopeBlockContraction B) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Configurable finite-window producer: certify one positive block length divisible by six, its initial strip, and its translation-invariant floor-slope contraction, and the prescribed point follows.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_carry_sqrt_bound
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_carry_sqrt_bound (hupper : ∀ N : ℕ, (twentyOneGreedyCarry N : ℝ) ≤ 21 * (2 * Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) + 4)) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: A concrete square-root carry strip is already enough to solve the prescribed-point endpoint. This is deliberately stated without assuming that the carry is tempered: tempering is derived from the strip and the unconditional nonnegativity theorem.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedySkipsCofinally
declarations.docstring: The most economical dynamical producer currently visible at the prescribed point: skipped exponents occur beyond every cutoff. A fatal greedy state would select every later exponent, so this condition alone rules out fatality; it asks for neither a carry bound nor a remainder cap.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedySelectedRunsBounded
declarations.docstring: A uniform bound on selected runs is a stronger, finite-window producer for cofinal skipping. The exact checker currently sees very short runs, but the theorem deliberately leaves the bound existential.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_cofinal_skips
declarations.docstring: Cofinal skipped exponents solve the prescribed-point endpoint directly through the absorbing-fatal-state theorem.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_bounded_selectedRuns
declarations.docstring: Any finite uniform selected-run bound therefore solves the endpoint.

declarations.name: target_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_twoChannelCap
declarations.signature: theorem target_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_twoChannelCap (x : ℝ) (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x ≤ 1) (hskip : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x n → greedyMersenneRemainder x n ≤ halfTwoChannelCap (n + 1)) : x ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Target-generic two-channel transport. Selected branches preserve the cap automatically; the only arithmetic burden is the omitted correction tail on the skipped branches.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_twoChannelCap
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_twoChannelCap (hskip : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) n → greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) n ≤ halfTwoChannelCap (n + 1)) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Prescribed-point form of the skipped two-channel endpoint. Relative to the dyadic cap, this admits the complete first correction channel and leaves only the higher-channel tail to exclude.

declarations.name: target_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_dyadicCap
declarations.signature: theorem target_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_dyadicCap (x : ℝ) (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x ≤ 1) (hskip : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x n → greedyMersenneRemainder x n ≤ halfDyadicCap (n + 1)) : x ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Target-generic dyadic-cap transport. Selected branches preserve the cap automatically; only skipped branches can enter the narrow unsafe sliver between `2^-(n+1)` and `1/(2^(n+1)-1)`.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_dyadicCap
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_skipped_dyadicCap (hskip : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ mersenneWeight (n + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) n → greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) n ≤ halfDyadicCap (n + 1)) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Local skipped-branch endpoint for the prescribed rational. This is strictly weaker than asking for the dyadic cap at every depth, because selected steps are discharged by the universal transport inequality.

declarations.name: supportDyadicCorrectionValue
declarations.signature: noncomputable def supportDyadicCorrectionValue (A : Set ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The correction made when the binary skeleton `2⁻ⁿ` is replaced by the Mersenne weight `(2ⁿ - 1)⁻¹`. Although the original half argument called this `halfCorrectionValue`, the quantity itself is target-independent.

declarations.name: targetDyadicComplementValue
declarations.signature: noncomputable def targetDyadicComplementValue (x : ℝ) (A : Set ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The binary value demanded by the fixed-point equation at target `x`.

declarations.name: positiveMersenneSupportValue_eq_target_iff_correction_eq_complement
declarations.signature: theorem positiveMersenneSupportValue_eq_target_iff_correction_eq_complement (x : ℝ) (A : Set ℕ) : positiveMersenneSupportValue A = x ↔ supportDyadicCorrectionValue A = targetDyadicComplementValue x A
declarations.docstring: Exact target-independent form of the correction fixed-point equation.

declarations.name: correctionBoundary_large_valuation_forces_empty_doublingBlock
declarations.signature: theorem correctionBoundary_large_valuation_forces_empty_doublingBlock (A : Set ℕ) (K v q : ℕ) (hv : K - 1 ≤ v) (hq : Odd q) (hprefix : supportDyadicPrefixNumerator A (2 * K) = 2 ^ v * (q - 1)) : ∀ n : ℕ, K < n → n ≤ 2 * K → n ∉ A
declarations.docstring: A shifted coarse-cell boundary has a concrete combinatorial consequence. If its odd coarse numerator is `q`, the lower coarse word has depth-`2*K` numerator `2^v * (q - 1)`. A valuation `v ≥ K - 1` therefore makes that word divisible by `2^K`, forcing every support bit in the doubling block `(K,2*K]` to vanish. This lemma is intentionally only about the displayed shifted-word equation. An actual left boundary has prefix `2^v*q`; an actual right boundary has `prefix + 1 = 2^v*q`. Those orientations require separate classifiers.

declarations.name: correctionBoundary_valuation_lt_of_mem_doublingBlock
declarations.signature: theorem correctionBoundary_valuation_lt_of_mem_doublingBlock (A : Set ℕ) (K v q : ℕ) (hq : Odd q) (hprefix : supportDyadicPrefixNumerator A (2 * K) = 2 ^ v * (q - 1)) (hhit : ∃ n : ℕ, K < n ∧ n ≤ 2 * K ∧ n ∈ A) : v < K - 1
declarations.docstring: Contrapositive for the shifted coarse-word equation: one selected exponent in `(K,2*K]` excludes its non-amplifying valuation range.

declarations.name: correctionBoundary_forceDepth_gt_of_mem_doublingBlock
declarations.signature: theorem correctionBoundary_forceDepth_gt_of_mem_doublingBlock (A : Set ℕ) (K v q : ℕ) (hK : 1 < K) (hq : Odd q) (hprefix : supportDyadicPrefixNumerator A (2 * K) = 2 ^ v * (q - 1)) (hhit : ∃ n : ℕ, K < n ∧ n ≤ 2 * K ∧ n ∈ A) : K < 2 * K - v - 1
declarations.docstring: Combining a support hit with the shifted coarse-word equation gives its strict-amplification inequality.

declarations.name: correctionBoundary_left_valuation_lt_or_singleton_doublingBlock
declarations.signature: theorem correctionBoundary_left_valuation_lt_or_singleton_doublingBlock (A : Set ℕ) (K v q : ℕ) (hK : 2 ≤ K) (_hq : Odd q) (hprefix : supportDyadicPrefixNumerator A (2 * K) = 2 ^ v * q) (hhit : ∃ n : ℕ, K < n ∧ n ≤ 2 * K ∧ n ∈ A) : v < K - 1 ∨ (v = K - 1 ∧ K + 1 ∈ A ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, K + 1 < n → n ≤ 2 * K → n ∉ A)
declarations.docstring: Orientation-correct form for a boundary met at the *left* edge of the actual depth-`2*K` support cell. If that boundary has numerator `2^v * q`, a hit in `(K,2*K]` rules out `v ≥ K`. The only case not already giving strict depth amplification is therefore `v = K-1`; in that case the whole doubling block is forced to be the singleton word `10...0`. This is deliberately separate from `correctionBoundary_valuation_lt_of_mem_doublingBlock`: an actual left boundary supplies `prefix = 2^v*q`, not `2^v*(q-1)`.

declarations.name: correctionBoundary_right_amplifies_or_longSelectedRun
declarations.signature: theorem correctionBoundary_right_amplifies_or_longSelectedRun (A : Set ℕ) (K v q : ℕ) (hK : 3 ≤ K) (_hq : Odd q) (hboundary : supportDyadicPrefixNumerator A (2 * K) + 1 = 2 ^ v * q) : K < 2 * K - v - 1 ∨ ∀ n : ℕ, K + 1 < n → n ≤ 2 * K → n ∈ A
declarations.docstring: Orientation-correct form for a boundary met at the *right* edge of the actual depth-`2*K` support cell. Here `prefix + 1 = 2^v*q`. Either the common parent is strictly deeper than `K`, or every bit from `K+2` through `2*K` is selected. Thus right-boundary non-amplification is exactly a long terminal selected run, rather than an untyped valuation obstruction.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainder_antitone
declarations.docstring: Greedy residuals can only decrease.

declarations.name: greedyMersenneRemainder_add_eq_of_support_gap
declarations.signature: theorem greedyMersenneRemainder_add_eq_of_support_gap (x : ℝ) (K : ℕ) : ∀ L : ℕ, (∀ n : ℕ, K < n → n ≤ K + L → n ∉ greedyMersenneSupport x) → greedyMersenneRemainder x (K + L) = greedyMersenneRemainder x K
declarations.docstring: If the greedy support has no selected exponent in the next `L` ranks, the residual is unchanged across that whole block.

declarations.name: greedyRemainder_sandwich_of_singleton_doublingBlock
declarations.signature: theorem greedyRemainder_sandwich_of_singleton_doublingBlock (x : ℝ) (K : ℕ) (hK : 2 ≤ K) (hfirst : K + 1 ∈ greedyMersenneSupport x) (hrest : ∀ n : ℕ, K + 1 < n → n ≤ 2 * K → n ∉ greedyMersenneSupport x) : mersenneWeight (K + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x K ∧ greedyMersenneRemainder x (2 * K - 1) = greedyMersenneRemainder x K - mersenneWeight (K + 1) ∧ greedyMersenneRemainder x K < mersenneWeight (K + 1) + mersenneWeight (2 * K)
declarations.docstring: The exceptional left-boundary word isolated above has an exact residual meaning. If `(K,2*K]` is `10...0`, the rank-`K+1` weight is taken and the post-take residual stays fixed until rank `2*K`; the final zero then places the old residual in the narrow interval `[w_(K+1), w_(K+1)+w_(2K))`.

declarations.name: greedyCorrectionBoundary_left_amplifies_or_singletonSandwich
declarations.signature: theorem greedyCorrectionBoundary_left_amplifies_or_singletonSandwich (x : ℝ) (K v q : ℕ) (hK : 3 ≤ K) (hq : Odd q) (hprefix : supportDyadicPrefixNumerator (greedyMersenneSupport x) (2 * K) = 2 ^ v * q) (hhit : ∃ n : ℕ, K < n ∧ n ≤ 2 * K ∧ n ∈ greedyMersenneSupport x) : K < 2 * K - v - 1 ∨ (mersenneWeight (K + 1) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x K ∧ greedyMersenneRemainder x K < mersenneWeight (K + 1) + mersenneWeight (2 * K))
declarations.docstring: Complete arithmetic output for an actual *left*-boundary crossing. Either its reduced dyadic depth strictly exceeds `K`, or the greedy residual is forced into the explicit singleton-block sandwich. Thus the left orientation no longer hides a generic "valuation obstruction": only one concrete greedy word and one two-weight interval remain.

declarations.name: mersenneWeight_two_mul_le_remainder_of_mem_doublingBlock
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneWeight_two_mul_le_remainder_of_mem_doublingBlock (x : ℝ) (K n : ℕ) (hKn : K < n) (hn2K : n ≤ 2 * K) (hnmem : n ∈ greedyMersenneSupport x) : mersenneWeight (2 * K) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x K
declarations.docstring: A selected exponent anywhere in `(K,2*K]` forces the residual at `K` above the smallest weight in that block.

declarations.name: greedySupport_mem_doublingBlock_iff_weight_le_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem greedySupport_mem_doublingBlock_iff_weight_le_remainder (x : ℝ) (K : ℕ) (hK : 0 < K) : (∃ n : ℕ, K < n ∧ n ≤ 2 * K ∧ n ∈ greedyMersenneSupport x) ↔ mersenneWeight (2 * K) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder x K
declarations.docstring: Exact scalar form of the doubling-block condition. Hitting `(K,2*K]` is equivalent to the single lower bound `w_(2K) ≤ R_K` on the greedy residual.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyHitsDoublingBlocks
declarations.docstring: The remaining combinatorial throat suggested by the correction certificate. The exact run verifies this from `K = 3` through `K = 5000`; an all-depth proof would rule out every non-amplifying crossed boundary.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyEventuallyHitsDoublingBlocks
declarations.docstring: The eventual form is the actual correction-boundary obligation. A finite initial collection of empty doubling blocks cannot affect an unbounded prefix-forcing construction.

declarations.name: TwentyOneGreedyEmptyDoublingBlocksCofinally
declarations.docstring: The complementary asymptotic branch: empty doubling blocks occur beyond every cutoff. This branch is already terminal, since each such block contains a skipped greedy rank arbitrarily far out.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_cofinal_emptyDoublingBlocks
declarations.docstring: Cofinal empty doubling blocks solve the prescribed point rather than obstructing it: their first ranks give cofinally many greedy skips.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_or_eventually_hits_doublingBlocks
declarations.docstring: Exhaustive asymptotic split. Either the empty-block branch already proves membership, or every sufficiently large doubling block is hit. Thus the correction route never needs the formerly stated all-depth hit hypothesis.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_or_eventual_correctionBoundary_amplification
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_or_eventual_correctionBoundary_amplification : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet ∨ ∃ K₀ : ℕ, ∀ K v q : ℕ, K₀ ≤ K → 3 ≤ K → Odd q → supportDyadicPrefixNumerator (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)) (2 * K) = 2 ^ v * (q - 1) → K < 2 * K - v - 1
declarations.docstring: Conditional shifted-word frontier. Either the target is already in the achievement set, or every sufficiently large boundary satisfying the displayed `2^v*(q-1)` prefix equation has larger forcing depth. This does not classify the actual left/right boundary orientations by itself.

declarations.name: twentyOneGreedyHitsDoublingBlocks_iff
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneGreedyHitsDoublingBlocks_iff : TwentyOneGreedyHitsDoublingBlocks ↔ ∀ K : ℕ, 3 ≤ K → mersenneWeight (2 * K) ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 21 : ℝ) K
declarations.docstring: Scalar residual form of the remaining no-gap throat.

declarations.name: targetGreedyMersennePrefix

declarations.docstring: The finite Mersenne prefix selected by the greedy itinerary of `x`.

declarations.name: targetGreedyDyadicPrefix
declarations.signature: noncomputable def targetGreedyDyadicPrefix (x : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The same finite greedy word evaluated in the binary skeleton.

declarations.name: targetGreedyCorrectionPrefix

declarations.docstring: The finite correction carried by the greedy word through depth `N`.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffPrefix_supportMembershipBit_eq_dyadicPrefix
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffPrefix_supportMembershipBit_eq_dyadicPrefix (A : Set ℕ) : ∀ N : ℕ, binaryCoeffPrefix (supportMembershipBit A) N = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, Set.indicator A (fun n : ℕ => ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ^ n) (k + 1)

declarations.name: targetGreedyDyadicPrefix_eq_supportNumerator_div_pow

declarations.docstring: Integer numerator form of the actual greedy dyadic prefix.

declarations.name: target_sub_greedyCorrectionPrefix_eq_dyadicPrefix_add_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem target_sub_greedyCorrectionPrefix_eq_dyadicPrefix_add_remainder (x : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : x - targetGreedyCorrectionPrefix x N = targetGreedyDyadicPrefix x N + greedyMersenneRemainder x N
declarations.docstring: Exact finite-stage identity used by the denominator-`21` correction checker. No limiting or membership assumption occurs here.

declarations.name: mersenneDyadicCorrectionWeight
declarations.docstring: One positive-index correction digit.

declarations.name: mersenneDyadicCorrectionWeight_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneDyadicCorrectionWeight_nonneg {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : 0 ≤ mersenneDyadicCorrectionWeight n

declarations.signature: noncomputable def supportDyadicCorrectionSuffix (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ
