declarations.name: positive_rational_difference_lower_bound
declarations.signature: theorem positive_rational_difference_lower_bound {whole pfx : ℚ} (hpositive : pfx < whole) : (1 : ℝ) / (((whole.den * pfx.den : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤ (whole : ℝ) - (pfx : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A positive rational difference is at least the reciprocal of the product of the two reduced denominators.

declarations.name: prefixDenominator_shell_power_bound_of_rational_difference
declarations.signature: theorem prefixDenominator_shell_power_bound_of_rational_difference (whole pfx : ℚ) (K X : ℕ) (hpositive : pfx < whole) (hX : 1 ≤ X) (hupper : (whole : ℝ) - (pfx : ℝ) ≤ (K : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ X + 2 / (2 : ℝ) ^ (2 * X)) : (2 : ℝ) ^ X ≤ ((whole.den * pfx.den : ℕ) : ℝ) * (K + 1)
declarations.docstring: Direct supply adapter for the prefix-denominator shell consumer. Once the analytic shell/far-tail upper bound is known, rationality alone supplies the matching lower bound with the actual reduced denominators.

declarations.name: nextSupport_power_bound_of_rational_difference
declarations.signature: theorem nextSupport_power_bound_of_rational_difference (whole pfx : ℚ) (m : ℕ) (hpositive : pfx < whole) (hupper : (whole : ℝ) - (pfx : ℝ) ≤ 4 / (2 : ℝ) ^ m) : (2 : ℝ) ^ m ≤ 4 * ((whole.den * pfx.den : ℕ) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Direct supply adapter for the next-support power consumer. Any analytic bound of the form `whole-prefix ≤ 4/2^m` forces the next exponent below the product-denominator power barrier.

declarations.name: primitivePrefix
declarations.signature: def primitivePrefix (A : Set ℕ) (X : ℕ) : Set ℕ
declarations.docstring: Support already present at or below the shell cutoff.

declarations.name: primitiveResidual
declarations.signature: def primitiveResidual (A : Set ℕ) (X : ℕ) : Set ℕ
declarations.docstring: Primitive innovations not present in the prefix through `X`.

declarations.name: primitiveBit
declarations.signature: noncomputable def primitiveBit (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Natural-valued primitive support bit, with classical membership hidden behind a stable definition.

declarations.name: divisor_eq_self_of_cutoff_lt_of_le_two_mul
declarations.signature: theorem divisor_eq_self_of_cutoff_lt_of_le_two_mul {d n X : ℕ} (hd : d ∣ n) (hn0 : n ≠ 0) (hX : X < d) (hn : n ≤ 2 * X) : d = n
declarations.docstring: A divisor of `n` lying in `(X,2X]` is necessarily `n` itself.

declarations.name: supportCoeff_primitiveResidual_first_shell
declarations.signature: theorem supportCoeff_primitiveResidual_first_shell (A : Set ℕ) (X n : ℕ) (hXn : X < n) (hn2X : n ≤ 2 * X) : supportCoeff (primitiveResidual A X) n = primitiveBit A n
declarations.docstring: On the first shell after removing the prefix, the divisor shadow is the primitive support bit.

declarations.name: supportCoeff_eq_primitivePrefix_add_residual
declarations.signature: theorem supportCoeff_eq_primitivePrefix_add_residual (A : Set ℕ) (X n : ℕ) : supportCoeff A n = supportCoeff (primitivePrefix A X) n + supportCoeff (primitiveResidual A X) n
declarations.docstring: The support coefficient splits exactly into prefix shadow and residual shadow.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_eq_prefix_add_residual
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_eq_prefix_add_residual (A : Set ℕ) (X N : ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N = binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff (primitivePrefix A X)) N + binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff (primitiveResidual A X)) N
declarations.docstring: Binary tails respect the exact prefix/residual support split.

declarations.name: scaledSupportCarry
declarations.signature: noncomputable def scaledSupportCarry (q : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Full support carry at a displayed multiplier `q`.

declarations.name: scaledPrefixCarry
declarations.signature: noncomputable def scaledPrefixCarry (D : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (X N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Finite-prefix background carry at its reduced denominator `D`.

declarations.name: primitiveCrossCarry
declarations.signature: noncomputable def primitiveCrossCarry (q D : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (X N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Cross-carry obtained by subtracting the deterministic prefix background from the full carry at common scale `qD`.

declarations.name: primitiveCrossCarry_eq_residualTail
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveCrossCarry_eq_residualTail (q D : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (X N : ℕ) : primitiveCrossCarry q D A X N = (q * D : ℕ) * binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff (primitiveResidual A X)) N
declarations.docstring: Exact cross-carry identity: the subtraction leaves the scaled residual tail and no prefix shadow.

declarations.name: primitiveCrossCarry_first_shell_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveCrossCarry_first_shell_recurrence (q D : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (X N : ℕ) (hXN : X < N + 1) (hN2X : N + 1 ≤ 2 * X) : primitiveCrossCarry q D A X (N + 1) = 2 * primitiveCrossCarry q D A X N - (q * D : ℕ) * primitiveBit A (N + 1)
declarations.docstring: On the first residual shell, the cross-carry is forced by the primitive bit rather than by the full divisor coefficient.

declarations.name: primitiveCrossCarry_pos
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveCrossCarry_pos (q D : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hD : 0 < D) (A : Set ℕ) (X N : ℕ) (hres : ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ a ∈ primitiveResidual A X) : 0 < primitiveCrossCarry q D A X N
declarations.docstring: A nonempty residual support makes the cross-carry strictly positive.

declarations.name: prefixDenominator_shell_power_bound
declarations.signature: theorem prefixDenominator_shell_power_bound (q D K X : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hD : 0 < D) (hX : 1 ≤ X) (beta : ℝ) (hlower : (1 : ℝ) / ((q * D : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ beta) (hupper : beta ≤ (K : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ X + 2 / (2 : ℝ) ^ (2 * X)) : ((2 : ℝ) ^ X) ≤ ((q * D : ℕ) : ℝ) * (K + 1)
declarations.docstring: If a positive residual is at least `1/(qD)` but its first dyadic shell and geometric far tail contribute at most `K/2^X + 2/2^(2X)`, then `2^X ≤ qD(K+1)`. This is the division-free denominator/shell pressure inequality; the analytic estimates are explicit hypotheses.

declarations.name: nextSupport_power_bound
declarations.signature: theorem nextSupport_power_bound (q D m : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hD : 0 < D) (beta : ℝ) (hlower : (1 : ℝ) / ((q * D : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ beta) (hupper : beta ≤ 4 / (2 : ℝ) ^ m) : (2 : ℝ) ^ m ≤ 4 * ((q * D : ℕ) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The same elementary pressure excludes a next support exponent whose power of two is larger than `4qD`.

declarations.name: primitiveCarry
declarations.docstring: The dyadic carry residue used by the landed totient gap consumer.

declarations.name: ReducedDenominatorUnitGapCert
declarations.signature: def ReducedDenominatorUnitGapCert (u N K : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: A reduced-denominator unit-gap certificate. Writing `u * primitiveCarry N K = J * 2^K + W`, the positive tail can only cross the integers `J+1, ..., J+L`, where `L = (W + u*(N+K+2))/2^K`. The certificate says that every such candidate is a nonunit modulo the odd reduced denominator `u`.

declarations.name: reducedDenominatorCandidateCount
declarations.signature: def reducedDenominatorCandidateCount (u N K : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The exact candidate count associated to a unit-gap certificate.

declarations.name: PrimitiveReducedDenominatorUnitGapSupply
declarations.docstring: The exact residual supply exposed by the reduced-denominator consumer. It is deliberately a proposition, not an axiom or a claimed theorem.

declarations.name: reducedDenominatorUnitGapCert_prime_pow_iff
declarations.signature: theorem reducedDenominatorUnitGapCert_prime_pow_iff {p e N K : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (he : 0 < e) : ReducedDenominatorUnitGapCert (p ^ e) N K ↔ let M
declarations.docstring: At a prime-power reduced denominator, nonunits are exactly multiples of the underlying prime. Since two consecutive integers are coprime, the unit-gap extension can admit at most one candidate lattice point.

declarations.name: reducedDenominatorCandidateCount_prime_pow_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem reducedDenominatorCandidateCount_prime_pow_le_one {p e N K : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (he : 0 < e) (hcert : ReducedDenominatorUnitGapCert (p ^ e) N K) : reducedDenominatorCandidateCount (p ^ e) N K ≤ 1
declarations.docstring: Numerical form of the prime-power ceiling: a certified interval for an odd prime power contains zero or one candidate, never two.

declarations.name: primitiveReducedDenominatorUnitGapSupply_prime_power_projection
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveReducedDenominatorUnitGapSupply_prime_power_projection (hsupply : PrimitiveReducedDenominatorUnitGapSupply) {p e a : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hpodd : Odd p) (he : 0 < e) : ∃ N K : ℕ, a ≤ N ∧ 0 < K ∧ ReducedDenominatorUnitGapCert (p ^ e) N K ∧ reducedDenominatorCandidateCount (p ^ e) N K ≤ 1
declarations.docstring: Every hypothetical all-denominator unit-gap supply must in particular solve the depth-growing zero-or-one-candidate problem for every odd prime power. This is the formal residual/no-go boundary, not a supply result.

declarations.name: primitiveCarry_three_window_3_5_eval
declarations.docstring: The first strict strengthening over the ordinary empty-gap certificate: at `(u,N,K)=(3,3,5)` the dyadic interval contains the single integer `3`, which is forbidden because it is a nonunit modulo the reduced denominator.

declarations.name: not_ordinary_gap_certificate_three_window_3_5
declarations.docstring: The same row is not an ordinary empty-gap certificate: its scaled residue plus tail height is `38`, while the dyadic modulus is `32`.

declarations.name: primitiveCarry_three_window_3_5
declarations.docstring: Exact arithmetic in the strict-strengthening regression row.

declarations.name: sum_powerset_singleton
declarations.signature: private theorem sum_powerset_singleton {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [AddCommMonoid β] (a : α) (f : Finset α → β) : ∑ t ∈ ({a} : Finset α).powerset, f t = f ∅ + f {a}

declarations.name: mersenne
declarations.docstring: The Mersenne denominator at exponent `n`.

declarations.name: squarefreeKernel
declarations.docstring: The squarefree kernel used by the numeric shadow: the product of the distinct prime factors of `n`. For `n = 0` this convention gives `1`; all development-facing scaling theorems assume `0 < n`.

declarations.name: squarefreeKernel_idem
declarations.signature: theorem squarefreeKernel_idem (n : ℕ) : squarefreeKernel (squarefreeKernel n) = squarefreeKernel n

declarations.name: squarefreeKernel_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem squarefreeKernel_dvd (n : ℕ) : squarefreeKernel n ∣ n

declarations.name: squarefreeKernel_squarefree
declarations.docstring: The canonical kernel is squarefree, including at the convention `squarefreeKernel 0 = 1`.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_squarefreeKernel_iff
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_squarefreeKernel_iff {n p : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (hp : p.Prime) : p ∣ squarefreeKernel n ↔ p ∣ n
declarations.docstring: Away from the exceptional zero convention, taking the squarefree kernel preserves exactly the prime divisors.

declarations.name: mobiusNumerator
declarations.docstring: The integral numerator, written as its squarefree-divisor expansion. For `s ⊆ primeFactors(r)`, put `d = ∏ p ∈ s, p`. Then the summand is `(-1)^|s| (r/d) ((2^r-1)/(2^d-1))`. This is exactly the nonzero part of `Σ_{d ∣ r} μ(d) (r/d) ((2^r-1)/(2^d-1))`: nonsquarefree divisors have Möbius coefficient zero. The subset form makes that finite support explicit and keeps the definition executable without factoring irrelevant divisors.

declarations.name: baseMobiusShadow
declarations.docstring: The unscaled radical shadow `B(r) = M_r / (2^r - 1)`.

declarations.name: numericMobiusShadow
declarations.docstring: The numeric shadow at an arbitrary scale. By construction it only sees the distinct prime factors of `H`.

declarations.name: numericMobiusShadow_radical
declarations.signature: theorem numericMobiusShadow_radical (H : ℕ) : numericMobiusShadow H = numericMobiusShadow (squarefreeKernel H)
declarations.docstring: Exact radical reduction: repeated prime powers do not change the numeric Möbius shadow.

declarations.name: scaledMobiusShadow_eq_radicalBase
declarations.signature: theorem scaledMobiusShadow_eq_radicalBase (H : ℕ) (_hH : 0 < H) : (H : ℚ) * numericMobiusShadow H = ((H / squarefreeKernel H : ℕ) : ℚ) * baseMobiusShadow (squarefreeKernel H)
declarations.docstring: Scaling by `H` is exactly scaling the unscaled radical shadow by `H / rad(H)`. This theorem deliberately leaves `B(r)` reduced separately; the factor `H / r` may cause further cancellation.

declarations.name: scaledMobiusShadow_eq_radicalNumerator
declarations.signature: theorem scaledMobiusShadow_eq_radicalNumerator (H : ℕ) (hH : 0 < H) : (H : ℚ) * numericMobiusShadow H = ((H / squarefreeKernel H : ℕ) : ℚ) * Rat.divInt (mobiusNumerator (squarefreeKernel H)) (mersenne (squarefreeKernel H) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The development's scaled formula with the numerator and Mersenne denominator displayed explicitly.

declarations.name: baseMobiusShadow_den
declarations.signature: theorem baseMobiusShadow_den (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) : (baseMobiusShadow r).den = mersenne r / (mobiusNumerator r).natAbs.gcd (mersenne r)
declarations.docstring: Exact reduced denominator of the unscaled shadow. This is the generic gcd formula in T6; no coprimality or channel-survival hypothesis is hidden.

declarations.name: baseMobiusShadow_den_of_gcd_eq
declarations.signature: theorem baseMobiusShadow_den_of_gcd_eq (r g : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (hgcd : (mobiusNumerator r).natAbs.gcd (mersenne r) = g) : (baseMobiusShadow r).den = mersenne r / g
declarations.docstring: A reusable corollary: a kernel-checked gcd certificate immediately gives the displayed reduced denominator.

declarations.name: mobiusNumerator_prime
declarations.signature: theorem mobiusNumerator_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : mobiusNumerator p = (p : ℤ) * (mersenne p : ℤ) - 1
declarations.docstring: For a prime radical there are only the empty and singleton subsets, so the Möbius numerator is `p(2^p-1)-1`.

declarations.name: mobiusNumerator_prime_gcd
declarations.signature: theorem mobiusNumerator_prime_gcd {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : (mobiusNumerator p).natAbs.gcd (mersenne p) = 1
declarations.docstring: The prime numerator is coprime to its Mersenne denominator.

declarations.name: baseMobiusShadow_den_prime
declarations.signature: theorem baseMobiusShadow_den_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : (baseMobiusShadow p).den = mersenne p
declarations.docstring: Exact prime-radical denominator from the generic gcd formula.

declarations.name: mobiusNumerator_twicePrime
declarations.signature: theorem mobiusNumerator_twicePrime {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) : mobiusNumerator (2 * p) = ((2 * p : ℕ) : ℤ) * (mersenne (2 * p) : ℤ) - (p : ℤ) * ((mersenne (2 * p) / 3 : ℕ) : ℤ) - 2 * ((mersenne (2 * p) / mersenne p : ℕ) : ℤ) + 1
declarations.docstring: The four-term numerator expansion for a twice-prime radical. This is the exact algebraic fixture used before proving the gcd is `3`; the natural quotients are exact because `3 = 2^2-1` and `2^p-1` divide `2^(2p)-1`.

declarations.name: prime_mod_six_eq_one_or_five
declarations.signature: private theorem prime_mod_six_eq_one_or_five {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) : p % 6 = 1 ∨ p % 6 = 5

declarations.name: prime_pow_two_mod_nine_cases
declarations.signature: private theorem prime_pow_two_mod_nine_cases {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) : (p % 6 = 1 ∧ 2 ^ p % 9 = 2) ∨ (p % 6 = 5 ∧ 2 ^ p % 9 = 5)

declarations.name: mobiusNumerator_twicePrime_gcd
declarations.signature: theorem mobiusNumerator_twicePrime_gcd {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) : (mobiusNumerator (2 * p)).natAbs.gcd (mersenne (2 * p)) = 3
declarations.docstring: For every prime `p ≥ 5`, the twice-prime numerator has exactly the factor `3` in common with its Mersenne denominator.

declarations.name: baseMobiusShadow_den_twicePrime
declarations.signature: theorem baseMobiusShadow_den_twicePrime {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hp5 : 5 ≤ p) : (baseMobiusShadow (2 * p)).den = mersenne (2 * p) / 3
declarations.docstring: Exact reduced denominator for a twice-prime radical.

declarations.name: divisor_dvd_divInt_den
declarations.signature: theorem divisor_dvd_divInt_den {a : ℤ} {D m : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (hmD : m ∣ D) (hcop : Nat.Coprime m a.natAbs) : m ∣ (Rat.divInt a (D : ℤ)).den
declarations.docstring: A divisor of a displayed denominator survives rational reduction when it is coprime to the displayed numerator.

declarations.name: survivingDivisor_dvd_scaled_divInt_den
declarations.signature: theorem survivingDivisor_dvd_scaled_divInt_den {a : ℤ} {D C h : ℕ} (hD : 0 < D) (hCD : C ∣ D) (hcop : Nat.Coprime C a.natAbs) : C / Nat.gcd C h ∣ (Rat.divInt ((h : ℤ) * a) (D : ℤ)).den
declarations.docstring: Scaling can cancel the part `gcd C h`, but no further part of `C` when `C` was coprime to the unscaled numerator.

declarations.name: doublingResidue
declarations.signature: def doublingResidue (p v n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Least nonnegative residue of `p * 2^n` modulo `v`. When `v` is odd and `p` is coprime to `v`, this residue is strictly positive.

declarations.name: doublingWrapDigit
declarations.signature: def doublingWrapDigit (p v n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The quotient expelled when a least residue is doubled. Since the residue is below `v`, this quotient is always zero or one.

declarations.name: doublingWrapCount
declarations.signature: def doublingWrapCount (p v h : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Number of binary wraps in the first `h` transitions.

declarations.name: IsDoublingPeriod
declarations.docstring: A period condition, without a minimality requirement: `h > 0` and `2^h ≡ 1 (mod v)`. The multiplicative order is one admissible choice.

declarations.name: doublingResidue_lt
declarations.signature: theorem doublingResidue_lt (p : ℕ) {v : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (n : ℕ) : doublingResidue p v n < v

declarations.name: doublingWrapDigit_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem doublingWrapDigit_le_one (p : ℕ) {v : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (n : ℕ) : doublingWrapDigit p v n ≤ 1

declarations.name: doublingWrapDigit_eq_zero_or_one
declarations.signature: theorem doublingWrapDigit_eq_zero_or_one (p : ℕ) {v : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (n : ℕ) : doublingWrapDigit p v n = 0 ∨ doublingWrapDigit p v n = 1

declarations.name: doublingResidue_pos
declarations.signature: theorem doublingResidue_pos (p : ℕ) {v : ℕ} (hv : 1 < v) (hvodd : Odd v) (hpv : p.Coprime v) (j : ℕ) : 0 < doublingResidue p v j
declarations.docstring: For an odd modulus and reduced numerator, every canonical residue is strictly positive.

declarations.name: doublingResidue_succ
declarations.signature: theorem doublingResidue_succ (p v n : ℕ) : doublingResidue p v (n + 1) = (2 * doublingResidue p v n) % v
declarations.docstring: Doubling and reducing advances the canonical residue cycle by one.

declarations.name: doublingResidue_carry
declarations.signature: theorem doublingResidue_carry (p v n : ℕ) : 2 * doublingResidue p v n = v * doublingWrapDigit p v n + doublingResidue p v (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact binary carry recurrence for canonical residues.

declarations.name: doublingResidue_add_period
declarations.signature: theorem doublingResidue_add_period (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (n : ℕ) : doublingResidue p v (n + h) = doublingResidue p v n
declarations.docstring: A doubling period closes every numerator residue cycle.

declarations.name: doublingResidue_add
declarations.signature: theorem doublingResidue_add (p v N j : ℕ) : doublingResidue p v (N + j) = doublingResidue (p * 2 ^ N) v j
declarations.docstring: Shifting the tail index multiplies the starting numerator by the same power of two.

declarations.name: sum_range_shift_one
declarations.signature: theorem sum_range_shift_one (r : ℕ → ℕ) (h : ℕ) : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, r (j + 1)) + r 0 = (∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, r j) + r h
declarations.docstring: Summing a shifted finite sequence differs only by its two endpoints.

declarations.name: sum_range_add_eq_sum_range_of_periodic
declarations.signature: theorem sum_range_add_eq_sum_range_of_periodic (r : ℕ → ℕ) (h : ℕ) (hperiod : ∀ N : ℕ, r (N + h) = r N) : ∀ N : ℕ, ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, r (N + j) = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, r j
declarations.docstring: Every complete block of a periodic natural sequence has the same sum.

declarations.name: sum_eq_modulus_mul_wrapCount_of_closed_cycle
declarations.signature: theorem sum_eq_modulus_mul_wrapCount_of_closed_cycle (v h : ℕ) (r k : ℕ → ℕ) (hcarry : ∀ j : ℕ, 2 * r j = v * k j + r (j + 1)) (hclosed : r h = r 0) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, r j = v * ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, k j
declarations.docstring: **Wrap identity for a closed binary residue cycle.**

declarations.name: sum_doublingResidue_eq_mul_wrapCount
declarations.signature: theorem sum_doublingResidue_eq_mul_wrapCount (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, doublingResidue p v j = v * doublingWrapCount p v h
declarations.docstring: Canonical form of the wrap identity.

declarations.name: doublingWrapCount_pos
declarations.signature: theorem doublingWrapCount_pos (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 1 < v) (hvodd : Odd v) (hpv : p.Coprime v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) : 0 < doublingWrapCount p v h
declarations.docstring: A nonempty positive closed residue cycle has at least one wrap.

declarations.name: doublingWrapCount_mul_pow_eq
declarations.signature: theorem doublingWrapCount_mul_pow_eq (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (N : ℕ) : doublingWrapCount (p * 2 ^ N) v h = doublingWrapCount p v h
declarations.docstring: The wrap count is invariant under rotation of a complete residue cycle.

declarations.name: exists_unique_wrap_of_sum_eq_one
declarations.signature: theorem exists_unique_wrap_of_sum_eq_one (h : ℕ) (wrap : ℕ → ℕ) (hbit : ∀ j < h, wrap j ≤ 1) (hone : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, wrap j = 1) : ∃ t < h, wrap t = 1 ∧ ∀ j < h, j ≠ t → wrap j = 0
declarations.docstring: A bit-valued family whose sum is one has one and only one nonzero position in the displayed range.

declarations.name: accumulatedWrap
declarations.signature: def accumulatedWrap (wrap : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ | 0 => 0 | n + 1 => 2 * accumulatedWrap wrap n + wrap n /-- Unroll the binary carry recurrence through a finite prefix. -/ theorem recurrence_unroll (v n : ℕ) (r wrap : ℕ → ℕ) (hrec : ∀ j < n, 2 * r j = v * wrap j + r (j + 1)) : 2 ^ n * r 0 = r n + v * accumulatedWrap wrap n
declarations.docstring: Binary value represented by a prefix of wrap digits, with the most recent digit least significant in `E(n+1)=2E(n)+wrap(n)`.

declarations.name: recurrence_unroll
declarations.signature: theorem recurrence_unroll (v n : ℕ) (r wrap : ℕ → ℕ) (hrec : ∀ j < n, 2 * r j = v * wrap j + r (j + 1)) : 2 ^ n * r 0 = r n + v * accumulatedWrap wrap n
declarations.docstring: Unroll the binary carry recurrence through a finite prefix.

declarations.name: accumulatedWrap_eq_zero_of_zero
declarations.signature: private theorem accumulatedWrap_eq_zero_of_zero (wrap : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hzero : ∀ j < n, wrap j = 0) : accumulatedWrap wrap n = 0

declarations.name: accumulatedWrap_eq_pow_of_unique
declarations.signature: theorem accumulatedWrap_eq_pow_of_unique (wrap : ℕ → ℕ) {h t : ℕ} (ht : t < h) (htone : wrap t = 1) (hother : ∀ j < h, j ≠ t → wrap j = 0) : accumulatedWrap wrap h = 2 ^ (h - 1 - t)

declarations.name: two_pow_sub_one_mod_two
declarations.signature: private theorem two_pow_sub_one_mod_two {h : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) : (2 ^ h - 1) % 2 = 1

declarations.name: one_wrap_cycle_classification
declarations.signature: theorem one_wrap_cycle_classification (v h : ℕ) (r wrap : ℕ → ℕ) (hh : 0 < h) (hrcop : (r 0).Coprime v) (hclosed : r h = r 0) (hrec : ∀ j < h, 2 * r j = v * wrap j + r (j + 1)) (hbit : ∀ j < h, wrap j ≤ 1) (hone : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, wrap j = 1) : v = 2 ^ h - 1 ∧ ∃ a < h, r 0 = 2 ^ a
declarations.docstring: Full algebraic classification of a one-wrap positive closed cycle. Its starting residue is a power of two and its modulus is Mersenne.

declarations.name: one_doublingWrap_classification
declarations.signature: theorem one_doublingWrap_classification (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 1 < v) (_hvodd : Odd v) (hpv : p.Coprime v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (hone : doublingWrapCount p v h = 1) : v = 2 ^ h - 1 ∧ ∃ a < h, doublingResidue p v 0 = 2 ^ a
declarations.docstring: Canonical one-wrap theorem: the odd denominator is `2^h-1`, and the numerator residue lies in the power-of-two orbit.

declarations.name: oddDoublingOrder
declarations.signature: noncomputable def oddDoublingOrder (v : ℕ) (hvodd : Odd v) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Mathlib realization of `ord_v(2)` for an odd modulus.

declarations.name: pow_oddDoublingOrder_mod_eq_one
declarations.signature: theorem pow_oddDoublingOrder_mod_eq_one {v : ℕ} (hv : 1 < v) (hvodd : Odd v) : 2 ^ oddDoublingOrder v hvodd % v = 1

declarations.name: oddDoublingOrder_pos
declarations.signature: theorem oddDoublingOrder_pos {v : ℕ} (hvodd : Odd v) : 0 < oddDoublingOrder v hvodd

declarations.name: oddDoublingOrder_isPeriod
declarations.signature: theorem oddDoublingOrder_isPeriod {v : ℕ} (hv : 1 < v) (hvodd : Odd v) : IsDoublingPeriod v (oddDoublingOrder v hvodd)
declarations.docstring: The actual multiplicative order closes the canonical residue cycle.

declarations.name: oddOrder_doublingWrapCount_pos
declarations.signature: theorem oddOrder_doublingWrapCount_pos (p : ℕ) {v : ℕ} (hv : 1 < v) (hvodd : Odd v) (hpv : p.Coprime v) : 0 < doublingWrapCount p v (oddDoublingOrder v hvodd)

declarations.name: one_oddOrder_doublingWrap_classification
declarations.signature: theorem one_oddOrder_doublingWrap_classification (p : ℕ) {v : ℕ} (hv : 1 < v) (hvodd : Odd v) (hpv : p.Coprime v) (hone : doublingWrapCount p v (oddDoublingOrder v hvodd) = 1) : v = 2 ^ oddDoublingOrder v hvodd - 1 ∧ ∃ a < oddDoublingOrder v hvodd, doublingResidue p v 0 = 2 ^ a
declarations.docstring: The one-wrap classification specialized to the multiplicative order of two modulo the odd modulus.

declarations.name: IsOddSupportTailState
declarations.signature: def IsOddSupportTailState (A : Set ℕ) (p v : ℕ) (u : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: A natural state which is simultaneously the odd-denominator scaling of the true support tail and the canonical doubling residue of a numerator. The rational-fraction bridge below constructs this state after removing the power of two from a displayed denominator.

declarations.name: oddTailExcess
declarations.signature: def oddTailExcess (u : ℕ → ℕ) (v N : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Integral excess of an odd tail state above its least residue.

declarations.name: oddSupportTail_eq_residue_div_add_excess
declarations.signature: theorem oddSupportTail_eq_residue_div_add_excess (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ) {v : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (u : ℕ → ℕ) (hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u) (N : ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N = (doublingResidue p v N : ℝ) / (v : ℝ) + (oddTailExcess u v N : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Exact pointwise decomposition of a genuine odd tail state into its least residue and a nonnegative integral excess.

declarations.name: sum_supportTail_block_eq_wrapCount_add_excess
declarations.signature: theorem sum_supportTail_block_eq_wrapCount_add_excess (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (u : ℕ → ℕ) (hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u) (N : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) (N + j) = (doublingWrapCount (p * 2 ^ N) v h : ℝ) + ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, (oddTailExcess u v (N + j) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Exact block identity: a complete residue cycle contributes its wrap count, and every additional lift of a tail state contributes one nonnegative integer. This is the finite algebra behind both the periodic lower bound and the exact excess-mean identity.

declarations.name: wrapCount_le_sum_supportTail_block
declarations.signature: theorem wrapCount_le_sum_supportTail_block (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (u : ℕ → ℕ) (hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u) (N : ℕ) : (doublingWrapCount (p * 2 ^ N) v h : ℝ) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) (N + j)
declarations.docstring: Dropping the nonnegative excess terms gives the order-sensitive local block lower bound.

declarations.name: numerator_pos_of_support_fraction
declarations.signature: theorem numerator_pos_of_support_fraction (A : Set ℕ) (hA : ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ a ∈ A) (p : ℤ) (c v : ℕ) (hv : 0 < v) (hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : ℝ) / ((2 ^ c * v : ℕ) : ℝ)) : 0 < p
declarations.docstring: A nonempty positive support forces the numerator of every displayed positive-denominator fraction to be positive.

declarations.name: exists_shifted_odd_tail_states_of_support_fraction
declarations.signature: theorem exists_shifted_odd_tail_states_of_support_fraction (A : Set ℕ) (hA : ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ a ∈ A) (p : ℤ) (c v : ℕ) (hv : 0 < v) (hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : ℝ) / ((2 ^ c * v : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ∃ u : ℕ → ℤ, (∀ n : ℕ, (u n : ℝ) = (v : ℝ) * binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) (c + n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < u n) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, u (n + 1) = 2 * u n - (v : ℤ) * (supportCoeff A (c + n + 1) : ℤ)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, u n ≡ (2 : ℤ) ^ n * p [ZMOD (v : ℤ)])
declarations.docstring: Removing the power-of-two part of a displayed denominator gives a positive integer state equal to `v` times the shifted true tail. The state also carries the exact additive recurrence and its numerator residue class.

declarations.name: exists_shifted_odd_tail_nat_states_of_support_fraction
declarations.signature: theorem exists_shifted_odd_tail_nat_states_of_support_fraction (A : Set ℕ) (hA : ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ a ∈ A) (p : ℤ) (c v : ℕ) (hv : 0 < v) (hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : ℝ) / ((2 ^ c * v : ℕ) : ℝ)) : ∃ u : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n : ℕ, (u n : ℝ) = (v : ℝ) * binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) (c + n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < u n) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, u (n + 1) + v * supportCoeff A (c + n + 1) = 2 * u n) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, u n ≡ p.toNat * 2 ^ n [MOD v])
declarations.docstring: Natural-number form of the shifted odd tail state.

declarations.name: wrapCount_le_sum_tail_of_modEq
declarations.signature: theorem wrapCount_le_sum_tail_of_modEq (coeff : ℕ → ℕ) (shift p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (u : ℕ → ℕ) (htail : ∀ n : ℕ, (u n : ℝ) = (v : ℝ) * binaryCoeffTail coeff (shift + n)) (hmod : ∀ n : ℕ, u n ≡ p * 2 ^ n [MOD v]) (N : ℕ) : (doublingWrapCount (p * 2 ^ N) v h : ℝ) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, binaryCoeffTail coeff (shift + (N + j))
declarations.docstring: Any shifted natural tail state with the correct numerator congruence inherits the canonical wrap-count lower bound on every complete block.

declarations.name: support_fraction_wrapCount_le_tail_block
declarations.signature: theorem support_fraction_wrapCount_le_tail_block (A : Set ℕ) (hA : ∃ a : ℕ, 0 < a ∧ a ∈ A) (p : ℤ) (c : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hvalue : erdosSupportSeries 2 A = (p : ℝ) / ((2 ^ c * v : ℕ) : ℝ)) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (N : ℕ) : (doublingWrapCount (p.toNat * 2 ^ N) v h : ℝ) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) (c + (N + j))
declarations.docstring: Fraction-facing local order-wrap theorem. The only normalization here is the explicit denominator `2^c*v`; reducedness and oddness enter the order corollary below.

declarations.name: reciprocalSupportTerm
declarations.signature: noncomputable def reciprocalSupportTerm (A : Set ℕ) (a : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The reciprocal summand of a support, with exponent zero harmlessly normalized to zero by real division.

declarations.name: reciprocalMass
declarations.signature: noncomputable def reciprocalMass (A : Set ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The reciprocal mass `ρ(A) = ∑_{a∈A} 1/a`.

declarations.name: ReciprocalMassDivergesOrAtLeast
declarations.signature: def ReciprocalMassDivergesOrAtLeast (A : Set ℕ) (r : ℝ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Extended-real-free statement of a reciprocal-mass lower bound: either the reciprocal family diverges, in which case every finite lower bound is automatic, or its real tsum is at least `r`.

declarations.name: divisorFrequency
declarations.signature: noncomputable def divisorFrequency (A : Set ℕ) (N a : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The finite divisor frequency of `a` in the first `N` positive integers.

declarations.name: sum_supportCoeff_range_eq_sum_div
declarations.signature: theorem sum_supportCoeff_range_eq_sum_div (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, supportCoeff A (n + 1) = ∑ a ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), Set.indicator A (fun a : ℕ => N / a) a
declarations.docstring: Exact finite double counting: summing the support coefficient through `N` is the sum of the counts `⌊N/a⌋` over the support.

declarations.name: tendsto_nat_div_frequency
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_nat_div_frequency (a : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => ((N / a : ℕ) : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)) atTop (nhds ((1 : ℝ) / (a : ℝ)))

declarations.name: tendsto_divisorFrequency
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_divisorFrequency (A : Set ℕ) (a : ℕ) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => divisorFrequency A N a) atTop (nhds (reciprocalSupportTerm A a))

declarations.name: norm_divisorFrequency_le_reciprocalSupportTerm
declarations.signature: theorem norm_divisorFrequency_le_reciprocalSupportTerm (A : Set ℕ) (N a : ℕ) : ‖divisorFrequency A N a‖ ≤ reciprocalSupportTerm A a

declarations.name: tsum_divisorFrequency_eq_supportCoeff_mean
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_divisorFrequency_eq_supportCoeff_mean (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ∑' a : ℕ, divisorFrequency A N a = ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, supportCoeff A (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The frequency tsum is exactly the Cesàro mean of `supportCoeff`.

declarations.name: tendsto_supportCoeff_mean_reciprocalMass
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_supportCoeff_mean_reciprocalMass (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, supportCoeff A (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)) atTop (nhds (reciprocalMass A))
declarations.docstring: If the reciprocal support terms are summable, the Cesàro mean of the divisor-count coefficients tends to `reciprocalMass A`.

declarations.name: le_reciprocalMass_of_eventually_le_supportCoeff_mean
declarations.signature: theorem le_reciprocalMass_of_eventually_le_supportCoeff_mean (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (r : ℝ) (hr : ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, r ≤ ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, supportCoeff A (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)) : r ≤ reciprocalMass A
declarations.docstring: A ready-to-use lower-bound corollary: any eventual lower bound on the support-coefficient Cesàro means is inherited by reciprocal mass.

declarations.name: cesaroMean
declarations.signature: noncomputable def cesaroMean (x : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Cesàro mean of a real sequence over indices `0,...,N-1`.

declarations.name: sum_supportCoeff_cast_eq_sum_binaryCoeffTail_add_boundary
declarations.signature: theorem sum_supportCoeff_cast_eq_sum_binaryCoeffTail_add_boundary (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, supportCoeff A (n + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) = (∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) n) + binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) 0 - binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N
declarations.docstring: Finite telescoping of the binary-tail recurrence.

declarations.name: tendsto_sqrt_nat_div_nat_zero
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_sqrt_nat_div_nat_zero : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => Real.sqrt (N : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)) atTop (nhds 0)

declarations.name: tendsto_binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_div_nat_zero
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_div_nat_zero (A : Set ℕ) : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N / (N : ℝ)) atTop (nhds 0)

declarations.name: tendsto_binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_mean_reciprocalMass
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_mean_reciprocalMass (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) : Tendsto (cesaroMean (binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A))) atTop (nhds (reciprocalMass A))
declarations.docstring: The Cesàro mean of the scaled binary support tails has the same limit as the coefficient mean, namely `reciprocalMass A`. A rational tail state can then be decomposed into a periodic residue fraction and a nonnegative integer excess.

declarations.name: le_reciprocalMass_of_eventually_le_binaryCoeffTail_mean
declarations.signature: theorem le_reciprocalMass_of_eventually_le_binaryCoeffTail_mean (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (r : ℝ) (hr : ∀ᶠ N : ℕ in atTop, r ≤ cesaroMean (binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A)) N) : r ≤ reciprocalMass A

declarations.name: sum_range_mul_eq_sum_blocks
declarations.signature: theorem sum_range_mul_eq_sum_blocks (x : ℕ → ℝ) (M h : ℕ) : ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (M * h), x n = ∑ q ∈ Finset.range M, ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, x (q * h + j)
declarations.docstring: Exact partition of a prefix of length `M*h` into `M` consecutive blocks of length `h`.

declarations.name: div_le_of_tendsto_cesaroMean_of_block_lower_bound
declarations.signature: theorem div_le_of_tendsto_cesaroMean_of_block_lower_bound (x : ℕ → ℝ) (limit : ℝ) (h w : ℕ) (hh : 0 < h) (hlimit : Tendsto (cesaroMean x) atTop (nhds limit)) (hblock : ∀ q : ℕ, (w : ℝ) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, x (q * h + j)) : (w : ℝ) / (h : ℝ) ≤ limit
declarations.docstring: A uniform lower bound `w` on every length-`h` block forces the Cesàro limit to be at least `w/h`.

declarations.name: wrapRatio_le_reciprocalMass_of_binaryCoeffTail_blocks
declarations.signature: theorem wrapRatio_le_reciprocalMass_of_binaryCoeffTail_blocks (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (h w : ℕ) (hh : 0 < h) (hblock : ∀ q : ℕ, (w : ℝ) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) (q * h + j)) : (w : ℝ) / (h : ℝ) ≤ reciprocalMass A
declarations.docstring: A lower bound `w` on every length-`h` block of support tails yields `reciprocalMass A ≥ w / h`.

declarations.name: blockRemainder
declarations.signature: noncomputable def blockRemainder (x : ℕ → ℝ) (h N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The incomplete final block after the `N / h` complete aligned blocks.

declarations.name: sum_range_eq_mul_blockSum_add_blockRemainder
declarations.signature: theorem sum_range_eq_mul_blockSum_add_blockRemainder (x : ℕ → ℝ) (h : ℕ) (blockSum : ℝ) (hblock : ∀ q : ℕ, ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, x (q * h + j) = blockSum) (N : ℕ) : ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, x n = ((N / h : ℕ) : ℝ) * blockSum + blockRemainder x h N

declarations.name: blockRemainder_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem blockRemainder_nonneg (x : ℕ → ℝ) (hx0 : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 ≤ x n) (h N : ℕ) : 0 ≤ blockRemainder x h N

declarations.name: blockRemainder_le_period
declarations.signature: theorem blockRemainder_le_period (x : ℕ → ℝ) (hx1 : ∀ n : ℕ, x n ≤ 1) {h : ℕ} (hh : 0 < h) (N : ℕ) : blockRemainder x h N ≤ (h : ℝ)

declarations.name: tendsto_cesaroMean_of_constant_blocks
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_cesaroMean_of_constant_blocks (x : ℕ → ℝ) (h : ℕ) (blockSum : ℝ) (hh : 0 < h) (hx0 : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 ≤ x n) (hx1 : ∀ n : ℕ, x n ≤ 1) (hblock : ∀ q : ℕ, ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, x (q * h + j) = blockSum) : Tendsto (cesaroMean x) atTop (nhds (blockSum / (h : ℝ)))
declarations.docstring: A nonnegative sequence bounded by one and having the same exact sum on every aligned length-`h` block has Cesàro mean `blockSum / h`.

declarations.name: tendsto_cesaroMean_excess_of_binaryCoeffTail_decomposition
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_cesaroMean_excess_of_binaryCoeffTail_decomposition (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (residue excess : ℕ → ℝ) (residueMean : ℝ) (hdecomp : ∀ N : ℕ, binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N = residue N + excess N) (hresidue : Tendsto (cesaroMean residue) atTop (nhds residueMean)) : Tendsto (cesaroMean excess) atTop (nhds (reciprocalMass A - residueMean))
declarations.docstring: If each tail is a periodic residue contribution plus an excess, the excess Cesàro mean converges automatically to `ρ(A) - residueMean`.

declarations.name: residueMean_le_reciprocalMass_of_binaryCoeffTail_decomposition
declarations.signature: theorem residueMean_le_reciprocalMass_of_binaryCoeffTail_decomposition (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (residue excess : ℕ → ℝ) (residueMean : ℝ) (hdecomp : ∀ N : ℕ, binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N = residue N + excess N) (hexcess : ∀ N : ℕ, 0 ≤ excess N) (hresidue : Tendsto (cesaroMean residue) atTop (nhds residueMean)) : residueMean ≤ reciprocalMass A
declarations.docstring: Direct wrap lower bound: a nonnegative tail excess over a residue word of Cesàro mean `r` forces `ρ(A) ≥ r`.

declarations.name: reciprocalMass_eq_residueMean_add_excessMean
declarations.signature: theorem reciprocalMass_eq_residueMean_add_excessMean (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (residue excess : ℕ → ℝ) (residueMean excessMean : ℝ) (hdecomp : ∀ N : ℕ, binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N = residue N + excess N) (hresidue : Tendsto (cesaroMean residue) atTop (nhds residueMean)) (hexcess : Tendsto (cesaroMean excess) atTop (nhds excessMean)) : reciprocalMass A = residueMean + excessMean
declarations.docstring: Exact `ρ = residueMean + lim-mean(excess)` identity when the excess mean is named explicitly.

declarations.name: doublingResidue_mul_period
declarations.signature: theorem doublingResidue_mul_period (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (q n : ℕ) : doublingResidue (p * 2 ^ (q * h)) v n = doublingResidue p v n

declarations.name: doublingWrapCount_mul_period
declarations.signature: theorem doublingWrapCount_mul_period (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (q : ℕ) : doublingWrapCount (p * 2 ^ (q * h)) v h = doublingWrapCount p v h

declarations.name: tendsto_cesaroMean_normalizedDoublingResidue
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_cesaroMean_normalizedDoublingResidue (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) : Tendsto (cesaroMean (fun N : ℕ => (doublingResidue p v N : ℝ) / (v : ℝ))) atTop (nhds ((doublingWrapCount p v h : ℝ) / (h : ℝ)))

declarations.name: tendsto_oddTailExcess_mean
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_oddTailExcess_mean (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (u : ℕ → ℕ) (hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u) : Tendsto (cesaroMean (fun N : ℕ => (oddTailExcess u v N : ℝ))) atTop (nhds (reciprocalMass A - (doublingWrapCount p v h : ℝ) / (h : ℝ)))
declarations.docstring: The Cesàro mean of the odd-tail excess exists and equals `reciprocalMass A - doublingWrapCount p v h / h`.

declarations.name: reciprocalMass_eq_wrapRatio_add_oddTailExcessMean
declarations.signature: theorem reciprocalMass_eq_wrapRatio_add_oddTailExcessMean (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (u : ℕ → ℕ) (hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u) (excessMean : ℝ) (hexcess : Tendsto (cesaroMean (fun N : ℕ => (oddTailExcess u v N : ℝ))) atTop (nhds excessMean)) : reciprocalMass A = (doublingWrapCount p v h : ℝ) / (h : ℝ) + excessMean
declarations.docstring: Explicit named-limit form of `ρ = w/h + lim mean(excess)`.

declarations.name: doublingWrapRatio_le_reciprocalMass
declarations.signature: theorem doublingWrapRatio_le_reciprocalMass (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (u : ℕ → ℕ) (hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u) : (doublingWrapCount p v h : ℝ) / (h : ℝ) ≤ reciprocalMass A
declarations.docstring: Fully instantiated wrap lower bound for a genuine odd support-tail state.

declarations.name: doublingWrapRatio_reciprocalMassDivergesOrAtLeast
declarations.signature: theorem doublingWrapRatio_reciprocalMassDivergesOrAtLeast (A : Set ℕ) (p : ℕ) {v h : ℕ} (hv : 0 < v) (hperiod : IsDoublingPeriod v h) (u : ℕ → ℕ) (hstate : IsOddSupportTailState A p v u) : ReciprocalMassDivergesOrAtLeast A ((doublingWrapCount p v h : ℝ) / (h : ℝ))

declarations.name: one_div_period_reciprocalMassDivergesOrAtLeast

declarations.signature: theorem orderWrap_minima_table_passes : wrapMinimumCertificate 3 2 1 = true ∧ wrapMinimumCertificate 5 4 2 = true ∧ wrapMinimumCertificate 7 3 1 = true ∧ wrapMinimumCertificate 15 4 1 = true ∧ wrapMinimumCertificate 31 5 1 = true
declarations.docstring: The checked minimum wrap ratios are respectively `1/2`, `2/4`, `1/3`, `1/4`, and `1/5`.

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneAtom
declarations.signature: noncomputable def shiftedMersenneAtom (N d : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The contribution of support rank `d` to the binary coefficient tail at shift `N`. Rank zero is normalized to zero, consistently with `erdosSupportSeries`.

declarations.name: shiftedSupportAtom
declarations.signature: noncomputable def shiftedSupportAtom (A : Set ℕ) (N d : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The shifted atom restricted to a support set.

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneAtom_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneAtom_nonneg (N d : ℕ) : 0 ≤ shiftedMersenneAtom N d

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneAtom_zero
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneAtom_zero (d : ℕ) : shiftedMersenneAtom 0 d = (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1)

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneOrbitMean
declarations.signature: noncomputable def shiftedMersenneOrbitMean (Q d : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The exact mean of the `d`-atom sampled along positive multiples of `Q`. The conductor-zero branch matches the normalization of `shiftedMersenneAtom`.

declarations.name: shiftedSupportOrbitMean
declarations.signature: noncomputable def shiftedSupportOrbitMean (A : Set ℕ) (Q d : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The GCD orbit mean restricted to a support set.

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneOrbitMean_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneOrbitMean_nonneg (Q d : ℕ) : 0 ≤ shiftedMersenneOrbitMean Q d

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneOrbitMean_le_reciprocal
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneOrbitMean_le_reciprocal (Q d : ℕ) : shiftedMersenneOrbitMean Q d ≤ (1 : ℝ) / (d : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Every GCD orbit mean is bounded by the reciprocal conductor. This is the `Q`-independent majorant used in the outer LCM-prefix limit.

declarations.name: shiftedSupportOrbitMean_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedSupportOrbitMean_nonneg (A : Set ℕ) (Q d : ℕ) : 0 ≤ shiftedSupportOrbitMean A Q d

declarations.name: shiftedSupportOrbitMean_le_reciprocalSupportTerm
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedSupportOrbitMean_le_reciprocalSupportTerm (A : Set ℕ) (Q d : ℕ) : shiftedSupportOrbitMean A Q d ≤ reciprocalSupportTerm A d

declarations.name: norm_shiftedSupportOrbitMean_le_reciprocalSupportTerm
declarations.signature: theorem norm_shiftedSupportOrbitMean_le_reciprocalSupportTerm (A : Set ℕ) (Q d : ℕ) : ‖shiftedSupportOrbitMean A Q d‖ ≤ reciprocalSupportTerm A d

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneOrbitMean_eq_zero_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneOrbitMean_eq_zero_of_dvd (Q d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hdiv : d ∣ Q) : shiftedMersenneOrbitMean Q d = shiftedMersenneAtom 0 d
declarations.docstring: When the conductor divides the sampling step, its orbit is frozen at the zero-shift atom.

declarations.name: shiftedSupportOrbitMean_eq_zero_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedSupportOrbitMean_eq_zero_of_dvd (A : Set ℕ) (Q d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hdiv : d ∣ Q) : shiftedSupportOrbitMean A Q d = shiftedSupportAtom A 0 d

declarations.name: sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_gcdOrbit
declarations.signature: theorem sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_gcdOrbit (Q d : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hd : 0 < d) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (d / Nat.gcd Q d), shiftedMersenneAtom ((k + 1) * Q) d = (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ Nat.gcd Q d - 1)
declarations.docstring: One complete GCD orbit of positive `Q`-multiples has the exact geometric atom mass `1 / (2^g - 1)`, where `g = gcd Q d`.

declarations.name: sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_gcdOrbit_block
declarations.signature: theorem sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_gcdOrbit_block (Q d : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hd : 0 < d) (b : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (d / Nat.gcd Q d), shiftedMersenneAtom ((b * (d / Nat.gcd Q d) + j + 1) * Q) d = (1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ Nat.gcd Q d - 1)
declarations.docstring: Every aligned block of length `d / gcd Q d` is the same complete GCD orbit.

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneAtom_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneAtom_le_one (N d : ℕ) : shiftedMersenneAtom N d ≤ 1

declarations.name: tendsto_cesaroMean_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_cesaroMean_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul (Q d : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hd : 0 < d) : Tendsto (cesaroMean (fun k : ℕ => shiftedMersenneAtom ((k + 1) * Q) d)) atTop (nhds (shiftedMersenneOrbitMean Q d))
declarations.docstring: Sampling a positive Mersenne atom along positive `Q`-multiples has the exact GCD-orbit Cesàro mean.

declarations.name: sum_pow_positiveMultiples_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_pow_positiveMultiples_le (Q K : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range K, 2 ^ ((k + 1) * Q) ≤ 2 ^ (K * Q + 1) - 1

declarations.name: blockRemainder_le_blockSum
declarations.signature: theorem blockRemainder_le_blockSum (x : ℕ → ℝ) (h : ℕ) (blockSum : ℝ) (hh : 0 < h) (hx0 : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 ≤ x n) (hblock : ∀ q : ℕ, ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, x (q * h + j) = blockSum) (N : ℕ) : blockRemainder x h N ≤ blockSum

declarations.name: sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le_blockCount
declarations.signature: theorem sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le_blockCount (Q d K : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hd : 0 < d) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range K, shiftedMersenneAtom ((k + 1) * Q) d ≤ ((K / (d / Nat.gcd Q d) : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1
declarations.docstring: In the wrapped range, complete GCD-orbit blocks and the final prefix give the sharp block-count upper bound.

declarations.name: sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le_inv_pow_gap_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le_inv_pow_gap_of_lt (Q d K : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hd : 0 < d) (hnowrap : K * Q < d) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range K, shiftedMersenneAtom ((k + 1) * Q) d ≤ (1 : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ (d - K * Q - 1)
declarations.docstring: Before the first wrap, the sampled numerator is a sparse subset of the initial binary geometric sum; the remaining exponent gap controls its mass.

declarations.name: cesaroMean_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le
declarations.signature: theorem cesaroMean_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le (Q d K : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hK : 0 < K) : cesaroMean (fun k : ℕ => shiftedMersenneAtom ((k + 1) * Q) d) K ≤ (2 * (Q + 1) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A finite Cesàro mean along positive `Q`-multiples has a conductor majorant independent of the averaging length. Complete gcd-orbit blocks control the wrapped range, while the initial geometric gap controls the range before the first wrap.

declarations.name: cesaroMean_shiftedSupportAtom_mul_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem cesaroMean_shiftedSupportAtom_mul_nonneg (A : Set ℕ) (Q d K : ℕ) : 0 ≤ cesaroMean (fun k : ℕ => shiftedSupportAtom A ((k + 1) * Q) d) K

declarations.name: tendsto_cesaroMean_shiftedSupportAtom_mul
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_cesaroMean_shiftedSupportAtom_mul (A : Set ℕ) (Q d : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) : Tendsto (fun K : ℕ => cesaroMean (fun k : ℕ => shiftedSupportAtom A ((k + 1) * Q) d) K) atTop (nhds (shiftedSupportOrbitMean A Q d))

declarations.name: norm_cesaroMean_shiftedSupportAtom_mul_le
declarations.signature: theorem norm_cesaroMean_shiftedSupportAtom_mul_le (A : Set ℕ) (Q d K : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hK : 0 < K) : ‖cesaroMean (fun k : ℕ => shiftedSupportAtom A ((k + 1) * Q) d) K‖ ≤ (2 * (Q + 1) : ℝ) * reciprocalSupportTerm A d
declarations.docstring: The finite means admit a fixed-`Q`, summable conductor majorant.

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneAtom_step
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneAtom_step (N d : ℕ) : 2 * shiftedMersenneAtom N d - shiftedMersenneAtom (N + 1) d = if 0 < d ∧ d ∣ N + 1 then 1 else 0
declarations.docstring: The real-valued atom inherits the exact carry step of the rational atom already present in `MersenneTailAtoms`.

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneAtom_le_pow_mul_zero
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneAtom_le_pow_mul_zero (N d : ℕ) : shiftedMersenneAtom N d ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ N * ((1 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1))

declarations.name: summable_shiftedSupportAtom
declarations.signature: theorem summable_shiftedSupportAtom (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : Summable (shiftedSupportAtom A N)

declarations.name: tsum_cesaroMean_shiftedSupportAtom_mul
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_cesaroMean_shiftedSupportAtom_mul (A : Set ℕ) (Q K : ℕ) : (∑' d : ℕ, cesaroMean (fun k : ℕ => shiftedSupportAtom A ((k + 1) * Q) d) K) = cesaroMean (fun k : ℕ => ∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A ((k + 1) * Q) d) K
declarations.docstring: Summing in the conductor commutes with the finite Cesàro mean.

declarations.name: tendsto_cesaroMean_tsum_shiftedSupportAtom_mul
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_cesaroMean_tsum_shiftedSupportAtom_mul (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (Q : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) : Tendsto (fun K : ℕ => cesaroMean (fun k : ℕ => ∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A ((k + 1) * Q) d) K) atTop (nhds (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportOrbitMean A Q d))
declarations.docstring: For a fixed positive step, the Cesàro means of the complete support tail converge to the sum of the gcd-orbit means.

declarations.name: tendsto_shiftedSupportOrbitMean_periodLcm
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_shiftedSupportOrbitMean_periodLcm (A : Set ℕ) (d : ℕ) : Tendsto (fun P : ℕ => shiftedSupportOrbitMean A (periodLcm P) d) atTop (nhds (shiftedSupportAtom A 0 d))

declarations.name: tendsto_tsum_shiftedSupportOrbitMean_periodLcm
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_tsum_shiftedSupportOrbitMean_periodLcm (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) : Tendsto (fun P : ℕ => ∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportOrbitMean A (periodLcm P) d) atTop (nhds (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A 0 d))
declarations.docstring: Along the LCM-prefix steps, the orbit-mean sum returns to the zero-shift support sum. This is the outer dominated-convergence limit.

declarations.name: tsum_shiftedSupportAtom_zero
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_shiftedSupportAtom_zero (A : Set ℕ) : (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A 0 d) = erdosSupportSeries 2 A
declarations.docstring: The support-atom sum at shift zero is the original support series.

declarations.name: shiftedSupportAtom_step
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedSupportAtom_step (A : Set ℕ) [DecidablePred (· ∈ A)] (N d : ℕ) : 2 * shiftedSupportAtom A N d - shiftedSupportAtom A (N + 1) d = if d ∈ A ∧ 0 < d ∧ d ∣ N + 1 then 1 else 0

declarations.name: tsum_shiftedSupportAtom_step
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_shiftedSupportAtom_step (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : 2 * (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A N d) - (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A (N + 1) d) = (supportCoeff A (N + 1) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Summing the atom carry steps recovers the support coefficient.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_eq_tsum_shiftedSupportAtom
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_eq_tsum_shiftedSupportAtom (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N = ∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A N d
declarations.docstring: The whole shifted-atom sum is exactly the binary coefficient tail. This is the atomization identity needed to transfer pointwise support information to the existing tail orbit.

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneAtom_zero_le
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneAtom_zero_le (N d : ℕ) : shiftedMersenneAtom 0 d ≤ shiftedMersenneAtom N d

declarations.name: shiftedMersenneAtom_zero_lt_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedMersenneAtom_zero_lt_of_lt (N d : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hNd : N < d) : shiftedMersenneAtom 0 d < shiftedMersenneAtom N d

declarations.name: shiftedSupportAtom_zero_le
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedSupportAtom_zero_le (A : Set ℕ) (N d : ℕ) : shiftedSupportAtom A 0 d ≤ shiftedSupportAtom A N d

declarations.name: shiftedSupportAtom_zero_lt_of_mem_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedSupportAtom_zero_lt_of_mem_of_lt (A : Set ℕ) (N d : ℕ) (hdA : d ∈ A) (hN : 0 < N) (hNd : N < d) : shiftedSupportAtom A 0 d < shiftedSupportAtom A N d

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_zero_strictMinimum
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_zero_strictMinimum (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) : binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) 0 < binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N
declarations.docstring: For an infinite support, shift zero is the strict global minimum of the binary support-tail orbit. The strict witness is any support rank above the positive shift.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_ne_initial_of_pos
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_supportCoeff_ne_initial_of_pos (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) : binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) N ≠ binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) 0
declarations.docstring: An infinite support tail orbit never returns to its initial value at a positive time.

declarations.name: irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_strictInitialMin_of_closeReturn
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_strictInitialMin_of_closeReturn (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (hstrict : ∀ N : ℕ, 0 < N → binaryCoeffTail c 0 < binaryCoeffTail c N) (hclose : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ binaryCoeffTail c N < binaryCoeffTail c 0 + ε) : Irrational (binaryCoeffSeries c)
declarations.docstring: A coefficient tail with a strict initial minimum and arbitrarily close positive returns cannot start from a rational binary series. Rationality would put every tail, after multiplication by one fixed positive integer, in the integer lattice; a positive return gap smaller than one lattice spacing is then impossible.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSupportSeries_two_of_infinite_of_shiftedAtom_closeReturn
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSupportSeries_two_of_infinite_of_shiftedAtom_closeReturn (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hclose : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A N d) < (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A 0 d) + ε) : Irrational (erdosSupportSeries 2 A)
declarations.docstring: Infinite support supplies the strict-minimum half of the generic integer-gap endgame. The remaining hypothesis is stated exactly as the positive shifted-atom near-return property; no summability-to-return theorem is assumed here.

declarations.name: exists_shiftedSupportAtom_closeReturn_of_summable_reciprocal
declarations.signature: theorem exists_shiftedSupportAtom_closeReturn_of_summable_reciprocal (A : Set ℕ) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A N d) < (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedSupportAtom A 0 d) + ε
declarations.docstring: Reciprocal summability supplies arbitrarily close positive returns of the complete shifted-atom sum. The proof first takes the LCM-prefix limit of the gcd-orbit means, then a Cesàro limit at the selected positive LCM step, and finally chooses one term no larger than that finite average.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSupportSeries_two_of_summable_reciprocal
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSupportSeries_two_of_summable_reciprocal (A : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hsum : Summable (reciprocalSupportTerm A)) : Irrational (erdosSupportSeries 2 A)
declarations.docstring: Every infinite reciprocal-summable support gives an irrational binary Mersenne subseries.

declarations.name: irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_shiftedTwoSidedReturn
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_shiftedTwoSidedReturn (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (c0 : ℕ) (hreturn : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ binaryCoeffTail c 0 + (c0 : ℝ) < binaryCoeffTail c N ∧ binaryCoeffTail c N < binaryCoeffTail c 0 + (c0 : ℝ) + ε) : Irrational (binaryCoeffSeries c)
declarations.docstring: **Generalised integer-gap endgame.** Irrationality follows from a single sequence of witnesses at which the tail exceeds `binaryCoeffTail c 0 + c0` and approaches it arbitrarily closely, for any NATURAL shift `c0`. Two weakenings of `irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_strictInitialMin_of_closeReturn`. First, that theorem's strict minimum is stated globally but its proof consumes it at exactly one `N` -- the witness produced by the close return -- so the two hypotheses merge into one two-sided condition at a common witness. Second, the return may be to a shifted value. **Integrality of the shift is essential**: the endgame closes because no integer lies strictly inside `(v*c0, v*c0 + 1)`, and a non-integer shift would leave exactly one integer there.

declarations.name: irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_strictInitialMin_of_closeReturn_of_shifted
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_strictInitialMin_of_closeReturn_of_shifted (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (hstrict : ∀ N : ℕ, 0 < N → binaryCoeffTail c 0 < binaryCoeffTail c N) (hclose : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ binaryCoeffTail c N < binaryCoeffTail c 0 + ε) : Irrational (binaryCoeffSeries c)
declarations.docstring: Regression: the previously stated form -- global strict minimum, shift zero -- is the special case `c0 = 0` of the generalised endgame.

declarations.name: coprime_succ_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem coprime_succ_of_dvd {k m : ℕ} (h : k ∣ m) : Nat.Coprime k (m + 1)
declarations.docstring: If `k` divides `m` then `k` is coprime to `m + 1`.

declarations.name: coprime_cofactor_of_sq_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem coprime_cofactor_of_sq_dvd {k Q : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (hsq : k * k ∣ Q) (n : ℕ) : Nat.Coprime k (n * (Q / k) + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The coprimality that makes the block factorisation work.** When `k^2 ∣ Q`, the cofactor `n * (Q / k) + 1` is coprime to `k`, because `k ∣ Q / k`.

declarations.name: block_factorisation
declarations.signature: theorem block_factorisation {k Q : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (hdvd : k ∣ Q) (n : ℕ) : n * Q + k = k * (n * (Q / k) + 1)
declarations.docstring: The block factorisation itself: `n * Q + k = k * (n * (Q / k) + 1)` whenever `k ∣ Q`.

declarations.name: card_primeFactors_mul_of_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem card_primeFactors_mul_of_coprime {a b : ℕ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) : (a * b).primeFactors.card = a.primeFactors.card + b.primeFactors.card
declarations.docstring: `omega` is additive on coprime factors.

declarations.name: card_primeFactors_block_of_sq_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem card_primeFactors_block_of_sq_dvd {k Q n : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (hsq : k * k ∣ Q) (hp : Nat.Prime (n * (Q / k) + 1)) : (n * Q + k).primeFactors.card = k.primeFactors.card + 1
declarations.docstring: **Pratt's shift identity.** If `k^2 ∣ Q`, `0 < k`, and the cofactor `n * (Q / k) + 1` is prime, then the block index `n * Q + k` carries exactly one more distinct prime factor than `k` does: omega (n * Q + k) = omega k + 1. This is the step that makes the tail reproduce the head shifted by one, and hence the step that produces a return to `y + 1/(t-1)` rather than to `y`.

declarations.name: geom_sum_half
declarations.signature: theorem geom_sum_half : ∀ K : ℕ, (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, ((1 : ℝ) / 2 ^ j)) = 1 - 1 / 2 ^ K

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_split
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_split (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (N : ℕ) : ∀ K : ℕ, binaryCoeffTail c N = (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, (c (N + j) : ℝ) / 2 ^ j) + binaryCoeffTail c (N + K) / 2 ^ K
declarations.docstring: **Finite split.** The tail at `N` is its first `K` coefficients, weighted dyadically, plus `2^-K` times the tail at `N + K`. Proved by induction from the one-step recurrence `binaryCoeffTail_succ`; no series rearrangement is needed.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_shifted_block
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_shifted_block (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (N K : ℕ) (hshift : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ K → c (N + j) = c j + 1) : binaryCoeffTail c N = binaryCoeffTail c 0 + 1 + (binaryCoeffTail c (N + K) - binaryCoeffTail c K - 1) / 2 ^ K
declarations.docstring: **The shifted-block identity.** If the coefficient sequence at `N` reproduces its own head shifted by one across `1 ≤ j ≤ K`, then the tail at `N` sits exactly one above the tail at `0`, up to a `2^-K`-scaled remainder. This is the `S_1` computation of Pratt's argument, as an exact identity rather than an estimate.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_ge_head
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_ge_head (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (M : ℕ) : (c (M + 1) : ℝ) / 2 ≤ binaryCoeffTail c M
declarations.docstring: The tail dominates half its own leading coefficient. Immediate from the finite split at `K = 1` together with non-negativity of the remaining tail.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_shifted_block_lower
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_shifted_block_lower (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (N K : ℕ) (B : ℝ) (hshift : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ K → c (N + j) = c j + 1) (hK : binaryCoeffTail c K ≤ B) (hbig : 2 * (B + 1) < (c (N + K + 1) : ℝ)) : binaryCoeffTail c 0 + 1 < binaryCoeffTail c N
declarations.docstring: **Lower half of the shifted return.** Under the `+1` shift on `1 ≤ j ≤ K`, a single large coefficient just past the block forces the tail at `N` strictly above `tail 0 + 1`. The bound `B` on `binaryCoeffTail c K` is taken as a hypothesis: for `c = omega` it needs an arithmetic input (`omega n << log n`) beyond `c n ≤ n`, and `binaryCoeffTail_le` is far too weak to supply it.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_shifted_block_upper
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_shifted_block_upper (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (N K : ℕ) (U eps : ℝ) (hshift : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ K → c (N + j) = c j + 1) (hU : binaryCoeffTail c (N + K) ≤ U) (hsmall : U - 1 < eps * 2 ^ K) : binaryCoeffTail c N < binaryCoeffTail c 0 + 1 + eps
declarations.docstring: **Upper half of the shifted return.** Under the `+1` shift on `1 ≤ j ≤ K`, a bound `U` on the tail just past the block caps the tail at `N` within `eps` of `tail 0 + 1`, provided `U - 1 < eps * 2^K`. Mirror of `binaryCoeffTail_shifted_block_lower`.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_shifted_block_two_sided
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_shifted_block_two_sided (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (N K : ℕ) (B U eps : ℝ) (hshift : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ K → c (N + j) = c j + 1) (hK : binaryCoeffTail c K ≤ B) (hbig : 2 * (B + 1) < (c (N + K + 1) : ℝ)) (hU : binaryCoeffTail c (N + K) ≤ U) (hsmall : U - 1 < eps * 2 ^ K) : binaryCoeffTail c 0 + 1 < binaryCoeffTail c N ∧ binaryCoeffTail c N < binaryCoeffTail c 0 + 1 + eps
declarations.docstring: **The per-witness two-sided return.** Both halves at a single `N`: exactly the body of the `hreturn` hypothesis consumed by `irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_shiftedTwoSidedReturn` at `c0 = 1`.

declarations.name: binaryCoeffTail_le_of_bound
declarations.signature: theorem binaryCoeffTail_le_of_bound (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (M : ℕ) (B : ℝ) (hb : ∀ j : ℕ, (c (M + j + 1) : ℝ) ≤ B) : binaryCoeffTail c M ≤ B
declarations.docstring: **Tail bound from a uniform coefficient bound.** If every coefficient past `M` is at most `B`, the whole tail at `M` is at most `B`. Unlike everything else in this development this genuinely needs the infinite sum: `binaryCoeffTail_split` leaves a `2^-K`-scaled remainder that is itself the quantity being bounded.

declarations.name: shiftedBlockWitnesses_coeffBounds_unsatisfiable
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedBlockWitnesses_coeffBounds_unsatisfiable (c : ℕ → ℕ) (N K : ℕ) (B : ℝ) (hBK : ∀ j : ℕ, (c (K + j + 1) : ℝ) ≤ B) (hbig : 2 * (B + 1) < (c (N + K + 1) : ℝ)) : False
declarations.docstring: **The pointwise-bound witness form is UNSATISFIABLE.** An earlier version of the assembly below took uniform *coefficient* bounds `forall j, c (K + j + 1) <= B` where the underlying lemma wants the *tail* bound `binaryCoeffTail c K <= B`. That form is self-contradictory: instantiating the coefficient bound at `j = N` gives `c (N + K + 1) <= B`, which the large-coefficient clause `2 * (B + 1) < c (N + K + 1)` contradicts outright, since `B >= c (K + 1) >= 0`. Recorded rather than deleted, because this defect is invisible to every check that was run on it: the wrapper elaborated, the build reported `rc = 0`, and `#print axioms` gave `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. A vacuously true theorem passes all three. A conditional theorem is worth exactly what its hypothesis is worth, and nothing in the toolchain checks that a hypothesis is satisfiable.

declarations.name: irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_shiftedBlockWitnesses
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_binaryCoeffSeries_of_shiftedBlockWitnesses (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (hwit : ∀ eps : ℝ, 0 < eps → ∃ N K : ℕ, ∃ B U : ℝ, 0 < N ∧ (∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ K → c (N + j) = c j + 1) ∧ binaryCoeffTail c K ≤ B ∧ 2 * (B + 1) < (c (N + K + 1) : ℝ) ∧ binaryCoeffTail c (N + K) ≤ U ∧ U - 1 < eps * 2 ^ K) : Irrational (binaryCoeffSeries c)
declarations.docstring: **Irrationality from a supply of shifted-block witnesses.** Given, for every `eps > 0`, a block `(N, K)` on which the coefficient sequence reproduces its own head shifted by one, a tail bound `B` at `K`, one anomalously large coefficient at `N + K + 1`, and a tail bound `U` at `N + K` small against `eps * 2 ^ K`, the series is irrational. The two bounds are on **tails**, not on individual coefficients; see `shiftedBlockWitnesses_coeffBounds_unsatisfiable`. The distinction is what keeps this statement non-vacuous for an unbounded `c`: `binaryCoeffTail c K <= B` forces only `c (N + K + 1) <= B * 2 ^ (N + 1)`, which leaves room for `2 * (B + 1) < c (N + K + 1)`. That matters because the intended instantiation `c = omega` is unbounded, so any hypothesis demanding a uniform coefficient bound past a point is unsatisfiable at the one instance the theorem exists to serve.

declarations.name: shiftedBlockWitness_forces_small_tail
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedBlockWitness_forces_small_tail (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (N K : ℕ) (B U eps : ℝ) (hK : binaryCoeffTail c K ≤ B) (hbig : 2 * (B + 1) < (c (N + K + 1) : ℝ)) (hU : binaryCoeffTail c (N + K) ≤ U) (hsmall : U - 1 < eps * 2 ^ K) : binaryCoeffTail c K < eps * 2 ^ K
declarations.docstring: **Any witness forces its own head-tail to be small against `2 ^ K`.** Chaining the four numeric clauses: `binaryCoeffTail_ge_head` gives `c (N+K+1) / 2 <= binaryCoeffTail c (N+K) <= U`, and `hbig` makes that lower bound exceed `B + 1`; with `U - 1 < eps * 2 ^ K` this pins `B`, hence the tail at `K`, below `eps * 2 ^ K`. No new analysis -- this is the engine's own hypotheses talking to each other. It matters because it converts a statement about coefficients into a lower bound on the BLOCK LENGTH `K`, which is the quantity the shift clause has to supply.

declarations.name: shiftedBlockWitness_forces_large_block
declarations.signature: theorem shiftedBlockWitness_forces_large_block (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n : ℕ, c n ≤ n) (N K : ℕ) (B U eps delta : ℝ) (hdelta : delta ≤ binaryCoeffTail c K) (hK : binaryCoeffTail c K ≤ B) (hbig : 2 * (B + 1) < (c (N + K + 1) : ℝ)) (hU : binaryCoeffTail c (N + K) ≤ U) (hsmall : U - 1 < eps * 2 ^ K) : delta < eps * 2 ^ K
declarations.docstring: **The block length diverges as `eps -> 0`.** If the head-tails are bounded below by `delta > 0` -- which holds whenever `c` is not eventually zero, i.e. for every infinite support set -- then every witness for `eps` satisfies `delta < eps * 2 ^ K`. So `2 ^ K > delta / eps`, and `K` is forced past any bound as `eps` shrinks. **Consequence.** The engine cannot be driven by short blocks. A support set that admits shift blocks only up to some fixed length `K_max` supplies no witness for `eps < delta / 2 ^ K_max`, and the conditional is unusable there -- however true it is.

declarations.name: socketRun_excludes_odd_coeff
declarations.signature: theorem socketRun_excludes_odd_coeff (c : ℕ → ℕ) (N K k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hkK : k ≤ K) (hrun : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ K → 2 ^ i ∣ c (N + i)) (hodd : ¬ (2 ∣ c (N + k))) : False
declarations.docstring: **A socket run cannot pass an odd coefficient.** Erdos's 1948 argument produces a run of `K` binary zeros in `sum_n c n / 2^n` by forcing `2 ^ k` to divide `c (N + k)` for `k = 1, ..., K`, which makes each of the first `K` terms of the shifted sum an integer. Since `1 <= k` gives `2 | 2 ^ k`, every coefficient inside the run is even. So a single odd coefficient anywhere in the window destroys the run.

declarations.name: no_socketRun_of_odd_in_window
declarations.signature: theorem no_socketRun_of_odd_in_window (c : ℕ → ℕ) (N g : ℕ) (hwin : ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ g ∧ ¬ (2 ∣ c (N + k))) : ¬ (∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ g → 2 ^ i ∣ c (N + i))
declarations.docstring: **The run length is bounded by the gaps of `{m : c m odd}`.** If every window of `g` consecutive indices past `N` contains an odd coefficient, no run of length `g` starts at `N`. Writing `Odd_c := {m : c m is odd}`, this says maxrun <= maxgap (Odd_c) - 1, so **arbitrarily long socket runs require `Odd_c` to have unbounded gaps** -- if `Odd_c` is syndetic the mechanism is unavailable, not merely unproven. At `c = tau_N = d` the odd set is exactly the perfect squares, whose gaps grow like `2 sqrt m`; the obstruction is vacuous there, as it must be, since Erdos carried the construction out. At `c = v_2` (support `{2,4,8,...}`) the odd set contains every `m = 2 mod 4`, so `g = 4` and the run caps at 3.

declarations.name: socketRun_forces_pow_le_coeff
declarations.signature: theorem socketRun_forces_pow_le_coeff (c : ℕ → ℕ) (N K k : ℕ) (hk1 : 1 ≤ k) (hkK : k ≤ K) (hrun : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ K → 2 ^ i ∣ c (N + i)) (hpos : 0 < c (N + k)) : 2 ^ k ≤ c (N + k)
declarations.docstring: **A socket run forces its nonzero coefficients to be exponentially large.** Inside a run, `2 ^ k` divides `c (N + k)`; a nonzero natural divisible by `2 ^ k` is at least `2 ^ k`. Zero coefficients are exempt -- zero is divisible by everything -- so the force lands only where `c` is actually positive.

declarations.name: socketRun_forces_pow_le_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem socketRun_forces_pow_le_of_le (c : ℕ → ℕ) (N K k j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ k) (hk1 : 1 ≤ k) (hkK : k ≤ K) (hrun : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ K → 2 ^ i ∣ c (N + i)) (hpos : 0 < c (N + k)) : 2 ^ j ≤ c (N + k)
declarations.docstring: **The search-depth law.** Combined with the fact that any `a` in the support divides one of every `a` consecutive integers -- so some index `k` in the top `a` of the window has `c (N + k) > 0` -- this gives `2 ^ (K - a + 1) <= max c` over the window. **This is NOT a cap.** Since `c = tau_A` is unbounded for every infinite `A`, the right side grows without bound and no `K` is ever excluded outright. What the bound gives is a DEPTH: to observe a run of length `K` one must search out to where `c` reaches `2 ^ K`. That is the quantitative form of "finite search never refutes existence" -- contrast the parity obstruction, which bounds the run for ALL `N` at once.

declarations.name: no_two_powers_two_apart
declarations.signature: theorem no_two_powers_two_apart {v w : ℕ} (hv : 2 ≤ v) (hw : 2 ≤ w) (h : 2 ^ w = 2 ^ v + 2) : False
declarations.docstring: **Two powers of two cannot differ by 2 once both are at least 4.** This is the load-bearing step of the block cap proved in `CertificateSocketCollapse.md` section 56: for the support set `A* = (N \ {2^i}) xor {4p}`, a shifted block of length `>= 4` starting at an EVEN `N` would force both `N+2` and `N+4` to be powers of two at least 8, and this lemma forbids it -- so the block length is at most 3. The argument is a residue count, not a valuation computation: both `2^v` and `2^w` are divisible by 4 once the exponents are at least 2, while `2^v + 2` is congruent to 2.

declarations.name: supportCoeff_primes_eq_omega_fun
declarations.signature: theorem supportCoeff_primes_eq_omega_fun : supportCoeff {p : ℕ | p.Prime} = fun n => n.primeFactors.card
declarations.docstring: `supportCoeff` at the primes, as a function identity, for rewriting under `binaryCoeffTail`.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSupportSeries_two_primes_of_shiftedBlockWitnesses
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSupportSeries_two_primes_of_shiftedBlockWitnesses (hwit : ∀ eps : ℝ, 0 < eps → ∃ N K : ℕ, ∃ B U : ℝ, 0 < N ∧ (∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ K → supportCoeff {p : ℕ | p.Prime} (N + j) = supportCoeff {p : ℕ | p.Prime} j + 1) ∧ binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff {p : ℕ | p.Prime}) K ≤ B ∧ 2 * (B + 1) < (supportCoeff {p : ℕ | p.Prime} (N + K + 1) : ℝ) ∧ binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff {p : ℕ | p.Prime}) (N + K) ≤ U ∧ U - 1 < eps * 2 ^ K) : Irrational (erdosSupportSeries 2 {p : ℕ | p.Prime})
declarations.docstring: **Erdos #69, conditional on block witnesses.** `CertificateKernel`'s `erdosSupportSeries_primes_eq_tsum_omega` records that `∑_p 1/(b^p - 1) = ∑_m omega(m)/b^m` and says the identity "places [the analytic input] at the exact theorem boundary where it belongs". This theorem consumes that boundary: the shift clause is `card_primeFactors_block_of_sq_dvd` in support language, and the remaining clauses are exactly Pratt's Proposition 2.1, which is **assumed here and never proved**.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSupportSeries_two_primes_of_omega_witnesses
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSupportSeries_two_primes_of_omega_witnesses (hwit : ∀ eps : ℝ, 0 < eps → ∃ N K : ℕ, ∃ B U : ℝ, 0 < N ∧ (∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → j ≤ K → (N + j).primeFactors.card = j.primeFactors.card + 1) ∧ binaryCoeffTail (fun n => n.primeFactors.card) K ≤ B ∧ 2 * (B + 1) < (((N + K + 1).primeFactors.card : ℕ) : ℝ) ∧ binaryCoeffTail (fun n => n.primeFactors.card) (N + K) ≤ U ∧ U - 1 < eps * 2 ^ K) : Irrational (erdosSupportSeries 2 {p : ℕ | p.Prime})
declarations.docstring: The same statement with every hypothesis phrased in `omega`, via `supportCoeff_primes_eq_card_primeFactors`. This is Erdos problem 69 verbatim: irrationality of `∑_p 1/(2^p - 1)`, conditional on the block witnesses.

declarations.name: rowResidualMonomialMatrix
