If `x = p/q` and `Δ = pT-q`, then `p/3 < Δ < p`. The third channel is decisive for the strict lower bound: the first two channels alone approach `p/3` from the wrong side.

declarations.name: lastTwentyOneSkip_dyadicExcess_window
declarations.signature: theorem lastTwentyOneSkip_dyadicExcess_window {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastTwentyOneGreedySkip M) : let x
declarations.docstring: At a final denominator-`21` skip, the reduced residual immediately before the skip lies in the three-channel dyadic window. Thus its exact excess `Δ = p * 2^M - q` satisfies `p / 3 < Δ < p`.

declarations.name: greedyTwentyOneRemainderRat_den_odd
declarations.signature: theorem greedyTwentyOneRemainderRat_den_odd (n : ℕ) : Odd (greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 21 : ℚ) n).den
declarations.docstring: Every reduced rational residual on the `1/21` greedy orbit has odd denominator. The target denominator and every selected Mersenne denominator are odd, and reduction can only divide their lcm.

declarations.name: rat_sub_inv_oddDen_num_parity_flip
declarations.signature: theorem rat_sub_inv_oddDen_num_parity_flip (x : ℚ) {Q : ℕ} (hQpos : 0 < Q) (hxdenOdd : Odd x.den) (hQOdd : Odd Q) (htake : (1 : ℚ) / Q < x) : let y
declarations.docstring: Subtracting the reciprocal of an odd denominator flips the parity of the reduced numerator, provided the subtraction stays positive. The point is that both stages of rational cancellation are odd: the common factor of the two odd denominators is odd, and so is the residual normalizing factor. Thus cancellation cannot alter the parity flip in `p * (Q / gcd(q,Q)) - q / gcd(q,Q)`.

declarations.name: lastTwentyOneSkip_remainder_num_ge_four
declarations.signature: theorem lastTwentyOneSkip_remainder_num_ge_four {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastTwentyOneGreedySkip M) : 4 ≤ (greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 21 : ℚ) (M - 1)).num.natAbs
declarations.docstring: The three-channel window excludes every small reduced numerator at a hypothetical final skip. Numerator `2` would be the already-forbidden Mersenne exceptional coordinate; numerator `3` would force an even denominator, contradicting the odd-denominator orbit invariant.

declarations.name: dyadicExcess_adjacent_gcd_parity
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicExcess_adjacent_gcd_parity {p q T delta : ℕ} (hTpos : 0 < T) (hqOdd : Odd q) (hdeltaOdd : Odd delta) (hcop : p.Coprime q) (hbalance : delta + q = p * T) (hlower : p < 3 * delta) (hupper : delta < p) (hp4 : 4 ≤ p) : (Odd p → 3 * Nat.gcd q (T - 1) < p) ∧ (Even p → 2 * Nat.gcd q (2 * T - 1) < p)
declarations.docstring: Parity-sensitive cancellation in a reduced dyadic excess window. Suppose `delta + q = p*T`, with `T` even, `q` and `delta` odd, and `p/3 < delta < p`. If `p` is odd, the predecessor gcd divides the even error `p-delta`, so its odd part is smaller than one third of `p`. If `p` is even, the successor gcd divides twice the distance from `delta` to `p/2`; coprimality excludes zero distance, so it is smaller than one half of `p`.

declarations.name: lastTwentyOneSkip_adjacent_gcd_parity
declarations.signature: theorem lastTwentyOneSkip_adjacent_gcd_parity {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastTwentyOneGreedySkip M) : let x
declarations.docstring: At a hypothetical final denominator-`21` skip, parity decides which adjacent Mersenne denominator has a quantitatively small common factor with the reduced residual denominator. Odd numerator gives a one-third predecessor bound; even numerator gives a one-half successor bound.

declarations.name: lastTwentyOneSkip_unsafe_numeratorProduct_gt
declarations.signature: theorem lastTwentyOneSkip_unsafe_numeratorProduct_gt {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastTwentyOneGreedySkip M) : 2 ^ M - 1 < (greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 21 : ℚ) (M - 1)).num.natAbs * (greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 21 : ℚ) (M + 1)).num.natAbs
declarations.docstring: A hypothetical final denominator-`21` skip is automatically a dyadically unsafe skip. The existing primitive-normalization theorem then forces an exponential product across the reduced numerators immediately before and after its forced successor take.

declarations.name: lastTwentyOneSkip_even_double_numeratorProduct_gt
declarations.signature: theorem lastTwentyOneSkip_even_double_numeratorProduct_gt {M : ℕ} (hlast : IsLastTwentyOneGreedySkip M) (heven : Even (greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 21 : ℚ) (M - 1)).num.natAbs) : 2 * (2 ^ M - 1) < (greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 21 : ℚ) (M - 1)).num.natAbs * (greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 21 : ℚ) (M + 1)).num.natAbs
declarations.docstring: If the reduced numerator before a hypothetical final skip is even, the parity-sensitive successor-gcd bound removes at least twice as much possible cancellation from the forced next take. The basic numerator product obstruction therefore gains a full factor of two.

declarations.name: exists_lastTwentyOneGreedySkip_of_not_mem
declarations.signature: theorem exists_lastTwentyOneGreedySkip_of_not_mem (hnot : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∉ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∃ M : ℕ, IsLastTwentyOneGreedySkip M
declarations.docstring: Nonmembership supplies a final actual skip, not merely an arbitrary finite fatal witness.

declarations.name: twentyOne_not_mem_forces_erdosBorwein_fatalInterval
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_not_mem_forces_erdosBorwein_fatalInterval (hnot : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∉ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∃ M : ℕ, IsLastTwentyOneGreedySkip M ∧ 0 < (1 / 21 : ℝ) + positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑(twentyOneSkippedPrefix M) : Set ℕ) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant ∧ (1 / 21 : ℝ) + positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑(twentyOneSkippedPrefix M) : Set ℕ) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant < mersenneGap M
declarations.docstring: **Erdős--Borwein fatal-interval reduction.** If the prescribed rational point is not represented, one finite exact Mersenne shift approximates the full Erdős--Borwein constant from above inside the sharp gap at its greatest exponent.

declarations.name: twentyOne_not_mem_forces_rational_erdosBorwein_fatalInterval
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_not_mem_forces_rational_erdosBorwein_fatalInterval (hnot : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∉ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∃ M : ℕ, IsLastTwentyOneGreedySkip M ∧ 0 < (1 / 21 : ℝ) + ((finiteErdosSum (twentyOneSkippedPrefix M) 2 : ℚ) : ℝ) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant ∧ (1 / 21 : ℝ) + ((finiteErdosSum (twentyOneSkippedPrefix M) 2 : ℚ) : ℝ) - erdosBorweinMersenneConstant < mersenneGap M
declarations.docstring: Exact rational form of the fatal interval. This is the form used by any height-aware irrationality-measure or primitive-denominator argument: the approximant is literally `1/21` plus a finite Mersenne sum, and its greatest denominator exponent is the final actual skip.

declarations.name: twentyOneEventualLeftCorrectionBoundaryAmplification_of_not_mem
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneEventualLeftCorrectionBoundaryAmplification_of_not_mem (hnot : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∉ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∃ K₀ : ℕ, ∀ K v q : ℕ, K₀ ≤ K → 3 ≤ K → Odd q → supportDyadicPrefixNumerator (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)) (2 * K) = 2 ^ v * q → K < 2 * K - v - 1
declarations.docstring: Non-membership eliminates the sole exceptional word in the actual left-boundary correction theorem. Past the fatal rank, both `K+1` and `K+2` are selected; the exceptional word would select the former and skip the latter. Hence every sufficiently late left boundary has forcing depth strictly larger than `K`. This removes one of the two orientation-specific correction obstructions: only the right-boundary long-selected-run case can survive.

declarations.name: twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_supportDyadicPrefix_factorization
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_supportDyadicPrefix_factorization (hbranch : TwentyOneFatalAlignedBranch) : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ t : ℕ, supportDyadicPrefixNumerator (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)) (n + t) + 1 = 2 ^ t * (supportDyadicPrefixNumerator (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)) n + 1)
declarations.docstring: The surviving right-boundary behavior has an exact, fixed ancestor. Once the fatal branch starts selecting every exponent, adding one more membership bit sends `P + 1` to `2 * (P + 1)`. Thus the entire later dyadic numerator is obtained by shifting the single numerator at the fatal rank. This is a negative result for the correction route: the right-boundary long-selected-run alternative does not hide fresh depth growth. Its power-of-two factor grows only by appending the already-forced terminal ones, so any contradiction must come from a different coordinate such as the denominator-`21` defect.

declarations.name: twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_rightBoundary_power_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_rightBoundary_power_dvd (hbranch : TwentyOneFatalAlignedBranch) : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ K : ℕ, n ≤ 2 * K → 2 ^ (2 * K - n) ∣ supportDyadicPrefixNumerator (greedyMersenneSupport (1 / 21 : ℝ)) (2 * K) + 1
declarations.docstring: In particular, every sufficiently late right boundary carries all of the power of two forced by the cofinite selected suffix.

declarations.name: TwentyOneEvenFullQuotientCoreBound
declarations.docstring: The full-row condition: only the coarse strict-core ceiling remains. The former exact-state exclusion has disappeared.

declarations.name: twentyOneEvenFullQuotientGreedyRemainder_le_three_of_coarseBound
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneEvenFullQuotientGreedyRemainder_le_three_of_coarseBound (hpre : TwentyOneEvenQuotientPreterminalCoarseBound) : ∀ R : ℕ, 2 ≤ R → twentyOneEvenFullQuotientGreedyRemainder R ≤ 3
declarations.docstring: The two finite rows below the preterminal range are exact, so the coarse condition gives a uniform defect-three full row at every required depth.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_fullGreedyRemainder_le_three
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_fullGreedyRemainder_le_three (hfull : ∀ R : ℕ, 2 ≤ R → twentyOneEvenFullQuotientGreedyRemainder R ≤ 3) : (1 / 21 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: **Bounded full-row endpoint.** A uniform defect bound of three already puts `1/21` in the achievement set. The constant is deliberately the one needed by the terminal-fringe absorption below; after normalization by `4^R`, it is as harmless as defect one.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_fullQuotientCoreBound
declarations.docstring: **Full-row quotient endpoint.** A coarse factor-two core ceiling is enough to put `1/21` in the achievement set. The complete binary suffix absorbs the old exceptional state with defect at most one, and the finite full rows converge without any coherence assumption.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_preterminalCoarseBound
declarations.docstring: **Six-state-free quotient endpoint.** The preterminal twice-last-coin ceiling alone proves membership. No equality exclusion survives: the full binary suffix absorbs every constant-width fringe state with defect at most three.

declarations.name: twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_mem_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_mem_bounds {R d : ℕ} (hd : d ∈ twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) : 2 ≤ d ∧ d ≤ R
declarations.docstring: Every decoded greedy rank lies in the prescribed lower window.

declarations.name: localPrefixQuotient_twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_add_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem localPrefixQuotient_twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_add_remainder {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) : localPrefixQuotient (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) (2 * R) + twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder R = twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * R)
declarations.docstring: The decoded quotient and the deterministic remainder exactly partition the denominator-`21` target.

declarations.name: twentyOneSuccessorQuotientPrefixSupport_eq_greedyMersennePrefixRat
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneSuccessorQuotientPrefixSupport_eq_greedyMersennePrefixRat {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) (halignSucc : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * (R + 1)) (2 * (R + 1))) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * (R + 1))) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * (R + 1) - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) : lowerSupportFromBits 2 (integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * (R + 1)) R) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * (R + 1)))) = greedyMersennePrefixRat (1 / 21 : ℚ) R
declarations.docstring: Full alignment at horizon `R+1` already fixes the quotient-greedy word through rank `R` to the exact rational prefix. This is the prefix identity needed before exposing the final boundary decision.

declarations.name: twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_eq_greedyMersennePrefixRat_of_fullAlignment
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_eq_greedyMersennePrefixRat_of_fullAlignment {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) (halign : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * R) (2 * R)) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * R)) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * R - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) : twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R = greedyMersennePrefixRat (1 / 21 : ℚ) R
declarations.docstring: Once a full quotient row aligns with exact rational greedy, its lower support is not merely pointwise compatible: it is the exact greedy prefix through rank `R`.

declarations.name: localMersennePrefixValue_twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_le_of_fullAlignment
declarations.signature: theorem localMersennePrefixValue_twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_le_of_fullAlignment {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) (halign : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * R) (2 * R)) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * R)) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * R - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) : localMersennePrefixValue (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) ≤ (1 / 21 : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: Aligned quotient supports inherit the exact rational greedy undershoot. The proof uses the nonnegative residual in the exact rational telescoping identity, so it does not assume membership of the infinite target.

declarations.name: localPrefixTwoStepPulse_twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_le_carry_of_fullAlignment
declarations.signature: theorem localPrefixTwoStepPulse_twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_le_carry_of_fullAlignment {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) (halign : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * R) (2 * R)) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * R)) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * R - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) : localPrefixTwoStepPulse (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) (2 * R) ≤ 4 * twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder R + twentyOneTargetTwoStepPulse (2 * R)
declarations.docstring: Full alignment therefore supplies the exact nonnegative carry inequality for the canonical lower state.

declarations.name: twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_eventually_canonical_carry_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_eventually_canonical_carry_nonneg (hbranch : TwentyOneFatalAlignedBranch) : ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ R : ℕ, K ≤ R → localPrefixTwoStepPulse (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) (2 * R) ≤ 4 * twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder R + twentyOneTargetTwoStepPulse (2 * R)
declarations.docstring: The fatal aligned branch has no eventual carry-sign obstruction. Beyond one cutoff, the canonical lower quotient state always supplies a genuine natural carry; only its upper closed-capacity bound can still fail.

declarations.name: twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_succ_eq_boundary_of_fullAlignment
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_succ_eq_boundary_of_fullAlignment {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) (halign : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * R) (2 * R)) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * R)) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * R - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) (halignSucc : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * (R + 1)) (2 * (R + 1))) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * (R + 1))) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * (R + 1) - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) :
declarations.docstring: Consecutive full quotient/rational alignment turns the canonical lower support into the exact one-bit boundary recurrence. In particular, the apparently horizon-dependent quotient-greedy rows are a genuine one-dimensional state machine on the surviving branch.

declarations.name: twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder_succ_eq_boundary_of_fullAlignment
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder_succ_eq_boundary_of_fullAlignment {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) (halign : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * R) (2 * R)) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * R)) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * R - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) (halignSucc : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * (R + 1)) (2 * (R + 1))) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * (R + 1))) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * (R + 1) - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) :
declarations.docstring: Consecutive full alignment also identifies the canonical scalar remainder with the one-dimensional boundary update. Together with the preceding support theorem, this removes all horizon dependence from the surviving denominator-`21` dynamics.

declarations.name: twentyOneAlignedSaturatedCrossing_forces_canonical_ancestor_hole
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneAlignedSaturatedCrossing_forces_canonical_ancestor_hole {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) (halign : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * R) (2 * R)) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * R)) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * R - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) (halignSucc : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * (R + 1)) (2 * (R + 1))) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * (R + 1))) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2
declarations.docstring: Consecutive exact alignment binds the abstract saturated-escape classifier to the canonical denominator-`21` row. Hence any aligned first crossing above capacity has a concrete missing greedy ancestor at one-third or two-thirds scale.

declarations.name: twentyOneAlignedSaturatedCrossing_forces_scaled_greedy_skip
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneAlignedSaturatedCrossing_forces_scaled_greedy_skip {R : ℕ} (hR : 5 ≤ R) (halign : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * R) (2 * R)) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * R)) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2 (2 * R - 1) (1 / 21 : ℚ)) (halignSucc : integerGreedyBits (localMersenneWeights (2 * (R + 1)) (2 * (R + 1))) (twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * (R + 1))) = rationalMersenneGreedyBitsFrom 2
declarations.docstring: An aligned supercapacity entrance produces a genuine omitted exponent in the real denominator-`21` greedy orbit, not merely a hole in the auxiliary quotient word. Moreover that exponent is at the same scale as the entrance: `d ≤ R ≤ 3d`. The universal skip estimate therefore makes the Boolean--Möbius defect at that ancestor only square-root sized. This is the quantitative descent bridge between the quotient escape and the Lambert carry orbit.

declarations.name: twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_eventually_canonical_transition
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_eventually_canonical_transition (hbranch : TwentyOneFatalAlignedBranch) : ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ R : ℕ, K ≤ R → twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport (R + 1) = twentyOneBoundaryLowerSupport (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) R (4 * twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder R + twentyOneTargetTwoStepPulse (2 * R) - localPrefixTwoStepPulse (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) (2 * R)) ∧ twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder (R + 1) = twentyOneBoundaryScalarState R (4 * twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder R + twentyOneTargetTwoStepPulse (2 * R) -
declarations.docstring: On the fatal branch the horizon-indexed canonical rows eventually become one exact non-autonomous state machine: the support appends precisely its boundary decision and the scalar follows the matching boundary remainder. The only remaining way this branch can survive is therefore an eventual escape above the closed binary capacity, not loss of alignment or carry sign.

declarations.name: localPrefixQuotient_twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_le
declarations.signature: theorem localPrefixQuotient_twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport_le {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) : localPrefixQuotient (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) (2 * R) ≤ twentyOneQuotientTarget (2 * R)
declarations.docstring: The quotient row is admissible simply because greedy never overspends.

declarations.name: twentyOneQuotientDefect_greedySupport
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneQuotientDefect_greedySupport {R : ℕ} (hR : 2 ≤ R) : twentyOneQuotientDefect (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) (2 * R) = twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder R
declarations.docstring: The abstract quotient defect is exactly the concrete greedy remainder.

declarations.name: TwentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyWindow
declarations.docstring: The sole arithmetic condition remaining after canonicalization.

declarations.name: TwentyOneEvenQuotientCoreControl
declarations.docstring: Equivalent strict-core arithmetic package: a coarse two-window bound and avoidance of one exact integer state.

declarations.name: TwentyOneEvenQuotientClosedCoreControl
declarations.docstring: The genuinely sufficient closed-core condition. Compared with strict core control, it has no exceptional equality and admits the two additional top states exposed by the exact classifier above.

declarations.name: twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyWindow_of_coreControl
declarations.docstring: Strict-core control is exactly what the canonical greedy window needs.

declarations.name: twentyOneEvenQuotientWindowSupply_of_greedyWindow
declarations.docstring: The canonical greedy window supplies every finite row required by the compactness theorem.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_greedyWindow
declarations.docstring: **One-scalar-state endpoint.** The terminal quotient-greedy remainder bound at every even depth proves that `1/21` is a Boolean Mersenne subseries sum.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_closedCoreControl
declarations.docstring: **Closed-core endpoint.** The prescribed point follows from the single weak preterminal inequality; neither strictness nor avoidance of an exact integer state remains.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_coreControl
declarations.docstring: Final endpoint phrased solely through strict-core arithmetic.

declarations.name: TwentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientGreedyWindow
declarations.docstring: Closedness only needs good quotient rows along one unbounded sequence; the all-depth window is stronger than the endpoint requires.

declarations.name: TwentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientGreedyDecay
declarations.docstring: Minimal asymptotic form of the quotient route. No fixed cap is built into the statement: the normalized deterministic defect (with only a linear support-cardinality allowance) must tend to zero along one unbounded sequence of rows.

declarations.name: TwentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientCoreControl
declarations.docstring: The same cofinal condition in the exact strict-core form.

declarations.name: twentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientGreedyWindow_of_coreControl
declarations.docstring: Cofinal strict-core control gives cofinal good greedy rows.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_cofinalGreedyDecay
declarations.docstring: **Minimal cofinal quotient endpoint.** Normalized deterministic defect decay on one unbounded sequence puts `1/21` in the achievement set.

declarations.name: twentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientGreedyDecay_of_window
declarations.docstring: The square-root window implies the cap-free normalized decay condition.

declarations.name: twentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientGreedyDecay_of_closedRows
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientGreedyDecay_of_closedRows {R : ℕ → ℕ} (hR : Tendsto R atTop atTop) (hrow : ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ R k ∧ twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder (R k) ≤ 2 ^ (R k)) : TwentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientGreedyDecay
declarations.docstring: Closed canonical rows along any unbounded sequence already give the cap-free decay required by compactness. Strictness is irrelevant at this stage: the quotient normalization is quadratic in the binary scale.

declarations.name: twentyOneCofinalEvenQuotientGreedyDecay_of_preterminalNextCoin
declarations.docstring: The canonical next-coin inequality implies the cap-free decay condition. The half-row remainder may be twice the old binary window; that still decays geometrically after the quotient normalization by `4^R`.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_cofinalGreedyWindow
declarations.docstring: **Cofinal quotient endpoint.** Arbitrarily deep square-root-window rows already put `1/21` in the achievement set; omitted depths are irrelevant.

declarations.name: twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_eventually_strict_supercapacity
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_eventually_strict_supercapacity (hbranch : TwentyOneFatalAlignedBranch) : ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ R : ℕ, K ≤ R → 2 ^ R < twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder R
declarations.docstring: **Exact permanent-escape form of the fatal branch.** If the prescribed point is not represented, the canonical quotient remainder is eventually strictly above its closed binary capacity at every depth. Any unbounded sequence of closed returns would already converge to `1/21` by compactness. Combined with `twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_eventually_canonical_transition`, this leaves one explicit dynamical regime: an exact aligned recurrence which eventually stays in `2^R < s_R`.

declarations.name: twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_eventually_affine_supercapacity
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOneFatalAlignedBranch_eventually_affine_supercapacity (hbranch : TwentyOneFatalAlignedBranch) : ∃ K : ℕ, ∀ R : ℕ, K ≤ R → twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport (R + 1) = insert (R + 1) (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) ∧ twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder (R + 1) = (4 * twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedyRemainder R + twentyOneTargetTwoStepPulse (2 * R) - localPrefixTwoStepPulse (twentyOneEvenQuotientGreedySupport R) (2 * R)) - (2 ^ (R + 1) + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Affine normal form of the only remaining fatal regime.** Once the canonical remainder has escaped strictly above `2^R`, its exponential margin dominates the entire linear divisor pulse. Consequently the new boundary coin always fits: the support appends `R+1`, and the scalar follows one literal affine recurrence with no residual Boolean branch.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_cofinalCoreControl
declarations.docstring: Cofinal strict-core control is therefore sufficient for the prescribed rational point.

declarations.name: one_div_twenty_one_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_preterminalNextCoin
declarations.docstring: **Canonical next-coin endpoint.** It is enough to prove the ordinary greedy invariant that every preterminal state lies below the next quotient coin. No fixed fringe width, exact equality exclusion, or full-row defect cap remains in the hypothesis.

declarations.name: mod_sub_of_le_mod
declarations.signature: theorem mod_sub_of_le_mod {A X P : ℕ} (hP : 0 < P) (h : X ≤ A % P) : (A - X) % P = A % P - X
declarations.docstring: Subtracting a quantity that already fits inside the low `P` block leaves the high blocks alone.

declarations.name: testBit_sub_of_le_mod
declarations.signature: theorem testBit_sub_of_le_mod {x a p j : ℕ} (ha : a ≤ x % 2 ^ p) (hj : p ≤ j) : Nat.testBit (x - a) j = Nat.testBit x j
declarations.docstring: Subtracting a quantity that already fits inside the low `p` bits leaves every bit at index `≥ p` untouched: no borrow escapes the low block.

declarations.name: lateCorrection
declarations.signature: def lateCorrection (s : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ | d => if h : d < s then 4 ^ (s - d) + lateCorrection s (d + 1) else 0 termination_by d => s - d decreasing_by omega theorem lateCorrection_eq_zero {s d : ℕ} (h : s ≤ d) : lateCorrection s d = 0
declarations.docstring: Total `4 ^ k` correction carried by the late weights `d, d+1, …, s-1`, i.e. `∑_{k=1}^{s-d} 4 ^ k`.

declarations.name: lateCorrection_eq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem lateCorrection_eq_zero {s d : ℕ} (h : s ≤ d) : lateCorrection s d = 0

declarations.name: lateCorrection_eq_cons
declarations.signature: theorem lateCorrection_eq_cons {s d : ℕ} (h : d < s) : lateCorrection s d = 4 ^ (s - d) + lateCorrection s (d + 1)

declarations.name: lateCorrection_succ_le
declarations.signature: theorem lateCorrection_succ_le (s d : ℕ) : lateCorrection s (d + 1) ≤ lateCorrection s d

declarations.name: three_mul_lateCorrection_add_four
declarations.signature: theorem three_mul_lateCorrection_add_four {s d : ℕ} (h : d ≤ s) : 3 * lateCorrection s d + 4 = 4 * 4 ^ (s - d)
declarations.docstring: Exact closed form `3 * ∑_{k=1}^{s-d} 4 ^ k + 4 = 4 ^ (s-d+1)`.

declarations.name: lateCorrection_lt_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem lateCorrection_lt_two_pow {s d : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) : lateCorrection s d < 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The corrections cannot reach the compared bits.** In the late zone the whole `4 ^ k` budget stays strictly below `2 ^ (s+1)`, while every compared bit sits at index `≥ s + 1`.

declarations.name: lateBitWord
declarations.signature: def lateBitWord (s C : ℕ) : ℕ → List Bool | d => if h : d < s then Nat.testBit C (2 * s - d) :: lateBitWord s C (d + 1) else [] termination_by d => s - d decreasing_by omega theorem lateBitWord_eq_nil {s C d : ℕ} (h : s ≤ d) : lateBitWord s C d = []
declarations.docstring: The word obtained by reading the bits of `C` at the positions `2 * s - d`, for `d` running over `d, d+1, …, s-1`.

declarations.name: lateBitWord_eq_nil
declarations.signature: theorem lateBitWord_eq_nil {s C d : ℕ} (h : s ≤ d) : lateBitWord s C d = []

declarations.name: lateBitWord_eq_cons
declarations.signature: theorem lateBitWord_eq_cons {s C d : ℕ} (h : d < s) : lateBitWord s C d = Nat.testBit C (2 * s - d) :: lateBitWord s C (d + 1)

declarations.name: lateBitWord_congr
declarations.signature: theorem lateBitWord_congr {s C C' : ℕ} (d : ℕ) (hbits : ∀ e : ℕ, d ≤ e → e < s → Nat.testBit C' (2 * s - e) = Nat.testBit C (2 * s - e)) : lateBitWord s C' d = lateBitWord s C d

declarations.name: lateBitWord_length
declarations.signature: theorem lateBitWord_length (s C d : ℕ) : (lateBitWord s C d).length = s - d

declarations.name: lateBitWord_getElem?
declarations.signature: theorem lateBitWord_getElem? {s C d e : ℕ} (hde : d ≤ e) (hes : e < s) : (lateBitWord s C d)[e - d]? = some (Nat.testBit C (2 * s - e))

declarations.name: integerGreedyBits_seamWeightsFrom_eq_lateBitWord
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyBits_seamWeightsFrom_eq_lateBitWord {s d C : ℕ} (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hhigh : C < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)) (hlow : lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)) : integerGreedyBits (seamWeightsFrom s d) C = lateBitWord s C d
declarations.docstring: **The late-zone greedy word is the binary expansion of the entering capacity.** In the late zone `2 * s < 3 * d` the descending integer greedy run over the actual truncated Mersenne weights `seamWeightsFrom s d`, started at capacity `C`, takes rank `e` exactly when bit `2 * s - e` of `C` is set — for every `e` in `[d, s)` at once, and reading the bits of the *entering* capacity `C`, not of any running remainder. The two hypotheses are: `C` does not overflow past bit `2 * s - d` (there are no larger weights left in the list to absorb it), and the low `s + 1` bits of `C` can pay for the entire `4 ^ k` correction budget, which is exactly what rules out a borrow into the compared bits.

declarations.name: getElem?_eq_testBit
declarations.signature: theorem getElem?_eq_testBit {s d C e : ℕ} (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hhigh : C < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)) (hlow : lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)) (hde : d ≤ e) (hes : e < s) : (integerGreedyBits (seamWeightsFrom s d) C)[e - d]? = some (Nat.testBit C (2 * s - e))
declarations.docstring: Position `e - d` of the late greedy word is bit `2 * s - e` of `C`.

declarations.name: takes_iff_testBit
declarations.signature: theorem takes_iff_testBit {s d C e : ℕ} (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hhigh : C < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)) (hlow : lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)) (hde : d ≤ e) (hes : e < s) : (integerGreedyBits (seamWeightsFrom s d) C)[e - d]? = some true ↔ Nat.testBit C (2 * s - e) = true
declarations.docstring: **Take/skip at a single late rank.** The greedy takes rank `e` iff bit `2 * s - e` of the entering capacity is one.

declarations.name: all_true_iff_forall_testBit
declarations.signature: theorem all_true_iff_forall_testBit {s d C : ℕ} (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hhigh : C < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)) (hlow : lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)) : (∀ e : ℕ, d ≤ e → e < s → (integerGreedyBits (seamWeightsFrom s d) C)[e - d]? = some true) ↔ (∀ e : ℕ, d ≤ e → e < s → Nat.testBit C (2 * s - e) = true)
declarations.docstring: **The forced run.** The greedy takes every late rank iff every bit of `C` in the window `(s, 2 * s - d]` is one. Contrapositively: a single zero bit in that window is a skipped late rank.

declarations.name: integerGreedyBits_append
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyBits_append (l₁ l₂ : List ℕ) (C : ℕ) : integerGreedyBits (l₁ ++ l₂) C = integerGreedyBits l₁ C ++ integerGreedyBits l₂ (C - weightedBoolSum l₁ (integerGreedyBits l₁ C))
declarations.docstring: Descending greedy over a concatenation runs the prefix first and then feeds its remainder to the suffix.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_drop
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_drop (s : ℕ) : ∀ (k d : ℕ), (seamWeightsFrom s d).drop k = seamWeightsFrom s (d + k)

declarations.name: seamWeights_eq_take_append
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeights_eq_take_append {s d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) : seamWeights s = (seamWeights s).take (d - 2) ++ seamWeightsFrom s d

declarations.name: earlyWeights
declarations.signature: def earlyWeights (s d : ℕ) : List ℕ
declarations.docstring: The seam weights strictly before the late zone.

declarations.name: earlyWeights_length
declarations.signature: theorem earlyWeights_length {s d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d ≤ s) : (earlyWeights s d).length = d - 2

declarations.name: lateEntryRemainder
declarations.docstring: **The remainder entering the late zone**: what the actual seam greedy run has left after processing ranks `2, …, d-1`.

declarations.name: seamGreedyBits_split
declarations.signature: theorem seamGreedyBits_split {s d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) : integerGreedyBits (seamWeights s) (seamSubsetTarget s) = integerGreedyBits (earlyWeights s d) (seamSubsetTarget s) ++ integerGreedyBits (seamWeightsFrom s d) (lateEntryRemainder s d)

declarations.name: mem_seamGreedySupport_iff_getElem
declarations.signature: theorem mem_seamGreedySupport_iff_getElem {s e : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ e) (hes : e < s) : e ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s) ↔ (integerGreedyBits (seamWeights s) (seamSubsetTarget s))[e - 2]? = some true

declarations.name: mem_seamGreedySupport_iff_testBit
declarations.signature: theorem mem_seamGreedySupport_iff_testBit {s d e : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d ≤ s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hhigh : lateEntryRemainder s d < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)) (hlow : lateCorrection s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1)) (hde : d ≤ e) (hes : e < s) : e ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s) ↔ Nat.testBit (lateEntryRemainder s d) (2 * s - e) = true
declarations.docstring: **Bit criterion for the corpus's own seam greedy word.** Once the entering remainder `lateEntryRemainder s d` satisfies the two side conditions, membership of a late rank `e` in `seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s)` is *exactly* bit `2 * s - e` of that remainder.

declarations.name: fourteen_is_first_late
declarations.docstring: `14` really is the first late rank at `s = 20`.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_twenty_fourteen
declarations.docstring: The six late weights at `s = 20`: ranks `14, …, 19`, computed from the corpus definition `truncatedMersenneWeight s d = 4 ^ s / (2 ^ d - 1)`.

declarations.name: hypotheses_hold
declarations.docstring: **The hypotheses of the main theorem are satisfiable.** This is the anti-vacuity certificate.

declarations.name: greedy_word
declarations.signature: theorem greedy_word : integerGreedyBits (seamWeightsFrom 20 14) 87217799 = [true, false, true, false, false, true]
declarations.docstring: The greedy word, computed from the actual truncated Mersenne weights.

declarations.name: bit_word
declarations.signature: theorem bit_word : lateBitWord 20 87217799 14 = [true, false, true, false, false, true]
declarations.docstring: The bit word, computed from the binary expansion of the capacity.

declarations.name: correspondence
declarations.docstring: The main theorem, instantiated: hypotheses verified, and the conclusion verified independently on both sides.

declarations.name: seamWeights_twenty
declarations.docstring: The eighteen seam weights at `s = 20`, from the corpus definition.

declarations.name: lateEntryRemainder_twenty_fourteen
declarations.docstring: The genuine remainder entering the late zone at `s = 20`.

declarations.name: actual_hypotheses_hold
declarations.docstring: **The side conditions hold for the actual seam remainder.**

declarations.name: actual_late_word
declarations.signature: theorem actual_late_word : integerGreedyBits (seamWeightsFrom 20 14) (lateEntryRemainder 20 14) = [true, false, false, false, false, false]
declarations.docstring: The actual late greedy word at `s = 20`: rank `14` is taken, ranks `15, …, 19` are all skipped.

declarations.name: fifteen_not_mem_seamGreedySupport_twenty
declarations.docstring: **A genuine skipped late rank at `s = 20`**, read straight off a zero bit of the entering remainder. Since `2 * 20 < 3 * 15`, rank `15` is in the late zone; this is exactly the input of `SkipD3.largestSkipLateAt_of_late_skip`.

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_twenty
declarations.docstring: **The bit criterion delivers the corpus predicate.** Rank `19` is the largest false rank of row `20` and it is late, so `LargestSkipLateAt 20` — the property whose cofinality is equivalent to `1/2 ∈ mersenneAchievementSet` — holds, proved here purely from a zero bit of the entering remainder.

declarations.name: seamSubsetTarget_succ
declarations.signature: theorem seamSubsetTarget_succ {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) : seamSubsetTarget (s + 1) = 4 * seamSubsetTarget s + 2 ^ (s + 1)

declarations.name: four_pow_eq_truncatedMersenneWeight_mul_add
declarations.signature: theorem four_pow_eq_truncatedMersenneWeight_mul_add {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) : 4 ^ s = truncatedMersenneWeight s d * (2 ^ d - 1) + 2 ^ ((2 * s) % d)
declarations.docstring: Euclidean identity for the truncated Mersenne weight: the remainder of `4 ^ s` modulo `2 ^ d - 1` is exactly `2 ^ ((2 * s) % d)`.

declarations.name: rowCarry
declarations.docstring: The carry that the row step `s ↦ s + 1` adds on top of the exact quadrupling of the rank-`d` weight.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_succ_row
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_succ_row {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) : truncatedMersenneWeight (s + 1) d = 4 * truncatedMersenneWeight s d + rowCarry s d
declarations.docstring: **Exact weight recurrence.** Every truncated Mersenne weight quadruples from row `s` to row `s + 1`, up to an additive carry `rowCarry s d ≤ 2`.

declarations.name: rowCarry_le_two
declarations.signature: theorem rowCarry_le_two {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) : rowCarry s d ≤ 2

declarations.name: mod_eq_pred_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem mod_eq_pred_of_dvd {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (h : d ∣ 2 * s + 1) : (2 * s) % d = d - 1

declarations.name: mod_eq_sub_two_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem mod_eq_sub_two_of_dvd {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (h : d ∣ 2 * s + 2) : (2 * s) % d = d - 2

declarations.name: dvd_of_mod_eq_pred
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_of_mod_eq_pred {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (h : (2 * s) % d = d - 1) : d ∣ 2 * s + 1

declarations.name: dvd_of_mod_eq_sub_two
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_of_mod_eq_sub_two {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (h : (2 * s) % d = d - 2) : d ∣ 2 * s + 2

declarations.name: rowCarry_eq_two
declarations.signature: theorem rowCarry_eq_two {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (h : d ∣ 2 * s + 1) : rowCarry s d = 2
declarations.docstring: Carry `2` exactly on the ranks dividing `2 * s + 1`.

declarations.name: rowCarry_eq_one
declarations.signature: theorem rowCarry_eq_one {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (h : d ∣ 2 * s + 2) : rowCarry s d = 1
declarations.docstring: Carry `1` exactly on the ranks dividing `2 * s + 2` (and not `2 * s + 1`).

declarations.name: rowCarry_eq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem rowCarry_eq_zero {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (h1 : ¬ d ∣ 2 * s + 1) (h2 : ¬ d ∣ 2 * s + 2) : rowCarry s d = 0
declarations.docstring: Carry `0` off both divisor families.

declarations.name: weightedBoolSum_seamWeightsFrom_succ
declarations.signature: theorem weightedBoolSum_seamWeightsFrom_succ (s d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) (bs : List Bool) (hlen : bs.length = (seamWeightsFrom s d).length) : ∃ δ : ℕ, δ ≤ 2 * (seamWeightsFrom s d).length ∧ weightedBoolSum (seamWeightsFrom (s + 1) d) (bs ++ [false]) = 4 * weightedBoolSum (seamWeightsFrom s d) bs + δ
declarations.docstring: Selecting the row-`s` greedy support inside row `s + 1` (and declining the brand-new rank `s`) multiplies the achieved subset sum by exactly four, up to a carry budget of at most two per selected rank.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_length
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_length (s d : ℕ) : (seamWeightsFrom s d).length = s - d

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_succ_le
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_succ_le {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) ≤ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The remainder recurrence.** The concrete seam integer-greedy remainder of row `s + 1` is at most four times the row-`s` remainder plus the exact target increment `2 ^ (s + 1)`. Unconditional for every `s ≥ 3`.

declarations.name: liftWeights
declarations.signature: def liftWeights (ws cs : List ℕ) : List ℕ
declarations.docstring: Row `s + 1`'s weight word on the shared ranks, written as a lift of row `s`'s: each weight quadruples and picks up its carry.

declarations.name: integerGreedyBits_append
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyBits_append (ws : List ℕ) : ∀ (vs : List ℕ) (C : ℕ), integerGreedyBits (ws ++ vs) C = integerGreedyBits ws C ++ integerGreedyBits vs (C - weightedBoolSum ws (integerGreedyBits ws C))

declarations.name: integerGreedyBits_lift_split
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyBits_lift_split (ws : List ℕ) : ∀ (cs : List ℕ), cs.length = ws.length → ∀ (C E : ℕ), cs.sum ≤ E → integerGreedyBits ws C = integerGreedyBits (liftWeights ws cs) (4 * C + E) ∨ ∃ (p b₁ b₂ : List Bool), integerGreedyBits ws C = p ++ false :: b₁ ∧ integerGreedyBits (liftWeights ws cs) (4 * C + E) = p ++ true :: b₂
declarations.docstring: **Parallel-run dichotomy.** If the successor capacity dominates by at least the total carry budget, then either the two descending greedy words agree outright, or the first place they differ is a rank that the base run *skips* and the lifted run *takes*. A take can never become a skip.

declarations.name: rowCarriesFrom
declarations.signature: def rowCarriesFrom (s : ℕ) : ℕ → List ℕ | d => if h : d < s then rowCarry s d :: rowCarriesFrom s (d + 1) else [] termination_by d => s - d decreasing_by omega theorem rowCarriesFrom_eq_cons {s d : ℕ} (h : d < s) : rowCarriesFrom s d = rowCarry s d :: rowCarriesFrom s (d + 1)
declarations.docstring: The carries at ranks `d, d+1, …, s-1`, aligned with `seamWeightsFrom s d`.

declarations.name: rowCarriesFrom_eq_cons
declarations.signature: theorem rowCarriesFrom_eq_cons {s d : ℕ} (h : d < s) : rowCarriesFrom s d = rowCarry s d :: rowCarriesFrom s (d + 1)

declarations.name: rowCarriesFrom_eq_nil
declarations.signature: theorem rowCarriesFrom_eq_nil {s d : ℕ} (h : s ≤ d) : rowCarriesFrom s d = []

declarations.name: rowCarriesFrom_length
declarations.signature: theorem rowCarriesFrom_length (s d : ℕ) : (rowCarriesFrom s d).length = s - d

declarations.name: rowCarriesFrom_sum_le
declarations.signature: theorem rowCarriesFrom_sum_le (s d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) : (rowCarriesFrom s d).sum ≤ 2 * (s - d)

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_succ_row
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_succ_row {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d ≤ s) : seamWeightsFrom (s + 1) d = liftWeights (seamWeightsFrom s d) (rowCarriesFrom s d) ++ [truncatedMersenneWeight (s + 1) s]
declarations.docstring: **Row-word recurrence.** The row-`s+1` weight word is exactly the lift of the row-`s` weight word, with the one brand-new rank `s` appended.

declarations.name: seamGreedy_succ_first_difference
declarations.signature: theorem seamGreedy_succ_first_difference {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) : integerGreedyBits (seamWeights s) (seamSubsetTarget s) <+: integerGreedyBits (seamWeights (s + 1)) (seamSubsetTarget (s + 1)) ∨ ∃ (p b₁ b₂ : List Bool), integerGreedyBits (seamWeights s) (seamSubsetTarget s) = p ++ false :: b₁ ∧ (p ++ true :: b₂) <+: integerGreedyBits (seamWeights (s + 1)) (seamSubsetTarget (s + 1))
declarations.docstring: **First-disagreement law for consecutive rows.** Either the row-`s` greedy take/skip word is a prefix of the row-`s+1` word (the two rows agree on every shared rank), or the first rank where they differ is one that row `s` *skips* and row `s+1` *takes*. No rank taken at row `s` on the common prefix can be dropped at row `s+1`.

declarations.name: seamGreedyBits_13
declarations.signature: theorem seamGreedyBits_13 : integerGreedyBits (seamWeights 13) (seamSubsetTarget 13) = [true, true, false, false, true] ++ false :: [true, true, true, true, true]

declarations.name: seamGreedyBits_14
declarations.signature: theorem seamGreedyBits_14 : integerGreedyBits (seamWeights 14) (seamSubsetTarget 14) = [true, true, false, false, true] ++ true :: [false, false, false, false, false, false]

declarations.name: seamGreedyBits_15
declarations.signature: theorem seamGreedyBits_15 : integerGreedyBits (seamWeights 15) (seamSubsetTarget 15) = [true, true, false, false, true, true, false, false, false, false, false, false, false]

declarations.name: first_difference_right_branch_thirteen
declarations.signature: theorem first_difference_right_branch_thirteen : ∃ (p b₁ b₂ : List Bool), integerGreedyBits (seamWeights 13) (seamSubsetTarget 13) = p ++ false :: b₁ ∧ (p ++ true :: b₂) <+: integerGreedyBits (seamWeights 14) (seamSubsetTarget 14)
declarations.docstring: The *right* branch of `seamGreedy_succ_first_difference` is realised at `s = 13`: rank `7` is skipped at row `13` and taken at row `14`.

declarations.name: first_difference_left_branch_fourteen
declarations.docstring: The *left* branch is realised at `s = 14`: rows `14` and `15` agree on every shared rank.

declarations.name: remainder_recurrence_witness_fourteen
declarations.docstring: The remainder recurrence instantiated, and nearly sharp: the true value is `34333`, the bound is `4 * 392 + 2 ^ 15 = 34336`, a defect of exactly `3`, which is the total carry `rowCarry 14 d` over the four selected ranks `d = 2, 3, 6, 7`.

declarations.name: lateFloor
declarations.docstring: The first rank of the late zone `(2s/3, s)`.

declarations.name: runNeeded
declarations.docstring: `K s`: the number of ranks in the late zone — the length of the run of consecutive takes at the top of row `s` that `¬ LargestSkipLateAt s` forces.

declarations.name: late_iff_lateFloor_le
declarations.signature: theorem late_iff_lateFloor_le {s d : ℕ} : 2 * s < 3 * d ↔ lateFloor s ≤ d
declarations.docstring: Lateness is exactly `lateFloor s ≤ d`.

declarations.name: runNeeded_lower_bound
declarations.signature: theorem runNeeded_lower_bound (s : ℕ) : s ≤ 3 * runNeeded s + 3
declarations.docstring: `K` really is of order `s / 3`.

declarations.name: topTaken
declarations.docstring: `topTaken s r` : the top `r` ranks `s-1, s-2, …, s-r` are all selected by the concrete integer seam greedy of row `s`.

declarations.name: mem_of_topTaken
declarations.signature: theorem mem_of_topTaken {s r k : ℕ} (h : topTaken s r = true) (hk : k < r) (hks : k + 3 ≤ s) : (s - 1 - k) ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s)
declarations.docstring: Reading a `true` out of a top run.

declarations.name: topTaken_eq_false_of_notMem
declarations.signature: theorem topTaken_eq_false_of_notMem {s r d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hr : s ≤ d + r) (hnot : d ∉ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s)) : topTaken s r = false
declarations.docstring: A skipped rank inside the top `r` breaks the run.

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_iff_topTaken_false
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_iff_topTaken_false {s : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) : LargestSkipLateAt s ↔ topTaken s (runNeeded s) = false
declarations.docstring: **The late largest skip is exactly a deficient top run.** Row `s` has a late largest false rank iff the greedy's run of takes at the top of the row is *shorter* than the whole late zone.

declarations.name: half_mem_iff_topRun_deficient
declarations.signature: theorem half_mem_iff_topRun_deficient : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet ↔ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ s : ℕ, N ≤ s ∧ topTaken s (runNeeded s) = false
declarations.docstring: **Erdos `#257`, as a statement about one run length per row.** `1/2` is achieved iff the greedy's top take-run falls short of the full late zone at cofinally many rows.

declarations.name: d0Table
declarations.docstring: The measured largest false rank `d₀(501 + k)`, `k < 700`. Every entry is certified below by `SkipD3.rowChk`.

declarations.name: d0At
declarations.docstring: Lookup into `d0Table`.

declarations.name: rowOk
declarations.docstring: The row certificate: the tabulated rank is a genuine rank of the row, sits within `13` of the row index (so the top take-run is at most `12`), is late, and really is the largest false rank of the concrete greedy word.

declarations.name: rowOk_of_chunk
declarations.signature: theorem rowOk_of_chunk {b : ℕ} (hb : (List.range 100).all (fun k => rowOk (b + k)) = true) {s : ℕ} (h1 : b ≤ s) (h2 : s < b + 100) : rowOk s = true
declarations.docstring: Reading a single row out of a hundred-row kernel check.

declarations.name: chunk0
declarations.signature: theorem chunk0 : (List.range 100).all (fun k => rowOk (501 + k)) = true

declarations.name: chunk1
declarations.signature: theorem chunk1 : (List.range 100).all (fun k => rowOk (601 + k)) = true

declarations.name: chunk2
declarations.signature: theorem chunk2 : (List.range 100).all (fun k => rowOk (701 + k)) = true

declarations.name: chunk3
declarations.signature: theorem chunk3 : (List.range 100).all (fun k => rowOk (801 + k)) = true

declarations.name: chunk4
declarations.signature: theorem chunk4 : (List.range 100).all (fun k => rowOk (901 + k)) = true

declarations.name: chunk5
declarations.signature: theorem chunk5 : (List.range 100).all (fun k => rowOk (1001 + k)) = true

declarations.name: chunk6
declarations.signature: theorem chunk6 : (List.range 100).all (fun k => rowOk (1101 + k)) = true

declarations.name: rowOk_of_block
declarations.signature: theorem rowOk_of_block {s : ℕ} (h1 : 501 ≤ s) (h2 : s ≤ 1200) : rowOk s = true
declarations.docstring: **The kernel check.** All `700` rows `501, …, 1200` pass.

declarations.name: exists_largestFalseRank_of_rowOk
declarations.signature: theorem exists_largestFalseRank_of_rowOk {s : ℕ} (h : rowOk s = true) : ∃ d : ℕ, IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d ∧ s ≤ d + 13 ∧ 2 * s < 3 * d

declarations.name: topRun_le_twelve_block
declarations.signature: theorem topRun_le_twelve_block {s : ℕ} (h1 : 501 ≤ s) (h2 : s ≤ 1200) : ∃ d : ℕ, IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d ∧ s - 1 - d ≤ 12 ∧ 2 * s < 3 * d
declarations.docstring: **The measured top run.** On every row of the block the greedy's run of takes at the top has length at most `12`.

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_block
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_block {s : ℕ} (h1 : 501 ≤ s) (h2 : s ≤ 1200) : LargestSkipLateAt s

declarations.name: topTaken_runNeeded_false_block
declarations.signature: theorem topTaken_runNeeded_false_block {s : ℕ} (h1 : 501 ≤ s) (h2 : s ≤ 1200) : topTaken s (runNeeded s) = false
declarations.docstring: The block, in the run language: the forced maximal run fails at every row.

declarations.name: topRun_deficit
declarations.signature: theorem topRun_deficit {s : ℕ} (h1 : 501 ≤ s) (h2 : s ≤ 1200) : ∃ d : ℕ, IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d ∧ (s - 1 - d) + s / 4 ≤ runNeeded s
declarations.docstring: **The run deficit, quantified.** On every row of the block the top take-run falls short of the run the negative branch of `#257` needs by at least `s / 4`.

declarations.name: topRun_record_1148
declarations.signature: theorem topRun_record_1148 : topTaken 1148 12 = true ∧ topTaken 1148 13 = false ∧ runNeeded 1148 = 382
declarations.docstring: **The record run of `[5, 3000]`, exactly.** At `s = 1148` the top twelve ranks are selected and the thirteenth is not: the run is exactly `12`. The negative branch of `#257` would need `runNeeded 1148 = 382`.

declarations.name: highTable
declarations.docstring: Row / largest-false-rank pairs at rows well past `H4`'s highest sample (`s = 3001`).

declarations.name: highAll
declarations.signature: theorem highAll : ∀ p ∈ highTable, pairOk p = true
declarations.docstring: **The kernel check at scale**, up to `s = 8000`.

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_high
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_high {s d : ℕ} (h : (s, d) ∈ highTable) : LargestSkipLateAt s

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_1148
declarations.docstring: `501 ≤ s ≤ 1200` is satisfiable — and the block conclusion holds there.

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_8000
declarations.docstring: The right-hand side of `largestSkipLateAt_iff_topTaken_false` is satisfied at a concrete row far outside the block.

declarations.name: topRun_deficient_witness
declarations.signature: theorem topRun_deficient_witness {N : ℕ} (hN : N ≤ 8000) : ∃ s : ℕ, N ≤ s ∧ topTaken s (runNeeded s) = false
declarations.docstring: The body of `half_mem_iff_topRun_deficient` is satisfied at every `N ≤ 8000`: the equivalence is not vacuous at the near end either.

declarations.name: wbs_nil_weights
declarations.signature: theorem wbs_nil_weights (bs : List Bool) : weightedBoolSum [] bs = 0

declarations.name: wbs_nil_bits
declarations.signature: theorem wbs_nil_bits (ws : List ℕ) : weightedBoolSum ws [] = 0

declarations.name: wbs_cons_true
declarations.signature: theorem wbs_cons_true (w : ℕ) (ws : List ℕ) (bs : List Bool) : weightedBoolSum (w :: ws) (true :: bs) = w + weightedBoolSum ws bs

declarations.name: wbs_cons_false
declarations.signature: theorem wbs_cons_false (w : ℕ) (ws : List ℕ) (bs : List Bool) : weightedBoolSum (w :: ws) (false :: bs) = weightedBoolSum ws bs

declarations.name: wbs_append
declarations.signature: theorem wbs_append : ∀ (l₁ : List ℕ) (b₁ : List Bool), b₁.length = l₁.length → ∀ (l₂ : List ℕ) (b₂ : List Bool), weightedBoolSum (l₁ ++ l₂) (b₁ ++ b₂) = weightedBoolSum l₁ b₁ + weightedBoolSum l₂ b₂
declarations.docstring: A weighted subset sum splits along a concatenation once the bit word is cut at the same place.

declarations.name: lift_cons
declarations.signature: theorem lift_cons (w c : ℕ) (ws cs : List ℕ) : liftWeights (w :: ws) (c :: cs) = (4 * w + c) :: liftWeights ws cs

declarations.name: lift_nil_left
declarations.signature: theorem lift_nil_left (cs : List ℕ) : liftWeights [] cs = []

declarations.name: liftWeights_length
declarations.signature: theorem liftWeights_length (ws cs : List ℕ) : (liftWeights ws cs).length = min ws.length cs.length

declarations.name: four_mul_wbs_le_lift
declarations.signature: theorem four_mul_wbs_le_lift : ∀ (ws cs : List ℕ), cs.length = ws.length → ∀ bs : List Bool, 4 * weightedBoolSum ws bs ≤ weightedBoolSum (liftWeights ws cs) bs
declarations.docstring: Selecting any bit word inside the lifted weights achieves at least four times what the same word achieves in the base weights.

declarations.name: wbs_lift_le
declarations.signature: theorem wbs_lift_le : ∀ (ws cs : List ℕ), cs.length = ws.length → ∀ bs : List Bool, weightedBoolSum (liftWeights ws cs) bs ≤ 4 * weightedBoolSum ws bs + cs.sum
declarations.docstring: …and at most four times that, plus the entire carry budget.

declarations.name: gapDominates_of_append_left
declarations.signature: theorem gapDominates_of_append_left {gap : ℕ} : ∀ (l₁ l₂ : List ℕ), GapDominates gap (l₁ ++ l₂) → GapDominates gap l₁
declarations.docstring: A prefix of a gap-dominating word is gap-dominating.

declarations.name: liftedRow
declarations.docstring: Row `s+1`'s weight word with its brand-new top rank `s` removed: every row-`s` weight quadruples and picks up its carry (`Corr2`).

declarations.name: preBits
declarations.docstring: The row-`s+1` greedy word restricted to that lifted prefix.

declarations.name: preSum
declarations.docstring: What the row-`s+1` greedy has already spent when it reaches its top rank.

declarations.name: seamWeights_succ_split
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeights_succ_split {s : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) : seamWeights (s + 1) = liftedRow s ++ [truncatedMersenneWeight (s + 1) s]

declarations.name: greedy_succ_split
declarations.signature: theorem greedy_succ_split {s : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) : integerGreedyBits (seamWeights (s + 1)) (seamSubsetTarget (s + 1)) = preBits s ++ integerGreedyBits [truncatedMersenneWeight (s + 1) s] (seamSubsetTarget (s + 1) - preSum s)

declarations.name: top_weight
declarations.signature: theorem top_weight {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) : truncatedMersenneWeight (s + 1) s = 2 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4
declarations.docstring: The brand-new top rank of row `s + 1` carries weight `2 ^ (s+2) + 4`.

declarations.name: top_mem_iff
declarations.signature: theorem top_mem_iff {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) : s ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord (s + 1)) ↔ truncatedMersenneWeight (s + 1) s ≤ seamSubsetTarget (s + 1) - preSum s
declarations.docstring: The top rank of row `s + 1` is selected exactly when the remainder entering the last greedy step can still pay for it.

declarations.name: remainder_step_of_top_mem
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_step_of_top_mem {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (htop : s ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord (s + 1))) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ≤ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ∧ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * s
declarations.docstring: **The row law.** Once the brand-new top rank of row `s+1` is selected, the concrete seam greedy defect obeys a two-sided recurrence: it is pinned to a window of width `2*s - 4` around `4 * R s - 2 ^ (s+1)`.

declarations.name: ForcedRun
declarations.docstring: The forced run: `LargestSkipLateAt` fails from row `N` on.

declarations.name: not_half_mem_iff_exists_forcedRun
declarations.signature: theorem not_half_mem_iff_exists_forcedRun : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∉ mersenneAchievementSet ↔ ∃ N : ℕ, ForcedRun N
declarations.docstring: Failure of half membership is exactly a forced run.

declarations.name: top_mem_of_not_largestSkipLateAt
declarations.signature: theorem top_mem_of_not_largestSkipLateAt {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h : ¬ LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)) : s ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord (s + 1))
declarations.docstring: Under the forced run, every brand-new top rank is selected.

declarations.name: remainder_step_of_not_largestSkipLateAt
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_step_of_not_largestSkipLateAt {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h : ¬ LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ≤ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ∧ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * s
declarations.docstring: **The row law, in `#257` vocabulary.**

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_ascent
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_ascent {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * s < 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s) : LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The certificate, ascent side.** If the defect falls too fast from row `s` to row `s+1`, row `s+1` has a late largest false rank.

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_descent
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_descent {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h : 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4) : LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The certificate, descent side.**

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_window_miss
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_window_miss {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h : ¬ (seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ≤ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ∧ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * s)) : LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The certificate.** A single scalar per row: if the one-step defect `4 * R s - R (s+1) - 2 ^ (s+1)` leaves the window `[4, 2*s]`, row `s+1` has a late largest false rank.

declarations.name: StepLaw
declarations.signature: def StepLaw (f : ℕ → ℕ) (N : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The abstract shape of the row law: a sequence obeying the same two-sided recurrence the forced run imposes on `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder`.

declarations.name: stepLaw_of_forcedRun
declarations.signature: theorem stepLaw_of_forcedRun {N : ℕ} (h : ForcedRun N) : StepLaw seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (max N 3)
declarations.docstring: The forced run makes the concrete defect obey the law from `max N 3` on.

declarations.name: stepLaw_pow_add_two
declarations.docstring: **The no-go.** The law is consistent: the explicit sequence `2 ^ s + 2` obeys it at every row `s ≥ 3`. So no contradiction can be extracted from the row law alone — the forced run survives the recurrence.

declarations.name: exists_stepLaw
declarations.signature: theorem exists_stepLaw : ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, StepLaw f 3 ∧ ∀ s, 0 < f s
declarations.docstring: The no-go, packaged: a strictly positive solution of the law exists.

declarations.name: forcedRun_defect_window
declarations.signature: theorem forcedRun_defect_window {N : ℕ} (h : ForcedRun N) {s : ℕ} (hs : max N 3 ≤ s) : ∃ c : ℕ, 4 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 2 * s ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + c = 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s
declarations.docstring: **The forced run in one equation.** Under the forced run the whole tail of the defect sequence is a *deterministic* quadrupling map, up to a correction confined to the window `[4, 2*s]` — a window of width `2*s - 4` sitting inside an a-priori range of size `2 ^ (s+2)`.

declarations.name: stepLaw_iterate
declarations.signature: theorem stepLaw_iterate {f : ℕ → ℕ} {N : ℕ} (h : StepLaw f N) {s : ℕ} (hs : N ≤ s) : ∀ k : ℕ, 4 ^ k * f s + 2 ^ s * 2 ^ k + (s + k) ≤ f (s + k) + 2 ^ s * 4 ^ k + (s + k) * 4 ^ k
declarations.docstring: **The backward iteration.** Any solution of the law is squeezed towards `2 ^ s` by the rows above it: dividing through by `4 ^ k`, this reads `f s ≤ f (s+k) / 4 ^ k + 2 ^ s * (1 - 2 ^ (-k)) + (s + k)`.

declarations.name: remainder_le_of_forcedRun_of_growth
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_le_of_forcedRun_of_growth {N : ℕ} (h : ForcedRun N) (hg : ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m → seamIntegerGreedyRemainder m ≤ 2 ^ (m + 1)) {s : ℕ} (hs : max N 3 ≤ s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ 2 ^ s + 2 * s + 1
declarations.docstring: **The pinning.** If the forced run holds from `N` on *and* the defect stays inside the size regime `R m ≤ 2 ^ (m+1)` measured at every computed row, then the defect is squeezed to within `2*s + 1` of the single value `2 ^ s`, out of an a-priori range of size `2 ^ (s+1)`. The growth hypothesis is **not** proved here; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: remainder_ge_of_no_late_window
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_ge_of_no_late_window {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h : ∀ t : ℕ, s ≤ t → t ≤ 2 * s + 1 → ¬ LargestSkipLateAt (t + 1)) : 2 ^ s + 2 ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s
declarations.docstring: **Forward iteration of the descent half, localised.** If `LargestSkipLateAt` fails on the whole window `[s+1, 2*s+2]`, the defect at row `s` cannot dip to `2 ^ s + 1`: the descent would drive it below zero within `s + 2` further rows.

declarations.name: remainder_ge_of_forcedRun
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_ge_of_forcedRun {N : ℕ} (h : ForcedRun N) {s : ℕ} (hs : max N 3 ≤ s) : 2 ^ s + 2 ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s
declarations.docstring: **The unconditional lower half of the pinning.** Under the forced run the defect never dips below `2 ^ s + 2`.

declarations.name: exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_remainder_small
declarations.signature: theorem exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_remainder_small {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ 2 ^ s + 1) : ∃ t : ℕ, s + 1 ≤ t ∧ t ≤ 2 * s + 2 ∧ LargestSkipLateAt t
declarations.docstring: **The window certificate.** A single scalar: whenever the defect of row `s` dips to `2 ^ s + 1`, some row of `[s+1, 2*s+2]` has a late largest false rank.

declarations.name: remainder_band_of_forcedRun_of_growth
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_band_of_forcedRun_of_growth {N : ℕ} (h : ForcedRun N) (hg : ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m → seamIntegerGreedyRemainder m ≤ 2 ^ (m + 1)) {s : ℕ} (hs : max N 3 ≤ s) : 2 ^ s + 2 ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ 2 ^ s + 2 * s + 1
declarations.docstring: **The band.** Under the forced run, and inside the measured size regime, the defect is confined to an interval of length `2*s` around `2 ^ s` — out of an a-priori range of size `2 ^ (s+1)`.

declarations.name: remOf
declarations.docstring: The concrete greedy defect, through `SkipD3`'s kernel-computable row word.

declarations.name: remOf_eq
declarations.signature: theorem remOf_eq (s : ℕ) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = remOf s

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_remOf_ascent
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_remOf_ascent {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h : remOf (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * s < 4 * remOf s) : LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_remOf_descent
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_remOf_descent {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h : 4 * remOf s < remOf (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4) : LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)

declarations.name: lateAt_1500
declarations.docstring: A scalar-interface certificate at row `1500`. The two remainders used by the certificate are computed from the concrete greedy words; the point is the form of the implication, not an extension of the corpus's certified range.

declarations.name: lateAt_1501
declarations.docstring: …and at row `1501`.

declarations.name: top_mem_eleven
declarations.docstring: The hypothesis of `remainder_step_of_top_mem` is satisfiable: the brand-new top rank `11` of row `12` really is selected.

declarations.name: remainder_step_eleven
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_step_eleven : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 12 + 2 ^ 12 + 4 ≤ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 11 ∧ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 11 ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 12 + 2 ^ 12 + 2 * 11
declarations.docstring: …so the row law fires at a concrete row.

declarations.name: not_largestSkipLateAt_twelve
declarations.docstring: The hypothesis of `remainder_step_of_not_largestSkipLateAt` is satisfiable: row `12` is one of the four rows of `[5, 3000]` at which `LargestSkipLateAt` genuinely fails. Every rank of its late zone — `9`, `10`, `11` — is selected.

declarations.name: remainder_step_eleven'
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_step_eleven' : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 12 + 2 ^ 12 + 4 ≤ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 11 ∧ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 11 ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 12 + 2 ^ 12 + 2 * 11
declarations.docstring: …so the row law in `#257` vocabulary fires at a concrete row too.

declarations.name: remainder_small_seven
declarations.docstring: The hypothesis of `exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_remainder_small` is satisfiable: row `7` has defect `3`, far below `2 ^ 7 + 1`.

declarations.name: exists_late_in_window_seven
declarations.signature: theorem exists_late_in_window_seven : ∃ t : ℕ, 8 ≤ t ∧ t ≤ 16 ∧ LargestSkipLateAt t
declarations.docstring: …and the window certificate then produces a late largest false rank somewhere in `[8, 16]` — `lateAt_8` says it is already at the left end.

declarations.name: defect_window_eleven
declarations.signature: theorem defect_window_eleven : ∃ c : ℕ, 4 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ 2 * 11 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 12 + 2 ^ 12 + c = 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 11
declarations.docstring: The defect window of `forcedRun_defect_window` is realised, with room to spare, at the same row: `4 * R 11 - R 12 - 2 ^ 12 = 8`, inside `[4, 22]`.

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_upperOrMiddle
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_upperOrMiddle {s : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hUM : SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt s hs) : LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: An upper-or-middle branch at `s` makes rank `s` a *late* largest false rank of row `s + 1`, so row `s + 1` is good.

declarations.name: not_upperOrMiddle_of_not_largestSkipLateAt_succ
declarations.signature: theorem not_upperOrMiddle_of_not_largestSkipLateAt_succ {s : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hbad : ¬ LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)) : ¬ SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt s hs
declarations.docstring: **The link.** A bad row `s + 1` forces the row-`s` step to be a right branch.

declarations.name: noLateSkip
declarations.docstring: `noLateSkip s`: every rank of the late zone of row `s` is selected by the concrete greedy. A `true` value certifies `¬ LargestSkipLateAt s`.

declarations.name: not_largestSkipLateAt_of_noLateSkip
declarations.signature: theorem not_largestSkipLateAt_of_noLateSkip {s : ℕ} (h : noLateSkip s = true) : ¬ LargestSkipLateAt s

declarations.name: deficit_step
declarations.signature: theorem deficit_step {s D : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hR : ¬ SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt s hs) (hD : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + D = 2 ^ s) : ∃ D' : ℕ, seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + D' = 2 ^ (s + 1) ∧ 4 * D + 4 ≤ D'
declarations.docstring: **Deficit step.** On a right branch the distance of the greedy remainder *below* the half point `2 ^ s` is more than quadrupled.

declarations.name: deficit_iter
declarations.signature: theorem deficit_iter {N : ℕ} (hN : 5 ≤ N) {D : ℕ} (hD : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N + D = 2 ^ N) : ∀ k : ℕ, (∀ j : ℕ, j < k → ¬ SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt (N + j) (by omega)) → ∃ D' : ℕ, seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (N + k) + D' = 2 ^ (N + k) ∧ 4 ^ k * D + 4 ^ k ≤ D' + 1
declarations.docstring: **Deficit iteration.** Along a run of right branches the deficit grows at least like `4 ^ k`, with an extra additive `4 ^ k`.

declarations.name: exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_remainder_le_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_remainder_le_two_pow {N : ℕ} (hN : 5 ≤ N) (hrem : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N ≤ 2 ^ N) : ∃ t : ℕ, N + 1 ≤ t ∧ t ≤ 2 * N + 1 ∧ LargestSkipLateAt t
declarations.docstring: **Theorem A (unconditional).** If the concrete seam greedy remainder of a row `N ≥ 5` has not risen above the half point `2 ^ N`, then a *late* largest false rank occurs at some row of the window `[N + 1, 2 * N + 1]`. Equivalently: a run of bad rows starting at `N + 1` has length at most `N` whenever `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N ≤ 2 ^ N`.

declarations.name: deficit_shrinks_along_rightRun
declarations.signature: theorem deficit_shrinks_along_rightRun {N k : ℕ} (hN : 5 ≤ N) (hle : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N ≤ 2 ^ N) (hblock : ∀ j : ℕ, j < k → ¬ SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt (N + j) (by omega)) : 4 ^ k * (2 ^ N - seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N) + 4 ^ k ≤ 2 ^ (N + k) + 1
declarations.docstring: **The counting law, explicitly.** Along a run of `k` right branches the *set of admissible base deficits* shrinks by a factor `4` per row: the deficit `2 ^ N - rem(N)` is confined to `[0, 2 ^ (N - k)]` up to the additive `4 ^ k` that the `+ 4` in the recurrence contributes. For `k > N` the confinement is empty, which is `exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_remainder_le_two_pow`.

declarations.name: RemainderReachesHalfPointCofinally
declarations.docstring: The concrete seam greedy remainder returns to or below the half point `2 ^ s` at arbitrarily large rows.

declarations.name: half_mem_of_remainderReachesHalfPointCofinally
declarations.docstring: **`1/2 ∈ mersenneAchievementSet` follows from one inequality, infinitely often.** No side condition, no unproved bit correspondence: it is enough that the deterministic remainder `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s` fails to exceed `2 ^ s` at arbitrarily large `s`.

declarations.name: surplus_step
declarations.signature: theorem surplus_step {s σ : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hR : ¬ SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt s hs) (hσ : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = 2 ^ s + σ) (hbig : 2 * s ≤ σ) : ∃ σ' : ℕ, seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) = 2 ^ (s + 1) + σ' ∧ 3 * σ ≤ σ' ∧ 2 * (s + 1) ≤ σ'
declarations.docstring: **Surplus step.** On a right branch a surplus of at least `2 * s` above the half point at least triples.

declarations.name: surplus_iter
declarations.signature: theorem surplus_iter {N : ℕ} (hN : 5 ≤ N) {σ : ℕ} (hσ : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N = 2 ^ N + σ) (hbig : 2 * N ≤ σ) : ∀ k : ℕ, (∀ j : ℕ, j < k → ¬ SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt (N + j) (by omega)) → ∃ σ' : ℕ, seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (N + k) = 2 ^ (N + k) + σ' ∧ 3 ^ k * σ ≤ σ' ∧ 2 * (N + k) ≤ σ'
declarations.docstring: **Surplus iteration.** Along a run of right branches a surplus above the half point grows at least like `3 ^ k`.

declarations.name: ObeysRemainderCeiling
declarations.docstring: The remainder ceiling `3 * rem(s) < 7 * 2 ^ s + 4`, i.e. `rem(s)` below `(7/3) * 2 ^ s`. Every *good* row obeys it automatically (`three_mul_remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLateAt`), and an arbitrary-precision replication finds it satisfied at every row of `[5, 299]`, with the worst ratio `0.856` at `s = 43`.

declarations.name: three_mul_remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLateAt
declarations.signature: theorem three_mul_remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLateAt {s : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hgood : LargestSkipLateAt s) : ObeysRemainderCeiling s
declarations.docstring: **Good rows obey the ceiling, unconditionally.** This is the exact adjacent-gap strip invariant `three_mul_remainder_lt_exactLateGap` with the late-zone margin `2 * s < 3 * d` used to collapse the correction `4 ^ (s - d)` into `2 ^ (s - 1)`.

declarations.name: not_surplus_run
declarations.signature: theorem not_surplus_run {N σ : ℕ} (hN : 5 ≤ N) (hσ : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N = 2 ^ N + σ) (hbig : 2 * N ≤ σ) (hblock : ∀ j : ℕ, j < 2 * N + 2 → ¬ SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt (N + j) (by omega)) (hceil : ObeysRemainderCeiling (3 * N + 2)) : False
declarations.docstring: **Theorem B.** A surplus of at least `2 * N` above the half point at row `N`, followed by `2 * N + 2` right branches, is impossible if the top row of the run still obeys the remainder ceiling: the tripling drives the remainder past every value a good row can carry.

declarations.name: exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_surplus
declarations.signature: theorem exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_surplus {N σ : ℕ} (hN : 5 ≤ N) (hσ : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N = 2 ^ N + σ) (hbig : 2 * N ≤ σ) (hceil : ObeysRemainderCeiling (3 * N + 2)) : ∃ t : ℕ, N + 1 ≤ t ∧ t ≤ 3 * N + 2 ∧ LargestSkipLateAt t
declarations.docstring: **Theorem B, positive form.** A row `N` carrying a surplus of at least `2 * N` above the half point *produces* a late largest false rank inside `[N + 1, 3 * N + 2]`, provided the top row of that window still obeys the remainder ceiling.

declarations.name: badRun_pins_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem badRun_pins_remainder {N : ℕ} (hN : 5 ≤ N) (hbad : ∀ t : ℕ, N + 1 ≤ t → t ≤ 3 * N + 2 → ¬ LargestSkipLateAt t) (hceil : ObeysRemainderCeiling (3 * N + 2)) : 2 ^ N < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N < 2 ^ N + 2 * N
declarations.docstring: **The pin.** Suppose every row of `[N + 1, 3 * N + 2]` is bad and the top row `3 * N + 2` of that block still obeys the remainder ceiling that every good row obeys. Then the remainder at the base row `N` is trapped in the window `(2 ^ N, 2 ^ N + 2 * N)` — an interval of width `2 * N` inside a range of size `2 ^ N`. The two clauses come from opposite sides: below the half point the deficit quadruples per bad row (`deficit_iter`), above it the surplus triples (`surplus_iter`). Only a window of relative width `O(N * 2 ^ (-N))` around the half point `2 ^ N` survives both.

declarations.name: RemainderMissesHalfPointWindowCofinally
declarations.docstring: Cofinally many rows `s` whose remainder avoids the width-`2 * s` window just above the half point `2 ^ s`, and whose companion row `3 * s + 2` obeys the remainder ceiling.

declarations.name: half_mem_of_remainderMissesHalfPointWindowCofinally
declarations.docstring: **The endpoint.** `1/2 ∈ mersenneAchievementSet` as soon as the deterministic seam greedy remainder misses the width-`2 * s` half-point window at arbitrarily large `s`.

declarations.name: not_upperOrMiddle_of_mem_succ
declarations.signature: theorem not_upperOrMiddle_of_mem_succ {s : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hmem : s ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord (s + 1))) : ¬ SeamGreedyUpperOrMiddleAt s hs
declarations.docstring: A right branch is exactly the statement that the new terminal rank is *taken*, so it is certified by a single bit of the successor row.

declarations.name: deficit_step_witness
declarations.signature: theorem deficit_step_witness : ∃ D' : ℕ, seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 7 + D' = 2 ^ 7 ∧ 4 * 30 + 4 ≤ D'
declarations.docstring: `deficit_step` at `s = 6`: the row-`6` remainder `34` sits `30` below the half point `2 ^ 6 = 64`, the step is a right branch, and the conclusion is realised with `D' = 125 ≥ 4 * 30 + 4`.

declarations.name: deficit_iter_witness
declarations.signature: theorem deficit_iter_witness : ∃ D' : ℕ, seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (6 + 1) + D' = 2 ^ (6 + 1) ∧ 4 ^ 1 * 30 + 4 ^ 1 ≤ D' + 1
declarations.docstring: `deficit_iter` at `N = 6`, `k = 1`: a genuine one-row right run below the half point.

declarations.name: deficit_shrinks_witness
declarations.docstring: The explicit counting law, instantiated at `N = 6`, `k = 1`: `4 * (2 ^ 6 - 34) + 4 = 124 ≤ 2 ^ 7 + 1`.

declarations.name: surplus_step_witness
declarations.signature: theorem surplus_step_witness : ∃ σ' : ℕ, seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (9 + 1) = 2 ^ (9 + 1) + σ' ∧ 3 * 29 ≤ σ' ∧ 2 * (9 + 1) ≤ σ'
declarations.docstring: `surplus_step` at `s = 9`: the row-`9` remainder `541` sits `29` above the half point `2 ^ 9 = 512`, `29 ≥ 2 * 9`, and the step is a right branch.

declarations.name: surplus_iter_witness
declarations.signature: theorem surplus_iter_witness : ∃ σ' : ℕ, seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (10 + 3) = 2 ^ (10 + 3) + σ' ∧ 3 ^ 3 * 111 ≤ σ' ∧ 2 * (10 + 3) ≤ σ'
declarations.docstring: The three bad rows `11, 12, 13` give a genuine **three-step** right run above the half point, based at `N = 10` where the surplus is `111 ≥ 2 * 10`. So `surplus_iter` is not vacuous even at `k = 3`: it predicts `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 13 ≥ 2 ^ 13 + 27 * 111 = 11189`, and the true value is `15147`.

declarations.name: obeysRemainderCeiling_fourteen
declarations.docstring: The good-row ceiling lemma, instantiated: row `14` is good (`largestSkipLateAt_fourteen`), so it obeys the ceiling; its remainder is `392` against a ceiling of `(7 * 2 ^ 14 + 4) / 3 = 38229`.

declarations.name: obeysRemainderCeiling_seventeen
declarations.docstring: The ceiling at the companion row `3 * 5 + 2 = 17`, checked directly.

declarations.name: theoremB_witness
declarations.signature: theorem theoremB_witness : ∃ t : ℕ, 6 ≤ t ∧ t ≤ 17 ∧ LargestSkipLateAt t
declarations.docstring: The hypotheses of `exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_surplus` hold at `N = 5`: `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 5 = 71 = 2 ^ 5 + 39` with `39 ≥ 2 * 5`, and the companion row `17` obeys the ceiling. The theorem therefore *produces* a late largest false rank somewhere in `[6, 17]`.

declarations.name: theoremA_witness
