declarations.name: cfaBracket
declarations.signature: def cfaBracket (n k : ℕ) (lam r : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The paper's displayed bracket (CF).

declarations.name: CFAPathConstruction
declarations.docstring: **External input for `res:constant-factor-path`.** The paper's construction: for a squarefree monic `f` of degree `n ≥ 3` with least critical modulus `μ > 0`, every `r ∈ (0,1)` and `λ > 1` give a selected component with `k ≥ 2` roots and a path in `{|f| < λμ}` between two zero occurrences of length at most the bracket (CF) times `ρ = μ^{1/n}`. Its ingredients are Pólya's area inequality, the Koebe distortion theorem, the coarea formula with the boundary identity `|dz| = σ dφ/|f'|` and total argument variation `2πk'`, the area formula for the disjoint images of the univalent inverse branches, and the mean-value selection of a regular level and of a direction avoiding the critical-value arguments. The containment is strict because the proof selects a regular level strictly inside its positive-measure window, which is what the paper's own `{|f| < 1}` clause uses.

declarations.name: cfaBracket_two_three_twentieths_lt
declarations.signature: theorem cfaBracket_two_three_twentieths_lt {n k : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : cfaBracket n k 2 (3 / 20) ≤ 71 / 10
declarations.docstring: The bracket at `λ = 2`, `r = 3/20` is below `71/10` in every degree `n ≥ 3` and for every root count `k ≥ 2`. The largest case is `n = 3`, `k = 2`.

declarations.name: cfaBracket_five_point_seven
declarations.signature: theorem cfaBracket_five_point_seven {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) : Real.sqrt (2 / (k : ℝ)) * (Real.sqrt 2 * (3 / 20) / (1 - 3 / 20) ^ 2 + (Real.sqrt (Real.log ((2 : ℝ) / (3 / 20))) + Real.pi / Real.sqrt (Real.log 2))) ≤ 5.7
declarations.docstring: At `μ ≤ 1/2` the same bracket is below `5.7`, because `λ^{1/n}ρ = (2μ)^{1/n} ≤ 1` and `ρ ≤ 1`. This is the closing numerical display of the theorem's proof.

declarations.name: cfaArityBracket
declarations.docstring: The arity corollary's bracket: the (CF) bracket after the reductions `ρ ≤ 1` and `(λμ)^{1/n} ≤ 1` that its proof performs.

declarations.name: CFAArityConstruction
declarations.signature: def CFAArityConstruction (n : ℕ) (f : ℂ[X]) (z : Fin n → ℂ) (k₀ : ℕ) (lam r : ℝ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: **External input for `res:constant-factor-arity`.** The same construction as `CFAPathConstruction`, in the shape its corollary's proof uses: every selected component contains the first-merge component, so its root count is at least `k₀`, and the reductions `ρ ≤ 1`, `(λμ)^{1/n} ≤ 1` available when `λμ ≤ 1` have already been made.

declarations.name: cfaArityBracket_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem cfaArityBracket_nonneg {lam r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hr1 : r < 1) (hlam : 1 < lam) : 0 ≤ cfaArityBracket lam r

declarations.name: cfaArityBracket_case_one
declarations.docstring: `λ = 2`, `r = 13/100`: the squared bracket is below `34`.

declarations.name: cfaArityBracket_case_two
declarations.docstring: `λ = 4`, `r = 3/25`: the squared bracket is below `24`.

declarations.name: cfaArityBracket_case_three
declarations.docstring: `λ = 8`, `r = 11/100`: the squared bracket is below `20`.

declarations.name: cfaArity_length_le
declarations.signature: theorem cfaArity_length_le {k₀ : ℕ} {B : ℝ} (hk : 2 ≤ k₀) (hB0 : 0 ≤ B) (hB : B ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (k₀ : ℝ)) : Real.sqrt (2 / (k₀ : ℝ)) * B ≤ 2
declarations.docstring: The arity step: a squared bracket below `2k₀` closes the path below `2`.

declarations.name: cfaTau
declarations.docstring: The paper's threshold `τ_k = (√(2k) - A)/B`.

declarations.name: cfaA_bound
declarations.docstring: The paper's exact bound `A ≥ √2·(1/20)/(19/20)²`.

declarations.name: cfaB_bound
declarations.signature: theorem cfaB_bound : Real.sqrt (Real.log 40) + Real.pi / Real.sqrt (Real.log 2) ≤ cfaB
declarations.docstring: The paper's exact bound `B ≥ √(log 40) + π/√(log 2)`.

declarations.name: CFACapacityConstruction
declarations.signature: def CFACapacityConstruction (n : ℕ) (f : ℂ[X]) (z : Fin n → ℂ) (κ : ℝ) (k₀ : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: **External input for `res:constant-factor-capacity`.** The averaging proof of `res:constant-factor-path`, rerun on the component `C` of `{|f| < 2μ}` containing the first-merge critical point, with the global area input replaced by the component form `Area(C) ≤ π cap(closure C)² = π κ²(2μ)^{2/n}` of the area–capacity inequality, at `λ = 2`, `r = 1/20`. `κ` is the paper's capacity ratio `cap(closure C)/(2μ)^{1/n}`; the pinned Mathlib has no logarithmic capacity, so `κ` enters as the real parameter this hypothesis is stated for.

declarations.name: cfa_capacity_criterion
declarations.signature: theorem cfa_capacity_criterion {n : ℕ} {f : ℂ[X]} {z : Fin n → ℂ} {κ : ℝ} {k₀ : ℕ} (hk₀ : 2 ≤ k₀) (hκ0 : 0 ≤ κ) (hκ : κ ≤ cfaTau k₀) (hext : CFACapacityConstruction n f z κ k₀) : cfaJoinedBelow f z 1 2
declarations.docstring: **`res:constant-factor-capacity`, main clause.** If the capacity ratio `κ` of the selected component is at most `τ_{k₀}`, the construction closes below `2`, so Erdős #1041 holds for `f`.

declarations.name: cfaTau_ge_of_sq
declarations.signature: theorem cfaTau_ge_of_sq {k : ℕ} {q : ℝ} (hq : 0 ≤ q) (h : (cfaA + cfaB * q) ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (k : ℝ)) : q ≤ cfaTau k
declarations.docstring: Every rational cutoff `q` with `(A + Bq)² ≤ 2k` lies below `τ_k`.

declarations.name: cfaTau_third
declarations.signature: theorem cfaTau_third {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) : (1 : ℝ) / 3 ≤ cfaTau k
declarations.docstring: **`κ ≤ 1/3` suffices for every root count `k₀ ≥ 2`.**

declarations.name: cfaTau_cutoffs
declarations.signature: theorem cfaTau_cutoffs : (2 / 5 : ℝ) ≤ cfaTau 3 ∧ (12 / 25 : ℝ) ≤ cfaTau 4 ∧ (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ cfaTau 5 ∧ (7 / 12 : ℝ) ≤ cfaTau 6 ∧ (16 / 25 : ℝ) ≤ cfaTau 7 ∧ (2 / 3 : ℝ) ≤ cfaTau 8 ∧ (7 / 10 : ℝ) ≤ cfaTau 9 ∧ (39 / 40 : ℝ) ≤ cfaTau 16
declarations.docstring: **The displayed rational cutoffs** `2/5, 12/25, 1/2, 7/12, 16/25, 2/3, 7/10` at `k₀ = 3, …, 9`, rising to `39/40` at `k₀ = 16`.

declarations.name: cfaJoinedBelow_mono_level
declarations.signature: theorem cfaJoinedBelow_mono_level {n : ℕ} {f : ℂ[X]} {z : Fin n → ℂ} {R R' L : ℝ} (h : cfaJoinedBelow f z R L) (hRR : R ≤ R') : cfaJoinedBelow f z R' L

declarations.name: cfa_degree_two_mu
declarations.signature: theorem cfa_degree_two_mu {f : ℂ[X]} {z : Fin 2 → ℂ} {μ : ℝ} (hz : RootEnumeration f z) (hμ : CriticalMinimum f μ) : μ = ‖(z 0 - z 1) / 2‖ ^ 2
declarations.docstring: In degree two the least critical modulus is the squared half-gap.

declarations.name: cfa_degree_two_below
declarations.signature: theorem cfa_degree_two_below {f : ℂ[X]} {z : Fin 2 → ℂ} {μ R L : ℝ} (hz' : f = ∏ i, (X - C (z i))) (hmu : μ = ‖(z 0 - z 1) / 2‖ ^ 2) (hR : μ < R) (hL : ‖z 0 - z 1‖ ≤ L) : cfaJoinedBelow f z R L
declarations.docstring: The degree-two root segment: it lies below every level above `μ` and has length `2ρ`.

declarations.name: cfa_constant_factor_path
declarations.signature: theorem cfa_constant_factor_path (hext : CFAPathConstruction) {n : ℕ} {f : ℂ[X]} {z : Fin n → ℂ} {μ : ℝ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.natDegree = n) (hz : RootEnumeration f z) (hμ : CriticalMinimum f μ) : cfaJoinedAtMost f z (2 * μ) ((71 / 10) * μ ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))) ∧ (μ ≤ 1 / 2 → cfaJoinedBelow f z 1 5.7)
declarations.docstring: **`res:constant-factor-path` (core.tex line 739).** Conditional on `CFAPathConstruction`: for every monic `f` of degree `n ≥ 2`, two zero occurrences are joined by a possibly degenerate path of length at most `(71/10)ρ` inside `K_{2μ}`, with distinct locations when `f` is squarefree; and if `μ ≤ 1/2` the construction may be chosen inside `{|f| < 1}` with length at most `5.7`.

declarations.name: cfa_arity_criterion
declarations.signature: theorem cfa_arity_criterion {n : ℕ} {f : ℂ[X]} {z : Fin n → ℂ} {μ : ℝ} {k₀ : ℕ} (hz : RootEnumeration f z) (hμ : CriticalMinimum f μ) (hcase : 0 < μ → (μ ≤ 1 / 2 ∧ 17 ≤ k₀ ∧ CFAArityConstruction n f z k₀ 2 (13 / 100)) ∨ (μ ≤ 1 / 4 ∧ 12 ≤ k₀ ∧ CFAArityConstruction n f z k₀ 4 (3 / 25)) ∨ (μ ≤ 1 / 8 ∧ 10 ≤ k₀ ∧ CFAArityConstruction n f z k₀ 8 (11 / 100))) : cfaJoinedBelow f z 1 2
declarations.docstring: **`res:constant-factor-arity` (core.tex line 882).** Conditional on `CFAArityConstruction` in the relevant case: Erdős #1041 holds for `f` in each of `μ ≤ 1/2` with `k₀ ≥ 17`, `μ ≤ 1/4` with `k₀ ≥ 12`, and `μ ≤ 1/8` with `k₀ ≥ 10`. The degenerate case `μ = 0` is proved outright.

declarations.name: DiscSepNormalised
declarations.signature: structure DiscSepNormalised (P : ℂ[X]) (n : ℕ) (w₀ S : ℝ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The hypotheses of the long record's Theorem `res:critical-value-separation` (`core.tex` line 1341) on the normalised polynomial `P`: degree `n ≥ 3`, leading coefficient of modulus one, `P(0) = 1`, `P'(0) = 0`, `P''(0) ≠ 0`, a real centre `w₀ ∈ [0,1]`, a radius `S > max(w₀, 1 - w₀)`, and the separation `|P(d) - w₀| ≥ S` at every other critical point.

declarations.name: DiscSepConnector
declarations.signature: structure DiscSepConnector (P : ℂ[X]) (Z : ℝ → ℂ) (L : ℝ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The paper's connector: the two local solutions of `P(Z ξ) = 1 - ξ²` with `Z 0 = 0`, continued along the real segment `[-1,1]` into one injective rectifiable curve of length at most `L`.

declarations.name: eval_right
declarations.signature: theorem eval_right (h : DiscSepConnector P Z L) : P.eval (Z 1) = 0
declarations.docstring: The right endpoint of the connector is a root of `P`.

declarations.name: eval_left
declarations.signature: theorem eval_left (h : DiscSepConnector P Z L) : P.eval (Z (-1)) = 0
declarations.docstring: The left endpoint of the connector is a root of `P`.

declarations.name: endpoints_ne
declarations.signature: theorem endpoints_ne (h : DiscSepConnector P Z L) : Z (-1) ≠ Z 1
declarations.docstring: The two endpoints are distinct.

declarations.name: contained
declarations.signature: theorem contained (h : DiscSepConnector P Z L) : ∀ ξ ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, ‖P.eval (Z ξ)‖ ≤ 1
declarations.docstring: `Γ ⊆ {|P| ≤ 1}`: the containment clause follows from the functional equation alone.

declarations.name: discSepQsq
declarations.docstring: The squared radius `q² = S/(S² + p)` of the image of `[-1,1]` under the paper's chart `ζ`.

declarations.name: discSepCoefficient
declarations.signature: def discSepCoefficient (n : ℕ) (S p : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The left-hand side of the paper's display (6), `(S/(n-1))^(2/n) · log((S² + S + p)/(S² - S + p))`.

declarations.name: discSep_denominator_factor
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_denominator_factor (w₀ S : ℝ) : S ^ 2 - S + w₀ * (1 - w₀) = (S - w₀) * (S - (1 - w₀))
declarations.docstring: The paper's factorisation `S² - S + p = (S - w₀)(S - (1 - w₀))`.

declarations.name: discSep_denominator_pos
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_denominator_pos {w₀ S : ℝ} (h : max w₀ (1 - w₀) < S) : 0 < S ^ 2 - S + w₀ * (1 - w₀)
declarations.docstring: This is exactly where `S > max(w₀, 1 - w₀)` enters the length estimate.

declarations.name: discSep_radius_pos
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_radius_pos {w₀ S : ℝ} (hw₀ : 0 ≤ w₀) (h : max w₀ (1 - w₀) < S) : 0 < S

declarations.name: discSep_qsq_mem
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_qsq_mem {w₀ S : ℝ} (hw₀ : 0 ≤ w₀) (h : max w₀ (1 - w₀) < S) : 0 < discSepQsq S (w₀ * (1 - w₀)) ∧ discSepQsq S (w₀ * (1 - w₀)) < 1
declarations.docstring: `0 < q² < 1`, as the Bergman segment inequality requires.

declarations.name: discSep_bergman_factor
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_bergman_factor {S p : ℝ} (hS : 0 < S) (hden : 0 < S ^ 2 - S + p) : (1 + discSepQsq S p) / (1 - discSepQsq S p) = (S ^ 2 + S + p) / (S ^ 2 - S + p)
declarations.docstring: The Bergman factor in the chart coordinate is the paper's ratio: `(1 + q²)/(1 - q²) = (S² + S + p)/(S² - S + p)`.

declarations.name: discSep_log_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_log_nonneg {S p : ℝ} (hS : 0 < S) (hden : 0 < S ^ 2 - S + p) : 0 ≤ Real.log ((S ^ 2 + S + p) / (S ^ 2 - S + p))
declarations.docstring: The logarithmic factor is nonnegative in the admissible range.

declarations.name: discSep_target_starShaped
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_target_starShaped {a S : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (haS : a < S) {ξ : ℂ} (hξ : ‖ξ ^ 2 - (a : ℂ)‖ < S) {t : ℝ} (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) : ‖((t : ℂ) * ξ) ^ 2 - (a : ℂ)‖ < S
declarations.docstring: The square-root target `Q̃ = {ξ : |ξ² - a| < S}` is star-shaped about `0`: `t²ξ²` is a convex combination of `ξ²` and `0`, both in the disc `D(a,S)` because `S > a ≥ 0`. Hence `Q̃` is connected and simply connected, which is what the paper's covering argument uses.

declarations.name: discSep_mobius_norm_lt
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_mobius_norm_lt {a S : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (haS : a < S) {w : ℂ} (hw : ‖w - (a : ℂ)‖ < S) : ‖(S : ℂ) * w‖ < ‖(S : ℂ) ^ 2 + (a : ℂ) * w - (a : ℂ) ^ 2‖
declarations.docstring: The paper's Möbius map `w ↦ Sw/(S² + aw - a²)` carries the disc `D(a,S)` into the unit disc. Stated as a strict comparison of the two moduli, which also shows that its denominator does not vanish on `D(a,S)`.

declarations.name: discSep_mobius_at_one
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_mobius_at_one (w₀ S : ℝ) : S * 1 / (S ^ 2 + (1 - w₀) * 1 - (1 - w₀) ^ 2) = discSepQsq S (w₀ * (1 - w₀))
declarations.docstring: At `ξ = 1` the chart lands on `q² = S/(S² + p)`, with `a = 1 - w₀` and `p = w₀(1 - w₀)`. This identifies the paper's radius `q`.

declarations.name: DiscSepBergmanArea
declarations.docstring: **The external classical input.** In the paper's proof of `res:critical-value-separation` this is the chain Riemann-mapping/covering theory (the proper local biholomorphism `ξ : U → Q̃` is a conformal bijection because `Q̃` is star-shaped, hence simply connected) → the Bergman segment inequality, display (7) → the exterior-Blaschke fibre capacity gap `cap(closure U')ⁿ/S' < 1/(n-1)` → Pólya's area–capacity inequality `Area(K) ≤ π cap(K)²`. None of Riemann mapping, the Bergman kernel, logarithmic capacity or Pólya is available in the pinned Mathlib, so the chain is taken here as one named hypothesis, in exactly the form the paper's proof delivers it.

declarations.name: discSep_squared_length_le
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_squared_length_le {n : ℕ} {w₀ S L area : ℝ} (hw₀ : 0 ≤ w₀) (hS : max w₀ (1 - w₀) < S) (hBergman : L ^ 2 ≤ 2 / Real.pi * Real.log ((1 + discSepQsq S (w₀ * (1 - w₀))) / (1 - discSepQsq S (w₀ * (1 - w₀)))) * area) (hArea : area ≤ Real.pi * (S / ((n : ℝ) - 1)) ^ ((2 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ))) : L ^ 2 ≤ 2 * discSepCoefficient n S (w₀ * (1 - w₀))
declarations.docstring: Substituting the area bound into the Bergman segment inequality gives the paper's display (5). This is the step where the chart radius `q` is eliminated in favour of `(S² + S + p)/(S² - S + p)`.

declarations.name: discSep_length_lt_two
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_length_lt_two {M L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hbound : L ^ 2 ≤ 2 * M) (hM : M < 2) : L < 2
declarations.docstring: The consumer of display (6): a squared bound by twice a coefficient below two forces the connector to be shorter than two.

declarations.name: discSep_separation_long
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_separation_long (hext : DiscSepBergmanArea) {P : ℂ[X]} {n : ℕ} {w₀ S : ℝ} (hyp : DiscSepNormalised P n w₀ S) : ∃ (Z : ℝ → ℂ) (L : ℝ), DiscSepConnector P Z L ∧ P.eval (Z (-1)) = 0 ∧ P.eval (Z 1) = 0 ∧ Z (-1) ≠ Z 1 ∧ (∀ ξ ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, ‖P.eval (Z ξ)‖ ≤ 1) ∧ L ^ 2 ≤ 2 * discSepCoefficient n S (w₀ * (1 - w₀)) ∧ (discSepCoefficient n S (w₀ * (1 - w₀)) < 2 → L < 2)
declarations.docstring: **`res:critical-value-separation`, long record (`core.tex` line 1341).** Conditional on the classical chain `DiscSepBergmanArea`, a normalised separation datum yields one injective connector `Z` obtained by continuing the two local solutions of `P(Z ξ) = 1 - ξ²` with `Z 0 = 0` along the real segment; its endpoints are distinct roots of `P`; it lies in `{|P| ≤ 1}`; its length obeys display (5); and, whenever display (6) holds, it is shorter than `2`.

declarations.name: discSepNormalise
declarations.signature: def discSepNormalise (f : ℂ[X]) (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (v : ℂ) : ℂ[X]
declarations.docstring: The paper's normalisation, as an actual polynomial.

declarations.name: discSepNormalise_eval
declarations.signature: theorem discSepNormalise_eval (f : ℂ[X]) (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (v w : ℂ) : (discSepNormalise f c r v).eval w = f.eval ((r : ℂ) * w + c) * v⁻¹

declarations.name: discSepNormalise_derivative
declarations.signature: theorem discSepNormalise_derivative (f : ℂ[X]) (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (v : ℂ) : (discSepNormalise f c r v).derivative = discSepNormalise f.derivative c r (v * (r : ℂ)⁻¹)
declarations.docstring: Differentiating the normalisation renormalises it: the same construction on `f'`, with `v` replaced by `v/r`.

declarations.name: discSepNormalise_natDegree
declarations.signature: theorem discSepNormalise_natDegree {f : ℂ[X]} {c v : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) (hv : v ≠ 0) (hf : f ≠ 0) : (discSepNormalise f c r v).natDegree = f.natDegree

declarations.name: discSepNormalise_leadingCoeff
declarations.signature: theorem discSepNormalise_leadingCoeff {f : ℂ[X]} {c v : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) (hv : v ≠ 0) : (discSepNormalise f c r v).leadingCoeff = f.leadingCoeff * (r : ℂ) ^ f.natDegree * v⁻¹

declarations.name: discSepNormalise_spec
declarations.signature: theorem discSepNormalise_spec {f : ℂ[X]} {n : ℕ} {c v : ℂ} {r w₀ S : ℝ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hdeg : f.natDegree = n) (hmonic : f.Monic) (hcrit : f.derivative.eval c = 0) (hsimple : f.derivative.derivative.eval c ≠ 0) (hvdef : v = f.eval c) (hv : v ≠ 0) (hrdef : r = ‖v‖ ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) (hw₀ : 0 ≤ w₀) (hw₁ : w₀ ≤ 1) (hS : max w₀ (1 - w₀) < S) (hsep : ∀ d : ℂ, d ≠ c → f.derivative.eval d = 0 → S ≤ ‖f.eval d / v - (w₀ : ℂ)‖) : DiscSepNormalised (discSepNormalise f c r v) n w₀ S
declarations.docstring: The construction satisfies every hypothesis of `DiscSepNormalised` when `f` is monic of degree `n ≥ 3`, `c` is a simple critical point, `v = f(c) ≠ 0` and `r = |v|^{1/n}`.

declarations.name: discSep_transport
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_transport {f P : ℂ[X]} {c v : ℂ} {r L : ℝ} {Z : ℝ → ℂ} (hr : 0 < r) (hv : v ≠ 0) (hP : ∀ w : ℂ, P.eval w = f.eval ((r : ℂ) * w + c) * v⁻¹) (hZ : DiscSepConnector P Z L) : ∃ γ : ℝ → ℂ, ContinuousOn γ (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) ∧ γ (-1) ≠ γ 1 ∧ f.eval (γ (-1)) = 0 ∧ f.eval (γ 1) = 0 ∧ (∀ ξ ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, ‖f.eval (γ ξ)‖ ≤ ‖v‖) ∧ BoundedVariationOn γ (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) ∧ eVariationOn γ (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (r * L)
declarations.docstring: Scaling the normalised connector by `z = c + r w`. This is the paper's closing step: the length is multiplied by `r`, the level `{|P| ≤ 1}` becomes `{|f| ≤ |v|}`, and the endpoints stay distinct roots.

declarations.name: discSep_separation_short
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_separation_short (hext : DiscSepBergmanArea) {f : ℂ[X]} {n : ℕ} {c : ℂ} {w₀ S : ℝ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hdeg : f.natDegree = n) (hmonic : f.Monic) (hcrit : f.derivative.eval c = 0) (hsimple : f.derivative.derivative.eval c ≠ 0) (hv : f.eval c ≠ 0) (hw₀ : 0 ≤ w₀) (hw₁ : w₀ ≤ 1) (hS : max w₀ (1 - w₀) < S) (hsep : ∀ d : ℂ, d ≠ c → f.derivative.eval d = 0 → S ≤ ‖f.eval d / f.eval c - (w₀ : ℂ)‖) : ∃ (a b : ℂ) (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (Lf : ℝ), a ≠ b ∧ f.eval a = 0 ∧ f.eval b = 0 ∧ ContinuousOn γ (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) ∧ γ (-1) = a ∧ γ 1 = b ∧ (∀ ξ ∈ Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, ‖f.eval (γ ξ)‖ ≤ ‖f.eval c‖) ∧ BoundedVariationOn γ (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) ∧ 0 ≤ Lf ∧ eVariationOn γ (Set.Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal Lf ∧
declarations.docstring: **`res:critical-value-separation`, short note (`erdos-1041-lemniscate-newton-flow.tex` line 653).** Conditional on `DiscSepBergmanArea`: with `f` monic of degree `n ≥ 3`, `c` a simple critical point, `v = f(c) ≠ 0`, `w₀ ∈ [0,1]`, `S > max(w₀, 1-w₀)` and `|f(d)/v - w₀| ≥ S` at every other critical point `d`, two distinct roots of `f` are joined inside `{|f| ≤ |v|}` by a rectifiable curve `Γ` with `length(Γ)² ≤ 2 |v|^{2/n} (S/(n-1))^{2/n} log((S²+S+p)/(S²-S+p))`, `p = w₀(1-w₀)`.

declarations.name: discSep_ratio_le_branch
declarations.signature: theorem discSep_ratio_le_branch {S p : ℝ} (hS : 1 < S) (hp : 0 ≤ p) : (S ^ 2 + S + p) / (S ^ 2 - S + p) ≤ (S + 1) / (S - 1)
declarations.docstring: For `S > 1` and `p ≥ 0`, the centre parameter only lowers the ratio.

declarations.name: discSep_branch_le_seven
declarations.docstring: The branch ratio is at most `7` once `S ≥ 4/3`.

declarations.name: discSepCoefficient_lt_two
declarations.signature: theorem discSepCoefficient_lt_two {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {S p : ℝ} (hS : 4 / 3 ≤ S) (hS2 : S ≤ 2) (hp0 : 0 ≤ p) : discSepCoefficient n S p < 2
declarations.docstring: **First clause of `res:critical-value-thresholds`.** The paper's display (6) holds for every degree `n ≥ 3`, every centre parameter `p ≥ 0` (in particular `p = w₀(1-w₀)` with `w₀ ∈ [0,1]`), and every radius `4/3 ≤ S ≤ 2`.

declarations.name: discSepCoefficient_three_six_fifths
declarations.docstring: **The degree-three branch-centred constant** of the short note's corollary: at `w₀ = 1` (so `p = 0`) the radius `6/5` already works, because `(3/5)^{2/3} log 11 < 2`.

declarations.name: discSep_uniform_radius

declarations.signature: theorem circle_slice_packing {k : ℕ} (d θ : Fin k → ℝ) (hd : ∀ j, 0 < d j) {D : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) (hsep : ∀ i j : Fin k, i ≠ j → D ≤ dist (polar (d i) (θ i)) (polar (d j) (θ j))) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) : ∑ j, sliceHalfAngle D (d j) r ≤ π
declarations.docstring: **`res:circle-slice-packing`** (`paper/reasoning-parts/erdos1041/core.tex`, line 378), unconditionally, in the hyperbolic plane. `k` points of the hyperbolic plane are given in geodesic polar coordinates `(d_j, θ_j)` about the centre (`exists_polar`: every point has such coordinates). Assuming `(eq:lc-separation)`, i.e. that the points are pairwise at hyperbolic distance at least `D`, the slice half-angles `w(d_j, r)` sum to at most `π` for every radius `r > 0`. No external hypothesis: the hyperbolic law of cosines is `cosh_dist_polar`, proved above.

declarations.name: dual_arity_floor
declarations.signature: theorem dual_arity_floor {k : ℕ} (d θ : Fin k → ℝ) (hd : ∀ j, 0 < d j) {D : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) (hsep : ∀ i j : Fin k, i ≠ j → D ≤ dist (polar (d i) (θ i)) (polar (d j) (θ j))) {p : ℕ} (r σ : Fin p → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i) (hσ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ σ i) {a x dlow U : ℝ} (hdlow : 0 < dlow) (hdlowval : lam dlow = delta a / 2) (hrad : ∀ j, lam (d j) ≤ delta a / 2) (hbudget : x ≤ ∑ j, lam (d j)) (hU : ∀ s : ℝ, dlow ≤ s → lam s - ∑ i, σ i * sliceHalfAngle D s (r i) ≤ U) (hUpos : 0 < U) : (x - π * ∑ i, σ i) / U ≤ (k : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **`res:dual-arity-floor`** (`paper/reasoning-parts/erdos1041/core.tex`, line 401), in the hyperbolic plane with no law-of-cosines hypothesis. Hypotheses are exactly the paper's: `(eq:lc-separation)` (`hsep`), and the two consequences `(eq:lc-radius-and-budget)` of the standing failure hypothesis, namely the radius bound `λ(d_j) ≤ δ(a)/2` (`hrad`, with `hdlowval : λ(d_low(a)) = δ(a)/2`) and the budget `∑_j λ(d_j) ≥ x` (`hbudget`). Nonnegative weights `σ_i` at radii `r_i > 0` with positive deficit `U` then force `k ≥ (x - πΣ)/U`. Here `U` is any upper bound for the paper's supremand on `[d_low(a), ∞)`; `dual_arity_floor_sup` is the form with `U` the supremum.

declarations.name: dual_arity_floor_sup
declarations.signature: theorem dual_arity_floor_sup {k : ℕ} (d θ : Fin k → ℝ) (hd : ∀ j, 0 < d j) {D : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) (hsep : ∀ i j : Fin k, i ≠ j → D ≤ dist (polar (d i) (θ i)) (polar (d j) (θ j))) {p : ℕ} (r σ : Fin p → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i) (hσ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ σ i) {a x dlow U : ℝ} (hdlow : 0 < dlow) (hdlowval : lam dlow = delta a / 2) (hrad : ∀ j, lam (d j) ≤ delta a / 2) (hbudget : x ≤ ∑ j, lam (d j)) (hU : IsLUB {y : ℝ | ∃ s : ℝ, dlow ≤ s ∧ y = lam s - ∑ i, σ i * sliceHalfAngle D s (r i)} U) (hUpos : 0 < U) : (x - π * ∑ i, σ i) / U ≤ (k : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: `res:dual-arity-floor` with `U` given exactly as the paper's supremum, and with no law-of-cosines hypothesis.

declarations.docstring: The closing `O(√δ)` sentence in the paper's own coordinate. At a simple critical point the local model is `f(z) - f(c) = A (z - c)^2` with `A = f''(c)/2 ≠ 0`; a value at distance `‖w‖` from the critical value therefore sits at spatial distance `√(‖w‖/‖A‖) = √(2‖w‖/‖f''(c)‖)` from the critical point, which is the asserted `O(√δ)` saddle scale.

declarations.name: orlicz_currency
declarations.signature: theorem orlicz_currency : (Tendsto orliczKernel (𝓝[≠] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 0) ∧ orliczKernel 0 = 0) ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r ≤ 1 → mergerIntegral k r = k * Phi (Real.log (1 / r) / k)) ∧ StrictMonoOn Phi (Ioi (0 : ℝ)) ∧ MonotoneOn Phi (Ioi (0 : ℝ)) ∧ StrictConvexOn ℝ (Ioi (0 : ℝ)) Phi ∧ Tendsto (fun x => Phi x / x) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 0) ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ r < 1 ∧ mergerIntegral k r < c * (Real.log (1 / r) / k)) ∧ ¬ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < 1 → c * (Real.log (1 / r) / k) ≤ mergerIntegral k r

declarations.name: ofReal_dist_le_hausdorffMeasure

declarations.name: tail_identity
declarations.signature: theorem tail_identity {a b c : ℂ} (w : Fin 5 → ℂ) (hf : ∀ z, value a b c z = rootProduct w z) (i : Fin 5) : b * w i + c = -(w i ^ 4 * (w i + a))

declarations.name: tail_norm_of_leading_zero

declarations.name: two_tails_closedDisc_of_ne_zero

declarations.docstring: Closed-disc form of `PaperPrimitiveCompletionR10.two_tails_of_rootProduct` for a nonzero leading tail coefficient. The moment route only ever needs `‖w i‖ ≤ 1`, so the open-disc hypothesis of the existing declaration is relaxed here without weakening the strict conclusion.

declarations.name: tail_le_one_and_eq_iff_of_leading_zero

declarations.name: primitive_quintic_two_tail
declarations.signature: theorem primitive_quintic_two_tail (a b c : ℂ) (w : Fin 5 → ℂ) (hf : ∀ z, value a b c z = rootProduct w z) : ((∀ i, ‖w i‖ ≤ 1) → (∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b * w i + c‖ ≤ 1 ∧ ‖b * w j + c‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (a ≠ 0 → ∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b * w i + c‖ < 1 ∧ ‖b * w j + c‖ < 1) ∧ (a = 0 → ∀ i : Fin 5, ‖b * w i + c‖ ≤ 1 ∧ (‖b * w i + c‖ = 1 ↔ ‖w i‖ = 1))) ∧ ((∀ i, ‖w i‖ < 1) → ∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b * w i + c‖ < 1 ∧ ‖b * w j + c‖ < 1 ∧ ConnectedBelow (value a b c) 1 2 (w i) (w j) ∧ (w i ≠ w j → HubBelow (value a b c) 1 2 (w i) 0 (w j)) ∧ (w i = w j → (∀ t : ℝ, ‖value a b c ((fun _ : ℝ => w i) t)‖ < 1) ∧
declarations.docstring: **The long-record theorem `thm:primitive-quintic-two-tail`.** For `p(z) = z ^ 5 + a z ^ 4 + b z + c` with five zero occurrences `w 0, …, w 4`: * if every occurrence lies in the closed unit disc, then two distinct indices satisfy `‖b * w i + c‖ ≤ 1`; when `a ≠ 0` two indices can be chosen with strict inequalities; and when `a = 0` every index satisfies the bound, with equality exactly at `‖w i‖ = 1`; * if every occurrence lies in the open unit disc, then two zero occurrences are joined inside `{|p| < 1}` by a rectifiable curve of variation below `2`, realised by the two radial spokes through `0` when the two occurrences are distinct points and by the constant path when they coincide.

declarations.name: primitive_quintic_two_tail_of_polynomial
declarations.signature: theorem primitive_quintic_two_tail_of_polynomial (p : ℂ[X]) (hp : p.Monic) (hd : p.natDegree = 5) (a b c : ℂ) (hvalue : ∀ z, p.eval z = value a b c z) : ∃ w : Fin 5 → ℂ, (∀ z, p.eval z = rootProduct w z) ∧ ((∀ i, ‖w i‖ ≤ 1) → (∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b * w i + c‖ ≤ 1 ∧ ‖b * w j + c‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (a ≠ 0 → ∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b * w i + c‖ < 1 ∧ ‖b * w j + c‖ < 1) ∧ (a = 0 → ∀ i : Fin 5, ‖b * w i + c‖ ≤ 1 ∧ (‖b * w i + c‖ = 1 ↔ ‖w i‖ = 1))) ∧ ((∀ i, ‖w i‖ < 1) → ∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b * w i + c‖ < 1 ∧ ‖b * w j + c‖ < 1 ∧ ConnectedBelow (value a b c) 1 2 (w i) (w j) ∧ (w i ≠ w j → HubBelow (value a b c) 1 2 (w i) 0 (w j)) ∧
declarations.docstring: The same theorem reached from the polynomial itself: the five zero occurrences exist by the fundamental theorem of algebra, so the hypothesis `hf` above is never vacuous.

declarations.name: ValueSeparatedAtCentre
declarations.signature: def ValueSeparatedAtCentre (f : ℂ[X]) (c : ℂ) (w₀ S : ℝ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The paper's normalised critical-value separation at a real centre `w₀`: every OTHER critical point `d` satisfies `|f(d)/f(c) - w₀| ≥ S`. For `w₀ = 1` this is `ConnectorR18.ValueSeparatedAt`.

declarations.name: separationCoefficient
declarations.signature: def separationCoefficient (n : ℕ) (S p : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The right side of the paper's displayed bound `eq:disk-family-length`, without the `2|v|^{2/n}` prefactor: `(S/(n-1))^{2/n} log((S² + S + p)/(S² - S + p))`.

declarations.name: CriticalValueSeparationTheorem
declarations.docstring: **The external analytic input**: the paper's Theorem `res:critical-value-separation` (separation of one simple critical value). `f` monic of degree `n ≥ 3`, `c` a simple critical point with `v = f(c) ≠ 0`, `w₀ ∈ [0,1]`, `S > max(w₀, 1-w₀)`, and every other critical point `d` obeying `|f(d)/v - w₀| ≥ S`; then two distinct roots are joined inside `{|f| ≤ |v|}` by a curve `Γ` with `length(Γ)² ≤ 2|v|^{2/n}(S/(n-1))^{2/n} log((S²+S+p)/(S²-S+p))`, `p = w₀(1-w₀)`.

declarations.name: ratio_le_seven
declarations.docstring: The logarithmic ratio at `S = 4/3` is at most `7` for every `p ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: separationCoefficient_lt_two
declarations.signature: theorem separationCoefficient_lt_two {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 ≤ p) : separationCoefficient n (4 / 3) p < 2
declarations.docstring: **The corollary's numerical threshold.** `separationCoefficient n (4/3) p < 2` for every degree `n ≥ 3` and `p ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: squared_bound_lt_four
declarations.signature: theorem squared_bound_lt_four {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {v p : ℝ} (hv0 : 0 < v) (hv1 : v < 1) (hp : 0 ≤ p) : 2 * v ^ ((2 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)) * separationCoefficient n (4 / 3) p < 4
declarations.docstring: The whole squared bound at `S = 4/3` stays below `4` once `|v| < 1`.

declarations.name: connectedBelow_of_connectedAtMost
declarations.signature: theorem connectedBelow_of_connectedAtMost {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R L R' L' : ℝ} {a b : ℂ} (h : PaperAnalyticTargets.ConnectedAtMost f R L a b) (hR : R < R') (hL : L < L') (hL0 : 0 ≤ L) : PaperCurve.ConnectedBelow f R' L' a b

declarations.name: separation_parent
declarations.signature: theorem separation_parent (hSep : CriticalValueSeparationTheorem) {f : ℂ[X]} {c : ℂ} {w₀ S : ℝ} (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : 3 ≤ f.natDegree) (hroots : PaperAnalyticTargets.RootsInOpenUnitDisc f) (hcrit : f.derivative.eval c = 0) (hsimple : f.derivative.derivative.eval c ≠ 0) (hv0 : f.eval c ≠ 0) (hv1 : ‖f.eval c‖ < 1) (hw0 : 0 ≤ w₀) (hw1 : w₀ ≤ 1) (hS : 4 / 3 ≤ S) (hsep : ValueSeparatedAtCentre f c w₀ S) : PaperAnalyticTargets.HasDistinctConnection f 1 2
declarations.docstring: **`res:separation-parent`, modulo the named external separation theorem.** `f` monic of degree `n ≥ 3` with all roots in the open unit disc, `c` a simple critical point with `0 < |f(c)| < 1`, and a real centre `w₀ ∈ [0,1]` admitting a radius `S ≥ 4/3` with `|f(d)/f(c) - w₀| ≥ S` at every other critical point. Then Erdős Problem #1041 holds for `f`: two distinct roots of `f` are joined inside `{|f| < 1}` by a rectifiable curve of length strictly below `2`.

declarations.name: exp_stoppingTime_lt

declarations.name: connectedAtMost_mono

declarations.name: connectedAtMost_symm
declarations.signature: theorem connectedAtMost_symm {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R L : ℝ} {a b : ℂ} (h : ConnectedAtMost f R L a b) : ConnectedAtMost f R L b a
declarations.docstring: Reversing a closed-sublevel connector.

declarations.name: connectedAtMost_trans
declarations.signature: theorem connectedAtMost_trans {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R L₁ L₂ : ℝ} {a c b : ℂ} (h₁ : ConnectedAtMost f R L₁ a c) (h₂ : ConnectedAtMost f R L₂ c b) (hL₁ : 0 ≤ L₁) (hL₂ : 0 ≤ L₂) : ConnectedAtMost f R (L₁ + L₂) a b
declarations.docstring: **Concatenation.** The paper's last step: "Concatenating the two paths gives length at most ...". The extended variation of the concatenation is the sum of the two variations by `eVariationOn.union`.

declarations.name: half_perimeter_selection
declarations.signature: theorem half_perimeter_selection {du dv lenA1 lenA2 lenA' uv H : ℝ} (hsplit : du + dv = uv) (hchord : uv ≤ lenA') (htotal : lenA1 + lenA2 + lenA' ≤ H) : min (du + lenA1) (dv + lenA2) ≤ H / 2
declarations.docstring: **The elementary selection behind the half-perimeter lemma.** The paper takes a line through `a` meeting `U` in an interval whose closure is `[u,v]`, splits `∂U` into the two arcs `A` (containing `c`) and `A'` from `u` to `v`, and writes the two candidate paths `a → u → c` and `a → v → c`. With `du + dv = |u - v|` (because `a` lies on `[u,v]`), `|u - v| ≤ length A'`, and `length A + length A' ≤ H¹(∂U)`, where `length A = lenA1 + lenA2` splits `A` at `c`, one of the two paths has length at most `H¹(∂U)/2`.

declarations.name: HalfPerimeterJoin
declarations.signature: def HalfPerimeterJoin (f : ℂ → ℂ) (R : ℝ) (U : Set ℂ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The Jordan-domain half-perimeter property of a component `U` of a closed sublevel set: any interior point is joined to any boundary point, inside the sublevel set `{|f| ≤ R}`, by a rectifiable path of length at most half of `H¹(∂U)`. The paper calls this elementary; its proof selects one of the two boundary arcs of a Jordan curve, which needs the Jordan curve theorem. Mathlib v4.29.1 has no Jordan curve theorem. `connectedAtMost_half_perimeter` below derives this property from the arc datum the Jordan curve supplies, so the only external part is the existence of that datum.

declarations.name: JordanArcDatum
declarations.signature: def JordanArcDatum (f : ℂ → ℂ) (R H : ℝ) (a c : ℂ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The datum the Jordan curve theorem supplies at an interior point `a` and a boundary point `c` of a rectifiable Jordan domain `U` with `H¹(∂U) ≤ H`: a chord `[u,v]` of `U` through `a` (so `|a - u| + |a - v| = |u - v|`, and both spokes lie in `closure U`), the two sub-arcs of the boundary arc `A` from `u` and from `v` to `c`, and the complementary boundary arc `A'`, which is at least as long as the chord, with `length A + length A' ≤ H`.

declarations.name: connectedAtMost_half_perimeter
declarations.signature: theorem connectedAtMost_half_perimeter {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R H : ℝ} {a c : ℂ} (h : JordanArcDatum f R H a c) : ConnectedAtMost f R (H / 2) a c
declarations.docstring: **The half-perimeter lemma, from the Jordan arc datum.** The two candidate paths `a → u → c` and `a → v → c` are built by concatenation and one of them has length at most `H/2` by `half_perimeter_selection`.

declarations.docstring: Three scalar values of a factorisation determine the cubic Vieta data.

declarations.name: cubic_root_count
declarations.docstring: B5's exact previously analytic root-count target, supplied algebraically.

declarations.name: affine
declarations.signature: def affine (a v : ℂ) (t : ℝ) : ℂ
declarations.docstring: An affine parametrisation, defined on the whole real line.

declarations.name: affine_dist
declarations.signature: theorem affine_dist (a v : ℂ) (s t : ℝ) : dist (affine a v s) (affine a v t) = dist s t * ‖v‖

declarations.name: affine_lipschitz
declarations.signature: theorem affine_lipschitz (a v : ℂ) : LipschitzWith ‖v‖₊ (affine a v)

declarations.name: affine_unit_variation
declarations.signature: theorem affine_unit_variation (a v : ℂ) (s : ℝ) : eVariationOn (affine a v) (Icc s (s + 1)) = (‖v‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞)
declarations.docstring: The variation of an affine curve on a unit interval is its speed.

declarations.name: hub
declarations.signature: def hub (a h b : ℂ) (t : ℝ) : ℂ
declarations.docstring: A continuous broken line `a → h → b`, with no division by a segment length.

declarations.name: hub_continuous
declarations.signature: theorem hub_continuous (a h b : ℂ) : Continuous (hub a h b)

declarations.name: hub_zero
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem hub_zero (a h b : ℂ) : hub a h b 0 = a

declarations.name: hub_one
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem hub_one (a h b : ℂ) : hub a h b 1 = h

declarations.name: hub_two
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem hub_two (a h b : ℂ) : hub a h b 2 = b

declarations.name: hub_eq_first
declarations.signature: theorem hub_eq_first {a h b : ℂ} {t : ℝ} (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) : hub a h b t = affine a (h - a) t

declarations.name: hub_eq_second
declarations.signature: theorem hub_eq_second {a h b : ℂ} {t : ℝ} (ht1 : 1 ≤ t) : hub a h b t = affine (2 * h - b) (b - h) t

declarations.name: hub_variation
declarations.signature: theorem hub_variation (a h b : ℂ) : eVariationOn (hub a h b) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 2) = (‖h - a‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) + (‖b - h‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞)
declarations.docstring: Both segments have their actual variation, and variations add at the hub.

declarations.name: hub_variation_ofReal
declarations.signature: theorem hub_variation_ofReal (a h b : ℂ) : eVariationOn (hub a h b) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 2) = ENNReal.ofReal (‖h - a‖ + ‖b - h‖)

declarations.name: hub_rectifiable
declarations.signature: theorem hub_rectifiable (a h b : ℂ) : BoundedVariationOn (hub a h b) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 2)

declarations.name: hub_length
declarations.signature: theorem hub_length (a h b : ℂ) : (eVariationOn (hub a h b) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 2)).toReal = ‖h - a‖ + ‖b - h‖

declarations.name: hub_mem
declarations.signature: theorem hub_mem {a h b : ℂ} {S : Set ℂ} (ha : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 → h + (u : ℂ) * (a - h) ∈ S) (hb : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 → h + (u : ℂ) * (b - h) ∈ S) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 2) : hub a h b t ∈ S
declarations.docstring: Containment is transported from the two actual spokes, not from an endpoint-only condition.

declarations.name: ConnectedBelow
declarations.signature: def ConnectedBelow (f : ℂ → ℂ) (R L : ℝ) (a b : ℂ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The geometric conclusion used by the paper: a continuous rectifiable curve with specified endpoints, containment at every parameter, and a strict variation bound.

declarations.name: connectedBelow_of_spokes
declarations.signature: theorem connectedBelow_of_spokes {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R L : ℝ} {a h b : ℂ} (ha : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 → ‖f (h + (u : ℂ) * (a - h))‖ < R) (hb : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 → ‖f (h + (u : ℂ) * (b - h))‖ < R) (hL : ‖h - a‖ + ‖b - h‖ < L) : ConnectedBelow f R L a b

declarations.name: HubBelow
declarations.signature: def HubBelow (f : ℂ → ℂ) (R L : ℝ) (a h b : ℂ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: A specified two-segment connector, rather than merely existence of some rectifiable curve. The public `hub` fixes its image and parametrisation.

declarations.name: hubBelow_of_spokes
declarations.signature: theorem hubBelow_of_spokes {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R L : ℝ} {a h b : ℂ} (ha : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 → ‖f (h + (u : ℂ) * (a - h))‖ < R) (hb : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 → ‖f (h + (u : ℂ) * (b - h))‖ < R) (hL : ‖h - a‖ + ‖b - h‖ < L) : HubBelow f R L a h b

declarations.name: HubBelow.connectedBelow
declarations.signature: theorem HubBelow.connectedBelow {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R L : ℝ} {a h b : ℂ} (H : HubBelow f R L a h b) : ConnectedBelow f R L a b

declarations.name: connectedBelow_refl
declarations.signature: theorem connectedBelow_refl {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R L : ℝ} {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖f a‖ < R) (hL : 0 < L) : ConnectedBelow f R L a a
declarations.docstring: A repeated root occurrence is dealt with by an actual constant curve.

declarations.name: affine_lipschitz
declarations.signature: theorem affine_lipschitz (h c : ℂ) : LipschitzWith ‖c‖₊ (fun z : ℂ => h + c * z)
declarations.docstring: The spatial affine map has exactly the expected Lipschitz constant.

declarations.name: transported_variation_le
declarations.signature: theorem transported_variation_le (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (s : Set ℝ) (h c : ℂ) : eVariationOn (fun t => h + c * γ t) s ≤ (‖c‖₊ : ℝ≥0∞) * eVariationOn γ s
declarations.docstring: Variation is controlled for every curve, with no differentiability assumption and no replacement of length by an endpoint distance.

declarations.name: connectedBelow_affine
declarations.signature: theorem connectedBelow_affine {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {R L : ℝ} {a b h c d : ℂ} (hc : c ≠ 0) (hd : d ≠ 0) (hid : ∀ z : ℂ, f (h + c * z) = d * g z) (H : ConnectedBelow g R L a b) : ConnectedBelow f (‖d‖ * R) (‖c‖ * L) (h + c * a) (h + c * b)
declarations.docstring: Transport both the level and the length. Both nonzero hypotheses are necessary for the strict conclusion with the scaled thresholds.

declarations.name: no_strict_zero_level
declarations.signature: theorem no_strict_zero_level (f : ℂ → ℂ) (a b : ℂ) (L : ℝ) : ¬ ConnectedBelow f 0 L a b
declarations.docstring: Strict containment cannot be obtained by multiplying a threshold by zero. Repeated occurrences are handled by the separate constant-curve constructor, not by a singular application of affine transport.

declarations.name: lower_moment
declarations.signature: theorem lower_moment {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (x : ι → ℝ) (hx : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) {α β : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hβ : 0 ≤ β) (hβα : β ≤ α) (H : ∑ i, x i ^ α ≤ (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)) : ∑ i, x i ^ β ≤ (Fintype.card ι : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A cardinality-normalised nonnegative moment bound passes to lower powers.

declarations.name: critical_moment_lowering
declarations.signature: theorem critical_moment_lowering {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) (x : Fin m → ℝ) (hx : ∀ i, 0 ≤ x i) (H : ∑ i, x i ^ (2 / (m : ℝ)) ≤ (m : ℝ)) : ∑ i, x i ^ (1 / ((m : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ (m : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The squared free-point/critical-value moment implies the 1/n moment, provided the polynomial has already supplied that squared moment.

declarations.name: weighted_first_of_second
declarations.signature: theorem weighted_first_of_second {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (w x : ι → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (hwsum : ∑ i, w i = 1) (H : ∑ i, w i * x i ^ 2 ≤ 1) : ∑ i, w i * x i ≤ 1
declarations.docstring: Weighted quadratic control implies weighted first-moment control. The argument is finite and uses the exact tangent inequality at one.

declarations.name: value_decay_at_continuous_endpoints
declarations.signature: theorem value_decay_at_continuous_endpoints {v : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hcont : ContinuousOn v (Icc a b)) (hderiv : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt v (-v t) t) : v b = (Real.exp (a - b) : ℂ) * v a
declarations.docstring: Exponential value decay with differentiability only in the interior. The endpoint continuity is stated rather than hidden in a trajectory type.

declarations.name: newton_endpoint_samePositiveRay
declarations.signature: theorem newton_endpoint_samePositiveRay {f f' : ℂ → ℂ} {z : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hcont : ContinuousOn (fun t => f (z t)) (Icc a b)) (hf : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (f' (z t)) (z t)) (hz : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt z (newtonFlowVector (f (z t)) (f' (z t))) t) (hnoncritical : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, f' (z t) ≠ 0) : SamePositiveRay (f (z a)) (f (z b))
declarations.docstring: An existing Newton trajectory with possibly critical continuous endpoints still has values on one positive ray. Endpoints may have zero value: the relation then forces both values to be zero.

declarations.name: newton_endpoint_samePositiveRay_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem newton_endpoint_samePositiveRay_of_le {f f' : ℂ → ℂ} {z : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hcont : ContinuousOn (fun t => f (z t)) (Icc a b)) (hf : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (f' (z t)) (z t)) (hz : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt z (newtonFlowVector (f (z t)) (f' (z t))) t) (hnoncritical : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, f' (z t) ≠ 0) : SamePositiveRay (f (z a)) (f (z b))
declarations.docstring: Include the degenerate compact interval as well: coincident endpoint values satisfy the positive-ray relation with multiplier one.

declarations.name: no_finite_connection_of_distinct_value_rays
declarations.signature: theorem no_finite_connection_of_distinct_value_rays {f f' : ℂ → ℂ} {z : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hcont : ContinuousOn (fun t => f (z t)) (Icc a b)) (hf : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (f' (z t)) (z t)) (hz : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt z (newtonFlowVector (f (z t)) (f' (z t))) t) (hnoncritical : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b, f' (z t) ≠ 0) (hrays : ¬ SamePositiveRay (f (z a)) (f (z b))) : False
declarations.docstring: The advertised obstruction to a finite saddle-to-saddle connection, with all trajectory and endpoint premises explicit.

declarations.name: rootProduct
declarations.signature: def rootProduct (w : Fin 5 → ℂ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ
declarations.docstring: Occurrences, not necessarily different locations.

declarations.name: list_length_five
declarations.signature: private lemma list_length_five {l : List ℂ} (hl : l.length = 5) : ∃ a b c d e : ℂ, l = [a, b, c, d, e]

declarations.name: monic_quintic_enumeration
declarations.signature: theorem monic_quintic_enumeration (p : ℂ[X]) (hp : p.Monic) (hd : p.natDegree = 5) : ∃ w : Fin 5 → ℂ, ∀ z : ℂ, p.eval z = rootProduct w z
declarations.docstring: No factorisation is imposed on the final polynomial theorem.

declarations.name: newton_moments
declarations.signature: theorem newton_moments {a b c : ℂ} (w : Fin 5 → ℂ) (hf : ∀ z, value a b c z = rootProduct w z) : (∑ i, w i) = -a ∧ (∑ i, w i ^ 2) = a ^ 2 ∧ (∑ i, w i ^ 3) = -a ^ 3
declarations.docstring: The first three power sums follow from the missing cubic and quadratic coefficients. The interpolation weights are recorded in certificates/.

declarations.name: norm_sq_coords
declarations.signature: private lemma norm_sq_coords (z : ℂ) : ‖z‖ ^ 2 = z.re ^ 2 + z.im ^ 2

declarations.name: real_cube
declarations.signature: private lemma real_cube (z : ℂ) : (z ^ 3).re = 4 * z.re ^ 3 - 3 * ‖z‖ ^ 2 * z.re

declarations.name: norm_add_real_sq
declarations.signature: private lemma norm_add_real_sq (z : ℂ) (r : ℝ) : ‖z + (r : ℂ)‖ ^ 2 = ‖z‖ ^ 2 + r ^ 2 + 2 * r * z.re

declarations.name: two_tails_of_rootProduct
declarations.signature: theorem two_tails_of_rootProduct {a b c : ℂ} (w : Fin 5 → ℂ) (hf : ∀ z, value a b c z = rootProduct w z) (hw : ∀ i, ‖w i‖ < 1) : ∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b * w i + c‖ < 1 ∧ ‖b * w j + c‖ < 1
declarations.docstring: Complete two-tail selector under the actual polynomial factorisation. The normalised moments, the coefficient bound and the rotation are all derived.

declarations.name: complete_primitive_quintic
declarations.signature: theorem complete_primitive_quintic (p : ℂ[X]) (hp : p.Monic) (hd : p.natDegree = 5) (a b c : ℂ) (hvalue : ∀ z, p.eval z = value a b c z) (hdisk : ∀ z, p.eval z = 0 → ‖z‖ < 1) : ∃ w : Fin 5 → ℂ, (∀ z, p.eval z = rootProduct w z) ∧ ∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b*w i+c‖ < 1 ∧ ‖b*w j+c‖ < 1 ∧ ConnectedBelow p.eval 1 2 (w i) (w j) ∧ (w i ≠ w j → HubBelow p.eval 1 2 (w i) 0 (w j)) ∧ (w i = w j → (∀ t : ℝ, ‖p.eval ((fun _ : ℝ => w i) t)‖ < 1) ∧ eVariationOn (fun _ : ℝ => w i) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 2) = 0)
declarations.docstring: End-to-end paper theorem, retaining actual root occurrences and the constant-path alternative. There is no additional selection hypothesis.

declarations.name: product_norm_lt_one
declarations.signature: private theorem product_norm_lt_one {s : Multiset ℂ} (hs : ∀ z ∈ s, ‖z‖ < 1) (hne : s ≠ 0) : ‖s.prod‖ < 1

declarations.name: constant_norm_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem constant_norm_lt_one (p : ℂ[X]) (hp : p.Monic) (hdeg : 0 < p.natDegree) (hdisk : ∀ z : ℂ, p.eval z = 0 → ‖z‖ < 1) : ‖p.eval 0‖ < 1
declarations.docstring: The constant term of any positive-degree monic open-disc-root polynomial.

declarations.name: value
declarations.signature: def value (a b c z : ℂ) : ℂ
declarations.docstring: The precise primitive quintic function.

declarations.name: spoke_of_tail
declarations.signature: theorem spoke_of_tail {a b c w : ℂ} (hroot : value a b c w = 0) (hw : ‖w‖ < 1) (hc : ‖c‖ < 1) (htail : ‖b * w + c‖ < 1) {t : ℝ} (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1) : ‖value a b c ((t : ℂ) * w)‖ < 1
declarations.docstring: A selected tail supplies a whole spoke; no low-coefficient bound is added.

declarations.name: path_of_selected_tails
declarations.signature: theorem path_of_selected_tails (p : ℂ[X]) (hp : p.Monic) (hdeg : p.natDegree = 5) (a b c : ℂ) (hvalue : ∀ z : ℂ, p.eval z = value a b c z) (hdisk : ∀ z : ℂ, p.eval z = 0 → ‖z‖ < 1) (w : Fin 5 → ℂ) (hroots : ∀ i, p.eval (w i) = 0) (hselected : ∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b * w i + c‖ < 1 ∧ ‖b * w j + c‖ < 1) : ∃ i j : Fin 5, i ≠ j ∧ ‖b * w i + c‖ < 1 ∧ ‖b * w j + c‖ < 1 ∧ ConnectedBelow p.eval 1 2 (w i) (w j) ∧ (w i ≠ w j → HubBelow p.eval 1 2 (w i) 0 (w j)) ∧ (w i = w j → (∀ t : ℝ, ‖p.eval ((fun _ : ℝ => w i) t)‖ < 1) ∧ eVariationOn (fun _ : ℝ => w i) (Icc (0 : ℝ) 2) = 0)
declarations.docstring: Once the polynomial moment selector supplies two tails, both distinct location and repeated-occurrence cases have actual rectifiable connections.

declarations.name: radial_fraction_identity
declarations.signature: theorem radial_fraction_identity (z a : ℂ) (hza : z-a ≠ 0) : (2*(z/(z-a)).re-1)*Complex.normSq (z-a) = Complex.normSq z-Complex.normSq a
declarations.docstring: The boundary half-plane estimate before any summation.

declarations.name: product_log_derivative
declarations.signature: theorem product_log_derivative {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → ℂ) (z : ℂ) (hnz : ∀ i ∈ s, z-a i ≠ 0) : (∏ i ∈ s, (X-C (a i))).derivative.eval z / (∏ i ∈ s, (X-C (a i))).eval z = ∑ i ∈ s, (z-a i)⁻¹
declarations.docstring: Exact finite logarithmic derivative; repeated roots are allowed.

declarations.name: polar_scalar_norm
declarations.signature: theorem polar_scalar_norm (n : ℝ) (L : ℂ) (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hL : n ≤ 2*L.re) : ‖(n : ℂ)-L‖ ≤ ‖L‖
declarations.docstring: A half-plane condition is equivalent to the needed scalar norm comparison.

declarations.name: polar_boundary_of_roots
declarations.signature: theorem polar_boundary_of_roots (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → ℂ) (ha : ∀ i, ‖a i‖ ≤ 1) (z : ℂ) (hz : ‖z‖ = 1) : let p : ℂ[X]
declarations.docstring: The actual boundary inequality for a factored polynomial, including boundary roots (the f(z)=0 case is treated without division).

declarations.name: CriticalDiscLocation_target
declarations.docstring: Localisation of the listed critical points, with the paper's exact root-location hypothesis. A proof candidate is in PaperReflectedCompletion.

declarations.name: ReflectedPolarInterior_target
declarations.docstring: The maximum-principle/reflection supplier is separate from the proved boundary inequality. Boundary zeros and root factorisation must be handled when this target is discharged; they are not silently excluded.

declarations.name: reflectedCriticalValue_of_polar
declarations.docstring: The critical-value consumer with explicit analytic inputs. Its full application, without those premises, is in PaperReflectedCompletion.

declarations.name: listed_critical_is_root
declarations.signature: theorem listed_critical_is_root {n : ℕ} {p : ℂ[X]} {c : Fin (n-1) → ℂ} (hc : CriticalEnumeration p c) (j : Fin (n-1)) : p.derivative.eval (c j) = 0

declarations.name: critical_disc_location
declarations.docstring: The exact critical-disc target, including boundary and multiple roots.

declarations.name: polar_boundary
declarations.signature: theorem polar_boundary (n : ℕ) (p : ℂ[X]) (hp : p.Monic) (hdeg : p.natDegree = n) (hroots : RootsInClosedDisc p 0 1) (z : ℂ) (hz : ‖z‖ = 1) : ‖(n : ℂ)*p.eval z-z*p.derivative.eval z‖ ≤ ‖p.derivative.eval z‖
declarations.docstring: Remove the auxiliary root enumeration from the boundary estimate.

declarations.name: reflected_factor_norm
declarations.docstring: Reflection on the unit circle, expressed without division.

declarations.name: regularised_factor_norm
declarations.signature: theorem regularised_factor_norm (x : ℂ) (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ 1) (t : ℝ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) : ‖1-x‖ ≤ ‖(t : ℂ)-x‖
declarations.docstring: Moving the positive real endpoint outward increases distance from any point of the unit disc.

declarations.name: regularised
declarations.signature: def regularised {m : ℕ} (c : Fin m → ℂ) (t : ℝ) : ℂ[X]
declarations.docstring: The regularised reflected denominator.

declarations.name: regularised_eval
declarations.signature: theorem regularised_eval {m : ℕ} (c : Fin m → ℂ) (t : ℝ) (z : ℂ) : (regularised c t).eval z = ∏ k, ((t : ℂ)-conj (c k)*z)

declarations.name: regularised_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem regularised_ne_zero {m : ℕ} (c : Fin m → ℂ) (hc : ∀ k, ‖c k‖ ≤ 1) (t : ℝ) (ht : 1 < t) (z : ℂ) (hz : ‖z‖ ≤ 1) : (regularised c t).eval z ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Zero-freeness on the closed disc, not just its interior.

declarations.name: reflected_product_domination
declarations.signature: theorem reflected_product_domination {m : ℕ} (U : ℂ[X]) (c : Fin m → ℂ) (hc : ∀ k, ‖c k‖ ≤ 1) (K : ℝ) (hK : 0 ≤ K) (hb : ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ = 1 → ‖U.eval z‖ ≤ K*∏ k, ‖1-conj (c k)*z‖) (z : ℂ) (hz : ‖z‖ ≤ 1) : ‖U.eval z‖ ≤ K*∏ k, ‖1-conj (c k)*z‖
declarations.docstring: A closed-disc maximum-modulus comparison allowing boundary zeros in all reflected factors. No root, simplicity or strict-radius assumption.

declarations.name: reflected_polar_interior
declarations.docstring: The complete polar-interior supplier; all its former premises are proved above from the original polynomial hypotheses.

declarations.name: reflected_critical_value
declarations.docstring: B4, against the exact desk target. No new analytic premise.

declarations.name: eval_P
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem eval_P (z : ℂ) : P.eval z = value z

declarations.name: eval_derivative
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem eval_derivative (z : ℂ) : P.derivative.eval z = 3 * z ^ 2 + 3 / 100

declarations.name: eval_second_derivative
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem eval_second_derivative (z : ℂ) : P.derivative.derivative.eval z = 6 * z

declarations.name: critical_factor
declarations.signature: theorem critical_factor (z : ℂ) : P.derivative.eval z = (3 : ℂ) * (z - plus) * (z - minus)

declarations.name: all_critical_points
declarations.signature: theorem all_critical_points (z : ℂ) : P.derivative.eval z = 0 ↔ z = plus ∨ z = minus

declarations.name: critical_points_simple
declarations.signature: theorem critical_points_simple (z : ℂ) (hz : P.derivative.eval z = 0) : P.derivative.derivative.eval z ≠ 0

declarations.name: values_normSq
declarations.signature: theorem values_normSq : Complex.normSq (P.eval plus) = (9 / 16 : ℝ) + 1 / 250000 ∧ Complex.normSq (P.eval minus) = (9 / 16 : ℝ) + 1 / 250000

declarations.name: mu_is_least
declarations.signature: theorem mu_is_least : IsLeast {x : ℝ | ∃ c : ℂ, P.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧ x = ‖P.eval c‖} mu

declarations.name: ratio_norm
declarations.signature: theorem ratio_norm : ‖1 - P.eval minus / P.eval plus‖ = (1 / 250 : ℝ) / mu

declarations.name: strict_separation_bound
declarations.signature: theorem strict_separation_bound : ‖1 - P.eval minus / P.eval plus‖ < (2 / 375 : ℝ)

declarations.name: complete_sep_or_counterexample

declarations.name: primitiveBoundary_exists_two_tailEnergy_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveBoundary_exists_two_tailEnergy_lt_one {r x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hr2 : r < 2) (hx0lo : -1 ≤ x0) (hx0hi : x0 ≤ 1) (hx1lo : -1 ≤ x1) (hx1hi : x1 ≤ 1) (hx2lo : -1 ≤ x2) (hx2hi : x2 ≤ 1) (hx3lo : -1 ≤ x3) (hx3hi : x3 ≤ 1) (hx4lo : -1 ≤ x4) (hx4hi : x4 ≤ 1) (hm1 : x0 + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 = -r) (hm2 : x0 ^ 2 + x1 ^ 2 + x2 ^ 2 + x3 ^ 2 + x4 ^ 2 = (5 + r ^ 2) / 2) (hm3 : x0 ^ 3 + x1 ^ 3 + x2 ^ 3 + x3 ^ 3 + x4 ^ 3 = -(r ^ 3 + 3 * r) / 4) : (1 + r ^ 2 + 2 * r * x0 < 1 ∧ 1 + r ^ 2 + 2 * r * x1 < 1) ∨
declarations.docstring: Strict tail-energy form of the boundary selector. For `r>0`, the inequality `x < -r/2` is exactly `1+r^2+2*r*x < 1`.

declarations.name: primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator
declarations.signature: noncomputable def primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator (r x s : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Real-coordinate form of the harmonic extension of the boundary separator. Here `x = re z` and `s = |z|^2`.

declarations.name: primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator_sum
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator_sum {r : ℝ} {x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 s0 s1 s2 s3 s4 : ℝ} (hm1 : x0 + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 = -r) (hm2 : (2 * x0 ^ 2 - s0) + (2 * x1 ^ 2 - s1) + (2 * x2 ^ 2 - s2) + (2 * x3 ^ 2 - s3) + (2 * x4 ^ 2 - s4) = r ^ 2) (hm3 : (4 * x0 ^ 3 - 3 * s0 * x0) + (4 * x1 ^ 3 - 3 * s1 * x1) + (4 * x2 ^ 3 - 3 * s2 * x2) + (4 * x3 ^ 3 - 3 * s3 * x3) + (4 * x4 ^ 3 - 3 * s4 * x4) = -r ^ 3) : primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator r x0 s0 + primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator r x1 s1 +
declarations.docstring: The harmonic separator still has total mass `5 - 2*r` under the first three interior Newton-moment identities.

declarations.name: primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator_le_single
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator_le_single {r x s : ℝ} (hr0 : 0 ≤ r) (hr2 : r < 2) (hs0 : 0 ≤ s) (hs1 : s ≤ 1) (hxs : x ^ 2 ≤ s) : primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator r x s ≤ 4 - 2 * r
declarations.docstring: The disk maximum of the harmonic separator is the boundary value `4 - 2*r`. The proof is purely algebraic in `x = re z` and `s = |z|^2`; `x^2 <= s <= 1` is the real-coordinate disk constraint.

declarations.name: primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator_le_of_tailEnergy_ge_one
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator_le_of_tailEnergy_ge_one {r x s : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hr2 : r < 2) (hs0 : 0 ≤ s) (hs1 : s ≤ 1) (hxhi : x ≤ 1) (hunsafe : 1 ≤ s ^ 4 * (s + r ^ 2 + 2 * r * x)) : primitiveInteriorHarmonicSeparator r x s ≤ 2 / 31
declarations.docstring: The quantitative interior gain. If the full root-tail energy `s^4 * (s + r^2 + 2*r*x)` is unsafe, the harmonic separator is at most `2/31`.

declarations.name: five_exists_two_lt_one_of_score_caps
declarations.docstring: Five energies contain two strict safe entries when every score has a global cap, every unsafe entry has the sharper cap, and the total beats both the one-safe and zero-safe extrema.

declarations.name: primitiveZeroCoefficient_tailEnergy_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveZeroCoefficient_tailEnergy_le_one {s : ℝ} (hs0 : 0 ≤ s) (hs1 : s ≤ 1) : s ^ 4 * s ≤ 1
declarations.docstring: When the rotated fourth-degree coefficient is zero, the primitive tail energy is simply `s^5`, so every closed-disk root is non-strictly safe.

declarations.name: primitiveInterior_exists_two_tailEnergy_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveInterior_exists_two_tailEnergy_lt_one {r : ℝ} {x0 x1 x2 x3 x4 s0 s1 s2 s3 s4 : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hr2 : r < 2) (hs0 : 0 ≤ s0) (hs0one : s0 ≤ 1) (hx0s : x0 ^ 2 ≤ s0) (hs1 : 0 ≤ s1) (hs1one : s1 ≤ 1) (hx1s : x1 ^ 2 ≤ s1) (hs2 : 0 ≤ s2) (hs2one : s2 ≤ 1) (hx2s : x2 ^ 2 ≤ s2) (hs3 : 0 ≤ s3) (hs3one : s3 ≤ 1) (hx3s : x3 ^ 2 ≤ s3) (hs4 : 0 ≤ s4) (hs4one : s4 ≤ 1) (hx4s : x4 ^ 2 ≤ s4) (hm1 : x0 + x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 = -r) (hm2 : (2 * x0 ^ 2 - s0) + (2 * x1 ^ 2 - s1) + (2 * x2 ^ 2 - s2) + (2 * x3 ^ 2 - s3) + (2 * x4 ^ 2 - s4) = r ^ 2) (hm3 : (4 * x0 ^ 3 - 3 * s0 * x0) +
declarations.docstring: Finite interior moment theorem for the primitive sparse quintic. The conclusion gives two distinct root-tail energies strictly below one.

declarations.name: DegreeFourFirstMergeResidual
declarations.docstring: The exact residual after also supplying the cubic branch.

declarations.name: constantFactor_iff_degreeFour_residual
declarations.docstring: Compose the two returns without replacing the endpoint by a stronger supplier.

declarations.name: connectedAtMost_mono
declarations.signature: theorem connectedAtMost_mono {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R R' L L' : ℝ} {a b : ℂ} (hR : R ≤ R') (hL : L ≤ L') (H : ConnectedAtMost f R L a b) : ConnectedAtMost f R' L' a b
declarations.docstring: Enlarge both bounds on an already constructed closed connector.

declarations.name: connectedBelow_of_closed_slack
declarations.signature: theorem connectedBelow_of_closed_slack {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R R' L L' : ℝ} {a b : ℂ} (hR : R < R') (hL : L < L') (hL' : 0 < L') (H : ConnectedAtMost f R L a b) : ConnectedBelow f R' L' a b
declarations.docstring: Closed containment plus genuine slack gives open containment and length.

declarations.name: connectedAtMost_of_spokes
declarations.signature: theorem connectedAtMost_of_spokes {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R L : ℝ} {a h b : ℂ} (ha : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 → ‖f (h + (u : ℂ) * (a - h))‖ ≤ R) (hb : ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → u ≤ 1 → ‖f (h + (u : ℂ) * (b - h))‖ ≤ R) (hL : ‖h - a‖ + ‖b - h‖ ≤ L) : ConnectedAtMost f R L a b
declarations.docstring: Two safe spokes produce their actual polygonal connector, also at level zero.

declarations.name: connectedAtMost_refl
declarations.signature: theorem connectedAtMost_refl {f : ℂ → ℂ} {R : ℝ} {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖f a‖ ≤ R) : ConnectedAtMost f R 0 a a
declarations.docstring: Coincident occurrences admit a constant curve with exactly zero variation.

declarations.name: connectedAtMost_affine
declarations.signature: theorem connectedAtMost_affine {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {R L : ℝ} {a b h c d : ℂ} (hid : ∀ z : ℂ, f (h + c * z) = d * g z) (H : ConnectedAtMost g R L a b) : ConnectedAtMost f (‖d‖ * R) (‖c‖ * L) (h + c * a) (h + c * b)
declarations.docstring: Exact spatial scaling of a closed connector, including singular maps. Unlike strict transport, this does not require nonzero scale factors.

declarations.name: open_zero_impossible
declarations.signature: theorem open_zero_impossible (f : ℂ → ℂ) (a b : ℂ) (L : ℝ) : ¬ ConnectedBelow f 0 L a b
declarations.docstring: A closed zero-level connector cannot be relabelled as an open zero-level one.

declarations.name: cyclic_cost_sum
declarations.signature: theorem cyclic_cost_sum {k : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (lift arc : Fin k → ℝ) : (∑ i, (lift i + lift (σ i) + arc i)) = 2 * (∑ i, lift i) + ∑ i, arc i
declarations.docstring: A permutation counts each lift twice in the cyclic concatenation budget.

declarations.name: exists_cyclic_cost_le
declarations.signature: theorem exists_cyclic_cost_le {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (lift arc : Fin k → ℝ) (B : ℝ) (hbudget : 2 * (∑ i, lift i) + ∑ i, arc i ≤ (k : ℝ) * B) : ∃ i : Fin k, lift i + lift (σ i) + arc i ≤ B
declarations.docstring: Select the whole cost of a pair of lifts and the connecting boundary arc.

declarations.name: exists_cyclic_cost_le_average
declarations.signature: theorem exists_cyclic_cost_le_average {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (lift arc : Fin k → ℝ) : ∃ i : Fin k, lift i + lift (σ i) + arc i ≤ (2 * (∑ j, lift j) + ∑ j, arc j) / (k : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Exact average form; no positivity of the individual costs is needed.

declarations.name: actual_cyclic_connector_of_budget
declarations.signature: theorem actual_cyclic_connector_of_budget {k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) (hσ : ∀ i, i ≠ σ i) (z : Fin k → ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (R B : ℝ) (lift arc : Fin k → ℝ) (Hpath : ∀ i, ConnectedAtMost f R (lift i + lift (σ i) + arc i) (z i) (z (σ i))) (hbudget : 2 * (∑ i, lift i) + ∑ i, arc i ≤ (k : ℝ) * B) : ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ ConnectedAtMost f R B (z i) (z j)
declarations.docstring: Actual-curve consumer: the analytic/topological construction has to supply all `Hpath` curves. This theorem is NOT a producer of those curves.

declarations.name: shortest_arc_not_shortest_total
declarations.signature: theorem shortest_arc_not_shortest_total : let lift : Fin 3 → ℝ
declarations.docstring: Minimal arc length alone need not select a minimal connector cost. The three cyclic edges have costs 100, 1, 101, but arc zero is shortest.

declarations.name: cyclic_budget_of_separate_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem cyclic_budget_of_separate_bounds {k : ℕ} (lift arc : Fin k → ℝ) {A P B : ℝ} (hlift : (∑ i, lift i) ≤ A) (harc : (∑ i, arc i) ≤ P) (hnum : 2 * A + P ≤ (k : ℝ) * B) : 2 * (∑ i, lift i) + ∑ i, arc i ≤ (k : ℝ) * B
declarations.docstring: The numerator bound can be assembled before any division by root count.

declarations.name: CFConclusion
declarations.signature: def CFConclusion (n : ℕ) (p : ℂ[X]) (z : Fin n → ℂ) (μ : ℝ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The exact two-part conclusion, without weakening open containment.

declarations.name: HighDegreeFirstMergeResidual

declarations.name: constantFactor_iff_highDegree_residual
declarations.docstring: Every branch omitted by the residual is supplied by an actual curve. This equivalence precisely identifies, but DOES NOT discharge, the gap.

declarations.name: lobe_eval

declarations.name: lobe_eval_factor

declarations.name: lobe_root_iff

declarations.name: lobe_inner_disk
declarations.docstring: A whole closed disk, not a finite sample, is strictly inside |p|<1.

declarations.name: lobe_outer_circle
declarations.docstring: Every point of the circle |z|=4/5 is outside the closed unit sublevel.

declarations.name: lobe_unique_root_in_barrier

declarations.name: lobe_no_common_root

declarations.name: lobe_perimeter_numeric_gap

declarations.name: closed_numeric_consumer

declarations.name: open_numeric_consumer

declarations.name: strict_threshold_needs_slack
declarations.signature: theorem strict_threshold_needs_slack : ¬ (∀ x L : ℝ, x ≤ L → x < L)
declarations.docstring: Guard against a tempting but invalid strict-threshold relabelling.

declarations.name: precritical_energy_of_area
declarations.signature: theorem precritical_energy_of_area {n : ℕ} (cr area : Fin n → ℝ) (ρ : ℝ) (hlocal : ∀ i, Real.pi * cr i ^ 2 ≤ area i) (hglobal : (∑ i, area i) ≤ Real.pi * ρ ^ 2) : (∑ i, cr i ^ 2) ≤ ρ ^ 2

declarations.name: precritical_sum_sq_le

declarations.name: precritical_sum_le
declarations.signature: theorem precritical_sum_le {n : ℕ} (cr : Fin n → ℝ) {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 ≤ ρ) (henergy : (∑ i, cr i ^ 2) ≤ ρ ^ 2) : (∑ i, cr i) ≤ Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) * ρ

declarations.name: summed_low_piece_budget

declarations.name: quadratic_critical_iff

declarations.name: quadratic_center_value

declarations.name: quadratic_critical_minimum

declarations.name: quadratic_minimum_eq

declarations.name: quadratic_radius_eq

declarations.name: quadratic_diameter_norm
declarations.signature: theorem quadratic_diameter_norm (a b : ℂ) {s : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1) : ‖(quadratic a b).eval (midpoint a b + (s : ℂ) * halfDifference a b)‖ = (1 - s ^ 2) * ‖halfDifference a b‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: quadratic_diameter_bound

declarations.name: quadratic_segment

declarations.name: constantFactor_quadratic_branch

declarations.name: lowCritical_quadratic

declarations.name: quadratic_open_connector

declarations.name: quadratic_distance

declarations.docstring: Exact endpoint distance; the segment budget is not a loose surrogate.

declarations.name: primitive_quintic_selector_exact_target
declarations.docstring: Exact primitive target, without an extra tail-selection assumption.

declarations.name: enumeration_eval

declarations.name: enumeration_root

declarations.name: enumeration_root_iff

declarations.name: enumeration_derivative_eval

declarations.name: enumeration_derivative_at_root

declarations.name: repeated_occurrence_critical
declarations.signature: theorem repeated_occurrence_critical {n : ℕ} {p : ℂ[X]} {z : Fin n → ℂ} (hp : RootEnumeration p z) {i j : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) (he : z i = z j) : p.derivative.eval (z i) = 0

declarations.name: squarefree_rootEnumeration_injective

declarations.name: criticalMinimum_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem criticalMinimum_nonneg {p : ℂ[X]} {μ : ℝ} (hμ : CriticalMinimum p μ) : 0 ≤ μ

declarations.name: criticalMinimum_zero_of_repeated

declarations.name: criticalMinimum_pos_of_injective

declarations.name: constantFactor_repeated_branch
declarations.signature: theorem constantFactor_repeated_branch {n : ℕ} (p : ℂ[X]) (z : Fin n → ℂ) (μ : ℝ) (hp : RootEnumeration p z) (hμ : CriticalMinimum p μ) (hrepeat : ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ z i = z j) : (∃ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j ∧ ConnectedAtMost p.eval (2 * μ) ((71 / 10 : ℝ) * μ ^ (1 / (n : ℝ))) (z i) (z j) ∧ (Squarefree p → z i ≠ z j)) ∧ (∃ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j ∧ ∃ γ : ℝ → ℂ, ContinuousOn γ (Icc (0 : ℝ) 2) ∧ γ 0 = z i ∧ γ 2 = z j ∧ (∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 2, ‖p.eval (γ t)‖ < 1) ∧ BoundedVariationOn γ (Icc (0 : ℝ) 2) ∧ eVariationOn γ (Icc (0 : ℝ) 2) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (57 / 10))

declarations.name: quartic_normalized_gap_minus_one

declarations.name: quartic_normalized_gap_plus_one
