declarations.name: antitone_interlaces_of_card_gt_interlaces
declarations.signature: theorem antitone_interlaces_of_card_gt_interlaces {n : ℕ} (large : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (small : Fin n → ℝ) (hlarge : Antitone large) (hsmall : Antitone small) (hcount : ∀ t : ℝ, #{j | t < small j} ≤ #{j | t < large j} ∧ #{j | t < large j} ≤ #{j | t < small j} + 1) : ∀ i : Fin n, small i ≤ large i.castSucc ∧ large i.succ ≤ small i
declarations.docstring: Threshold-count interlacing implies the usual non-strict interlacing of two decreasing tuples. Repetitions are retained: the counts use strict thresholds, while the conclusion is non-strict.

declarations.name: determinantPencil_roots_eq_normalized_eigenvalues
declarations.signature: theorem determinantPencil_roots_eq_normalized_eigenvalues {n : ℕ} {A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.IsHermitian) : ∃ (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hH : H.IsHermitian), (determinantPencil A B).roots = Multiset.map (RCLike.ofReal ∘ hH.eigenvalues₀) Finset.univ.val
declarations.docstring: A positive-definite symmetric pencil is a nonzero scalar multiple of a Hermitian characteristic polynomial. Consequently this equality identifies the complete root multisets, including every algebraic multiplicity.

declarations.name: nested_pencils_inertia_and_root_multiplicity
declarations.signature: theorem nested_pencils_inertia_and_root_multiplicity {n : ℕ} (A B : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.IsHermitian) : (∀ t : ℝ, _root_.sigPos (pencilQuadratic (A.submatrix Fin.castSucc Fin.castSucc) (B.submatrix Fin.castSucc Fin.castSucc) t) ≤ _root_.sigPos (pencilQuadratic A B t) ∧ _root_.sigPos (pencilQuadratic A B t) ≤ _root_.sigPos (pencilQuadratic (A.submatrix Fin.castSucc Fin.castSucc) (B.submatrix Fin.castSucc Fin.castSucc) t) + 1) ∧ (∃ (H : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) (hH : H.IsHermitian), (determinantPencil A B).roots =
declarations.docstring: The exact original-coordinate information available for two consecutive principal pencils: their positive indices interlace at every threshold and both determinant polynomials carry their full normalized spectra as root multisets. No relation between the two normalization matrices is used.

declarations.name: nested_pencil_ordered_root_interlaces
declarations.signature: theorem nested_pencil_ordered_root_interlaces {n : ℕ} (A B : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.IsHermitian) : ∃ (Hlarge : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℝ) (hHlarge : Hlarge.IsHermitian) (Hsmall : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hHsmall : Hsmall.IsHermitian), (determinantPencil A B).roots = Multiset.map (RCLike.ofReal ∘ hHlarge.eigenvalues₀) Finset.univ.val ∧ (determinantPencil (A.submatrix Fin.castSucc Fin.castSucc) (B.submatrix Fin.castSucc Fin.castSucc)).roots = Multiset.map (RCLike.ofReal ∘ hHsmall.eigenvalues₀) Finset.univ.val ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, hHsmall.eigenvalues₀ (Fin.cast (Fintype.card_fin n).symm i) ≤
declarations.docstring: Exact non-strict consecutive-rank interlacing for the roots of the original nested symmetric definite pencils. The displayed multiset equalities record algebraic multiplicity; the ordered inequalities use the antitone `eigenvalues₀` enumerations of those same multisets.

declarations.name: associated_toQuadraticMap'_apply_of_isSymm
declarations.signature: theorem associated_toQuadraticMap'_apply_of_isSymm {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] {M : Matrix n n ℝ} (hM : M.IsSymm) (x y : n → ℝ) : QuadraticMap.associated (M.toQuadraticMap') x y = Matrix.toLinearMap₂' ℝ M x y
declarations.docstring: For a symmetric real matrix, polarizing its matrix quadratic form returns the original bilinear form.

declarations.name: hermitian_sub_smul_one_equivalent_weightedSumSquares
declarations.signature: theorem hermitian_sub_smul_one_equivalent_weightedSumSquares {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (H : Matrix n n ℝ) (hH : H.IsHermitian) (t : ℝ) : QuadraticMap.Equivalent ((H - t • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)).toQuadraticMap') (QuadraticMap.weightedSumSquares ℝ (fun i : n ↦ hH.eigenvalues i - t))
declarations.docstring: The matrix quadratic form of a Hermitian matrix shifted by `t I` is equivalent to the weighted sum of squares whose weights are `λᵢ - t`.

declarations.name: hermitian_sub_smul_one_sigPos_eq_card
declarations.signature: theorem hermitian_sub_smul_one_sigPos_eq_card {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (H : Matrix n n ℝ) (hH : H.IsHermitian) (t : ℝ) : _root_.sigPos ((H - t • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)).toQuadraticMap') = {i | t < hH.eigenvalues i}.ncard
declarations.docstring: Sylvester inertia in an eigenbasis: the positive index is the number of Hermitian eigenvalues strictly above the threshold.

declarations.name: card_eigenvalues_gt_eq_card_eigenvalues₀_gt
declarations.signature: theorem card_eigenvalues_gt_eq_card_eigenvalues₀_gt {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (H : Matrix n n ℝ) (hH : H.IsHermitian) (t : ℝ) : {i | t < hH.eigenvalues i}.ncard = {i | t < hH.eigenvalues₀ i}.ncard
declarations.docstring: Reindexing Mathlib's eigenvalues by the original finite type preserves every strict-threshold count.

declarations.name: congr_toQuadraticMap'_equivalent
declarations.signature: theorem congr_toQuadraticMap'_equivalent {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] (S M : Matrix n n ℝ) (hS : IsUnit S) : QuadraticMap.Equivalent ((Sᴴ * M * S).toQuadraticMap') M.toQuadraticMap'
declarations.docstring: Congruence by an invertible real matrix preserves the quadratic form up to linear equivalence.

declarations.name: pencil_sigPos_eq_card_normalized_eigenvalues
declarations.signature: theorem pencil_sigPos_eq_card_normalized_eigenvalues {n : ℕ} (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.IsHermitian) : ∃ (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (hH : H.IsHermitian), (∀ t : ℝ, _root_.sigPos (pencilQuadratic A B t) = {i | t < hH.eigenvalues₀ i}.ncard) ∧ (determinantPencil A B).roots = Multiset.map (RCLike.ofReal ∘ hH.eigenvalues₀) Finset.univ.val
declarations.docstring: The source-level Sylvester identity for a real symmetric definite pencil. The normalization is produced from positive definiteness, and the result is stated as an existential so no independently chosen normalization is compared with another rank.

declarations.name: realPolynomialEval
declarations.docstring: Evaluation of an integer polynomial on the real line.

declarations.name: HasLambertPolynomialPartLimit
declarations.docstring: The precise analytic assertion that `lambertPolynomialPart P` is the polynomial part at infinity of `P(p) * F(p⁻¹)`. Naming this assertion keeps the algebraic uniqueness theorem independent of a particular tail estimate.

declarations.name: polynomial_eq_zero_of_eval_tendsto_zero
declarations.signature: theorem polynomial_eq_zero_of_eval_tendsto_zero (P : ℤ[X]) (hP : Tendsto (realPolynomialEval P) atTop (𝓝 0)) : P = 0
declarations.docstring: A real polynomial whose values tend to zero at positive infinity is the zero polynomial. This is the small algebraic rigidity fact used below.

declarations.name: eq_lambertPolynomialPart_sub_one_of_tendsto
declarations.signature: theorem eq_lambertPolynomialPart_sub_one_of_tendsto (P B : ℤ[X]) (hP : HasLambertPolynomialPartLimit P) (hB : Tendsto (fun p : ℝ => realPolynomialEval P p * PaperR16.lambert p⁻¹ - realPolynomialEval B p) atTop (𝓝 1)) : B = lambertPolynomialPart P - 1
declarations.docstring: The polynomial part is unique. The first hypothesis is the genuine Lambert-tail estimate; the second says that a candidate subtraction has limit one. No moment or Padé identity is hidden among the hypotheses.

declarations.name: eq_lambertPolynomialPart_sub_one_of_eventual_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem eq_lambertPolynomialPart_sub_one_of_eventual_remainder (P B : ℤ[X]) (μ : ℝ → ℝ) (hP : HasLambertPolynomialPartLimit P) (hμ : Tendsto μ atTop (𝓝 1)) (hremainder : ∀ᶠ p : ℝ in atTop, μ p = realPolynomialEval P p * PaperR16.lambert p⁻¹ - realPolynomialEval B p) : B = lambertPolynomialPart P - 1
declarations.docstring: A remainder function tending to one forces its subtracting polynomial. The equality need only hold eventually, which is convenient for formulas valid for `p > 1`.

declarations.name: coefficientBetaPoly_unique_of_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem coefficientBetaPoly_unique_of_remainder (m : ℕ) (B : ℤ[X]) (hLambert : HasLambertPolynomialPartLimit (coefficientAlphaPoly m)) (hMoment : Tendsto (fun p : ℝ => PaperR12.actualMoment p⁻¹ m) atTop (𝓝 1)) (hremainder : ∀ p : ℝ, 1 < p → PaperR12.actualMoment p⁻¹ m = coefficientAlpha p m * PaperR16.lambert p⁻¹ - realPolynomialEval B p) : B = coefficientBetaPoly m
declarations.docstring: Concrete endpoint for the paper's coefficient polynomials. It records exactly the two analytic inputs still required from the Padé calculation: the Lambert-tail estimate and convergence of the literal moment.

declarations.name: sigPos_restrict_le
declarations.signature: theorem sigPos_restrict_le (Q : QuadraticForm ℝ V) (W : Submodule ℝ V) : _root_.sigPos (Q.restrict W) ≤ _root_.sigPos Q
declarations.docstring: Restricting a quadratic form to a subspace cannot increase its positive index.

declarations.name: sigPos_restrict_codim_one
declarations.signature: theorem sigPos_restrict_codim_one (Q : QuadraticForm ℝ V) (W : Submodule ℝ V) (hcodim : finrank ℝ W + 1 = finrank ℝ V) : _root_.sigPos (Q.restrict W) ≤ _root_.sigPos Q ∧ _root_.sigPos Q ≤ _root_.sigPos (Q.restrict W) + 1
declarations.docstring: Restriction to a codimension-one subspace changes the positive index by at most one.

declarations.name: sourceQuotient_clearing_balance
declarations.signature: theorem sourceQuotient_clearing_balance (m : ℕ) : (∑ j ∈ range (m + 1), (m + 1 + j)) + sourceQuotientClearD m = 4 * (∑ j ∈ range m, (j + 1)) + sourceQuotientClearE m
declarations.docstring: The source choices of `d` and `e` satisfy the exponent balance used by `momentRationalKernel_clear`, for every `m`, including `m=0,1`.

declarations.name: evalBivariate_clearedMomentNumeratorPoly_zero
declarations.signature: theorem evalBivariate_clearedMomentNumeratorPoly_zero (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : evalBivariate (clearedMomentNumeratorPoly m (sourceQuotientClearE m)) p 0 = 0
declarations.docstring: The cleared source numerator vanishes at the origin.

declarations.name: evalBivariate_clearedMomentNumeratorPoly_at_source_root
declarations.signature: theorem evalBivariate_clearedMomentNumeratorPoly_at_source_root (m s : ℕ) (hs : s < m) (p : ℝ) : evalBivariate (clearedMomentNumeratorPoly m (sourceQuotientClearE m)) p (p ^ (s + 1)) = 0
declarations.docstring: The cleared source numerator vanishes at each of its literal numerator roots `p^(s+1)`, `s<m`.

declarations.name: sourcePade_partial_fraction_at_zero
declarations.signature: theorem sourcePade_partial_fraction_at_zero (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : evalBivariate (sourceClearedQuotientPoly m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m + residueCertificatePoly m (sourceQuotientClearD m) (fun k => sourceResiduePoly m k.val)) p 0 = 0
declarations.docstring: Evaluation at zero of the unconditional source partial-fraction identity. This is the raw polynomial equation from which constant cancellation is obtained by evaluating the displayed products.

declarations.name: sourcePade_partial_fraction_at_numerator_root
declarations.signature: theorem sourcePade_partial_fraction_at_numerator_root (m s : ℕ) (hs : s < m) (p : ℝ) : evalBivariate (sourceClearedQuotientPoly m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m + residueCertificatePoly m (sourceQuotientClearD m) (fun k => sourceResiduePoly m k.val)) p (p ^ (s + 1)) = 0
declarations.docstring: Evaluation at every numerator root of the unconditional source partial-fraction identity. After the zero-evaluation cancellation and division by the nonzero denominator, this is exactly the `hzero` input of `kernelZero_correction_identity`.

declarations.name: sourcePositiveCoeffEval
declarations.signature: private def sourcePositiveCoeffEval (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (d j : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: sourcePade_constant_cancellation
declarations.signature: private theorem sourcePade_constant_cancellation (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) : parameterEval p (sourceClearedQuotientCoeff m m) + p ^ sourceQuotientClearD m * coefficientAlpha p m = 0

declarations.name: sourcePade_scaled_kernel_identity
declarations.signature: private theorem sourcePade_scaled_kernel_identity (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) (x : ℝ) (hx : x < p ^ (m + 1)) : p ^ sourceQuotientClearD m * momentRationalKernel p⁻¹ m x = (∑ j : Fin m, parameterEval p (sourceQuotientPositiveCoeff m j) * x ^ (j.val + 1)) + p ^ sourceQuotientClearD m * ∑ k : Fin (m + 1), parameterEval p (sourceResiduePoly m k.val) * x / (p ^ (m + 1 + k.val) - x)
declarations.docstring: The evaluated source Padé identity after exact normalization by `p^d`. The only domain condition is the one needed to keep every pole denominator nonzero; it covers both the summation orbit and all numerator roots.

declarations.name: sourcePade_rationalKernel_certificate
declarations.signature: private theorem sourcePade_rationalKernel_certificate (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) : let d
declarations.docstring: The source partial fraction is the exact rational-kernel certificate on all summation points. The coefficient normalization includes `p^d`.

declarations.name: sourcePade_kernelZero_correction
declarations.signature: private theorem sourcePade_kernelZero_correction (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) : let d
declarations.docstring: The normalized numerator zeros provide exactly the hypotheses of the finite kernel-zero correction.

declarations.name: sourcePade_actualMoment_remainder
declarations.signature: theorem sourcePade_actualMoment_remainder (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) : PaperR12.actualMoment p⁻¹ m = coefficientAlpha p m * PaperR16.lambert p⁻¹ - parameterEval p (sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly m)
declarations.docstring: Exact source remainder before identifying its finite polynomial with the paper's `β_m`.

declarations.name: sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly_eq_coefficientBetaPoly
declarations.signature: theorem sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly_eq_coefficientBetaPoly (m : ℕ) : sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly m = coefficientBetaPoly m
declarations.docstring: The finite source correction is the paper's literal `β_m`, for every index `m`, including the exceptional clearing cases `m=0,1`.

declarations.name: sourcePade_actualMoment_eq_coefficientLinearForm
declarations.signature: theorem sourcePade_actualMoment_eq_coefficientLinearForm (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hp : 1 < p) : PaperR12.actualMoment p⁻¹ m = coefficientAlpha p m * PaperR16.lambert p⁻¹ - coefficientBeta p m
declarations.docstring: Unconditional all-index analytic remainder identity.

declarations.name: sourceDeltaExceptPoly
declarations.docstring: The product `Delta_m` with its `j`th factor removed.

declarations.name: sourceDelta_factor
declarations.signature: theorem sourceDelta_factor (m j : ℕ) (hj : j < m) : sourceDeltaPoly m = (X ^ (j + 1) - 1) * sourceDeltaExceptPoly m j

declarations.name: sourceQuotientPositiveCoeff
declarations.signature: def sourceQuotientPositiveCoeff (m : ℕ) (j : Fin m) : ParameterPolynomial
declarations.docstring: The coefficient of the positive outer power `Y^(j+1)` in the concrete cleared quotient (the outer polynomial variable is written `Y` here only in the prose).

declarations.name: sourceQuotientQuotientPoly
declarations.signature: def sourceQuotientQuotientPoly (m : ℕ) (j : Fin m) : ParameterPolynomial
declarations.docstring: Remove one forced copy of `X^(j+1)-1` from the positive quotient coefficient. Two untouched copies remain in `Delta_m^3`.

declarations.name: sourceQuotientPositiveCoeff_factor
declarations.signature: theorem sourceQuotientPositiveCoeff_factor (m : ℕ) (j : Fin m) : sourceQuotientPositiveCoeff m j = (X ^ (j.val + 1) - 1) * sourceQuotientQuotientPoly m j

declarations.name: sourceShiftedQuotientCorrectionPoly
declarations.signature: def sourceShiftedQuotientCorrectionPoly (m : ℕ) (j : Fin m) : ParameterPolynomial
declarations.docstring: The shifted positive quotient coefficient after removing both its geometric denominator and the global clearing power `X^d`. Polynomiality is termwise at the shifted evaluation point; it does not use cancellation between different quotient coefficients.

declarations.name: sourceQuotientClearD_le_shiftedExponent
declarations.signature: private theorem sourceQuotientClearD_le_shiftedExponent (m : ℕ) (j : Fin m) : sourceQuotientClearD m ≤ (m + 1) * (j.val + 1) + (m - (j.val + 1) + 1).choose 2 + sourceQuotientClearE m

declarations.name: sourceShiftedQuotientCorrection_scale
declarations.signature: theorem sourceShiftedQuotientCorrection_scale (m : ℕ) (j : Fin m) : X ^ sourceQuotientClearD m * sourceShiftedQuotientCorrectionPoly m j = X ^ ((m + 1) * (j.val + 1)) * sourceQuotientQuotientPoly m j
declarations.docstring: Exact removal of the global clearing power from every shifted quotient term used by the kernel-zero correction.

declarations.name: coeff_sourceClearedQuotientPoly
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_sourceClearedQuotientPoly (m r : ℕ) (hr : r ≤ m) : (sourceClearedQuotientPoly m).coeff r = sourceClearedQuotientCoeff m (m - r)
declarations.docstring: Coefficient extraction from the descending-power presentation of the cleared quotient.

declarations.name: sourceClearedQuotientPoly_split
declarations.signature: theorem sourceClearedQuotientPoly_split (m : ℕ) : sourceClearedQuotientPoly m = C (sourceClearedQuotientCoeff m m) + ∑ j : Fin m, C (sourceQuotientPositiveCoeff m j) * X ^ (j.val + 1)
declarations.docstring: The concrete quotient is its constant coefficient plus its `m` positive coefficients. This is the split expected by the rational-kernel consumer.

declarations.name: sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly
declarations.docstring: The finite polynomial produced by the source partial fractions after the kernel-zero correction: short residue prefixes minus the quotient evaluated at the shifted power `p^(m+1)`.

declarations.name: parameterEval_sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly
declarations.signature: theorem parameterEval_sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : parameterEval p (sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly m) = (∑ k : Fin (m + 1), ∑ n : Fin k.val, parameterEval p (sourceResidueQuotientPoly m k.val n.val)) - ∑ j : Fin m, parameterEval p (sourceShiftedQuotientCorrectionPoly m j)
declarations.docstring: Evaluation exposes exactly the short-prefix correction occurring on the right side of `kernelZero_correction_identity`.

declarations.name: parameterEval_sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly_cleared
declarations.signature: theorem parameterEval_sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly_cleared (m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : p ^ sourceQuotientClearD m * parameterEval p (sourceFiniteCorrectionPoly m) = p ^ sourceQuotientClearD m * (∑ k : Fin (m + 1), ∑ n : Fin k.val, parameterEval p (sourceResidueQuotientPoly m k.val n.val)) - ∑ j : Fin m, p ^ ((m + 1) * (j.val + 1)) * parameterEval p (sourceQuotientQuotientPoly m j)
declarations.docstring: Cleared evaluation form of the source correction. This is the exact normalization needed to compare with `kernelZero_correction_identity`.

declarations.name: sourceReciprocalCoeff
declarations.docstring: The coefficient `[m+r choose m]_p` of the reciprocal denominator.

declarations.name: sourceReciprocalSeries
declarations.docstring: The reciprocal-denominator series with Gaussian coefficients.

declarations.name: sourceDenominatorSeries
declarations.signature: def sourceDenominatorSeries : ℕ → PadeGeneratingSeries | 0 => 1 - PowerSeries.X | m + 1 => sourceDenominatorSeries m * (1 - PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1)) * PowerSeries.X) /-- The recursive denominator is the literal product `∏_{j=0}^m(1-p^j z)`. -/ theorem sourceDenominatorSeries_eq_prod (m : ℕ) : sourceDenominatorSeries m = ∏ j ∈ range (m + 1), (1 - PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ j) * PowerSeries.X)
declarations.docstring: The literal denominator `∏_{j=0}^m (1-p^j z)`, recursively ordered.

declarations.name: sourceDenominatorSeries_eq_prod
declarations.signature: theorem sourceDenominatorSeries_eq_prod (m : ℕ) : sourceDenominatorSeries m = ∏ j ∈ range (m + 1), (1 - PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ j) * PowerSeries.X)
declarations.docstring: The recursive denominator is the literal product `∏_{j=0}^m(1-p^j z)`.

declarations.name: sourceReciprocalCoeff_succ
declarations.signature: theorem sourceReciprocalCoeff_succ (m r : ℕ) : sourceReciprocalCoeff (m + 1) (r + 1) = sourceReciprocalCoeff m (r + 1) + (X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1) * sourceReciprocalCoeff (m + 1) r
declarations.docstring: The second Pascal recurrence, obtained from the existing Gaussian symmetry theorem and the defining first Pascal recurrence.

declarations.name: denominatorFactor_mul_sourceReciprocalSeries
declarations.signature: theorem denominatorFactor_mul_sourceReciprocalSeries (m : ℕ) : (1 - PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1)) * PowerSeries.X) * sourceReciprocalSeries (m + 1) = sourceReciprocalSeries m
declarations.docstring: Multiplying by the newest denominator factor lowers `m` by one.

declarations.name: denominator_zero_mul_sourceReciprocalSeries
declarations.docstring: The `m=0` geometric series is inverse to `1-z`.

declarations.name: sourceDenominator_mul_sourceReciprocalSeries
declarations.signature: theorem sourceDenominator_mul_sourceReciprocalSeries (m : ℕ) : sourceDenominatorSeries m * sourceReciprocalSeries m = 1
declarations.docstring: Exact reciprocal-product identity `∏_{j=0}^m(1-p^j z) * Σ_r [m+r choose m]_p z^r = 1`.

declarations.name: gaussBinom_succ_alt
declarations.signature: theorem gaussBinom_succ_alt (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) : gaussBinom (X : PadeParameterPolynomial) (m + 1) (k + 1) = X ^ (k + 1) * gaussBinom X m (k + 1) + gaussBinom X m k
declarations.docstring: The Gaussian recurrence in the orientation needed when a new numerator factor `p^(m+1)-z` is appended.

declarations.name: sourceNumeratorCoeff
declarations.docstring: Coefficient of `z^k` in `∏_{j=1}^m(p^j-z)`. Only the range `k≤m` is used below, so every displayed natural subtraction is exact.

declarations.name: sourceNumeratorCoeff_zero_succ
declarations.signature: theorem sourceNumeratorCoeff_zero_succ (m : ℕ) : sourceNumeratorCoeff (m + 1) 0 = X ^ (m + 1) * sourceNumeratorCoeff m 0

declarations.name: sourceNumeratorCoeff_succ
declarations.signature: theorem sourceNumeratorCoeff_succ (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) : sourceNumeratorCoeff (m + 1) (k + 1) = X ^ (m + 1) * sourceNumeratorCoeff m (k + 1) - sourceNumeratorCoeff m k
declarations.docstring: Coefficient recursion induced by multiplying by `p^(m+1)-z`.

declarations.name: sourceNumeratorSeries
declarations.docstring: The finite numerator series, defined from its exact finite coefficients.

declarations.name: sourceNumeratorSeries_succ
declarations.signature: theorem sourceNumeratorSeries_succ (m : ℕ) : sourceNumeratorSeries (m + 1) = sourceNumeratorSeries m * (PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1)) - PowerSeries.X)
declarations.docstring: Appending the next literal factor gives exactly the coefficient recursion above.

declarations.name: sourceNumeratorSeries_eq_prod
declarations.signature: theorem sourceNumeratorSeries_eq_prod (m : ℕ) : sourceNumeratorSeries m = ∏ j ∈ range m, (PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ (j + 1)) - PowerSeries.X)
declarations.docstring: The coefficient-defined numerator is the literal finite product `∏_{j=1}^m(p^j-z)`.

declarations.name: sourceTriangularCoeff
declarations.docstring: The triangular convolution appearing in the source quotient.

declarations.name: coeff_sourceNumerator_mul_sourceReciprocalSeries
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_sourceNumerator_mul_sourceReciprocalSeries (m l : ℕ) (hl : l ≤ m) : PowerSeries.coeff l (sourceNumeratorSeries m * sourceReciprocalSeries m) = sourceTriangularCoeff m l
declarations.docstring: The coefficient of the numerator times the reciprocal denominator is the literal triangular Gaussian convolution `S_(m,l)`.

declarations.name: sourceTriangular_generating_identity
declarations.signature: theorem sourceTriangular_generating_identity (m : ℕ) : sourceDenominatorSeries m * (sourceNumeratorSeries m * sourceReciprocalSeries m) = sourceNumeratorSeries m
declarations.docstring: Formal generating identity for the triangular quotient coefficients.

declarations.name: sourceTriangular_literal_generating_identity
declarations.signature: theorem sourceTriangular_literal_generating_identity (m : ℕ) : (∏ j ∈ range (m + 1), (1 - PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ j) * PowerSeries.X)) * (sourceNumeratorSeries m * sourceReciprocalSeries m) = ∏ j ∈ range m, (PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ (j + 1)) - PowerSeries.X)
declarations.docstring: The same generating identity with both finite products displayed literally.

declarations.name: natDegree_linear_le
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_linear_le (a : ParameterPolynomial) : (C a - (X : BivariatePolynomial)).natDegree ≤ 1

declarations.name: natDegree_prod_linear_le
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_prod_linear_le (n shift : ℕ) : (∏ j ∈ range n, (C ((X : ParameterPolynomial) ^ (shift + j)) - X : BivariatePolynomial)).natDegree ≤ n

declarations.name: natDegree_sourceOuterQuotientCore_le
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_sourceOuterQuotientCore_le (m : ℕ) : (sourceOuterQuotientCore m).natDegree ≤ m

declarations.name: reflect_prod_C_sub_X
declarations.signature: private theorem reflect_prod_C_sub_X (n shift : ℕ) : (∏ j ∈ range n, (C ((X : ParameterPolynomial) ^ (shift + j)) - X : BivariatePolynomial)).reflect n = (-1 : BivariatePolynomial) ^ n * ∏ j ∈ range n, (1 - C ((X : ParameterPolynomial) ^ (shift + j)) * X)

declarations.name: reflect_sourceOuterQuotientCore
declarations.signature: private theorem reflect_sourceOuterQuotientCore (m : ℕ) : (sourceOuterQuotientCore m).reflect m = sourceInfinityQuotientPoly m

declarations.name: reflect_sourceOuterNumeratorCore
declarations.signature: private theorem reflect_sourceOuterNumeratorCore (m : ℕ) : (sourceOuterNumeratorCore m).reflect (2 * m + 1) = (-1 : BivariatePolynomial) ^ m * sourceInfinityNumeratorPoly m

declarations.name: reflect_cleared_denominator
declarations.signature: private theorem reflect_cleared_denominator (m : ℕ) : (clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m).reflect (m + 1) = (-1 : BivariatePolynomial) ^ (m + 1) * sourceInfinityDenominatorPoly m

declarations.name: natDegree_sourceOuterNumeratorCore_le
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_sourceOuterNumeratorCore_le (m : ℕ) : (sourceOuterNumeratorCore m).natDegree ≤ 2 * m + 1

declarations.name: natDegree_cleared_denominator_le
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_cleared_denominator_le (m : ℕ) : (clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m).natDegree ≤ m + 1

declarations.name: natDegree_source_core_residual_le
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_source_core_residual_le (m : ℕ) : (sourceOuterNumeratorCore m + sourceOuterQuotientCore m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m).natDegree ≤ 2 * m + 1

declarations.name: natDegree_le_of_reflect_X_pow_dvd
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_le_of_reflect_X_pow_dvd (P : BivariatePolynomial) (m : ℕ) (hdeg : P.natDegree ≤ 2 * m + 1) (hdvd : (X : BivariatePolynomial) ^ (m + 1) ∣ P.reflect (2 * m + 1)) : P.natDegree ≤ m

declarations.name: reflect_source_core_residual
declarations.signature: private theorem reflect_source_core_residual (m : ℕ) : (sourceOuterNumeratorCore m + sourceOuterQuotientCore m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m).reflect (2 * m + 1) = (-1 : BivariatePolynomial) ^ m * (sourceInfinityNumeratorPoly m - sourceInfinityDenominatorPoly m * sourceInfinityQuotientPoly m)

declarations.name: natDegree_source_core_residual_at_most
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_source_core_residual_at_most (m : ℕ) : (sourceOuterNumeratorCore m + sourceOuterQuotientCore m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m).natDegree ≤ m

declarations.name: cleared_difference_eq_scaled_core
declarations.signature: private theorem cleared_difference_eq_scaled_core (m : ℕ) : clearedMomentNumeratorPoly m (sourceQuotientClearE m) - sourceClearedQuotientPoly m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m = C (X ^ sourceQuotientClearE m * sourceDeltaPoly m ^ 3) * (sourceOuterNumeratorCore m + sourceOuterQuotientCore m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m)

declarations.name: natDegree_cleared_difference_le
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_cleared_difference_le (m : ℕ) : (clearedMomentNumeratorPoly m (sourceQuotientClearE m) - sourceClearedQuotientPoly m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m).natDegree ≤ m

declarations.name: natDegree_denominatorExcept_le
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_denominatorExcept_le (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (m + 1)) : (clearedMomentDenominatorExceptPoly m k.val).natDegree ≤ m

declarations.name: natDegree_residueCertificate_le
declarations.signature: private theorem natDegree_residueCertificate_le (m : ℕ) : (residueCertificatePoly m (sourceQuotientClearD m) (fun k => sourceResiduePoly m k.val)).natDegree ≤ m

declarations.name: eval_cleared_denominator_at_pole_zero
declarations.signature: private theorem eval_cleared_denominator_at_pole_zero (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (m + 1)) : (clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m).eval ((X : ParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1 + k.val)) = 0

declarations.name: eval_residueCertificate_at_pole
declarations.signature: private theorem eval_residueCertificate_at_pole (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (m + 1)) : (residueCertificatePoly m (sourceQuotientClearD m) (fun r => sourceResiduePoly m r.val)).eval ((X : ParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1 + k.val)) = X ^ sourceQuotientClearD m * sourceResiduePoly m k.val * X ^ (m + 1 + k.val) * (clearedMomentDenominatorExceptPoly m k.val).eval ((X : ParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1 + k.val))

declarations.name: source_partial_fraction_residual_eval_zero
declarations.signature: private theorem source_partial_fraction_residual_eval_zero (m : ℕ) (k : Fin (m + 1)) : (clearedMomentNumeratorPoly m (sourceQuotientClearE m) - (sourceClearedQuotientPoly m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m + residueCertificatePoly m (sourceQuotientClearD m) (fun r => sourceResiduePoly m r.val))).eval ((X : ParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1 + k.val)) = 0

declarations.name: polePower_injective
declarations.signature: private theorem polePower_injective (m : ℕ) : Function.Injective (fun k : Fin (m + 1) => (X : ParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1 + k.val))

declarations.name: sourcePade_partial_fraction_identity
declarations.signature: theorem sourcePade_partial_fraction_identity (m : ℕ) : clearedMomentNumeratorPoly m (sourceQuotientClearE m) = sourceClearedQuotientPoly m * clearedMomentDenominatorPoly m + residueCertificatePoly m (sourceQuotientClearD m) (fun k => sourceResiduePoly m k.val)
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional all-index partial fraction identity.**

declarations.name: sourcePoleDenominatorPower
declarations.signature: private def sourcePoleDenominatorPower (m k : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: triangle_succ_div
declarations.signature: private theorem triangle_succ_div (n : ℕ) : n * (n + 1) / 2 = n * (n - 1) / 2 + n
declarations.docstring: `n(n+1)/2 = n(n-1)/2 + n`, the step between consecutive triangular numbers.

declarations.name: two_mul_triangle_pred_add
declarations.signature: private theorem two_mul_triangle_pred_add (n : ℕ) : 2 * (n * (n - 1) / 2) + n = n * n
declarations.docstring: `n(n-1)` is even, so twice its half plus `n` is `n²`.

declarations.name: sourceTriangle_eq
declarations.signature: private theorem sourceTriangle_eq (m : ℕ) : sourceTriangle m = m * (m + 1) / 2

declarations.name: sourcePoleDenominatorPower_eq
declarations.signature: private theorem sourcePoleDenominatorPower_eq (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) : sourcePoleDenominatorPower m k = m * (m + 1) + k * m - k * (k + 1) / 2

declarations.name: pow_sub_pow_factor
declarations.signature: private theorem pow_sub_pow_factor (a b : ℕ) (hab : a ≤ b) : (X : ℤ[X]) ^ a - X ^ b = -(X ^ a * (X ^ (b - a) - 1))

declarations.name: sourceNumeratorPoleProduct
declarations.signature: private theorem sourceNumeratorPoleProduct (m k : ℕ) : (∏ j ∈ range m, ((X : ℤ[X]) ^ (j + 1) - X ^ (m + 1 + k))) = (-1 : ℤ[X]) ^ m * X ^ sourceTriangle m * sourceDeltaSegmentPoly k m
declarations.docstring: Product in the cleared numerator after substituting the pole `x=p^(m+1+k)`.

declarations.name: erase_range_pole_split
declarations.signature: private theorem erase_range_pole_split (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) : (range (m + 1)).erase k = range k ∪ (range (m - k)).image (fun r => k + 1 + r)

declarations.name: sourceDenominatorExceptPoleProduct
declarations.signature: private theorem sourceDenominatorExceptPoleProduct (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) : (∏ j ∈ (range (m + 1)).erase k, ((X : ℤ[X]) ^ (m + 1 + j) - X ^ (m + 1 + k))) = (-1 : ℤ[X]) ^ k * X ^ sourcePoleDenominatorPower m k * sourceDeltaPoly k * sourceDeltaPoly (m - k)
declarations.docstring: Product of all denominator factors except the pole factor.

declarations.name: sourceResidue_mul_denominatorDeltas
declarations.signature: private theorem sourceResidue_mul_denominatorDeltas (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) : sourceResiduePoly m k * sourceDeltaPoly k * sourceDeltaPoly (m - k) = C ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (m + k)) * X ^ (m + 1 + k * (k + 1) / 2) * sourceDeltaPoly m ^ 3 * sourceDeltaSegmentPoly k m
declarations.docstring: The Delta factors in the residue and in the erased denominator collapse to `Delta_m^3` times the remaining numerator segment.

declarations.name: sourcePoleExponentBalance
declarations.signature: private theorem sourcePoleExponentBalance (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) : sourceQuotientClearE m + (m + 1 + k) * (m + 1) + sourceTriangle m = sourceQuotientClearD m + (m + 1 + k * (k + 1) / 2) + (m + 1 + k) + sourcePoleDenominatorPower m k

declarations.name: eval_clearedMomentNumeratorPoly_at_pole
declarations.signature: theorem eval_clearedMomentNumeratorPoly_at_pole (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) : (clearedMomentNumeratorPoly m (sourceQuotientClearE m)).eval ((X : ℤ[X]) ^ (m + 1 + k)) = X ^ sourceQuotientClearD m * sourceResiduePoly m k * X ^ (m + 1 + k) * (clearedMomentDenominatorExceptPoly m k).eval ((X : ℤ[X]) ^ (m + 1 + k))
declarations.docstring: **Exact pole evaluation.** At the pole indexed by `k`, the literal cleared numerator is the `k`th residue contribution times the erased denominator.

declarations.name: sourceQuotientClearD
declarations.docstring: `d=max(m(m-1)/2-1,0)` in natural-subtraction form.

declarations.name: sourceQuotientClearE
declarations.docstring: `e=max(1-m(m-1)/2,0)` in natural-subtraction form.

declarations.name: sourceQuotientClearD_sub_E
declarations.signature: theorem sourceQuotientClearD_sub_E (m : ℕ) : sourceQuotientClearD m + 1 = m * (m - 1) / 2 + sourceQuotientClearE m

declarations.name: sourceNormalizedTriangularCoeff
declarations.docstring: The forced `p`-power is removed termwise from the triangular coefficient. Every exponent is a natural number when `k≤l≤m`.

declarations.name: sourceTriangularCoeff_eq_X_pow_mul_normalized
declarations.signature: theorem sourceTriangularCoeff_eq_X_pow_mul_normalized (m l : ℕ) (hl : l ≤ m) : sourceTriangularCoeff m l = X ^ (m - l + 1).choose 2 * sourceNormalizedTriangularCoeff m l
declarations.docstring: Exact extraction of the common triangular `p`-valuation.

declarations.name: sourceClearedQuotientCoeff
declarations.docstring: The integral coefficient of `X^(m-l)` in the cleared quotient `Qbar`. The exceptional extra power for `m=0,1` is exactly `e`; for `m≥2`, `e=0`.

declarations.name: sourceClearedQuotientPoly
declarations.docstring: The concrete all-`m` cleared quotient, with coefficients ordered by descending powers `X^(m-l)` of the kernel variable.

declarations.name: sourceTriangularTruncation
declarations.docstring: The triangular series truncated exactly through the polynomial quotient range `0≤l≤m`.

declarations.name: coeff_sourceTriangularTruncation
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem coeff_sourceTriangularTruncation (m l : ℕ) (hl : l ≤ m) : PowerSeries.coeff l (sourceTriangularTruncation m) = sourceTriangularCoeff m l

declarations.name: coeff_mul_eq_of_right_coeff_eq_up_to
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_mul_eq_of_right_coeff_eq_up_to {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (A B C : PowerSeries R) (m l : ℕ) (hl : l ≤ m) (hcoeff : ∀ n, n ≤ m → PowerSeries.coeff n B = PowerSeries.coeff n C) : PowerSeries.coeff l (A * B) = PowerSeries.coeff l (A * C)

declarations.name: source_truncated_generating_remainder_coeff_zero
declarations.signature: theorem source_truncated_generating_remainder_coeff_zero (m l : ℕ) (hl : l ≤ m) : PowerSeries.coeff l (sourceNumeratorSeries m - sourceDenominatorSeries m * sourceTriangularTruncation m) = 0
declarations.docstring: Multiplying the truncated quotient series by the literal denominator matches the literal numerator in every degree at most `m`. Equivalently, the residual starts in degree `m+1`; after reversal this is the desired polynomial remainder degree bound `<m+1`.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff
declarations.docstring: Coefficient of `z^k` in `∏_{a=1}^m (1-p^a z)`.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityNumeratorSeries
declarations.docstring: The reversed numerator series at infinity.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff_zero_succ
declarations.signature: theorem sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff_zero_succ (m : ℕ) : sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff (m + 1) 0 = sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff m 0

declarations.name: sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff_succ
declarations.signature: theorem sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff_succ (m k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ m) : sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff (m + 1) (k + 1) = sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff m (k + 1) - X ^ (m + 1) * sourceInfinityNumeratorCoeff m k
declarations.docstring: Coefficient recursion induced by appending `1-p^(m+1)z`.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityNumeratorSeries_eq_prod
declarations.signature: theorem sourceInfinityNumeratorSeries_eq_prod (m : ℕ) : sourceInfinityNumeratorSeries m = ∏ j ∈ range m, (1 - PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ (j + 1)) * PowerSeries.X)
declarations.docstring: The reversed numerator is the literal finite product.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityDenominatorSeries
declarations.docstring: Denominator at infinity, obtained by the variable rescaling `z ↦ p^(m+1)z`.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityReciprocalSeries
declarations.docstring: Reciprocal denominator at infinity, with coefficient `p^((m+1)r)[m+r choose m]_p`.

declarations.name: coeff_sourceInfinityReciprocalSeries
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem coeff_sourceInfinityReciprocalSeries (m r : ℕ) : PowerSeries.coeff r (sourceInfinityReciprocalSeries m) = X ^ ((m + 1) * r) * sourceReciprocalCoeff m r

declarations.name: sourceInfinityDenominator_mul_reciprocal
declarations.signature: theorem sourceInfinityDenominator_mul_reciprocal (m : ℕ) : sourceInfinityDenominatorSeries m * sourceInfinityReciprocalSeries m = 1

declarations.name: sourceInfinityTriangularCoeff
declarations.docstring: Coefficient of the reversed quotient expansion at infinity.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityTriangularCoeff_eq_normalized
declarations.signature: theorem sourceInfinityTriangularCoeff_eq_normalized (m l : ℕ) (hl : l ≤ m) : sourceInfinityTriangularCoeff m l = X ^ (l + 1).choose 2 * sourceNormalizedTriangularCoeff m l
declarations.docstring: The reversed convolution is exactly the normalized triangular coefficient used in `sourceClearedQuotientPoly`.

declarations.name: coeff_sourceInfinityNumerator_mul_reciprocal
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_sourceInfinityNumerator_mul_reciprocal (m l : ℕ) (hl : l ≤ m) : PowerSeries.coeff l (sourceInfinityNumeratorSeries m * sourceInfinityReciprocalSeries m) = sourceInfinityTriangularCoeff m l
declarations.docstring: Coefficient extraction from the full reversed numerator/reciprocal product.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityTriangularTruncation
declarations.docstring: Truncation of the concrete reversed quotient through degree `m`.

declarations.name: source_infinity_truncated_remainder_coeff_zero
declarations.signature: theorem source_infinity_truncated_remainder_coeff_zero (m l : ℕ) (hl : l ≤ m) : PowerSeries.coeff l (sourceInfinityNumeratorSeries m - sourceInfinityDenominatorSeries m * sourceInfinityTriangularTruncation m) = 0
declarations.docstring: The finite reversed quotient is exact through order `m`; hence the unreversed polynomial remainder has outer degree at most `m`.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityDenominatorSeries_eq_prod
declarations.signature: theorem sourceInfinityDenominatorSeries_eq_prod (m : ℕ) : sourceInfinityDenominatorSeries m = ∏ j ∈ range (m + 1), (1 - PowerSeries.C ((X : PadeParameterPolynomial) ^ (m + 1 + j)) * PowerSeries.X)

declarations.name: sourceInfinityNumeratorPoly
declarations.docstring: Finite polynomial forms of the three reversed series.

declarations.name: sourceInfinityNumeratorPoly_toPowerSeries
declarations.signature: theorem sourceInfinityNumeratorPoly_toPowerSeries (m : ℕ) : (sourceInfinityNumeratorPoly m : PadeGeneratingSeries) = sourceInfinityNumeratorSeries m

declarations.name: sourceInfinityDenominatorPoly_toPowerSeries
declarations.signature: theorem sourceInfinityDenominatorPoly_toPowerSeries (m : ℕ) : (sourceInfinityDenominatorPoly m : PadeGeneratingSeries) = sourceInfinityDenominatorSeries m

declarations.name: sourceInfinityQuotientPoly_toPowerSeries
declarations.signature: theorem sourceInfinityQuotientPoly_toPowerSeries (m : ℕ) : (sourceInfinityQuotientPoly m : PadeGeneratingSeries) = sourceInfinityTriangularTruncation m

declarations.name: source_infinity_remainder_X_pow_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem source_infinity_remainder_X_pow_dvd (m : ℕ) : PowerSeries.X ^ (m + 1) ∣ sourceInfinityNumeratorSeries m - sourceInfinityDenominatorSeries m * sourceInfinityTriangularTruncation m
declarations.docstring: **Finite generating-function truncation.** The reversed residual has a zero of order at least `m+1`. Since all three series in the residual are finite through the relevant quotient range, reversing this statement is the outer polynomial remainder bound `≤m`.

declarations.name: source_infinity_polynomial_remainder_X_pow_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem source_infinity_polynomial_remainder_X_pow_dvd (m : ℕ) : (X : (ℤ[X])[X]) ^ (m + 1) ∣ sourceInfinityNumeratorPoly m - sourceInfinityDenominatorPoly m * sourceInfinityQuotientPoly m
declarations.docstring: Polynomial version of the finite truncation. This is the direct input to the final `reflect` step that turns an order-`m+1` zero at the origin into an outer remainder degree bound `≤m`.

declarations.name: sourceClearedQuotientCoeff_eq_infinity
declarations.signature: theorem sourceClearedQuotientCoeff_eq_infinity (m l : ℕ) (hl : l ≤ m) : sourceClearedQuotientCoeff m l = -(sourceDeltaPoly m ^ 3 * X ^ sourceQuotientClearE m * sourceInfinityTriangularCoeff m l)
declarations.docstring: The displayed integral quotient coefficient is exactly the reversed generating coefficient, multiplied by the numerator's clearing factor.

declarations.name: sourceClearedQuotientPoly_eq_reversed
declarations.signature: theorem sourceClearedQuotientPoly_eq_reversed (m : ℕ) : sourceClearedQuotientPoly m = C (-(sourceDeltaPoly m ^ 3 * X ^ sourceQuotientClearE m)) * ∑ l ∈ range (m + 1), C (sourceInfinityTriangularCoeff m l) * X ^ (m - l)
declarations.docstring: Concrete reversal formula for the bivariate quotient used by the finite remainder consumer. The outer exponent `m-l` is the reversal of the generating index `l`; the inner scalar is exactly the integral clearing factor, including the exceptional `e` at `m=0,1`.

declarations.name: sourceDeltaPoly
declarations.docstring: The product of `X^a - 1` for `1 ≤ a ≤ m`.

declarations.name: sourceDeltaSegmentPoly
declarations.docstring: The consecutive product with exponents `a+1` through `a+n`.

declarations.name: sourceDeltaSegment_eq_signed_pochhammer
declarations.signature: theorem sourceDeltaSegment_eq_signed_pochhammer (a n : ℕ) : sourceDeltaSegmentPoly a n = (-1 : ℤ[X]) ^ n * qPochhammer X (X ^ (a + 1)) n

declarations.name: sourceDelta_eq_signed_pochhammer
declarations.signature: theorem sourceDelta_eq_signed_pochhammer (m : ℕ) : sourceDeltaPoly m = (-1 : ℤ[X]) ^ m * qPochhammer X X m

declarations.name: sourceDelta_add
declarations.signature: theorem sourceDelta_add (a n : ℕ) : sourceDeltaPoly (a + n) = sourceDeltaPoly a * sourceDeltaSegmentPoly a n

declarations.name: gaussBinom_mul_sourceDelta
declarations.signature: theorem gaussBinom_mul_sourceDelta {n k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ n) : gaussBinom (X : ℤ[X]) n k * sourceDeltaPoly k = sourceDeltaSegmentPoly (n - k) k

declarations.name: sourceDelta_cube_mul_gauss
declarations.signature: theorem sourceDelta_cube_mul_gauss {m k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ m) : sourceDeltaPoly m ^ 3 * gaussBinom X m k * gaussBinom X (m + k) k = sourceDeltaSegmentPoly k (m - k) ^ 2 * sourceDeltaSegmentPoly (m - k) k * sourceDeltaPoly (m + k)
declarations.docstring: The two Gaussian factors clear exactly against three factorial products.

declarations.name: sourceResiduePoly
declarations.docstring: The fully factored integer residue at the pole indexed by `k`.

declarations.name: sourceResidue_eq_gauss
declarations.signature: theorem sourceResidue_eq_gauss {m k : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ m) : sourceResiduePoly m k = X ^ (m + 1) * sourceDeltaPoly m ^ 3 * (C ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (m + k)) * X ^ (k * (k + 1) / 2) * gaussBinom X m k * gaussBinom X (m + k) k)

declarations.name: sourceDelta_eq_qFactorial
declarations.signature: theorem sourceDelta_eq_qFactorial (m : ℕ) : sourceDeltaPoly m = (X - 1) ^ m * coefficientQFactorialPoly m
declarations.docstring: The Gaussian factorial is the ordinary product with `(X-1)^m` removed.

declarations.name: sum_sourceResidue_eq_coefficientAlpha
declarations.signature: theorem sum_sourceResidue_eq_coefficientAlpha (m : ℕ) : (∑ k ∈ range (m + 1), sourceResiduePoly m k) = coefficientAlphaPoly m
declarations.docstring: Every index, with no finite rank bound: the residues sum to literal alpha.

declarations.name: sum_sourceResidue_fin_eq_coefficientAlpha
declarations.signature: theorem sum_sourceResidue_fin_eq_coefficientAlpha (m : ℕ) : (∑ k : Fin (m + 1), sourceResiduePoly m k.val) = coefficientAlphaPoly m
declarations.docstring: Literal finite-index version consumed by the remainder certificate.

declarations.name: sourceResidueQuotientPoly
declarations.signature: def sourceResidueQuotientPoly (m k n : ℕ) : ℤ[X]
declarations.docstring: Remove the required denominator from the final Delta factor explicitly.

declarations.name: sourceResidue_factor
declarations.signature: theorem sourceResidue_factor (m k n : ℕ) (hn : n < m + k) : sourceResiduePoly m k = (X ^ (n + 1) - 1) * sourceResidueQuotientPoly m k n
declarations.docstring: Every denominator of the full residue prefix is cleared, not only the short source prefix. No assumption `k ≤ m` is needed for this factor identity.

declarations.name: posDef_one_coordinate_extension
declarations.signature: private theorem posDef_one_coordinate_extension {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {A : Matrix ι ι ℝ} (hA : A.PosDef) (B : Matrix ι (Fin 1) ℝ) (D : Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) ℝ) (hdet : 0 < (Matrix.fromBlocks A B Bᴴ D).det) : (Matrix.fromBlocks A B Bᴴ D).PosDef

declarations.name: leadingPrincipalMatrix
declarations.signature: def leadingPrincipalMatrix {n : ℕ} (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ n) : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℝ
declarations.docstring: The first k rows and columns, retaining their original coordinate order.

declarations.name: posDef_of_positive_leading_determinants
declarations.signature: theorem posDef_of_positive_leading_determinants : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, M.IsHermitian → (∀ k : ℕ, ∀ hk : k ≤ n, 0 < k → 0 < (leadingPrincipalMatrix M k hk).det) → M.PosDef
declarations.docstring: Sylvester's sufficient criterion, with every nonempty leading minor explicitly required. The empty matrix is included without a spurious premise.

declarations.name: shifted_diagonal_product
declarations.signature: private theorem shifted_diagonal_product (D : ℕ → R) (h0 : D 0 = 1) : ∀ n : ℕ, (∏ i : Fin n, D (i.val + 1)) = (∏ i : Fin n, D i.val) * D n

declarations.name: determinant_of_triangular_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem determinant_of_triangular_certificate {n : ℕ} (M U : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) (D : ℕ → R) (h0 : D 0 = 1) (hU : ∀ i j, j < i → U i j = 0) (hMU : ∀ i j, i < j → (M * U) i j = 0) (hUdiag : ∀ i, U i i = D i.val) (hMUdiag : ∀ i, (M * U) i i = D (i.val + 1)) (hprev : ∀ i : Fin n, D i.val ≠ 0) : M.det = D n
declarations.docstring: Every premise is either a scalar polynomial identity, a zero entry, or a nonzero previously certified determinant. The witness U may come from any producer; the conclusion refers to the original literal matrix M.

declarations.name: leading_submatrix_mul_upper

declarations.name: leading_determinant_of_triangular_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem leading_determinant_of_triangular_certificate {N : ℕ} (M U : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) R) (D : ℕ → R) (h0 : D 0 = 1) (hU : ∀ i j, j < i → U i j = 0) (hMU : ∀ i j, i < j → (M * U) i j = 0) (hUdiag : ∀ i, U i i = D i.val) (hMUdiag : ∀ i, (M * U) i i = D (i.val + 1)) (hprev : ∀ i : Fin N, D i.val ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ N) : (M.submatrix (Fin.castLE hn) (Fin.castLE hn)).det = D n
declarations.docstring: Prefixes inherit the same determinant sequence from one full witness.

declarations.name: eventually_int_zero_of_tendsto_zero

declarations.docstring: Integer discreteness applied to an actual convergent sequence.

declarations.name: eventually_first_coefficient_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem eventually_first_coefficient_ne_zero (A B : ℕ → ℤ) (ξ : ℝ) (hne : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n ≠ 0) (hlim : Tendsto (fun n => (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n) atTop (𝓝 0)) : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, A n ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: A nonzero sufficiently small integral form must have nonzero first coefficient. In particular this does not assume nonvanishing polynomials.

declarations.name: no_small_forms_with_adjacent_determinants_tending_zero
declarations.signature: theorem no_small_forms_with_adjacent_determinants_tending_zero (A B : ℕ → ℤ) (ξ : ℝ) (hne : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n ≠ 0) (hlim : Tendsto (fun n => (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n) atTop (𝓝 0)) (hdet : Tendsto (fun n => ((A n * B (n + 1) - A (n + 1) * B n : ℤ) : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0)) : False
declarations.docstring: Nonzero integral forms tending to zero cannot have adjacent determinants that ALSO tend to zero. This is independent of the particular real target.

declarations.name: no_small_forms_of_cross_product_limits
declarations.signature: theorem no_small_forms_of_cross_product_limits (A B : ℕ → ℤ) (ξ : ℝ) (hne : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n ≠ 0) (hlim : Tendsto (fun n => (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n) atTop (𝓝 0)) (hleft : Tendsto (fun n => (A n : ℝ) * ((A (n + 1) : ℝ) * ξ - B (n + 1))) atTop (𝓝 0)) (hright : Tendsto (fun n => (A (n + 1) : ℝ) * ((A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n)) atTop (𝓝 0)) : False

declarations.name: logarithmic_region_iff_negative_balance

declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem qBinomialRatioCoeff_one_succ (q : ℝ) (k : ℕ) : qBinomialRatioCoeff 1 q (k + 1) = 0
declarations.docstring: The a=1 endpoint is important: all positive-degree coefficients vanish.

declarations.name: qBinomialRatioCoeff_lower
declarations.signature: theorem qBinomialRatioCoeff_lower {a q : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q < 1) (k : ℕ) : qPochhammerInfinity a q ≤ qBinomialRatioCoeff a q k
declarations.docstring: The lower comparison used at a=sqrt(q), with a strict endpoint.

declarations.name: qBinomialRatioCoeff_upper
declarations.signature: theorem qBinomialRatioCoeff_upper {a q : ℝ} (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) (hq0 : 0 ≤ q) (hq1 : q < 1) (k : ℕ) : qBinomialRatioCoeff a q k ≤ (qPochhammerInfinity q q)⁻¹
declarations.docstring: Uniform upper coefficient bound, including the a=1 endpoint.

declarations.name: ApproximationExponentUpper
declarations.docstring: The eventual approximation formulation of an upper irrationality exponent. It uses every integer numerator, so in particular covers reduced fractions.

declarations.name: separation_of_exponential_envelope
declarations.signature: theorem separation_of_exponential_envelope (A B p : ℤ) (q : ℕ) (ξ u v w : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hlo : Real.exp (-u) ≤ |(A : ℝ) * ξ - B|) (hup : |(A : ℝ) * ξ - B| ≤ Real.exp (-v)) (hA : |(A : ℝ)| ≤ Real.exp w) (hcross : Real.log (2 * (q : ℝ)) ≤ v) : Real.exp (-(u + w)) ≤ |ξ - (p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)|
declarations.docstring: The exponential form of the finite separation lemma.

declarations.name: exists_quadratic_crossing
declarations.signature: lemma exists_quadratic_crossing (T x : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) : ∃ n : ℕ, x ≤ T * (n : ℝ) ^ 2
declarations.docstring: A positive quadratic crosses every fixed real level.

declarations.name: approximationExponentUpper_of_quadratic_forms
declarations.signature: theorem approximationExponentUpper_of_quadratic_forms (A B : ℕ → ℤ) (ξ α τ : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hτ : 0 < τ) (hne : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n ≠ 0) (hA : QuadExpUpper (fun n => (A n : ℝ)) α) (hL : QuadLogRate (fun n => (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n) (-τ)) : ApproximationExponentUpper ξ (1 + α / τ)
declarations.docstring: Exact two-sided quadratic error rate and an upper coefficient rate imply an upper approximation exponent. This proof includes the integer-mesh choice and discards only a finite initial segment of the supplied estimates.

declarations.name: irrational_and_measure_of_quadratic_forms
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_and_measure_of_quadratic_forms (A B : ℕ → ℤ) (ξ α τ : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hτ : 0 < τ) (hne : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n ≠ 0) (hA : QuadExpUpper (fun n => (A n : ℝ)) α) (hL : QuadLogRate (fun n => (A n : ℝ) * ξ - B n) (-τ)) : Irrational ξ ∧ ApproximationExponentUpper ξ (1 + α / τ)
declarations.docstring: The same hypotheses also prove irrationality, including when some early forms vanish or early coefficient pairs are degenerate.

declarations.name: exists_same_signature_same_bin_different_value
declarations.signature: theorem exists_same_signature_same_bin_different_value {α β γ ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [DecidableEq ι] (f : α → β) (g : α → γ) (bin : α → ι) (k : ℕ) (hg : ∀ x : α, (Finset.univ.filter fun y => g y = g x).card ≤ k) (hcard : (Fintype.card β * Fintype.card ι) * k < Fintype.card α) : ∃ x y : α, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y ∧ bin x = bin y ∧ g x ≠ g y
declarations.docstring: Add a finite bin label to the modular signature before applying bounded-fibre escape. The cardinal cost is the product of signature count, bin count, and maximum multiplicity of an exact observable value.

declarations.name: exists_same_signature_small_nonzero_real_difference
declarations.signature: theorem exists_same_signature_small_nonzero_real_difference {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq ι] (f : α → β) (g : α → ℝ) (bin : α → ι) (k : ℕ) (δ : ℝ) (hg : ∀ x : α, (Finset.univ.filter fun y => g y = g x).card ≤ k) (hdiam : ∀ x y : α, bin x = bin y → |g x - g y| < δ) (hcard : (Fintype.card β * Fintype.card ι) * k < Fintype.card α) : ∃ x y : α, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y ∧ 0 < |g x - g y| ∧ |g x - g y| < δ
declarations.docstring: A finite binning certificate whose cells have real diameter less than δ turns the previous result into a small, nonzero real difference.

declarations.name: exists_same_signature_same_bin_different_value_conditional
declarations.signature: theorem exists_same_signature_same_bin_different_value_conditional {α β γ ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] [DecidableEq ι] (f : α → β) (g : α → γ) (bin : α → ι) (k : ℕ) (hg : ∀ x : α, (Finset.univ.filter fun y => f y = f x ∧ g y = g x).card ≤ k) (hcard : (Fintype.card β * Fintype.card ι) * k < Fintype.card α) : ∃ x y : α, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y ∧ bin x = bin y ∧ g x ≠ g y
declarations.docstring: Only multiplicity inside one modular fibre needs to be controlled. Values that agree in different modular fibres cannot be the bad collision here.

declarations.name: exists_small_real_escape_of_conditional_multiplicity
declarations.signature: theorem exists_small_real_escape_of_conditional_multiplicity {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq ι] (f : α → β) (g : α → ℝ) (bin : α → ι) (k : ℕ) (δ : ℝ) (hg : ∀ x : α, (Finset.univ.filter fun y => f y = f x ∧ g y = g x).card ≤ k) (hdiam : ∀ x y : α, bin x = bin y → |g x - g y| < δ) (hcard : (Fintype.card β * Fintype.card ι) * k < Fintype.card α) : ∃ x y : α, x ≠ y ∧ f x = f y ∧ 0 < |g x - g y| ∧ |g x - g y| < δ
declarations.docstring: Quantitative real escape with the sharper, conditional multiplicity.

declarations.name: rational_separation_of_small_integer_form
declarations.signature: theorem rational_separation_of_small_integer_form (A B p q : ℤ) (ξ : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hsmall : 2 * (q : ℝ) * |(A : ℝ) * ξ - B| ≤ 1) : |(A : ℝ) * ξ - B| ≤ |(A : ℝ)| * |ξ - (p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)|
declarations.docstring: An integral form of size at most `1/(2*q)` controls separation from every rational with denominator `q`, even when that rational equals the row ratio.

declarations.name: trigammaSeries
declarations.docstring: The series representation of the trigamma function. Only this series is used; the identification with `d²/dx² log Γ` is classical and not needed.

declarations.name: summable_trigammaTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_trigammaTerm {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => 1 / ((k : ℝ) + x) ^ 2)

declarations.name: trigammaSeries_antitone
declarations.signature: theorem trigammaSeries_antitone {x y : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (hxy : x ≤ y) : trigammaSeries y ≤ trigammaSeries x
declarations.docstring: The trigamma series is decreasing on the positive axis.

declarations.name: sum_le_trigammaSeries_sub
declarations.signature: theorem sum_le_trigammaSeries_sub {u v : ℝ} (hu : 0 < u) (huv : u < v) (K : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range K, (1 / ((k : ℝ) + u) ^ 2 - 1 / ((k : ℝ) + v) ^ 2) ≤ trigammaSeries u - trigammaSeries v
declarations.docstring: Any finite partial sum of the termwise difference bounds `ψ₁(u) - ψ₁(v)` from below when `0 < u < v`.

declarations.name: firstTerm_le_trigammaSeries_sub
declarations.signature: theorem firstTerm_le_trigammaSeries_sub {u v : ℝ} (hu : 0 < u) (huv : u < v) : 1 / u ^ 2 - 1 / v ^ 2 ≤ trigammaSeries u - trigammaSeries v
declarations.docstring: The `k = 0` term alone.

declarations.name: trigammaSeries_le
declarations.signature: theorem trigammaSeries_le (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) : trigammaSeries x ≤ 1 / x ^ 2 + Real.pi ^ 2 / 6
declarations.docstring: `ψ₁(x) ≤ 1/x² + π²/6` for `0 < x`: split off the `k = 0` term and compare the rest with `ζ(2)`.

declarations.name: zudilinJTerm
declarations.signature: noncomputable def zudilinJTerm (u v : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: One interval's contribution `ψ₁(u) - ψ₁(v)`.

declarations.name: zudilinJ
declarations.docstring: `J = ∫₀¹ ω(x) d(-ψ'(x))` over the thirteen intervals on which `ω = 1` (Zudilin 2004, end of Section 5), written as the trigamma series.

declarations.name: zudilinC1
declarations.docstring: `C₁ = (α₀+α₁+α₂)β - (α₁²+α₂²+β²)/2 = 1091/2`, Zudilin's (25).

declarations.name: zudilinC0
declarations.docstring: `C₀ = α₁²/2 + α₀α₁ + (β-α₂)(α₂-α₁) - (3/π²)(m² - J)` with `m = 15`, Zudilin's (26).

declarations.name: zudilinContour
declarations.docstring: The rational-base threshold `θ* = C₀/C₁ = 1/μ`, where `μ = C₁/C₀` is the irrationality-exponent bound of Zudilin's Theorem 1.

declarations.name: ZudilinContourRegion
declarations.docstring: The parameter region of the authored rational-base theorem: reduced bases `a/b` with `log b / log a < θ*`. Membership is the hypothesis the ordinary proof consumes; it is not an irrationality statement.

declarations.name: zudilinJTerm_ge
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinJTerm_ge {u v : ℝ} (hu : 0 < u) (huv : u < v) : 1 / u ^ 2 - 1 / v ^ 2 ≤ zudilinJTerm u v

declarations.name: zudilinJ_ge
declarations.docstring: The `k = 0` terms already give `J ≥ 77.6` (the exact value is `J = 77.943…`; the thirteen first terms sum to `77.609…`).

declarations.name: eightyOne_twoHundredths_lt_zudilinContour
declarations.docstring: **`81/200 < θ*`.** The older `81/200` cutoff is a rational sub-boundary of the contour.

declarations.name: zudilinJ_le
declarations.docstring: Telescoping through the ordered, disjoint intervals: every right endpoint `vᵢ` is at most the next left endpoint `uᵢ₊₁`, and `ψ₁` is decreasing, so `J ≤ ψ₁(1/14) - ψ₁(14/15) ≤ ψ₁(1/14)`.

declarations.name: zudilinContour_lt_half
declarations.docstring: **`θ* < 1/2`.** With `C₁ = 545.5` and `C₀ < 266`, the contour sits below `266/545.5 = 0.4876`.

declarations.name: zudilinContourRegion_of_zudilinHeightRegion
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinContourRegion_of_zudilinHeightRegion {a b : ℕ} (h : ZudilinHeightRegion a b) : ZudilinContourRegion a b
declarations.docstring: The older `81/200` region is contained in the contour region.

declarations.name: thirtyoneFour_mem_zudilinContourRegion
declarations.docstring: `31/4` lies in the contour region.

declarations.name: zudilinContourRegion_pow
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinContourRegion_pow (a b r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (h : ZudilinContourRegion a b) : ZudilinContourRegion (a ^ r) (b ^ r)
declarations.docstring: The logarithmic height ratio is invariant under a common positive power.

declarations.name: thirtyoneFour_power_mem_zudilinContourRegion
declarations.signature: theorem thirtyoneFour_power_mem_zudilinContourRegion (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) : ZudilinContourRegion (31 ^ r) (4 ^ r)
declarations.docstring: Every positive power of `31/4` lies in the contour region.

declarations.name: half_lt_threeHalves_log_ratio
declarations.docstring: `1/2 < log 2 / log 3`, from `3 < 2²`.

declarations.name: threeHalves_outside_zudilinContourRegion
declarations.docstring: `3/2` lies outside the full contour region, not only outside its `81/200` sub-boundary. This is a method boundary for this family of forms, not a statement about the arithmetic nature of `F(3/2)`.

declarations.name: two_mul_zudilinM
declarations.signature: theorem two_mul_zudilinM (n : ℤ) : zudilinA1 n * (zudilinA1 n - 1) + 2 * zudilinA0 n * zudilinA1 n + 2 * (zudilinB n - zudilinA2 n) * (zudilinA2 n - zudilinA1 n) = 2 * (266 * n ^ 2 + 34 * n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Zudilin's (16): `2M(a;b) = a₁(a₁-1) + 2a₀a₁ + 2(b-a₂)(a₂-a₁)` equals `2(266n² + 34n + 1)`.

declarations.name: twoMulZudilinSummandDegree
declarations.docstring: Twice the `p`-degree of the `k`-th summand `A_k p^{a₀k}` of `A(p)`: `2a₀k` plus twice the exponent of (8), plus twice the degrees `(a₁-1)(k-a₁)` and `(b-k-1)(k-a₂)` of the two Gaussian binomials.

declarations.name: twoMulZudilinSummandDegree_succ_sub
declarations.signature: theorem twoMulZudilinSummandDegree_succ_sub (n k : ℤ) : twoMulZudilinSummandDegree n (k + 1) - twoMulZudilinSummandDegree n k = 2 * (40 * n + 1 - k)
declarations.docstring: The degree step `d_{k+1} - d_k = 40n + 1 - k`, positive for `k ≤ b - 2 = 27n`; hence the top summand `k = b - 1` carries the degree of `A(p)` alone and no cancellation can occur.

declarations.name: twoMulZudilinSummandDegree_top
declarations.signature: theorem twoMulZudilinSummandDegree_top (n : ℤ) : twoMulZudilinSummandDegree n (zudilinB n - 1) = 1091 * n ^ 2 + 81 * n + 2
declarations.docstring: The top degree: `2 deg A_n = 1091n² + 81n + 2`, so `deg A_n / n² → C₁`.

declarations.name: twoMulZudilinSummandDegree_step_pos
declarations.signature: theorem twoMulZudilinSummandDegree_step_pos (n k : ℤ) (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hk : k ≤ zudilinB n - 2) : 0 < twoMulZudilinSummandDegree n (k + 1) - twoMulZudilinSummandDegree n k
declarations.docstring: The step is positive on the whole summation range `a₂ ≤ k ≤ b - 2`.

declarations.name: sevenHalves_power_certificate
declarations.docstring: The integer-power comparison underlying the logarithmic height bound.

declarations.name: sevenHalves_rational_margin
declarations.docstring: The exact rational boundary used after `1 / π² < 1 / 9`.

declarations.name: BundschuhVaananenHeightRegion
declarations.docstring: The elementary parameter region occurring in the external Bundschuh--Väänänen theorem for a positive reduced rational base `a / b`. This definition records only the height inequality; it does not internalize the external analytic irrationality theorem.

declarations.name: sevenHalves_log_ratio_lt
declarations.docstring: The power certificate implies the strict logarithmic ratio bound.

declarations.name: one_div_pi_sq_lt_one_nine
declarations.docstring: The elementary Archimedean estimate used in the published height test.

declarations.name: sevenHalves_bundschuhVaananen_margin
declarations.signature: theorem sevenHalves_bundschuhVaananen_margin : Real.log 2 / Real.log 7 < (1 : ℝ) / 2 - 1 / Real.pi ^ 2
declarations.docstring: The exact margin needed to verify the special `α = -1` case of the Bundschuh--Väänänen height criterion at `q = 7/2`.

declarations.name: sevenHalves_archimedean_height_condition
declarations.signature: theorem sevenHalves_archimedean_height_condition : Real.log 7 / Real.log ((7 : ℝ) / 2) < ((1 : ℝ) / 2 + 1 / Real.pi ^ 2)⁻¹
declarations.docstring: The complete elementary Archimedean height inequality for `q = 7/2`. Applying the external analytic irrationality theorem remains a separate step.

declarations.name: CoordinatewiseCorridor
declarations.signature: def CoordinatewiseCorridor (a b N K Q digit : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The finite arithmetic core of a coordinatewise rational-base corridor. `digit` abstracts the final divisor coefficient that is individually cleared.

declarations.name: coordinatewiseCorridor_implies_pow_lt_linear
declarations.signature: theorem coordinatewiseCorridor_implies_pow_lt_linear {a b N K Q digit : ℕ} (h : CoordinatewiseCorridor a b N K Q digit) : b ^ (N + K + 1) < a * (N + K)
declarations.docstring: Clearing the `K`-th coordinate and making the positive remainder smaller than one forces the numerator base to satisfy a power-versus-linear bound.

declarations.name: three_mul_lt_two_pow_succ
declarations.docstring: Exponential growth already dominates the required linear corridor for all `x ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: threeHalves_no_coordinatewiseCorridor
declarations.signature: theorem threeHalves_no_coordinatewiseCorridor {N K Q digit : ℕ} (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hK : 1 ≤ K) : ¬ CoordinatewiseCorridor 3 2 N K Q digit
declarations.docstring: The literal coordinatewise Erdős corridor cannot occur at base `3/2` once both the shift and cleared window are nonempty.

declarations.name: rationalBasePrefixQ
declarations.signature: def rationalBasePrefixQ (r s : ℚ) (coeff : ℕ → ℚ) (N : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The first `N` terms of a rational-base divisor-series coordinate. The coefficient sequence is kept abstract so the recurrence is reusable beyond the divisor function.

declarations.name: rationalBasePrefixQ_succ
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem rationalBasePrefixQ_succ (r s : ℚ) (coeff : ℕ → ℚ) (N : ℕ) : rationalBasePrefixQ r s coeff (N + 1) = rationalBasePrefixQ r s coeff N + coeff (N + 1) * s ^ (N + 1) / r ^ (N + 1)

declarations.name: rationalBaseClearedTailQ
declarations.signature: def rationalBaseClearedTailQ (r s B F : ℚ) (coeff : ℕ → ℚ) (N : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: Denominator-cleared tail state for a putative rational value `F`.

declarations.name: rationalBaseClearedTailQ_succ
declarations.signature: theorem rationalBaseClearedTailQ_succ {r s B F : ℚ} {coeff : ℕ → ℚ} (hr : r ≠ 0) (N : ℕ) : rationalBaseClearedTailQ r s B F coeff (N + 1) = r * rationalBaseClearedTailQ r s B F coeff N - B * coeff (N + 1) * s ^ (N + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact rational-base recurrence. The forcing term contains `s^(N+1)`; this is the denominator-base tax absent from the integer-base case `s = 1`.

declarations.name: rationalBaseForcingNat
declarations.signature: def rationalBaseForcingNat (s B : ℕ) (coeff : ℕ → ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Natural-valued magnitude of the forcing term in the cleared recurrence.

declarations.name: twoPow_le_rationalBaseForcingNat
declarations.signature: theorem twoPow_le_rationalBaseForcingNat {s B : ℕ} {coeff : ℕ → ℕ} {N : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) (hB : 1 ≤ B) (hc : 1 ≤ coeff (N + 1)) : 2 ^ (N + 1) ≤ rationalBaseForcingNat s B coeff N
declarations.docstring: At every genuine noninteger denominator base `s ≥ 2`, positive coefficients force at least exponential `2^(N+1)` growth.

declarations.name: rationalBaseForcingNat_one
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem rationalBaseForcingNat_one (B : ℕ) (coeff : ℕ → ℕ) (N : ℕ) : rationalBaseForcingNat 1 B coeff N = B * coeff (N + 1)
declarations.docstring: In the integer-base case the denominator-base tax collapses exactly.

declarations.name: rationalPadeDenExpTwice
declarations.docstring: Twice the proposed common denominator exponent `Eₙ = (3n² - n) / 2`.

declarations.name: rationalPadePSummandDenExpTwice
declarations.docstring: Twice the denominator exponent of the `k`-th summand in the homogenised little-`q` Legendre `P` polynomial.

declarations.name: rationalPadePSummandDenExpTwice_le
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadePSummandDenExpTwice_le {n k : ℤ} (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hkn : k ≤ n) : rationalPadePSummandDenExpTwice n k ≤ rationalPadeDenExpTwice n
declarations.docstring: The doubled `P`-summand exponent never exceeds the proposed common exponent when `0 ≤ k ≤ n`. The gap factors as `(n-k)(3n-k-1)`.

declarations.name: rationalPadeQMaxDenExpTwice
declarations.docstring: Twice the maximal denominator exponent in the `Q`-summand calculation, after the change of variables `j = n - m - 1`.

declarations.name: rationalPadeQMaxDenExpTwice_gap
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadeQMaxDenExpTwice_gap (n m : ℤ) : rationalPadeDenExpTwice n - rationalPadeQMaxDenExpTwice n m = 2 * (n + m * (m - 1))
declarations.docstring: Exact doubled gap identity for the rational `Q`-summand maximum: `2(Eₙ-Fmax) = 2(n + m(m-1))`.

declarations.name: rationalPadeQMaxDenExpTwice_le
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadeQMaxDenExpTwice_le {n m : ℤ} (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hm : 1 ≤ m) : rationalPadeQMaxDenExpTwice n m ≤ rationalPadeDenExpTwice n
declarations.docstring: In the nonvanishing `m ≥ 1` range, the doubled `Q` exponent is bounded by the same common exponent.

declarations.name: rationalPadeError
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rationalPadeError (S : ℝ) (U V : ℤ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The real error of an integer Padé coefficient pair `(U,V)` at `S`.

declarations.name: rationalPadeExteriorDet
declarations.signature: def rationalPadeExteriorDet (Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The exterior determinant of two integer Padé coefficient pairs. For the adjacent Zudilin construction this is `Uₙ Vₘ - Uₘ Vₙ`. Unlike either individual coefficient pair, the determinant can inherit every divisor common to the two `U` coefficients and every divisor common to the two `V` coefficients.

declarations.name: rationalPadeError_mul
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadeError_mul (S : ℝ) (c U V : ℤ) : rationalPadeError S (c * U) (c * V) = (c : ℝ) * rationalPadeError S U V
declarations.docstring: Scaling both coefficients in one Padé row scales its error by exactly the same factor. Row content therefore carries no hidden analytic improvement.

declarations.name: rationalPadeExteriorDet_mul_contents
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadeExteriorDet_mul_contents (cn cm Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ) : rationalPadeExteriorDet (cn * Un) (cn * Vn) (cm * Um) (cm * Vm) = cn * cm * rationalPadeExteriorDet Un Vn Um Vm
declarations.docstring: Rowwise contents factor from the exterior determinant exactly. Thus any local divisor coming only from independent contents of the two rows is paid for by the same product in the Archimedean determinant height.

declarations.name: natAbs_rationalPadeExteriorDet_mul_contents
declarations.signature: theorem natAbs_rationalPadeExteriorDet_mul_contents (cn cm Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ) : Int.natAbs (rationalPadeExteriorDet (cn * Un) (cn * Vn) (cm * Um) (cm * Vm)) = Int.natAbs cn * Int.natAbs cm * Int.natAbs (rationalPadeExteriorDet Un Vn Um Vm)
declarations.docstring: The Archimedean determinant height acquires exactly the absolute product of the two row contents—no less and no more.

declarations.name: contentProduct_dvd_rationalPadeExteriorDet
declarations.signature: theorem contentProduct_dvd_rationalPadeExteriorDet (cn cm Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ) : cn * cm ∣ rationalPadeExteriorDet (cn * Un) (cn * Vn) (cm * Um) (cm * Vm)
declarations.docstring: The product of the two row contents is therefore an explicit divisor of the scaled exterior determinant. The residual arithmetic object is precisely the determinant of the primitive rows.

declarations.name: rationalPadeExteriorDet_cast_eq
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadeExteriorDet_cast_eq (S : ℝ) (Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ) : (rationalPadeExteriorDet Un Vn Um Vm : ℝ) = (Um : ℝ) * rationalPadeError S Un Vn - (Un : ℝ) * rationalPadeError S Um Vm
declarations.docstring: Exact cancellation of the target value in the exterior determinant.

declarations.name: commonU_dvd_rationalPadeExteriorDet

declarations.docstring: A divisor common to the two `U` coefficients divides their exterior determinant. This is the abstract arithmetic core of the returned common `3`-adic gain.

declarations.name: commonV_dvd_rationalPadeExteriorDet
declarations.signature: theorem commonV_dvd_rationalPadeExteriorDet {d Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ} (hVn : d ∣ Vn) (hVm : d ∣ Vm) : d ∣ rationalPadeExteriorDet Un Vn Um Vm
declarations.docstring: A divisor common to the two `V` coefficients also divides their exterior determinant. This is the companion interface for local factors carried by the second coefficient channel.

declarations.name: rationalPadeExteriorDet_pos_of_left_neg_right_pos
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadeExteriorDet_pos_of_left_neg_right_pos {S : ℝ} {Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ} (hLn : 0 < rationalPadeError S Un Vn) (hLm : 0 < rationalPadeError S Um Vm) (hUn : Un < 0) (hUm : 0 < Um) : 0 < rationalPadeExteriorDet Un Vn Um Vm
declarations.docstring: If both Padé errors are positive while the first coefficients have signs `Uₙ < 0 < Uₘ`, the exterior determinant is strictly positive.

declarations.name: rationalPadeExteriorDet_neg_of_left_pos_right_neg
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadeExteriorDet_neg_of_left_pos_right_neg {S : ℝ} {Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ} (hLn : 0 < rationalPadeError S Un Vn) (hLm : 0 < rationalPadeError S Um Vm) (hUn : 0 < Un) (hUm : Um < 0) : rationalPadeExteriorDet Un Vn Um Vm < 0

declarations.name: rationalPadeExteriorDet_ne_zero_of_left_neg_right_pos
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadeExteriorDet_ne_zero_of_left_neg_right_pos {S : ℝ} {Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ} (hLn : 0 < rationalPadeError S Un Vn) (hLm : 0 < rationalPadeError S Um Vm) (hUn : Un < 0) (hUm : 0 < Um) : rationalPadeExteriorDet Un Vn Um Vm ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Positive errors and alternating coefficient signs rule out cancellation in the adjacent exterior determinant.

declarations.name: rationalPadeExteriorDet_ne_zero_of_left_pos_right_neg
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPadeExteriorDet_ne_zero_of_left_pos_right_neg {S : ℝ} {Un Vn Um Vm : ℤ} (hLn : 0 < rationalPadeError S Un Vn) (hLm : 0 < rationalPadeError S Um Vm) (hUn : 0 < Un) (hUm : Um < 0) : rationalPadeExteriorDet Un Vn Um Vm ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The other alternating coefficient-sign configuration also rules out cancellation.

declarations.name: erased_geometric_pole_product

declarations.name: twoSelector_det_height_decay_tradeoff
declarations.signature: theorem twoSelector_det_height_decay_tradeoff (A₁ B₁ A₂ B₂ F ε : ℝ) (h₁ : |B₁ * F - A₁| ≤ ε) (h₂ : |B₂ * F - A₂| ≤ ε) : |A₁ * B₂ - A₂ * B₁| ≤ ε * (|B₁| + |B₂|)
declarations.docstring: The exterior determinant forces a denominator-height versus remainder tradeoff. If both real forms are at most `ε`, their determinant is at most `ε` times the sum of their denominator-coordinate heights.

declarations.name: twoSelector_unimodular_height_decay_tradeoff
declarations.signature: theorem twoSelector_unimodular_height_decay_tradeoff (A₁ B₁ A₂ B₂ u v w z F H ε : ℝ) (hunimod : |u * z - v * w| = 1) (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hu : |u| ≤ H) (hv : |v| ≤ H) (hw : |w| ≤ H) (hz : |z| ≤ H) (h₁ : |(u * B₁ + v * B₂) * F - (u * A₁ + v * A₂)| ≤ ε) (h₂ : |(w * B₁ + z * B₂) * F - (w * A₁ + z * A₂)| ≤ ε) : |A₁ * B₂ - A₂ * B₁| ≤ 2 * H * ε * (|B₁| + |B₂|)
declarations.docstring: For a unimodular recombination whose four coefficients have height at most `H`, simultaneous decay to `ε` forces `|det| ≤ 2 H ε (|B₁|+|B₂|)`. Thus the enormous continued-fraction coefficients in the finite #1049 certificate are constrained by the preserved determinant, rather than being merely a weak search artefact.

declarations.name: rational_integerLinearForm_gap
declarations.signature: theorem rational_integerLinearForm_gap (a q A B : ℤ) (hq : 0 < q) (hne : (B : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) - (A : ℝ) ≠ 0) : (1 : ℝ) / q ≤ |(B : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) - (A : ℝ)|
declarations.docstring: A nonzero integral linear form at the rational target `a / q` has absolute value at least `1 / q`. Coprimality is unnecessary for this lower bound.

declarations.name: rational_twoSelector_remainder_gap
declarations.signature: theorem rational_twoSelector_remainder_gap (a q A₁ B₁ A₂ B₂ : ℤ) (hq : 0 < q) (hdet : A₁ * B₂ - A₂ * B₁ ≠ 0) : (1 : ℝ) / q ≤ |(B₁ : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) - (A₁ : ℝ)| ∨ (1 : ℝ) / q ≤ |(B₂ : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) - (A₂ : ℝ)|
declarations.docstring: At a rational target, two non-collinear integral coefficient rows cannot both have sub-`1/q` remainders.

declarations.name: rational_twoSelector_not_both_tendsto_zero
declarations.signature: theorem rational_twoSelector_not_both_tendsto_zero (a q : ℤ) (hq : 0 < q) (A₁ B₁ A₂ B₂ : ℕ → ℤ) (hdet : ∀ n, A₁ n * B₂ n - A₂ n * B₁ n ≠ 0) : ¬(Tendsto (fun n ↦ (B₁ n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) - (A₁ n : ℝ)) atTop (nhds 0) ∧ Tendsto (fun n ↦ (B₂ n : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) - (A₂ n : ℝ)) atTop (nhds 0))
declarations.docstring: Cofinal two-form decay through non-collinear integral rows is impossible at every rational target. This is the exact obstruction to treating the continued-fraction recombination as an independent irrationality engine.

declarations.name: sourceIntervals
declarations.docstring: The thirteen rational half-open intervals, not a replacement support.

declarations.name: sourceIntervals_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem sourceIntervals_bounds (uv : ℚ × ℚ) (huv : uv ∈ sourceIntervals) : (0 : ℝ) < uv.1 ∧ (uv.1 : ℝ) < uv.2 ∧ (uv.2 : ℝ) ≤ 1

declarations.name: omegaSupport_iff_sourceIntervals
declarations.signature: theorem omegaSupport_iff_sourceIntervals (x : ℝ) : PaperR7.InOmegaSupport x ↔ ∃ uv ∈ sourceIntervals, (uv.1 : ℝ) ≤ x ∧ x < (uv.2 : ℝ)

declarations.name: reciprocal_block_iff
declarations.signature: theorem reciprocal_block_iff (n l k u v : ℝ) (hl : 0 < l) (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hu : 0 < u) (huv : u < v) : k + u ≤ n / l ∧ n / l < k + v ↔ n / (k + v) < l ∧ l ≤ n / (k + u)
declarations.docstring: Reversing reciprocals reverses which boundary is strict.

declarations.name: fract_mem_iff_reciprocal_block
declarations.signature: theorem fract_mem_iff_reciprocal_block (n l u v : ℝ) (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hl : 0 < l) (hu : 0 < u) (huv : u < v) (hv : v ≤ 1) : u ≤ Int.fract (n / l) ∧ Int.fract (n / l) < v ↔ ∃ k : ℤ, 0 ≤ k ∧ n / ((k : ℝ) + v) < l ∧ l ≤ n / ((k : ℝ) + u)
declarations.docstring: The integer block index is forced to be the actual floor. This proves both directions, including points exactly at rational endpoints.

declarations.name: actual_sourceWeight_indicator
declarations.signature: theorem actual_sourceWeight_indicator (n l : ℕ) : sourceWeight n l = if PaperR7.InOmegaSupport (Int.fract ((n : ℝ) / l)) then 1 else 0
