declarations.docstring: The exact source weight is the indicator of the literal interval union.

declarations.name: actual_sourceWeight_one_iff_blocks
declarations.signature: theorem actual_sourceWeight_one_iff_blocks (n l : ℕ) (hl : 0 < l) : sourceWeight n l = 1 ↔ ∃ uv ∈ sourceIntervals, ∃ k : ℤ, 0 ≤ k ∧ (n : ℝ) / ((k : ℝ) + (uv.2 : ℝ)) < l ∧ (l : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) / ((k : ℝ) + (uv.1 : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: All thirteen blocks are connected to the actual weight, not merely to an unrelated periodic step function.

declarations.name: finiteTotientPrefix
declarations.signature: noncomputable def finiteTotientPrefix (N : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: A finite totient prefix retains the exact integer cut-off.

declarations.name: finite_totient_block
declarations.signature: theorem finite_totient_block (N : ℕ) (lo hi : ℝ) (h : lo ≤ hi) : (∑ l ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, if lo < (l : ℝ) ∧ (l : ℝ) ≤ hi then (l.totient : ℤ) else 0) = finiteTotientPrefix N hi - finiteTotientPrefix N lo
declarations.docstring: Exact finite interval summation, before any analytic approximation.

declarations.name: actual_reciprocal_totient_block
declarations.signature: theorem actual_reciprocal_totient_block (N : ℕ) (n k u v : ℝ) (hn : 0 ≤ n) (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hu : 0 < u) (huv : u < v) : (∑ l ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, if n / (k + v) < (l : ℝ) ∧ (l : ℝ) ≤ n / (k + u) then (l.totient : ℤ) else 0) = finiteTotientPrefix N (n / (k + u)) - finiteTotientPrefix N (n / (k + v))
declarations.docstring: A reciprocal block is a difference S(n/(k+u))-S(n/(k+v)), not the difference with either endpoint shifted by one.

declarations.name: actual_weighted_totient_indicator
declarations.signature: theorem actual_weighted_totient_indicator (n : ℕ) : actualWeightedTotientSum n = ∑ l ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (15 * n), if ∃ uv ∈ sourceIntervals, (uv.1 : ℝ) ≤ Int.fract ((n : ℝ) / l) ∧ Int.fract ((n : ℝ) / l) < (uv.2 : ℝ) then (l.totient : ℤ) else 0
declarations.docstring: Literal weighted sum to literal thirteen-interval indicator.

declarations.name: zudilinNormExpTwice
declarations.signature: def zudilinNormExpTwice (a0 a1 a2 b : ℤ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Twice the normalising exponent used in the finite Heine--Zudilin coefficient calculation. Doubling removes every parity and integer-division side condition from the algebraic certificate.

declarations.name: zudilinPartialFractionExpTwice
declarations.signature: def zudilinPartialFractionExpTwice (a1 a2 b k : ℤ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The explicit monomial exponent in the `k`-th partial-fraction coefficient.

declarations.name: zudilinBottomExpTwice
declarations.signature: def zudilinBottomExpTwice (a0 a1 a2 b k : ℤ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The bottom exponent of the normalised `U` summand indexed by `k`.

declarations.name: zudilinRawDegreeTwice
declarations.signature: def zudilinRawDegreeTwice (a0 a1 a2 b k : ℤ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The degree of the raw `U` summand indexed by `k`, before the common normalisation and cyclotomic factor.

declarations.name: zudilinBottomExpTwice_at_a2
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinBottomExpTwice_at_a2 (a0 a1 a2 b : ℤ) : zudilinBottomExpTwice a0 a1 a2 b a2 = 2 * (a2 - a1) * (a0 + a2 - b)
declarations.docstring: At the bottom endpoint, the normalised exponent is exactly `(a₂-a₁)(a₀+a₂-b)`.

declarations.name: zudilinBottomExpTwice_succ_sub
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinBottomExpTwice_succ_sub (a0 a1 a2 b k : ℤ) : zudilinBottomExpTwice a0 a1 a2 b (k + 1) - zudilinBottomExpTwice a0 a1 a2 b k = 2 * (a0 - b + k + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact first difference of consecutive normalised bottom exponents.

declarations.name: zudilinBottomExpTwice_strict_step
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinBottomExpTwice_strict_step {a0 a1 a2 b k : ℤ} (hcone : b ≤ a0 + a2) (hk : a2 ≤ k) : zudilinBottomExpTwice a0 a1 a2 b k < zudilinBottomExpTwice a0 a1 a2 b (k + 1)
declarations.docstring: Inside the source cone, bottom exponents strictly increase from `a₂` onward.

declarations.name: zudilinRawDegreeTwice_succ_sub
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinRawDegreeTwice_succ_sub (a0 a1 a2 b k : ℤ) : zudilinRawDegreeTwice a0 a1 a2 b (k + 1) - zudilinRawDegreeTwice a0 a1 a2 b k = 2 * (a0 + a1 + a2 - k - 2)
declarations.docstring: Exact first difference of consecutive raw degrees.

declarations.name: zudilinRawDegreeTwice_strict_step
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinRawDegreeTwice_strict_step {a0 a1 a2 b k : ℤ} (ha1 : 0 < a1) (hcone : b ≤ a0 + a2) (hk : k ≤ b - 2) : zudilinRawDegreeTwice a0 a1 a2 b k < zudilinRawDegreeTwice a0 a1 a2 b (k + 1)
declarations.docstring: Inside the source cone, raw summand degrees strictly increase through the last allowed index `b-1`.

declarations.name: homEvalThreeTwo
declarations.signature: def homEvalThreeTwo (W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Integer homogeneous evaluation of an integral polynomial at `(3,2)`, using the declared ambient width `W`.

declarations.name: bottomJet3
declarations.signature: def bottomJet3 (R W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : ZMod (3 ^ R)
declarations.docstring: The bottom `3`-adic endpoint jet of depth `R`.

declarations.name: topJet2
declarations.signature: def topJet2 (S W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : ZMod (2 ^ S)
declarations.docstring: The top `2`-adic endpoint jet of depth `S`.

declarations.name: FourJetSignature
declarations.docstring: The four simultaneous endpoint congruences for a coefficient pair: bottom and top jets in both channels.

declarations.name: fourJetSignature
declarations.signature: def fourJetSignature (R S W : ℕ) (U V : Polynomial ℤ) : FourJetSignature R S
declarations.docstring: Four-jet signature of one integral coefficient pair.

declarations.name: selectedFourJetSum
declarations.signature: def selectedFourJetSum {n : ℕ} (R S W : ℕ) (forms : Fin n → Polynomial ℤ × Polynomial ℤ) (ε : Fin n → Bool) : FourJetSignature R S
declarations.docstring: Sum of the four-jet signatures selected by a binary coefficient vector.

declarations.name: fourJetSignature_card
declarations.signature: theorem fourJetSignature_card (R S : ℕ) : Fintype.card (FourJetSignature R S) = (3 ^ R) ^ 2 * (2 ^ S) ^ 2
declarations.docstring: Exact size of the simultaneous four-jet target. Each coefficient channel contributes one copy of the relevant endpoint modulus.

declarations.name: exists_distinct_binary_selectors_same_fourJet
declarations.signature: theorem exists_distinct_binary_selectors_same_fourJet {n R S W : ℕ} (forms : Fin n → Polynomial ℤ × Polynomial ℤ) (hcard : Fintype.card (FourJetSignature R S) < 2 ^ n) : ∃ ε η : Fin n → Bool, ε ≠ η ∧ selectedFourJetSum R S W forms ε = selectedFourJetSum R S W forms η
declarations.docstring: Once the binary selector space is larger than the four-jet target, two distinct subsets have the same simultaneous endpoint signature. Subtracting their indicator vectors gives a nonzero coefficient vector in `{-1,0,1}` whose four endpoint jets cancel. This theorem supplies kernel existence only; it does not prove that the resulting analytic remainder is nonzero or that its height beats the local gain.

declarations.name: exists_distinct_binary_selectors_same_fourJet_of_rank
declarations.signature: theorem exists_distinct_binary_selectors_same_fourJet_of_rank {n R S W : ℕ} (forms : Fin n → Polynomial ℤ × Polynomial ℤ) (hR : 0 < R) (hrank : 4 * R + 2 * S ≤ n) : ∃ ε η : Fin n → Bool, ε ≠ η ∧ selectedFourJetSum R S W forms ε = selectedFourJetSum R S W forms η
declarations.docstring: A concrete rank--depth threshold for four-jet cancellation. At positive bottom depth, `3 ^ R < 2 ^ (2 * R)`, so `4 * R + 2 * S` available binary forms already outnumber the exact four-jet target. No independence or nonvanishing conclusion is hidden here: the resulting selector difference is nonzero, but its polynomial pair or analytic remainder may still vanish.

declarations.name: bottomJet3_eq_zero_iff_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem bottomJet3_eq_zero_iff_dvd (R W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : bottomJet3 R W P = 0 ↔ ((3 ^ R : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W P
declarations.docstring: Vanishing of the bottom jet is exactly divisibility of the homogeneous evaluation by the requested power of `3`.

declarations.name: topJet2_eq_zero_iff_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem topJet2_eq_zero_iff_dvd (S W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : topJet2 S W P = 0 ↔ ((2 ^ S : ℕ) : ℤ) ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W P
declarations.docstring: Vanishing of the top jet is exactly divisibility of the homogeneous evaluation by the requested power of `2`.

declarations.name: homEvalThreeTwo_mod_three
declarations.signature: theorem homEvalThreeTwo_mod_three (W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : (homEvalThreeTwo W P : ZMod 3) = (P.coeff 0 : ZMod 3) * 2 ^ W
declarations.docstring: Modulo `3`, homogeneous evaluation retains only the constant coefficient.

declarations.name: homEval
declarations.signature: def homEval (a b W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Integer homogeneous evaluation at a reduced numerator--denominator pair. The existing `homEvalThreeTwo` is the specialization `(a,b) = (3,2)`. This generic form is the arithmetic object used in Proposition 3.6 of the paper.

declarations.name: homEval_mod_left
declarations.signature: theorem homEval_mod_left (a b W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : (homEval a b W P : ZMod a) = (P.coeff 0 : ZMod a) * b ^ W
declarations.docstring: Modulo the numerator, homogeneous evaluation retains only the constant coefficient. No primality assumption on the modulus is needed.

declarations.name: homEval_mod_right
declarations.signature: theorem homEval_mod_right (a b W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : (homEval a b W P : ZMod b) = (P.coeff W : ZMod b) * a ^ W
declarations.docstring: Modulo the denominator, homogeneous evaluation retains only the coefficient at the declared top width.

declarations.name: homEval_isCoprime_left_of_const_unit
declarations.signature: theorem homEval_isCoprime_left_of_const_unit {a b W : ℕ} (P : Polynomial ℤ) (hab : a.Coprime b) (hconst : P.coeff 0 = 1 ∨ P.coeff 0 = -1) : IsCoprime (homEval a b W P) (a : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: A unit constant coefficient makes the homogeneous value coprime to the numerator whenever the numerator and denominator are coprime.

declarations.name: homEval_isCoprime_right_of_top_unit
declarations.signature: theorem homEval_isCoprime_right_of_top_unit {a b W : ℕ} (P : Polynomial ℤ) (hab : a.Coprime b) (htop : P.coeff W = 1 ∨ P.coeff W = -1) : IsCoprime (homEval a b W P) (b : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: A unit top coefficient makes the homogeneous value coprime to the denominator whenever the numerator and denominator are coprime.

declarations.name: homEval_isCoprime_mul_of_endpoint_units
declarations.signature: theorem homEval_isCoprime_mul_of_endpoint_units {a b W : ℕ} (P : Polynomial ℤ) (hab : a.Coprime b) (htop : P.coeff W = 1 ∨ P.coeff W = -1) (hconst : P.coeff 0 = 1 ∨ P.coeff 0 = -1) : IsCoprime (homEval a b W P) ((a * b : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Unit endpoints make one homogeneous evaluation coprime to the full numerator--denominator product.

declarations.name: cyclotomicHomEval_isCoprime_mul
declarations.signature: theorem cyclotomicHomEval_isCoprime_mul {a b m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hab : a.Coprime b) : IsCoprime (homEval a b (Nat.totient m) (Polynomial.cyclotomic m ℤ)) ((a * b : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Proposition 3.6: for a reduced rational base, every positive-index homogenized cyclotomic value is coprime to the numerator and denominator. The order assumptions `a > b ≥ 1` used in the paper identify a rational base greater than one; the coprimality conclusion itself needs only `Coprime a b`.

declarations.name: homEvalThreeTwo_mod_two
declarations.signature: theorem homEvalThreeTwo_mod_two (W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) : (homEvalThreeTwo W P : ZMod 2) = (P.coeff W : ZMod 2) * 3 ^ W
declarations.docstring: Modulo `2`, homogeneous evaluation retains only the coefficient at the declared top width.

declarations.name: three_not_dvd_homEvalThreeTwo_of_const_unit
declarations.signature: theorem three_not_dvd_homEvalThreeTwo_of_const_unit (W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) (hunit : P.coeff 0 = 1 ∨ P.coeff 0 = -1) : ¬ (3 : ℤ) ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W P
declarations.docstring: A unit constant coefficient prevents any factor `3` in the homogeneous specialisation.

declarations.name: two_not_dvd_homEvalThreeTwo_of_top_unit
declarations.signature: theorem two_not_dvd_homEvalThreeTwo_of_top_unit (W : ℕ) (P : Polynomial ℤ) (hunit : P.coeff W = 1 ∨ P.coeff W = -1) : ¬ (2 : ℤ) ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W P
declarations.docstring: A unit coefficient at the declared top width prevents any factor `2` in the homogeneous specialisation.

declarations.name: not_two_dvd_both_homEval_of_left_top_unit
declarations.signature: theorem not_two_dvd_both_homEval_of_left_top_unit (W : ℕ) (U V : Polynomial ℤ) (hunit : U.coeff W = 1 ∨ U.coeff W = -1) : ¬ ((2 : ℤ) ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W U ∧ (2 : ℤ) ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W V)
declarations.docstring: If one channel has a unit top coefficient, the two coefficient channels cannot have a common factor `2` after homogeneous specialisation.

declarations.name: not_three_dvd_both_homEval_of_right_const_unit
declarations.signature: theorem not_three_dvd_both_homEval_of_right_const_unit (W : ℕ) (U V : Polynomial ℤ) (hunit : V.coeff 0 = 1 ∨ V.coeff 0 = -1) : ¬ ((3 : ℤ) ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W U ∧ (3 : ℤ) ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W V)
declarations.docstring: If one channel has a unit constant coefficient, the two coefficient channels cannot have a common factor `3` after homogeneous specialisation.

declarations.name: commonMultiplier_not_two_not_three_of_endpoint_units
declarations.signature: theorem commonMultiplier_not_two_not_three_of_endpoint_units (c : ℤ) (W : ℕ) (U V : Polynomial ℤ) (hUtop : U.coeff W = 1 ∨ U.coeff W = -1) (hVconst : V.coeff 0 = 1 ∨ V.coeff 0 = -1) (hcU : c ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W U) (hcV : c ∣ homEvalThreeTwo W V) : (¬ (2 : ℤ) ∣ c) ∧ (¬ (3 : ℤ) ∣ c)
declarations.docstring: A genuine common multiplier of the two specialised coefficient channels cannot contain either local prime needed at the rational base `3 / 2`, provided the left channel has a unit top endpoint and the right channel has a unit bottom endpoint. Hence any useful `2`-adic or `3`-adic gain must survive rowwise primitive normalisation; it cannot be manufactured by common content of one Padé pair.

declarations.name: twice_le_of_irrationalityExponent_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem twice_le_of_irrationalityExponent_bounds {μ C0 C1 : ℝ} (hC0 : 0 < C0) (hlower : 2 ≤ μ) (hupper : μ ≤ C1 / C0) : 2 * C0 ≤ C1
declarations.docstring: The only analytic input needed from an irrationality-exponent argument: if an irrational number has exponent at least `2` and a source construction bounds that exponent by `C₁ / C₀`, then `2 C₀ ≤ C₁`.

declarations.name: three_two_scalar_margin_neg
declarations.signature: theorem three_two_scalar_margin_neg {C0 C1 : ℝ} (hC1 : 0 < C1) (hsource : C0 ≤ 0 ∨ 2 * C0 ≤ C1) : C0 * Real.log 3 - C1 * Real.log 2 < 0
declarations.docstring: The parameter inequality forced by an integer-base irrationality-exponent estimate makes the rational-base `3/2` product-formula margin strictly negative. The theorem deliberately consumes the source-backed inequality as a hypothesis rather than importing the analytic construction.

declarations.name: ZudilinHeightRegion
declarations.docstring: The parameter region cut out by the single inequality `log b / log a < 81 / 200`; no analytic hypotheses are included.

declarations.name: thirtyoneFour_power_certificate
declarations.docstring: The exact integer comparison behind the `31 / 4` parameter certificate.

declarations.name: thirtyoneFour_log_ratio_lt_eightyOne_twoHundredths
declarations.docstring: The power certificate gives the required logarithmic height inequality.

declarations.name: thirtyoneFour_mem_zudilinHeightRegion
declarations.docstring: The base `31 / 4` lies in the height region.

declarations.name: zudilinHeightRegion_pow
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinHeightRegion_pow (a b r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (h : ZudilinHeightRegion a b) : ZudilinHeightRegion (a ^ r) (b ^ r)
declarations.docstring: The logarithmic height ratio is invariant under a common positive power.

declarations.name: thirtyoneFour_power_mem_zudilinHeightRegion
declarations.signature: theorem thirtyoneFour_power_mem_zudilinHeightRegion (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) : ZudilinHeightRegion (31 ^ r) (4 ^ r)
declarations.docstring: Every positive power of `31 / 4` satisfies the same height threshold.

declarations.name: twoFifths_lt_thirtyoneFour_log_ratio
declarations.docstring: The rational number `2 / 5` is a strict lower bound for `log 4 / log 31`.

declarations.name: bundschuhVaananenMargin_lt_twoFifths
declarations.docstring: The old Bundschuh--Väänänen margin lies below `2 / 5`.

declarations.name: thirtyoneFour_outside_bundschuhVaananenHeightRegion
declarations.docstring: The base `31 / 4` lies outside the Bundschuh--Väänänen height region.

declarations.name: threeHalves_zudilin_power_obstruction
declarations.docstring: The exact integer comparison placing `3 / 2` beyond the `81 / 200` threshold defined above.

declarations.name: eightyOneTwoHundredths_lt_threeHalves_log_ratio
declarations.docstring: The height ratio of `3 / 2` is strictly larger than `81 / 200`.

declarations.name: threeHalves_outside_zudilinHeightRegion
declarations.docstring: The height region defined above does not contain `3 / 2`. This is a method boundary, not a rationality or irrationality theorem for the corresponding Lambert value.

declarations.name: threeHalves_outside_bundschuhVaananenHeightRegion
declarations.docstring: The Bundschuh--Väänänen height region also does not contain `3 / 2`; its margin is smaller than the threshold already crossed above.

declarations.name: coeff_prod_eq_zero_of_lt_sum
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_prod_eq_zero_of_lt_sum {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (f : ι → PowerSeries ℤ) (e : ι → ℕ) : ∀ s : Finset ι, (∀ i ∈ s, ∀ d, d < e i → PowerSeries.coeff d (f i) = 0) → ∀ d, d < ∑ i ∈ s, e i → PowerSeries.coeff d (∏ i ∈ s, f i) = 0
declarations.docstring: A finite product of power series has no coefficient strictly below the sum of the entrywise vanishing thresholds.

declarations.name: coeff_prod_sum_eq_prod_coeff
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_prod_sum_eq_prod_coeff {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (f : ι → PowerSeries ℤ) (e : ι → ℕ) : ∀ s : Finset ι, (∀ i ∈ s, ∀ d, d < e i → PowerSeries.coeff d (f i) = 0) → PowerSeries.coeff (∑ i ∈ s, e i) (∏ i ∈ s, f i) = ∏ i ∈ s, PowerSeries.coeff (e i) (f i)
declarations.docstring: At the sum of the entrywise thresholds, the coefficient of a finite product of power series is the product of the entrywise threshold coefficients.

declarations.name: coeff_mul_first
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_mul_first {φ ψ : PowerSeries ℤ} {m₁ m₂ : ℕ} (h₁ : ∀ d, d < m₁ → PowerSeries.coeff d φ = 0) (h₂ : ∀ d, d < m₂ → PowerSeries.coeff d ψ = 0) : (∀ d, d < m₁ + m₂ → PowerSeries.coeff d (φ * ψ) = 0) ∧ PowerSeries.coeff (m₁ + m₂) (φ * ψ) = PowerSeries.coeff m₁ φ * PowerSeries.coeff m₂ ψ
declarations.docstring: Two-factor form of the filtered product calculus. Used repeatedly below to peel a known initial monomial off a source tail.

declarations.name: coeff_det_eq_of_unique_minimizing_permutation
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_det_eq_of_unique_minimizing_permutation {N : ℕ} (M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) (PowerSeries ℤ)) (e : Fin N → Fin N → ℕ) (a : Fin N → Fin N → ℤ) (σ₀ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) (B : ℕ) (hzero : ∀ i j d, d < e i j → PowerSeries.coeff d (M i j) = 0) (hlead : ∀ i j, PowerSeries.coeff (e i j) (M i j) = a i j) (hmain : ∑ i, e (σ₀ i) i = B) (hother : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N), σ ≠ σ₀ → B < ∑ i, e (σ i) i) : PowerSeries.coeff B M.det = (Equiv.Perm.sign σ₀ : ℤ) * ∏ i, a (σ₀ i) i
declarations.docstring: **Unique-minimum Leibniz coefficient bridge.** If every entry of `M` vanishes below its own threshold `e i j` and has coefficient `a i j` there, and if one permutation `σ₀` minimizes the entry-order weight `∑ i, e (σ i) i` strictly, then the first determinant coefficient is exactly the signed product of the entrywise threshold coefficients. This is the coefficient companion of `order_det_eq_of_unique_minimizing_permutation`, and unlike that theorem it needs no nonvanishing hypothesis on the `a i j`.

declarations.name: zudilinLeadingEntryOrder
declarations.signature: def zudilinLeadingEntryOrder {N : ℕ} (j l : Fin N) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The exact `X`-order of the associated-graded entry in row `j`, column `l`.

declarations.name: val_revPerm_add_val
declarations.signature: theorem val_revPerm_add_val {N : ℕ} (i : Fin N) : ((((Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) i : Fin N) : ℕ) : ℤ) + ((i : ℕ) : ℤ) = (N : ℤ) - 1
declarations.docstring: The reversal is characterized pointwise by `rev i + i = N - 1`.

declarations.name: sum_sq_shift_eq_two_mul_sub
declarations.signature: theorem sum_sq_shift_eq_two_mul_sub {N : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) : (∑ i : Fin N, (((σ i : ℕ) : ℤ) + ((i : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((N : ℤ) - 1)) ^ 2) = 2 * (∑ i : Fin N, ((σ i : ℕ) : ℤ) * ((i : ℕ) : ℤ)) - 2 * ∑ i : Fin N, ((((Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) i : Fin N) : ℕ) : ℤ) * ((i : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: **The exact square identity.** The entry-order excess of an arbitrary permutation over the reversal is exactly a sum of squares. This replaces the usual transposition or rearrangement argument by a single algebraic identity.

declarations.name: sum_val_mul_val_lt_of_ne_revPerm
declarations.signature: theorem sum_val_mul_val_lt_of_ne_revPerm {N : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) (hσ : σ ≠ Fin.revPerm) : (∑ i : Fin N, (((Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) i : Fin N) : ℕ) * (i : ℕ)) < ∑ i : Fin N, ((σ i : ℕ)) * (i : ℕ)
declarations.docstring: **Strict uniqueness of the reversal.** Every other permutation has strictly larger column-index weight `∑_i (σ i)·i`.

declarations.name: sum_zudilinLeadingEntryOrder_revPerm
declarations.signature: theorem sum_zudilinLeadingEntryOrder_revPerm (N : ℕ) : (∑ i : Fin N, zudilinLeadingEntryOrder ((Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) i) i) = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, j ^ 2
declarations.docstring: The reversal's Hankel entry-order weight is exactly `∑_{j<N} j²`, i.e. Zudilin's exponent `B_N`.

declarations.name: sum_zudilinLeadingEntryOrder_lt_of_ne_revPerm
declarations.signature: theorem sum_zudilinLeadingEntryOrder_lt_of_ne_revPerm {N : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) (hσ : σ ≠ Fin.revPerm) : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, j ^ 2) < ∑ i : Fin N, zudilinLeadingEntryOrder (σ i) i
declarations.docstring: **The reversal is the unique minimizer of the Hankel entry-order weight.** Every other permutation strictly exceeds Zudilin's exponent `B_N`, so no cancellation can occur at degree `B_N`.

declarations.name: zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix_apply
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix_apply (N : ℕ) (j l : Fin N) : zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix N j l = PowerSeries.C (((-1 : ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ)) * (zudilinTransformedRowCoeff (j : ℕ) : ℤ)) * PowerSeries.X ^ zudilinLeadingEntryOrder j l
declarations.docstring: Every entry of the associated-graded leading matrix is a signed monomial.

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix_eq_zero_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix_eq_zero_of_lt (N : ℕ) (j l : Fin N) (d : ℕ) (hd : d < zudilinLeadingEntryOrder j l) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix N j l) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix_first
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix_first (N : ℕ) (j l : Fin N) : PowerSeries.coeff (zudilinLeadingEntryOrder j l) (zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix N j l) = ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ)) * (zudilinTransformedRowCoeff (j : ℕ) : ℤ)

declarations.name: coeff_X_pow_sub_X_pow_eq_zero_of_lt
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_X_pow_sub_X_pow_eq_zero_of_lt {a b d : ℕ} (hab : a < b) (hd : d < a) : PowerSeries.coeff d ((PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℤ) ^ b - PowerSeries.X ^ a) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_X_pow_sub_X_pow_first
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_X_pow_sub_X_pow_first {a b : ℕ} (hab : a < b) : PowerSeries.coeff a ((PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℤ) ^ b - PowerSeries.X ^ a) = -1

declarations.name: coeff_vandermondeRow_eq_zero_of_lt
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_vandermondeRow_eq_zero_of_lt {N : ℕ} (i : Fin N) (d : ℕ) (hd : d < ∑ _j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (i : ℕ)) : PowerSeries.coeff d (∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, ((PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) - PowerSeries.X ^ (i : ℕ))) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_vandermondeRow_first
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_vandermondeRow_first {N : ℕ} (i : Fin N) : PowerSeries.coeff (∑ _j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (i : ℕ)) (∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, ((PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) - PowerSeries.X ^ (i : ℕ))) = (-1 : ℤ) ^ (Finset.Ioi i).card

declarations.name: coeff_vandermondeProd_eq_zero_of_lt
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_vandermondeProd_eq_zero_of_lt (N : ℕ) (d : ℕ) (hd : d < ∑ i : Fin N, ∑ _j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (i : ℕ)) : PowerSeries.coeff d (∏ i : Fin N, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, ((PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) - PowerSeries.X ^ (i : ℕ))) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_vandermondeProd_first
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_vandermondeProd_first (N : ℕ) : PowerSeries.coeff (∑ i : Fin N, ∑ _j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (i : ℕ)) (∏ i : Fin N, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, ((PowerSeries.X : PowerSeries ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) - PowerSeries.X ^ (i : ℕ))) = (-1 : ℤ) ^ (∑ i : Fin N, (Finset.Ioi i).card)

declarations.name: prod_zudilinAssociatedLeadingRowScale
declarations.signature: private theorem prod_zudilinAssociatedLeadingRowScale (N : ℕ) : (∏ j : Fin N, zudilinAssociatedLeadingRowScale j) = PowerSeries.C (∏ j : Fin N, ((-1 : ℤ) ^ (j : ℕ) * (zudilinTransformedRowCoeff (j : ℕ) : ℤ))) * PowerSeries.X ^ (∑ j : Fin N, (j : ℕ) * ((j : ℕ) + 1) / 2)

declarations.name: sum_card_Ioi_eq_sum_val
declarations.signature: private theorem sum_card_Ioi_eq_sum_val (N : ℕ) : (∑ i : Fin N, (Finset.Ioi i).card) = ∑ j : Fin N, (j : ℕ)

declarations.name: sum_vandermondeExponent
declarations.signature: private theorem sum_vandermondeExponent (N : ℕ) : (∑ j : Fin N, (j : ℕ) * ((j : ℕ) + 1) / 2) + (∑ i : Fin N, ∑ _j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (i : ℕ)) = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, j ^ 2

declarations.name: coeff_det_zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_det_zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix (N : ℕ) : PowerSeries.coeff (∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, j ^ 2) (zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix N).det = ∏ j ∈ Finset.range N, (zudilinTransformedRowCoeff j : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: **Exact leading coefficient of the associated-graded determinant.** This sharpens the landed nonvanishing statement `det_zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix_ne_zero` to the exact value `∏_{j<N} (j+1)²(j+2)/2 = (N!)²(N+1)!/2^N`, by reading the Vandermonde product coefficientwise. The two sign contributions `∏_j (-1)^j` and `∏_{i<j} (-1)` cancel.

declarations.name: coeff_det_zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix_leibniz
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_det_zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix_leibniz (N : ℕ) : PowerSeries.coeff (∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, j ^ 2) (zudilinAssociatedLeadingMatrix N).det = ((Equiv.Perm.sign (Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) : ℤˣ) : ℤ) * ∏ i : Fin N, ((-1 : ℤ) ^ ((((Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) i : Fin N)) : ℕ) * (zudilinTransformedRowCoeff ((((Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) i : Fin N)) : ℕ) : ℤ))

declarations.name: signedRowProduct_revPerm
declarations.signature: theorem signedRowProduct_revPerm (N : ℕ) : ((Equiv.Perm.sign (Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) : ℤˣ) : ℤ) * ∏ i : Fin N, ((-1 : ℤ) ^ ((((Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) i : Fin N)) : ℕ) * (zudilinTransformedRowCoeff ((((Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) i : Fin N)) : ℕ) : ℤ)) = ∏ j ∈ Finset.range N, (zudilinTransformedRowCoeff j : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: **The reversal's sign cancels the row signs.** Equating the two evaluations of the same leading determinant coefficient leaves precisely the positive product of row coefficients.

declarations.name: sum_range_id_eq_choose_two
declarations.signature: theorem sum_range_id_eq_choose_two (N : ℕ) : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, j) = N.choose 2

declarations.name: prod_neg_one_pow_range
declarations.signature: theorem prod_neg_one_pow_range (N : ℕ) : (∏ j ∈ Finset.range N, (-1 : ℤ) ^ j) = (-1 : ℤ) ^ (N.choose 2)
declarations.docstring: The row signs assemble to `(-1)^(N choose 2)`.

declarations.name: sign_finRevPerm
declarations.signature: theorem sign_finRevPerm (N : ℕ) : ((Equiv.Perm.sign (Fin.revPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin N)) : ℤˣ) : ℤ) = (-1 : ℤ) ^ (N.choose 2)
declarations.docstring: **Sign of the reversing permutation on `Fin N`.** Reading one and the same leading determinant coefficient through the Vandermonde product and through the Leibniz expansion at the unique minimizing permutation forces `sgn(rev) = (-1)^(N choose 2)`, which is exactly the sign that cancels the row signs `∏_j (-1)^j`.

declarations.name: zudilinBackwardShiftedMomentMatrix_apply
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinBackwardShiftedMomentMatrix_apply (N : ℕ) (v : ℕ → PowerSeries ℤ) (j l : Fin N) : zudilinBackwardShiftedMomentMatrix N v j l = zudilinBackwardShiftApply (j : ℕ) ((j : ℕ) + (l : ℕ)) v
declarations.docstring: Reindexing the lower-unitriangular row operation as the source operator `D_j` applied to moment index `j+l`.

declarations.name: zudilinNormalizedHankelDet
declarations.signature: noncomputable def zudilinNormalizedHankelDet (N : ℕ) : PowerSeries ℤ
declarations.docstring: Zudilin's normalized Hankel determinant `V_N^*`.

declarations.name: zudilinTransformedMomentMatrix
declarations.signature: noncomputable def zudilinTransformedMomentMatrix (N : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) (PowerSeries ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The matrix of source-transformed moments `D_j v_{j+l}^*`.

declarations.name: det_zudilinTransformedMomentMatrix
declarations.signature: theorem det_zudilinTransformedMomentMatrix (N : ℕ) : (zudilinTransformedMomentMatrix N).det = zudilinNormalizedHankelDet N
declarations.docstring: The source row operations do not change the Hankel determinant.

declarations.name: one_sub_X_pow_fifth_expand
declarations.signature: private theorem one_sub_X_pow_fifth_expand (m : ℕ) : ((1 : PowerSeries ℤ) - PowerSeries.X ^ m) ^ 5 = 1 - PowerSeries.C (5 : ℤ) * PowerSeries.X ^ m + PowerSeries.C (10 : ℤ) * PowerSeries.X ^ (2 * m) - PowerSeries.C (10 : ℤ) * PowerSeries.X ^ (3 * m) + PowerSeries.C (5 : ℤ) * PowerSeries.X ^ (4 * m) - PowerSeries.X ^ (5 * m)

declarations.name: coeff_one_sub_X_pow_fifth_middle
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_one_sub_X_pow_fifth_middle (m d : ℕ) (h1 : m < d) (h2 : d < 2 * m) : PowerSeries.coeff d ((1 - PowerSeries.X ^ m : PowerSeries ℤ) ^ 5) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_one_sub_X_pow_fifth_double
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_one_sub_X_pow_fifth_double (m d : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hd : d = 2 * m) : PowerSeries.coeff d ((1 - PowerSeries.X ^ m : PowerSeries ℤ) ^ 5) = 10

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit_eq_numerator
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit_eq_numerator (n t d : ℕ) (hd : d < 2 * n + t + 2) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n t) = PowerSeries.coeff d ((1 - PowerSeries.X ^ (n + 1) : PowerSeries ℤ) ^ 3 * (1 - PowerSeries.X ^ (n + t + 1)) ^ 2)
declarations.docstring: Below the first moving denominator factor the source step unit agrees with its exact numerator `(1-q^{n+1})^3 (1-q^{n+t+1})^2`.

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit_zero_middle
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit_zero_middle (n d : ℕ) (h1 : n + 1 < d) (h2 : d < 2 * n + 2) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n 0) = 0
declarations.docstring: Between its first and second associated grades the zero-state source step is exactly the constant series.

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit_zero_double
declarations.docstring: **The second associated grade of the zero-state source step is `11`.** Ten from `(1-q^{n+1})^5` and one from the denominator factor `(1-q^{2n+2})^{-1}`.

declarations.name: coeff_step_sub_one_low
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_step_sub_one_low (m t d : ℕ) (hd : d ≤ m) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit m t - 1) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_step_zero_sub_one_of_ne
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_step_zero_sub_one_of_ne (m d : ℕ) (hd : d ≤ 2 * m + 1) (hne : d ≠ m + 1) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit m 0 - 1) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_step_zero_sub_one_first
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_step_zero_sub_one_first (m d : ℕ) (hd : d = m + 1) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit m 0 - 1) = -5

declarations.name: coeff_step_zero_sub_one_double
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_step_zero_sub_one_double (m d : ℕ) (hd : d = 2 * m + 2) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit m 0 - 1) = 11

declarations.name: coeff_step_pos_sub_one_first
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_step_pos_sub_one_first (m t d : ℕ) (ht : t ≠ 0) (hd : d = m + 1) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit m t - 1) = -3

declarations.name: zudilinTwoStepTail
declarations.signature: noncomputable def zudilinTwoStepTail (n t : ℕ) : PowerSeries ℤ
declarations.docstring: The exact two-step combination `D_2` applied to the `t`-th source tail.

declarations.name: zudilinTwoStepFactor
declarations.signature: noncomputable def zudilinTwoStepFactor (n t : ℕ) : PowerSeries ℤ
declarations.docstring: The exact cofactor multiplying the `t`-th source tail after two backward shifts.

declarations.name: zudilinTwoStepTail_eq
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinTwoStepTail_eq (n t : ℕ) : zudilinTwoStepTail n t = zudilinNormalizedTail n t * zudilinTwoStepFactor n t

declarations.name: coeff_mul_first_at
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_mul_first_at {φ ψ : PowerSeries ℤ} {m₁ m₂ D : ℕ} (h₁ : ∀ d, d < m₁ → PowerSeries.coeff d φ = 0) (h₂ : ∀ d, d < m₂ → PowerSeries.coeff d ψ = 0) (hD : D = m₁ + m₂) : PowerSeries.coeff D (φ * ψ) = PowerSeries.coeff m₁ φ * PowerSeries.coeff m₂ ψ

declarations.name: coeff_normalizedTail_leading'
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_normalizedTail_leading' (n t d : ℕ) (hd : d = (n + 1) * t) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedTail n t) = 1

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinTwoStepFactor_constant_of_pos
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinTwoStepFactor_constant_of_pos (n t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) : PowerSeries.coeff 0 (zudilinTwoStepFactor n t) = 0
declarations.docstring: Every positive source state contributes a factor of `q`, so the two-step cofactor has no constant term.

declarations.name: zudilinTwoStepFactor_zero_eq
declarations.signature: private theorem zudilinTwoStepFactor_zero_eq (n : ℕ) : zudilinTwoStepFactor n 0 = (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit (n + 1) 0 - 1) - PowerSeries.X * (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n 0 - 1) + (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n 0 - 1) * (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit (n + 1) 0 - 1)

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinTwoStepFactor_zero_eq_zero_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinTwoStepFactor_zero_eq_zero_of_lt (n d : ℕ) (hd : d < 2 * n + 3) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinTwoStepFactor n 0) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinTwoStepFactor_zero_first
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinTwoStepFactor_zero_first (n : ℕ) : PowerSeries.coeff (2 * n + 3) (zudilinTwoStepFactor n 0) = 14

declarations.name: zudilinTwoStepFactor_one_eq
declarations.signature: private theorem zudilinTwoStepFactor_one_eq (n : ℕ) : zudilinTwoStepFactor n 1 = PowerSeries.X ^ 2 * (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit (n + 1) 1 - 1) - PowerSeries.X * (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n 1 - 1) + PowerSeries.X ^ 2 * ((zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n 1 - 1) * (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit (n + 1) 1 - 1))

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinTwoStepFactor_one_eq_zero_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinTwoStepFactor_one_eq_zero_of_lt (n d : ℕ) (hd : d < n + 2) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinTwoStepFactor n 1) = 0

declarations.name: zudilinTwoStepFactor_two_eq
declarations.signature: private theorem zudilinTwoStepFactor_two_eq (n : ℕ) : zudilinTwoStepFactor n 2 = (PowerSeries.X - PowerSeries.X ^ 2 - PowerSeries.X ^ 3 + PowerSeries.X ^ 4) + PowerSeries.X ^ 2 * (PowerSeries.X ^ 2 * (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n 2 - 1) + PowerSeries.X ^ 2 * (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit (n + 1) 2 - 1) + PowerSeries.X ^ 2 * ((zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n 2 - 1) * (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit (n + 1) 2 - 1)) - (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n 2 - 1) - PowerSeries.X * (zudilinNormalizedTailStepUnit n 2 - 1))

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinTwoStepTail_eq_zero_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinTwoStepTail_eq_zero_of_lt (n t d : ℕ) (hd : d < 2 * n + 3) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinTwoStepTail n t) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinTwoStepTail_first
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinTwoStepTail_first (n t : ℕ) : PowerSeries.coeff (2 * n + 3) (zudilinTwoStepTail n t) = if t = 0 then 14 else if t = 1 then 3 else if t = 2 then 1 else 0

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinNormalizedMoment_range
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinNormalizedMoment_range (n d T : ℕ) (hT : d < (n + 1) * T) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedMoment n) = ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinNormalizedTail n t)
declarations.docstring: Only finitely many source tails reach any fixed degree, so the exact moment coefficient is any sufficiently long finite sum.

declarations.name: coeff_moment_eq_sum_range
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_moment_eq_sum_range (m d e : ℕ) (he : e ≤ d) : PowerSeries.coeff e (zudilinNormalizedMoment m) = PowerSeries.coeff e (∑ t ∈ Finset.range (d + 1), zudilinNormalizedTail m t)

declarations.name: coeff_X_mul_congr
declarations.signature: private theorem coeff_X_mul_congr (A B : PowerSeries ℤ) (d : ℕ) (h : ∀ e, e < d → PowerSeries.coeff e A = PowerSeries.coeff e B) : PowerSeries.coeff d (PowerSeries.X * A) = PowerSeries.coeff d (PowerSeries.X * B)

declarations.name: sum_zudilinTwoStepTail
declarations.signature: private theorem sum_zudilinTwoStepTail (l T : ℕ) : (∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, zudilinTwoStepTail l t) = ((∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, zudilinNormalizedTail (l + 1 + 1) t) - ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, zudilinNormalizedTail (l + 1) t) - PowerSeries.X * ((∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, zudilinNormalizedTail (l + 1) t) - ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, zudilinNormalizedTail l t)

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment_two_eq
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment_two_eq (l d : ℕ) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment 2 l) = ∑ t ∈ Finset.range (d + 1), PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinTwoStepTail l t)
declarations.docstring: The second transformed row is the exact coefficientwise sum of two-step source tails.

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment_two_eq_zero_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment_two_eq_zero_of_lt (l d : ℕ) (hd : d < 2 * l + 3) : PowerSeries.coeff d (zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment 2 l) = 0

declarations.name: coeff_zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment_two_first
declarations.docstring: **The second transformed row, uniformly in the column.** The exact coefficient of `q^(2l+3)` in `D_2 v_{2+l}^*` is `18 = 3²·4/2`, assembled from the three surviving source states `t = 0, 1, 2` as `14 + 3 + 1`.

declarations.name: order_zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment_two
declarations.docstring: The exact order of the second transformed row.

declarations.name: zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment_two_initialMonomial
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment_two_initialMonomial (l : ℕ) : PowerSeries.order (zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment 2 l) = 2 * l + 3 ∧ PowerSeries.coeff (2 * l + 3) (zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment 2 l) = 18
declarations.docstring: **Complete second transformed-row initial monomial, in every column.** This is the first row beyond `zudilinTransformedNormalizedMoment_one_initialMonomial` of `AdelicHeightBridge.lean`; `AllRow/Producer.lean` treats every row.

declarations.name: ZudilinRowInitialMonomial
declarations.docstring: The source-row input: in every column, transformed row `j` has initial monomial `(-1)^j (j+1)²(j+2)/2 · q^{j(j+1)/2 + jl}`. Rows `j ≤ 2` are proved here (`zudilinRowInitialMonomial_of_le_two`); all rows by `zudilinRowInitialMonomial_all`.

declarations.name: zudilinRowInitialMonomial_of_le_two
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinRowInitialMonomial_of_le_two {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ 2) : ZudilinRowInitialMonomial j

declarations.name: zudilinSharpHankelOrderAndCoeff_of_rowInitialMonomial
declarations.signature: theorem zudilinSharpHankelOrderAndCoeff_of_rowInitialMonomial (h : ∀ j : ℕ, ZudilinRowInitialMonomial j) (N : ℕ) : PowerSeries.order (zudilinNormalizedHankelDet N) = ((∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, j ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ∧ PowerSeries.coeff (∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, j ^ 2) (zudilinNormalizedHankelDet N) = ∏ j ∈ Finset.range N, (zudilinTransformedRowCoeff j : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: **Conditional sharp order and leading coefficient of `V_N^*`.** Given the row initial monomials (proved above for `j ≤ 2`, open for `j ≥ 3`), the normalized Hankel determinant has exactly Zudilin's exponent `∑_{j<N} j²` *and* leading coefficient `∏_{j<N} (j+1)²(j+2)/2 = (N!)²(N+1)!/2^N`. The hypothesis is purely row level; everything determinant level — the Leibniz bridge, the unique-minimizer combinatorics and the sign cancellation — is unconditional and proved in this module. Feeding the closed forms of `zudilinSharpHankelOrderAndCoeff_algebraicAssembly` then gives `6·ord = N(N-1)(2N-1)` and `2^N·lc = (N!)²(N+1)!`.

declarations.name: divides_jump
declarations.signature: theorem divides_jump (a b L u v m : ℤ) (hstep : v = a * u - b * L) (hu : m ∣ u) (hL : m ∣ L) : m ∣ v - u
declarations.docstring: A persistent divisor of the state and clearing denominator divides the jump, independently of the integral forcing coefficient.

declarations.name: no_jump_through_fence
declarations.signature: theorem no_jump_through_fence (a b L u v rho B z : ℤ) (hv : 0 < v) (hrho : 1 ≤ rho) (_hB : 0 ≤ B) (hcap : rho * v ≤ u + B) (hstep : rho * v = a * u - b * L) (hz : B < z) (hbefore : u < z + B) (hcover : ∀ x : ℤ, z ≤ x → x < z + B → ∃ m : ℤ, B < m ∧ m ∣ x ∧ m ∣ L) : v < z + B
declarations.docstring: An exact transition cannot cross a covered interval whose persistent moduli all exceed the positive jump budget. All variables are integers; `rho ≥ 1` is enough for this finite implication.

declarations.name: stays_below_fence
declarations.signature: theorem stays_below_fence (a b L U rho : ℕ → ℤ) (B z : ℤ) (hU : ∀ n, 0 < U n) (hrho : ∀ n, 1 ≤ rho n) (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hz : B < z) (hcap : ∀ n, rho n * U (n + 1) ≤ U n + B) (hstep : ∀ n, rho n * U (n + 1) = a n * U n - b n * L n) (hstart : U 0 < z + B) (hcover : ∀ n, ∀ x : ℤ, z ≤ x → x < z + B → ∃ m : ℤ, B < m ∧ m ∣ x ∧ m ∣ L n) : ∀ n, U n < z + B
declarations.docstring: Iterate the finite fence. This theorem does not construct its cover.

declarations.name: centred_error_eq_decrement
declarations.signature: theorem centred_error_eq_decrement (a b C D Cnext : ℤ) (hC : Cnext = a * C - b * D) : b * D - (a - 1) * C = C - Cnext
declarations.docstring: The weighted centred error is the raw numerator decrement.

declarations.name: weighted_recurrence_of_two_zero
declarations.signature: theorem weighted_recurrence_of_two_zero (a anext b bnext C D Dnext : ℤ) (hC : C ≠ 0) (hD : Dnext = a * D) (hzero : b * D = (a - 1) * C) (hzeronext : bnext * Dnext = (anext - 1) * C) : b * (anext - 1) = bnext * a * (a - 1)
declarations.docstring: Two zero-error states give the weighted Sylvester equality, without assuming that the numerator coefficient is invertible.

declarations.name: two_cycle_first_step
declarations.docstring: The two-step coefficient-(1,3) example, parameterised polynomially.

declarations.name: two_cycle_second_step
declarations.signature: theorem two_cycle_second_step (k : ℤ) : 2 * (6 * k ^ 2 + 12 * k + 5) - 3 * ((2 * k + 1) * (2 * k + 3)) = 1

declarations.name: cubicProfile
declarations.signature: def cubicProfile (k c x : R) : R
declarations.docstring: Rising-factorial cubic template over a commutative ring. The coefficient `k` is the already-cleared leading factor (so `k = m/6` in the rational normalisation).

declarations.name: cubicProfile_left_identity
declarations.signature: theorem cubicProfile_left_identity (k c α : R) : (α + 2) * cubicProfile k c (α - 1) - (α - 1) * cubicProfile k c α = 3 * c
declarations.docstring: Unconditional left neighbour identity, with no division.

declarations.name: cubicProfile_right_identity
declarations.signature: theorem cubicProfile_right_identity (k c α : R) : α * cubicProfile k c (α + 1) - (α + 3) * cubicProfile k c α = -3 * c
declarations.docstring: Unconditional right neighbour identity, with no division.

declarations.name: cubicProfile_left_cleared
declarations.signature: theorem cubicProfile_left_cleared (k c α : R) (hroot : cubicProfile k c α = 0) : (α + 2) * cubicProfile k c (α - 1) = 3 * c
declarations.docstring: At a root, the left identity clears the neighbour without inverting `α + 2`.

declarations.name: cubicProfile_right_cleared
declarations.signature: theorem cubicProfile_right_cleared (k c α : R) (hroot : cubicProfile k c α = 0) : α * cubicProfile k c (α + 1) = -3 * c
declarations.docstring: At a root, the right identity clears the neighbour without inverting `α`.

declarations.name: cubicProfile_square_cleared
declarations.signature: theorem cubicProfile_square_cleared (k c α : R) (hroot : cubicProfile k c α = 0) : -(α * (α + 2) * cubicProfile k c (α - 1) * cubicProfile k c (α + 1)) = 9 * c ^ 2
declarations.docstring: Product identity at a root: no division. Over a field, if `α(α + 2) ≠ 0`, this recovers `-Q(α-1)Q(α+1) = 9c²/(α(α+2))`.

declarations.name: cubicQ
declarations.signature: def cubicQ (m c x : ℚ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: Rising-factorial cubic template over `ℚ`, with the historical `m/6` normalisation.

declarations.name: cubicQ_root_prod
declarations.signature: lemma cubicQ_root_prod {m c α : ℚ} (hroot : cubicQ m c α = 0) : (m / 6) * α * (α + 1) * (α + 2) = -c

declarations.name: cubicQ_neighbour_left
declarations.signature: theorem cubicQ_neighbour_left {m c α : ℚ} (hα : α + 2 ≠ 0) (hroot : cubicQ m c α = 0) : cubicQ m c (α - 1) = 3 * c / (α + 2)
declarations.docstring: Left neighbour at a rational root: `Q(α-1) = 3c/(α+2)`. This does not instantiate an irreducible cubic.

declarations.name: cubicQ_neighbour_right
declarations.signature: theorem cubicQ_neighbour_right {m c α : ℚ} (hα : α ≠ 0) (hroot : cubicQ m c α = 0) : cubicQ m c (α + 1) = -3 * c / α
declarations.docstring: Right neighbour at a rational root: `Q(α+1) = -3c/α`.

declarations.name: cubicQ_square_identity
declarations.signature: theorem cubicQ_square_identity {m c α : ℚ} (h0 : α ≠ 0) (h2 : α + 2 ≠ 0) (hroot : cubicQ m c α = 0) : -(cubicQ m c (α - 1) * cubicQ m c (α + 1)) = 9 * c ^ 2 / (α * (α + 2))
declarations.docstring: Square identity over `ℚ` after inverting `α(α+2)`.

declarations.name: two_primitive_profile_mod7_period
declarations.docstring: Word-period accounting `4 * 7 = 28`, equivalently `1/(4·7) = 1/28`. This is not a uniform lower density over all original `(A,B)`.

declarations.name: cubic_plus_word_mod7
declarations.signature: theorem cubic_plus_word_mod7 : (fun n : ZMod 7 => (2 : ZMod 7) * n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) + 1) 0 = 1 ∧ (fun n : ZMod 7 => (2 : ZMod 7) * n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) + 1) 1 = 6 ∧ (fun n : ZMod 7 => (2 : ZMod 7) * n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) + 1) 2 = 0 ∧ (fun n : ZMod 7 => (2 : ZMod 7) * n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) + 1) 3 = 2
declarations.docstring: Plus-profile word `(1,6,0,2)` at starts `0 (mod 7)`. Word evaluation is not orbit exclusion.

declarations.name: cubic_minus_word_mod7
declarations.signature: theorem cubic_minus_word_mod7 : (fun n : ZMod 7 => (2 : ZMod 7) * n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) - 1) 1 = 4 ∧ (fun n : ZMod 7 => (2 : ZMod 7) * n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) - 1) 2 = 5 ∧ (fun n : ZMod 7 => (2 : ZMod 7) * n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) - 1) 3 = 0 ∧ (fun n : ZMod 7 => (2 : ZMod 7) * n * (n + 1) * (n + 2) - 1) 4 = 1
declarations.docstring: Minus-profile word `(4,5,0,1)` at starts `1 (mod 7)`. Word evaluation is not orbit exclusion.

declarations.name: cubic_plus_word_exact_transport_impossible
declarations.signature: theorem cubic_plus_word_exact_transport_impossible : ¬ ∃ a b d : ZMod 7, a * (1 : ZMod 7) - d = 6 ∧ b * (6 : ZMod 7) - a * d = 0 ∧ -(b * (a * d)) = 2
declarations.docstring: Exact three-step transport of the plus word is impossible over `𝔽_7`, including zero residues.

declarations.name: cubic_minus_word_exact_transport_impossible
declarations.signature: theorem cubic_minus_word_exact_transport_impossible : ¬ ∃ a b d : ZMod 7, a * (4 : ZMod 7) - d = 5 ∧ b * (5 : ZMod 7) - a * d = 0 ∧ -(b * (a * d)) = 1
declarations.docstring: Exact three-step transport of the minus word is impossible over `𝔽_7`, including zero residues.

declarations.name: cumulativeDigitLcm_dvd_succ
declarations.signature: theorem cumulativeDigitLcm_dvd_succ (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : cumulativeDigitLcm q a n ∣ cumulativeDigitLcm q a (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: The cumulative LCM grows only by divisibility.

declarations.name: cumulativeDigitLcm_dvd_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem cumulativeDigitLcm_dvd_of_le (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) : cumulativeDigitLcm q a m ∣ cumulativeDigitLcm q a n
declarations.docstring: Monotone divisibility of the cumulative LCM.

declarations.name: digit_dvd_cumulativeDigitLcm_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem digit_dvd_cumulativeDigitLcm_of_lt (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) {i n : ℕ} (hin : i < n) : a i ∣ cumulativeDigitLcm q a n
declarations.docstring: Every consumed digit divides every strictly later cumulative LCM.

declarations.name: cumulativeDigitLcm_pos
declarations.signature: theorem cumulativeDigitLcm_pos {q : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) : ∀ n, 0 < cumulativeDigitLcm q a n
declarations.docstring: The cumulative LCM is positive on any orbit with positive seed and positive multipliers.

declarations.name: lcmOverlap
declarations.signature: def lcmOverlap (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The one-step LCM overlap payment `ρₙ = gcd(Λₙ, aₙ)`.

declarations.name: lcmOverlap_def
declarations.signature: theorem lcmOverlap_def (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : lcmOverlap q a n = Nat.gcd (cumulativeDigitLcm q a n) (a n)

declarations.name: cumulativeOverlapDebt_succ'
declarations.signature: theorem cumulativeOverlapDebt_succ' (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : cumulativeOverlapDebt q a (n + 1) = cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n * lcmOverlap q a n

declarations.name: lcmOverlap_dvd_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem lcmOverlap_dvd_lcm (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : lcmOverlap q a n ∣ cumulativeDigitLcm q a n

declarations.name: lcmOverlap_dvd_digit
declarations.signature: theorem lcmOverlap_dvd_digit (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : lcmOverlap q a n ∣ a n

declarations.name: lcmOverlap_pos
declarations.signature: theorem lcmOverlap_pos {q : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (n : ℕ) : 0 < lcmOverlap q a n

declarations.name: cumulativeOverlapDebt_pos
declarations.signature: theorem cumulativeOverlapDebt_pos {q : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) : ∀ n, 0 < cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n

declarations.name: cumulativeOverlapDebt_dvd_productScale
declarations.signature: theorem cumulativeOverlapDebt_dvd_productScale (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n ∣ digitProductScale q a n
declarations.docstring: The overlap debt divides the product-cleared denominator scale.

declarations.name: cumulativeOverlapDebt_dvd_tailNumerator
declarations.signature: theorem cumulativeOverlapDebt_dvd_tailNumerator (q : ℕ) (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) : ∀ n, cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n ∣ C n
declarations.docstring: **Exact overlap-debt divisibility.** Along any exact reciprocal-tail orbit `Cₙ₊₁ + Dₙ = aₙ Cₙ` whose denominator is the product-cleared scale, the cumulative overlap debt divides the numerator state: `Mₙ ∣ Cₙ`. This is the transfer of the relocation identity `Mₙ Λₙ = Dₙ` from the denominator to the numerator. The induction needs no positivity, and no subtraction inside `ℕ` occurs anywhere in it: `Mₙ₊₁ = Mₙ ρₙ` divides `aₙ Cₙ` and `Dₙ` separately — `ρₙ ∣ aₙ` gives the first, `ρₙ ∣ Λₙ` together with `Mₙ Λₙ = Dₙ` gives the second — so the additive update `Cₙ₊₁ + Dₙ = aₙ Cₙ` transfers the divisibility directly. The base case is `M₀ = 1`.

declarations.name: cumulativeOverlapDebt_dvd_centeredState
declarations.signature: theorem cumulativeOverlapDebt_dvd_centeredState (q : ℕ) (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) (n : ℕ) : (cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℤ) ∣ centeredState (a n : ℤ) (D n : ℤ) (C n : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: **The centred state carries the same debt.** `Mₙ ∣ Eₙ` over `ℤ`, where `Eₙ = Dₙ - (aₙ - 1) Cₙ` is the signed centred error of `ReciprocalTailRigidity`.

declarations.name: lcmLiftedNumerator
declarations.signature: def lcmLiftedNumerator (q : ℕ) (a C : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The LCM-normalised numerator `Uₙ = Cₙ / Mₙ`. Every theorem below consumes it only through the exact reconstruction `Mₙ Uₙ = Cₙ`, never through the truncated quotient.

declarations.name: lcmLiftedDigit
declarations.signature: def lcmLiftedDigit (q : ℕ) (a C : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The LCM-normalised centred digit `Vₙ = Λₙ - (aₙ - 1) Uₙ`, defined by the centred formula so that the centring identity is definitional. That it really is `Eₙ / Mₙ` is the content of `lcmLiftedDigit_mul_overlapDebt`.

declarations.name: lcmLiftedNumerator_spec
declarations.signature: theorem lcmLiftedNumerator_spec (q : ℕ) (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) (n : ℕ) : cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n * lcmLiftedNumerator q a C n = C n
declarations.docstring: Exact reconstruction of the numerator from its LCM-normalised form.

declarations.name: lcmLiftedNumerator_cast_spec
declarations.signature: theorem lcmLiftedNumerator_cast_spec (q : ℕ) (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) (n : ℕ) : (cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℤ) * (lcmLiftedNumerator q a C n : ℤ) = (C n : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Integer form of the reconstruction.

declarations.name: lcmLifted_centered
declarations.signature: theorem lcmLifted_centered (q : ℕ) (a C : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : lcmLiftedDigit q a C n = (cumulativeDigitLcm q a n : ℤ) - ((a n : ℤ) - 1) * (lcmLiftedNumerator q a C n : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: **Centring in LCM coordinates**, definitionally `Vₙ = Λₙ - (aₙ - 1) Uₙ`.

declarations.name: lcmLiftedDigit_mul_overlapDebt
declarations.signature: theorem lcmLiftedDigit_mul_overlapDebt (q : ℕ) (a C D : ℕ → ℕ) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) (n : ℕ) : (cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n : ℤ) * lcmLiftedDigit q a C n = centeredState (a n : ℤ) (D n : ℤ) (C n : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The LCM-normalised digit really is the centred error divided by the overlap debt: `Mₙ Vₙ = Eₙ`, exactly.

declarations.name: lcmLifted_step
declarations.signature: theorem lcmLifted_step {q : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (C D : ℕ → ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) (n : ℕ) : (lcmOverlap q a n : ℤ) * (lcmLiftedNumerator q a C (n + 1) : ℤ) = (lcmLiftedNumerator q a C n : ℤ) - lcmLiftedDigit q a C n
declarations.docstring: **The exact LCM-normalised recurrence** `ρₙ Uₙ₊₁ = Uₙ - Vₙ`. This is the pseudo-Euclidean update of `globalLcm_numerator_update` realised on the actual cumulative-LCM coordinates, with the overlap payment `ρₙ` charged explicitly.

declarations.name: lcmNonFreshCount
declarations.signature: def lcmNonFreshCount (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ | 0 => 0 | n + 1 => lcmNonFreshCount q a n + if 1 < lcmOverlap q a n then 1 else 0 @[simp] theorem lcmNonFreshCount_zero (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) : lcmNonFreshCount q a 0 = 0
declarations.docstring: Number of LCM-non-fresh steps strictly before `n`: the indices where the current multiplier shares a factor with the accumulated LCM.

declarations.name: lcmNonFreshCount_zero
declarations.signature: theorem lcmNonFreshCount_zero (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) : lcmNonFreshCount q a 0 = 0

declarations.name: lcmNonFreshCount_succ
declarations.signature: theorem lcmNonFreshCount_succ (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : lcmNonFreshCount q a (n + 1) = lcmNonFreshCount q a n + if 1 < lcmOverlap q a n then 1 else 0

declarations.name: pow_lcmNonFreshCount_le_overlapDebt
declarations.signature: theorem pow_lcmNonFreshCount_le_overlapDebt {q : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) : ∀ n, 2 ^ lcmNonFreshCount q a n ≤ cumulativeOverlapDebt q a n
declarations.docstring: **The division-free freshness budget.** Every non-fresh step pays at least one binary factor into the cumulative overlap debt, so `2^{#{j < n : ρⱼ > 1}} ≤ Mₙ`. This is the exact finite inequality underlying the density-one freshness statement.

declarations.name: pow_lcmNonFreshCount_le_tailNumerator
declarations.signature: theorem pow_lcmNonFreshCount_le_tailNumerator {q : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (C D : ℕ → ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) {n : ℕ} (hCpos : 0 < C n) : 2 ^ lcmNonFreshCount q a n ≤ C n
declarations.docstring: Composed with the keystone: the freshness budget is carried by the numerator state itself, `2^{#{j < n : ρⱼ > 1}} ≤ Cₙ`.

declarations.name: lcmFresh_pairwiseCoprime
declarations.signature: theorem lcmFresh_pairwiseCoprime (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) {i j : ℕ} (hij : i < j) (hj : lcmOverlap q a j = 1) : Nat.Coprime (a i) (a j)
declarations.docstring: **Fresh multipliers are coprime to every earlier multiplier.** If the step at `j` is LCM-fresh then `aⱼ` is coprime to `aᵢ` for every `i < j`, because `aᵢ` has already entered `Λⱼ` along the monotone divisibility chain. Only freshness at the *later* index is used; the brief's hypothesis that both indices are fresh is redundant.

declarations.name: lcmFresh_coprime_of_ne
declarations.signature: theorem lcmFresh_coprime_of_ne (q : ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℕ) {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≠ j) (hi : lcmOverlap q a i = 1) (hj : lcmOverlap q a j = 1) : Nat.Coprime (a i) (a j)
declarations.docstring: Symmetric form: distinct indices, freshness at the larger one.

declarations.name: lcmNonFreshCount_sublinear_of_subexponential
declarations.signature: theorem lcmNonFreshCount_sublinear_of_subexponential {q : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (C D : ℕ → ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (hCpos : ∀ n, 0 < C n) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) (hsubexp : ∀ K, 0 < K → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → C n ^ K < 2 ^ n) : ∀ K, 0 < K → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → K * lcmNonFreshCount q a n < n
declarations.docstring: **Division-free density-one core.** If every fixed power of the numerator state is eventually dominated by `2ⁿ`, then the LCM-non-fresh count is sublinear in the division-free sense `K · count < n`.

declarations.name: lcmNonFreshCount_sublinear_of_normalizedVanishes
declarations.signature: theorem lcmNonFreshCount_sublinear_of_normalizedVanishes {q : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (C D : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℕ → ℤ) (hq : 0 < q) (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (hCpos : ∀ n, 0 < C n) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (hstep : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) (hE : ∀ n, E n = centeredState (a n : ℤ) (D n : ℤ) (C n : ℤ)) (hvanish : ∀ K, ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → K * Int.natAbs (E n) < C n) : ∀ K, 0 < K → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → K * lcmNonFreshCount q a n < n
declarations.docstring: Exact-orbit specialisation: normalised centred-state vanishing forces the LCM-non-fresh count to be sublinear. This composes the keystone budget with `tailState_subexponential_of_normalizedVanishes`, so the density-one freshness statement of the return is available in the same regime as the corpus's subexponential tail growth.

declarations.name: no_lcmState_of_freshBlock
declarations.signature: theorem no_lcmState_of_freshBlock (U Λ a ρ : ℕ → ℕ) (V : ℕ → ℤ) {B : ℕ} (m : Fin B → ℕ) (T : ℕ) (hB : 0 < B) (hm : ∀ i, B < m i) (hpair : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (m i) (m j)) (hmOld : ∀ (i : Fin B) (s : ℕ), T ≤ s → m i ∣ Λ s) (hρpos : ∀ n, T ≤ n → 0 < ρ n) (hstep : ∀ n, T ≤ n → (ρ n : ℤ) * (U (n + 1) : ℤ) = (U n : ℤ) - V n) (hcenter : ∀ n, T ≤ n → V n = (Λ n : ℤ) - ((a n : ℤ) - 1) * (U n : ℤ)) (hstart : U T < ∏ i, m i) (hsmall : ∀ n, T ≤ n → U n < 2 * (∏ i, m i) + B → -(B : ℤ) ≤ V n) (hUtop : Filter.Tendsto U Filter.atTop Filter.atTop) : False
declarations.docstring: **The finite combinatorial core.** Take `B` pairwise-coprime moduli, each strictly larger than `B`, all of which have already entered the cumulative LCM by time `T`. Suppose the LCM-normalised state starts below the block product, obeys the exact recurrence `ρₙ Uₙ₊₁ = Uₙ - Vₙ` with positive overlap payments and the centring identity `Vₙ = Λₙ - (aₙ - 1) Uₙ`, has negative part at most `B` while it is below `2P + B`, and tends to infinity. This is contradictory. The argument is a first crossing, so no persistence of divisors is required. Placing the CRT block in `[P, 2P)` makes the crossing land on a block position `x + r`; the modulus `m r` divides the state and the cumulative LCM there, so it divides `V`, which is strictly negative at a strict rise and bounded by `B` in absolute value. A modulus exceeding `B` cannot divide a nonzero integer of absolute value at most `B`. Unlike `no_boundedNegative_lcmState_of_oldPrimeSupply` the moduli here are whole numbers rather than primes, and only

declarations.name: no_lcmLiftedState_of_freshMultiplierBlock
declarations.signature: theorem no_lcmLiftedState_of_freshMultiplierBlock {q : ℕ} {a : ℕ → ℕ} (C D : ℕ → ℕ) {B : ℕ} (idx : Fin B → ℕ) (T : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (ha : ∀ n, 0 < a n) (hD : ∀ n, D n = digitProductScale q a n) (horbit : ∀ n, C (n + 1) + D n = a n * C n) (hB : 0 < B) (hidxNe : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → idx i ≠ idx j) (hidxLt : ∀ i, idx i < T) (hfresh : ∀ i, lcmOverlap q a (idx i) = 1) (hlarge : ∀ i, B < a (idx i)) (hstart : lcmLiftedNumerator q a C T < ∏ i, a (idx i)) (hsmall : ∀ n, T ≤ n → lcmLiftedNumerator q a C n < 2 * (∏ i, a (idx i)) + B → -(B : ℤ) ≤ lcmLiftedDigit q a C n)
declarations.docstring: **The barrier on the actual cumulative-LCM coordinates.** Instantiating `no_lcmState_of_freshBlock` at `Uₙ = Cₙ / Mₙ`, `Vₙ = Λₙ - (aₙ - 1) Uₙ`, `ρₙ = gcd(Λₙ, aₙ)`: a block of `B` LCM-fresh multipliers taken before time `T`, each exceeding `B`, is inconsistent with a normalised state that starts below their product, keeps its negative part at most `B` while below twice that product, and tends to infinity. Freshness supplies pairwise coprimality (`lcmFresh_coprime_of_ne`) and the monotone LCM chain supplies oldness (`digit_dvd_cumulativeDigitLcm_of_lt`), so the moduli are whole multipliers already present in the cumulative denominator. The analytic input — that such a block exists by time `B + o(B)` on a counterexample orbit — is not formalised here.

declarations.name: rawNext_coprime_currentNumerator
declarations.signature: theorem rawNext_coprime_currentNumerator {a u v q : ℕ} (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v) (hq : q + v = a * u) : Nat.Coprime u q
declarations.docstring: The raw next numerator is coprime to the current reduced numerator.

declarations.name: rawNext_gcd_eq_gcd_sq
declarations.signature: theorem rawNext_gcd_eq_gcd_sq {a u v q : ℕ} (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v) (hq : q + v = a * u) : Nat.gcd q (a * v) = Nat.gcd q (a ^ 2)
declarations.docstring: For a primitive input pair, the content removed from the raw next pair is controlled exactly by the square of the current multiplier.

declarations.name: rawNext_gcd_exact_overlap
declarations.signature: theorem rawNext_gcd_exact_overlap {a u v q : ℕ} (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v) (hq : q + v = a * u) : let d
declarations.docstring: Quotient-level overlap formula for the removed content. The first copy of `d = gcd(a,v)` is forced, while the second copy is precisely the overlap between `d` and the residual raw numerator `q/d`.

declarations.name: gcd_scaled_square_eq
declarations.signature: theorem gcd_scaled_square_eq {d α ω c : ℕ} (hαω : Nat.Coprime α ω) (hc : c = Nat.gcd ω d) : Nat.gcd (d * ω) ((d * α) ^ 2) = d * c
declarations.docstring: The algebraic heart of the square-overlap normal form. Once common content `d` has been factored from both the multiplier and raw numerator, coprimality of their primitive parts leaves only the overlap of `ω` with `d` available for a second copy in the square.

declarations.name: cancellationOverlap_normalForm_explicit
declarations.signature: theorem cancellationOverlap_normalForm_explicit {a w h d α ω c b : ℕ} (ha : a = d * α) (hw : w = d * ω) (hαω : Nat.Coprime α ω) (hc : c = Nat.gcd ω d) (hd : d = b * c) (hh : h = Nat.gcd w (a ^ 2)) : h = b * c ^ 2 ∧ a = b * c * α ∧ Nat.Coprime c α
declarations.docstring: Explicit-factor version of the exact square-cancellation normal form. It deliberately separates quotient bookkeeping from its reusable algebraic core: if `d = b*c`, then the removed content is `b*c^2`, and the overlap factor `c` is coprime to the surviving primitive multiplier `α`.

declarations.name: cancellation_denominator_transport_explicit
declarations.signature: theorem cancellation_denominator_transport_explicit {a h v vNext d α c t : ℕ} (hdPos : 0 < d) (hcPos : 0 < c) (ha : a = d * α) (hh : h = d * c) (hv : v = c * t) (hstep : h * vNext = a * v) : vNext = α * (v / c)
declarations.docstring: Transport of the reduced denominator through the exact overlap factors. When `h=d*c`, the overlap factor is deleted and only the primitive multiplier `α` survives.

declarations.name: deletedFactor_eq_oldDenominator_div_gcd
declarations.signature: theorem deletedFactor_eq_oldDenominator_div_gcd {c α t v vNext : ℕ} (htPos : 0 < t) (hcop : Nat.Coprime c α) (hv : v = c * t) (hvNext : vNext = α * t) : c = v / Nat.gcd v vNext
declarations.docstring: The overlap factor is exactly the part deleted from the old primitive denominator.

declarations.name: lcm_eq_overlap_mul_nextDenominator
declarations.signature: theorem lcm_eq_overlap_mul_nextDenominator {a v vNext d α c t : ℕ} (hdPos : 0 < d) (hd : d = Nat.gcd a v) (ha : a = d * α) (hv : v = c * t) (hvNext : vNext = α * t) : Nat.lcm a v = c * vNext
declarations.docstring: Equivalent lcm form of exact denominator deletion: the lcm of the current multiplier and reduced denominator is the overlap factor times the next reduced denominator.

declarations.name: reducedStep_consecutiveNumerator_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem reducedStep_consecutiveNumerator_coprime {a u v q h uNext : ℕ} (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v) (hq : q + v = a * u) (hqu : q = h * uNext) : Nat.Coprime u uNext
declarations.docstring: Dividing a primitive raw next pair by its full common content leaves consecutive reduced numerators coprime.

declarations.name: reducedStep_cancellationFactor_eq_square
declarations.signature: theorem reducedStep_cancellationFactor_eq_square {a u v q h uNext vNext : ℕ} (hcop : Nat.Coprime u v) (hcopNext : Nat.Coprime uNext vNext) (hq : q + v = a * u) (hqu : q = h * uNext) (hav : a * v = h * vNext) : h = Nat.gcd q (a ^ 2)
declarations.docstring: If `h` is the full common content removed from the raw next pair, then it is exactly `gcd q (a^2)`.

declarations.name: reducedStep_secondOrder
declarations.signature: theorem reducedStep_secondOrder {a aNext u uNext uNextNext v vNext h hNext : ℕ} (hu : h * uNext + v = a * u) (hv : h * vNext = a * v) (huNext : hNext * uNextNext + vNext = aNext * uNext) : a ^ 2 * u + h * hNext * uNextNext = h * (a + aNext) * uNext
declarations.docstring: Two consecutive dynamically reduced steps satisfy an exact non-autonomous second-order recurrence for their primitive numerators.

declarations.name: cancellationFree_dualRemainder
declarations.signature: theorem cancellationFree_dualRemainder {a Δ p pNext e eNext s : ℤ} (hpNext : pNext = p - e) (hdefect : Δ * pNext = a ^ 2 * e - eNext) (hs : s = a ^ 2 - 1 + Δ) : s * e - Δ * p = eNext - e
declarations.docstring: On a cancellation-free step, the centered error satisfies the dual nearest-remainder identity. This integer form avoids all sign side conditions and exposes the changing modulus used by the anti-shadowing problem.

declarations.name: cancellationFree_curvature_square
declarations.signature: theorem cancellationFree_curvature_square {a aNext p pNext pNextNext q : ℤ} (hq : q = a * p - pNext) (hrec : pNextNext + a ^ 2 * p = (a + aNext) * pNext) : q ^ 2 + (p * pNextNext - pNext ^ 2) = (aNext - a) * p * pNext
declarations.docstring: Exact square/curvature identity on a cancellation-free pair of steps. It packages the primitive second-order cocycle as a changing quadratic norm, without asserting the still-open global anti-shadowing conclusion.

declarations.name: excursionMatrix_det_square
declarations.signature: theorem excursionMatrix_det_square {A B aStart aStop K α β : ℤ} (hK : K = A - (aStart - 1) * B) (hα : α = A + (aStop - 1) * B) (hβ : β = A * (aStart - 1) - (aStop - 1) * K) : α * K + β * B = A ^ 2
declarations.docstring: The centered-state transfer matrix attached to an excursion has square determinant. The theorem is stated as its scalar algebraic interface so that later block producers can choose their preferred matrix representation.

declarations.name: primitiveMatrix_gcd_eq_det_gcd
declarations.signature: theorem primitiveMatrix_gcd_eq_det_gcd {p q r s x y : ℤ} (hrow : Int.gcd r s = 1) (hinput : Int.gcd x y = 1) : Int.gcd (p * x + q * y) (r * x + s * y) = Int.gcd (p * s - q * r) (r * x + s * y)
declarations.docstring: Primitive matrix gcd lemma. If both the input vector and the second matrix row are primitive, then the common content of the output is exactly the gcd of the determinant with the second output coordinate. This is the generic arithmetic consumer behind the exact block-cancellation payment.

declarations.name: blockCancellationPayment_explicit
declarations.signature: theorem blockCancellationPayment_explicit {σ : ℕ} {Λ A0 B0 K0 α0 β0 e u eStop uStop : ℤ} (hinput : Int.gcd e u = 1) (houtput : Int.gcd eStop uStop = 1) (hrow : Int.gcd (-B0) K0 = 1) (hdet : α0 * K0 + β0 * B0 = A0 ^ 2) (he : Λ * eStop = (σ : ℤ) * (α0 * e + β0 * u)) (hu : Λ * uStop = (σ : ℤ) * ((-B0) * e + K0 * u)) : Λ.natAbs = σ * Int.gcd (A0 ^ 2) (K0 * u - B0 * e)
declarations.docstring: Exact cancellation payment for a normalized excursion block. After the common matrix content `σ` is removed, primitivity of the second row and of both endpoint states turns the transfer scale into the square-determinant gcd predicted by `primitiveMatrix_gcd_eq_det_gcd`. The signed coordinate `K0 * u - B0 * e` is the reduced terminal tail state.

declarations.name: excursionCancellationPayment
declarations.signature: theorem excursionCancellationPayment {σ : ℕ} {Λ A B aStart aStop K α β e u eStop uStop : ℤ} (hσ : σ = Int.gcd A B) (hσpos : 0 < σ) (hK : K = A - (aStart - 1) * B) (hα : α = A + (aStop - 1) * B) (hβ : β = A * (aStart - 1) - (aStop - 1) * K) (hinput : Int.gcd e u = 1) (houtput : Int.gcd eStop uStop = 1) (he : Λ * eStop = α * e + β * u) (hu : Λ * uStop = (-B) * e + K * u) : Λ.natAbs = σ * Int.gcd ((A / (σ : ℤ)) ^ 2) ((K * u - B * e) / (σ : ℤ))
declarations.docstring: Quotient form of the exact excursion payment. Here `σ = gcd(A,B)` is constructed from the unnormalised block data. The excursion formulas imply `gcd(B,K)=σ`, so dividing the second row by `σ` makes it primitive; the square determinant then gives the literal payment `|Λ| = σ * gcd((A/σ)^2, (K*u-B*e)/σ)`.

declarations.name: blockScale_product_telescopes
declarations.signature: theorem blockScale_product_telescopes (G t Λ : ℕ → ℕ) (hscale : ∀ i, Λ i * G (t i) = G (t (i + 1))) : ∀ m, (∏ i ∈ Finset.range m, Λ i) * G (t 0) = G (t m)
declarations.docstring: Exact telescoping for a sequence of excursion scales. The endpoint equations alone force the product of all block payments to be the total gcd scale growth; no independence assumption on the intervening prime factors is needed.

declarations.name: blockScale_product_subexponential
declarations.signature: theorem blockScale_product_subexponential (G C t Λ : ℕ → ℕ) (hGpos : ∀ n, 0 < G n) (hGleC : ∀ n, G n ≤ C n) (hscale : ∀ i, Λ i * G (t i) = G (t (i + 1))) (hCsubexp : ∀ K, 0 < K → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → C n ^ K < 2 ^ n) : ∀ K, 0 < K → ∃ N, ∀ m, N ≤ t m → (∏ i ∈ Finset.range m, Λ i) ^ K < 2 ^ (t m)
declarations.docstring: Multiplicative form of the logarithmic cancellation-mass budget. If the ambient tail state is subexponential in physical time, then the product of all exact excursion payments is subexponential at the corresponding endpoint. This is the honest global accumulation supplied by the gcd budget; it does not by itself exclude arbitrarily sparse large payments.

declarations.name: scaledRecord_forces_payment
declarations.signature: theorem scaledRecord_forces_payment {GStart GStop Λ mStart mStop : ℕ} (hGStart : 0 < GStart) (hscale : GStop = Λ * GStart) (hrecord : GStart * mStart < GStop * mStop) : mStart < Λ * mStop
declarations.docstring: A new scale-weighted record must be paid for by the intervening gcd scale. This is the order-theoretic half of the record-payment corollary, separated from the determinantal computation of that scale.

declarations.name: squareResiduePayment_of_scaledRecord
declarations.signature: theorem squareResiduePayment_of_scaledRecord {GStart GStop Λ mStart mStop σ : ℕ} {A0 z : ℤ} (hGStart : 0 < GStart) (hscale : GStop = Λ * GStart) (hrecord : GStart * mStart < GStop * mStop) (hpayment : Λ = σ * Int.gcd (A0 ^ 2) z) : mStart < σ * Int.gcd (A0 ^ 2) z * mStop
declarations.docstring: Record-payment corollary in the square-residue coordinates supplied by `excursionCancellationPayment`. If the primitive magnitude does not itself account for a new scale-weighted record, the exact `σ * gcd(A0²,z)` payment does.

declarations.name: feedback_transport_defect
declarations.signature: theorem feedback_transport_defect {a aNext u uNext h : ℕ} {e eNext Δ : ℤ} (hq : (h * uNext : ℤ) = (u : ℤ) - e) (hres : (h : ℤ) * eNext = (a : ℤ) ^ 2 * e - Δ * ((u : ℤ) - e)) : (h : ℤ) * (((aNext : ℤ) - 1) * (uNext : ℤ) + eNext) - (a : ℤ) * (((a : ℤ) - 1) * (u : ℤ) + e) = ((u : ℤ) - e) * ((aNext : ℤ) - ((a : ℤ) ^ 2 - (a : ℤ) + 1 + Δ))
declarations.docstring: The denominator-transport defect is exactly the failure of the centered quotient to generate the next multiplier. This is the local realizability condition missing from a bare square-residue congruence.

declarations.name: feedback_denominator_transport
declarations.signature: theorem feedback_denominator_transport {a aNext u uNext h : ℕ} {e eNext Δ : ℤ} (hq : (h * uNext : ℤ) = (u : ℤ) - e) (hres : (h : ℤ) * eNext = (a : ℤ) ^ 2 * e - Δ * ((u : ℤ) - e)) (haNext : (aNext : ℤ) = (a : ℤ) ^ 2 - (a : ℤ) + 1 + Δ) : (h : ℤ) * (((aNext : ℤ) - 1) * (uNext : ℤ) + eNext) = (a : ℤ) * (((a : ℤ) - 1) * (u : ℤ) + e)
declarations.docstring: Once the next multiplier is generated by the centered quotient, the reduced denominator transports exactly.

declarations.name: feedback_denominator_transport_iff
declarations.signature: theorem feedback_denominator_transport_iff {a aNext u uNext h : ℕ} {e eNext Δ : ℤ} (hq : (h * uNext : ℤ) = (u : ℤ) - e) (hres : (h : ℤ) * eNext = (a : ℤ) ^ 2 * e - Δ * ((u : ℤ) - e)) (hq0 : (u : ℤ) - e ≠ 0) : (h : ℤ) * (((aNext : ℤ) - 1) * (uNext : ℤ) + eNext) = (a : ℤ) * (((a : ℤ) - 1) * (u : ℤ) + e) ↔ (aNext : ℤ) = (a : ℤ) ^ 2 - (a : ℤ) + 1 + Δ
declarations.docstring: Exact converse: when the raw next numerator is nonzero, denominator transport holds precisely when the centered quotient generates the next multiplier.

declarations.name: primitive_squareRoot_feedback
declarations.signature: theorem primitive_squareRoot_feedback {a aNext u uNext : ℤ} {e eNext Δ L r t v : ℤ} (huNext : uNext ≠ 0) (hU : uNext = u - e) (hV : v = (a - 1) * u + e) (hfirst : a * e = L * uNext + t) (hsecond : a * t = r * uNext + eNext) (hdefect : a ^ 2 * e = Δ * uNext + eNext) (haNext : aNext = a ^ 2 - a + 1 + Δ) : Δ = a * L + r ∧ v = (a - 1 + L) * uNext + t ∧ aNext = a * (a - 1 + L) + (r + 1)
declarations.docstring: On a cancellation-free step, two centered multiplications by `a` recover the square quotient. The same quotients generate both the current denominator and the next multiplier.

declarations.name: primitive_squareRoot_norm
declarations.signature: theorem primitive_squareRoot_norm {a e eNext L r t uNext : ℤ} (hfirst : a * e = L * uNext + t) (hsecond : a * t = r * uNext + eNext) : t ^ 2 - e * eNext = (r * e - L * t) * uNext
declarations.docstring: The intermediate centered residue has an exact norm defect divisible by the next primitive numerator.

declarations.name: artificial_squareUnit_true_nextMultiplier
declarations.signature: theorem artificial_squareUnit_true_nextMultiplier {u aNext : ℤ} (haNext : aNext = (u + 2) ^ 2 - (u + 2) + 1 - (u + 3)) : aNext = u * (u + 2)
declarations.docstring: In the artificial square-unit pattern `a = u+2`, `e = -1`, the true centered quotient is `-(u+3)` and therefore forces the quadratic next multiplier `u*(u+2)`.

declarations.name: artificial_squareUnit_not_realizable
declarations.signature: theorem artificial_squareUnit_not_realizable {u : ℤ} (hu : 3 ≤ u) : u + 3 ≠ u * (u + 2)
declarations.docstring: The linear fake continuation `u+3` cannot equal the multiplier required by true feedback once `u ≥ 3`.

declarations.name: forcedNumerator
declarations.docstring: Numerator of the forced normalized constant-negative update.

declarations.name: forcedNumerator_modEq
declarations.signature: theorem forcedNumerator_modEq {n : ℕ} {a b modulus : ℤ} (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD modulus]) : forcedNumerator n a ≡ forcedNumerator n b [ZMOD modulus]
declarations.docstring: The forced numerator is polynomially compatible with congruence.

declarations.name: quotient_modEq_of_modEq_mul
declarations.signature: theorem quotient_modEq_of_modEq_mul {d m a b : ℤ} (hd : d ≠ 0) (ha : d ∣ a) (hb : d ∣ b) (h : a ≡ b [ZMOD d * m]) : a / d ≡ b / d [ZMOD m]
declarations.docstring: Exact division cancels the same nonzero factor from values and modulus.

declarations.name: horizonModulus
declarations.signature: def horizonModulus : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ | 0, _ => 1 | remaining + 1, index => (index + 2) * horizonModulus remaining (index + 1) /-- The recursive modulus is the corresponding ascending factorial. -/ theorem horizonModulus_eq_ascFactorial (remaining index : ℕ) : horizonModulus remaining index = (index + 2).ascFactorial remaining
declarations.docstring: Modulus sufficient for `remaining` forced updates starting at `index`. It is represented recursively so each exact division removes the visible first factor.

declarations.name: horizonModulus_eq_ascFactorial
declarations.signature: theorem horizonModulus_eq_ascFactorial (remaining index : ℕ) : horizonModulus remaining index = (index + 2).ascFactorial remaining
declarations.docstring: The recursive modulus is the corresponding ascending factorial.

declarations.name: horizonModulus_zero_eq_factorial
declarations.docstring: At the initial index, the finite-horizon modulus is exactly `(h + 1)!`.

declarations.name: ForcedSurvives
declarations.signature: def ForcedSurvives : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ → Prop | 0, _, _ => True | remaining + 1, index, a => let d : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Exact survival predicate for the first `remaining` forced divisions.

declarations.name: forcedQuotient_modEq
