declarations.signature: theorem integralRelationBasis_apply (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) (i : OmittedIntegralChannel k e hk he) : (integralRelationBasis k e hk he i : AllBaseThroughLevelIndex k e →₀ ℤ) = Finsupp.single i.val 1 - (integralRelationSystem k e hk he).includeKept (integralNormalCoefficients k e hk i.val)

declarations.name: integralChannelEvaluation_surjective
declarations.signature: theorem integralChannelEvaluation_surjective (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) : Function.Surjective (integralChannelEvaluation k e hk he)
declarations.docstring: Evaluation really is onto the integral span, rather than a formal map to an unspecified ambient module.

declarations.name: channel_count_split
declarations.signature: private theorem channel_count_split (k d : ℕ) : (∑ j ∈ Finset.range (d + 2), k ^ j) = k ^ (d + 1) + 1 + ∑ j ∈ Finset.range d, k ^ (j + 1)
declarations.docstring: Elementary identity for the number of omitted coordinates.

declarations.name: card_omittedIntegralChannel
declarations.signature: theorem card_omittedIntegralChannel (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) : Fintype.card (OmittedIntegralChannel k e hk he) = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (e - 1), k ^ (j + 1)

declarations.name: finrank_integralRelations
declarations.signature: theorem finrank_integralRelations (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) : Module.finrank ℤ (IntegralRelations k e hk he) = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (e - 1), k ^ (j + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact integral rank; this follows from the exhibited basis and its pivots.

declarations.name: integral_normal_form_complete
declarations.signature: theorem integral_normal_form_complete (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) : Nonempty (Module.Basis (AllBaseCanonicalIndex k e) ℤ (IntegralChannelSpan k e)) ∧ (∃ b : Module.Basis (OmittedIntegralChannel k e hk he) ℤ (IntegralRelations k e hk he), ∀ i, (b i : AllBaseThroughLevelIndex k e →₀ ℤ) = Finsupp.single i.val 1 - (integralRelationSystem k e hk he).includeKept (integralNormalCoefficients k e hk i.val)) ∧ Module.finrank ℤ (IntegralRelations k e hk he) = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (e - 1), k ^ (j + 1)
declarations.docstring: Combined displayed statement: coordinate basis AND relation basis AND rank.

declarations.name: channel_omitted_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem channel_omitted_of_dvd (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) (i : AllBaseThroughLevelIndex k e) (hi : 2 ≤ i.1.val) (hdiv : k ∣ i.2.val) : i ∉ Set.range (retainedChannel k e hk he)
declarations.docstring: Every channel at level at least two with a residue divisible by k is omitted.

declarations.name: integral_scalar_reduction_row
declarations.signature: theorem integral_scalar_reduction_row (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) (o : OmittedIntegralChannel k e hk he) (b : AllBaseCanonicalIndex k e) (a : ℤ) (h : allBaseThroughLevelFamily k e o.val = a • allBaseCanonicalFamily k e b) : (integralRelationBasis k e hk he o : AllBaseThroughLevelIndex k e →₀ ℤ) = Finsupp.single o.val 1 - Finsupp.single (retainedChannel k e hk he b) a
declarations.docstring: Any supplied canonical target and scalar identity produce the exact maximal-reduction basis vector. This includes the printed Euler-product scalar; the next theorem gives that scalar's integral value.

declarations.name: integral_zero_reduction_row
declarations.signature: theorem integral_zero_reduction_row (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) (j : ℕ) (hj : 2 ≤ j) (hje : j ≤ e) : let i : AllBaseThroughLevelIndex k e
declarations.docstring: The zero-residue basis vector has exactly its advertised two entries.

declarations.name: integralPowerScalar
declarations.signature: def integralPowerScalar (k t u : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: An integer expression for the maximal-power Euler-product coefficient.

declarations.name: integralPowerScalar_cast
declarations.signature: theorem integralPowerScalar_cast (k t u : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (ht : 1 ≤ t) : (integralPowerScalar k t u : ℚ) = (k : ℚ) ^ t * missingEulerProduct k u

declarations.name: integral_maximal_power_reduction
declarations.signature: theorem integral_maximal_power_reduction (k j t u : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (ht : 1 ≤ t) (htj : t < j) : allBaseTotientKernelSeq k j (k ^ t * u) = (integralPowerScalar k t u : ℤ) • allBaseTotientKernelSeq k (j - t) u

declarations.name: canonical_family_contains_nondiv
declarations.signature: theorem canonical_family_contains_nondiv (k e h u : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hh : 1 ≤ h) (hhe : h ≤ e) (hu : u < k ^ h) (hku : ¬ k ∣ u) : ∃ b : AllBaseCanonicalIndex k e, allBaseCanonicalFamily k e b = allBaseTotientKernelSeq k h u
declarations.docstring: A positive residue not divisible by the base names a retained channel. The arithmetic construction is the same Euclidean digit decomposition as the repaired r7 spanning proof, but returns the index rather than span membership.

declarations.name: scalar_canonical_reduction
declarations.signature: theorem scalar_canonical_reduction (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : ∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ e → ∀ r : ℕ, r < k ^ j → ∃ b : AllBaseCanonicalIndex k e, ∃ a : ℕ, allBaseTotientKernelSeq k j r = (a : ℤ) • allBaseCanonicalFamily k e b
declarations.docstring: Every original channel reduces to ONE canonical channel with an integer scalar. This is stronger than membership in the canonical integer span.

declarations.name: integralRelationBasis_two_term
declarations.signature: theorem integralRelationBasis_two_term (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) (o : OmittedIntegralChannel k e hk he) : ∃ b : AllBaseCanonicalIndex k e, ∃ a : ℕ, allBaseThroughLevelFamily k e o.val = (a : ℤ) • allBaseCanonicalFamily k e b ∧ (integralRelationBasis k e hk he o : AllBaseThroughLevelIndex k e →₀ ℤ) = Finsupp.single o.val 1 - Finsupp.single (retainedChannel k e hk he b) (a : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Each actual basis vector is a literal two-term unit-pivot reduction. There is no undisplayed many-term coordinate choice in this conclusion.

declarations.name: integral_maximal_reduction_row
declarations.signature: theorem integral_maximal_reduction_row (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) (o : OmittedIntegralChannel k e hk he) (t u : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) (htj : t < o.val.1.val) (hres : o.val.2.val = k ^ t * u) (hku : ¬ k ∣ u) : ∃ b : AllBaseCanonicalIndex k e, allBaseCanonicalFamily k e b = allBaseTotientKernelSeq k (o.val.1.val - t) u ∧ (integralPowerScalar k t u : ℚ) = (k : ℚ)^t * missingEulerProduct k u ∧ (integralRelationBasis k e hk he o : AllBaseThroughLevelIndex k e →₀ ℤ) = Finsupp.single o.val 1 - Finsupp.single (retainedChannel k e hk he b) (integralPowerScalar k t u : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The nonzero maximal-power row has the paper's Euler-product coefficient, with a proved canonical target. The residue and level hypotheses merely name an omitted channel; there is no linear-independence hypothesis to discharge.

declarations.name: integralTotientKernelBasis_values
declarations.signature: theorem integralTotientKernelBasis_values (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) (i : AllBaseCanonicalIndex k e) : (integralTotientKernelBasis k e hk he i : ℕ → ℚ) = allBaseCanonicalFamily k e i
declarations.docstring: The coordinate basis has the literal canonical family as its values.

declarations.name: displayed_integral_normal_form
declarations.signature: theorem displayed_integral_normal_form (k e : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (he : 1 ≤ e) : (∃ c : Module.Basis (AllBaseCanonicalIndex k e) ℤ (IntegralChannelSpan k e), ∀ i, (c i : ℕ → ℚ) = allBaseCanonicalFamily k e i) ∧ (∃ b : Module.Basis (OmittedIntegralChannel k e hk he) ℤ (IntegralRelations k e hk he), ∀ o, ∃ j : AllBaseCanonicalIndex k e, ∃ a : ℕ, allBaseThroughLevelFamily k e o.val = (a : ℤ) • allBaseCanonicalFamily k e j ∧ (b o : AllBaseThroughLevelIndex k e →₀ ℤ) = Finsupp.single o.val 1 - Finsupp.single (retainedChannel k e hk he j) (a : ℤ)) ∧ Module.finrank ℤ (IntegralRelations k e hk he) = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (e - 1), k ^ (j + 1)
declarations.docstring: Complete displayed integral normal form, now including the elementary basis vectors of the kernel and its exact rank.

declarations.name: System
declarations.signature: structure System (R I J M : Type*) [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
declarations.docstring: Data for a generating family with an explicitly retained independent subfamily. `coeff` is a finite normal form for each original channel.

declarations.name: evaluation
declarations.docstring: The actual free-module evaluation whose kernel is the relation module.

declarations.name: Omitted
declarations.docstring: Only a non-retained coordinate is used as a pivot.

declarations.name: row
declarations.signature: noncomputable def row (i : I) : I →₀ R

declarations.name: rows
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rows : D.Omitted → I →₀ R

declarations.name: coeff_keep
declarations.signature: theorem coeff_keep (j : J) : D.coeff (D.keep j) = Finsupp.single j 1
declarations.docstring: The normal-form coefficients of a retained generator are its unit vector. This uses independence, not a choice convention for `coeff`.

declarations.name: includeKept_single
declarations.signature: theorem includeKept_single (j : J) (a : R) : D.includeKept (Finsupp.single j a) = Finsupp.single (D.keep j) a

declarations.name: evaluation_includeKept
declarations.signature: theorem evaluation_includeKept (c : J →₀ R) : D.evaluation (D.includeKept c) = D.keptEvaluation c
declarations.docstring: The evaluation of the kept inclusion is the independent evaluation.

declarations.name: keptEvaluation_normalCoordinates
declarations.signature: theorem keptEvaluation_normalCoordinates (c : I →₀ R) : D.keptEvaluation (D.normalCoordinates c) = D.evaluation c
declarations.docstring: Reconstructing the normal coordinates recovers the original evaluation.

declarations.name: normalCoordinates_eq_zero_of_relation
declarations.signature: theorem normalCoordinates_eq_zero_of_relation (c : I →₀ R) (hc : D.evaluation c = 0) : D.normalCoordinates c = 0

declarations.name: includeKept_at_omitted
declarations.signature: theorem includeKept_at_omitted (o : D.Omitted) (c : J →₀ R) : D.includeKept c o.val = 0
declarations.docstring: A kept inclusion has no coefficient at an omitted index.

declarations.name: row_at_omitted
declarations.signature: theorem row_at_omitted (i : I) (o : D.Omitted) : D.row i o.val = Finsupp.single i (1 : R) o.val
declarations.docstring: Unit pivots survive subtraction of the retained normal form.

declarations.name: combination_at_pivot
declarations.signature: theorem combination_at_pivot (c : D.Omitted →₀ R) (o : D.Omitted) : (Finsupp.linearCombination R D.rows c) o.val = c o
declarations.docstring: Evaluating a combination of reduction rows at its omitted pivot recovers that coefficient, even for an infinite family of channels.

declarations.name: rows_independent
declarations.docstring: Independence uses pivots of coefficient one and needs no division.

declarations.name: subtraction_eq_rows
declarations.signature: theorem subtraction_eq_rows (c : I →₀ R) : c - D.includeKept (D.normalCoordinates c) = Finsupp.linearCombination R D.row c
declarations.docstring: The elimination operator is the linear combination of elementary rows.

declarations.name: row_mem_span_rows
declarations.signature: theorem row_mem_span_rows (i : I) : D.row i ∈ Submodule.span R (Set.range D.rows)
declarations.docstring: Every row, including a retained row (which is zero), belongs to the span of the omitted-pivot rows.

declarations.name: span_rows_eq_ker
declarations.signature: theorem span_rows_eq_ker : Submodule.span R (Set.range D.rows) = LinearMap.ker D.evaluation
declarations.docstring: Spanning of the *kernel*, not merely spanning of the image.

declarations.name: relationBasis
declarations.signature: noncomputable def relationBasis : Module.Basis D.Omitted R (LinearMap.ker D.evaluation)
declarations.docstring: The reduction rows form an actual module basis of the relation module.

declarations.name: relationBasis_apply
declarations.signature: theorem relationBasis_apply (o : D.Omitted) : (D.relationBasis o : I →₀ R) = D.row o.val

declarations.name: row_of_scalar_reduction
declarations.signature: theorem row_of_scalar_reduction (i : I) (j : J) (a : R) (h : D.value i = a • D.value (D.keep j)) : D.row i = Finsupp.single i 1 - Finsupp.single (D.keep j) a
declarations.docstring: A scalar reduction has precisely the paper's two-term elementary row.

declarations.name: omittedFintype
declarations.signature: noncomputable instance omittedFintype [Fintype I] : Fintype D.Omitted

declarations.name: indexSplit
declarations.signature: noncomputable def indexSplit [Nontrivial R] : (J ⊕ D.Omitted) ≃ I
declarations.docstring: The retained/omitted partition counts the pivots without a field argument.

declarations.name: card_omitted_add_card_kept
declarations.signature: theorem card_omitted_add_card_kept [Nontrivial R] [Fintype I] [Fintype J] : Fintype.card D.Omitted + Fintype.card J = Fintype.card I

declarations.name: digit
declarations.docstring: The digit extracted from `x`: `⌊4x + 2/3⌋`.

declarations.name: step
declarations.docstring: One centred base-four step: `x ↦ 4x - ⌊4x + 2/3⌋`.

declarations.name: rem
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rem (x : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ | 0 => x | m + 1 => step (rem x m) /-- The `m`-th digit (`m ≥ 0`), carrying weight `4^{-(m+1)}`. -/ noncomputable def dig (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Iterated remainders.

declarations.name: dig
declarations.signature: noncomputable def dig (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The `m`-th digit (`m ≥ 0`), carrying weight `4^{-(m+1)}`.

declarations.name: InJ
declarations.docstring: The remainder interval `J = [-2/3, 1/3)`.

declarations.name: digit_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem digit_bounds {x : ℝ} (hx : InJ x) : -2 ≤ digit x ∧ digit x ≤ 1

declarations.name: rem_mem
declarations.signature: theorem rem_mem {x : ℝ} (hx : InJ x) (m : ℕ) : InJ (rem x m)

declarations.name: dig_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem dig_bounds {x : ℝ} (hx : InJ x) (m : ℕ) : -2 ≤ dig x m ∧ dig x m ≤ 1

declarations.name: rem_succ
declarations.signature: theorem rem_succ (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : rem x (m + 1) = 4 * rem x m - (dig x m : ℝ)

declarations.name: abs_rem_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_rem_le {x : ℝ} (hx : InJ x) (m : ℕ) : |rem x m| ≤ 2 / 3

declarations.name: expansion
declarations.signature: theorem expansion (x : ℝ) (M : ℕ) : x = (∑ m ∈ Finset.range M, (dig x m : ℝ) / 4 ^ (m + 1)) + rem x M / 4 ^ M
declarations.docstring: Finite expansion with exact remainder.

declarations.name: abs_dig_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_dig_le {x : ℝ} (hx : InJ x) (m : ℕ) : |(dig x m : ℝ)| ≤ 2

declarations.name: summable_digits
declarations.signature: theorem summable_digits {x : ℝ} (hx : InJ x) : Summable (fun m : ℕ => (dig x m : ℝ) / 4 ^ (m + 1))

declarations.name: hasSum_digits
declarations.signature: theorem hasSum_digits {x : ℝ} (hx : InJ x) : HasSum (fun m : ℕ => (dig x m : ℝ) / 4 ^ (m + 1)) x
declarations.docstring: The centred digits sum to `x`.

declarations.name: S
declarations.docstring: The binary totient series in the repository's coefficient-series coordinate: `∑' n, φ(n+1)/2^(n+1)`.

declarations.name: summable_totientTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_totientTerm : Summable (fun n : ℕ => (Nat.totient (n + 1) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1))

declarations.name: summable_idTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_idTerm : Summable (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1))

declarations.name: xi
declarations.docstring: `ξ = 5/4 - S`, the quantity expanded in centred base four.

declarations.name: delta
declarations.docstring: The perturbation: the `m`-th centred digit at the even argument `2m`, zero at odd arguments and at `0`.

declarations.name: control
declarations.docstring: The control coefficient sequence `c = φ + δ`.

declarations.name: delta_odd
declarations.signature: theorem delta_odd {n : ℕ} (hn : n % 2 = 1) : delta n = 0

declarations.name: delta_even
declarations.signature: theorem delta_even (m : ℕ) : delta (2 * m + 2) = dig xi m

declarations.name: delta_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem delta_bounds (n : ℕ) : -2 ≤ delta n ∧ delta n ≤ 1

declarations.name: totient_ge_two_of_even
declarations.signature: theorem totient_ge_two_of_even {n : ℕ} (hn : n % 2 = 0) (h4 : 4 ≤ n) : 2 ≤ Nat.totient n

declarations.name: totient_add_delta_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem totient_add_delta_nonneg (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ (Nat.totient n : ℤ) + delta n

declarations.name: control_cast
declarations.signature: theorem control_cast (n : ℕ) : (control n : ℤ) = (Nat.totient n : ℤ) + delta n

declarations.name: control_cast_real
declarations.signature: theorem control_cast_real (n : ℕ) : (control n : ℝ) = (Nat.totient n : ℝ) + (delta n : ℝ)

declarations.name: control_odd
declarations.signature: theorem control_odd {n : ℕ} (hn : n % 2 = 1) : control n = Nat.totient n

declarations.name: control_le
declarations.signature: theorem control_le (n : ℕ) : control n ≤ n

declarations.name: control_sub_totient_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem control_sub_totient_bounds (n : ℕ) : -2 ≤ (control n : ℤ) - Nat.totient n ∧ (control n : ℤ) - Nat.totient n ≤ 1

declarations.name: abs_control_sub_totient_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_control_sub_totient_le (n : ℕ) : |(control n : ℤ) - Nat.totient n| ≤ 2

declarations.name: summable_deltaTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_deltaTerm : Summable (fun n : ℕ => (delta (n + 1) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1))

declarations.name: tsum_deltaTerm
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_deltaTerm : ∑' n : ℕ, (delta (n + 1) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1) = xi

declarations.name: control_series
declarations.docstring: **Main identity.** The control series is exactly `5/4`.

declarations.name: parity_perturbed_rational_control
declarations.signature: theorem parity_perturbed_rational_control : (∀ n, control n ≤ n) ∧ (∀ n, n % 2 = 1 → control n = Nat.totient n) ∧ (∀ n, |(control n : ℤ) - Nat.totient n| ≤ 2) ∧ binaryCoeffSeries control = 5 / 4
declarations.docstring: **Summary.** A coefficient sequence bounded by `n`, equal to `φ` at every odd argument, within `2` of `φ` everywhere, with rational binary series.

declarations.name: oddAgree_carryKernel_diff
declarations.signature: theorem oddAgree_carryKernel_diff {c : ℕ → ℕ} (hodd : ∀ n, n % 2 = 1 → c n = Nat.totient n) {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit c v u) (j r : ℕ) : (fun n => (v : ℚ) * totientKernelSeq (j + 1) (2 * r + 1) n) = fun n => 2 * carryKernelSeq u (j + 1) (2 * r + 1 - 1) n - carryKernelSeq u (j + 1) (2 * r + 1) n
declarations.docstring: For a tempered orbit of any coefficient sequence that agrees with `φ` on odd arguments, every odd totient channel at a positive level is a two-term difference of carry sections.

declarations.name: canonicalCarryDifferenceFamily_eq_smul_totient_of_oddAgree
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalCarryDifferenceFamily_eq_smul_totient_of_oddAgree {c : ℕ → ℕ} (hodd : ∀ n, n % 2 = 1 → c n = Nat.totient n) {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit c v u) (e : ℕ) : canonicalCarryDifferenceFamily u e = fun i => (v : ℚ) • canonicalTotientOddKernelFamily e i

declarations.name: finrank_canonicalCarryKernel_ge_of_oddAgree
declarations.signature: theorem finrank_canonicalCarryKernel_ge_of_oddAgree {c : ℕ → ℕ} (hodd : ∀ n, n % 2 = 1 → c n = Nat.totient n) {v : ℕ} {u : ℕ → ℤ} (hv : 0 < v) (hu : IsTemperedBinaryOrbit c v u) (e : ℕ) : 2 ^ e - 1 ≤ finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalCarryKernelFamily u e)))
declarations.docstring: **Carry anti-compression for odd-agreeing coefficients.** The finite-level carry sections of any tempered orbit of a coefficient sequence agreeing with `φ` at odd arguments have rank at least `2^e - 1`. This is the existing totient theorem with its only totient input, the odd channels, kept.

declarations.name: control_temperedOrbit_carryRank_unbounded
declarations.signature: theorem control_temperedOrbit_carryRank_unbounded : ∃ v : ℕ, 0 < v ∧ ∃ u : ℕ → ℤ, IsTemperedBinaryOrbit control v u ∧ ∀ e : ℕ, 2 ^ e - 1 ≤ finrank ℚ (Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range (canonicalCarryKernelFamily u e)))
declarations.docstring: **The control satisfies the whole anti-compression architecture.** It has a tempered integral binary carry whose dyadic section rank is at least `2^e - 1` at every level, exactly as a rational value of the totient series would force; and its series is the rational number `5/4`.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_self_eq_totientBlock_sub
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_self_eq_totientBlock_sub (h N : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy h N h = totientBlock h (N + h) - totientBlock h N
declarations.docstring: **Depth = period bridge.** The full-depth window discrepancy is the difference of two adjacent period blocks: `W(h,N) = Q_{h,N+h} - Q_{h,N}`.

declarations.name: totientBlock_add
declarations.signature: theorem totientBlock_add (a b N : ℕ) : totientBlock (a + b) N = 2 ^ b * totientBlock a N + totientBlock b (N + a)
declarations.docstring: **Block concatenation.** `Q_{a+b,N} = 2^b·Q_{a,N} + Q_{b,N+a}`. This is the identity that nests the cyclotomic fan: the order-4 channel at height `h` is the order-2 channel at height `2h`.

declarations.name: pureDyadicEndpointError
declarations.signature: def pureDyadicEndpointError (H c : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : ℤ

declarations.name: totientBlock_height_succ
declarations.signature: theorem totientBlock_height_succ (H c : ℕ) : totientBlock (H + 1) c = 2 * totientBlock H c + (Nat.totient (c + H + 1) : ℤ)

declarations.name: pureDyadicEndpointError_succ
declarations.signature: theorem pureDyadicEndpointError_succ (H c : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : pureDyadicEndpointError (H + 1) c k = 2 * pureDyadicEndpointError H c k + (Nat.totient (c + H + 1) : ℤ) - k

declarations.name: pureDyadicEndpointError_add
declarations.signature: theorem pureDyadicEndpointError_add (H L c : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : pureDyadicEndpointError (H + L) c k = 2 ^ L * pureDyadicEndpointError H c k + pureDyadicEndpointError L (c + H) k

declarations.name: prime_forces_pureDyadicEndpointError_excursion
declarations.signature: theorem prime_forces_pureDyadicEndpointError_excursion (H c : ℕ) (k : ℤ) (hp : Nat.Prime (c + H + 1)) : (c + H : ℤ) - k ≤ |pureDyadicEndpointError (H + 1) c k| + 2 * |pureDyadicEndpointError H c k|

declarations.name: exists_late_pureDyadicEndpointError_excursion
declarations.signature: theorem exists_late_pureDyadicEndpointError_excursion (c B : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : ∃ H, B ≤ H ∧ (c + H : ℤ) - k ≤ |pureDyadicEndpointError (H + 1) c k| + 2 * |pureDyadicEndpointError H c k|

declarations.name: exists_late_pureDyadicEndpointError_oneThird_excursion
declarations.signature: theorem exists_late_pureDyadicEndpointError_oneThird_excursion (c B : ℕ) (k : ℤ) : ∃ H, B ≤ H ∧ ((c + H : ℤ) - k ≤ 3 * |pureDyadicEndpointError H c k| ∨ (c + H : ℤ) - k ≤ 3 * |pureDyadicEndpointError (H + 1) c k|)

declarations.name: exists_late_pureDyadicEndpointError_oneThird

This deliberately forgets that the witnesses must be the consecutive arguments `c+H`. -/ def PointwiseTotientValued (digit : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop

declarations.docstring: Doubling instance of concatenation: the two `2h`-blocks entering the order-2 test at height `2h` are built from the four `h`-blocks of the fan.

declarations.name: tail_diff_mul_mem_int_of_forall_step
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_mul_mem_int_of_forall_step {h₀ N₀ : ℕ} (hint : ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → totientTail (N + h₀) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : ∀ t N, N₀ ≤ N → totientTail (N + t * h₀) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Integrality of the step tail difference from `N₀` on telescopes to every multiple of the period.

declarations.name: PeriodMultipleKillSupply
declarations.docstring: **The supply normal form.** For every ray `d ≥ 1` and every basepoint threshold `c`, some multiple period `t·d` admits a certified kill at some `N ≥ c`. The odd part of a hypothetical denominator selects the ray; the kill contradicts the tail-period law on it.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_periodMultipleKillSupply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_periodMultipleKillSupply (hsupply : PeriodMultipleKillSupply) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **Supply ⇒ irrationality.** Rationality yields a period `h₀` with the step tail difference integral from `N₀` on; telescoping makes every multiple period integral there; the supplied kill on the ray of `h₀` is a contradiction.

declarations.name: periodMultipleKillSupply_of_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem periodMultipleKillSupply_of_irrational (hirr : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)) : PeriodMultipleKillSupply
declarations.docstring: **Irrationality ⇒ supply** (certificate completeness on each ray, at `t = 1` and the exact basepoint).

declarations.name: periodMultipleKillSupply_iff_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem periodMultipleKillSupply_iff_irrational : PeriodMultipleKillSupply ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **The exact open core of #249 in ray form.** The period-multiple kill supply is not a sufficient surrogate: it is equivalent to irrationality.

declarations.name: ApFullDepthEscape
declarations.docstring: **Depth = period escape (locked depth `L = h`).** The single-inequality form: on every ray and at every basepoint, some multiple period is central at its own depth. Sufficient for irrationality; not known necessary.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_apFullDepthEscape

declarations.name: periodic_add_mul
declarations.signature: theorem periodic_add_mul {K : Type*} (w : ℕ → K) (Q : ℕ) (hw : ∀ n, w (n + Q) = w n) (n t : ℕ) : w (n + Q * t) = w n
declarations.docstring: Iterating a period, stated without any division or residue conventions.

declarations.name: periodic_coefficients_zero
declarations.signature: theorem periodic_coefficients_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (a b : ι → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) (hcross : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → a i * b j ≠ a j * b i) (Q : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (w : ι → ℕ → ℚ) (hw : ∀ i n, w i (n + Q) = w i n) (hrel : ∀ n, ∑ i, w i n * (Nat.totient (a i * n + b i) : ℚ) = 0) : ∀ i n, w i n = 0
declarations.docstring: Periodic coefficients in a finite affine-totient relation all vanish. The affine forms may have zero intercepts; slopes are positive.

declarations.name: checkerboard
declarations.signature: def checkerboard (F : Bool → Bool → ℤ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Mixed Boolean curvature on a two-anchor rectangle.

declarations.name: checkerboard_separable
declarations.signature: theorem checkerboard_separable (u v : Bool → ℤ) : checkerboard (fun i j => u i + v j) = 0
declarations.docstring: The checkerboard kills every sum of one-coordinate backgrounds.

declarations.name: checkerboard_unique
declarations.signature: theorem checkerboard_unique (c00 c10 c01 c11 : ℤ) (hrow0 : c00 + c01 = 0) (hrow1 : c10 + c11 = 0) (hcol0 : c00 + c10 = 0) (hcol1 : c01 + c11 = 0) : c10 = -c00 ∧ c01 = -c00 ∧ c11 = c00
declarations.docstring: The checkerboard is the unique two-by-two joint annihilator up to scale.

declarations.name: fourPoint_layer_identity
declarations.signature: theorem fourPoint_layer_identity (A C : ℕ → ℕ) (r s q : ℕ) (hq : A q = C 1 * C q) (hrq : A (r * q) = C 1 * C r * C q * C (r * q)) (hsq : A (s * q) = C 1 * C s * C q * C (s * q)) (hrsq : A (r * s * q) = C 1 * C r * C s * C q * C (r * s) * C (r * q) * C (s * q) * C (r * s * q)) : A (r * s * q) * A q = A (r * q) * A (s * q) * C (r * s) * C (r * s * q)
declarations.docstring: Abstract squarefree divisor-layer cancellation. The hypotheses are the four explicit divisor factorizations, so no resultant API is hidden here.

declarations.name: residueClass_step_has_centred_completion
declarations.signature: theorem residueClass_step_has_centred_completion (b a e M R : ℤ) (hR : 0 < R) (hM : M = 2 * R) : ∃ c e' : ℤ, (∃ z : ℤ, c = a + M * z) ∧ e' = b * e + c ∧ |e'| ≤ R
declarations.docstring: Any prescribed residue class modulo an even modulus admits a digit which recentres an affine carry step. This generalises the legacy fixed-precision valuation/unit completion no-go.

declarations.name: PrimeRayLayerSupply
declarations.signature: def PrimeRayLayerSupply (C : ℕ → ℕ) (m : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Eventual nontrivial, clean cyclotomic layers on the prime ray `m*q`.

declarations.name: BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer
declarations.signature: def BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer (C : ℕ → ℕ) (m d : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Every rational prime divisor of a layer supplies an exact-order witness in extension degree at most `d`.

declarations.name: EventualBoundedDegreeOrderConsumer
declarations.signature: def EventualBoundedDegreeOrderConsumer (C : ℕ → ℕ) (m d : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Bounded-degree order witnesses beyond a prime-index cutoff. Unlike `BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer`, this permits the finitely many characteristic primes that occur naturally in cyclotomic layers.

declarations.name: primeRay_divisor_pow_gt
declarations.signature: theorem primeRay_divisor_pow_gt {C : ℕ → ℕ} {m d q p : ℕ} (horder : BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer C m d) (hq : q.Prime) (hp : p.Prime) (hpC : p ∣ C (m * q)) : m * q < p ^ d
declarations.docstring: If a prime `p` divides `C (m*q)`, then a bounded-degree order witness forces the exact natural-number inequality `m * q < p ^ d`.

declarations.name: primeRay_divisor_gt_of_pow_le
declarations.signature: theorem primeRay_divisor_gt_of_pow_le {C : ℕ → ℕ} {m d q p B : ℕ} (horder : BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer C m d) (hq : q.Prime) (hp : p.Prime) (hpC : p ∣ C (m * q)) (hB : B ^ d ≤ m * q) : B < p
declarations.docstring: If in addition `B ^ d ≤ m * q`, then the prime divisor `p` is strictly larger than `B`.

declarations.name: FinitePrimeSupportEscape
declarations.signature: def FinitePrimeSupportEscape (C : ℕ → ℕ) (m : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Large prime-ray layers escape every prescribed finite prime support.

declarations.name: UnboundedPrimeDivisorSupply
declarations.signature: def UnboundedPrimeDivisorSupply (C : ℕ → ℕ) (m : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The prime divisors appearing on the ray `m*q` are unbounded, even after imposing an arbitrary lower bound on the prime index `q`.

declarations.name: finitePrimeSupportEscape_of_orderConsumer
declarations.signature: theorem finitePrimeSupportEscape_of_orderConsumer {C : ℕ → ℕ} {m d : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (horder : BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer C m d) : FinitePrimeSupportEscape C m
declarations.docstring: Bounded-degree exact-order realisability already excludes every fixed finite set of characteristics on a sufficiently remote prime ray. The Archimedean layer-supply hypothesis is not needed for this exclusion step.

declarations.name: finitePrimeSupportEscape_of_eventualOrderConsumer
declarations.signature: theorem finitePrimeSupportEscape_of_eventualOrderConsumer {C : ℕ → ℕ} {m d : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (horder : EventualBoundedDegreeOrderConsumer C m d) : FinitePrimeSupportEscape C m
declarations.docstring: Eventual bounded-degree order realisability is already enough to exclude every fixed finite set of characteristics on a sufficiently remote prime ray. This is the version matched by actual cyclotomic layers.

declarations.name: unboundedPrimeDivisorSupply_of_layerSupply_of_finitePrimeSupportEscape
declarations.signature: theorem unboundedPrimeDivisorSupply_of_layerSupply_of_finitePrimeSupportEscape {C : ℕ → ℕ} {m : ℕ} (hsupply : PrimeRayLayerSupply C m) (hescape : FinitePrimeSupportEscape C m) : UnboundedPrimeDivisorSupply C m
declarations.docstring: Nontrivial layers together with finite-support escape force genuinely new, arbitrarily large prime divisors on cofinally large prime indices.

declarations.name: unboundedPrimeDivisorSupply_of_orderConsumer
declarations.signature: theorem unboundedPrimeDivisorSupply_of_orderConsumer {C : ℕ → ℕ} {m d : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hsupply : PrimeRayLayerSupply C m) (horder : BoundedDegreeOrderConsumer C m d) : UnboundedPrimeDivisorSupply C m
declarations.docstring: Bounded-degree order witnesses give finite-support escape; if nontrivial prime-ray layers are also supplied, their prime divisors are unbounded.

declarations.name: unboundedPrimeDivisorSupply_of_eventualOrderConsumer
declarations.signature: theorem unboundedPrimeDivisorSupply_of_eventualOrderConsumer {C : ℕ → ℕ} {m d : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hsupply : PrimeRayLayerSupply C m) (horder : EventualBoundedDegreeOrderConsumer C m d) : UnboundedPrimeDivisorSupply C m
declarations.docstring: Eventual order witnesses and eventual nontrivial layers suffice for cofinally unbounded prime divisors. No conclusion about phase escape or irrationality is asserted.

declarations.name: not_forall_rankOneSubrankQuotient_sub_theta_two_gt_one_div_fifteen

declarations.docstring: `1/15` is not a uniform unit-fraction lower bound: it already fails at the unique minimiser.

declarations.name: positive_direct_sum_sub_theta_two_gt_twentyOne_div_threeTwenty
declarations.signature: theorem positive_direct_sum_sub_theta_two_gt_twentyOne_div_threeTwenty {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (w : ι → ℝ) (e Y : ι → ℕ) (hw : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < w i) (he : ∀ i ∈ s, 1 ≤ e i) (hY : ∀ i ∈ s, 4 ≤ Y i) : (21 : ℝ) / 320 < (∑ i ∈ s, w i * rankOneSubrankQuotient (e i) (Y i)) / (∑ i ∈ s, w i) - mobiusMersenneTheta 2

declarations.name: primitive_form_abs_gt_twentyOne_div_threeTwenty
declarations.signature: theorem primitive_form_abs_gt_twentyOne_div_threeTwenty {e Y q : ℕ} {p : ℤ} (he : 1 ≤ e) (hY : 4 ≤ Y) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hquot : rankOneSubrankQuotient e Y = (p : ℝ) / q) : (q : ℝ) * (21 : ℝ) / 320 < |(q : ℝ) * mobiusMersenneTheta 2 - p|

declarations.name: mobiusMersennePrefix
declarations.signature: noncomputable def mobiusMersennePrefix (Y r : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The first `Y` atoms of the Möbius--Mersenne rung `r`.

declarations.name: mobiusMersenneTailAfter

declarations.name: rankOneSubrankQuotient
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rankOneSubrankQuotient (e Y : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The rank-one strict-subrank quotient from the first `Y` atoms.

declarations.name: two_pow_three_le_two_pow
declarations.signature: private lemma two_pow_three_le_two_pow {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) : (2 : ℝ) ^ 3 ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ r

declarations.name: geometric_base_le_eighth
declarations.signature: private lemma geometric_base_le_eighth {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) : (1 : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ r ≤ 1 / 8

declarations.name: norm_term_le_eighth_geometric
declarations.signature: private lemma norm_term_le_eighth_geometric {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) (n : ℕ) : ‖mobiusMersenneTerm r n‖ ≤ ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ^ n

declarations.name: mobiusMersenneTheta_eq_prefix_add_tail
declarations.signature: theorem mobiusMersenneTheta_eq_prefix_add_tail (Y r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : mobiusMersenneTheta r = mobiusMersennePrefix Y r + mobiusMersenneTailAfter Y r

declarations.name: abs_mobiusMersenneTheta_sub_prefix_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_mobiusMersenneTheta_sub_prefix_le {Y r : ℕ} (hY : 4 ≤ Y) (hr : 3 ≤ r) : |mobiusMersenneTheta r - mobiusMersennePrefix Y r| ≤ (1 : ℝ) / 3584
declarations.docstring: Uniform prefix error: after four atoms, every rung `r ≥ 3` is within `1/3584` of its finite prefix.

declarations.name: three_pow_lt_mersenne_product
declarations.signature: private lemma three_pow_lt_mersenne_product : ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → (3 : ℝ) ^ r < (2 : ℝ) ^ r * ((2 : ℝ) ^ r - 1)

declarations.name: mobiusMersenneTheta_ge_alpha
declarations.signature: theorem mobiusMersenneTheta_ge_alpha {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) : (1429 : ℝ) / 1512 ≤ mobiusMersenneTheta r
declarations.docstring: Every rung `r ≥ 3` is bounded below by the fixed rational `1429/1512`.

declarations.name: mobiusMersenneTheta_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem mobiusMersenneTheta_lt_one {r : ℕ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) : mobiusMersenneTheta r < 1
declarations.docstring: Every rung `r ≥ 3` is strictly below `1`.

declarations.name: mobiusMersenneTheta_two_lt_eight_ninths
declarations.docstring: The target rung itself lies strictly below `8/9`.

declarations.name: rankOneSubrankQuotient_sub_theta_two_gt
declarations.signature: theorem rankOneSubrankQuotient_sub_theta_two_gt {e Y : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e) (hY : 4 ≤ Y) : (1 : ℝ) / 480 < rankOneSubrankQuotient e Y - mobiusMersenneTheta 2
declarations.docstring: **Uniform rank-one no-go.** Every strict-subrank monomial quotient in this family overshoots `Θ₂` by more than `1/480`.

declarations.name: positive_direct_sum_sub_theta_two_gt
declarations.signature: theorem positive_direct_sum_sub_theta_two_gt {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (w : ι → ℝ) (e Y : ι → ℕ) (hw : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < w i) (he : ∀ i ∈ s, 1 ≤ e i) (hY : ∀ i ∈ s, 4 ≤ Y i) : (1 : ℝ) / 480 < (∑ i ∈ s, w i * rankOneSubrankQuotient (e i) (Y i)) / (∑ i ∈ s, w i) - mobiusMersenneTheta 2
declarations.docstring: Positive finite direct sums do not evade the obstruction: a positively weighted average of admissible rank-one quotients still overshoots `Θ₂` by more than `1/480`.

declarations.name: primitive_form_abs_gt
declarations.signature: theorem primitive_form_abs_gt {e Y q : ℕ} {p : ℤ} (he : 1 ≤ e) (hY : 4 ≤ Y) (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hquot : rankOneSubrankQuotient e Y = (p : ℝ) / q) : (q : ℝ) / 480 < |(q : ℝ) * mobiusMersenneTheta 2 - p|
declarations.docstring: Primitive integer linear forms arising from these quotients are bounded away from zero. In fact the lower bound grows linearly with the denominator.

declarations.name: dyadicValue
declarations.signature: noncomputable def dyadicValue (a : ℕ → ℤ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The binary value `∑ a n / 2 ^ n` of an integer coefficient sequence.

declarations.name: dyadicTail
declarations.signature: noncomputable def dyadicTail (a : ℕ → ℤ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The exact tail `R_N = ∑_{j ≥ 1} a (N + j) / 2 ^ j`.

declarations.name: summable_const_div_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem summable_const_div_two_pow (c : ℝ) : Summable fun n : ℕ => c / 2 ^ n

declarations.name: summable_const_div_two_pow_succ
declarations.signature: theorem summable_const_div_two_pow_succ (c : ℝ) : Summable fun j : ℕ => c / 2 ^ (j + 1)

declarations.name: tsum_const_div_two_pow_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_const_div_two_pow_succ (c : ℝ) : (∑' j : ℕ, c / 2 ^ (j + 1)) = c

declarations.name: summable_dyadicTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_dyadicTerm (hC : ∀ n, |(a n : ℝ)| ≤ C) : Summable fun n : ℕ => (a n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n

declarations.name: summable_dyadicTailTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_dyadicTailTerm (hC : ∀ n, |(a n : ℝ)| ≤ C) (N : ℕ) : Summable fun j : ℕ => (a (N + 1 + j) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (j + 1)

declarations.name: abs_dyadicTail_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_dyadicTail_le (hC : ∀ n, |(a n : ℝ)| ≤ C) (N : ℕ) : |dyadicTail a N| ≤ C
declarations.docstring: The tail is bounded by the same constant that bounds the coefficients.

declarations.name: exists_int_add_dyadicTail
declarations.signature: theorem exists_int_add_dyadicTail (hC : ∀ n, |(a n : ℝ)| ≤ C) (N : ℕ) : ∃ P : ℤ, (2 : ℝ) ^ N * dyadicValue a = (P : ℝ) + dyadicTail a N
declarations.docstring: `2 ^ N * value = integer + tail`.

declarations.name: dyadicTail_pulse
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicTail_pulse (hC : ∀ n, |(a n : ℝ)| ≤ C) {N L : ℕ} {t : ℤ} (hcentre : a (N + 1 + L) = t) (hzero : ∀ i, i ≤ 2 * L → i ≠ L → a (N + 1 + i) = 0) : dyadicTail a N = (t : ℝ) / 2 ^ (L + 1) + dyadicTail a (N + 2 * L + 1) / 2 ^ (2 * L + 1)
declarations.docstring: Splitting the tail at an isolated pulse: a `2L+1`-window whose only nonzero letter is the centre `t`, plus a rescaled remainder.

declarations.name: abs_le_abs_add_abs
declarations.signature: private theorem abs_le_abs_add_abs (X Y : ℝ) : |X| ≤ |X + Y| + |Y|

declarations.name: abs_int_add_ge
declarations.signature: private theorem abs_int_add_ge (M : ℤ) {x : ℝ} (hx : |x| < 1 / 2) : |x| ≤ |(M : ℝ) + x|

declarations.name: isolated_pulse_separation
declarations.signature: theorem isolated_pulse_separation (hC : ∀ n, |(a n : ℝ)| ≤ C) {N L q : ℕ} {t : ℤ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) (hL : 2 * (q : ℝ) * C < 2 ^ L) (hcentre : a (N + 1 + L) = t) (ht : t ≠ 0) (hzero : ∀ i, i ≤ 2 * L → i ≠ L → a (N + 1 + i) = 0) (k : ℤ) : (q : ℝ) * (|(t : ℝ)| - C / 2 ^ L) / 2 ^ (N + 1 + L) ≤ |(q : ℝ) * dyadicValue a - (k : ℝ)|
declarations.docstring: **Isolated pulse separation** (r02 Lemma 3, quantitative form). If the bounded integer sequence `a` has a nonzero letter `t` at `p = N + 1 + L` with a two-sided block of `L` zeros around it, then for every `q ≥ 1` with `2 ^ L > 2 * q * C` the number `q * dyadicValue a` stays at distance at least `q * (|t| - C / 2 ^ L) / 2 ^ p` from every integer `k`.

declarations.name: irrational_dyadicValue_of_pulses
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_dyadicValue_of_pulses (hC : ∀ n, |(a n : ℝ)| ≤ C) (hpulse : ∀ L : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, L + 1 < p ∧ a p ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ j, 0 < j → j ≤ L → a (p - j) = 0 ∧ a (p + j) = 0) : Irrational (dyadicValue a)
declarations.docstring: Arbitrarily long two-sided isolated pulses force irrationality of the binary value. This is the packaged consumer of `isolated_pulse_separation`.

declarations.name: coprime_of_modEq
declarations.signature: private theorem coprime_of_modEq {x y n : ℕ} (h : x ≡ y [MOD n]) (hy : Nat.Coprime y n) : Nat.Coprime x n

declarations.name: coprime_prime_of_lt
declarations.signature: private theorem coprime_prime_of_lt {l n : ℕ} (hl : l.Prime) (hn0 : 0 < n) (hn : n < l) : Nat.Coprime l n

declarations.name: dvd_totient_of_prime_dvd
declarations.signature: private theorem dvd_totient_of_prime_dvd {m l n : ℕ} (hl : l.Prime) (hlm : l ≡ 1 [MOD m]) (hdvd : l ∣ n) : m ∣ Nat.totient n

declarations.name: exists_isolation_modulus
declarations.signature: theorem exists_isolation_modulus (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (L : ℕ) : ∃ Q b : ℕ, 0 < Q ∧ Nat.Coprime Q m ∧ Nat.Coprime b Q ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, L < p → p ≡ b [MOD Q] → ∀ j, 0 < j → j ≤ L → m ∣ Nat.totient (p - j) ∧ m ∣ Nat.totient (p + j)
declarations.docstring: The Chinese-remainder modulus that forces `m ∣ φ (p ± j)` on a window of half-width `L` around any `p` in a prescribed residue class.

declarations.name: two_sided_prime_isolation
declarations.signature: theorem two_sided_prime_isolation {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (L N r : ℕ) (hr : Nat.Coprime (r + 1) m) : ∃ p : ℕ, N < p ∧ L + 1 < p ∧ p.Prime ∧ Nat.totient p ≡ r [MOD m] ∧ ∀ j, 0 < j → j ≤ L → m ∣ Nat.totient (p - j) ∧ m ∣ Nat.totient (p + j)
declarations.docstring: **Two-sided prime isolation** (r02 Lemma 2). For `m ≥ 2` and any `r` with `gcd (r+1, m) = 1` there are arbitrarily large primes `p` with `φ p ≡ r [MOD m]` and `m ∣ φ (p ± j)` for every `0 < j ≤ L`.

declarations.name: totientObservableCoeff
declarations.signature: def totientObservableCoeff (f : ℕ → ℤ) (m n : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The coefficient sequence of a fixed-resolution observable: read the totient word at resolution `m` and apply an integer-valued letter map `f`.

declarations.name: totientObservableValue
declarations.signature: noncomputable def totientObservableValue (f : ℕ → ℤ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The binary value of a fixed-resolution observable of the totient word.

declarations.name: irrational_totientObservable
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totientObservable {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (f : ℕ → ℤ) (hf0 : f 0 = 0) {r : ℕ} (hr : r < m) (hcop : Nat.Coprime (r + 1) m) (hfr : f r ≠ 0) : Irrational (totientObservableValue f m)
declarations.docstring: **The special-value irrationality theorem for fixed-resolution observables.** If `f` vanishes at the zero residue and is nonzero at some residue `r < m` with `gcd (r + 1, m) = 1`, then `∑ f (φ n mod m) / 2 ^ n` is irrational. This is the strongest correct form of r02 Theorem 1: the classification at `m = 2 ^ k` is complete precisely because there the unit condition `gcd (r+1, m) = 1` is automatic for every even `r`.

declarations.name: fixed_resolution_observable_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem fixed_resolution_observable_irrational {k : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (f : ℕ → ℤ) (hf0 : f 0 = 0) {r : ℕ} (hr : r < 2 ^ k) (hreven : r % 2 = 0) (hfr : f r ≠ 0) : Irrational (totientObservableValue f (2 ^ k))
declarations.docstring: **r02 Theorem 1, forward direction.** At dyadic resolution `2 ^ k` every integer-valued letter map that vanishes on the zero residue and is nonzero on some even residue has irrational binary value. Here the unit condition of `irrational_totientObservable` is automatic: `r` even makes `r + 1` odd. This is the substantive half of the complete rational-relation classification. The remaining half — clearing denominators of a rational-valued letter map, and the converse direction supplied by `∑_{r even} V_{k,r} = 1/4` — is not formalised here.

declarations.name: totientResidueValue
declarations.docstring: `A_m = ∑_{n} (φ n mod m) / 2 ^ n`, least nonnegative residues.

declarations.name: totientResidueValue_eq
declarations.signature: theorem totientResidueValue_eq (m : ℕ) : totientResidueValue m = totientObservableValue (fun x => (x : ℤ)) m

declarations.name: residue_series_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem residue_series_irrational {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : Irrational (totientResidueValue m)
declarations.docstring: **Corollary 5 of r02.** For every `m ≥ 3` the least-residue totient series `A_m = ∑ (φ n mod m) / 2 ^ n` is irrational. (`A_1 = 0` and `A_2 = 3/4`, so the hypothesis `3 ≤ m` is sharp.)

declarations.name: hankelTruncation
declarations.signature: noncomputable def hankelTruncation (D i j : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The same Möbius truncation, with the indices of `totientHankel`.

declarations.name: hankelTruncation_triangular_rank
declarations.signature: theorem hankelTruncation_triangular_rank (D : ℕ) : ∃ f g : Fin (D * (D + 1) / 2) → ℕ → ℝ, ∀ i j, hankelTruncation D i j = ∑ k : Fin (D * (D + 1) / 2), f k i * g k j
declarations.docstring: Shifting both factors by one preserves the explicit triangular budget.

declarations.name: sum_Icc_one_eq_sum_range_succ
declarations.signature: private theorem sum_Icc_one_eq_sum_range_succ (f : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) : (∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f i) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, f (i + 1)

declarations.name: hankelTruncation_mean_error_le
declarations.signature: theorem hankelTruncation_mean_error_le (D N : ℕ) (hD : 0 < D) (hN : 0 < N) : (∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, |totientHankel i j - hankelTruncation D i j|) / ((N : ℝ) ^ 2) ≤ 2 / (D : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The finite-square mean estimate, for exactly the uniform-barrier matrix.

declarations.name: hankelTruncation_uniform_error_lower
declarations.signature: theorem hankelTruncation_uniform_error_lower (D : ℕ) : ENNReal.ofReal ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ≤ uniformError totientHankel (hankelTruncation D)

declarations.name: totient_approximation_dichotomy
declarations.signature: theorem totient_approximation_dichotomy (D : ℕ) (hD : 0 < D) : (∃ f g : Fin (D * (D + 1) / 2) → ℕ → ℝ, ∀ i j, hankelTruncation D i j = ∑ k : Fin (D * (D + 1) / 2), f k i * g k j) ∧ (∀ N : ℕ, 0 < N → (∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, |totientHankel i j - hankelTruncation D i j|) / ((N : ℝ) ^ 2) ≤ 2 / (D : ℝ)) ∧ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 : ℝ) / 2) ≤ uniformError totientHankel (hankelTruncation D) ∧ (⨅ A : FiniteRankMatrix, uniformError totientHankel A.val) = ENNReal.ofReal ((1 : ℝ) / 2)
declarations.docstring: One explicit family has arbitrarily small finite-square mean bounds, but every member retains the uniform gap shared by all finite-rank matrices.

declarations.name: normalizedTotient
declarations.docstring: The normalized totient on positive integers.

declarations.name: truncatedTotient
declarations.signature: noncomputable def truncatedTotient (D m : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The `D`-term Möbius approximation to the normalized totient.

declarations.name: divisor_indicator_factor
declarations.signature: private theorem divisor_indicator_factor (d i n : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) : (if d ∣ i + n then (1 : ℝ) else 0) = ∑ a : Fin d, (if i % d = a.val then (1 : ℝ) else 0) * (if (n : ZMod d) = -(a.val : ZMod d) then (1 : ℝ) else 0)
declarations.docstring: A modular divisibility test is a sum of `d` separated residue tests.

declarations.name: truncatedTotient_factor
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedTotient_factor (D i n : ℕ) : truncatedTotient D (i + n) = ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 D, ∑ a : Fin d, (((moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ) / d * (if i % d = a.val then 1 else 0)) * (if (n : ZMod d) = -(a.val : ZMod d) then 1 else 0)
declarations.docstring: The explicit residue expansion of the truncated Hankel matrix.

declarations.name: truncatedTotient_separated
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedTotient_separated (D : ℕ) : ∃ r : ℕ, r = ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 D, d ∧ ∃ f g : Fin r → ℕ → ℝ, ∀ i n, truncatedTotient D (i + n) = ∑ k : Fin r, f k i * g k n
declarations.docstring: An explicit finite separated representation, with one factor for every residue class modulo every `d ≤ D`.

declarations.name: truncatedTotient_finite_rank
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedTotient_finite_rank (D : ℕ) : ErdosProblems.Erdos269.PaperR8.FiniteSeparatedRank (fun i n => truncatedTotient D (i + n))
declarations.docstring: The Möbius truncations are finite-rank matrices in the #269 interface.

declarations.name: truncatedTotient_factor_count
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedTotient_factor_count (D : ℕ) : (∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 D, d) = D * (D + 1) / 2
declarations.docstring: The number of displayed residue factors is the triangular number.

declarations.name: truncatedTotient_triangular_rank
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedTotient_triangular_rank (D : ℕ) : ∃ f g : Fin (D * (D + 1) / 2) → ℕ → ℝ, ∀ i n, truncatedTotient D (i + n) = ∑ k : Fin (D * (D + 1) / 2), f k i * g k n
declarations.docstring: A concrete separated-rank budget for every Möbius truncation.

declarations.name: normalizedTotient_eq_divisor_sum
declarations.signature: theorem normalizedTotient_eq_divisor_sum (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : normalizedTotient m = ∑ d ∈ m.divisors, ((moebius d : ℤ) : ℝ) / d
declarations.docstring: Möbius inversion in the normalized form needed by the matrix estimate.

declarations.name: abs_normalizedTotient_sub_truncated_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_normalizedTotient_sub_truncated_le (D m : ℕ) (hD : 0 < D) (hm : 0 < m) : |normalizedTotient m - truncatedTotient D m| ≤ ∑ d ∈ Finset.Ioc D m, if d ∣ m then (1 : ℝ) / d else 0
declarations.docstring: The discarded Möbius divisors dominate the pointwise truncation error.

declarations.name: square_translate_sum_le
declarations.signature: private theorem square_translate_sum_le (N : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ m, 0 ≤ f m) : (∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, f (i + n)) ≤ (N : ℝ) * ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (2 * N), f m
declarations.docstring: Each antidiagonal in a leading `N × N` square has at most `N` cells.

declarations.name: tailWeight
declarations.signature: private noncomputable def tailWeight (D m : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: tailWeight_prefix_sum_le
declarations.signature: private theorem tailWeight_prefix_sum_le (D N : ℕ) (hD : 0 < D) : (∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (2 * N), tailWeight D m) ≤ (2 * N : ℝ) / D
declarations.docstring: Divisibility counting and the square-summable tail give an `N`-independent bound after averaging the antidiagonals.

declarations.name: normalizedTotient_mean_error_le
declarations.signature: theorem normalizedTotient_mean_error_le (D N : ℕ) (hD : 0 < D) (hN : 0 < N) : (∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, |normalizedTotient (i + n) - truncatedTotient D (i + n)|) / ((N : ℝ) ^ 2) ≤ 2 / (D : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Every leading square has mean absolute error at most `2/D`, regardless of its size `N`. The approximation has the separated representation above.

declarations.name: TotientTailOrbitBlockGap
declarations.docstring: On arbitrarily late dyadic blocks, the mean real part of the infinite tail-orbit phase is at most `89/100`. The hypotheses include every positive shift `h`; no such estimate is currently known for the totient orbit.

declarations.name: TotientTailOrbitNonpositiveBlockDensity
declarations.docstring: On arbitrarily late dyadic blocks, at least an `11/100` proportion of the tail-orbit phases have nonpositive real part. This is a sufficient density hypothesis, not a statement proved here for the totient orbit.

declarations.name: tailOrbitBlockGap_of_nonpositiveBlockDensity
declarations.docstring: A density of nonpositive phases gives the `89/100` block gap. The other phases contribute at most `1` because every tail-orbit phase has norm one.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_tailOrbitBlockGap
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_tailOrbitBlockGap (hgap : TotientTailOrbitBlockGap) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: A uniform `89/100` block gap for the infinite orbit yields the finite `9/10` gap after choosing one truncation depth for the whole block.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_nonpositiveBlockDensity
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_nonpositiveBlockDensity (hdensity : TotientTailOrbitNonpositiveBlockDensity) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: The nonpositive-density hypothesis implies irrationality through the uniform block-gap theorem.

declarations.name: DTWNaturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap
declarations.docstring: Cofinal prime indices at which the infinite-orbit real part is strictly below `9/10`. The positive margin may depend on the chosen index.

declarations.name: tailOrbitFirstExp_succ

This equivalence does not prove the visit supply or promote unaligned visits to the stronger natural-prime condition.

declarations.name: prime_sparse_rational_value
declarations.signature: theorem prime_sparse_rational_value {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (K : ℕ) : ∃ S : Set ℕ, ∃ e : ℕ → ℕ, ∃ r : ℚ, S ⊆ Set.Ici K ∧ UpperBanachZero S ∧ (∑' n, primeGapDyadicTerm n) < (r : ℝ) ∧ (∀ n, e n ≠ 0 → n ∈ S) ∧ (∀ n < K, primeGap0 n + e n = primeGap0 n) ∧ (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (e n : ℝ) ≤ polylog ε n) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, q ∣ e n ∧ q ∣ ∑ i ∈ range n, e i) ∧ HasSum (fun n => ((primeGap0 n + e n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) (r : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The common nondegenerate interval contains an actual rational number.

declarations.name: odd_perturbation_does_not_preserve_parity
declarations.docstring: Why the arbitrary-M parity remark needs an even-M qualification.

declarations.name: evenIntegral_of_affinePowTwo
declarations.signature: theorem evenIntegral_of_affinePowTwo {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N r : ℕ) (hAff : RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h (N + r)) (dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r) r) : RatEvenIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: **The converse of `affinePowTwo_of_evenIntegral`.** Membership of the depth-`r` affine cylinder forces even integrality at the basepoint, with the *same* witness. This is the theorem the landed strategic reading excludes.

declarations.name: ratAffinePowTwo_iff_evenIntegral
declarations.signature: theorem ratAffinePowTwo_iff_evenIntegral {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N r : ℕ) : RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h (N + r)) (dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r) r ↔ RatEvenIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: **The affine cylinder is exactly even integrality at its basepoint.** The depth and the observed digit block carry no information whatsoever.

declarations.name: ratAffinePowTwo_depth_independent
declarations.signature: theorem ratAffinePowTwo_depth_independent {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N r s : ℕ) : RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h (N + r)) (dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r) r ↔ RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h (N + s)) (dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N s) s
declarations.docstring: **Every alleged depth tests the same basepoint property.** There is no `2`-adic hierarchy: depth `r` and depth `s` are interchangeable.

declarations.name: ratAffinePowTwo_zero_iff
declarations.signature: theorem ratAffinePowTwo_zero_iff {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) : RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h N) (dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N 0) 0 ↔ RatEvenIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: **The block-free corner.** Depth `0` is legal in the landed statement and carries an empty block, so the supply hypothesis can be witnessed with no arithmetic input at all.

declarations.name: evenIntegral_succ_iff_integral
declarations.signature: theorem evenIntegral_succ_iff_integral {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) (heven : ∃ k : ℤ, g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2 * k) : RatEvenIntegral (tailShift T h (N + 1)) ↔ RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: The converse of `evenIntegral_succ`: with an even difference digit, even integrality one step later is *equivalent* to ordinary integrality before.

declarations.name: affinePowTwo_succ_iff_orderOf_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem affinePowTwo_succ_iff_orderOf_dvd {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N r : ℕ) (heven : ∃ k : ℤ, g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2 * k) : RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h (N + 1 + r)) (dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) (N + 1) r) r ↔ orderOf (2 : ZMod (T N).den) ∣ h
declarations.docstring: **The cylinder is the landed `orderOf` lattice.** After the obligatory parity-lift step the affine class is exactly `OrderLatticeDiagonal`'s classifier — independently of the depth `r` and of the observed block. It is therefore not a refinement of that lattice.

declarations.name: cofinal_affinePowTwo_escape_iff_not_eventuallyIntegral
declarations.signature: theorem cofinal_affinePowTwo_escape_iff_not_eventuallyIntegral {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) (hdiffEven : ∀ N, ∃ k : ℤ, g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2 * k) : (∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ N r : ℕ, N₀ < N ∧ ¬ RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h (N + r)) (dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r) r) ↔ ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: **Circularity.** The cofinal affine-escape hypothesis of `not_eventuallyIntegralTailShift_of_cofinal_affinePowTwo_escape` is logically equivalent to the non-eventual-integrality it was introduced to derive. The reverse implication needs no arithmetic: depth `0` witnesses it.

declarations.name: blockResidue_eq_terminal_of_integral
declarations.signature: theorem blockResidue_eq_terminal_of_integral {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N r : ℕ) (hInt : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)) : ∃ z : ℤ, ((dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r : ℤ) : ℚ) - 2 ^ r * (z : ℚ) = -tailShift T h (N + r)
declarations.docstring: **Eventual integrality pins the finite block to `2^r·ℤ`.** If the shift is integral at `N`, then the block `B_{h,N,r}` differs from a point of `2^r·ℤ` by exactly the terminal shift `T_h(N+r)`. Nothing here is a pullback: the lattice `2^r·ℤ` does not mention the block.

declarations.name: not_eventuallyIntegral_of_cofinal_blockResidue_escape
declarations.signature: theorem not_eventuallyIntegral_of_cofinal_blockResidue_escape {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) (bound : ℕ → ℚ) (hbound : ∀ N, |tailShift T h N| ≤ bound N) (hsupply : ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ N r : ℕ, N₀ < N ∧ ∀ z : ℤ, bound (N + r) < |((dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r : ℤ) : ℚ) - 2 ^ r * (z : ℚ)|) : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: **The corrected producer.** Given any archimedean bound on the shifts, cofinally many finite blocks lying further than that bound from `2^r·ℤ` rule out eventual integrality. Unlike the affine cylinder, the target here is a fixed lattice, so the hypothesis is not a restatement of the conclusion.

declarations.name: DyadicScaleDominates
declarations.docstring: A bound is dyadically dominated when every fixed rational denominator is eventually overwhelmed by the depth scale. Polynomial bounds have this property; the definition isolates exactly the growth input used below.

declarations.name: one_div_den_le_abs_sub_int_of_ne
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_den_le_abs_sub_int_of_ne (x : ℚ) (z : ℤ) (hne : x ≠ z) : (1 : ℚ) / x.den ≤ |x - z|
declarations.docstring: A nonzero rational is separated from every integer by the reciprocal of its reduced denominator.

declarations.name: exists_blockResidue_escape_of_not_integral
declarations.signature: theorem exists_blockResidue_escape_of_not_integral {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) (bound : ℕ → ℚ) (hbound : ∀ n, |tailShift T h n| ≤ bound n) (hscale : DyadicScaleDominates bound) (N : ℕ) (hNon : ¬ RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)) : ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ z : ℤ, bound (N + r) < |((dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r : ℤ) : ℚ) - 2 ^ r * (z : ℚ)|
declarations.docstring: **The alleged fixed-lattice escape is forced by basepoint nonintegrality.** Under a dyadically dominated terminal bound, every nonintegral rational basepoint automatically has some depth whose observed block lies farther than the terminal bound from `2^r * ℤ`. No property of the digit word is used beyond the recurrence identity.

declarations.name: cofinal_blockResidue_escape_iff_not_eventuallyIntegral
declarations.signature: theorem cofinal_blockResidue_escape_iff_not_eventuallyIntegral {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) (bound : ℕ → ℚ) (hbound : ∀ N, |tailShift T h N| ≤ bound N) (hscale : DyadicScaleDominates bound) : (∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ N r : ℕ, N₀ < N ∧ ∀ z : ℤ, bound (N + r) < |((dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r : ℤ) : ℚ) - 2 ^ r * (z : ℚ)|) ↔ ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: **Second circularity theorem.** For every dyadically dominated bound, cofinal escape of the non-adaptive block from `2^r * ℤ` is equivalent to the non-eventual-integrality conclusion it was meant to prove. Thus polynomial terminal bounds cannot turn this fixed-lattice formulation into an independent prime-theoretic producer.

declarations.name: digit_eq_two_or_neg_two_of_small_pair
declarations.signature: theorem digit_eq_two_or_neg_two_of_small_pair {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) (heven : ∃ k : ℤ, g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2 * k) (hlow : -1 < tailShift T h N) (hhigh : tailShift T h N < 1) (hlow' : -1 < tailShift T h (N + 1)) (hhigh' : tailShift T h (N + 1) < 1) (hne : g (N + h + 1) ≠ g (N + 1)) : g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2 ∨ g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = -2
declarations.docstring: **The ±2 wall.** Under exactly the hypotheses of the existing adjacent-small-mismatch consumer, an even nonzero digit is forced to be `±2`. The requested producer is therefore a prescribed-magnitude gap event, not a mere inequality of digits.

declarations.name: shift_gt_half_of_digit_eq_two
declarations.signature: theorem shift_gt_half_of_digit_eq_two {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) (hdigit : g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2) (hlow' : -1 < tailShift T h (N + 1)) : 1 / 2 < tailShift T h N
declarations.docstring: **Sign alignment.** A `+2` digit pins the shift into the *upper half* of its window: the digit magnitude and the shift sign are not independent.

declarations.name: shift_lt_neg_half_of_digit_eq_neg_two
declarations.signature: theorem shift_lt_neg_half_of_digit_eq_neg_two {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) (hdigit : g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = -2) (hhigh' : tailShift T h (N + 1) < 1) : tailShift T h N < -(1 / 2)
declarations.docstring: The mirror statement for a `-2` digit.

declarations.name: adjacent_small_mismatch_iff_signed_two_window
declarations.signature: theorem adjacent_small_mismatch_iff_signed_two_window {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) (heven : ∃ k : ℤ, g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2 * k) : (-1 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < 1 ∧ -1 < tailShift T h (N + 1) ∧ tailShift T h (N + 1) < 1 ∧ g (N + h + 1) ≠ g (N + 1)) ↔ ((g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2 ∧ 1 / 2 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < 1) ∨ (g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = -2 ∧ -1 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < -(1 / 2)))
declarations.docstring: **Signed-window normal form.** Under the hypotheses of the adjacent-small- mismatch producer, its two unit-window conditions are equivalent to the exact `±2` digit event with the corresponding half-window condition. This packages the reduction used by the computational and analytic consumers without claiming that the event is cofinal for the actual primes.

declarations.name: RatEvenIntegral
declarations.docstring: A rational that is the cast of an even integer.

declarations.name: RatAffinePowTwo
declarations.signature: def RatAffinePowTwo (x : ℚ) (c : ℤ) (r : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: `x` lies in the affine class `-c` modulo `2^(r+1)`.

declarations.name: shiftDigit
declarations.signature: def shiftDigit (g : ℕ → ℤ) (h n : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The digit sequence governing the fixed `h`-shift cocycle.

declarations.name: tailShift_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_recurrence {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) : DyadicTailRecurrence (shiftDigit g h) (tailShift T h)
declarations.docstring: A fixed tail shift is itself a dyadic recurrence, with difference digits.

declarations.name: evenIntegral_succ
declarations.signature: theorem evenIntegral_succ {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) (hInt : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)) (heven : ∃ k : ℤ, g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2 * k) : RatEvenIntegral (tailShift T h (N + 1))
declarations.docstring: **One step lifts integrality to evenness.** Because every digit difference is even, an integral shift becomes an *even* integral shift after one step.

declarations.name: affinePowTwo_of_evenIntegral
declarations.signature: theorem affinePowTwo_of_evenIntegral {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N r : ℕ) (hEven : RatEvenIntegral (tailShift T h N)) : RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h (N + r)) (dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r) r
declarations.docstring: **The affine ladder.** Each additional step fixes one further binary digit: an even-integral shift lands, `r` steps later, in one affine class modulo `2^(r+1)` determined by the observed finite digit block.

declarations.name: affinePowTwo_one
declarations.signature: theorem affinePowTwo_one {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) (hEven : RatEvenIntegral (tailShift T h N)) : RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h (N + 1)) (g (N + 1 + h) - g (N + 1)) 1
declarations.docstring: The original small-pair certificate is the `r = 1` corner of the ladder.

declarations.name: not_eventuallyIntegralTailShift_of_cofinal_affinePowTwo_escape
declarations.signature: theorem not_eventuallyIntegralTailShift_of_cofinal_affinePowTwo_escape {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) (hdiffEven : ∀ N, ∃ k : ℤ, g (N + h + 1) - g (N + 1) = 2 * k) (hsupply : ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ N r : ℕ, N₀ < N ∧ ¬ RatAffinePowTwo (tailShift T h (N + r)) (dyadicTailBlock (shiftDigit g h) N r) r) : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: **The replacement producer.** Cofinal escape from the data-dependent affine cylinders rules out eventual integrality of the fixed shift. Only one tail is tested at each witness, and no unit window is required.

declarations.name: allResidueGap
declarations.docstring: `a_0` is unused; for `n ≥ 1` this is `2 U_{n-1} - U_n`.

declarations.name: allResidue_partial_telescope
declarations.signature: theorem allResidue_partial_telescope (N m : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range m, (allResidueGap (N + 1 + j) : ℚ) / 2 ^ (j + 1) = (allResidueCarry N : ℚ) - (allResidueCarry (N + m) : ℚ) / 2 ^ m

declarations.name: allResidueCarry_at_noncentre

declarations.name: allResidueCarry_at_centre

declarations.name: allResidueGap_at_centre

declarations.name: rationalisingPerturbationDigits
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rationalisingPerturbationDigits (S r : ℝ) (M : ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The rationalising digits: binary expansion of `(r - S) / M`.

declarations.name: exists_bounded_perturbation_digits
declarations.signature: theorem exists_bounded_perturbation_digits {g : ℕ → ℕ} {S : ℝ} (hS : HasSum (fun n => (g n : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) S) (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (r : ℝ) (hr₁ : S < r) (K : ℕ) (hK : r < S + M / 2 ^ K) : (∀ n, rationalisingPerturbationDigits S r M n ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ n < K, rationalisingPerturbationDigits S r M n = 0) ∧ HasSum (fun n => ((g n + M * rationalisingPerturbationDigits S r M n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) r
declarations.docstring: **Named encoding.** For `S < r < S + M / 2^K`, the digits of `(r - S) / M` lie in `{0,1}`, vanish before `K`, and realise the perturbation sum `r`. Equivalently, they are the binary digits of the scaled remainder `2^K (r - S) / M`, placed after the cutoff.

declarations.name: exists_bounded_perturbation
declarations.signature: theorem exists_bounded_perturbation {g : ℕ → ℕ} {S : ℝ} (hS : HasSum (fun n => (g n : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) S) (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (r : ℝ) (hr₁ : S < r) (K : ℕ) (hK : r < S + M / 2 ^ K) : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, δ n ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ n < K, δ n = 0) ∧ HasSum (fun n => ((g n + M * δ n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) r
declarations.docstring: **Bounded-perturbation countermodel, general form.** If the natural-digit dyadic series `Σ g_n/2^{n+1}` has sum `S`, then for every `M ≥ 1`, every real `r` with `S < r < S + M/2^K`, there are digits `δ_n ∈ {0,1}`, vanishing for `n < K`, with `Σ (g_n + M δ_n)/2^{n+1} = r`.

declarations.name: exists_rational_bounded_perturbation_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem exists_rational_bounded_perturbation_primeGap (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (K : ℕ) : ∃ (δ : ℕ → ℕ) (r : ℚ), (∀ n, δ n ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ n < K, δ n = 0) ∧ HasSum (fun n => ((primeGap0 n + M * δ n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) r
declarations.docstring: **Bounded-perturbation countermodel for the prime-gap series.** For every `M ≥ 1` and every `K`, there are digits `δ_n ∈ {0,1}`, zero for `n < K`, and a rational `r` with `Σ (g_n + M δ_n)/2^{n+1} = r`, where `g_n` are the actual consecutive prime gaps. The perturbed gaps satisfy `g_n ≤ g_n + M δ_n ≤ g_n + M` and `g_n + M δ_n ≡ g_n (mod M)` at every index.

declarations.name: not_irrational_bounded_perturbation_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_bounded_perturbation_primeGap (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (K : ℕ) : ∃ δ : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, δ n ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ n < K, δ n = 0) ∧ ¬ Irrational (∑' n, ((primeGap0 n + M * δ n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1))
declarations.docstring: The perturbed prime-gap series is rational.

declarations.name: perturbed_gap_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem perturbed_gap_bounds (M : ℕ) (δ : ℕ → ℕ) (hδ : ∀ n, δ n ≤ 1) (n : ℕ) : primeGap0 n ≤ primeGap0 n + M * δ n ∧ primeGap0 n + M * δ n ≤ primeGap0 n + M ∧ (primeGap0 n + M * δ n) % M = primeGap0 n % M
declarations.docstring: Pointwise form of the perturbation bounds, for the record: every perturbed gap lies in `[g_n, g_n + M]` and is congruent to `g_n` modulo `M`.

declarations.name: binaryDigit_shift
declarations.signature: theorem binaryDigit_shift (D : ℝ) (K n : ℕ) : binaryDigit D (K + n) = binaryDigit ((2 : ℝ) ^ K * D) n
declarations.docstring: Shifting the index by `K` is the binary expansion of the scaled remainder. This is the identity behind writing the correction as the binary digits of `2^K (r - S) / M`.

declarations.name: orderOf_two_zmod_den_pos

declarations.name: free_pair_integral_iff_modEq
declarations.signature: theorem free_pair_integral_iff_modEq {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) {N₀ : ℕ} (hodd : Odd (T N₀).den) {N M : ℕ} (hN : N₀ ≤ N) (hM : N₀ ≤ M) : RatIntegral (T M - T N) ↔ N ≡ M [MOD orderOf (2 : ZMod (T N₀).den)]
declarations.docstring: **The free-pair lattice (F) with its converse.** At and beyond an odd-denominator state with reduced denominator `d`, the difference of two tail states is an integer exactly when the indices are congruent modulo the multiplicative order of `2` modulo `d`. The offset is free: `M - N` is any multiple of the order, not a fixed `h`.

declarations.name: exists_free_pair_lattice

declarations.name: irrational_initial_iff_nonintegral_on_schedule
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_initial_iff_nonintegral_on_schedule {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (s : ℕ → ℕ) (hpos : ∀ j, 0 < s j) (hdvd : ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → ∃ J : ℕ, ∀ j : ℕ, J ≤ j → h ∣ s j) (hgrow : ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ J : ℕ, ∀ j : ℕ, J ≤ j → N ≤ s j) : Irrational (T 0) ↔ ∀ j : ℕ, ¬ RealIntegral (realTailShift T (s j) (s j))

declarations.name: irrational_initial_iff_all_factorialDiagonal_nonintegral

declarations.name: irrational_initial_iff_all_lcmDiagonal_nonintegral

declarations.docstring: **Long paper, `long251:res:jointcountermodel`.** For every prescribed finite prime-gap prefix `K` and every `0 < ε ≤ 1` there is a nonnegative integer correction `e`, vanishing on the prefix and eventually at most `(log (n+3))^ε`, for which the altered sequence `b = g + e` simultaneously has * a rational dyadic value; * every fixed eventual coefficient and cumulative congruence; * fixed-block polynomial nonconcentration; * vanishing total variation distance between the unnormalised block distributions for block lengths `o(log log X)`; * cumulative positions `P n = 2 + ∑_{i<n} b i` with `0 ≤ P n − p n = O_ε(n (log (n+3))^ε / log log n)` and `P n ∼ n log n`. The two literature inputs appear as the explicit hypotheses `hSP` and `hPNT`.

declarations.docstring: **Short paper, `res:jointcountermodel`.** The same countermodel written for the altered sequence `b` itself: `b` has a rational dyadic sum, agrees with the prime gaps below `K`, dominates them, exceeds them by at most `(log (n+3))^ε` eventually, keeps every fixed eventual residue of the coefficients and of the cumulative positions, has vanishing block total variation for lengths `o(log log X)`, has fixed-block polynomial nonconcentration (`|{n < N : F(b n, …, b (n+k)) = 0}| = o(N)` for every fixed nonzero `F`), and its cumulative positions satisfy `0 ≤ P n − p n = O_ε(n (log (n+3))^ε / log log n)` and `P n ∼ n log n`. The positions are not asserted to be prime.

declarations.docstring: The whole affine/fixed-lattice theorem as one logical package; all three mechanisms are reused from the supplied source, without treating one of them as coverage of the other two.

declarations.name: rational_small_pair_bundle

declarations.docstring: Local rational obstruction and its cofinal consequence, exactly the two clauses in `res:smallpair`.

declarations.name: real_small_pair_bundle
declarations.signature: theorem real_small_pair_bundle {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) : (∀ N, ((-1 < realTailShift T h N ∧ realTailShift T h N < 1) ∧ (-1 < realTailShift T h (N + 1) ∧ realTailShift T h (N + 1) < 1)) → g (N + h + 1) ≠ g (N + 1) → ¬ (RealIntegral (realTailShift T h N) ∧ RealIntegral (realTailShift T h (N + 1)))) ∧ ((∀ N₀, ∃ N, N₀ ≤ N ∧ ((-1 < realTailShift T h N ∧ realTailShift T h N < 1) ∧ (-1 < realTailShift T h (N + 1) ∧ realTailShift T h (N + 1) < 1)) ∧ g (N + h + 1) ≠ g (N + 1)) → ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RealIntegral (realTailShift T h N))
declarations.docstring: The same complete bundle in real states.

declarations.name: real_small_pair_prime_endpoint

declarations.docstring: Long-record `res:smallpair-real`: both the generic real statement and the explicitly conditional actual-prime conclusion are kept together.

declarations.name: prime_perturbation_of_nonconcentration
declarations.signature: theorem prime_perturbation_of_nonconcentration (hNC : FixedBlockNonconcentration (fun n => (primeGap0 n : ℤ))) (M K : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : ∃ (b : ℕ → ℕ) (r : ℚ), HasSum (fun n => (b n : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) (r : ℝ) ∧ (∀ n < K, b n = primeGap0 n) ∧ (∀ n, b n = primeGap0 n ∨ b n = primeGap0 n + M) ∧ (∀ n, b n ≡ primeGap0 n [MOD M]) ∧ FixedBlockNonconcentration (fun n => (b n : ℤ)) ∧ (∀ n, prime0 n ≤ 2 + ∑ i ∈ range n, b i) ∧ (∀ n, 2 + ∑ i ∈ range n, b i ≤ prime0 n + M * n)

declarations.name: small_mismatch_zeroDensity_of_nonconcentration
