declarations.signature: theorem polylog_positions_preserve_growth (p e : ℕ → ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hp : Tendsto (fun n => (p n : ℝ) / scale n) atTop (𝓝 1)) (hε : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε < 1) (he : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (e n : ℝ) ≤ polylog ε n) : Tendsto (fun n => ((p n + ∑ i ∈ range n, e i : ℕ) : ℝ) / scale n) atTop (𝓝 1)
declarations.docstring: The PNT premise concerns only the unmodified positions.

declarations.name: sandwich_preserves_growth
declarations.signature: theorem sandwich_preserves_growth (p P : ℕ → ℝ) (M : ℝ) (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hp : Tendsto (fun n => p n / scale n) atTop (𝓝 1)) (hlo : ∀ n, p n ≤ P n) (hhi : ∀ n, P n ≤ p n + M * n) : Tendsto (fun n => P n / scale n) atTop (𝓝 1)
declarations.docstring: Uniformly bounded perturbations need no sparse-support hypothesis.

declarations.name: polynomialGapDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: The real dyadic term of the polynomial countermodel series, indexed so that `n = 0` carries the gap `g_1 / 2`. The zero-index gap `g_0` is the initial carry and is not part of the series.

declarations.name: polynomialGap_partialSum_eq
declarations.signature: theorem polynomialGap_partialSum_eq (N : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, (polynomialGapWord (j + 1) : ℚ) / 2 ^ (j + 1) = 32 - polynomialTailOrbit N / 2 ^ N
declarations.docstring: Exact finite telescope for the countermodel: the partial sum of the gap series is `32` minus the scaled terminal state.

declarations.name: polynomialGapDyadicTerm_partialSum_eq
declarations.signature: theorem polynomialGapDyadicTerm_partialSum_eq (N : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, polynomialGapDyadicTerm j = 32 - ((polynomialTailOrbit N : ℚ) : ℝ) / 2 ^ N
declarations.docstring: Real cast of the finite telescope.

declarations.name: tendsto_polynomialTailOrbit_div_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_polynomialTailOrbit_div_two_pow : Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => ((polynomialTailOrbit N : ℚ) : ℝ) / 2 ^ N) atTop (𝓝 0)
declarations.docstring: The scaled terminal state `2(N+4)^2 / 2^N` tends to zero.

declarations.name: hasSum_polynomialGapDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: **The countermodel series sums to `32`.**

declarations.name: tsum_polynomialGapDyadicTerm_eq
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_polynomialGapDyadicTerm_eq : ∑' n : ℕ, polynomialGapDyadicTerm n = 32
declarations.docstring: **`Σ_{j ≥ 1} g_j / 2^j = 32` as a `tsum`.** This replaces the Python receipt for the countermodel series value.

declarations.name: tsum_polynomialGapWord_div_two_pow
declarations.docstring: The same identity with the term written out.

declarations.name: tsum_polynomialGapDyadicTerm_eq_orbit_zero
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_polynomialGapDyadicTerm_eq_orbit_zero : ∑' n : ℕ, polynomialGapDyadicTerm n = ((polynomialTailOrbit 0 : ℚ) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The series value is the initial tail state of the countermodel orbit.

declarations.name: not_irrational_tsum_polynomialGapDyadicTerm
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_tsum_polynomialGapDyadicTerm : ¬ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, polynomialGapDyadicTerm n)
declarations.docstring: The positive, even, strictly increasing, unbounded, nonperiodic gap word therefore produces a rational dyadic series. This is the infinite countermodel in its final analytic form.

declarations.name: prime0
declarations.docstring: Zero-based prime enumeration.

declarations.name: primeGap0
declarations.docstring: Zero-based consecutive prime gap.

declarations.name: exists_primeGap0_gt
declarations.signature: theorem exists_primeGap0_gt (M : ℕ) : ∃ n, M < primeGap0 n
declarations.docstring: The classical factorial construction gives arbitrarily long prime-free intervals, hence the actual consecutive-prime gaps are unbounded.

declarations.name: dyadicPartialSumQ
declarations.signature: def dyadicPartialSumQ (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: Finite zero-based dyadic partial sum of a rational sequence.

declarations.name: prime0DisplayedPartialSumQ
declarations.docstring: The finite zero-based normalization with denominator `2^i`, matching the displayed indexing used by the formal conjecture.

declarations.name: prime0DisplayedPartialSumQ_eq_two_mul
declarations.signature: theorem prime0DisplayedPartialSumQ_eq_two_mul (n : ℕ) : prime0DisplayedPartialSumQ n = 2 * dyadicPartialSumQ (fun i => (prime0 i : ℚ)) n
declarations.docstring: Exact factor-of-two indexing normalization: the zero-based displayed partial sum is twice the convention with denominator `2^(i+1)`.

declarations.name: dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ
declarations.signature: def dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: Finite dyadic partial sum of the forward differences of a sequence.

declarations.name: dyadicPartialSumQ_succ
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem dyadicPartialSumQ_succ (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : dyadicPartialSumQ P (n + 1) = dyadicPartialSumQ P n + P n / 2 ^ (n + 1)

declarations.name: dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ_succ
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ_succ (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ P (n + 1) = dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ P n + (P (n + 1) - P n) / 2 ^ (n + 1)

declarations.name: dyadicPartialSumQ_eq_start_add_differences
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicPartialSumQ_eq_start_add_differences (P : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : dyadicPartialSumQ P (n + 1) = P 0 + dyadicDifferencePartialSumQ P n - P n / 2 ^ (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite summation by parts. The endpoint term is retained, so the theorem can be used before any analytic convergence argument.

declarations.name: prime0_mono_step
declarations.signature: theorem prime0_mono_step (n : ℕ) : prime0 n ≤ prime0 (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Consecutive zero-based primes are increasing.

declarations.name: primeGap0_cast
declarations.signature: theorem primeGap0_cast (n : ℕ) : (primeGap0 n : ℚ) = (prime0 (n + 1) : ℚ) - prime0 n
declarations.docstring: Casting the natural prime gap agrees with subtraction in `ℚ`.

declarations.name: primeGapPartialSumQ
declarations.docstring: Finite dyadic partial sum of the actual consecutive prime gaps.

declarations.name: primeGapPartialSumQ_succ
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem primeGapPartialSumQ_succ (n : ℕ) : primeGapPartialSumQ (n + 1) = primeGapPartialSumQ n + (primeGap0 n : ℚ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)

declarations.name: prime0_dyadic_summation_by_parts
declarations.signature: theorem prime0_dyadic_summation_by_parts (n : ℕ) : dyadicPartialSumQ (fun i => (prime0 i : ℚ)) (n + 1) = 2 + primeGapPartialSumQ n - (prime0 n : ℚ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite prime-gap reformulation, including the initial gap and the endpoint correction. Passing to an infinite series requires a separate proof that the endpoint tends to zero.

declarations.name: primeDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: The real term in the normalized zero-based prime series.

declarations.name: primeDisplayedDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: The term with denominator `2^n` used by the displayed formal conjecture.

declarations.name: primeGapDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: The real term in the corresponding consecutive-prime-gap series.

declarations.name: primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_eq_two_mul
declarations.signature: theorem primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_eq_two_mul (n : ℕ) : primeDisplayedDyadicTerm n = 2 * primeDyadicTerm n
declarations.docstring: Infinite-series version of the exact factor-two normalization.

declarations.name: primeGapDyadicTerm_eq
declarations.signature: theorem primeGapDyadicTerm_eq (n : ℕ) : primeGapDyadicTerm n = 2 * primeDyadicTerm (n + 1) - primeDyadicTerm n
declarations.docstring: Each gap term is the dyadic discrete derivative of the prime term.

declarations.name: summable_primeDyadicTerm_of_polynomial_growth
declarations.signature: theorem summable_primeDyadicTerm_of_polynomial_growth (C k : ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n, prime0 n ≤ C * (n + 1) ^ k) : Summable primeDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: Any polynomial upper bound on the `n`th prime implies convergence of the normalized prime series.

declarations.name: centralBinom_le_two_mul_pow_primeCounting
declarations.signature: theorem centralBinom_le_two_mul_pow_primeCounting (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : m.centralBinom ≤ (2 * m) ^ Nat.primeCounting (2 * m)
declarations.docstring: The central binomial coefficient is bounded by one factor `2m` for each prime at most `2m`. Multiplicities cause no loss here because the complete prime-power contribution to a binomial coefficient is itself at most its top parameter.

declarations.name: binomial_count_growth_bound
declarations.docstring: A deliberately generous elementary inequality balancing the polynomial test point `(n+5)^4` against central-binomial exponential growth.

declarations.name: lt_primeCounting_two_mul_fourth
declarations.docstring: The prime-counting function exceeds `n` at the explicit polynomial test point `2(n+5)^4`.

declarations.name: prime0_le_polynomial
declarations.docstring: An unconditional polynomial upper bound for the zero-based `n`th prime. It is intentionally loose but entirely elementary and sufficient for every dyadic convergence argument in this module.

declarations.name: summable_primeDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: The normalized prime series converges unconditionally, using the explicit elementary polynomial bound above.

declarations.name: summable_primeGapDyadicTerm_of_summable_primeDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: Summability of the normalized prime series implies summability of the corresponding consecutive-prime-gap series.

declarations.name: summable_primeGapDyadicTerm
declarations.docstring: The actual consecutive-prime-gap dyadic series also converges unconditionally.

declarations.name: tsum_primeDyadicTerm_eq_two_add_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_primeDyadicTerm_eq_two_add_primeGap (hprime : Summable primeDyadicTerm) : (∑' n : ℕ, primeDyadicTerm n) = 2 + ∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n
declarations.docstring: Exact infinite prime-gap reformulation. Whenever the normalized prime series is summable, its sum is `2` plus the sum of the actual consecutive prime gaps.

declarations.name: tsum_primeDyadicTerm_eq_two_add_primeGap_unconditional
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_primeDyadicTerm_eq_two_add_primeGap_unconditional : (∑' n : ℕ, primeDyadicTerm n) = 2 + ∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n
declarations.docstring: Unconditional form of the exact infinite prime-gap reformulation.

declarations.name: irrational_tsum_primeDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_tsum_primeDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap (hprime : Summable primeDyadicTerm) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeDyadicTerm n) ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n)
declarations.docstring: Erdős #251 is therefore exactly equivalent to irrationality of the consecutive-prime-gap dyadic series, once summability of the displayed prime series is supplied.

declarations.name: tsum_primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_eq_four_add_two_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_eq_four_add_two_primeGap (hprime : Summable primeDyadicTerm) : (∑' n : ℕ, primeDisplayedDyadicTerm n) = 4 + 2 * ∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n
declarations.docstring: The zero-based displayed series is `4` plus twice the normalized prime-gap series.

declarations.name: irrational_tsum_primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_tsum_primeDisplayedDyadicTerm_iff_primeGap (hprime : Summable primeDyadicTerm) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeDisplayedDyadicTerm n) ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n)
declarations.docstring: Direct irrationality equivalence for the indexing used in the formal conjecture.

declarations.name: primeGapPartialSumQ_cast
declarations.signature: theorem primeGapPartialSumQ_cast (n : ℕ) : ((primeGapPartialSumQ n : ℚ) : ℝ) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, primeGapDyadicTerm i
declarations.docstring: The rational finite prime-gap sum casts exactly to the corresponding finite real sum.

declarations.name: DyadicTailRecurrence
declarations.signature: def DyadicTailRecurrence (g : ℕ → ℤ) (T : ℕ → ℚ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Abstract dyadic tail recurrence with integer digits. The rational candidate state below is an exact actual-gap instance; identifying a candidate with the genuine infinite sum remains analytic.

declarations.name: rationalPrimeGapTailState
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rationalPrimeGapTailState (S : ℚ) (N : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The exact rational tail state attached to a proposed rational value `S` of the prime-gap dyadic series. It subtracts the first `N+1` gap terms and rescales the remainder by `2^(N+1)`. The definition is algebraic: no summability or identification of `S` with an infinite sum is assumed.

declarations.name: cast_rationalPrimeGapTailState_eq_scaled_tsum_nat_add
declarations.signature: theorem cast_rationalPrimeGapTailState_eq_scaled_tsum_nat_add (S : ℚ) (hS : (S : ℝ) = ∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n) (N : ℕ) : ((rationalPrimeGapTailState S N : ℚ) : ℝ) = 2 ^ (N + 1) * ∑' k : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm (k + (N + 1))
declarations.docstring: If the genuine real prime-gap sum equals the rational number `S`, the algebraic candidate state is exactly the corresponding scaled real tail.

declarations.name: exists_rationalPrimeGapTailState_representation_of_not_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem exists_rationalPrimeGapTailState_representation_of_not_irrational (h : ¬ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n)) : ∃ S : ℚ, (S : ℝ) = ∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n ∧ ∀ N, ((rationalPrimeGapTailState S N : ℚ) : ℝ) = 2 ^ (N + 1) * ∑' k : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm (k + (N + 1))
declarations.docstring: Non-irrationality therefore supplies a single rational candidate whose states represent every scaled real tail.

declarations.name: rationalPrimeGapTailState_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPrimeGapTailState_recurrence (S : ℚ) : DyadicTailRecurrence (fun n => (primeGap0 n : ℤ)) (rationalPrimeGapTailState S)
declarations.docstring: The proposed rational prime-gap tail satisfies the actual prime-gap recurrence identically. Under non-irrationality the preceding existence theorem identifies this candidate with every scaled real tail; a contradiction still requires a smallness statement for a suitable fixed shift.

declarations.name: rationalPrimeGapTailState_zero
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem rationalPrimeGapTailState_zero (S : ℚ) : rationalPrimeGapTailState S 0 = 2 * S - 1

declarations.name: tailShift
declarations.signature: def tailShift (T : ℕ → ℚ) (h N : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: Difference between two tail states separated by `h` steps.

declarations.name: cast_rationalPrimeGapTailShift_eq_scaled_tsum_sub
declarations.signature: theorem cast_rationalPrimeGapTailShift_eq_scaled_tsum_sub (S : ℚ) (hS : (S : ℝ) = ∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n) (h N : ℕ) : ((tailShift (rationalPrimeGapTailState S) h N : ℚ) : ℝ) = 2 ^ (N + h + 1) * ∑' k : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm (k + (N + h + 1)) - 2 ^ (N + 1) * ∑' k : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm (k + (N + 1))
declarations.docstring: Under a rationality witness, the rational tail shift is exactly the difference of two scaled real tails.

declarations.name: tailShift_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_succ {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) : tailShift T h (N + 1) = 2 * tailShift T h N - ((g (N + h + 1) : ℚ) - (g (N + 1) : ℚ))
declarations.docstring: The exact propagation identity for a fixed tail shift.

declarations.name: RatIntegral
declarations.docstring: A rational number is integral when it is the cast of an integer.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_int_mul_rationalPrimeGapTailState
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_int_mul_rationalPrimeGapTailState (S : ℚ) (m : ℤ) (hS : RatIntegral ((m : ℚ) * S)) : ∀ N, RatIntegral ((m : ℚ) * rationalPrimeGapTailState S N) | 0 =>
declarations.docstring: An integral multiplier of the proposed value remains an integral multiplier of every actual prime-gap tail state. This is the denominator transport missing from a purely abstract recurrence: the initial gap is one, and each later recurrence step subtracts an integer digit.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_int_mul_tailState_succ
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_int_mul_tailState_succ {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (m : ℤ) {N : ℕ} (hInt : RatIntegral ((m : ℚ) * T N)) : RatIntegral ((m : ℚ) * T (N + 1))
declarations.docstring: Integral scaling propagates through any integer-digit dyadic tail recurrence.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_int_mul_tailState_add
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_int_mul_tailState_add {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (m : ℤ) {N : ℕ} (hInt : RatIntegral ((m : ℚ) * T N)) : ∀ k, RatIntegral ((m : ℚ) * T (N + k)) | 0 =>
declarations.docstring: Integral scaling at one tail index therefore persists at every later index.

declarations.name: dyadicTailBlock
declarations.signature: def dyadicTailBlock (g : ℕ → ℤ) (N : ℕ) : ℕ → ℤ | 0 => 0 | h + 1 => 2 * dyadicTailBlock g N h + g (N + h + 1) /-- Iterating the tail recurrence for `h` steps gives the exact finite block identity `T_(N+h) = 2^h T_N - B_(h,N)`. -/ theorem tail_iterate_eq_pow_mul_sub_block {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : T (N + h) = 2 ^ h * T N - dyadicTailBlock g N h
declarations.docstring: The integer block accumulated through `h` dyadic tail steps beginning at index `N`. Recursively, this is `g (N+1) * 2^(h-1) + ⋯ + g (N+h)`.

declarations.name: tail_iterate_eq_pow_mul_sub_block
declarations.signature: theorem tail_iterate_eq_pow_mul_sub_block {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : T (N + h) = 2 ^ h * T N - dyadicTailBlock g N h
declarations.docstring: Iterating the tail recurrence for `h` steps gives the exact finite block identity `T_(N+h) = 2^h T_N - B_(h,N)`.

declarations.name: tailShift_eq_scaled_sub_block
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_eq_scaled_sub_block {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : tailShift T h N = ((2 ^ h : ℚ) - 1) * T N - dyadicTailBlock g N h
declarations.docstring: The shifted-tail difference is a scaled copy of `T_N`, up to the explicit integer block.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_sub_int_iff
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_sub_int_iff (x : ℚ) (z : ℤ) : RatIntegral (x - z) ↔ RatIntegral x
declarations.docstring: Subtracting an integer does not change whether a rational number is integral.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_totientMultiplier_of_odd_den
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_totientMultiplier_of_odd_den (x : ℚ) (hodd : Odd x.den) : RatIntegral (((2 : ℚ) ^ x.den.totient - 1) * x)
declarations.docstring: Euler's congruence turns an odd reduced denominator into an explicit integral multiplier: if `d = x.den` is odd, then `(2^(phi d) - 1) * x` is an integer.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_scaled_of_den_eq_pow_two_mul_odd
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_scaled_of_den_eq_pow_two_mul_odd (S : ℚ) (a q : ℕ) (hden : S.den = 2 ^ a * q) (hodd : Odd q) : RatIntegral (((2 : ℚ) ^ q.totient - 1) * (2 : ℚ) ^ (a + 1) * S)
declarations.docstring: Split a rational denominator as `2^a * q` with odd `q`. Euler's multiplier for `q`, together with `2^(a+1)`, clears the entire denominator of the candidate value.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_multiplier_tail_at_twoExponent
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_multiplier_tail_at_twoExponent (S : ℚ) (a q : ℕ) (hden : S.den = 2 ^ a * q) (hodd : Odd q) : RatIntegral ((((2 : ℤ) ^ q.totient - 1 : ℤ) : ℚ) * rationalPrimeGapTailState S a)
declarations.docstring: At the index where the power-of-two part has been shifted away, the odd Euler multiplier is integral on the actual prime-gap candidate tail.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_iff_scaledTail
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_iff_scaledTail {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N) ↔ RatIntegral (((2 ^ h : ℚ) - 1) * T N)
declarations.docstring: Exact algebraic core of the integral-shift criterion: one tail shift is integral exactly when `(2^h - 1) * T_N` is integral.

declarations.name: rationalPrimeGapTailShift_integral_of_odd_den
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPrimeGapTailShift_integral_of_odd_den (S : ℚ) (hodd : Odd S.den) (N : ℕ) : RatIntegral (tailShift (rationalPrimeGapTailState S) S.den.totient N)
declarations.docstring: If a proposed rational prime-gap value has odd reduced denominator, one fixed positive-period candidate supplied by Euler's theorem is integral at every tail index. Unlike the abstract per-state lemma below, the shift here depends only on the denominator of `S`, not on `N`.

declarations.name: rationalPrimeGapTailShift_eventuallyIntegral_of_den_eq
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPrimeGapTailShift_eventuallyIntegral_of_den_eq (S : ℚ) (a q : ℕ) (hden : S.den = 2 ^ a * q) (hodd : Odd q) : ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift (rationalPrimeGapTailState S) q.totient N)
declarations.docstring: Denominator decomposition upgrades the preceding odd-denominator calculation to every rational candidate: after the power-of-two part has been shifted out, one fixed Euler-period shift is integral at every later index.

declarations.name: rationalPrimeGapTailShift_eventuallyIntegral
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPrimeGapTailShift_eventuallyIntegral (S : ℚ) : ∃ h, 0 < h ∧ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift (rationalPrimeGapTailState S) h N)
declarations.docstring: Every rational candidate supplies a positive fixed shift which is eventually integral along its actual prime-gap tail state. The shift is the totient of the odd part of the candidate denominator.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_totient_of_odd_den
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_totient_of_odd_den {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N : ℕ) (hodd : Odd (T N).den) : RatIntegral (tailShift T (T N).den.totient N)
declarations.docstring: If one tail state has odd reduced denominator `d`, its shift by `Nat.totient d` steps is integral. This is the explicit finite-algebraic consequence of rationality supplied by Euler's theorem.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_succ {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) {h N : ℕ} (hInt : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)) : RatIntegral (tailShift T h (N + 1))
declarations.docstring: Once a fixed tail shift is integral, the recurrence keeps it integral at the next index. This is the exact finite algebra behind the eventual-shift criterion; no prime-distribution input is used.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_add
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_add {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) {h N : ℕ} (hInt : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)) : ∀ k, RatIntegral (tailShift T h (N + k)) | 0 =>
declarations.docstring: Integrality therefore propagates through every later index.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_eq_zero_of_neg_one_lt_of_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_eq_zero_of_neg_one_lt_of_lt_one {x : ℚ} (hInt : RatIntegral x) (hlow : -1 < x) (hhigh : x < 1) : x = 0
declarations.docstring: An integral rational lying strictly between `-1` and `1` is zero.

declarations.name: tailShift_eventually_zero_of_eventually_integral_of_eventually_small
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_eventually_zero_of_eventually_integral_of_eventually_small {T : ℕ → ℚ} {h : ℕ} (hInt : ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)) (hsmall : ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → -1 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < 1) : ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → tailShift T h N = 0
declarations.docstring: If one fixed tail shift is eventually integral and eventually lies in the open unit interval around zero, then that shift is eventually identically zero. This is the discrete rigidity step needed to turn an analytic small-shift estimate into exact arithmetic information.

declarations.name: digits_eventually_periodic_of_eventually_integralTailShift_of_eventually_small
declarations.signature: theorem digits_eventually_periodic_of_eventually_integralTailShift_of_eventually_small {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) (hInt : ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)) (hsmall : ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → -1 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < 1) : ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → g (N + h + 1) = g (N + 1)
declarations.docstring: For an integer-digit dyadic recurrence, eventual integrality plus an eventually small fixed shift forces the digit sequence to be eventually periodic with that shift.

declarations.name: not_eventuallyIntegralTailShift_of_eventually_small_of_not_periodic
declarations.signature: theorem not_eventuallyIntegralTailShift_of_eventually_small_of_not_periodic {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) (hsmall : ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → -1 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < 1) (hnotPeriodic : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → g (N + h + 1) = g (N + 1)) : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: Contrapositive form: if the digit sequence is not eventually periodic with shift `h`, an eventually small `h`-shift cannot also be eventually integral.

declarations.name: tailShift_not_both_integral_of_small_pair_of_digit_ne
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_not_both_integral_of_small_pair_of_digit_ne {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) (hsmall : (-1 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < 1) ∧ (-1 < tailShift T h (N + 1) ∧ tailShift T h (N + 1) < 1)) (hdigit : g (N + h + 1) ≠ g (N + 1)) : ¬ (RatIntegral (tailShift T h N) ∧ RatIntegral (tailShift T h (N + 1)))
declarations.docstring: A single adjacent pair of small shifts with unequal corresponding digits already excludes simultaneous integrality.

declarations.name: not_eventuallyIntegralTailShift_of_cofinal_small_mismatch
declarations.signature: theorem not_eventuallyIntegralTailShift_of_cofinal_small_mismatch {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h : ℕ) (hsupply : ∀ N₀, ∃ N, N₀ ≤ N ∧ ((-1 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < 1) ∧ (-1 < tailShift T h (N + 1) ∧ tailShift T h (N + 1) < 1)) ∧ g (N + h + 1) ≠ g (N + 1)) : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: To rule out eventual integrality of a fixed shift, it is enough to find beyond every level one adjacent pair of strictly small shifts whose corresponding digits differ.

declarations.name: primeGap0_not_eventually_periodic
declarations.signature: theorem primeGap0_not_eventually_periodic {h : ℕ} (hpos : 0 < h) : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → primeGap0 (N + h + 1) = primeGap0 (N + 1)
declarations.docstring: Consecutive prime gaps cannot become periodic with any positive period. The proof combines the exact factorial prime-free intervals above with the finite range of a periodic natural-valued sequence.

declarations.name: primeGapTailShift_not_eventuallyIntegral_of_eventually_small
declarations.signature: theorem primeGapTailShift_not_eventuallyIntegral_of_eventually_small {T : ℕ → ℚ} {h : ℕ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence (fun n => (primeGap0 n : ℤ)) T) (hpos : 0 < h) (hsmall : ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → -1 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < 1) : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: For the actual prime gaps, an eventually small positive tail shift cannot also be eventually integral: together those properties would force eventual periodicity, contradicting the factorial gap theorem.

declarations.name: rationalPrimeGapTailShift_not_eventually_small_of_odd_den
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPrimeGapTailShift_not_eventually_small_of_odd_den (S : ℚ) (hodd : Odd S.den) : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → -1 < tailShift (rationalPrimeGapTailState S) S.den.totient N ∧ tailShift (rationalPrimeGapTailState S) S.den.totient N < 1
declarations.docstring: No rational candidate with odd reduced denominator can have an eventually small Euler-period tail shift along the actual consecutive prime gaps. Under non-irrationality this candidate is the genuine scaled tail, but no theorem here supplies the required eventual smallness.

declarations.name: rationalPrimeGapTail_has_positive_shift_not_eventually_small
declarations.signature: theorem rationalPrimeGapTail_has_positive_shift_not_eventually_small (S : ℚ) : ∃ h, 0 < h ∧ ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → -1 < tailShift (rationalPrimeGapTailState S) h N ∧ tailShift (rationalPrimeGapTailState S) h N < 1
declarations.docstring: Every rational `S` has some positive fixed tail shift which cannot eventually remain in the open unit interval: denominator arithmetic makes that shift eventually integral, while eventual smallness would force the actual prime gaps to become periodic. This is compatible with rationality; it identifies a shift for which smallness must fail.

declarations.name: primeGapTailShift_not_eventuallyIntegral_of_cofinal_small_mismatch
declarations.signature: theorem primeGapTailShift_not_eventuallyIntegral_of_cofinal_small_mismatch {T : ℕ → ℚ} (h : ℕ) (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence (fun n => (primeGap0 n : ℤ)) T) (hsupply : ∀ N₀, ∃ N, N₀ ≤ N ∧ ((-1 < tailShift T h N ∧ tailShift T h N < 1) ∧ (-1 < tailShift T h (N + 1) ∧ tailShift T h (N + 1) < 1)) ∧ primeGap0 (N + h + 1) ≠ primeGap0 (N + 1)) : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → RatIntegral (tailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: Actual-prime-gap specialization of the cofinal small-mismatch criterion.

declarations.name: carryCoeff
declarations.signature: def carryCoeff (K : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The coefficient emitted by an unrestricted integer carry.

declarations.name: carryPartialSum
declarations.signature: def carryPartialSum (K : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.docstring: The finite dyadic series emitted by `carryCoeff`.

declarations.name: carryPartialSum_eq
declarations.signature: theorem carryPartialSum_eq (K : ℕ → ℚ) (n : ℕ) : carryPartialSum K n = K 0 - K n / 2 ^ n
declarations.docstring: Exact finite telescoping for an arbitrary rational-valued carry.

declarations.name: carryCoeff_natCast_eq
declarations.signature: theorem carryCoeff_natCast_eq (n : ℕ) : carryCoeff (fun j => (j : ℚ)) n = (n : ℚ) - 1
declarations.docstring: The carry `K n = n` emits the linear coefficient stream `n - 1`.

declarations.name: carryPartialSum_natCast_eq
declarations.signature: theorem carryPartialSum_natCast_eq (n : ℕ) : carryPartialSum (fun j => (j : ℚ)) n = -((n : ℚ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: The partial sums emitted by the linear carry have the exact endpoint `-n / 2^n`; in particular their ordinary real limit is rational once the standard exponential-dominance limit is applied.

declarations.name: carryCoeff_natCast_not_eventually_periodic
declarations.signature: theorem carryCoeff_natCast_not_eventually_periodic {h : ℕ} (hpos : 0 < h) : ¬ ∃ N₀, ∀ N, N₀ ≤ N → carryCoeff (fun j => (j : ℚ)) (N + h) = carryCoeff (fun j => (j : ℚ)) N
declarations.docstring: The coefficient stream emitted by the linear carry cannot become periodic with any positive period.

declarations.name: natCarryCoeff
declarations.signature: def natCarryCoeff (K : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Natural-valued carries emit nonnegative coefficients when the next carry is at most twice the current one.

declarations.name: natCarryCoeff_cast
declarations.signature: theorem natCarryCoeff_cast (K : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hK : K (n + 1) ≤ 2 * K n) : (natCarryCoeff K n : ℚ) = carryCoeff (fun j => (K j : ℚ)) n

declarations.name: den_two_mul
declarations.signature: theorem den_two_mul (x : ℚ) : ((2 : ℚ) * x).den = x.den / Nat.gcd 2 x.den
declarations.docstring: Doubling a reduced rational removes exactly the common factor of its denominator with `2`.

declarations.name: tail_den_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tail_den_succ {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N : ℕ) : (T (N + 1)).den = (T N).den / Nat.gcd 2 (T N).den
declarations.docstring: Exact one-step denominator dynamics for a rational dyadic tail: the next denominator is the current denominator divided by its gcd with `2`.

declarations.name: tail_den_succ_eq_of_odd
declarations.signature: theorem tail_den_succ_eq_of_odd {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N : ℕ) (hodd : Odd (T N).den) : (T (N + 1)).den = (T N).den
declarations.docstring: An odd rational tail denominator is unchanged by the next recurrence step. Since it remains odd, the same conclusion can then be iterated.

declarations.name: tail_den_succ_eq_half_of_even
declarations.signature: theorem tail_den_succ_eq_half_of_even {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N : ℕ) (heven : Even (T N).den) : (T (N + 1)).den = (T N).den / 2
declarations.docstring: An even rational tail denominator loses exactly one factor of `2` at the next recurrence step.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_iff_den_eq_one
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_iff_den_eq_one (x : ℚ) : RatIntegral x ↔ x.den = 1
declarations.docstring: A rational number is integral exactly when its reduced denominator is one.

declarations.name: ratIntegral_nat_mul_iff_den_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem ratIntegral_nat_mul_iff_den_dvd (x : ℚ) (m : ℕ) : RatIntegral ((m : ℚ) * x) ↔ x.den ∣ m
declarations.docstring: Multiplication by a natural number clears a rational denominator exactly when that denominator divides the multiplier.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_iff_den_dvd_mersenne
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_iff_den_dvd_mersenne {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N) ↔ (T N).den ∣ 2 ^ h - 1
declarations.docstring: Exact denominator classification of all integral shift lengths. A shift by `h` steps is integral precisely when the reduced denominator of the current tail divides the Mersenne number `2^h - 1`.

declarations.name: tailShift_integral_iff_two_pow_modEq_one
declarations.signature: theorem tailShift_integral_iff_two_pow_modEq_one {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : RatIntegral (tailShift T h N) ↔ 2 ^ h ≡ 1 [MOD (T N).den]
declarations.docstring: Congruence form of the exact shift-length classification: the integral shifts are precisely the exponents for which `2^h` is congruent to `1` modulo the current reduced denominator.

declarations.name: exists_twoPow_mul_odd_den
declarations.signature: theorem exists_twoPow_mul_odd_den (q : ℚ) : ∃ k : ℕ, Odd (((2 : ℚ) ^ k * q).den)
declarations.docstring: Repeated doubling removes the entire power-of-two part of a rational denominator. The remaining reduced denominator is therefore odd.

declarations.name: exists_odd_den_state
declarations.signature: theorem exists_odd_den_state {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) : ∃ N : ℕ, Odd (T N).den
declarations.docstring: Every rational-valued dyadic tail recurrence has an odd-denominator state. The index is exactly the number of doublings needed to clear the initial power-of-two denominator.

declarations.name: exists_eventually_integral_tailShift
declarations.signature: theorem exists_eventually_integral_tailShift {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℚ} (hrec : DyadicTailRecurrence g T) : ∃ h N : ℕ, 0 < h ∧ ∀ k, RatIntegral (tailShift T h (N + k))
declarations.docstring: Rationality forces one fixed positive shift to be integral from some point onwards. This is the rational-side obstruction paired with any prime-specific cofinal nonintegrality theorem.

declarations.name: RealDyadicTailRecurrence
declarations.signature: def RealDyadicTailRecurrence (g : ℕ → ℤ) (T : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: Real-valued version of the dyadic tail recurrence.

declarations.name: realTailShift
declarations.signature: def realTailShift (T : ℕ → ℝ) (h N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Difference between two real tail states separated by `h` steps.

declarations.name: RealIntegral
declarations.docstring: A real number is integral when it is the cast of an integer.

declarations.name: rationalDyadicOrbit
declarations.signature: def rationalDyadicOrbit (g : ℕ → ℤ) (q : ℚ) : ℕ → ℚ | 0 => q | N + 1 => 2 * rationalDyadicOrbit g q N - g (N + 1) theorem rationalDyadicOrbit_recurrence (g : ℕ → ℤ) (q : ℚ) : DyadicTailRecurrence g (rationalDyadicOrbit g q)
declarations.docstring: Rational orbit with prescribed initial state and integer digits.

declarations.name: rationalDyadicOrbit_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem rationalDyadicOrbit_recurrence (g : ℕ → ℤ) (q : ℚ) : DyadicTailRecurrence g (rationalDyadicOrbit g q)

declarations.name: realTail_eq_ratCast_rationalDyadicOrbit
declarations.signature: theorem realTail_eq_ratCast_rationalDyadicOrbit {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (q : ℚ) (hzero : T 0 = q) : ∀ N, T N = (rationalDyadicOrbit g q N : ℝ) | 0 =>
declarations.docstring: A real recurrence with rational initial state is the real cast of the corresponding rational recurrence at every later index.

declarations.name: CofinalNonintegralTailShifts
declarations.docstring: Cofinal failure of integral shifts for every fixed positive length.

declarations.name: irrational_initial_of_cofinalNonintegralTailShifts
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_initial_of_cofinalNonintegralTailShifts {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (hescape : CofinalNonintegralTailShifts T) : Irrational (T 0)
declarations.docstring: Cofinal nonintegrality for every fixed positive shift rules out a rational initial state: rationality produces one fixed positive shift that is integral at every sufficiently late index. The converse is recorded after the pointwise classifier below.

declarations.name: not_ratIntegral_of_approximation_gap
declarations.signature: theorem not_ratIntegral_of_approximation_gap (full approx R : ℚ) (herror : |full - approx| ≤ R) (hgap : ∀ z : ℤ, R < |approx - z|) : ¬ RatIntegral full
declarations.docstring: A finite approximation certifies nonintegrality when its error is no larger than `R` and the approximation stays farther than `R` from every integer.

declarations.name: real_tail_iterate_eq_pow_mul_sub_block
declarations.signature: theorem real_tail_iterate_eq_pow_mul_sub_block {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : T (N + h) = 2 ^ h * T N - dyadicTailBlock g N h
declarations.docstring: Iterating a real dyadic tail recurrence produces the same integer block as in the rational orbit.

declarations.name: realTailShift_eq_scaled_sub_block
declarations.signature: theorem realTailShift_eq_scaled_sub_block {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (N h : ℕ) : realTailShift T h N = ((2 ^ h : ℝ) - 1) * T N - dyadicTailBlock g N h
declarations.docstring: A real tail difference is a nonzero integer multiple of its initial state, up to the explicit integer block.

declarations.name: not_irrational_initial_iff_exists_integral_positive_tailShift
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_initial_iff_exists_integral_positive_tailShift {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) : ¬ Irrational (T 0) ↔ ∃ h N : ℕ, 0 < h ∧ RealIntegral (realTailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: Exact classifier for an integer-digit dyadic tail orbit: the initial state is rational if and only if one positive-length tail difference is integral. For a rational state, choose `h` so that the Mersenne multiplier `2^h - 1` clears the odd part of its denominator. Conversely, the block identity has nonzero multiplier `2^h - 1`, so one integral shift recovers rationality.

declarations.name: not_irrational_initial_iff_exists_eventually_integral_positive_tailShift
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_initial_iff_exists_eventually_integral_positive_tailShift {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) : ¬ Irrational (T 0) ↔ ∃ h N : ℕ, 0 < h ∧ ∀ k, RealIntegral (realTailShift T h (N + k))
declarations.docstring: Equivalent eventual form of the classifier: rationality is exactly the existence of a fixed positive shift that is integral at every later index.

declarations.name: irrational_initial_iff_all_positive_tailShifts_nonintegral
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_initial_iff_all_positive_tailShifts_nonintegral {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) : Irrational (T 0) ↔ ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → ∀ N : ℕ, ¬ RealIntegral (realTailShift T h N)
declarations.docstring: Exact irrationality normal form: an integer-digit dyadic tail starts at an irrational value exactly when none of its positive-length tail differences is an integer.

declarations.name: irrational_initial_iff_cofinalNonintegralTailShifts
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_initial_iff_cofinalNonintegralTailShifts {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) : Irrational (T 0) ↔ CofinalNonintegralTailShifts T
declarations.docstring: Exact cofinal form of the irrationality classifier. For an integer-digit dyadic tail recurrence, irrationality of the initial state is equivalent to finding, beyond every basepoint, a nonintegral tail difference of each fixed positive length.

declarations.name: polynomialGapWord
declarations.docstring: A positive even polynomial gap word. It is not the actual prime-gap word; it is an exact stress test for attempts using only coarse gap properties.

declarations.name: polynomialTailOrbit
declarations.docstring: The rational polynomial tail orbit paired with `polynomialGapWord`.

declarations.name: polynomialTailOrbit_recurrence
declarations.docstring: The polynomial word and orbit obey the exact dyadic tail recurrence.

declarations.name: polynomialGapWord_pos
declarations.docstring: Every polynomial countermodel gap is positive.

declarations.name: polynomialGapWord_even
declarations.signature: theorem polynomialGapWord_even (n : ℕ) : ∃ k : ℤ, polynomialGapWord n = 2 * k
declarations.docstring: Every polynomial countermodel gap is even.

declarations.name: polynomialGapWord_succ_sub
declarations.signature: theorem polynomialGapWord_succ_sub (n : ℕ) : polynomialGapWord (n + 1) - polynomialGapWord n = ((4 * n + 10 : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Adjacent differences grow linearly and in particular never equal `±2`.

declarations.name: polynomialGapWord_strictMono
declarations.docstring: The word is strictly increasing, hence unbounded and not eventually periodic; this is stronger than merely inserting isolated large gaps.

declarations.name: polynomialTailOrbit_integral
declarations.docstring: Every tail state is integral, so every fixed tail shift is integral.

declarations.name: polynomialGapWord_no_adjacent_two_digit
declarations.signature: theorem polynomialGapWord_no_adjacent_two_digit (N : ℕ) : polynomialGapWord (N + 2) - polynomialGapWord (N + 1) ≠ 2 ∧ polynomialGapWord (N + 2) - polynomialGapWord (N + 1) ≠ -2
declarations.docstring: The `h=1` digit required by an adjacent small-mismatch certificate is never `±2` in this rational, positive, even, polynomially growing orbit.

declarations.name: polynomialTailOrbit_shift_integral
declarations.signature: theorem polynomialTailOrbit_shift_integral (h N : ℕ) : RatIntegral (tailShift polynomialTailOrbit h N)
declarations.docstring: Every fixed tail shift of the polynomial countermodel is integral. This is the consumer-ready obstruction: positivity, evenness, strict growth, and the dyadic recurrence do not force a nonintegral shift.

declarations.name: prime0
declarations.docstring: The actual zero-based prime enumeration, not an arbitrary model.

declarations.name: prime0_mono_step
declarations.signature: theorem prime0_mono_step (n : ℕ) : prime0 n ≤ prime0 (n + 1)

declarations.name: primeGap0_even
declarations.signature: theorem primeGap0_even (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : 2 ∣ primeGap0 n

declarations.name: primeGapDyadicTerm_eq
declarations.signature: theorem primeGapDyadicTerm_eq (n : ℕ) : primeGapDyadicTerm n = 2 * primeDyadicTerm (n + 1) - primeDyadicTerm n

declarations.name: summable_primeDyadicTerm_of_polynomial_growth
declarations.signature: theorem summable_primeDyadicTerm_of_polynomial_growth (C k : ℕ) (hgrowth : ∀ n, prime0 n ≤ C * (n + 1) ^ k) : Summable primeDyadicTerm

declarations.name: centralBinom_le_two_mul_pow_primeCounting
declarations.signature: theorem centralBinom_le_two_mul_pow_primeCounting (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : m.centralBinom ≤ (2 * m) ^ Nat.primeCounting (2 * m)

declarations.name: sum_prime_gaps
declarations.signature: theorem sum_prime_gaps (n : ℕ) : 2 + ∑ i ∈ range n, primeGap0 i = prime0 n
declarations.docstring: Finite cumulative identity from the checked PaperCoreR7 proof.

declarations.name: actualTail
declarations.docstring: The actual scaled tail is defined using the convergent series.

declarations.name: actualTail_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem actualTail_recurrence (N : ℕ) : actualTail (N + 1) = 2 * actualTail N - (primeGap0 (N + 1) : ℝ)

declarations.name: actualTail_eq_shifted_sum
declarations.signature: theorem actualTail_eq_shifted_sum (N : ℕ) : actualTail N = ∑' k : ℕ, (primeGap0 (N + k + 1) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (k + 1)
declarations.docstring: The series-tail formulation used in the paper, not just a recurrence model.

declarations.name: realPrimeGapTail
declarations.docstring: The genuine scaled tail after the first `N+1` prime-gap terms.

declarations.name: realPrimeGapTail_eq_scaled_tsum
declarations.signature: theorem realPrimeGapTail_eq_scaled_tsum (N : ℕ) : realPrimeGapTail N = 2 ^ (N + 1) * ∑' k : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm (k + (N + 1))
declarations.docstring: The finite-prefix definition equals the convergent infinite tail.

declarations.name: realPrimeGapTail_eq_tsum_shifted_gaps
declarations.signature: theorem realPrimeGapTail_eq_tsum_shifted_gaps (N : ℕ) : realPrimeGapTail N = ∑' k : ℕ, (primeGap0 (N + k + 1) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (k + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact agreement with the manuscript's shifted-gap series, with denominator `2^(k+1)` and no rational-state hypothesis.

declarations.name: realPrimeGapTail_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem realPrimeGapTail_recurrence : RealDyadicTailRecurrence (fun n => (primeGap0 n : ℤ)) realPrimeGapTail
declarations.docstring: The actual real tail satisfies the integer-digit recurrence unconditionally.

declarations.name: realPrimeGapTail_zero
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem realPrimeGapTail_zero : realPrimeGapTail 0 = 2 * (∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n) - 1

declarations.name: irrational_realPrimeGapTail_zero_iff
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_realPrimeGapTail_zero_iff : Irrational (realPrimeGapTail 0) ↔ Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeGapDyadicTerm n)
declarations.docstring: The tail's initial value has exactly the arithmetic status of the gap sum.

declarations.name: irrational_primeSeries_iff_realPrimeGapTail_escape
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_primeSeries_iff_realPrimeGapTail_escape : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeDyadicTerm n) ↔ CofinalNonintegralTailShifts realPrimeGapTail
declarations.docstring: Cofinal escape now refers to the actual real prime-gap tail.

declarations.name: realIntegral_eq_zero_of_small
declarations.signature: theorem realIntegral_eq_zero_of_small {x : ℝ} (hint : RealIntegral x) (hlo : -1 < x) (hhi : x < 1) : x = 0
declarations.docstring: An integer in the open unit interval is zero, also in the real state space.

declarations.name: realTailShift_succ
declarations.signature: theorem realTailShift_succ {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) : realTailShift T h (N + 1) = 2 * realTailShift T h N - ((g (N + h + 1) : ℝ) - g (N + 1))
declarations.docstring: The real shift obeys the same difference recurrence as the rational shift.

declarations.name: realTailShift_not_both_integral_of_small_pair_of_digit_ne
declarations.signature: theorem realTailShift_not_both_integral_of_small_pair_of_digit_ne {g : ℕ → ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℝ} (hrec : RealDyadicTailRecurrence g T) (h N : ℕ) (hsmall : (-1 < realTailShift T h N ∧ realTailShift T h N < 1) ∧ (-1 < realTailShift T h (N + 1) ∧ realTailShift T h (N + 1) < 1)) (hdigit : g (N + h + 1) ≠ g (N + 1)) : ¬ (RealIntegral (realTailShift T h N) ∧ RealIntegral (realTailShift T h (N + 1)))
declarations.docstring: Two adjacent small real shifts cannot both be integral when their digits differ.

declarations.name: irrational_primeSeries_of_realPrimeGapTail_small_mismatch
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_primeSeries_of_realPrimeGapTail_small_mismatch (hsupply : ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → ∀ N₀ : ℕ, ∃ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N ∧ ((-1 < realTailShift realPrimeGapTail h N ∧ realTailShift realPrimeGapTail h N < 1) ∧ (-1 < realTailShift realPrimeGapTail h (N + 1) ∧ realTailShift realPrimeGapTail h (N + 1) < 1)) ∧ primeGap0 (N + h + 1) ≠ primeGap0 (N + 1)) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, primeDyadicTerm n)
declarations.docstring: The paper's real small-mismatch supply implies irrationality of the actual prime series. The supply is an explicit unproved hypothesis, not a consequence of nonperiodicity or of convergence.

declarations.name: progressionCapacity
declarations.signature: theorem progressionCapacity {A M r : ℕ} (hM : 0 < M) (hr : r < M) (hA : 2 * M ≤ A) : r + M * ((A - r) / M) ≤ A ∧ A ≤ r + M * ((A - r) / M) + M
declarations.docstring: The last digit in one residue class loses fewer than M units of capacity.

declarations.name: progressionDigit
declarations.signature: def progressionDigit (r M D : ℕ) (w lo x : ℝ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: An explicit digit in the progression r + M * {0,...,D}.

declarations.name: progressionDigit_le
declarations.signature: theorem progressionDigit_le (r M D : ℕ) (w lo x : ℝ) : progressionDigit r M D w lo x ≤ r + M * D

declarations.name: progressionDigit_spec
declarations.signature: theorem progressionDigit_spec {A M r D : ℕ} {w lo hi x : ℝ} (hM : 0 < M) (hw : 0 < w) (hr : r ≤ M) (hcap : r + M * D ≤ A) (htop : A ≤ r + M * D + M) (hov : (M : ℝ) * w ≤ hi - lo) (hxl : (M : ℝ) * w + lo ≤ x) (hxu : x ≤ ((A : ℝ) - M) * w + hi) : progressionDigit r M D w lo x ≤ A ∧ lo ≤ x - (progressionDigit r M D w lo x : ℝ) * w ∧ x - (progressionDigit r M D w lo x : ℝ) * w ≤ hi
declarations.docstring: Uniform interval selection for every residue r. The hypotheses are stated with a general progression capacity D to separate floor arithmetic.

declarations.name: cumulativeResidue

declarations.name: cumulativeResidue_spec

declarations.name: feedbackDigit
declarations.signature: def feedbackDigit (A M C : ℕ) (w lo x : ℝ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: One correction site simultaneously encodes a digit and repairs the sum.

declarations.name: feedbackDigit_spec
declarations.signature: theorem feedbackDigit_spec {A M C : ℕ} {w lo hi x : ℝ} (hM : 0 < M) (hA : 2 * M ≤ A) (hw : 0 < w) (hov : (M : ℝ) * w ≤ hi - lo) (hxl : (M : ℝ) * w + lo ≤ x) (hxu : x ≤ ((A : ℝ) - M) * w + hi) : feedbackDigit A M C w lo x ≤ A ∧ (M : ℤ) ∣ (C : ℤ) + (feedbackDigit A M C w lo x : ℤ) ∧ lo ≤ x - (feedbackDigit A M C w lo x : ℝ) * w ∧ x - (feedbackDigit A M C w lo x : ℝ) * w ≤ hi

declarations.name: feedbackState_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem feedbackState_bounds {A M : ℕ → ℕ} {w lo hi : ℕ → ℝ} {y : ℝ} (hM : ∀ n, 0 < M n) (hA : ∀ n, 2 * M n ≤ A n) (hw : ∀ n, 0 < w n) (hl : ∀ n, lo n = (M n : ℝ) * w n + lo (n + 1)) (hu : ∀ n, hi n = ((A n : ℝ) - M n) * w n + hi (n + 1)) (hov : ∀ n, (M n : ℝ) * w n ≤ hi (n + 1) - lo (n + 1)) (hyl : lo 0 ≤ y) (hyu : y ≤ hi 0) : ∀ n, lo n ≤ (feedbackState A M w lo y n).2 ∧ (feedbackState A M w lo y n).2 ≤ hi n

declarations.signature: theorem upperTail_tendsto_zero (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) : Tendsto (upperTail f start) atTop (𝓝 0)

declarations.name: generated_interval_nonempty
declarations.signature: theorem generated_interval_nonempty (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) (hstart : Ready f start 0) : lowerTail f start 0 < upperTail f start 0
declarations.docstring: There is a single nondegenerate interval for all digit choices.

declarations.name: lowerTail_positive
declarations.signature: theorem lowerTail_positive (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) (hstart : Ready f start 0) : 0 < lowerTail f start 0

declarations.name: generated_interval_filling
declarations.signature: theorem generated_interval_filling (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) (hstart : Ready f start 0) {y : ℝ} (hyl : lowerTail f start 0 ≤ y) (hyu : y ≤ upperTail f start 0) : ∃ d : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ j, d j ≤ capacity f start j) ∧ (∀ j, (modulus f start j : ℤ) ∣ ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), d i : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧ HasSum (fun j => (d j : ℝ) / 2 ^ (centre f start j + 1)) y
declarations.docstring: The variable-capacity hypotheses have now all been discharged for the constructed schedule. This is an indexed sum, not an ambient-word endpoint.

declarations.name: arbitrary_envelope_indexed_interval
declarations.signature: theorem arbitrary_envelope_indexed_interval (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : Tendsto f atTop atTop) (K : ℕ) : ∃ start : ℕ, ∃ lo hi : ℝ, K ≤ start ∧ (Set.range (centre f start) ⊆ Set.Ici K) ∧ UpperBanachZero (Set.range (centre f start)) ∧ 0 < lo ∧ lo < hi ∧ ∀ y : ℝ, lo ≤ y → y ≤ hi → ∃ d : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ j, (d j : ℝ) ≤ f (centre f start j)) ∧ (∀ j, (modulus f start j : ℤ) ∣ ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), d i : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧ HasSum (fun j => (d j : ℝ) / 2 ^ (centre f start j + 1)) y
declarations.docstring: Main partial endpoint: one support, one nondegenerate positive interval, and all indexed correction targets, constructed from f and K alone. The seed is chosen before y, and every capacity hypothesis is discharged.

declarations.name: AmbientSparseRationalisation_target
declarations.docstring: Remaining ambient-word endpoint, made explicit rather than assumed. The constructed indexed digits must still be embedded with the corresponding finite-prefix identity. This definition is not asserted as a theorem.

declarations.name: PolylogarithmicRate_target
declarations.docstring: The quantitative polylogarithmic counting input is NOT supplied by upper Banach density zero. Its proof remains part of the paper label.

declarations.name: UniformZeroDensity
declarations.docstring: The reciprocal-integer and epsilon formulations agree uniformly in translation.

declarations.name: upperBanachZero_iff_uniform
declarations.signature: theorem upperBanachZero_iff_uniform (S : Set ℕ) : UpperBanachZero S ↔ UniformZeroDensity S

declarations.name: arbitrary_word_sparse_rational_target
declarations.signature: theorem arbitrary_word_sparse_rational_target (a : ℕ → ℕ) {A : ℝ} (ha : HasSum (fun n => (a n : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) A) (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : Tendsto f atTop atTop) (K : ℕ) : ∃ S : Set ℕ, ∃ e : ℕ → ℕ, ∃ r : ℚ, S ⊆ Set.Ici K ∧ UpperBanachZero S ∧ A < (r : ℝ) ∧ (∀ n, e n ≠ 0 → n ∈ S) ∧ (∀ n < K, a n + e n = a n) ∧ (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (e n : ℝ) ≤ f n) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, q ∣ e n ∧ q ∣ ∑ i ∈ range n, e i) ∧ HasSum (fun n => ((a n + e n : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) (r : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A rational target really exists inside the common interval.

declarations.name: polylogarithmic_word_interval
declarations.signature: theorem polylogarithmic_word_interval (a : ℕ → ℕ) {A ε : ℝ} (ha : HasSum (fun n => (a n : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) A) (hε : 0 < ε) (K : ℕ) : ∃ start : ℕ, ∃ l u C : ℝ, (Set.range (centre (polylog ε) start) ⊆ Set.Ici K) ∧ UpperBanachZero (Set.range (centre (polylog ε) start)) ∧ A < l ∧ l < u ∧ 0 < C ∧ (∃ X₀ : ℕ, ∀ X L : ℕ, X₀ ≤ X → L ≤ 2 * X → ((supportSlice (centre (polylog ε) start) X L).card : ℝ) ≤ C * X / iterlog X) ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, l ≤ r → r ≤ u → ∃ e : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, e n ≠ 0 → n ∈ Set.range (centre (polylog ε) start)) ∧ (∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (e n : ℝ) ≤ polylog ε n) ∧ (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, q ∣ e n ∧ q ∣ ∑ i ∈ range n, e i) ∧
declarations.docstring: The polylogarithmic clause and the actual statistical endpoint, with the support, interval and implied constant chosen before the target r.

declarations.name: polylogarithmic_word_interval_uniform
declarations.signature: theorem polylogarithmic_word_interval_uniform (a : ℕ → ℕ) {A ε : ℝ} (ha : HasSum (fun n => (a n : ℝ) / 2 ^ (n + 1)) A) (hε : 0 < ε) (K : ℕ) : ∃ start : ℕ, ∃ l u C : ℝ, ∃ Nq : ℕ → ℕ, (Set.range (centre (polylog ε) start) ⊆ Set.Ici K) ∧ UpperBanachZero (Set.range (centre (polylog ε) start)) ∧ A < l ∧ l < u ∧ 0 < C ∧ (∃ X₀ : ℕ, ∀ X L : ℕ, X₀ ≤ X → L ≤ 2 * X → ((supportSlice (centre (polylog ε) start) X L).card : ℝ) ≤ C * X / iterlog X) ∧ (∀ m : ℕ → ℕ, Tendsto (fun X => (m X : ℝ) / Real.log (Real.log (X : ℝ))) atTop (𝓝 0) → ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∀ᶠ X : ℕ in atTop, ∀ b : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, a n ≠ b n → n ∈ Set.range (centre (polylog ε) start)) →
declarations.docstring: The printed polylogarithmic statement, retaining the exact finite-window bound and choosing every congruence cutoff before the target. The statistical limit is uniform over all words changed on the common support; it therefore applies uniformly to the corrections in the final clause.

declarations.name: cumulative_modEq
declarations.signature: theorem cumulative_modEq (a e : ℕ → ℕ) (p₀ q n : ℕ) (he : q ∣ ∑ i ∈ range n, e i) : p₀ + ∑ i ∈ range n, (a i + e i) ≡ p₀ + ∑ i ∈ range n, a i [MOD q]
declarations.docstring: Every fixed congruence profile of the cumulative positions is preserved.

declarations.name: polylog_mono
declarations.signature: theorem polylog_mono {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) : Monotone (polylog α)

declarations.name: log_shift_tendsto_atTop
declarations.signature: theorem log_shift_tendsto_atTop : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 3)) atTop atTop

declarations.name: polylog_tendsto_atTop
declarations.signature: theorem polylog_tendsto_atTop {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) : Tendsto (polylog α) atTop atTop

declarations.name: iterlog_tendsto_atTop
declarations.signature: theorem iterlog_tendsto_atTop : Tendsto iterlog atTop atTop

declarations.name: iterlog_pos
declarations.signature: theorem iterlog_pos {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) : 0 < iterlog n

declarations.name: iterlog_le_nat
declarations.signature: theorem iterlog_le_nat {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) : iterlog n ≤ n

declarations.name: amplitude_le_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem amplitude_le_two_pow (k : ℕ) : amplitude k ≤ 2 ^ (3 * gap k)

declarations.name: gap_succ_le_twice
declarations.signature: theorem gap_succ_le_twice (k : ℕ) : gap (k + 1) ≤ 2 * gap k

declarations.name: gap_succ_ge
declarations.signature: theorem gap_succ_ge (k : ℕ) : gap k + 1 ≤ gap (k + 1)

declarations.name: gap_le_threshold
declarations.signature: theorem gap_le_threshold (Q k : ℕ) (hQ : 1 ≤ Q) : gap k ≤ threshold Q k

declarations.name: threshold_double
declarations.signature: theorem threshold_double (Q k : ℕ) (hQ : 1 ≤ Q) : 2 * threshold Q k ≤ threshold Q (k + 1)

declarations.name: threshold_step
declarations.signature: theorem threshold_step (Q k : ℕ) (hQ : 1 ≤ Q) : threshold Q (k + 1) + gap k ≤ threshold Q (k + 2)

declarations.name: log_threshold
declarations.signature: theorem log_threshold (Q k : ℕ) : Real.log (threshold Q k : ℝ) = (2 : ℝ) ^ (Q * gap k) * Real.log 2

declarations.name: log_log_threshold
declarations.signature: theorem log_log_threshold (Q k : ℕ) : Real.log (Real.log (threshold Q k : ℝ)) = (Q : ℝ) * (gap k : ℝ) * Real.log 2 + Real.log (Real.log 2)

declarations.name: threshold_ready
declarations.signature: theorem threshold_ready {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (Q : ℕ) (hQ : 4 ≤ Q) (hαQ : 8 ≤ α * Q) (k : ℕ) : Ready (polylog α) (threshold Q k) k
declarations.docstring: An explicit readiness supplier, including the independent linear cap.

declarations.name: centre_le_readiness_threshold
declarations.signature: theorem centre_le_readiness_threshold (f : ℕ → ℝ) (T : ℕ → ℕ) (hT : ∀ k, Ready f (T k) k) (hstep : ∀ k, T (k + 1) + gap k ≤ T (k + 2)) (start : ℕ) : ∀ j, centre f start j ≤ start + T (level f start j + 1)
declarations.docstring: A non-upgrading step cannot have crossed the next readiness threshold. This is the quantitative lag invariant missing from the old candidates.

declarations.name: iterlog_centre_bound
declarations.signature: theorem iterlog_centre_bound {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (Q : ℕ) (hQ : 4 ≤ Q) (hαQ : 8 ≤ α * Q) (start j : ℕ) (hj : start + 3 ≤ level (polylog α) start j) : iterlog (centre (polylog α) start j) ≤ 4 * Q * gap (level (polylog α) start j)

declarations.name: supportSlice_card_le_local
declarations.signature: theorem supportSlice_card_le_local (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hc : StrictMono c) (a L R : ℕ) (hR : 0 < R) (hsep : ∀ j, a ≤ c j → R ≤ c (j + 1) - c j) : (supportSlice c a L).card ≤ L / R + 1
declarations.docstring: Local, rather than global-prefix, bin counting.

declarations.name: polylog_extended_rate_withQ
declarations.signature: theorem polylog_extended_rate_withQ {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (Q : ℕ) (hQ : 4 ≤ Q) (hαQ : 8 ≤ α * Q) (start : ℕ) : ∃ X₀ : ℕ, ∀ X L : ℕ, X₀ ≤ X → L ≤ 2 * X → ((supportSlice (centre (polylog α) start) X L).card : ℝ) ≤ (8 * Q + 1) * X / iterlog X
declarations.docstring: Quantitative support bound for every interval [X,X+L) of length at most 2X.

declarations.name: polylog_extended_rate_uniform
declarations.signature: theorem polylog_extended_rate_uniform {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ start : ℕ, ∃ X₀ : ℕ, ∀ X L : ℕ, X₀ ≤ X → L ≤ 2 * X → ((supportSlice (centre (polylog α) start) X L).card : ℝ) ≤ C * X / iterlog X
declarations.docstring: The implied constant depends only on α, not on the initial prefix or seed.

declarations.name: polylog_extended_rate
declarations.signature: theorem polylog_extended_rate {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (start : ℕ) : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ X₀ : ℕ, ∀ X L : ℕ, X₀ ≤ X → L ≤ 2 * X → ((supportSlice (centre (polylog α) start) X L).card : ℝ) ≤ C * X / iterlog X

declarations.name: gap_upper_of_ready
declarations.signature: theorem gap_upper_of_ready {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (start : ℕ) (hready : Ready (polylog α) start 0) (j : ℕ) : (gap (level (polylog α) start j) : ℝ) ≤ (α / Real.log 2) * iterlog (centre (polylog α) start j)
declarations.docstring: Readiness supplies the other side of the asserted log-log spacing scale.

declarations.name: polylogarithmic_rate
declarations.docstring: The old target is now a proved declaration, not an assumed interface.

declarations.name: pair_total
declarations.signature: theorem pair_total (M D d : ℕ) (hd : d ≤ D) : M * d + M * (D - d) = M * D
declarations.docstring: The unweighted total is independent of the free digit.

declarations.name: pair_weighted
declarations.signature: theorem pair_weighted (M D d n : ℕ) (hd : d ≤ D) : (M * d : ℚ) / 2 ^ (n + 1) + ((M : ℚ) * ((D - d : ℕ) : ℚ)) / 2 ^ (n + 2) = (M : ℚ) * (D + d) / 2 ^ (n + 2)
declarations.docstring: The same pair retains one free digit in the dyadic weighted total.

declarations.name: repairBuffer
declarations.docstring: A deterministic repair to the next cumulative modulus.

declarations.name: repairBuffer_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem repairBuffer_nonneg (C : ℤ) {M : ℤ} (hM : 0 < M) : 0 ≤ repairBuffer C M

declarations.name: repairBuffer_lt
declarations.signature: theorem repairBuffer_lt (C : ℤ) {M : ℤ} (hM : 0 < M) : repairBuffer C M < M

declarations.name: repairBuffer_repairs
declarations.signature: theorem repairBuffer_repairs (C M : ℤ) : M ∣ C + repairBuffer C M

declarations.name: repairBuffer_preserves
declarations.signature: theorem repairBuffer_preserves {q C M : ℤ} (hC : q ∣ C) (hM : q ∣ M) : q ∣ repairBuffer C M
declarations.docstring: Repairing a larger modulus does not spoil previously imposed divisors.

declarations.name: capacity_telescope
declarations.signature: theorem capacity_telescope (M : ℚ) (n s : ℕ) : ((2 : ℚ) ^ s - 1) * M / 2 ^ (n + s + 2) = M / 2 ^ (n + 2) - M / 2 ^ (n + s + 2)
declarations.docstring: The preceding spacing, not the following spacing, gives this telescope.

declarations.name: variableDigit
declarations.signature: def variableDigit (D : ℕ) (w y : ℝ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: A clipped greedy digit with a capacity that may vary with the index.

declarations.name: variableDigit_le
declarations.signature: theorem variableDigit_le (D : ℕ) (w y : ℝ) : variableDigit D w y ≤ D

declarations.name: variableDigit_spec
declarations.signature: theorem variableDigit_spec {D : ℕ} {w S y : ℝ} (hw : 0 < w) (hy0 : 0 ≤ y) (hy1 : y ≤ (D : ℝ) * w + S) (hoverlap : w ≤ S) : 0 ≤ y - (variableDigit D w y : ℝ) * w ∧ y - (variableDigit D w y : ℝ) * w ≤ S
declarations.docstring: One-step interval filling with an arbitrary remaining-tail capacity S.

declarations.name: greedyRemainder
declarations.signature: def greedyRemainder (w : ℕ → ℝ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (y : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ | 0 => y | n + 1 => greedyRemainder w D y n - (variableDigit (D n) (w n) (greedyRemainder w D y n) : ℝ) * w n def greedyDigit (w : ℕ → ℝ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (y : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The remainder recursion is defined without assuming any invariant.

declarations.name: greedyDigit
declarations.signature: def greedyDigit (w : ℕ → ℝ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (y : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: greedyDigit_le
declarations.signature: theorem greedyDigit_le (w : ℕ → ℝ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (y : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : greedyDigit w D y n ≤ D n

declarations.name: greedyRemainder_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem greedyRemainder_bounds {w S : ℕ → ℝ} {D : ℕ → ℕ} {y : ℝ} (hw : ∀ n, 0 < w n) (hstep : ∀ n, S n = (D n : ℝ) * w n + S (n + 1)) (hoverlap : ∀ n, w n ≤ S (n + 1)) (hy0 : 0 ≤ y) (hy1 : y ≤ S 0) : ∀ n, 0 ≤ greedyRemainder w D y n ∧ greedyRemainder w D y n ≤ S n
declarations.docstring: Bounds for every remainder, including the full unprescribed infinite tail.

declarations.name: greedy_partial_sum
declarations.signature: theorem greedy_partial_sum (w : ℕ → ℝ) (D : ℕ → ℕ) (y : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ∑ n ∈ range N, (greedyDigit w D y n : ℝ) * w n = y - greedyRemainder w D y N
declarations.docstring: The finite telescope used for the infinite-series endpoint.

declarations.name: exists_digits_hasSum_of_capacity
declarations.signature: theorem exists_digits_hasSum_of_capacity {w S : ℕ → ℝ} {D : ℕ → ℕ} {y : ℝ} (hw : ∀ n, 0 < w n) (hstep : ∀ n, S n = (D n : ℝ) * w n + S (n + 1)) (hoverlap : ∀ n, w n ≤ S (n + 1)) (hvanish : Tendsto S atTop (𝓝 0)) (hy0 : 0 ≤ y) (hy1 : y ≤ S 0) : ∃ d : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, d n ≤ D n) ∧ HasSum (fun n => (d n : ℝ) * w n) y
declarations.docstring: Infinite variable-alphabet interval filling from a given capacity sequence. The actual sparse schedule must still establish these hypotheses separately.

declarations.name: supportSlice
declarations.signature: def supportSlice (c : ℕ → ℕ) (a L : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.docstring: Actual support points in the half-open interval [a,a+L).

declarations.name: indexSlice
declarations.signature: def indexSlice (c : ℕ → ℕ) (a L : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.docstring: Indices of those support points. A strictly increasing natural map satisfies j <= c j, so range(a+L) suffices.

declarations.name: supportSlice_card
declarations.signature: theorem supportSlice_card (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hc : StrictMono c) (a L : ℕ) : (supportSlice c a L).card = (indexSlice c a L).card

declarations.name: equal_bin_close
declarations.signature: theorem equal_bin_close {x y R : ℕ} (hR : 0 < R) (h : x / R = y / R) : y < x + R
declarations.docstring: Equal quotient bins have width strictly less than R.

declarations.name: supportSlice_card_le
declarations.signature: theorem supportSlice_card_le (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hc : StrictMono c) (J R : ℕ) (hR : 0 < R) (hsep : ∀ j, J ≤ j → R ≤ c (j + 1) - c j) (a L : ℕ) : (supportSlice c a L).card ≤ J + L / R + 1
declarations.docstring: Quantitative bound, including the finite irregular prefix J.

declarations.name: UpperBanachZero
declarations.docstring: Reciprocal-integer characterisation of upper Banach density zero.

declarations.name: upperBanachZero_of_eventual_spacing
declarations.signature: theorem upperBanachZero_of_eventual_spacing (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hc : StrictMono c) (hgap : ∀ R, ∃ J, ∀ j, J ≤ j → R ≤ c (j + 1) - c j) : UpperBanachZero (Set.range c)
declarations.docstring: Divergent successive spacings imply upper Banach density zero, uniformly over every translate of the interval.

declarations.name: generated_support_upperBanachZero
declarations.signature: theorem generated_support_upperBanachZero (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : Tendsto f atTop atTop) (start : ℕ) : UpperBanachZero (Set.range (centre f start))
declarations.docstring: The generated support satisfies the requested translated-interval zero-density condition, not just a cofinal spacing assertion.

declarations.name: exists_sparse_budgeted_support
declarations.signature: theorem exists_sparse_budgeted_support (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : Tendsto f atTop atTop) (K : ℕ) : ∃ start : ℕ, K ≤ start ∧ Ready f start 0 ∧ (Set.range (centre f start) ⊆ Set.Ici K) ∧ UpperBanachZero (Set.range (centre f start)) ∧ (∀ j, (capacity f start j : ℝ) ≤ f (centre f start j) ∧ capacity f start j ≤ centre f start j + 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact arbitrary-envelope support package. The polylogarithmic *rate* is deliberately not inferred from upper Banach density zero.

declarations.name: index_le_of_strictMono
declarations.signature: theorem index_le_of_strictMono (c : ℕ → ℕ) (hc : StrictMono c) (j : ℕ) : j ≤ c j
declarations.docstring: Every increasing map from naturals dominates its input index.

declarations.name: gap
declarations.docstring: A level-k step. The square is convenient; sharp constants are not claimed.

declarations.name: amplitude
declarations.docstring: A level-k capacity, allowing two successive modulus upgrades.

declarations.name: level_le_gap
declarations.signature: theorem level_le_gap (k : ℕ) : k ≤ gap k

declarations.name: Ready
declarations.signature: def Ready (f : ℕ → ℝ) (n k : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: ready_mono
declarations.signature: theorem ready_mono {f : ℕ → ℝ} {n n' k : ℕ} (h : Ready f n k) (hn : n ≤ n') : Ready f n' k

declarations.name: eventually_ready
declarations.signature: theorem eventually_ready (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : Tendsto f atTop atTop) (k : ℕ) : ∃ n, Ready f n k

declarations.name: upgrade

declarations.name: upgrade_bounds

declarations.name: upgrade_of_ready
declarations.signature: theorem upgrade_of_ready {f : ℕ → ℝ} {n k : ℕ} (h : Ready f n (k + 1)) : upgrade f n k = k + 1

declarations.name: state
declarations.signature: def state (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ × ℕ | 0 => (start, 0) | j + 1 => let s
declarations.docstring: State = (centre, level), with no assumed rate for the envelope.

declarations.name: centre
declarations.signature: def centre (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start j : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: level
declarations.signature: def level (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start j : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem centre_zero (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) : centre f start 0 = start

declarations.name: level_zero
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem level_zero (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) : level f start 0 = 0

declarations.name: level_succ

declarations.signature: theorem centre_strictMono (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) : StrictMono (centre f start)

declarations.name: level_mono
declarations.signature: theorem level_mono (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) : Monotone (level f start)

declarations.name: level_succ_le
declarations.signature: theorem level_succ_le (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start j : ℕ) : level f start (j + 1) ≤ level f start j + 1

declarations.name: level_le_index
declarations.signature: theorem level_le_index (f : ℕ → ℝ) (start : ℕ) : ∀ j, level f start j ≤ j
