declarations.signature: theorem primeSetOf_not_dvd_Lv {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ insert q (s.tagIndexOf q)) : ¬ a ∣ s.Lv

declarations.name: primeSetOf_dvd_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem primeSetOf_dvd_lcm {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ insert q (s.tagIndexOf q)) : a ∣ s.support.lcm id

declarations.name: primeSetOf_dvd_quotient
declarations.signature: theorem primeSetOf_dvd_quotient {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) (hLdvd : s.Lv ∣ s.support.lcm id) {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ insert q (s.tagIndexOf q)) : a ∣ s.support.lcm id / s.Lv

declarations.name: periodOf_eq_prod
declarations.signature: theorem periodOf_eq_prod {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) : s.periodOf q = ∏ a ∈ insert q (s.tagIndexOf q), a

declarations.name: periodOf_pos
declarations.signature: theorem periodOf_pos {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) : 0 < s.periodOf q

declarations.name: periodOf_dvd_quotient
declarations.signature: theorem periodOf_dvd_quotient {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) (hLdvd : s.Lv ∣ s.support.lcm id) : s.periodOf q ∣ s.support.lcm id / s.Lv

declarations.name: tagIndexOf_disjoint
declarations.signature: theorem tagIndexOf_disjoint {q q' : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) (hq' : q' ∈ s.parents) (hne : q ≠ q') {p : ℕ} (hp : p ∈ s.tagIndexOf q) : p ∉ s.tagIndexOf q'

declarations.name: periodOf_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem periodOf_coprime {q q' : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) (hq' : q' ∈ s.parents) (hne : q ≠ q') : Nat.Coprime (s.periodOf q) (s.periodOf q')

declarations.name: prod_periodOf_dvd_quotient
declarations.signature: theorem prod_periodOf_dvd_quotient (hLdvd : s.Lv ∣ s.support.lcm id) : (∏ q ∈ s.parents, s.periodOf q) ∣ s.support.lcm id / s.Lv

declarations.name: Lv_dvd_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem Lv_dvd_lcm {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) {p : ℕ} (hp : p ∈ s.tagSets (q, s.Lv)) : s.Lv ∣ s.support.lcm id
declarations.docstring: "The nonempty tag sets with `d = L` also show `L ∣ Q`."

declarations.name: card_succSetOf_ge
declarations.signature: theorem card_succSetOf_ge {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) (G : Finset ℕ) (hG : G ⊆ s.Lv.divisors) (hmu : ∀ r ∈ G, 4 * (r : ℝ) ≤ ∑ d ∈ s.Lv.divisors.filter (fun d => d ∣ r), ∑ p ∈ s.tagSets (q, d), 1 / (p : ℝ)) : (G.card : ℝ) * ((s.periodOf q : ℝ) / (2 * (q : ℝ))) ≤ (((s.succSetOf G q).card : ℕ) : ℝ)

declarations.name: succSetOf_subset
declarations.signature: theorem succSetOf_subset (G : Finset ℕ) (q : ℕ) : s.succSetOf G q ⊆ Finset.range (s.periodOf q)

declarations.name: card_succ_add_card_fail
declarations.signature: theorem card_succ_add_card_fail (G : Finset ℕ) (q : ℕ) : (s.succSetOf G q).card + (s.failSetOf G q).card = s.periodOf q

declarations.name: mem_failSetOf_iff
declarations.signature: theorem mem_failSetOf_iff (G : Finset ℕ) {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) (m : ℕ) : (m % s.periodOf q ∈ s.failSetOf G q) ↔ ¬ (∃ r ∈ G, q ∣ s.Lv * m + (s.Lv + r) ∧ r ≤ ((s.condTagsOf q r).filter (fun p => p ∣ s.Lv * m + (s.Lv + r))).card)

declarations.name: card_good_add_card_bad
declarations.signature: theorem card_good_add_card_bad (G : Finset ℕ) (P0 : ℕ) : (s.goodSet G P0).card + (s.badSet G P0).card = P0

declarations.name: one_lt_framePotential_of_success
declarations.signature: theorem one_lt_framePotential_of_success {G : Finset ℕ} (hG : G ⊆ s.Lv.divisors) {q : ℕ} (hq : q ∈ s.parents) {m r : ℕ} (hr : r ∈ G) (h1 : q ∣ s.Lv * m + (s.Lv + r)) (h2 : r ≤ ((s.condTagsOf q r).filter (fun p => p ∣ s.Lv * m + (s.Lv + r))).card) : 1 < framePotential s.support (s.Lv * m + s.Lv)

declarations.name: condExceedProb_support_ge
declarations.signature: theorem condExceedProb_support_ge (G : Finset ℕ) (hG : G ⊆ s.Lv.divisors) (hGcard : (s.Lv.divisors.card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * (G.card : ℝ)) (hmu : ∀ q ∈ s.parents, ∀ r ∈ G, 4 * (r : ℝ) ≤ ∑ d ∈ s.Lv.divisors.filter (fun d => d ∣ r), ∑ p ∈ s.tagSets (q, d), 1 / (p : ℝ)) (hqD : ∀ q ∈ s.parents, (s.Lv.divisors.card : ℝ) ≤ (q : ℝ)) (hsumB : 4 / (s.Lv.divisors.card : ℝ) ≤ ∑ q ∈ s.parents, 1 / (q : ℝ)) (hLdvd : s.Lv ∣ s.support.lcm id) : 1 - Real.exp (-1) ≤ condExceedProb s.support s.Lv

declarations.name: sum_five_div_aux
declarations.signature: theorem sum_five_div_aux {Dv bv S : ℝ} (hD : 0 < Dv) (hb : 0 < bv) (hDb : Dv ≤ bv) (h : S ≤ 4 / Dv + 1 / bv) : S ≤ 5 / Dv

declarations.name: tag_sum_upper_aux
declarations.signature: theorem tag_sum_upper_aux {Hr dr S : ℝ} (hH : 0 < Hr) (hd : 1 ≤ dr) (h : S ≤ 4 * dr / Hr + 1 / Hr) : S ≤ 5 * dr / Hr

declarations.name: mu_lower_aux
declarations.signature: theorem mu_lower_aux {Hr rr sg : ℝ} (hH : 0 < Hr) (hsig : Hr * rr ≤ sg) : 4 * rr ≤ 4 * sg / Hr

declarations.name: divisors_filter_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem divisors_filter_dvd {L r : ℕ} (hr : r ∈ L.divisors) : L.divisors.filter (fun d => d ∣ r) = r.divisors

declarations.name: kappaOne_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem kappaOne_nonneg (F : Finset ℕ) : 0 ≤ kappaOne F 1

declarations.name: arithmetic_logarithmic_counterexample
declarations.signature: theorem arithmetic_logarithmic_counterexample (H : ℕ) (hH : 2 ≤ H) (A₀ : ℝ) (hA₀ : 0 ≤ A₀) : ∃ (L : ℕ) (F : Finset ℕ), 0 < L ∧ Squarefree L ∧ F.Nonempty ∧ (0 : ℕ) ∉ F ∧ (∀ a ∈ F, 0 < a ∧ Squarefree a) ∧ (∀ a ∈ F, max (L : ℝ) A₀ < (a : ℝ)) ∧ L ∣ F.lcm id ∧ kappaOne F 1 ≤ 30 * Real.log 2 / (H : ℝ) ∧ 1 - Real.exp (-1) ≤ condExceedProb F L ∧ ∃ R : ℕ, 1 / 2 < dyadicMean L R L (exceedInd F)
declarations.docstring: Long `thm` "arithmetic logarithmic counterexample" (`paper/reasoning-parts/erdos257/a257_front.tex:9212`), clauses (i)-(iv). For every integer `H ≥ 2` and every real `A₀ ≥ 0` there are a squarefree `L > 0` and a finite nonempty set `F` of distinct squarefree positive integers with * `min F > max {L, A₀}`, * `κ₁(F;1) ≤ 30 log 2 / H`, * `ℙ_L(U_F > 1) ≥ 1 - e^{-1}`, * `𝒟_{L;R,L} 1_{U_F > 1} > 1/2` for some `R ≥ 0`. The extra clause `L ∣ lcm F` is the paper's "since `L ∣ Q`", used by the corollary.

declarations.name: no_absolute_dyadic_kappaOne_constant
declarations.signature: theorem no_absolute_dyadic_kappaOne_constant : ¬ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ (F : Finset ℕ), F.Nonempty → (0 : ℕ) ∉ F → ∀ (L M : ℕ), 0 < L → 0 < M → ∀ (R : ℕ) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → t ≤ 1 → dyadicMean L R M (fun N => if t < framePotential F N then (1 : ℝ) else 0) ≤ C * (1 + (L : ℝ) / (M : ℝ)) * kappaOne F t
declarations.docstring: Clause (v) of the long `thm` "arithmetic logarithmic counterexample": no absolute constant `C` satisfies `𝒟_{L;R,M} 1_{U_F > t} ≤ C (1 + L/M) κ₁(F;t)` uniformly in finite `F`, positive integers `L, M`, integers `R ≥ 0` and `0 < t ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: exists_support_paperCoverCost_ge
declarations.signature: theorem exists_support_paperCoverCost_ge (H : ℕ) (hH : 2 ≤ H) : ∃ F : Finset ℕ, F.Nonempty ∧ (0 : ℕ) ∉ F ∧ 1 - Real.exp (-1) ≤ paperCoverCost (F : Set ℕ) ∧ kappaOne F 1 ≤ 30 * Real.log 2 / (H : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Long `cor` "finite-functional separation" (`paper/reasoning-parts/erdos257/a257_front.tex:9369`), clauses 2 and 3: the supports of the theorem satisfy `K_*(F) ≥ 1 - e^{-1}` and `κ₁(F;1) ≤ 30 log 2 / H`, so no absolute `C` gives `K_*(F) ≤ C κ₁(F;1)`.

declarations.name: no_absolute_paperCoverCost_kappaOne_constant
declarations.signature: theorem no_absolute_paperCoverCost_kappaOne_constant : ¬ ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ F : Finset ℕ, F.Nonempty → (0 : ℕ) ∉ F → paperCoverCost (F : Set ℕ) ≤ C * kappaOne F 1
declarations.docstring: Clause 3 of the corollary: "no absolute `C` gives `K_*(F) ≤ C κ₁(F;1)` for all finite nonempty `F`, even after all covering sets, exponents, coefficients and positive weights have been optimised."

declarations.name: sum_indicator_eq_card
declarations.signature: theorem sum_indicator_eq_card {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {Ω A : Finset α} (hA : A ⊆ Ω) : (∑ ω ∈ Ω, (if ω ∈ A then (1 : ℝ) else 0)) = (A.card : ℝ)

declarations.name: sum_indicator_mul_eq_card
declarations.signature: theorem sum_indicator_mul_eq_card {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {Ω A B : Finset α} (hA : A ⊆ Ω) : (∑ ω ∈ Ω, (if ω ∈ A then (1 : ℝ) else 0) * (if ω ∈ B then (1 : ℝ) else 0)) = ((A ∩ B).card : ℝ)

declarations.name: sum_sq_sub_mean_eq
declarations.signature: theorem sum_sq_sub_mean_eq {α ι : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq ι] (Ω : Finset α) (S : Finset ι) (A : ι → Finset α) (a : ι → ℝ) (hA : ∀ p ∈ S, A p ⊆ Ω) (hmarg : ∀ p ∈ S, ((A p).card : ℝ) = (Ω.card : ℝ) * a p) (hpair : ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ p' ∈ S, p ≠ p' → ((A p ∩ A p').card : ℝ) = (Ω.card : ℝ) * (a p * a p')) : (∑ ω ∈ Ω, ((∑ p ∈ S, (if ω ∈ A p then (1 : ℝ) else 0)) - ∑ p ∈ S, a p) ^ 2) = (Ω.card : ℝ) * ((∑ p ∈ S, a p) - ∑ p ∈ S, a p ^ 2)
declarations.docstring: The paper's "the mean of `Z_q(N+r)` is `μ_r` and its variance is at most `μ_r`", as an exact second-moment computation from the marginal frequencies `a p` and the pairwise joint frequencies `a p · a p'` alone.

declarations.name: sum_sq_sub_mean_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_sq_sub_mean_le {α ι : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq ι] (Ω : Finset α) (S : Finset ι) (A : ι → Finset α) (a : ι → ℝ) (hA : ∀ p ∈ S, A p ⊆ Ω) (hmarg : ∀ p ∈ S, ((A p).card : ℝ) = (Ω.card : ℝ) * a p) (hpair : ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ p' ∈ S, p ≠ p' → ((A p ∩ A p').card : ℝ) = (Ω.card : ℝ) * (a p * a p')) : (∑ ω ∈ Ω, ((∑ p ∈ S, (if ω ∈ A p then (1 : ℝ) else 0)) - ∑ p ∈ S, a p) ^ 2) ≤ (Ω.card : ℝ) * ∑ p ∈ S, a p
declarations.docstring: "its variance is at most `μ_r`".

declarations.name: card_lt_le_of_sum_sq
declarations.signature: theorem card_lt_le_of_sum_sq {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (Ω : Finset α) (X : α → ℝ) (μ V r : ℝ) (hr : r < μ) (hV : (∑ ω ∈ Ω, (X ω - μ) ^ 2) ≤ (Ω.card : ℝ) * V) : (((Ω.filter (fun ω => X ω < r)).card : ℝ)) * (μ - r) ^ 2 ≤ (Ω.card : ℝ) * V
declarations.docstring: Chebyshev's inequality in the counting form the paper's uniform sampling gives: a second-moment bound `∑_ω (X ω - μ)² ≤ |Ω| V` bounds the number of samples with `X < r` by `|Ω| V/(μ - r)²`.

declarations.name: mean_div_sq_le
declarations.signature: theorem mean_div_sq_le {μ r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hμ : 4 * r ≤ μ) : μ / (μ - r) ^ 2 ≤ 4 / (9 * r)
declarations.docstring: The paper's `μ_r/(μ_r - r)² ≤ 4/(9r)` for `μ_r ≥ 4r`: the bound is decreasing in the mean, so the extreme case `μ_r = 4r` is the worst.

declarations.name: prod_one_sub_le_exp_neg_sum
declarations.signature: theorem prod_one_sub_le_exp_neg_sum {ι : Type*} (B : Finset ι) (x : ι → ℝ) (hx1 : ∀ q ∈ B, x q ≤ 1) : ∏ q ∈ B, (1 - x q) ≤ Real.exp (-∑ q ∈ B, x q)
declarations.docstring: "It follows that `ℙ_L(U_F > 1) ≥ 1 - ∏_q(1 - ℙ_L(E_q)) ≥ exp(-∑_q ℙ_L(E_q))` subtracted from one", from `1 - x ≤ e^{-x}`.

declarations.name: crtCard_filter_mod_eq
declarations.signature: theorem crtCard_filter_mod_eq {M a r : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hr : r < a) (hdvd : a ∣ M) : ((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => m % a = r)).card = M / a
declarations.docstring: A residue class modulo `a` meets `{0, …, M-1}` in exactly `M/a` points when `a ∣ M`. (Fresh-name copy of `card_filter_mod_eq`; see the module docstring.)

declarations.name: crtExists_residue_dvd_linear
declarations.signature: theorem crtExists_residue_dvd_linear {L a c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hcop : Nat.Coprime a L) : ∃ r, r < a ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, (a ∣ L * m + c ↔ m % a = r)
declarations.docstring: With `a` coprime to `L`, the solutions of `a ∣ L m + c` form a single residue class modulo `a`. For `L = 1` this is "the event `q ∣ N + r` has probability `1/q`"; the general `L` is the paper's sampling of `N = L m`.

declarations.name: crtModEq_prod_iff
declarations.signature: theorem crtModEq_prod_iff {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (n : ι → ℕ) (hcop : ∀ i ∈ S, ∀ j ∈ S, i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (n i) (n j)) (x y : ℕ) : (x ≡ y [MOD ∏ i ∈ S, n i]) ↔ ∀ i ∈ S, x ≡ y [MOD n i]
declarations.docstring: A family of congruences with pairwise coprime moduli is one congruence modulo the product.

declarations.name: crtExists_common
declarations.signature: theorem crtExists_common {ι : Type*} (S : Finset ι) (n r : ι → ℕ) (hn : ∀ i ∈ S, 0 < n i) (hcop : ∀ i ∈ S, ∀ j ∈ S, i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (n i) (n j)) : ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ i ∈ S, k ≡ r i [MOD n i]
declarations.docstring: A simultaneous system of congruences with pairwise coprime moduli has a solution: `Nat.chineseRemainderOfFinset`.

declarations.name: crtCard_filter_mod_family
declarations.signature: theorem crtCard_filter_mod_family {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {M : ℕ} (S : Finset ι) (n r : ι → ℕ) (hn : ∀ i ∈ S, 0 < n i) (hr : ∀ i ∈ S, r i < n i) (hcop : ∀ i ∈ S, ∀ j ∈ S, i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (n i) (n j)) (hdvd : (∏ i ∈ S, n i) ∣ M) : ((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => ∀ i ∈ S, m % n i = r i)).card = M / ∏ i ∈ S, n i
declarations.docstring: The count of a simultaneous residue condition over a full period.

declarations.name: crtCard_filter_dvd_linear_family
declarations.signature: theorem crtCard_filter_dvd_linear_family {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {M L : ℕ} (S : Finset ι) (n c : ι → ℕ) (hn : ∀ i ∈ S, 0 < n i) (hcopL : ∀ i ∈ S, Nat.Coprime (n i) L) (hcop : ∀ i ∈ S, ∀ j ∈ S, i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (n i) (n j)) (hdvd : (∏ i ∈ S, n i) ∣ M) : ((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => ∀ i ∈ S, n i ∣ L * m + c i)).card = M / ∏ i ∈ S, n i
declarations.docstring: The paper's independence of the sampled divisibility events, as an exact count: for pairwise coprime moduli each coprime to `L`, with the product dividing the period, `#{m < M : ∀ i ∈ S, n i ∣ L m + c i} = M / ∏_{i ∈ S} n i`.

declarations.name: crtFreq_dvd_linear_family
declarations.signature: theorem crtFreq_dvd_linear_family {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {M L : ℕ} (S : Finset ι) (n c : ι → ℕ) (hn : ∀ i ∈ S, 0 < n i) (hcopL : ∀ i ∈ S, Nat.Coprime (n i) L) (hcop : ∀ i ∈ S, ∀ j ∈ S, i ≠ j → Nat.Coprime (n i) (n j)) (hdvd : (∏ i ∈ S, n i) ∣ M) : ((((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => ∀ i ∈ S, n i ∣ L * m + c i)).card : ℕ) : ℝ) = ((Finset.range M).card : ℝ) * (1 / ((∏ i ∈ S, n i : ℕ) : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: The same count as a frequency, in the shape the second-moment estimate of `ArithmeticCounterexampleChebyshev.lean` consumes.

declarations.name: ParentTagData
declarations.docstring: The paper's labelled-pair data `𝓘_q` for one parent prime `q`: a finite index set of pairs, each carrying its modulus `d p` and its tag prime `p`, with the separation properties the construction arranges — "every tag prime occurs in just one labelled pair", the tag sets are disjoint from `𝓑` and from `P`, and the parent primes exceed `L`.

declarations.name: frame
declarations.docstring: The paper's `F_q = { q · lcm{ d p : (d,p) ∈ I } : I ⊆ 𝓘_q }`, with the least common multiple of the empty set equal to one.

declarations.name: tagCount
declarations.docstring: The paper's `Z_q(n) = ∑_{(d,p) ∈ 𝓘_q} 1_{d p ∣ n}`.

declarations.name: coprime_parent_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem coprime_parent_lcm {I : Finset ℕ} (hI : I ⊆ P.idx) : Nat.Coprime P.parent (I.lcm P.modulus)

declarations.name: mem_dvd_iff
declarations.signature: theorem mem_dvd_iff {I : Finset ℕ} (hI : I ⊆ P.idx) (n : ℕ) : P.parent * I.lcm P.modulus ∣ n ↔ P.parent ∣ n ∧ ∀ i ∈ I, P.modulus i ∣ n
declarations.docstring: The paper's "when `q ∣ n`, a selected least common multiple divides `n` exactly when every selected pair does".

declarations.name: tag_dvd_iff
declarations.signature: theorem tag_dvd_iff {I : Finset ℕ} (hI : I ⊆ P.idx) {i : ℕ} (hi : i ∈ P.idx) : P.tag i ∣ P.parent * I.lcm P.modulus ↔ i ∈ I
declarations.docstring: "Every tag prime occurs in just one labelled pair. Its presence in the least common multiple therefore recovers whether that pair was selected."

declarations.name: frameMap_injOn
declarations.signature: theorem frameMap_injOn : Set.InjOn (fun I : Finset ℕ => P.parent * I.lcm P.modulus) (P.idx.powerset : Set (Finset ℕ))
declarations.docstring: "Hence different subsets give distinct exponents."

declarations.name: incidenceCount_frame
declarations.signature: theorem incidenceCount_frame (n : ℕ) : incidenceCount P.frame n = if P.parent ∣ n then 2 ^ P.tagCount n else 0
declarations.docstring: The paper's exact identity `f_{F_q}(n) = 1_{q ∣ n} 2^{Z_q(n)}`.

declarations.name: parent_mem_frame
declarations.docstring: `q` itself belongs to `F_q`: "later positive terms, for example those supplied by the exponent `q ∈ F_q`".

declarations.name: parent_mul_modulus_mem_frame
declarations.signature: theorem parent_mul_modulus_mem_frame {i : ℕ} (hi : i ∈ P.idx) : P.parent * P.modulus i ∈ P.frame
declarations.docstring: Each `q d p` belongs to `F_q`, so every modulus of the logarithmic majorant below divides `lcm(F_q)`.

declarations.name: parent_dvd_of_mem_frame
declarations.signature: theorem parent_dvd_of_mem_frame {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ P.frame) : P.parent ∣ a
declarations.docstring: Every exponent of `F_q` is a multiple of `q`; in particular all of them exceed `max {L, A₀}` once `q` does.

declarations.name: pos_of_mem_frame
declarations.signature: theorem pos_of_mem_frame {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ P.frame) : 0 < a

declarations.name: dvd_parent_mul_prod
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_parent_mul_prod {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ P.frame) : a ∣ P.parent * ∏ i ∈ P.idx, P.modulus i
declarations.docstring: Every exponent divides `q ∏_{(d,p) ∈ 𝓘_q} d p`, so "all exponents are squarefree" whenever that single product is.

declarations.name: squarefree_of_mem_frame
declarations.signature: theorem squarefree_of_mem_frame (hsq : Squarefree (P.parent * ∏ i ∈ P.idx, P.modulus i)) {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ P.frame) : Squarefree a

declarations.name: log_one_add_incidenceCount_le
declarations.signature: theorem log_one_add_incidenceCount_le (n : ℕ) : Real.log (1 + (incidenceCount P.frame n : ℝ)) ≤ Real.log 2 * ((if P.parent ∣ n then (1 : ℝ) else 0) + ∑ i ∈ P.idx, (if P.parent * P.modulus i ∣ n then (1 : ℝ) else 0))
declarations.docstring: The paper's majorant `log(1 + f_{F_q}(n)) ≤ (log 2)(1_{q ∣ n} + ∑_{(d,p) ∈ 𝓘_q} 1_{q d p ∣ n})`.

declarations.name: majorantCost
declarations.docstring: The paper's cost `(log 2 / q)(1 + ∑_{(d,p) ∈ 𝓘_q} 1/(d p))` of the majorant of `log(1 + f_{F_q})`, which for the constructed tag sets is `(log 2 / q)(1 + ∑_{d ∣ L} S_{q,d}/d)`.

declarations.name: modulus_injOn
declarations.signature: theorem modulus_injOn : Set.InjOn P.modulus (P.idx : Set ℕ)
declarations.docstring: The moduli of the majorant are pairwise distinct: the parent `q` is not one of the `q d p`, and distinct labelled pairs have distinct moduli because a tag prime divides its own modulus and no other.

declarations.name: parent_ne_parent_mul_modulus
declarations.signature: theorem parent_ne_parent_mul_modulus {i : ℕ} (hi : i ∈ P.idx) : P.parent ≠ P.parent * P.modulus i

declarations.name: majorantCost_le
declarations.signature: theorem majorantCost_le {c : ℝ} (hc : (∑ i ∈ P.idx, 1 / (P.modulus i : ℝ)) ≤ c) : P.majorantCost ≤ Real.log 2 / P.parent * (1 + c)
declarations.docstring: The paper's cost bound `(log 2 / q)(1 + ∑_{d ∣ L} S_{q,d}/d) ≤ (log 2/q)(1 + 5D/H)` in the form used: any uniform bound on the modulus reciprocal sum transfers.

declarations.name: majorantSupport
declarations.docstring: The moduli of the paper's majorant of `log(1 + f_{F_q})`: the parent `q` itself and the `q d p`.

declarations.name: mul_modulus_injOn
declarations.signature: theorem mul_modulus_injOn (Q : ParentTagData) : Set.InjOn (fun i => Q.parent * Q.modulus i) (Q.idx : Set ℕ)

declarations.name: parent_notMem_image
declarations.signature: theorem parent_notMem_image (Q : ParentTagData) : Q.parent ∉ Q.idx.image (fun i => Q.parent * Q.modulus i)

declarations.name: sum_majorantSupport
declarations.signature: theorem sum_majorantSupport (Q : ParentTagData) (g : ℕ → ℝ) : ∑ d ∈ majorantSupport Q, g d = g Q.parent + ∑ i ∈ Q.idx, g (Q.parent * Q.modulus i)

declarations.name: majorantSupport_subset_frame
declarations.signature: theorem majorantSupport_subset_frame (Q : ParentTagData) : majorantSupport Q ⊆ Q.frame

declarations.name: cost_majorantSupport
declarations.signature: theorem cost_majorantSupport (Q : ParentTagData) : ∑ d ∈ majorantSupport Q, Real.log 2 / (d : ℝ) = Q.majorantCost
declarations.docstring: The cost of the paper's majorant for one parent is `(log 2 / q)(1 + ∑_{(d,p) ∈ 𝓘_q} 1/(d p))`.

declarations.name: sum_majorantSupport_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem sum_majorantSupport_dvd (Q : ParentTagData) (s : ℕ) : ∑ d ∈ majorantSupport Q, (if d ∣ s then Real.log 2 else 0) = Real.log 2 * ((if Q.parent ∣ s then (1 : ℝ) else 0) + ∑ i ∈ Q.idx, (if Q.parent * Q.modulus i ∣ s then (1 : ℝ) else 0))

declarations.name: totalCoefficient
declarations.signature: def totalCoefficient (B : Finset ℕ) (P : ℕ → ParentTagData) (d : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The summed majorant coefficients of the whole support.

declarations.name: totalCoefficient_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem totalCoefficient_nonneg (B : Finset ℕ) (P : ℕ → ParentTagData) (d : ℕ) : 0 ≤ totalCoefficient B P d

declarations.name: sum_divisors_totalCoefficient
declarations.signature: theorem sum_divisors_totalCoefficient (B : Finset ℕ) (P : ℕ → ParentTagData) {s : ℕ} (hs : 0 < s) : ∑ d ∈ s.divisors, totalCoefficient B P d = ∑ q ∈ B, ∑ d ∈ majorantSupport (P q), (if d ∣ s then Real.log 2 else 0)

declarations.name: divisorMajorantCost_totalCoefficient
declarations.signature: theorem divisorMajorantCost_totalCoefficient (B : Finset ℕ) (P : ℕ → ParentTagData) (D : Finset ℕ) (hsub : ∀ q ∈ B, majorantSupport (P q) ⊆ D) : divisorMajorantCost D (totalCoefficient B P) = ∑ q ∈ B, (P q).majorantCost

declarations.name: log_one_add_sum_le
declarations.signature: theorem log_one_add_sum_le (B : Finset ℕ) (x : ℕ → ℝ) (hx : ∀ q ∈ B, 0 ≤ x q) : Real.log (1 + ∑ q ∈ B, x q) ≤ ∑ q ∈ B, Real.log (1 + x q)
declarations.docstring: The paper's `log(1 + ∑_q x_q) ≤ ∑_q log(1 + x_q)` for `x_q ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: incidenceCount_biUnion
declarations.signature: theorem incidenceCount_biUnion (B : Finset ℕ) (G : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (hdisj : ∀ i ∈ B, ∀ j ∈ B, i ≠ j → Disjoint (G i) (G j)) (n : ℕ) : incidenceCount (B.biUnion G) n = ∑ q ∈ B, incidenceCount (G q) n
declarations.docstring: "Different parent primes give disjoint sets", so `f_F = ∑_q f_{F_q}`.

declarations.name: logMajorantCosts_bddBelow
declarations.signature: theorem logMajorantCosts_bddBelow (F : Finset ℕ) (t : ℝ) : BddBelow (logMajorantCosts F t)

declarations.name: kappaOne_biUnion_frame_le
declarations.signature: theorem kappaOne_biUnion_frame_le (B : Finset ℕ) (P : ℕ → ParentTagData) (hdisj : ∀ i ∈ B, ∀ j ∈ B, i ≠ j → Disjoint (P i).frame (P j).frame) : kappaOne (B.biUnion fun q => (P q).frame) 1 ≤ ∑ q ∈ B, (P q).majorantCost
declarations.docstring: The paper's cost estimate for the whole support: `κ₁(F;1) ≤ ∑_{q ∈ 𝓑} (log 2 / q)(1 + ∑_{(d,p) ∈ 𝓘_q} 1/(d p))`, which for the constructed tag sets is `≤ (5 log 2 / D)(1 + 5D/H) ≤ 30 log 2/H`. The hypothesis is the paper's "different parent primes give disjoint sets".

declarations.name: card_filter_mod_eq
declarations.signature: theorem card_filter_mod_eq {M a r : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hr : r < a) (hdvd : a ∣ M) : ((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => m % a = r)).card = M / a
declarations.docstring: A residue class modulo `a` meets `{0, …, M-1}` in exactly `M/a` points when `a ∣ M`.

declarations.name: exists_residue_dvd_add
declarations.signature: theorem exists_residue_dvd_add (a c : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) : ∃ r, r < a ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, (a ∣ m + c ↔ m % a = r)
declarations.docstring: The solutions of `a ∣ m + c` form one residue class modulo `a`.

declarations.name: card_filter_dvd_add
declarations.signature: theorem card_filter_dvd_add {M a c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hdvd : a ∣ M) : ((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => a ∣ m + c)).card = M / a
declarations.docstring: The paper's "the event `q ∣ N + r` has probability `1/q`", as a count.

declarations.name: card_filter_dvd_add_pair
declarations.signature: theorem card_filter_dvd_add_pair {M a b c d : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) (hdvd : a * b ∣ M) : ((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => a ∣ m + c ∧ b ∣ m + d)).card = M / (a * b)
declarations.docstring: "Conditional on one such event, the tag-prime events remain independent by the Chinese remainder theorem": two divisibility conditions with coprime moduli merge into one residue class modulo the product.

declarations.name: freq_dvd_add
declarations.signature: theorem freq_dvd_add {M a c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hdvd : a ∣ M) : ((((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => a ∣ m + c)).card : ℕ) : ℝ) = ((Finset.range M).card : ℝ) * (1 / (a : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: `ℙ(a ∣ m + c) = 1/a` over a full period.

declarations.name: freq_dvd_add_pair
declarations.signature: theorem freq_dvd_add_pair {M a b c d : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) (hdvd : a * b ∣ M) : ((((Finset.range M).filter (fun m => a ∣ m + c ∧ b ∣ m + d)).card : ℕ) : ℝ) = ((Finset.range M).card : ℝ) * ((1 / (a : ℝ)) * (1 / (b : ℝ)))
declarations.docstring: `ℙ(a ∣ m + c and b ∣ m + d) = (1/a)(1/b)` over a full period, for coprime `a` and `b`.

declarations.name: exp_half_le_one_add
declarations.signature: theorem exp_half_le_one_add {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x ≤ 1) : Real.exp (x / 2) ≤ 1 + x

declarations.name: half_le_log_one_add
declarations.signature: theorem half_le_log_one_add {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x ≤ 1) : x / 2 ≤ Real.log (1 + x)
declarations.docstring: The paper's `log(1 + 1/p) ≥ 1/(2p)`, in the general form `log(1 + x) ≥ x/2` for `0 ≤ x ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: FreshPrime
declarations.signature: def FreshPrime (b : ℕ) (E : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The paper's admissibility condition for each successive prime selection: a prime above a cutoff `b` and outside the finite set `E` of primes already used.

declarations.name: decidableFreshPrime
declarations.signature: instance decidableFreshPrime (b : ℕ) (E : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) : Decidable (FreshPrime b E n)

declarations.name: not_summable_freshPrime_inv
declarations.signature: theorem not_summable_freshPrime_inv (b : ℕ) (E : Finset ℕ) : ¬ Summable (fun n : ℕ => if FreshPrime b E n then (1 : ℝ) / n else 0)
declarations.docstring: "Divergence of the prime reciprocal sum after any finite cutoff": excluding an initial segment and a finite set leaves a divergent reciprocal sum.

declarations.name: exists_freshPrimes_sum_inv_ge_le
declarations.signature: theorem exists_freshPrimes_sum_inv_ge_le (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (E : Finset ℕ) (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 ≤ a) : ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime ∧ b < p ∧ p ∉ E) ∧ a ≤ ∑ p ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / p ∧ ∑ p ∈ S, (1 : ℝ) / p ≤ a + 1 / b
declarations.docstring: The paper's stopping argument, in the form both of its prime selections use: for every target `a ≥ 0`, every cutoff `b ≥ 1` and every finite set `E` of primes already used, there is a finite set `S` of primes, all greater than `b` and none in `E`, whose reciprocal sum first crosses `a`, so that `a ≤ ∑_{p ∈ S} 1/p ≤ a + 1/b`, "the overshoot" being at most the reciprocal of the cutoff.

declarations.name: exists_freshPrimes_family
declarations.signature: theorem exists_freshPrimes_family {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (target : ι → ℝ) (htarget : ∀ j, 0 ≤ target j) (J : Finset ι) : ∀ E : Finset ℕ, ∃ S : ι → Finset ℕ, (∀ j ∈ J, ∀ p ∈ S j, p.Prime ∧ b < p ∧ p ∉ E) ∧ (∀ j ∈ J, ∀ j' ∈ J, j ≠ j' → Disjoint (S j) (S j')) ∧ (∀ j ∈ J, target j ≤ ∑ p ∈ S j, (1 : ℝ) / p) ∧ (∀ j ∈ J, ∑ p ∈ S j, (1 : ℝ) / p ≤ target j + 1 / b)
declarations.docstring: "The same stopping argument works successively: each new reciprocal is less than `1/H ≤ d/H`, and only finitely many primes have been excluded." The whole family of tag sets `T_{q,d}` at once: pairwise disjoint finite sets of primes, all above the cutoff and outside the finite set already used, each meeting its own target with overshoot at most `1/b`.

declarations.name: exists_freshPrimes_prod_one_add_inv_ge
declarations.signature: theorem exists_freshPrimes_prod_one_add_inv_ge (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (E : Finset ℕ) (Y : ℝ) : ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ S, p.Prime ∧ b < p ∧ p ∉ E) ∧ Y ≤ ∏ p ∈ S, (1 + 1 / (p : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: The paper's first selection: a finite set of primes, above any cutoff and avoiding any finite set already used, with `∏ (1 + 1/p)` at least any target. "Such a set exists because the sum of reciprocal primes diverges and `log(1 + 1/p) ≥ 1/(2p)`."

declarations.name: sigmaRatio
declarations.docstring: The paper's `σ(n)/n`, where `σ` is the sum of positive divisors.

declarations.name: one_le_sigmaRatio
declarations.signature: theorem one_le_sigmaRatio {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : 1 ≤ sigmaRatio n

declarations.name: sigmaRatio_pos
declarations.signature: theorem sigmaRatio_pos {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : 0 < sigmaRatio n

declarations.name: sigmaRatio_mul
declarations.signature: theorem sigmaRatio_mul {m n : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hn : 0 < n) (h : Nat.Coprime m n) : sigmaRatio (m * n) = sigmaRatio m * sigmaRatio n
declarations.docstring: `σ(n)/n` is multiplicative on coprime arguments.

declarations.name: sigmaRatio_mul_complement
declarations.signature: theorem sigmaRatio_mul_complement {L r : ℕ} (hL : Squarefree L) (hL0 : 0 < L) (hr : r ∣ L) : sigmaRatio r * sigmaRatio (L / r) = sigmaRatio L
declarations.docstring: The paper's `σ(r)/r · σ(L/r)/(L/r) = B` for `r ∣ L` and `L` squarefree.

declarations.name: primeProd
declarations.docstring: The paper's `L = ∏_{p ∈ P} p`.

declarations.name: primeProd_pos
declarations.signature: theorem primeProd_pos {P : Finset ℕ} (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) : 0 < primeProd P

declarations.name: coprime_primeProd
declarations.signature: theorem coprime_primeProd {P : Finset ℕ} (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hnot : p ∉ P) : Nat.Coprime p (primeProd P)

declarations.name: primeProd_squarefree
declarations.signature: theorem primeProd_squarefree {P : Finset ℕ} (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) : Squarefree (primeProd P)

declarations.name: sigmaRatio_prime
declarations.signature: theorem sigmaRatio_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : sigmaRatio p = 1 + 1 / (p : ℝ)

declarations.name: sigmaRatio_primeProd
declarations.signature: theorem sigmaRatio_primeProd {P : Finset ℕ} (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) : sigmaRatio (primeProd P) = ∏ p ∈ P, (1 + 1 / (p : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: The paper's `B = ∏_{p ∈ P}(1 + 1/p)` is `σ(L)/L`.

declarations.name: card_divisors_primeProd
declarations.signature: theorem card_divisors_primeProd {P : Finset ℕ} (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) : (primeProd P).divisors.card = 2 ^ P.card
declarations.docstring: The paper's `D = τ(L) = 2^{|P|}`.

declarations.name: sigmaRatio_primeProd_le_card_divisors
declarations.signature: theorem sigmaRatio_primeProd_le_card_divisors {P : Finset ℕ} (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) : sigmaRatio (primeProd P) ≤ ((primeProd P).divisors.card : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The paper's "also `D ≥ B`".

declarations.name: bigRatioDivisors
declarations.signature: def bigRatioDivisors (L : ℕ) (Hr : ℝ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.docstring: The paper's `G = {r ∣ L : σ(r)/r ≥ H}`.

declarations.name: mem_bigRatioDivisors
declarations.signature: theorem mem_bigRatioDivisors {L : ℕ} {Hr : ℝ} {r : ℕ} : r ∈ bigRatioDivisors L Hr ↔ r ∈ L.divisors ∧ Hr ≤ sigmaRatio r

declarations.name: bigRatioDivisors_subset
declarations.signature: theorem bigRatioDivisors_subset (L : ℕ) (Hr : ℝ) : bigRatioDivisors L Hr ⊆ L.divisors

declarations.name: card_divisors_le_two_mul_card_bigRatioDivisors
declarations.signature: theorem card_divisors_le_two_mul_card_bigRatioDivisors {L : ℕ} (hL : Squarefree L) (hL0 : 0 < L) {Hr : ℝ} (hHr : 0 < Hr) (hB : Hr * Hr ≤ sigmaRatio L) : L.divisors.card ≤ 2 * (bigRatioDivisors L Hr).card
declarations.docstring: The paper's "thus the set `G = {r ∣ L : σ(r)/r ≥ H}` has at least `D/2` elements", given `B = σ(L)/L ≥ H²`. The complementary divisor `L/r` of a divisor outside `G` lies in `G`, and `r ↦ L/r` is injective on divisors.

declarations.name: TagFamily
declarations.docstring: The tag data selected for one parent prime `q`: for each divisor `d` of `L` a finite set `T_{q,d}` of tag primes, pairwise disjoint as `d` varies, none dividing `L` and none equal to the parent, with the parent above `L`.

declarations.name: tagIndex
declarations.docstring: The paper's `𝓘_q`, indexed by the tag prime itself.

declarations.name: tagModulus
declarations.docstring: The modulus `d p` of the labelled pair carrying the tag prime `p`.

declarations.name: mem_tagIndex_iff
declarations.signature: theorem mem_tagIndex_iff {p : ℕ} : p ∈ T.tagIndex ↔ ∃ d ∈ T.L.divisors, p ∈ T.tags d

declarations.name: tagModulus_eq
declarations.signature: theorem tagModulus_eq {d p : ℕ} (hd : d ∈ T.L.divisors) (hp : p ∈ T.tags d) : T.tagModulus p = d * p
declarations.docstring: "Every tag prime occurs in just one labelled pair": the disjointness of the tag sets makes `p` determine `d`.

declarations.name: tagIndex_prime
declarations.signature: theorem tagIndex_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : p ∈ T.tagIndex) : p.Prime

declarations.name: tagModulus_pos
declarations.signature: theorem tagModulus_pos {p : ℕ} (hp : p ∈ T.tagIndex) : 0 < T.tagModulus p

declarations.name: toParentTagData
declarations.docstring: The `ParentTagData` of one parent group, with the tag prime as the index of its labelled pair.

declarations.name: sum_inv_tagModulus
declarations.signature: theorem sum_inv_tagModulus : (∑ p ∈ T.tagIndex, 1 / (T.tagModulus p : ℝ)) = ∑ d ∈ T.L.divisors, (1 / (d : ℝ)) * ∑ p ∈ T.tags d, 1 / (p : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The cost input: `∑_{(d,p) ∈ 𝓘_q} 1/(d p) = ∑_{d ∣ L} S_{q,d}/d`.

declarations.name: parent_le_of_mem_frame
declarations.signature: theorem parent_le_of_mem_frame {a : ℕ} (ha : a ∈ T.toParentTagData.frame) : T.parent ≤ a
declarations.docstring: "Their minimum is greater than `max{L, A₀}`": every exponent of `F_q` is a positive multiple of the parent prime.

declarations.name: periodicMean_sub_le
declarations.signature: theorem periodicMean_sub_le (v : ℕ → ℝ) (P : ℕ) (hP : 0 < P) (hper : ∀ m, v (m + P) = v m) (hv0 : ∀ m, 0 ≤ v m) (hv1 : ∀ m, v m ≤ 1) (T : ℕ) (hT : 0 < T) : (∑ m ∈ Finset.range P, v m) / (P : ℝ) - (P : ℝ) / (T : ℝ) ≤ (∑ m ∈ Finset.range T, v m) / (T : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A bounded `P`-periodic sequence: its mean over `range T` is below its mean over one period by at most `P/T`. This is the paper's `|T⁻¹ ∑_{m ≤ T} 1_{U_F(Lm) > 1} - p| ≤ P₀/T`, in the one-sided form used.

declarations.name: exceedInd
declarations.signature: def exceedInd (F : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The indicator of the paper's event `{U_F > 1}`.

declarations.name: exceedInd_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem exceedInd_nonneg (F : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ) : 0 ≤ exceedInd F N

declarations.name: exceedInd_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem exceedInd_le_one (F : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ) : exceedInd F N ≤ 1

declarations.name: framePotential_add_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem framePotential_add_lcm (F : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ) : framePotential F (N + F.lcm id) = framePotential F N
declarations.docstring: `U_F` has period `Q = lcm F`.

declarations.name: condExceedProb
declarations.signature: def condExceedProb (F : Finset ℕ) (ℓ : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The paper's `ℙ_ℓ(U_F > 1)`: uniform sampling of `N = ℓ m` over one period `Q/ℓ` of `m ↦ U_F(ℓ m)`. For `ℓ ∣ Q` the sampled points `ℓ, 2ℓ, …, Q` are a complete set of representatives of the multiples of `ℓ` modulo `Q`, so this is `ℙ(U_F(N) > 1 | ℓ ∣ N)` for `N` uniform modulo `Q`.

declarations.name: condExceedProb_sub_le_dyadicMean
declarations.signature: theorem condExceedProb_sub_le_dyadicMean (F : Finset ℕ) (hF : 0 ∉ F) (ℓ : ℕ) (hℓ0 : 0 < ℓ) (hℓ : ℓ ∣ F.lcm id) (R M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : condExceedProb F ℓ - ((F.lcm id / ℓ : ℕ) : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ R ≤ dyadicMean ℓ R M (exceedInd F)
declarations.docstring: The dyadic observation mean of the indicator is at most `P/2^R` below `ℙ_ℓ(U_F > 1)`.

declarations.name: coverData
declarations.signature: def coverData {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) : PositiveCoverData
declarations.docstring: The fractional-cover data underlying a `LogBudgetCover`.

declarations.name: coverBudget
declarations.signature: def coverBudget {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) (j : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The paper's `j`-th cost term `C_j η_j^{-α_j}/(2^{α_j} - 1)`.

declarations.name: scaledCoverPotential
declarations.signature: def scaledCoverPotential {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) (j N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The paper's `j`-th pointwise majorant `η_j^{-α_j} V_j(N)`.

declarations.name: coverBudget_summable
declarations.signature: theorem coverBudget_summable {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) : Summable (coverBudget C)

declarations.name: cost_eq_tsum_coverBudget
declarations.signature: theorem cost_eq_tsum_coverBudget {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) : C.cost = ∑' j, coverBudget C j

declarations.name: scaledCoverPotential_eq
declarations.signature: theorem scaledCoverPotential_eq {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) (j N : ℕ) : scaledCoverPotential C j N = (C.weight j ^ C.exponent j)⁻¹ * coverPotential (coverData C) j N

declarations.name: scaledCoverPotential_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem scaledCoverPotential_nonneg {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) (j N : ℕ) : 0 ≤ scaledCoverPotential C j N

declarations.name: coverBudget_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem coverBudget_nonneg {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) (j : ℕ) : 0 ≤ coverBudget C j

declarations.name: scaled_cost_eq
declarations.signature: theorem scaled_cost_eq {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) (j : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : (C.weight j ^ C.exponent j)⁻¹ * (x * ((coverData C).cost j / (coverBase (coverData C) j - 1))) = x * coverBudget C j
declarations.docstring: Rewriting the scaled column cost as the paper's budget term.

declarations.name: scaledCoverPotential_le
declarations.signature: theorem scaledCoverPotential_le {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) (j N : ℕ) : scaledCoverPotential C j N ≤ (2 * (N : ℝ) + 1) * coverBudget C j

declarations.name: summable_scaledCoverPotential
declarations.signature: theorem summable_scaledCoverPotential {A : Set ℕ} (C : LogBudgetCover A) (N : ℕ) : Summable (fun j => scaledCoverPotential C j N)

declarations.name: framePotential_le_sum_frames
declarations.signature: theorem framePotential_le_sum_frames (F J : Finset ℕ) (G : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (hcover : F ⊆ J.biUnion G) (N : ℕ) : framePotential F N ≤ ∑ j ∈ J, framePotential (G j) N
declarations.docstring: `U_F ≤ ∑_{j ∈ J} U_{F_j}` for a finite subcover.

declarations.name: exists_frame_gt_weight
declarations.signature: theorem exists_frame_gt_weight (F : Finset ℕ) (C : LogBudgetCover (F : Set ℕ)) (N : ℕ) (hgt : 1 < framePotential F N) : ∃ j, C.weight j < framePotential (C.frame j) N

declarations.name: balancedPulseFamily
declarations.docstring: The displayed balanced-pulse family at location `m`: the coefficient sequences `balancedPulseCoeff m r` for the admissible parameters `0 ≤ r ≤ balancedPulseRadius m`. These are exactly the parameters for which the pulse is mass preserving and stays in the linear-growth class (`balancedPulseCoeff_le_self`).

declarations.name: radius_eq
declarations.signature: private theorem radius_eq (m : ℕ) : balancedPulseRadius m = (m + 1) / 2
declarations.docstring: The radius is the manuscript's `⌊(m+1)/2⌋`.

declarations.name: balancedPulseCoeff_injective
declarations.docstring: Distinct pulse parameters give distinct members: the right site already separates them, since `balancedPulseCoeff m r (m+1) = 2r`.

declarations.name: paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_is_radius_succ
declarations.signature: theorem paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_is_radius_succ (m : ℕ) : (balancedPulseFamily m).ncard = balancedPulseRadius m + 1 ∧ (balancedPulseFamily m).ncard = (m + 1) / 2 + 1
declarations.docstring: **The exact fan-out.** The balanced-pulse family at location `m` has exactly `balancedPulseRadius m + 1 = ⌊(m+1)/2⌋ + 1` members.

declarations.name: paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_floor_bound_fails_at_even
declarations.signature: theorem paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_floor_bound_fails_at_even (k : ℕ) : (balancedPulseFamily (2 * k)).ncard = k + 1 ∧ ¬ (2 * k / 2 + 2 ≤ (balancedPulseFamily (2 * k)).ncard)
declarations.docstring: **The defect.** At every even location `m = 2k` the family has exactly `k + 1` members, so the manuscript's parenthetical lower bound `⌊m/2⌋ + 2 = k + 2` fails: it is one too large.

declarations.name: paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_floor_bound_sharp_at_odd
declarations.docstring: At every odd location `m = 2k+1` the family has exactly `k + 2` members, which is the manuscript's `⌊m/2⌋ + 2`; there the parenthetical constant is correct, and attained with equality.

declarations.name: paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_unbounded_corrected
declarations.signature: theorem paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_unbounded_corrected : (∀ m : ℕ, m / 2 + 1 ≤ (balancedPulseFamily m).ncard) ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, N ≤ (balancedPulseFamily m).ncard
declarations.docstring: The corrected fan-out statement, in the manuscript's "unbounded" form: the fan-out at `m` is `⌊(m+1)/2⌋ + 1`, it never drops below `⌊m/2⌋ + 1`, and it exceeds every `N` for suitable `m`.

declarations.name: paper_pulse_family_no_autonomous_decoder
declarations.signature: theorem paper_pulse_family_no_autonomous_decoder {State : Type*} (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (state : Fin (balancedPulseRadius m + 1) → State) (hstate : ∀ r, state r = state ⟨0,
declarations.docstring: `prop:finite-state-nogo`, decoder clause. For a balanced-pulse family at location `m ≥ 2`, a predecessor state constant across the family admits no function `decode : State → ℕ` recovering the parameter `r` from `state r` for every `r`.

declarations.name: paper_pulse_family_finite_state_card
declarations.signature: theorem paper_pulse_family_finite_state_card {m : ℕ} {State : Type*} [Fintype State] (state : Fin (balancedPulseRadius m + 1) → State) (decode : State → ℕ) (hdecode : ∀ r, decode (state r) = r) : balancedPulseRadius m + 1 ≤ Fintype.card State ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ m' : ℕ, N ≤ balancedPulseRadius m' + 1
declarations.docstring: `prop:finite-state-nogo`, cardinality clause. A finite state type carrying an exact decoder for the family at `m` has at least `balancedPulseRadius m + 1` elements, and that quantity is unbounded in `m`.

declarations.name: paper_upper_branch_needs_no_exceptional_cell
declarations.signature: theorem paper_upper_branch_needs_no_exceptional_cell {s : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hcarry : (seamAdjacentCut s hs).successorCarries) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) ≤ 2 ^ (s + 1) ∧ 0 ≤ 4 * (seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot + (seamAdjacentCut s hs).abovePulse ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + (4 * (seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot + (seamAdjacentCut s hs).abovePulse) = 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: Long `prop:upper-unconditional`. Both asserted clauses at a row `s ≥ 5` whose adjacent cut carries: the next remainder is at most `2^(s+1)`, and the reset identity expresses `2^(s+1)` as that remainder plus the (nonnegative) reset charge `4 * overshoot + abovePulse`.

declarations.name: paper_final_middle_cell_at_least_neg_two
declarations.signature: theorem paper_final_middle_cell_at_least_neg_two (D : ℕ) (hD13 : 13 ≤ D) (hncarry : ¬ (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).successorCarries) (hmiddle : 4 * (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder + (seamPerturbedFamily D (by omega)).gap - (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse < (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).terminalWeight) (hright : ∀ s : ℕ, D + 1 ≤ s → seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true) : (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse + 2 ≤ 4 * (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder ∧ (-2 : ℤ) ≤ 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 ∧
declarations.docstring: Long `thm:cd-neg3-impossible`, all three asserted clauses. Hypotheses: a middle transition at row `D ≥ 13` (no carry, plus the middle-branch inequality) followed by an all-right tail. Conclusions: the displayed bound `belowPulse D + 2 ≤ 4 * rem D`; equivalently `-2 ≤ C_D`; hence `C_D ≠ -3`, and with it every more negative value.

declarations.name: paper_final_middle_cell_remaining_cells
declarations.signature: theorem paper_final_middle_cell_remaining_cells (D : ℕ) (hD13 : 13 ≤ D) (hncarry : ¬ (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).successorCarries) (hmiddle : 4 * (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder + (seamPerturbedFamily D (by omega)).gap - (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse < (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).terminalWeight) (hright : ∀ s : ℕ, D + 1 ≤ s → seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true) : (4 * ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 = -3 ∨ 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 = -2 ∨
declarations.docstring: Long `cor:cd-remaining`. Under the same final-middle hypotheses, the exclusion of `-3` leaves exactly `-2` and `-1` inside the exceptional set `{-3, -2, -1}`. The statement is the implication: it does not assert that `C_D` lies in that set, since nonnegative values are not excluded.

declarations.name: paper_centred_completion_of_fixed_precision
declarations.signature: theorem paper_centred_completion_of_fixed_precision (u : ℕ) (hu : 1 ≤ u) (m : ℕ) (v : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ℕ → ℤ) (hodd : ∀ i, i < m → Odd (a i)) (e₀ : ℤ) : ∃ e z : ℕ → ℤ, e 0 = e₀ ∧ ∀ i, i < m → e (i + 1) = 2 * e i + 2 ^ (v i) * (a i + 2 ^ u * z i) ∧ |e (i + 1)| ≤ 2 ^ (v i + u - 1)
declarations.docstring: Long `prop:2adic-nogo`, in the manuscript's indexed form. Fix `u ≥ 1` and a finite list of valuations `v i` and odd units `a i`, `i < m`. For every initial integer `e 0 = e₀` there are integers `z i` and successors `e (i+1)` with `e (i+1) = 2 * e i + 2 ^ (v i) * (a i + 2 ^ u * z i)` and `|e (i+1)| ≤ 2 ^ (v i + u - 1)`.

declarations.name: paper_one_sided_finite_decision_boundary
declarations.signature: theorem paper_one_sided_finite_decision_boundary : (∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ mersenneAchievementSet ↔ 0 ≤ x ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, greedyMersenneRemainder x n ≤ mersenneTail n) ∧ (∀ x : ℝ, (∃ n : ℕ, mersenneTail n < greedyMersenneRemainder x n) → x ∉ mersenneAchievementSet) ∧ (∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ mersenneAchievementSet → ∀ n : ℕ, greedyMersenneRemainder x n ≤ mersenneTail n)
declarations.docstring: Long untitled Theorem C (line 7153), its three mathematical clauses. The checked equivalence; a fatal greedy state at a finite rank is a certificate of nonmembership; membership requires survival at every rank.

declarations.name: paper_balanced_pulse_no_autonomous_decoder
declarations.signature: theorem paper_balanced_pulse_no_autonomous_decoder {State : Type*} (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (state : Fin (balancedPulseRadius m + 1) → State) (hstate : ∀ r, state r = state ⟨0,
declarations.docstring: Long `prop:finite-state-nogo`, decoder clause. For a balanced-pulse family at location `m ≥ 2` with radius `(m+1)/2`, a predecessor state that is constant across the family admits no function `decode : State → ℕ` recovering the parameter `r` from `state r` for every `r`.

declarations.name: paper_balanced_pulse_finite_state_card
declarations.signature: theorem paper_balanced_pulse_finite_state_card {m : ℕ} {State : Type*} [Fintype State] (state : Fin (balancedPulseRadius m + 1) → State) (decode : State → ℕ) (hdecode : ∀ r, decode (state r) = r) : balancedPulseRadius m + 1 ≤ Fintype.card State ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ m' : ℕ, N ≤ balancedPulseRadius m' + 1
declarations.docstring: Long `prop:finite-state-nogo`, cardinality clause. A finite state type carrying an exact decoder for the balanced-pulse family at `m` has at least `balancedPulseRadius m + 1` elements, which is unbounded in `m`.

declarations.name: paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_count
declarations.signature: theorem paper_balanced_pulse_fanout_count (k : ℕ) : balancedPulseRadius (2 * k) + 1 = k + 1 ∧ balancedPulseRadius (2 * k + 1) + 1 = (2 * k + 1) / 2 + 2 ∧ ∀ m : ℕ, m / 2 + 1 ≤ balancedPulseRadius m + 1
declarations.docstring: The exact fan-out of the balanced-pulse family: at `m = 2k` the family has `balancedPulseRadius (2k) + 1 = k + 1` members, so the manuscript's parenthetical lower bound `⌊m/2⌋ + 2 = k + 2` at `m = 2k` is one too large; the bound `⌊m/2⌋ + 2` is the correct count at odd `m = 2k+1`.

declarations.docstring: "The bit condition fixes coordinate `d` from row `2d` onward."

declarations.name: paper_compatible_finite_row_conditions
declarations.signature: theorem paper_compatible_finite_row_conditions (T : BooleanMobiusGlobalRepairTrajectory) : GlobalBooleanMobiusRepairFeasible T ↔ ((∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → 2 ^ (endpointDivisorContribution (globalRepairLowerSupport T.bit n) n - 1) - 1 ≤ localBinarySuffix (globalRepairLowerSupport T.bit n) 1 (n - 1)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ((∑ d ∈ (globalRepairStageSupport T.bit n).filter (fun d ↦ n / 2 < d), 2 ^ (n - d) : ℕ) : ℤ) = localRepairInteger (globalRepairLowerSupport T.bit n) 1 n) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → localRepairInteger (globalRepairLowerSupport T.bit n) 1 n < ((2 ^ (n - n / 2) : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
declarations.docstring: Paper display of `record:257bm-c3`: the feasibility package of the compatible-limit construction is exactly the four conditions on the finite rows, required for every `n ≥ 2`: * `2^(max{c_{D_n}(n)-1,0}) - 1 ≤ S(D_n,1,n-1)`; * `∑_{d ∈ E_n, d > ⌊n/2⌋} 2^(n-d) = H(D_n,1,n)`; * `H(D_n,1,n) < 2^(n-⌊n/2⌋)`; * `Q(E_n,n) = 2^(n-1) - 1`. The maximum in the first line is natural-number subtraction at `c_{D_n}(n) = 0`.

declarations.name: paper_compatible_first_condition_gives_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem paper_compatible_first_condition_gives_nonneg (T : BooleanMobiusGlobalRepairTrajectory) (hbound : ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → 2 ^ (endpointDivisorContribution (globalRepairLowerSupport T.bit n) n - 1) - 1 ≤ localBinarySuffix (globalRepairLowerSupport T.bit n) 1 (n - 1)) {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 0 ≤ localRepairInteger (globalRepairLowerSupport T.bit n) 1 n

declarations.name: paper_compatible_rows_agree_with_limit
declarations.signature: theorem paper_compatible_rows_agree_with_limit (T : BooleanMobiusGlobalRepairTrajectory) {n d : ℕ} (hd : d ≤ n / 2) : d ∈ globalRepairStageSupport T.bit n ↔ d ∈ globalRepairLimitSupport T

declarations.name: paper_critical_band_index_collapse
declarations.signature: theorem paper_critical_band_index_collapse : (∀ d E : ℕ, DyadicBandEscape d E ↔ ∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ d → 2 ^ (d - j + 1) < E ∨ E + 2 * (d + j) ≤ 2 ^ (d - j + 1)) ∧ (∀ d E : ℕ, E ≤ 2 ^ (d + 1) → (DyadicBandEscape d E ↔ ∃ j : ℕ, CriticalDyadicBandIndex d E j ∧ E + 2 * (d + j) ≤ 2 ^ (d - j + 1))) ∧ (∀ d E : ℕ, E ≤ 2 ^ (d + 1) → ∃ j : ℕ, CriticalDyadicBandIndex d E j) ∧ (∀ d E : ℕ, 2 ^ (d + 1) < E → DyadicBandEscape d E) ∧ (∀ d E : ℕ, 2 ^ (d + 1) < E → ¬ ∃ j : ℕ, CriticalDyadicBandIndex d E j) ∧ (2 ^ (0 + 1) < 3 ∧ ∀ d E : ℕ, 2 ^ (d + 1) < E → 0 ≤ d ∧ 3 ≤ E) ∧ (SeamUpperResetCriticalBandEscape ↔ SeamUpperResetDyadicBandEscape)
declarations.docstring: Long `prop:critical-band-index`, every asserted clause.

declarations.name: weighted_denominator_budget
declarations.signature: theorem weighted_denominator_budget (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (S : Finset ℕ) (hS : S ⊆ Finset.Ico 2 n) : Real.logb 2 (((skipSum S).den : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ∑ d ∈ S, Real.logb 2 ((2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1) ∧ (∑ d ∈ S, Real.logb 2 ((2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1)) ≤ ∑ d ∈ S, (d : ℝ) ∧ (∑ d ∈ S, (d : ℝ)) ≤ (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) - 1) / 2 - 1 ∧ (S.Nonempty → (∑ d ∈ S, Real.logb 2 ((2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1)) < ∑ d ∈ S, (d : ℝ)) ∧ (S = ∅ → (∑ d ∈ S, Real.logb 2 ((2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1)) = 0 ∧ (∑ d ∈ S, (d : ℝ)) = 0)

declarations.name: paper_critical_dyadic_band_index_unique
declarations.signature: theorem paper_critical_dyadic_band_index_unique {d E : ℕ} (hE : E ≤ 2 ^ (d + 1)) : ∃! j : ℕ, CriticalDyadicBandIndex d E j

declarations.name: paper_critical_dyadic_boundary_is_smallest
declarations.signature: theorem paper_critical_dyadic_boundary_is_smallest {d E j : ℕ} (hj : CriticalDyadicBandIndex d E j) : E ≤ 2 ^ (d - j + 1) ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ d → E ≤ 2 ^ (d - i + 1) → (2 : ℕ) ^ (d - j + 1) ≤ 2 ^ (d - i + 1)
declarations.docstring: "The boundary `2^(d-j_*+1)` is the smallest power at least `E` among the finite list `2, 4, …, 2^(d+1)`."

declarations.name: paper_critical_dyadic_band_index_eq_top_of_le_two

declarations.name: paper_dyadic_band_escape_iff_single_test
declarations.signature: theorem paper_dyadic_band_escape_iff_single_test {d E j : ℕ} (hj : CriticalDyadicBandIndex d E j) : DyadicBandEscape d E ↔ E + 2 * (d + j) ≤ 2 ^ (d - j + 1)
declarations.docstring: Paper display of `record:257bm-c11`: for `E ≤ 2^(d+1)` and the critical index `j_*`, the universal band family `∀ 0 ≤ j ≤ d, 2^(d-j+1) < E ∨ E + 2(d+j) ≤ 2^(d-j+1)` is equivalent to the single inequality `E + 2(d+j_*) ≤ 2^(d-j_*+1)`.

declarations.name: paper_two_sided_dyadic_bound
declarations.signature: theorem paper_two_sided_dyadic_bound (hescape : SeamTwoSidedDyadicCellEscape) (s : ℕ) (hs : 5 ≤ s) : min (seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s) ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot) ≤ 2 ^ s

declarations.name: paper_halfGreedyPrefixSupport_eq_greedy_inter_Icc

declarations.name: paper_greedyHalfRemainder_ne_dyadicCap

declarations.docstring: At positive depth the greedy half remainder never lands exactly on the next dyadic cap: the reduced excess numerator is odd, hence nonzero. This is the environment's clause "at positive `k`, oddness of the reduced excess numerator excludes equality at zero".

declarations.name: paper_eventual_nonnegative_margin_equivalence

declarations.name: paper_frozen_margin_normalised_value
declarations.signature: theorem paper_frozen_margin_normalised_value (k J : ℕ) : (greedyHalfFrozenMargin k J : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ J = (∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 J, (supportCoeff (↑(halfGreedyPrefixSupport k) : Set ℕ) (k + 1 + i) : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ i) - (mobiusCenteredHalfCarry (↑(halfGreedyPrefixSupport k) : Set ℕ) k : ℝ)

declarations.name: paper_frozen_margin_normalised_monotone

declarations.docstring: The environment's monotonicity clause: the normalised expression, not necessarily `F_k(J)` itself, is nondecreasing in `J`.

declarations.name: paper_eta_eq_coeffTail_sub_carry
declarations.signature: theorem paper_eta_eq_coeffTail_sub_carry (k : ℕ) : 1 - (2 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) k = binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff (↑(halfGreedyPrefixSupport k) : Set ℕ)) (k + 1) - (mobiusCenteredHalfCarry (↑(halfGreedyPrefixSupport k) : Set ℕ) k : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The finite-support Lambert identity in carry coordinates: the quantity `η = 1 - 2^(k+1) r_k(1/2)` is the complete coefficient tail of `D` after row `k+1` minus the centred carry `C_D(k)`.

declarations.name: paper_frozen_margin_normalised_tendsto
declarations.signature: theorem paper_frozen_margin_normalised_tendsto (k : ℕ) : Tendsto (fun J : ℕ ↦ (greedyHalfFrozenMargin k J : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ J) atTop (nhds (1 - (2 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) k))
declarations.docstring: The environment's limit clause: the normalised expression converges to `1 - 2^(k+1) r_k(1/2)`.

declarations.name: paper_frozen_margin_limit_pos_iff
declarations.signature: theorem paper_frozen_margin_limit_pos_iff (k : ℕ) : 0 < 1 - (2 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) k ↔ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) k < halfDyadicCap (k + 1)
declarations.docstring: The environment's positivity clause: the limit is positive exactly under the strict dyadic inequality `r_k(1/2) < 2^(-(k+1))`.

declarations.name: paper_coeffTail_le_index_add_two
declarations.signature: theorem paper_coeffTail_le_index_add_two (A : Set ℕ) (m : ℕ) : binaryCoeffTail (supportCoeff A) m ≤ (m : ℝ) + 2
declarations.docstring: The environment's tail bound `∑_{r≥1} c_D(m+r) 2^(-r) ≤ m + 2`. It holds for every support, in particular for the finite support `D`: the divisor count `c_A(n)` never exceeds `n`, and a coefficient sequence of at most linear growth has this uniform dyadic tail bound.

declarations.name: paper_effective_horizon_test
declarations.signature: theorem paper_effective_horizon_test (k J : ℕ) (heta : 0 < 1 - (2 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) k) (htest : ((k + J + 3 : ℕ) : ℝ) / (2 : ℝ) ^ J < 1 - (2 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) * greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) k) : 0 < greedyHalfFrozenMargin k J
declarations.docstring: The environment's effective sufficient test. Write `η = 1 - 2^(k+1) r_k(1/2) > 0`. Since the omitted tail after row `k+1+J` is at most `k+J+3`, the inequality `(k+J+3) 2^(-J) < η` forces `F_k(J) > 0`.

declarations.name: paper_eta_hasRationalValue

declarations.name: paper_exact_row_example_six_and_eleven
declarations.signature: theorem paper_exact_row_example_six_and_eleven : localPrefixQuotient ({2, 3, 6} : Finset ℕ) 6 = 2 ^ (6 - 1) - 1 ∧ ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow 6 ∧ localPrefixQuotient ({2, 3, 6, 7, 11} : Finset ℕ) 11 = 2 ^ (11 - 1) - 1 ∧ ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow (2 * 6 - 1) ∧ (4 ≤ 4 ∧ 4 ≤ 6 ∧ ExactLocalMersenneHalfRow (2 * 4 - 2)) ∧ 2 * 4 - 2 = 6
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-k-dich`, the worked example at `n = 6`. The support `{2,3,6}` is an exact row at depth `6`; `{2,3,6,7,11}` is an exact row at depth `11 = 2·6 - 1`; and the second conclusion also holds with `c = 4`, whose returned depth `2c - 2 = 6` is exactly the original depth, so it allows no depth increase.

declarations.name: paper_bounded_double_or_recycle_countermodel
declarations.signature: theorem paper_bounded_double_or_recycle_countermodel : (∀ n : ℕ, boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel n ↔ n = 6) ∧ boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel 6 ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 6 ≤ n → boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel n → boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel (2 * n - 1) ∨ ∃ c : ℕ, 4 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ n ∧ boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel (2 * c - 2)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 6 ≤ n → boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel n → 4 ≤ 4 ∧ 4 ≤ n ∧ boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel (2 * 4 - 2)) ∧ ¬ (∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ n ∧ boundedDoubleOrRecycleModel n)
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-k1`. The predicate `n = 6` satisfies exactly the same two-branch transition shape as the dichotomy above (seed at `6`, and the transition always takes the recycle branch with `c = 4`, whose conclusion is back at `2·4 - 2 = 6`), yet it is not cofinal: it is only ever true at `n = 6`. Hence the transition shape together with an endpoint-six seed is logically insufficient for cofinal exact rows.

declarations.name: paper_exists_seeded_bounded_double_or_recycle_model
declarations.signature: theorem paper_exists_seeded_bounded_double_or_recycle_model : ∃ P : ℕ → Prop, P 6 ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, 6 ≤ n → P n → P (2 * n - 1) ∨ ∃ c : ℕ, 4 ≤ c ∧ c ≤ n ∧ P (2 * c - 2)) ∧ ¬ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ n ∧ P n
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-k1`, the existential packaging.

declarations.name: paper_fractional_mass_bound_not_necessary
declarations.signature: theorem paper_fractional_mass_bound_not_necessary : localMersennePrefixValue ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) = 10 / 21 ∧ localMersennePrefixValue ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) < (1 / 2 : ℚ) ∧ localMersennePrefixValue (insert 5 ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ)) = 331 / 651 ∧ (1 / 2 : ℚ) < localMersennePrefixValue (insert 5 ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ)) ∧ localBinarySuffix ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) 1 8 = 6 ∧ localBinarySuffix ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) 1 8 < 8 ∧ localBinarySuffix ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) 1 8 < 2 ^ (5 - 2) ∧ localFractionMass (insert 5 ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ)) 8 = 757 / 651 ∧ 1 < localFractionMass (insert 5 ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ)) 8 ∧ localFractionMass (insert 5 ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ)) 8 = localFractionMass ({2, 3} : Finset ℕ) 8 + localMersenneFraction 8 5
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-k2`, exact arithmetic at `D = {2,3}`, `c = 5`. Direct calculation gives `X_D(2) = 10/21 < 1/2 < 331/651 = X_{D∪{5}}(2)` and `S(D,1,8) = 6 < 8`, while the combined fractional mass at depth `8` is `757/651 > 1`. So the one-unit fractional-mass bound, which suffices for the sharp capacity estimate, is not necessary for it, and it cannot hold at every real crossing core.

declarations.name: paper_fractional_mass_bound_suffices_for_sharp_capacity
declarations.signature: theorem paper_fractional_mass_bound_suffices_for_sharp_capacity {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ} (hc : 4 ≤ c) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d < c) (hbelow : localMersennePrefixValue D < (1 / 2 : ℚ)) (hcross : (1 / 2 : ℚ) < localMersennePrefixValue (insert c D)) (hfrac : localFractionMass (insert c D) (2 * c - 2) ≤ 1) : localBinarySuffix D 1 (2 * c - 2) < 2 ^ (c - 2)
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-k2`, the sufficiency being tested: a combined fractional mass at most one does give the sharp capacity estimate at a genuine crossing. The fixture above shows this sufficient condition is not necessary.

This is the paper's statement with no depth restriction: the hypothesis `27 ≤ halfStripBound (N + 1)` of `paper_shared_prefix_family_strip_witness_after_feedback` is absent, and the redundant `1 ≤ N` is derived from `K + 1 ≤ N`.

declarations.docstring: Long `thm:fatal-absorbing`. `r n x` is `greedyMersenneRemainder x n` and `R n` is `mersenneTail n`. Both asserted clauses: once `r n > R n`, every later rank is selected and every later state is again fatal; consequently infinitely many omitted positive ranks give `x ∈ 𝒜`.

declarations.name: straddle_all_depths_iff_mem
declarations.signature: theorem straddle_all_depths_iff_mem (t : ℝ) : (∀ d : ℕ, ∃ D : Finset ℕ, (∀ n ∈ D, 0 < n ∧ n ≤ d) ∧ positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑D : Set ℕ) ≤ t ∧ t ≤ positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑D : Set ℕ) + mersenneTail d) ↔ t ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: Long `thm:straddle-closed-set`, both directions. `X_D(2)` is `positiveMersenneSupportValue ↑D` and `R_d` is `mersenneTail d`; the supports at different depths are unrelated.

declarations.name: straddle_limiting_support_inputs
declarations.signature: theorem straddle_limiting_support_inputs : IsCompact mersenneAchievementSet ∧ Filter.Tendsto mersenneTail Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
declarations.docstring: Long `thm:straddle-closed-set`, the two inputs named in the environment for the limiting support: compactness of `𝒜` and `R_d → 0`.

declarations.name: fatal_gap_endpoint_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem fatal_gap_endpoint_bounds {A : Set ℕ} {u : Finset ℕ} {d : ℕ} (hu : ∀ n ∈ u, 0 < n ∧ n ≤ d) (hagree : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → n ≤ d → (n ∈ A ↔ n ∈ u)) : (d + 1 ∉ A → positiveMersenneSupportValue A ≤ positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneTail (d + 1)) ∧ (d + 1 ∈ A → positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneWeight (d + 1) ≤ positiveMersenneSupportValue A)
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:fatal-gap-exclusion`, the displayed endpoint computation: for a support agreeing with `u` through rank `d`, omitting `d+1` leaves value at most the lower endpoint `X_u(2) + R_{d+1}`, while including it gives value at least the upper endpoint `X_u(2) + w_{d+1}`.

declarations.name: depth_prefix_interval_disjoint
declarations.signature: theorem depth_prefix_interval_disjoint {t : ℝ} {u v : Finset ℕ} {d : ℕ} (hu : ∀ n ∈ u, 0 < n ∧ n ≤ d) (hv : ∀ n ∈ v, 0 < n ∧ n ≤ d) (hut : positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) ≤ t ∧ t ≤ positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneTail d) (hvt : positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑v : Set ℕ) ≤ t ∧ t ≤ positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑v : Set ℕ) + mersenneTail d) : u = v
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:fatal-gap-exclusion`, the disjointness of the containing intervals of distinct length-`d` prefixes: a target in both intervals forces the two prefixes to agree.

declarations.name: fatal_gap_within_prefix_interval
declarations.signature: theorem fatal_gap_within_prefix_interval {t : ℝ} {u : Finset ℕ} {d : ℕ} (hlo : positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneTail (d + 1) < t) (hhi : t < positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneWeight (d + 1)) : positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) ≤ t ∧ t ≤ positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneTail d
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:fatal-gap-exclusion`: the displayed gap lies inside the containing interval of its own prefix `u`.

declarations.name: fatal_gap_excludes_every_representation
declarations.signature: theorem fatal_gap_excludes_every_representation {t : ℝ} {u : Finset ℕ} {d : ℕ} (hu : ∀ n ∈ u, 0 < n ∧ n ≤ d) (hlo : positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneTail (d + 1) < t) (hhi : t < positiveMersenneSupportValue (↑u : Set ℕ) + mersenneWeight (d + 1)) : ∀ A : Set ℕ, 0 ∉ A → positiveMersenneSupportValue A ≠ t
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:fatal-gap-exclusion`. A strict gap over the finite prefix `u` excludes *every* positive support, not merely those agreeing with `u` through rank `d`: the conclusion quantifies over all `A` with `0 ∉ A`.

declarations.name: skipPositive_iff_lt_weight
declarations.signature: theorem skipPositive_iff_lt_weight {k u L a : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hu : 0 < u) (hL : 0 < L) (hdecomp : 2 ^ k * u + a = 2 * L + u) : 0 < a ↔ (u : ℝ) / (2 * L) < mersenneWeight k
declarations.docstring: The skip condition: `0 < a` is exactly `ρ < w_k`.

declarations.name: skipPositive_iff_greedy_skips
declarations.signature: theorem skipPositive_iff_greedy_skips {k u L a : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hu : 0 < u) (hL : 0 < L) (hdecomp : 2 ^ k * u + a = 2 * L + u) : 0 < a ↔ ¬ (mersenneWeight k ≤ (u : ℝ) / (2 * L))
declarations.docstring: The same equivalence in the paper's second phrasing: `0 < a` says exactly that the greedy rule skips the weight `w_k`.

declarations.name: dyadic_test_iff_le
declarations.signature: theorem dyadic_test_iff_le {k u L a : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hu : 0 < u) (hL : 0 < L) (hdecomp : 2 ^ k * u + a = 2 * L + u) : (u : ℝ) / (2 * L) ≤ 1 / 2 ^ k ↔ u ≤ a
declarations.docstring: The dyadic sufficient test `ρ ≤ 2^{-k}` is exactly `u ≤ a`.

declarations.name: three_channel_lt_mersenneTail
declarations.signature: theorem three_channel_lt_mersenneTail (k : ℕ) : (1 : ℝ) / 2 ^ k + 1 / (3 * 4 ^ k) + 1 / (7 * 8 ^ k) < mersenneTail k
declarations.docstring: The paper's displayed comparison series, literally: `2^{-k} + (3·4^k)^{-1} + (7·8^k)^{-1} < R_k`.

declarations.name: sharp_test_skipSafe
declarations.signature: theorem sharp_test_skipSafe {k u L a : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hu : 0 < u) (ha : 0 < a) (hdecomp : 2 ^ k * u + a = 2 * L + u) (hsharp : 2 * u ≤ 3 * a) : (u : ℝ) / (2 * L) < mersenneTail k
declarations.docstring: The weaker sufficient condition `2u ≤ 3a` places the skipped residual strictly below the remaining tail mass `R_k`.

declarations.name: dyadic_test_contained_in_sharp
declarations.signature: theorem dyadic_test_contained_in_sharp {u a : ℕ} (h : u ≤ a) : 2 * u ≤ 3 * a
declarations.docstring: Containment: the dyadic test implies the sharp test.

declarations.name: sharp_strict_containment
declarations.docstring: Strict containment of the two sufficient tests on valid rational data: `(k, u, L, a) = (2, 7, 13, 5)` satisfies the parity relation and `2u ≤ 3a`, fails `u ≤ a`, and gives `1/4 < 7/26 < R_2`.

declarations.name: three_two_not_realisable
declarations.signature: theorem three_two_not_realisable (k L : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : 2 ^ k * 3 + 2 ≠ 2 * L + 3
declarations.docstring: The scalar pair `(u, a) = (3, 2)` does not arise from an integral `L` under the parity relation: `2^k·3 + 2` is even for `k ≥ 1` while `2L + 3` is odd.

declarations.name: unit_numerator_nonfatal
declarations.signature: theorem unit_numerator_nonfatal {k L a : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (ha : 0 < a) (hdecomp : 2 ^ k * 1 + a = 2 * L + 1) : (1 : ℝ) / (2 * L) < mersenneTail k
declarations.docstring: Unit numerators are nonfatal at a skipped step, since then `a ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: fatal_forces_numerator
declarations.signature: theorem fatal_forces_numerator {k u L a : ℕ} (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hu : 0 < u) (ha : 0 < a) (hdecomp : 2 ^ k * u + a = 2 * L + u) (hfatal : mersenneTail k < (u : ℝ) / (2 * L)) : 3 * a < 2 * u ∧ 2 ≤ u ∧ (Odd u → 3 ≤ u)
declarations.docstring: Conversely a fatal step requires `3a < 2u`, hence `u ≥ 2`, and `u ≥ 3` when `u` is odd.

declarations.name: paper_sharp_fatal_gap
declarations.docstring: Every clause of long `thm:sharp-fatal-gap`, assembled.

declarations.name: mem_greedyMersennePrefixRat_le
declarations.signature: theorem mem_greedyMersennePrefixRat_le {x : ℚ} {n d : ℕ} (hd : d ∈ greedyMersennePrefixRat x n) : d ≤ n
declarations.docstring: Every rank selected by a finite rational greedy run is at most the run length.

declarations.name: cast_halfGreedyRemainderRat
declarations.signature: theorem cast_halfGreedyRemainderRat (n : ℕ) : ((greedyMersenneRemainderRat (1 / 2 : ℚ) n : ℚ) : ℝ) = greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n
declarations.docstring: The rational greedy residual for the target `1/2`, cast to `ℝ`, is the real greedy residual.

declarations.name: irrational_mersenneTail
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_mersenneTail : ∀ n : ℕ, Irrational (mersenneTail n)
declarations.docstring: Every Mersenne tail is irrational. The base case is Erdős's 1948 theorem for the Erdős–Borwein constant, instantiated at `b = 2`; each further tail differs from the previous one by a rational weight.

declarations.name: paper_no_ties_take
declarations.signature: theorem paper_no_ties_take (n : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ≠ mersenneWeight (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:no-ties`, take boundary (parity). The residual after any finite greedy prefix has even reduced denominator, while every Mersenne weight has odd denominator, so the take comparison is never a tie.

declarations.name: paper_no_ties_skip
declarations.signature: theorem paper_no_ties_skip (n : ℕ) : greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) n ≠ mersenneTail (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:no-ties`, skip-safety boundary (irrationality). The residual after a finite Boolean prefix is rational, while every tail `T_{k+1}` is irrational, so the skip-safety comparison is never a tie either.

declarations.name: paper_no_ties
declarations.signature: theorem paper_no_ties (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) (k - 1) ≠ mersenneWeight k ∧ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) (k - 1) ≠ mersenneTail k
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:no-ties`, in the paper's indexing. At every rank `k ≥ 2` of the full greedy orbit for the target `1/2`, both defining comparisons are strict: `ρ ≠ x_k` and `ρ ≠ T_{k+1}`. Both boundaries of the fatal interval `(T_{k+1}, x_k)` are therefore approached only strictly, at every rank, unconditionally.

declarations.name: tailGreedyRemainder
declarations.signature: noncomputable def tailGreedyRemainder (t : ℝ) (v : ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ | 0 => t | m + 1 => if v (m + 1 + 1) ≤ tailGreedyRemainder t v m then tailGreedyRemainder t v m - v (m + 1 + 1) else tailGreedyRemainder t v m theorem tailGreedyRemainder_zero (t : ℝ) (v : ℕ → ℝ) : tailGreedyRemainder t v 0 = t
declarations.docstring: The greedy rule applied to an arbitrary target `t` and an arbitrary weight system `v`, in increasing order of rank, starting at rank `2`. `tailGreedyRemainder t v m` is the residual after the ranks `2, …, m + 1`, so the decision at rank `n ≥ 2` is `v n ≤ tailGreedyRemainder t v (n - 2)`.

declarations.name: tailGreedyRemainder_zero
declarations.signature: theorem tailGreedyRemainder_zero (t : ℝ) (v : ℕ → ℝ) : tailGreedyRemainder t v 0 = t

declarations.name: tailGreedyRemainder_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tailGreedyRemainder_succ (t : ℝ) (v : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) : tailGreedyRemainder t v (m + 1) = if v (m + 1 + 1) ≤ tailGreedyRemainder t v m then tailGreedyRemainder t v m - v (m + 1 + 1) else tailGreedyRemainder t v m

declarations.name: halfGreedyRemainder_one
declarations.docstring: Rank one is always skipped by the real half-greedy rule, since `x_1 = 1 > 1/2`; so the real orbit on ranks `≥ 2` starts from `1/2`.

declarations.name: tailGreedyRemainder_mersenne
declarations.signature: theorem tailGreedyRemainder_mersenne (m : ℕ) : tailGreedyRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) mersenneWeight m = greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) (m + 1)
declarations.docstring: The real half-greedy rule, read as a rule on ranks `≥ 2`.

declarations.name: approx_orbit_induction
declarations.signature: theorem approx_orbit_induction (t : ℕ → ℝ) (v : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (ht : Filter.Tendsto t Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / 2 : ℝ))) (hv : ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → Filter.Tendsto (fun j => v j n) Filter.atTop (nhds (mersenneWeight n))) : ∀ r : ℕ, Filter.Tendsto (fun j => tailGreedyRemainder (t j) (v j) r) Filter.atTop (nhds (greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) (r + 1))) ∧ ∀ᶠ j in Filter.atTop, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ r + 1 → ((v j n ≤ tailGreedyRemainder (t j) (v j) (n - 2)) ↔ (mersenneWeight n ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) (n - 1)))
declarations.docstring: The inductive core of `prop:one-orbit`: at every fixed depth the approximate residual converges to the real one, and the decisions up to that depth eventually agree.

declarations.name: paper_one_orbit_stability
declarations.signature: theorem paper_one_orbit_stability (t : ℕ → ℝ) (v : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (dep : ℕ → ℕ) (ht : Filter.Tendsto t Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / 2 : ℝ))) (hv : ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → Filter.Tendsto (fun j => v j n) Filter.atTop (nhds (mersenneWeight n))) (hvpos : ∀ j n : ℕ, 0 < v j n) (hdep : Filter.Tendsto dep Filter.atTop Filter.atTop) (K : ℕ) : ∀ᶠ j in Filter.atTop, K ≤ dep j ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ K → ((v j n ≤ tailGreedyRemainder (t j) (v j) (n - 2)) ↔ (mersenneWeight n ≤ greedyMersenneRemainder (1 / 2 : ℝ) (n - 1)))
declarations.docstring: Long `prop:one-orbit` (line 5888). Let `t_j → 1/2` and, for each fixed `n ≥ 2`, let `v_n^{(j)} → x_n` with `v_n^{(j)} > 0`. Apply the greedy rule with target `t_j` and weights `v_n^{(j)}` in increasing order of `n`, through depths `m_j → ∞`. Then for every fixed depth `K`, the decisions at the ranks `2, …, K` eventually agree with those of the real half-greedy rule (and the approximate run eventually reaches depth `K`).

declarations.name: paper_relationInvariant_channels_rank_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem paper_relationInvariant_channels_rank_le_one {V ι : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℚ V] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ev : V →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ) (channel : ι → V →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ) (hker : ∀ j : ι, LinearMap.ker ev ≤ LinearMap.ker (channel j)) (row : ι → V) : ∃ u w : ι → ℚ, ∀ i j : ι, channel j (row i) = u i * w j
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-k9`, rank clause. Over `ℚ`, if every functional `channel j` vanishes on `ker ev`, then the matrix `(channel j (row i))` has rank at most one: it factors as `u i * w j`. No hypothesis on `ev` beyond linearity is used, so the degenerate case `ev = 0` is included.

declarations.name: paper_relationInvariant_channels_det_eq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem paper_relationInvariant_channels_det_eq_zero {V ι : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℚ V] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nontrivial ι] (ev : V →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ) (channel : ι → V →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ) (hker : ∀ j : ι, LinearMap.ker ev ≤ LinearMap.ker (channel j)) (row : ι → V) : Matrix.det (fun i j : ι => channel j (row i)) = 0
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-k9`, determinant clause. Every square minor of size at least two vanishes: the statement is universally quantified over the finite index type, so it applies at every matrix size.

declarations.name: paper_unsafe_middle_range_is_three_integers
declarations.signature: theorem paper_unsafe_middle_range_is_three_integers {s : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) : ¬ (4 * ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 ≤ -4 ∨ 0 ≤ 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4) ↔ 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 = -3 ∨ 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 = -2 ∨ 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 = -1
declarations.docstring: Long untitled proposition (line 5298). For `s ≥ 5`, the complement of the two safe integer ranges for the signed middle coordinate `4R - P - 4` is exactly `{-3, -2, -1}`.

declarations.name: paper_final_middle_cell_ne_neg_three
declarations.signature: theorem paper_final_middle_cell_ne_neg_three (D : ℕ) (hD13 : 13 ≤ D) (hncarry : ¬ (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).successorCarries) (hmiddle : 4 * (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder + (seamPerturbedFamily D (by omega)).gap - (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse < (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).terminalWeight) (hright : ∀ s : ℕ, D + 1 ≤ s → seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true) : 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 ≠ -3
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257hg-k12`, main clause. At a middle row `D ≥ 13` followed only by right transitions, the signed middle coordinate is never `-3`.

declarations.name: paper_final_middle_cell_remaining_negative_values
declarations.signature: theorem paper_final_middle_cell_remaining_negative_values (D : ℕ) (hD13 : 13 ≤ D) (hncarry : ¬ (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).successorCarries) (hmiddle : 4 * (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder + (seamPerturbedFamily D (by omega)).gap - (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse < (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).terminalWeight) (hright : ∀ s : ℕ, D + 1 ≤ s → seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true) : 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 ≤ -4 ∨ 0 ≤ 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega)).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 ∨
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257hg-k12`, residual clause. With `-3` excluded under the all-right-tail hypothesis, the values `-2` and `-1` remain among the three exceptional negative cells, and the nonnegative range of the coordinate is untouched.

declarations.name: paper_mobiusCenteredHalfCarry_add_two
declarations.signature: theorem paper_mobiusCenteredHalfCarry_add_two (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : mobiusCenteredHalfCarry A (N + 2) = 4 * mobiusCenteredHalfCarry A N - pairedCenteredForcing A N
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257hg-k12`, the paired centred-carry recurrence named as the proof input: two centred half-carry steps combine into one base-four step.

declarations.name: paper_cofiniteRightTail_ne_zero_centeredEndpoint
declarations.signature: theorem paper_cofiniteRightTail_ne_zero_centeredEndpoint (A : Set ℕ) (D : ℕ) (hone : 1 ∉ A) (hseries : erdosSupportSeries 2 A < (1 : ℝ) / 2) (hcofinite : Set.Ioi D ⊆ A) : mobiusCenteredHalfCarry A (2 * D + 1) ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257hg-k12`, the nonnegative-centred-carry input for a completed support: if every rank after `D` is selected and the support value is strictly below one half, the centred endpoint at row `2D+1` is nonzero.

declarations.name: dvd_frameLcm

declarations.name: divisorMajorant_nonneg

declarations.name: divisorMajorant_le_cost_mul
declarations.signature: theorem divisorMajorant_le_cost_mul {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ → ℝ} (hc : ∀ d, 0 ≤ c d) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 0 < d) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : divisorMajorant D c n ≤ divisorMajorantCost D c * (n : ℝ)

declarations.name: sum_divisorMajorant_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_divisorMajorant_le {D : Finset ℕ} {c : ℕ → ℝ} (hc : ∀ d, 0 ≤ c d) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 0 < d) {Y : ℕ} (hY : 0 < Y) : (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 Y, divisorMajorant D c n) ≤ divisorMajorantCost D c * (Y : ℝ)
