declarations.name: rungSupportWeight
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rungSupportWeight (J : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The mass that the support `A` puts at rank `n`: this is `Set.indicator A (rungWeight J)`, so `∑' n, rungSupportWeight J A n` is the manuscript's `∑_{n ∈ A} w_n^{(J)}`.

declarations.name: rungSupportWeight_of_mem
declarations.signature: theorem rungSupportWeight_of_mem {J : ℕ} {A : Set ℕ} {n : ℕ} (h : n ∈ A) : rungSupportWeight J A n = rungWeight J n

declarations.name: rungSupportWeight_of_notMem
declarations.signature: theorem rungSupportWeight_of_notMem {J : ℕ} {A : Set ℕ} {n : ℕ} (h : n ∉ A) : rungSupportWeight J A n = 0

declarations.name: rungSupportWeight_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem rungSupportWeight_nonneg (J : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ rungSupportWeight J A n

declarations.name: rungSupportWeight_le
declarations.signature: theorem rungSupportWeight_le (J : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : rungSupportWeight J A n ≤ rungWeight J n

declarations.name: rungSupportWeight_summable
declarations.signature: theorem rungSupportWeight_summable (J : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) : Summable (rungSupportWeight J A)

declarations.name: HalfRung
declarations.docstring: The manuscript's `HalfRung(J)`: some `A ⊆ {2,3,…}` has `∑_{n ∈ A} w_n^{(J)} = 1/2`.

declarations.name: rungSupportRem
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rungSupportRem (J : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The residual of the support `A` after the ranks below `n`.

declarations.name: rungSupportRem_succ
declarations.signature: private theorem rungSupportRem_succ (J : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (n : ℕ) : rungSupportRem J A (n + 1) = rungSupportRem J A n - rungSupportWeight J A n

declarations.name: rungRem
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rungRem (J : ℕ) : ℕ → ℝ | 0 => 1 / 2 | n + 1 => if rungWeight J n ≤ rungRem J n then rungRem J n - rungWeight J n else rungRem J n theorem rungRem_zero (J : ℕ) : rungRem J 0 = 1 / 2
declarations.docstring: The greedy residual just before rank `n` is examined; `rungRem J 0 = 1/2`.

declarations.name: rungRem_succ
declarations.signature: theorem rungRem_succ (J n : ℕ) : rungRem J (n + 1) = if rungWeight J n ≤ rungRem J n then rungRem J n - rungWeight J n else rungRem J n

declarations.name: rungGreedySupport
declarations.docstring: The greedy support: the ranks the greedy rule takes.

declarations.name: mem_rungGreedySupport
declarations.signature: theorem mem_rungGreedySupport {J n : ℕ} : n ∈ rungGreedySupport J ↔ rungWeight J n ≤ rungRem J n

declarations.name: RungFatal
declarations.docstring: Rank `n` is **fatal** when the residual sits strictly inside the gap `(T_{n+1}^{(J)}, w_n^{(J)})`, which no later tail can repair.

declarations.name: rungRem_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem rungRem_nonneg (J n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ rungRem J n

declarations.name: rungRem_one
declarations.signature: theorem rungRem_one {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) : rungRem J 1 = 1 / 2
declarations.docstring: Rank `0` is skipped: its weight is `J ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: zero_notMem_rungGreedySupport
declarations.signature: theorem zero_notMem_rungGreedySupport {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) : 0 ∉ rungGreedySupport J

declarations.name: one_notMem_rungGreedySupport
declarations.signature: theorem one_notMem_rungGreedySupport {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) : 1 ∉ rungGreedySupport J

declarations.name: rungRem_eq_supportRem_greedy
declarations.signature: theorem rungRem_eq_supportRem_greedy (J n : ℕ) : rungRem J n = rungSupportRem J (rungGreedySupport J) n
declarations.docstring: The greedy residual as `1/2` minus the mass already taken.

declarations.name: rungRem_succ_le_tail
declarations.signature: private theorem rungRem_succ_le_tail {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) (hsurv : ∀ n, ¬ RungFatal J n) (n : ℕ) : rungRem J (n + 1) ≤ rungTail J n

declarations.name: rungRem_tendsto_zero
declarations.signature: private theorem rungRem_tendsto_zero {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) (hsurv : ∀ n, ¬ RungFatal J n) : Tendsto (fun n => rungRem J n) atTop (nhds 0)

declarations.name: rungGreedy_tsum_eq_half
declarations.signature: private theorem rungGreedy_tsum_eq_half {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) (hsurv : ∀ n, ¬ RungFatal J n) : ∑' n : ℕ, rungSupportWeight J (rungGreedySupport J) n = 1 / 2
declarations.docstring: Survival at every rank makes the greedy support achieve the target.

declarations.name: rungRem_eq_of_tsum
declarations.signature: private theorem rungRem_eq_of_tsum {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) {A : Set ℕ} (hsum : ∑' n : ℕ, rungSupportWeight J A n = 1 / 2) : ∀ n, rungRem J n = rungSupportRem J A n
declarations.docstring: Any support achieving the target runs in lockstep with the greedy orbit.

declarations.name: paper_forced_greedy_unique_support_and_criterion
declarations.signature: theorem paper_forced_greedy_unique_support_and_criterion {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) : (∀ A : Set ℕ, ∑' n : ℕ, rungSupportWeight J A n = 1 / 2 → A = rungGreedySupport J) ∧ (HalfRung J ↔ ∀ n : ℕ, ¬ RungFatal J n)
declarations.docstring: **Long `lem:tr-forced-greedy`, clause two.** For `J ≥ 2` the greedy support is the unique candidate support, and `HalfRung(J)` holds exactly when the greedy orbit for `1/2` under the weights `w_n^{(J)}` never lands in a fatal interval `(T_{n+1}^{(J)}, w_n^{(J)})`.

declarations.name: paper_forced_greedy_low_ranks
declarations.signature: theorem paper_forced_greedy_low_ranks {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) : (1 ∉ rungGreedySupport J ∧ rungRem J 1 ≤ rungTail J 1) ∧ 2 ∈ rungGreedySupport J ∧ 3 ∈ rungGreedySupport J
declarations.docstring: **Long `lem:tr-forced-greedy`, clause three.** Rank `1` is a safe skip and ranks `2` and `3` are takes.

declarations.name: rung_witness_exclusion
declarations.signature: private theorem rung_witness_exclusion {J n M : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) (hn : 4 ≤ n) (hMlow : n ≤ M) (hMhigh : M + 2 ≤ 2 * n) (hmu : rungMisalign J M ≤ 11 / 15) (D : Finset ℕ) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d + 1 ≤ n) : ¬ (rungTail J n < 1 / 2 - ∑ d ∈ D, rungWeight J d ∧ 1 / 2 - ∑ d ∈ D, rungWeight J d < rungWeight J n)

declarations.name: rung_half_lcm_horizon
declarations.signature: private theorem rung_half_lcm_horizon {J n : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) (hn4 : 4 ≤ n) (hn : rungLcm J / 2 + 1 ≤ n) : ∃ M : ℕ, n ≤ M ∧ M + 2 ≤ 2 * n ∧ rungMisalign J M < 11 / 15

declarations.name: RungBad
declarations.docstring: A rank `n` is **bad** for `J` when no `M ∈ [n, 2n-2]` passes the witness test `μ_J(M) ≤ 11/15`.

declarations.name: rungBadFinset
declarations.signature: noncomputable def rungBadFinset (J : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.docstring: The bad ranks inside the manuscript's finite window `[4, L_J/2]`.

declarations.name: mem_rungBadFinset
declarations.signature: theorem mem_rungBadFinset {J n : ℕ} : n ∈ rungBadFinset J ↔ (4 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ rungLcm J / 2) ∧ RungBad J n

declarations.name: rungDecisionHorizon
declarations.docstring: The manuscript's `B(J) = max(bad ∪ {3})`.

declarations.name: rungBad_le_horizon
declarations.signature: theorem rungBad_le_horizon {J n : ℕ} (h : n ∈ rungBadFinset J) : n ≤ rungDecisionHorizon J

declarations.name: paper_rung_finite_decision
declarations.signature: theorem paper_rung_finite_decision {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) : HalfRung J ↔ ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ rungDecisionHorizon J → ¬ RungFatal J n
declarations.docstring: **Long `thm:tr-finite-decision`.** For `J ≥ 2`, `HalfRung(J)` holds iff the greedy orbit for `1/2` under the weights `w_n^{(J)}` survives every rank from `2` through `B(J)`. Since `B(J)` is computed from the finite window `[4, L_J/2]`, this is a finite exact decision procedure.

declarations.name: truncWeight
declarations.signature: noncomputable def truncWeight (J n : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The manuscript's `w_n^{(J)} = ∑_{q=1}^{J} 2^{-qn}`.

declarations.name: truncTail
declarations.signature: noncomputable def truncTail (J n : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: misalignMass
declarations.signature: noncomputable def misalignMass (J M : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The manuscript's misalignment mass `μ_J(M) = ∑_{q=2}^{J} 2^{M mod q}/(2^q-1)`.

declarations.name: truncLcm
declarations.docstring: The manuscript's `L_J = lcm(2,3,…,J)`.

declarations.name: two_le_two_pow
declarations.signature: private theorem two_le_two_pow {q : ℕ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) : (2 : ℝ) ≤ 2 ^ q

declarations.name: inv_pow_eq
declarations.signature: private theorem inv_pow_eq (n q : ℕ) : ((1 : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) ^ q = 1 / 2 ^ (q * n)

declarations.name: geom_range_mul
declarations.signature: private theorem geom_range_mul (x : ℝ) (K : ℕ) : (∑ i ∈ Finset.range K, x ^ i) * (1 - x) = 1 - x ^ K

declarations.name: geom_range_le
declarations.signature: private theorem geom_range_le {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x < 1) (K : ℕ) : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range K, x ^ i ≤ 1 / (1 - x)

declarations.name: sum_pow_le_of_le_index
declarations.signature: private theorem sum_pow_le_of_le_index {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x < 1) (a : ℕ) (s : Finset ℕ) (hs : ∀ q ∈ s, a ≤ q) : ∑ q ∈ s, x ^ q ≤ x ^ a / (1 - x)
declarations.docstring: Geometric tail bound over an arbitrary finite index set bounded below.

declarations.name: truncWeight_le_inv
declarations.signature: private theorem truncWeight_le_inv {J n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) : truncWeight J n ≤ 1 / (2 ^ n - 1)

declarations.name: paper_forced_greedy_tail_lt_weight
declarations.signature: theorem paper_forced_greedy_tail_lt_weight {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) (n : ℕ) : truncTail J n < truncWeight J n
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:tr-forced-greedy`, first clause. For every `J ≥ 2` and every `n`, the truncated weight `w_n^{(J)}` strictly exceeds the complete later tail `T_{n+1}^{(J)}`: the `q = 1` terms agree and every `q ≥ 2` tail term is strictly smaller than the matching weight term.

declarations.name: paper_forced_greedy_rank_one_safe_skip
declarations.signature: theorem paper_forced_greedy_rank_one_safe_skip {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) : (1 : ℝ) / 2 < truncWeight J 1 ∧ (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ truncTail J 1
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:tr-forced-greedy`, third clause, rank one. The rank-`1` weight exceeds the target `1/2`, so the greedy rule skips it, and the skip is safe: the whole later tail `T_2^{(J)}` is still at least `1/2`.

declarations.name: paper_forced_greedy_ranks_two_three_taken
declarations.signature: theorem paper_forced_greedy_ranks_two_three_taken (J : ℕ) : truncWeight J 2 ≤ 1 / 2 ∧ truncWeight J 3 ≤ 1 / 2 - truncWeight J 2
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:tr-forced-greedy`, third clause, ranks two and three. With target `1/2` the greedy rule takes rank `2` (its weight is at most the residual `1/2`) and then takes rank `3` (its weight is at most the new residual `1/2 - w_2^{(J)}`).

declarations.name: paper_parity_excludes_finite_support
declarations.signature: theorem paper_parity_excludes_finite_support {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) (A : Finset ℕ) (hA : ∀ n ∈ A, 2 ≤ n) : ∑ n ∈ A, truncWeight J n ≠ 1 / 2
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:tr-parity`. For every `J ≥ 2`, no finite `A ⊆ {2,3,…}` has `∑_{n ∈ A} w_n^{(J)} = 1/2`.

declarations.name: paper_witness_exclusion
declarations.signature: theorem paper_witness_exclusion {J n M : ℕ} (hJ : 3 ≤ J) (hn : 4 ≤ n) (hMlow : n ≤ M) (hMhigh : M + 2 ≤ 2 * n) (hmu : misalignMass J M ≤ 11 / 15) (D : Finset ℕ) (hD : ∀ d ∈ D, 2 ≤ d ∧ d + 1 ≤ n) : ¬ (truncTail J n < 1 / 2 - ∑ d ∈ D, truncWeight J d ∧ 1 / 2 - ∑ d ∈ D, truncWeight J d < truncWeight J n)
declarations.docstring: Long `thm:tr-witness-exclusion`. Let `J ≥ 3`, `n ≥ 4`, and suppose some `M ∈ [n, 2n-2]` has `μ_J(M) ≤ 11/15`. Then no Boolean prefix `D ⊆ {2,…,n-1}` leaves a residual strictly inside the fatal gap `(T_{n+1}^{(J)}, w_n^{(J)})`. The exclusion is for every prefix, not only the greedy one.

declarations.name: paper_half_lcm_horizon
declarations.signature: theorem paper_half_lcm_horizon {J n : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) (hn4 : 4 ≤ n) (hn : truncLcm J / 2 + 1 ≤ n) : ∃ M : ℕ, n ≤ M ∧ M + 2 ≤ 2 * n ∧ misalignMass J M < 11 / 15
declarations.docstring: Long `cor:tr-half-lcm`. For `J ≥ 2` and every `n ≥ max{4, L_J/2 + 1}` there is a witness `M ∈ [n, 2n-2]` with `μ_J(M) < 11/15`; only the finite window `[4, L_J/2]` can escape the witness test.

declarations.name: paper_mod_twelve_filter
declarations.signature: theorem paper_mod_twelve_filter {J M : ℕ} (hJ : 7 ≤ J) (hmu : misalignMass J M ≤ 11 / 15) : 12 ∣ M
declarations.docstring: Long `lem:tr-mod12`. For `J ≥ 7`, the witness inequality `μ_J(M) ≤ 11/15` forces `12 ∣ M`, so only multiples of `12` need to be tested as witnesses.

declarations.name: paper_finite_band_check_thirteen_to_thirty
declarations.signature: theorem paper_finite_band_check_thirteen_to_thirty (d : ℕ) (hd13 : 13 ≤ d) (hd30 : d ≤ 30) (hd5 : 5 ≤ d) (hcarry : (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).successorCarries) : ∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ d → 2 ^ (d - j + 1) < 4 * (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).overshoot + (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).abovePulse ∨ 4 * (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).overshoot + (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).abovePulse + 2 * (d + j) ≤ 2 ^ (d - j + 1)
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-i14`, first clause. For every actual upper-reset index `13 ≤ d ≤ 30` (an upper reset is `successorCarries`) and every `0 ≤ j ≤ d`, either `2^{d-j+1}` is strictly below the reset charge, or the reset charge plus the linear width `2(d+j)` is at most `2^{d-j+1}`.

declarations.name: paper_successor_remainders_fourteen_through_thirtyone
declarations.signature: theorem paper_successor_remainders_fourteen_through_thirtyone : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 14 = 392 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 15 = 34333 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 16 = 71791 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 17 = 156085 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 18 = 362187 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 19 = 924455 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 20 = 549353 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 21 = 100251 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 22 = 4595307 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 23 = 9992613 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 24 = 23193229 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 25 = 59218477 ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 26 = 35546625 ∧
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-i14`, second clause: the successor remainder at each row `d + 1` for `13 ≤ d ≤ 30`, from `rem(14) = 392` through `rem(31) = 4187487147`.

declarations.name: paper_universal_band_condition_would_close_half
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-i14`, third clause, in its exact conditional form: the finite range is not the universal condition. What the universal condition would give is recorded here, so that the gap between the certified band `13 ≤ d ≤ 30` and the hypothesis `∀ d ≥ 13` is explicit.

declarations.name: paper_universal_band_condition_unfolded
declarations.signature: theorem paper_universal_band_condition_unfolded : SeamUpperResetDyadicBandEscape ↔ ∀ (d : ℕ) (hd5 : 5 ≤ d), 13 ≤ d → (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).successorCarries → ∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ d → 2 ^ (d - j + 1) < 4 * (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).overshoot + (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).abovePulse ∨ 4 * (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).overshoot + (seamAdjacentCut d hd5).abovePulse + 2 * (d + j) ≤ 2 ^ (d - j + 1)
declarations.docstring: The universal hypothesis spelled out, for comparison with the finite band check above: the same disjunction at every `d ≥ 13`, not only `d ≤ 30`.

declarations.name: paper_perturbed_order_preservation
declarations.signature: theorem paper_perturbed_order_preservation (F : PerturbedFamily α) {x y : α} (hxy : F.oldSum x < F.oldSum y) : F.newSum x < F.newSum y
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-i15`, order preservation. The structure hypothesis `B < 3g` alone preserves the order of the updated values `t(x) = 4 s(x) + p(x)`.

declarations.name: paper_perturbed_prefixChoice_maximal
declarations.signature: theorem paper_perturbed_prefixChoice_maximal (F : PerturbedFamily α) {C : ℕ} (K : F.AdjacentCut C) [Decidable K.successorCarries] (hcap : F.pulseCap < F.gap) : K.newCapacity = 4 * C + F.gap ∧ K.successorCarries = (4 * K.overshoot + K.abovePulse ≤ F.gap) ∧ K.prefixChoice = (if K.successorCarries then K.above else K.below) ∧ F.newSum K.prefixChoice ≤ K.newCapacity ∧ ∀ x : α, F.newSum x ≤ K.newCapacity → F.newSum x ≤ F.newSum K.prefixChoice
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-i15`, maximality clause with the additional hypothesis `B < g`. At the new capacity `C' = 4C + g` the selected updated value is `t(x₊)` when `4o + p₊ ≤ g` and `t(x₋)` otherwise; it is admissible, and it is the largest admissible updated value.

declarations.name: paper_perturbed_nextRemainder_three_branches
declarations.signature: theorem paper_perturbed_nextRemainder_three_branches (F : PerturbedFamily α) {C : ℕ} (K : F.AdjacentCut C) [Decidable K.successorCarries] : K.terminalWeight = 2 * F.gap + 4 ∧ K.nextRemainder = if K.successorCarries then F.gap - (4 * K.overshoot + K.abovePulse) else if 4 * K.remainder + F.gap - K.belowPulse < K.terminalWeight then 4 * K.remainder + F.gap - K.belowPulse else 4 * K.remainder - F.gap - K.belowPulse - 4
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-i15`, the exact three-branch remainder after testing the extra weight `W = 2g + 4` by the take-if-possible rule.

declarations.name: paper_perturbed_separation_global_maximality
declarations.signature: theorem paper_perturbed_separation_global_maximality (F : PerturbedFamily α) {C : ℕ} (K : F.AdjacentCut C) [Decidable K.successorCarries] (hsep : K.terminalWeight ≤ 4 * F.gap - F.pulseCap) {x : α} (hx : F.oldSum x < F.oldSum K.prefixChoice) : F.newSum x + K.terminalWeight ≤ F.newSum K.prefixChoice
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-i15`, the separation clause: under `4g - B ≥ W` every earlier updated value plus the extra weight is at most the selected updated value. This is the extra hypothesis needed for a genuine maximum over both choices of the extra weight, rather than the stated two-stage rule.

declarations.name: paper_perturbed_two_stage_is_global_maximum
declarations.signature: theorem paper_perturbed_two_stage_is_global_maximum (F : PerturbedFamily α) {C : ℕ} (K : F.AdjacentCut C) [Decidable K.successorCarries] (hcap : F.pulseCap < F.gap) (hsep : K.terminalWeight ≤ 4 * F.gap - F.pulseCap) : F.newSum K.prefixChoice + (if K.terminalWeight ≤ K.prefixRemainder then K.terminalWeight else 0) ≤ K.newCapacity ∧ (∀ x : α, F.newSum x ≤ K.newCapacity → F.newSum x ≤ F.newSum K.prefixChoice + (if K.terminalWeight ≤ K.prefixRemainder then K.terminalWeight else 0)) ∧ (∀ x : α, F.newSum x + K.terminalWeight ≤ K.newCapacity → F.newSum x + K.terminalWeight ≤
declarations.docstring: Long `record:257bm-i15`, the separation clause in the form the paper states it: under `B < g` and `4g - B ≥ W` the two-stage rule really is the maximum of `{t(x) + εW : x ∈ α, ε ∈ {0,1}}` below the new capacity. The first conjunct says the two-stage value is admissible; the next two say no `ε = 0` and no `ε = 1` candidate beats it.

declarations.name: weakCapOldSum
declarations.docstring: Old values `0, 2, 4`.

declarations.name: weakCapPulse
declarations.docstring: Perturbations `0, 3, 0`.

declarations.name: weakCapFamily
declarations.docstring: The family with `g = 2`, `B = 3`: it satisfies `B < 3g` but not `B < g`.

declarations.name: weakCapCut
declarations.docstring: The adjacent pair at capacity `C = 2`: `x₋` is the old value `2`, `x₊` is the old value `4`.

declarations.name: paper_perturbed_weak_cap_counterexample
declarations.signature: theorem paper_perturbed_weak_cap_counterexample : ¬ weakCapFamily.pulseCap < weakCapFamily.gap ∧ weakCapFamily.pulseCap < 3 * weakCapFamily.gap ∧ ¬ weakCapCut.successorCarries ∧ weakCapCut.newCapacity = 10 ∧ weakCapFamily.newSum weakCapCut.below = 11 ∧ ¬ weakCapFamily.newSum weakCapCut.below ≤ weakCapCut.newCapacity ∧ weakCapFamily.newSum (0 : Fin 3) ≤ weakCapCut.newCapacity
declarations.docstring: The updated value selected at capacity `C' = 4C + g = 10` is `t(x₋) = 11`, which exceeds `C'`, although the updated value `t` of the old value `0` is `0` and therefore admissible. So the maximality statement genuinely needs `B < g` and does not follow from the structure hypothesis `B < 3g`.

declarations.name: prefixChoice_eq_below

declarations.name: rpow_sum_le_sum_rpow
declarations.signature: theorem rpow_sum_le_sum_rpow {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → ℝ) (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) : (∑ i ∈ s, f i) ^ p ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, f i ^ p
declarations.docstring: Subadditivity of a fractional power over a finite sum of nonnegative reals. This is the finite form of the step `U_j(N) ^ α_j ≤ V_j(N)`.

declarations.name: rpow_tsum_le_tsum_rpow
declarations.signature: theorem rpow_tsum_le_tsum_rpow (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) {p : ℝ} (hp : 0 < p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) (hsum : Summable f) (hsump : Summable fun i => f i ^ p) : (∑' i, f i) ^ p ≤ ∑' i, f i ^ p
declarations.docstring: The countable form of the same subadditivity, under the summability that the paper's nonnegative double series supplies on both sides.

declarations.name: rpow_neg_le_max_one_inv
declarations.signature: theorem rpow_neg_le_max_one_inv {t α : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (hα : 0 < α) (hα1 : α ≤ 1) : t ^ (-α) ≤ max 1 t⁻¹
declarations.docstring: The scalar tail-budget bound `ε ^ (-α) ≤ max 1 ε⁻¹`, uniform over the exponents `0 < α ≤ 1`.

declarations.name: tsum_inv_pow_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_inv_pow_succ {B : ℝ} (hB : 1 < B) : ∑' r : ℕ, (B ^ (r + 1))⁻¹ = 1 / (B - 1)
declarations.docstring: The geometric factor of the displayed cost condition.

declarations.name: tsum_rpow_two_inv_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_rpow_two_inv_succ {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) : ∑' r : ℕ, (((2 : ℝ) ^ α) ^ (r + 1))⁻¹ = 1 / ((2 : ℝ) ^ α - 1)
declarations.docstring: The cost factor specialised to the base `2 ^ α` used in the displayed condition (V), for every admissible exponent.

declarations.name: mul_sub_one_le_pow_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem mul_sub_one_le_pow_sub_one (B : ℝ) (hB : 1 ≤ B) (g : ℕ) : (g : ℝ) * (B - 1) ≤ B ^ g - 1
declarations.docstring: Bernoulli in the form the complete-cycle step uses.

declarations.name: cycle_ratio_le_inv_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem cycle_ratio_le_inv_sub_one {B : ℝ} (hB : 1 < B) (g : ℕ) (hg : 0 < g) : (g : ℝ) / (B ^ g - 1) ≤ 1 / (B - 1)
declarations.docstring: The complete-cycle ratio bound `g / (B ^ g - 1) ≤ 1 / (B - 1)`, which is what makes the main term of (S) uniform in the modulus.

declarations.name: sum_cycle_weight_eq
declarations.signature: theorem sum_cycle_weight_eq {B : ℝ} (hB : 1 < B) (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range d, B ^ i / (B ^ d - 1) = 1 / (B - 1)
declarations.docstring: One full residue cycle of the kernel weight has total mass exactly `1 / (B - 1)`.

declarations.name: two_rpow_sub_one_le_self
declarations.signature: theorem two_rpow_sub_one_le_self {α : ℝ} (hα0 : 0 ≤ α) (hα1 : α ≤ 1) : (2 : ℝ) ^ α - 1 ≤ α
declarations.docstring: Convexity of `2 ^ ·` on the unit interval, the exact step the note cites.

declarations.name: exp_one_mul_le_exp
declarations.signature: theorem exp_one_mul_le_exp {u : ℝ} (_hu : 0 < u) : Real.exp 1 * u ≤ Real.exp u
declarations.docstring: `e u ≤ exp u`, the scalar form of `e ^ u / u ≥ e`.

declarations.name: exp_one_mul_log_le_rpow_div
declarations.signature: theorem exp_one_mul_log_le_rpow_div {t α : ℝ} (ht : 1 ≤ t) (hα : 0 < α) (hα1 : α ≤ 1) : Real.exp 1 * Real.log t ≤ t ^ α / ((2 : ℝ) ^ α - 1)
declarations.docstring: The cover-cost lower bound `t ^ α / (2 ^ α - 1) ≥ e log t`, uniformly over the admissible exponents `0 < α ≤ 1`. Taking the infimum over `α` gives `Ψ(t) ≥ e log t`.

declarations.name: three_mul_two_pow_le_two_mul_three_pow
declarations.signature: theorem three_mul_two_pow_le_two_mul_three_pow {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) : 3 * (2 : ℝ) ^ m ≤ 2 * (3 : ℝ) ^ m
declarations.docstring: The geometric comparison the base-transfer envelope needs: at every positive exponent, three copies of `2 ^ m` are below two copies of `3 ^ m`.

declarations.name: atom_base_transfer
declarations.signature: theorem atom_base_transfer (b r d : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hrd : r < d) : ((b : ℝ) ^ r - 1) / ((b : ℝ) ^ d - 1) ≤ 2 * ((2 : ℝ) ^ r - 1) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ d - 1)

declarations.name: exists_lt_of_mean_lt
declarations.signature: theorem exists_lt_of_mean_lt {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : ι → ℝ) {c : ℝ} (hmean : (∑ i ∈ s, f i) / (s.card : ℝ) < c) : ∃ i ∈ s, f i < c
declarations.docstring: A nonnegative test whose mean over a nonempty finite range is below a threshold is below that threshold at one sample of the range.

declarations.name: two_mul_sqrt_mul_le_add
declarations.signature: theorem two_mul_sqrt_mul_le_add {x y : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) : 2 * Real.sqrt (x * y) ≤ x + y
declarations.docstring: Two-term AM-GM in the form the pairing uses.

declarations.name: card_mul_sqrt_le_geom_sum
declarations.signature: theorem card_mul_sqrt_le_geom_sum {B : ℝ} (hB : 0 ≤ B) (d : ℕ) : (d : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (B ^ (d - 1)) ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range d, B ^ i
declarations.docstring: The geometric lower bound of the no-wrap case: a complete block of `d` powers is at least `d` copies of the central power.

declarations.name: displacementAtom
declarations.signature: def displacementAtom (b N d : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Pointwise nonnegative displacement, with the existing zero-index convention.

declarations.name: displacement
declarations.signature: def displacement (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The actual infinite support displacement, not a free abstract error stream.

declarations.name: displacementAtom_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem displacementAtom_nonneg (b N d : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : 0 ≤ displacementAtom b N d

declarations.name: summable_displacementAtom
declarations.signature: theorem summable_displacementAtom (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : Summable (Set.indicator A (displacementAtom b N))
declarations.docstring: Infinite sums of displacement atoms are absolutely summable.

declarations.name: displacement_eq_tsum
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_eq_tsum (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : displacement b A N = ∑' d : ℕ, Set.indicator A (displacementAtom b N) d

declarations.name: displacement_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_nonneg (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : 0 ≤ displacement b A N

declarations.name: displacement_pos
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_pos (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hA : A.Infinite) (hN : 0 < N) : 0 < displacement b A N

declarations.name: displacement_mono
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_mono (b : ℕ) (A B : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hAB : A ⊆ B) : displacement b A N ≤ displacement b B N
declarations.docstring: Hereditary control follows from positivity of actual displacement atoms.

declarations.name: displacement_partition
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_partition (b : ℕ) (A B : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hBA : B ⊆ A) : displacement b A N = displacement b B N + displacement b (A \ B) N
declarations.docstring: Exact disjoint decomposition; this is not an irrationality claim about sums.

declarations.name: displacement_union_le
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_union_le (b : ℕ) (A B : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : displacement b (A ∪ B) N ≤ displacement b A N + displacement b B N
declarations.docstring: Union subadditivity without a disjointness hypothesis.

declarations.name: displacement_finset_eq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_finset_eq_zero (b : ℕ) (F : Finset ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hdiv : ∀ d ∈ F, d ∣ N) : displacement b (↑F : Set ℕ) N = 0
declarations.docstring: A finite prefix is annihilated at any common multiple.

declarations.name: displacementAtom_le_amplified
declarations.signature: theorem displacementAtom_le_amplified (b N d : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : displacementAtom b N d ≤ ((b : ℝ) ^ N - 1) * (1 / ((b : ℝ) ^ d - 1))
declarations.docstring: Every atom is bounded by amplified initial mass, even if it has wrapped.

declarations.name: displacement_le_amplified_mass
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_le_amplified_mass (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : displacement b A N ≤ ((b : ℝ) ^ N - 1) * erdosSupportSeries b A
declarations.docstring: The infinite residual-mass budget, extending the supplied finite draft.

declarations.name: displacement_future_eq
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_future_eq (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hfuture : ∀ d ∈ A, N < d) : displacement b A N = ((b : ℝ) ^ N - 1) * erdosSupportSeries b A
declarations.docstring: Exact future-tail identity. The no-wrap hypothesis is stated for every selected exponent and is not hidden in a free error term.

declarations.name: displacement_residual_budget
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_residual_budget (b : ℕ) (A B : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hBA : B ⊆ A) : displacement b A N ≤ displacement b B N + ((b : ℝ) ^ N - 1) * erdosSupportSeries b (A \ B)
declarations.docstring: R6 amplified-tail inequality, now for the actual infinite series.

declarations.name: displacement_le_two_mul_binary
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_le_two_mul_binary (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : displacement b A N ≤ 2 * displacement 2 A N
declarations.docstring: The packet's pointwise radix comparison, lifted to infinite supports.

declarations.name: irrational_of_displacement_returns
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_of_displacement_returns (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hA : A.Infinite) (hreturn : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ displacement b A N < ε) : Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b A)
declarations.docstring: General arithmetic consumer. The analytic input is *exactly* arbitrarily small positive-time displacements; no summable-reciprocal assumption remains.

declarations.name: all_base_hereditary_of_binary_returns
declarations.signature: theorem all_base_hereditary_of_binary_returns (H : Set ℕ) (hreturn : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ displacement 2 H N < ε) : ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A ⊆ H → A.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b A)
declarations.docstring: Exact all-base hereditary consumer for both short-note analytic producers.

declarations.name: primeSetPart
declarations.signature: def primeSetPart (P : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The full prime-power part determined by a finite set of primes.

declarations.name: primeWeightedTerm
declarations.signature: def primeWeightedTerm (b : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (a : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The literal weighted term at an integer base.

declarations.name: FinitePrimeWeighted
declarations.signature: def FinitePrimeWeighted (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The weighted hypothesis, not its irrationality conclusion.

declarations.name: supportSeries_le_mersenneTail
declarations.signature: theorem supportSeries_le_mersenneTail (A : Set ℕ) (R : ℕ) (hfuture : ∀ a ∈ A, R < a) : erdosSupportSeries 2 A ≤ mersenneTail R
declarations.docstring: All selected exponents beyond R contribute at most the full tail.

declarations.name: mersenneTail_le_dyadic_budget
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneTail_le_dyadic_budget (R : ℕ) : mersenneTail R ≤ 2 / (2 : ℝ) ^ R
declarations.docstring: A coarse dyadic enclosure valid at R=0 as well as at positive indices.

declarations.name: displacement_future_budget
declarations.signature: theorem displacement_future_budget (A : Set ℕ) (N R : ℕ) (hfuture : ∀ a ∈ A, R < a) : displacement 2 A N ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (N + 1) / (2 : ℝ) ^ R
declarations.docstring: The actual infinite future-support budget. No relation between N and R is needed for this upper bound.

declarations.name: ReturnAdmissible
declarations.docstring: Return admissibility with a prescribed divisor and arbitrarily late shifts.

declarations.name: returnAdmissible_mono
declarations.signature: theorem returnAdmissible_mono {A B : Set ℕ} (hBA : B ⊆ A) (hA : ReturnAdmissible A) : ReturnAdmissible B

declarations.name: returnAdmissible_hereditary_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem returnAdmissible_hereditary_irrational {H : Set ℕ} (hH : ReturnAdmissible H) : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A ⊆ H → A.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b A)
declarations.docstring: Return admissibility supplies hereditary irrationality, not conversely.

declarations.name: returnAdmissible_of_samples
declarations.signature: theorem returnAdmissible_of_samples (A : Set ℕ) (N : ℕ → ℕ) (hlarge : ∀ j, j + 1 ≤ N j) (hdiv : ∀ j, Nat.factorial (j + 1) ∣ N j) (hsmall : ∀ j, displacement 2 A (N j) ≤ 1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ j) : ReturnAdmissible A
declarations.docstring: A sequence of factorial-divisible samples with a geometric error envelope contains a return for every prescribed divisor, tolerance, and lower index.

declarations.name: hostPrefix
declarations.signature: def hostPrefix (E : ℕ → Set ℕ) (j : ℕ) : Set ℕ
declarations.docstring: Finite host union through index j, including both endpoints.

declarations.name: delayed_countable_gluing
declarations.signature: theorem delayed_countable_gluing (E : ℕ → Set ℕ) (hfinite : ∀ j, ReturnAdmissible (hostPrefix E j)) : ∃ s : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono s ∧ ReturnAdmissible {a : ℕ | ∃ i, a ∈ E i ∧ s i < a}
declarations.docstring: The landed r6 gluing theorem, in its general finite-union form. The cutoffs are *chosen*; the untruncated countable union is not asserted to be admissible. Every host is retained beyond its own finite cutoff.

declarations.name: strengthened_term_le_oldCostTerm
declarations.signature: theorem strengthened_term_le_oldCostTerm (C : PositiveCoverData) (j : ℕ) : C.cost j * (2 : ℝ) ^ (((j + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * C.exponent j) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ C.exponent j - 1) ≤ C.oldCostTerm j
declarations.docstring: The older cost actually dominates the strengthened cost term by term.

declarations.name: hasStrengthenedPositiveCover_of_old
declarations.signature: theorem hasStrengthenedPositiveCover_of_old {A : Set ℕ} (hA : HasOldPositiveCover A) : HasStrengthenedPositiveCover A

declarations.name: old_cover_class_strictly_smaller
declarations.signature: theorem old_cover_class_strictly_smaller : (∀ A : Set ℕ, HasOldPositiveCover A → HasStrengthenedPositiveCover A) ∧ ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ (∀ a ∈ A, Squarefree a) ∧ HasStrengthenedPositiveCover A ∧ ¬ HasOldPositiveCover A
declarations.docstring: The class inclusion is strict with a constructed, squarefree witness.

declarations.name: exists_incomparable_hosts_with_mixed_heredity
declarations.signature: theorem exists_incomparable_hosts_with_mixed_heredity : ∃ W V : Set ℕ, W.Infinite ∧ V.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ W ∧ 0 ∉ V ∧ FinitePrimeWeighted 2 W ∧ ¬ HasStrengthenedPositiveCover W ∧ HasStrengthenedPositiveCover V ∧ ¬ HasOldPositiveCover V ∧ (∀ α : ℝ, 0 < α → α ≤ 1 → ¬ HasFixedExponentPositiveCover V α) ∧ (∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → ¬ FinitePrimeWeighted b V) ∧ (∀ A : Set ℕ, A ⊆ W ∪ V → A.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b A))
declarations.docstring: Both directions of incomparability and the mixed all-base hereditary consumer use actual witnesses. The weighted-only witness is imported from `AnalyticSeparationReturn`; this assembly is elaborated and axiom-audited as stated in the file header.

declarations.name: exists_weighted_not_strengthened_host
declarations.signature: theorem exists_weighted_not_strengthened_host : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ FinitePrimeWeighted 2 A ∧ ¬ Summable (Set.indicator A (fun a : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / a)) ∧ ¬ HasStrengthenedPositiveCover A ∧ IsEmpty (LogBudgetCover A) ∧ (∀ B : Set ℕ, B ⊆ A → B.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b B))
declarations.docstring: A_W satisfies the literal weighted criterion but fails the literal strengthened-cover predicate, not just a differently typed obstruction.

declarations.name: exists_weighted_obstruction_with_mixed_heredity
declarations.signature: theorem exists_weighted_obstruction_with_mixed_heredity : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ FinitePrimeWeighted 2 A ∧ IsEmpty (LogBudgetCover A) ∧ (∀ V : Set ℕ, HasStrengthenedPositiveCover V → ∀ B : Set ℕ, B ⊆ A ∪ V → B.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b B))
declarations.docstring: The constructed weighted obstruction can still be synchronised with any actual strengthened-cover host. This does not assume A-star exists.

declarations.name: arbitraryWeightPositiveCover_allBase_hereditary
declarations.signature: theorem arbitraryWeightPositiveCover_allBase_hereditary {V : Set ℕ} (D : LogBudgetCover V) : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A ⊆ V → A.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b A)
declarations.docstring: The paper's arbitrary positive-weight cover conclusion, exposed under the data structure that records the weights and their sum-one hypothesis.

declarations.name: mixedLogBudget_binary_returns_of_mean_target
declarations.signature: theorem mixedLogBudget_binary_returns_of_mean_target (htarget : WeightedDyadicMeanTarget) (E V : Set ℕ) (hE0 : 0 ∉ E) (hE : FinitePrimeWeighted 2 E) (D : LogBudgetCover V) : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ displacement 2 (E ∪ V) N < ε
declarations.docstring: Weighted support and an arbitrary positive-weight logarithmic cover have binary returns at a common sample. No separate return times are combined.

declarations.name: arbitraryWeightMixedSupport_allBase_hereditary
declarations.signature: theorem arbitraryWeightMixedSupport_allBase_hereditary (E V : Set ℕ) (hE0 : 0 ∉ E) (hE : FinitePrimeWeighted 2 E) (D : LogBudgetCover V) : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A ⊆ E ∪ V → A.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b A)
declarations.docstring: Exact arbitrary-weight mixed conclusion: every infinite subset of the union has irrational support series in every integer base at least two.

declarations.signature: theorem logBudgetCover_allBase_hereditary {A : Set ℕ} (D : LogBudgetCover A) : ∀ B : Set ℕ, B ⊆ A → B.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b B)

declarations.name: common_displacement_return

declarations.name: hereditary_irrational_of_jointDyadicMeanSupply

declarations.name: MixedDyadicSchedule_target

declarations.signature: theorem cube_log_incidence_lower (q : ℕ) (P F : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hn : 0 < n) (hqn : q ∣ n) (hF : divisorCube q P ⊆ F) : Real.log 2 * (cubePrimeRank q P n : ℝ) ≤ Real.log ((F.filter (fun a => a ∣ n)).card : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A containing finite support inherits the cube's first logarithmic moment.

declarations.name: dyadicBlockCount
declarations.signature: def dyadicBlockCount (P : Finset ℕ) (r n : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Exact dyadic row events, counted as a finite cardinality.

declarations.name: dyadicBlockCount_cast
declarations.signature: theorem dyadicBlockCount_cast (P : Finset ℕ) (r n : ℕ) : (dyadicBlockCount P r n : ℝ) = ∑ p ∈ P, if 2 ^ r * p ∣ n ∧ ¬ 2 * (2 ^ r * p) ∣ n then (1 : ℝ) else 0

declarations.name: odd_cofactor_of_dyadic_event
declarations.signature: theorem odd_cofactor_of_dyadic_event (r p n : ℕ) (hp : ¬ 2 ∣ p) (he : 2 ^ r * p ∣ n ∧ ¬ 2 * (2 ^ r * p) ∣ n) : ∃ u : ℕ, ¬ 2 ∣ u ∧ n = 2 ^ r * u
declarations.docstring: An event supplies the exact odd cofactor; density is not assumed.

declarations.name: dyadic_event_row_unique
declarations.signature: theorem dyadic_event_row_unique (k l p q n : ℕ) (hp : ¬ 2 ∣ p) (hq : ¬ 2 ∣ q) (he : 2 ^ (k + 2) * p ∣ n ∧ ¬ 2 * (2 ^ (k + 2) * p) ∣ n) (hf : 2 ^ (l + 2) * q ∣ n ∧ ¬ 2 * (2 ^ (l + 2) * q) ∣ n) : k = l
declarations.docstring: Row events at different exact dyadic valuations cannot coexist.

declarations.name: dyadic_union_log_pointwise
declarations.signature: theorem dyadic_union_log_pointwise (P : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (J : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hP : ∀ k p, p ∈ P k → Nat.Prime p ∧ 2 < p) : Real.log 2 * (∑ k ∈ J, (dyadicBlockCount (P k) (k + 2) n : ℝ)) ≤ Real.log (((J.biUnion (fun k => dyadicDivisorFrame ((P k).prod id) k)).filter (fun a => a ∣ n)).card : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: First-moment lower bound over any finite collection of dyadic rows.

declarations.name: cubePrimeRank_zero_of_not_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem cubePrimeRank_zero_of_not_dvd (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hqn : ¬ q ∣ n) : cubePrimeRank q P n = 0

declarations.name: cube_log_incidence_exact
declarations.signature: theorem cube_log_incidence_exact (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hn : 0 < n) : Real.log (((divisorCube q P).filter (fun a => a ∣ n)).card : ℝ) = Real.log 2 * (cubePrimeRank q P n : ℝ)

declarations.name: cube_rank_square_mean_lower
declarations.signature: theorem cube_rank_square_mean_lower (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : (primeReciprocalMass P) ^ 2 / (q : ℝ) ≤ (∑ n ∈ Icc 1 (q * P.prod id), (cubePrimeRank q P n : ℝ) ^ 2) / (q * P.prod id : ℕ)
declarations.docstring: A finite variance calculation restricted to the multiples of q. Using the whole period without this restriction would lose a factor q.

declarations.name: cube_logSquare_mean_lower
declarations.signature: theorem cube_logSquare_mean_lower (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : (Real.log 2) ^ 2 * (primeReciprocalMass P) ^ 2 / (2 * (q : ℝ)) ≤ finiteLogSquareMean (divisorCube q P) (q * P.prod id)
declarations.docstring: The exact old-cover obstruction constant on a finite cube.

declarations.name: half_le_log_one_add
declarations.signature: theorem half_le_log_one_add {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hx1 : x ≤ 1) : x / 2 ≤ Real.log (1 + x)
declarations.docstring: Logarithmic lower bound on every Euler-product factor in the needed range.

declarations.name: cubeProductCost_exp_lower
declarations.signature: theorem cubeProductCost_exp_lower (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (z : ℝ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hz : 0 ≤ z) (hz1 : z ≤ 1) : Real.exp (z * primeReciprocalMass P / 2) / (q : ℝ) ≤ cubeProductCost q P z
declarations.docstring: A lower product bound sufficient for both reciprocal and fixed-alpha divergence.

declarations.name: cubeProductCost_quadratic_lower
declarations.signature: theorem cubeProductCost_quadratic_lower (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (z : ℝ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hz : 0 ≤ z) (hz1 : z ≤ 1) : z ^ 2 * (primeReciprocalMass P) ^ 2 / (4 * (q : ℝ)) ≤ cubeProductCost q P z
declarations.docstring: A polynomial lower bound avoids any unproved asymptotic comparison.

declarations.name: cube_reciprocal_sum
declarations.signature: theorem cube_reciprocal_sum (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : (∑ a ∈ divisorCube q P, (1 : ℝ) / a) = cubeProductCost q P 1

declarations.name: squarefree_prime_product
declarations.signature: theorem squarefree_prime_product (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : Squarefree (P.prod id)

declarations.name: prime_product_divisors_eq_powerset
declarations.signature: theorem prime_product_divisors_eq_powerset (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : (P.prod id).divisors = P.powerset.image (fun T => T.prod id)

declarations.name: divisorCube_eq_powerset_image
declarations.signature: theorem divisorCube_eq_powerset_image (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : divisorCube q P = P.powerset.image (fun T => q * T.prod id)

declarations.name: cube_subset_dvd_iff
declarations.signature: theorem cube_subset_dvd_iff (q : ℕ) (P T : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hTP : T ⊆ P) (hn : 0 < n) (hqn : q ∣ n) : q * T.prod id ∣ n ↔ ∀ p ∈ T, q * p ∣ n
declarations.docstring: Divisibility by a squarefree subset product is exactly the collection of its prime-coordinate divisibilities, after cancelling q.

declarations.name: cube_incidence_exact
declarations.signature: theorem cube_incidence_exact (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hn : 0 < n) (hqn : q ∣ n) : ((divisorCube q P).filter (fun a => a ∣ n)).card = 2 ^ cubePrimeRank q P n

declarations.name: cube_incidence_zero
declarations.signature: theorem cube_incidence_zero (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (n : ℕ) (hqn : ¬ q ∣ n) : ((divisorCube q P).filter (fun a => a ∣ n)).card = 0

declarations.name: sum_subset_powers
declarations.signature: theorem sum_subset_powers (P B : Finset ℕ) (hBP : B ⊆ P) (z : ℝ) : (∑ T ∈ P.powerset, if T ⊆ B then z ^ T.card else 0) = (1 + z) ^ B.card
declarations.docstring: Restricted subset sums are the appropriate coordinate product.

declarations.name: cube_fractional_expansion
declarations.signature: theorem cube_fractional_expansion (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (α : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hα : 0 < α) (hn : 0 < n) : (((divisorCube q P).filter (fun a => a ∣ n)).card : ℝ) ^ α = ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, cubeCoefficient q P ((2 : ℝ) ^ α - 1) d
declarations.docstring: Exact positive fractional incidence expansion, including the off-q case.

declarations.name: cubeCoefficient_cost
declarations.signature: theorem cubeCoefficient_cost (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (z : ℝ) : (∑' d : ℕ, cubeCoefficient q P z d / (d : ℝ)) = cubeProductCost q P z
declarations.docstring: Exact cost of the canonical finite majorant.

declarations.name: cubeCoverFrame
declarations.signature: def cubeCoverFrame (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (α : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hα : 0 < α) (hα1 : α ≤ 1) : FiniteCoverFrame
declarations.docstring: All finite-cube data required by the infimum theorem are constructed.

declarations.name: cubeCoverFrame_cost
declarations.signature: theorem cubeCoverFrame_cost (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (α : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hα : 0 < α) (hα1 : α ≤ 1) : (cubeCoverFrame q P α hq hP hα hα1).cost = cubeProductCost q P ((2 : ℝ) ^ α - 1)

declarations.name: cubeProductCost_le_exp
declarations.signature: theorem cubeProductCost_le_exp (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (z : ℝ) (hz : 0 ≤ z) : cubeProductCost q P z ≤ Real.exp (z * primeReciprocalMass P) / (q : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Finite prime products, including the empty prime set.

declarations.name: cube_fractional_mean
declarations.signature: theorem cube_fractional_mean (q : ℕ) (P : Finset ℕ) (α : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) (hα : 0 < α) : (∑ n ∈ Icc 1 (q * P.prod id), (((divisorCube q P).filter (fun a => a ∣ n)).card : ℝ) ^ α) / (q * P.prod id : ℕ) = cubeProductCost q P ((2 : ℝ) ^ α - 1)
declarations.docstring: The complete-period fractional moment equals the canonical cost.

declarations.name: primeSetPart_two_dyadic

declarations.name: dyadic_frame_canonical_weight_sum
declarations.signature: theorem dyadic_frame_canonical_weight_sum (M k : ℕ) (hodd : ¬ 2 ∣ M) : (∑ a ∈ dyadicDivisorFrame M k, primeWeightedTerm 2 {2} a) = (∑ d ∈ M.divisors, (1 : ℝ) / d) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ (2 ^ (k + 2) : ℕ) - 1)

declarations.name: summable_indicator_frame_union
declarations.signature: theorem summable_indicator_frame_union (G : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : ∀ a, 0 ≤ w a) (hs : Summable (fun k => ∑ a ∈ G k, w a)) : Summable (Set.indicator {a | ∃ k, a ∈ G k} w)

declarations.name: summable_canonical_dyadic_host
declarations.signature: theorem summable_canonical_dyadic_host (P : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ k p, p ∈ P k → Nat.Prime p ∧ 2 < p) (hS : ∀ k, (∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ k + 1) : Summable (Set.indicator (dyadicDivisorHost (fun k => (P k).prod id)) (primeWeightedTerm 2 {2}))

declarations.name: exists_infinite_dyadic_weighted_host
declarations.signature: theorem exists_infinite_dyadic_weighted_host : ∃ P : ℕ → Finset ℕ, Pairwise (fun k l => Disjoint (P k) (P l)) ∧ (∀ k, (∀ p ∈ P k, Nat.Prime p ∧ 2 < p) ∧ (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ ∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p ∧ (∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ k + 1) ∧ (dyadicDivisorHost (fun k => (P k).prod id)).Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ dyadicDivisorHost (fun k => (P k).prod id) ∧ FinitePrimeWeighted 2 (dyadicDivisorHost (fun k => (P k).prod id))
declarations.docstring: The prime-block construction supplies an infinite positive host satisfying the original binary finite-prime weighted criterion.

declarations.name: sum_divisors_prime_product
declarations.signature: theorem sum_divisors_prime_product (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : (∑ d ∈ (P.prod id).divisors, d) = ∏ p ∈ P, (p + 1)
declarations.docstring: Sum of divisors of a product of distinct primes.

declarations.name: reciprocal_divisor_sum_eq
declarations.signature: theorem reciprocal_divisor_sum_eq (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) : (∑ d ∈ M.divisors, (1 : ℝ) / d) = (∑ d ∈ M.divisors, (d : ℝ)) / (M : ℝ)

declarations.name: reciprocal_divisor_prime_product
declarations.signature: theorem reciprocal_divisor_prime_product (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : (∑ d ∈ (P.prod id).divisors, (1 : ℝ) / d) = ∏ p ∈ P, (1 + (1 : ℝ) / p)

declarations.name: reciprocal_divisor_prime_product_le_exp
declarations.signature: theorem reciprocal_divisor_prime_product_le_exp (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : (∑ d ∈ (P.prod id).divisors, (1 : ℝ) / d) ≤ Real.exp (∑ p ∈ P, (1 : ℝ) / p)
declarations.docstring: Harmonic mass bounds the actual reciprocal divisor sum.

declarations.name: divisorFrameBudget_le_geometric

declarations.name: summable_divisorFrameBudget
declarations.signature: theorem summable_divisorFrameBudget (P : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ k p, p ∈ P k → Nat.Prime p) (hS : ∀ k, (∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ k + 1) : Summable (fun k => divisorFrameBudget (P k) k)

declarations.name: exists_disjoint_prime_blocks_summable_divisor_budgets
declarations.signature: theorem exists_disjoint_prime_blocks_summable_divisor_budgets : ∃ P : ℕ → Finset ℕ, Pairwise (fun k l => Disjoint (P k) (P l)) ∧ (∀ k, (∀ p ∈ P k, Nat.Prime p ∧ 2 < p) ∧ (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ ∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p ∧ (∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ k + 1) ∧ Summable (fun k => divisorFrameBudget (P k) k)
declarations.docstring: Concrete disjoint odd-prime blocks have a summable divisor-frame budget; the harmonic supply is proved, not an assumed supplier.

declarations.name: dyadic_exponent_eq_of_odd_cofactors

declarations.name: exists_dyadic_event_period

declarations.name: mean_dyadicBlockCounts
declarations.signature: theorem mean_dyadicBlockCounts (P : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (J : Finset ℕ) (X : ℕ) (hP : ∀ k p, p ∈ P k → 0 < p) (hX : 0 < X) (hperiod : ∀ k ∈ J, ∀ p ∈ P k, 2 * (2 ^ (k + 2) * p) ∣ X) : (∑ n ∈ Icc 1 X, ∑ k ∈ J, (dyadicBlockCount (P k) (k + 2) n : ℝ)) / X = ∑ k ∈ J, (∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p) / (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))

declarations.name: harmonic_row_event_lower
declarations.signature: theorem harmonic_row_event_lower (P : Finset ℕ) (k : ℕ) (hS : (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ ∑ p ∈ P, (1 : ℝ) / p) : (1 / 8 : ℝ) ≤ (∑ p ∈ P, (1 : ℝ) / p) / (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (k + 2))
declarations.docstring: Each prescribed row contributes at least one eighth to the event mean.

declarations.name: dyadic_finite_logarithmic_growth
declarations.signature: theorem dyadic_finite_logarithmic_growth (P : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ) (hP : ∀ k p, p ∈ P k → Nat.Prime p ∧ 2 < p) (hS : ∀ k, (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ ∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p) : ∃ X : ℕ, 0 < X ∧ Real.exp 1 * Real.log 2 * (m : ℝ) / 8 ≤ finiteLogarithmicMean ((Finset.range m).biUnion (fun k => dyadicDivisorFrame ((P k).prod id) k)) X

declarations.name: dyadic_host_unbounded_finite_logarithmic_means
declarations.signature: theorem dyadic_host_unbounded_finite_logarithmic_means (P : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ k p, p ∈ P k → Nat.Prime p ∧ 2 < p) (hS : ∀ k, (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ ∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p) : ∀ R : ℝ, ∃ F : Finset ℕ, (F : Set ℕ) ⊆ dyadicDivisorHost (fun k => (P k).prod id) ∧ ∃ X : ℕ, 0 < X ∧ R < finiteLogarithmicMean F X

declarations.name: finiteLogarithmicMean_le_reciprocal
declarations.signature: theorem finiteLogarithmicMean_le_reciprocal (F : Finset ℕ) (hF : 0 ∉ F) (X : ℕ) (hX : 0 < X) : finiteLogarithmicMean F X ≤ Real.exp 1 * (∑ a ∈ F, (1 : ℝ) / a)
declarations.docstring: An elementary universal upper bound: logarithmic incidence costs at most ordinary reciprocal mass. This includes cardinality zero without log-positive notation.

declarations.name: not_summable_reciprocal_of_unbounded_finite_means
declarations.signature: theorem not_summable_reciprocal_of_unbounded_finite_means (A : Set ℕ) (hA0 : 0 ∉ A) (hlarge : ∀ R : ℝ, ∃ F : Finset ℕ, (F : Set ℕ) ⊆ A ∧ ∃ X : ℕ, 0 < X ∧ R < finiteLogarithmicMean F X) : ¬ Summable (Set.indicator A (fun a : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / a))

declarations.name: no_logBudgetCover_dyadic_host
declarations.signature: theorem no_logBudgetCover_dyadic_host (P : ℕ → Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ k p, p ∈ P k → Nat.Prime p ∧ 2 < p) (hS : ∀ k, (2 : ℝ) ^ k ≤ ∑ p ∈ P k, (1 : ℝ) / p) : IsEmpty (LogBudgetCover (dyadicDivisorHost (fun k => (P k).prod id)))

declarations.name: exists_weighted_host_outside_every_logBudgetCover
declarations.signature: theorem exists_weighted_host_outside_every_logBudgetCover : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ 0 ∉ A ∧ FinitePrimeWeighted 2 A ∧ ¬ Summable (Set.indicator A (fun a : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / a)) ∧ IsEmpty (LogBudgetCover A) ∧ (∀ B : Set ℕ, B ⊆ A → B.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b B))
declarations.docstring: The complete A_W endpoint, including its actual construction and all-base heredity. There is no moment-growth or no-cover hypothesis in this theorem.

declarations.name: normalised_geom_prefix_le

declarations.name: pow_sub_one_ratio_le

declarations.name: kernelWeight_le_of_twice_lt
declarations.signature: theorem kernelWeight_le_of_twice_lt {B : ℝ} (hB : 1 < B) (d N : ℕ) (hfar : 2 * N < d) : kernelWeight B d N ≤ 1 / ((d : ℝ) * (B - 1))

declarations.name: progressionMean_kernel_le_of_far

declarations.name: ReverseRow
declarations.docstring: Arithmetic row data only: no analytic endpoint occurs among the fields.

declarations.name: exists_reverseRow
declarations.docstring: Every row is supplied by Euclid's prime theorem and the checked finite harmonic-block theorem. No cover or obstruction is supplied as a premise.

declarations.name: ReverseRow.scale_le_sqrt
declarations.signature: theorem ReverseRow.scale_le_sqrt {j : ℕ} (R : ReverseRow j) : (reverseScale j : ℝ) ≤ Real.sqrt R.q

declarations.name: ReverseRow.q_gt_index

declarations.name: ReverseRow.mass_ge_index

declarations.docstring: The strengthened first-log cost is geometrically summable.

declarations.name: ReverseRow.square_mass_ratio

declarations.name: reverse_strengthened_term_bound

declarations.name: progressionMean_far_conductors_le

declarations.name: progressionMean_frame_le_profile
declarations.signature: theorem progressionMean_frame_le_profile (B : ℝ) (hB2 : 2 ≤ B) (Q G j : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hG : 0 < G) (h : ℕ → ℕ) (hprof : GcdProfile Q G h) (F : Finset ℕ) (hF : ∀ a ∈ F, 0 < a) : progressionMean Q (2^j) (fun N => ∑ a ∈ F, kernelWeight B a N) ≤ (∑ a ∈ F, profileWeight B h a) + profileErrorSum B h F Q j + ((G:ℝ)*((Q:ℝ)+j)+(Q:ℝ)+1)/(B^G-1) + 4*(1/2 : ℝ)^j

declarations.name: dyadicMean_finite_frame_le_profile

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_radix_closeReturn
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_radix_closeReturn (b : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hA : A.Infinite) (hclose : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedRadixSupportAtom b A N d) < (∑' d : ℕ, shiftedRadixSupportAtom b A 0 d) + ε) : Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b A)
declarations.docstring: The all-base lattice endgame accepts the close-return property itself. The weighted and fractional returns need no reciprocal-summability premise.

declarations.name: squarefreeSupport
declarations.docstring: The squarefree support of Erdős #257: squarefree integers `d ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: squarefreeShiftedSupport
declarations.docstring: The squarefree support with the element `1` adjoined. Since `1/(b^1 − 1) = 1/(b − 1)` is rational, this support poses the same irrationality question; see `irrational_erdosSupportSeries_squarefreeSupport_iff_shifted`.

declarations.name: squarefreeDivisors_eq_image
declarations.signature: theorem squarefreeDivisors_eq_image {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : {d ∈ n.divisors | Squarefree d} = n.primeFactors.powerset.image (fun s => ∏ p ∈ s, p)
declarations.docstring: The squarefree divisors of `n` are exactly the products of sets of its prime factors.

declarations.name: card_squarefreeDivisors
declarations.signature: theorem card_squarefreeDivisors {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : #{d ∈ n.divisors | Squarefree d} = 2 ^ n.primeFactors.card
declarations.docstring: **The squarefree divisor count.** A nonzero `n` has exactly `2^ω(n)` squarefree divisors, where `ω(n)` is the number of distinct prime factors.

declarations.name: squarefreeIncidence
declarations.docstring: The divisor incidence of the squarefree support `{d ≥ 2 : d squarefree}`: the number of squarefree divisors of `n` other than `1`.

declarations.name: squarefreeIncidence_eq
declarations.signature: theorem squarefreeIncidence_eq {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : squarefreeIncidence n = 2 ^ n.primeFactors.card - 1
declarations.docstring: **Exact incidence of the squarefree support.** For every `n ≥ 1`, `sc_A(n) = 2^ω(n) − 1`.

declarations.name: odd_squarefreeIncidence
declarations.signature: theorem odd_squarefreeIncidence {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : Odd (squarefreeIncidence n)
declarations.docstring: **The squarefree incidence is odd at every `n ≥ 2`.** This is what closes the parity door: the block conditions of both engines force an even coefficient somewhere inside the first block (`dvd_last_of_carry_block`), and no even value ever occurs.

declarations.name: one_le_squarefreeIncidence
declarations.signature: theorem one_le_squarefreeIncidence {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 1 ≤ squarefreeIncidence n
declarations.docstring: **The squarefree support is dense in the coefficient sense**: every `n ≥ 2` has at least one squarefree divisor `≥ 2`, namely any prime factor. This is what closes the *gap* door: the engines' other regime, `K = 0`, needs the coefficients to be small over a long block, and here they never vanish.

declarations.name: two_pow_card_primeFactors_le
declarations.signature: theorem two_pow_card_primeFactors_le {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : 2 ^ n.primeFactors.card ≤ n
declarations.docstring: The shifted coefficient `2^ω(n)` never leaves the Erdős coefficient range `1 ≤ c(n) ≤ n`, so the repair of the parity by adjoining `1` to the support keeps the sequence admissible for the engines.

declarations.name: supportCoeff_squarefreeSupport
declarations.signature: theorem supportCoeff_squarefreeSupport (n : ℕ) : Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport n = squarefreeIncidence n
declarations.docstring: The engine's coefficient at the squarefree support is exactly the incidence computed above.

declarations.name: dvd_last_of_carry_block
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_last_of_carry_block {b N K : ℕ} {c : ℕ → ℕ} (hK : 1 ≤ K) (h : b ^ K ∣ ∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, c (N + r) * b ^ (K - r)) : b ∣ c (N + K)
declarations.docstring: **The parity kernel of both block conditions.** A first block certified in carried aggregate — the weaker of the two conditions — still forces the base to divide the coefficient at the *last* position of the block. Every other term of the carry sum carries a positive power of `b`.

declarations.name: no_carry_block_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem no_carry_block_certificate {b N K L C : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hbeven : 2 ∣ b) (hcarry : b ^ K ∣ ∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, squarefreeIncidence (N + r) * b ^ (K - r)) (hmiddle : ∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, squarefreeIncidence (N + r) * b ^ (L - r) ≤ C) (harith : b ^ 2 * (C + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L) : False
declarations.docstring: **No carry block certificate exists at the squarefree support.** For every even base `b ≥ 2` the single precision `q = b²` already admits no tuple `(N, K, L, C)` satisfying the carry-aware block certificate. Two independent facts about the support are used, one for each regime the schema allows: * `K ≥ 1` is impossible by parity — `dvd_last_of_carry_block` forces `b ∣ sc_A(N+K)`, and `sc_A` is odd at every argument `≥ 2` while `b` is even, so the block would have to reach the single position `n = 1`; * `K ≤ 1` is then impossible by density — the coefficient at `N + 2` is at least `1`, so the middle block alone spends the whole budget `b^L`. The obstruction is therefore uniform in the block position, and quantitative: it is not that a search has not gone far enough.

declarations.name: not_exists_carry_certificates_squarefreeSupport
declarations.signature: theorem not_exists_carry_certificates_squarefreeSupport {b : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hbeven : 2 ∣ b) : ¬ (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∃ N K L C : ℕ, K ≤ L ∧ (b ^ K ∣ ∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport (N + r) * b ^ (K - r)) ∧ (∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport (N + r) * b ^ (L - r) ≤ C) ∧ (∃ t : ℕ, 0 < Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport (N + L + 1 + t)) ∧ q * (C + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L)
declarations.docstring: **The carry-aware engine has no instance at the squarefree support.** The statement quotes the hypothesis of `Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_weighted_coeff_carry_certificates` verbatim, at the squarefree support, and refutes it for every even base.

declarations.name: not_exists_digitwise_certificates_squarefreeSupport
declarations.signature: theorem not_exists_digitwise_certificates_squarefreeSupport {b : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hbeven : 2 ∣ b) : ¬ (∀ q : ℕ, 0 < q → ∃ N K L C : ℕ, K ≤ L ∧ (∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, b ^ r ∣ Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport (N + r)) ∧ (∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc (K + 1) L, Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport (N + r) * b ^ (L - r) ≤ C) ∧ (∃ t : ℕ, 0 < Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeSupport (N + L + 1 + t)) ∧ q * (C + (N + L + 2)) < b ^ L)
declarations.docstring: **The digitwise engine has no instance at the squarefree support.** The statement quotes the hypothesis of `Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_weighted_coeff_certificates` verbatim. It is refuted through the carry form, using the development's own proof that the carry interface subsumes the digitwise one.

declarations.name: supportCoeff_squarefreeShiftedSupport
declarations.signature: theorem supportCoeff_squarefreeShiftedSupport {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeShiftedSupport n = 2 ^ n.primeFactors.card
declarations.docstring: The shifted support has coefficient `2^ω(n)`.

declarations.name: irrational_erdosSupportSeries_squarefreeSupport_iff_shifted
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_erdosSupportSeries_squarefreeSupport_iff_shifted (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : Irrational (Erdos249257.erdosSupportSeries b squarefreeSupport) ↔ Irrational (Erdos249257.erdosSupportSeries b squarefreeShiftedSupport)
declarations.docstring: **The shift is free.** Adjoining `1` to the squarefree support changes the value by `1/(b − 1)`, a rational, so the two supports pose the same irrationality question. Both directions go through the development's own finite-prefix invariance theorems.

declarations.name: coprime_primeBlockModulus

declarations.name: exists_omega_ge_block
declarations.signature: theorem exists_omega_ge_block (K : ℕ) : ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, r ≤ (N + r).primeFactors.card
declarations.docstring: **Arbitrarily long prescribed `ω`-blocks.** For every `K` there is a positive `N` with `ω(N + r) ≥ r` for every `1 ≤ r ≤ K`. Chinese remainder over disjoint blocks of primes.

declarations.name: exists_digitwise_block_squarefreeShiftedSupport
declarations.signature: theorem exists_digitwise_block_squarefreeShiftedSupport (K : ℕ) : ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ ∀ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 K, 2 ^ r ∣ Erdos249257.supportCoeff squarefreeShiftedSupport (N + r)
declarations.docstring: **The parity obstruction does not survive the shift.** For every block length `K` the shifted support admits a position `N` at which the *full* digitwise opening condition of the base-`2` engine holds — the condition whose failure at the unshifted support is `no_carry_block_certificate`.

declarations.name: sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le_gcdBlockCount
declarations.signature: theorem sum_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le_gcdBlockCount (Q d K : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hd : 0 < d) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range K, shiftedMersenneAtom ((k + 1) * Q) d ≤ (((K / (d / Nat.gcd Q d) : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1) / ((2 : ℝ) ^ Nat.gcd Q d - 1)
declarations.docstring: Retain the geometric factor in both full blocks and the incomplete block.

declarations.name: cesaroMean_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le_gcdMean_add_error
declarations.signature: theorem cesaroMean_shiftedMersenneAtom_mul_le_gcdMean_add_error (Q d K : ℕ) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hd : 0 < d) (hK : 0 < K) : cesaroMean (fun k => shiftedMersenneAtom ((k + 1) * Q) d) K ≤ (Nat.gcd Q d : ℝ) / ((d : ℝ) * ((2 : ℝ) ^ Nat.gcd Q d - 1)) + 1 / ((K : ℝ) * ((2 : ℝ) ^ Nat.gcd Q d - 1))
declarations.docstring: The error of a finite progression average is at most one GCD orbit.

declarations.name: sum_half_pow_le_twice_min
declarations.signature: theorem sum_half_pow_le_twice_min (s : Finset ℕ) (m : ℕ) (hm : ∀ j ∈ s, m ≤ j) : ∑ j ∈ s, (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ j ≤ 2 * (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ m
declarations.docstring: A finite geometric tail, indexed by an arbitrary finite set.

declarations.name: sum_dyadic_observation_weights_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_dyadic_observation_weights_le (J : Finset ℕ) (Q a : ℕ) (ha : 0 < a) : ∑ j ∈ J.filter (fun j => a ≤ Q * 2 ^ j), (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ j ≤ 2 * (Q : ℝ) / a
declarations.docstring: A conductor's dyadic observation weights have total mass at most `2Q/a`. No infinite sum or interchange of limits occurs.

declarations.name: dyadic_observation_sum_le
declarations.signature: theorem dyadic_observation_sum_le (J F : Finset ℕ) (Q : ℕ) (α : ℕ → ℝ) (hF : ∀ a ∈ F, 0 < a) (hα : ∀ a ∈ F, 0 ≤ α a) : (∑ j ∈ J, (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ j * ∑ a ∈ F.filter (fun a => a ≤ Q * 2 ^ j), α a) ≤ 2 * (Q : ℝ) * ∑ a ∈ F, α a / a
declarations.docstring: The finite weighted dyadic averaging inequality used to control the incomplete-period term when the ordinary reciprocal mass diverges.

declarations.name: witnessClauseSupport
declarations.signature: def witnessClauseSupport (C : Finset ℕ) : Set ℕ
declarations.docstring: The arithmetic support for one nonempty clause of primes.

declarations.name: clause_product_pos
declarations.signature: theorem clause_product_pos (C : Finset ℕ) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p) : 0 < C.prod id

declarations.name: clause_product_factorization
declarations.signature: theorem clause_product_factorization (C : Finset ℕ) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p) (p : ℕ) : (C.prod id).factorization p = if p ∈ C then 1 else 0
declarations.docstring: A product over a finite prime set is squarefree, including its valuations at primes outside that set.

declarations.name: coprime_clause_factorization
declarations.signature: theorem coprime_clause_factorization (C : Finset ℕ) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p) (m : ℕ) (hm : Nat.Coprime m (C.prod id)) {p : ℕ} (hp : p ∈ C) : m.factorization p = 0
declarations.docstring: All clause primes have zero valuation in an allowed cofactor.

declarations.name: clause_layer_factorization
declarations.signature: theorem clause_layer_factorization (C : Finset ℕ) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p) (k m p : ℕ) (hm : m ≠ 0) : (C.prod id ^ k * m).factorization p = k * (if p ∈ C then 1 else 0) + m.factorization p

declarations.name: clause_layer_factorization_of_mem
declarations.signature: theorem clause_layer_factorization_of_mem (C : Finset ℕ) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p) (k m : ℕ) (hm : m ≠ 0) (hcop : Nat.Coprime m (C.prod id)) {p : ℕ} (hp : p ∈ C) : (C.prod id ^ k * m).factorization p = k
declarations.docstring: Every clause prime reads off the unique layer index.

declarations.name: clause_layer_index_unique
declarations.signature: theorem clause_layer_index_unique (C : Finset ℕ) (hCn : C.Nonempty) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p) (k l m n : ℕ) (hm : m ≠ 0) (hn : n ≠ 0) (hmc : Nat.Coprime m (C.prod id)) (hnc : Nat.Coprime n (C.prod id)) (heq : C.prod id ^ k * m = C.prod id ^ l * n) : k = l
declarations.docstring: Distinct positive coprime layers are disjoint.

declarations.name: clause_layer_pair_unique
declarations.signature: theorem clause_layer_pair_unique (C : Finset ℕ) (hCn : C.Nonempty) (hC : ∀ p ∈ C, Nat.Prime p) (k l m n : ℕ) (hm : m ≠ 0) (hn : n ≠ 0) (hmc : Nat.Coprime m (C.prod id)) (hnc : Nat.Coprime n (C.prod id)) (heq : C.prod id ^ k * m = C.prod id ^ l * n) : k = l ∧ m = n
declarations.docstring: The cofactor is unique as well as the layer index.

declarations.name: restricted_prime_part_clause_layer

declarations.name: dyadic_progressionHarmonicMass_half_lower

declarations.name: clauseProgression_row_reciprocal

declarations.name: clauseProgression_row_reciprocal_lower

declarations.name: summable_indicator_union_iff
declarations.signature: theorem summable_indicator_union_iff (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : ∀ a, 0 ≤ w a) (A B : Set ℕ) : Summable (Set.indicator (A ∪ B) w) ↔ Summable (Set.indicator A w) ∧ Summable (Set.indicator B w)

declarations.name: finiteBlockHost

declarations.docstring: The support selected by a finite family of blocks.

declarations.name: summable_finiteBlockHost_iff
declarations.signature: theorem summable_finiteBlockHost_iff {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : ∀ a, 0 ≤ w a) (B : ι → Set ℕ) (H : Finset ι) : Summable (Set.indicator (finiteBlockHost B H) w) ↔ ∀ i ∈ H, Summable (Set.indicator (B i) w)
declarations.docstring: Overlapping blocks cause no problem: a nonnegative weighted series over their finite union converges exactly when every block series converges.

declarations.name: upward_rule_iff_hits_forbidden
declarations.signature: theorem upward_rule_iff_hits_forbidden (E P : Finset ℕ) (U : Finset ℕ → Prop) (hUp : ∀ S T : Finset ℕ, S ⊆ T → U S → U T) (hPE : P ⊆ E) : U P ↔ ∀ M : Finset ℕ, M ⊆ E → ¬ U M → (P ∩ (E \ M)).Nonempty
declarations.docstring: An upward-closed rule on subsets of a finite prime set is determined by which complements of forbidden sets a proposed witness meets. This version uses all forbidden sets; discarding nonmaximal ones is a later simplification.

declarations.name: ruleBlockHost

declarations.docstring: The finite union implementing a rule from blocks for the complements of its forbidden sets. This definition supplies no arithmetic block theorem.

declarations.name: summable_ruleBlockHost_iff
declarations.signature: theorem summable_ruleBlockHost_iff (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : ∀ a, 0 ≤ w a) (E P : Finset ℕ) (U : Finset ℕ → Prop) (B : Finset ℕ → Set ℕ) (hUp : ∀ S T : Finset ℕ, S ⊆ T → U S → U T) (hPE : P ⊆ E) (hblock : ∀ M : Finset ℕ, M ⊆ E → ¬ U M → (Summable (Set.indicator (B (E \ M)) w) ↔ (P ∩ (E \ M)).Nonempty)) : Summable (Set.indicator (ruleBlockHost E U B) w) ↔ U P
declarations.docstring: Once each clause block has its stated summability classification, the explicit finite union realizes the complete upward-closed rule. The clause classification is an explicit hypothesis, not a claimed arithmetic result.

declarations.name: forbidden_clause_nonempty

declarations.name: summable_primeWeightedTerm_witnessLogicHost_iff
declarations.signature: theorem summable_primeWeightedTerm_witnessLogicHost_iff (E : Finset ℕ) (hE : ∀ p ∈ E, Nat.Prime p) (U : Finset ℕ → Prop) (hUp : ∀ S T : Finset ℕ, S ⊆ T → U S → U T) (hUE : U E) (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (P : Finset ℕ) (hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) : Summable (Set.indicator (witnessLogicHost E U) (primeWeightedTerm b P)) ↔ U (P ∩ E)

declarations.name: zero_not_mem_witnessLogicHost

declarations.docstring: The host contains no zero: each clause element is a positive multiple.

declarations.name: not_summable_reciprocal_witnessLogicHost

declarations.name: witnessLogicHost_allBase_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem witnessLogicHost_allBase_irrational (E : Finset ℕ) (hE : ∀ p ∈ E, Nat.Prime p) (U : Finset ℕ → Prop) (hUp : ∀ S T : Finset ℕ, S ⊆ T → U S → U T) (hUE : U E) (hU0 : ¬ U ∅) : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A ⊆ witnessLogicHost E U → A.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b A)
declarations.docstring: Every infinite subset of the host has irrational support series in every base `b ≥ 2`, through the full witness `E` at base two and the checked weighted theorem.

declarations.name: finite_monotone_witness_rule_realised
declarations.signature: theorem finite_monotone_witness_rule_realised (E : Finset ℕ) (hE : ∀ p ∈ E, Nat.Prime p) (U : Finset ℕ → Prop) (hUp : ∀ S T : Finset ℕ, S ⊆ T → U S → U T) (hUE : U E) (hU0 : ¬ U ∅) : ∃ H : Set ℕ, 0 ∉ H ∧ (∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → ∀ P : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) → (Summable (Set.indicator H (primeWeightedTerm b P)) ↔ U (P ∩ E))) ∧ ¬ Summable (Set.indicator H (fun a : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / a)) ∧ (∀ A : Set ℕ, A ⊆ H → A.Infinite → ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → Irrational (erdosSupportSeries b A))
declarations.docstring: **Finite monotone witness logic is realisable.** For each finite prime set `E` and each nonconstant upward-closed rule `U`, one host `H` without zero has: weighted summability at every base `b ≥ 2` and every finite prime witness `P` exactly when `U (P ∩ E)`; a divergent reciprocal sum; and irrational support series for every infinite subset in every base.

declarations.name: summable_nat_div_pow_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem summable_nat_div_pow_sub_one (b : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) : Summable (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ n - 1))
declarations.docstring: The Lambert coefficient series is bounded by a polynomial times a geometric series. At `n = 0`, total division makes the term zero.

declarations.name: summable_clause_series

declarations.docstring: For a nonempty prime intersection, the clause comparison series is a subseries of a summable Lambert coefficient series.

declarations.name: summable_clause_series_iff
declarations.signature: theorem summable_clause_series_iff (b g : ℕ) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hg : 1 ≤ g) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => ((g ^ k : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((b : ℝ) ^ (g ^ k) - 1)) ↔ 2 ≤ g
declarations.docstring: A missing intersection (`g = 1`) yields a nonzero constant series; every larger intersection product yields a summable series.

declarations.name: suffixCorrection
declarations.signature: def suffixCorrection : List ℤ → ℤ | [] => 0 | p :: ps => (p - 1) * ps.prod + suffixCorrection ps /-- **The suffix telescope.** A product is one plus the sum of its suffix corrections. Applied to the list of internal primes lying after a block element, this is exactly the expansion of the height quotient that produces the checker's block digit. -/ theorem List.prod_eq_one_add_suffixCorrection (ps : List ℤ) : ps.prod = 1 + suffixCorrection ps
declarations.docstring: The telescoping correction of a list of factors: the `r`-th term is `(p_r - 1)` times the product of everything after it.

declarations.name: List.prod_eq_one_add_suffixCorrection
declarations.signature: theorem List.prod_eq_one_add_suffixCorrection (ps : List ℤ) : ps.prod = 1 + suffixCorrection ps
declarations.docstring: **The suffix telescope.** A product is one plus the sum of its suffix corrections. Applied to the list of internal primes lying after a block element, this is exactly the expansion of the height quotient that produces the checker's block digit.

declarations.name: suffixCorrection_pair
declarations.signature: theorem suffixCorrection_pair (p q : ℤ) : suffixCorrection [p, q] = (p - 1) * q + (q - 1)
declarations.docstring: The two-jump case in closed form: the three possible suffix products of a block element sitting below both, between, or above the internal jumps.

declarations.name: tailCap
declarations.docstring: The checker's state cap `9·T_a ≤ κ(J_a)`, in numerator form.

declarations.name: tailCap_bellman
declarations.signature: theorem tailCap_bellman (J : ℕ) : 2 * tailCap J = (J + 4) ^ 2 + tailCap (J + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The Bellman identity.** Doubling the cap at rank `J` splits exactly into the current shell bound `(J+4)²` and the cap at rank `J+1`. This is why the constant is `27` and not something smaller: `κ` is the exact fixed point of the backwards shell recursion under a jump multiplier of at least `2`.

declarations.name: tailCap_lt_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tailCap_lt_succ (J : ℕ) : tailCap J < tailCap (J + 1)
declarations.docstring: The cap is strictly increasing, so a later anchor never tightens it.

declarations.name: tailCap_step_of_shellMass
declarations.signature: theorem tailCap_step_of_shellMass {J b d : ℕ} (hb : 2 ≤ b) (hd : 9 * d ≤ (J + 4) ^ 2) : 9 * d + tailCap (J + 1) ≤ b * tailCap J
declarations.docstring: A single shell bound feeds the affine-cylinder cap inequality. The only source-specific input is the shell mass estimate `9 * d ≤ (J + 4)²`; every jump multiplier at least two then has enough Bellman budget to absorb that mass and advance the rank by one.

declarations.name: tailCap_step_compose
declarations.signature: theorem tailCap_step_compose {A A' A'' b c d e : ℕ} (h₁ : 9 * d + A' ≤ b * A) (h₂ : 9 * e + A'' ≤ c * A') : 9 * (c * d + e) + A'' ≤ (c * b) * A
declarations.docstring: Consecutive affine cap inequalities compose without loss. If the first step has digit `d` and the next has digit `e`, their compressed digit is `c*d+e`; the resulting cap inequality has radix `c*b`. Together with `tailCap_step_of_shellMass`, this is the exact algebra needed to compress the one, two, or three pure-power jumps in an actual dyadic `{2,3,5}` block.

declarations.name: NearInteger
declarations.docstring: A real number lies strictly within `δ` of an integer.

declarations.name: FarFromIntegers
declarations.docstring: A real number is at least `δ` from every integer.

declarations.name: affine_nearInteger_alignment_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem affine_nearInteger_alignment_of_le {B P : ℕ} {x y : ℝ} {c m n : ℤ} (hP : P ≤ B) (hrec : y = (P : ℝ) * x - (c : ℝ)) (hx : |x - (m : ℝ)| < 1 / ((B : ℝ) + 1)) (hy : |y - (n : ℝ)| < 1 / ((B : ℝ) + 1)) : n = (P : ℤ) * m - c
declarations.docstring: Two consecutive `1/(B+1)`-near-integer witnesses in an affine step of integer radix at most `B` must obey the same affine integer recurrence.

declarations.name: one_div_thirtyOne_eq
declarations.docstring: The `1/31` threshold is `1/(B+1)` at `B = 30`.

declarations.name: affine_nearInteger_alignment

declarations.name: cubic_difference_boundary_strips

declarations.name: dSum_eq

declarations.name: heckeMahlerSeries
declarations.signature: def heckeMahlerSeries (θ β α : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The Hecke--Mahler series `F_θ(β,α) = ∑_{n≥1} ∑_{k=1}^{⌊nθ⌋} β^n α^k`. The outer index runs over all `n ≥ 0`; the inner sum is empty at `n = 0`.

declarations.name: BugeaudLaurentTranscendence
declarations.docstring: Bugeaud and Laurent, Theorem 1.1, in the case `ρ = 0` due to Loxton and van der Poorten, Theorem 8, p. 40: the Hecke--Mahler series takes transcendental values at nonzero algebraic arguments inside the stated region. This is the one external input of the two-prime theorem.

declarations.name: sum_Icc_pow
declarations.signature: theorem sum_Icc_pow {y : ℝ} (hy : y ≠ 1) (m : ℕ) : ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, y ^ k = (y - y ^ (m + 1)) / (1 - y)

declarations.name: qExp_eq_floor

declarations.name: aSum_eq_heckeValue
declarations.signature: theorem aSum_eq_heckeValue {p q : ℕ} (hp : 1 < p) (hq : 1 < q) : (∑' n : ℕ, aTerm p q n) = PaperR7.twoPrimeHeckeValue p q
declarations.docstring: The paper's `A`: the series over the pure powers of `p` is the boundary value already recorded in the tree.

declarations.name: heckeValue_boundary
declarations.signature: theorem heckeValue_boundary {p q : ℕ} (hp : 1 < p) (hq : 1 < q) : (∑' n : ℕ, aTerm p q n) = (p : ℝ) / ((p : ℝ) - 1) - ((q : ℝ) - 1) * heckeMahlerSeries (Real.logb q p) ((p : ℝ)⁻¹) ((q : ℝ)⁻¹)

declarations.name: transcendental_heckeValue
declarations.signature: theorem transcendental_heckeValue (hBL : BugeaudLaurentTranscendence) {p q : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) : Transcendental ℚ (PaperR7.twoPrimeHeckeValue p q)

declarations.name: two_prime_affine_and_quadratic
declarations.signature: theorem two_prime_affine_and_quadratic {p q : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) : distinctSum p q = (((q : ℝ) - (p : ℝ)) * PaperR7.twoPrimeHeckeValue p q + (p : ℝ)) / ((q : ℝ) - 1) ∧ repeatedSum p q = (((p : ℝ) + (q : ℝ) - 1) * PaperR7.twoPrimeHeckeValue p q - ((p : ℝ) - 1) * (PaperR7.twoPrimeHeckeValue p q) ^ 2) / ((q : ℝ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: The short paper's displayed identities `eq:two-prime-affine`: both two-prime sums are explicit polynomials over `ℚ` in the single boundary value `A`.

declarations.name: two_prime_sums_transcendental
declarations.signature: theorem two_prime_sums_transcendental (hBL : BugeaudLaurentTranscendence) {p q : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hpq : p < q) : Transcendental ℚ (distinctSum p q) ∧ Transcendental ℚ (repeatedSum p q)
