declarations.docstring: A canonical radix-`m` factorial digit is strictly smaller than `m`.

declarations.name: canonicalRemainder_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalRemainder_recurrence (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : canonicalRemainder x (m + 1) = (m + 1 : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder x m - (canonicalDigit x (m + 1) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Exact remainder recurrence: multiply by the next radix and subtract the new canonical digit.

declarations.name: canonicalRemainder_div_factorial_step
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalRemainder_div_factorial_step (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : canonicalRemainder x m / (m.factorial : ℝ) = (canonicalDigit x (m + 1) : ℝ) / ((m + 1).factorial : ℝ) + canonicalRemainder x (m + 1) / ((m + 1).factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Telescoping step for the factorial expansion.

declarations.name: factorial_expansion_partial
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_expansion_partial (x : ℝ) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) : x = (⌊x⌋ : ℝ) + ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 N, (canonicalDigit x m : ℝ) / (m.factorial : ℝ) + canonicalRemainder x N / (N.factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite canonical factorial expansion with an explicit remainder.

declarations.name: zero_remainder_step
declarations.signature: theorem zero_remainder_step (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) (hzero : canonicalRemainder x m = 0) : canonicalDigit x (m + 1) = 0 ∧ canonicalRemainder x (m + 1) = 0
declarations.docstring: A zero remainder forces the next digit and next remainder to vanish.

declarations.name: zero_remainder_add
declarations.signature: theorem zero_remainder_add (x : ℝ) (m k : ℕ) (hzero : canonicalRemainder x m = 0) : canonicalRemainder x (m + k) = 0
declarations.docstring: Once a canonical remainder is zero, every later remainder is zero.

declarations.name: zero_remainder_forces_zero_digit_tail
declarations.signature: theorem zero_remainder_forces_zero_digit_tail (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) (hzero : canonicalRemainder x m = 0) : ∀ r > m, canonicalDigit x r = 0
declarations.docstring: A zero remainder is an exact certificate for a terminating factorial-digit tail.

declarations.name: canonicalRemainder_linear_growth_of_zero_digits
declarations.signature: private theorem canonicalRemainder_linear_growth_of_zero_digits (x : ℝ) {N : ℕ} (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hzero : ∀ n ≥ N, canonicalDigit x (n + 1) = 0) (k : ℕ) : ((k : ℝ) + 1) * canonicalRemainder x N ≤ canonicalRemainder x (N + k)

declarations.name: canonicalRemainder_eq_zero_of_zero_digit_tail
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalRemainder_eq_zero_of_zero_digit_tail (x : ℝ) {N : ℕ} (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hzero : ∀ n ≥ N, canonicalDigit x (n + 1) = 0) : canonicalRemainder x N = 0
declarations.docstring: An eventually zero canonical digit sequence cannot conceal a positive fractional remainder at the start of the tail.

declarations.name: exists_rat_eq_of_canonicalRemainder_eq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem exists_rat_eq_of_canonicalRemainder_eq_zero (x : ℝ) (N : ℕ) (hzero : canonicalRemainder x N = 0) : ∃ q : ℚ, (q : ℝ) = x
declarations.docstring: A zero canonical remainder gives the explicit rational value obtained by dividing its factorial-scale floor by the corresponding factorial.

declarations.name: exists_rat_eq_of_eventually_zero_canonicalDigit
declarations.signature: theorem exists_rat_eq_of_eventually_zero_canonicalDigit (x : ℝ) (hzero : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, canonicalDigit x (n + 1) = 0) : ∃ q : ℚ, (q : ℝ) = x
declarations.docstring: Termination of the canonical factorial digits implies rationality.

declarations.name: exists_rat_eq_iff_eventually_zero_canonicalDigit
declarations.signature: theorem exists_rat_eq_iff_eventually_zero_canonicalDigit (x : ℝ) : (∃ q : ℚ, (q : ℝ) = x) ↔ ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, canonicalDigit x (n + 1) = 0
declarations.docstring: A real number is rational exactly when its canonical factorial digits eventually vanish. The floor convention fixes the expansion, so there is no ambiguity from alternative maximal-digit tails.

declarations.name: scaledPrefixInt
declarations.docstring: Integer part of the factorially scaled prefix.

declarations.name: scaledPrefixFrac
declarations.docstring: Fractional carrier of the factorially scaled prefix.

declarations.name: compConstPartial
declarations.docstring: Partial sums of the companion constant series `C_m`.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefix_mul_eq_split
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefix_mul_eq_split (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : ((m.factorial : ℚ)) * factorialGapPrefix m = ((scaledPrefixInt m : ℚ) + scaledPrefixFrac m)

declarations.name: strictSuccessorRat_eq_split
declarations.signature: theorem strictSuccessorRat_eq_split (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : strictFacTopRat (factorialGapPrefix m) m = scaledPrefixInt m + ⌊scaledPrefixFrac m⌋ + 1

declarations.name: scaledPrefixInt_mod_eq_one
declarations.signature: theorem scaledPrefixInt_mod_eq_one {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : scaledPrefixInt m % m = 1

declarations.name: scaledPrefixInt_succ
declarations.signature: theorem scaledPrefixInt_succ {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : scaledPrefixInt (m + 1) = (m + 1) * scaledPrefixInt m + 1
declarations.docstring: The integral carrier obeys the exact factorial-radix recurrence.

declarations.name: scaledPrefixInt_succ_mod_mul_eq_add_two
declarations.signature: theorem scaledPrefixInt_succ_mod_mul_eq_add_two {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : scaledPrefixInt (m + 1) % (m * (m + 1)) = m + 2
declarations.docstring: Two radix steps expose a quadratic-modulus residue: the integral carrier at `m+1` is always `m+2` modulo `m(m+1)`.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_iff_floor_frac_congruence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_iff_floor_frac_congruence {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 ↔ ((⌊scaledPrefixFrac m⌋ + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0
declarations.docstring: **Carry congruence normal form.** The unit carry at index `m` is exactly the congruence `⌊F_m⌋ ≡ −2 (mod m)` on the fractional carrier.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_eq_zero_iff_floor_frac_congruence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_eq_zero_iff_floor_frac_congruence {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : factorialGapStepCarry m = 0 ↔ ((⌊scaledPrefixFrac m⌋ + 1 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0
declarations.docstring: **Zero-carry congruence normal form.** The lower rare carry at index `m` is exactly the adjacent residue class `⌊factorialGapScaledFrac m⌋ ≡ -1 (mod m)`. Together with the unit-carry criterion above, the two exceptional carry values are consecutive companion floor residues.

declarations.name: scaledPrefixFrac_succ
declarations.signature: theorem scaledPrefixFrac_succ {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : scaledPrefixFrac (m + 1) = (m + 1 : ℚ) * scaledPrefixFrac m + 1 / ((((m + 1).factorial : ℕ) : ℚ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: The companion carrier is itself a non-autonomous factorial orbit. The new endpoint contributes the tiny positive kick `1 / ((m+1)!-1)`.

declarations.name: floor_scaledPrefixFrac_succ
declarations.signature: theorem floor_scaledPrefixFrac_succ {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : ⌊scaledPrefixFrac (m + 1)⌋ = (m + 1 : ℤ) * ⌊scaledPrefixFrac m⌋ + ⌊(m + 1 : ℚ) * Int.fract (scaledPrefixFrac m) + 1 / ((((m + 1).factorial : ℕ) : ℚ) - 1)⌋
declarations.docstring: After removing the integral part of the current carrier, the next carrier floor splits into the old floor multiplied by the new radix and one local digit. This is the exact thin-cylinder coordinate for consecutive carries.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_succ_eq_one_iff_local_digit_congruence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_succ_eq_one_iff_local_digit_congruence {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : factorialGapStepCarry (m + 1) = 1 ↔ ((⌊(m + 1 : ℚ) * Int.fract (scaledPrefixFrac m) + 1 / ((((m + 1).factorial : ℕ) : ℚ) - 1)⌋ + 2 : ℤ) % (m + 1 : ℤ)) = 0
declarations.docstring: The successor unit carry is a congruence on one local digit of the companion orbit. The old integral carrier disappears modulo the new radix.

declarations.name: scaledPrefixFrac_eq_compConstPartial_mul
declarations.signature: theorem scaledPrefixFrac_eq_compConstPartial_mul (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : scaledPrefixFrac m = (m.factorial : ℚ) * compConstPartial m

declarations.name: factorialMoment
declarations.signature: def factorialMoment {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Factorial-weighted sum of a finite coefficient family.

declarations.name: channelNumerator
declarations.signature: def channelNumerator {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The integer numerator of the `d`-th divisor channel.

declarations.name: factorial_pow_dvd_factorial_mul
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_pow_dvd_factorial_mul (d k : ℕ) : d.factorial ^ k ∣ (k * d).factorial
declarations.docstring: `k` labelled blocks of size `d` inject into their union, so `(d!)^k` divides `(kd)!`. This is the exact divisibility behind quotient-band rigidity.

declarations.name: channel_coefficient_band
declarations.signature: theorem channel_coefficient_band {d i k : ℕ} (hlo : k * d ≤ i) (hhi : i < (k + 1) * d) : d.factorial ^ k * (i.factorial / d.factorial ^ (i / d)) = i.factorial
declarations.docstring: On any single quotient band `[kd, (k+1)d)`, the `d`-channel coefficient is the factorial coefficient divided by the fixed integer `(d!)^k`.

declarations.name: channel_coefficient_firstBand
declarations.signature: theorem channel_coefficient_firstBand {d i : ℕ} (hlo : d ≤ i) (hhi : i < 2 * d) : d.factorial * (i.factorial / d.factorial ^ (i / d)) = i.factorial
declarations.docstring: Inside the first quotient band `[d, 2d)`, the `d`-channel coefficient is exactly the factorial coefficient divided by `d!`.

declarations.name: factorialMoment_eq_factorial_pow_mul_channelNumerator_band
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_eq_factorial_pow_mul_channelNumerator_band {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d k : ℕ) (hlo : ∀ j, k * d ≤ index j) (hhi : ∀ j, index j < (k + 1) * d) : factorialMoment coeff index = (d.factorial ^ k : ℤ) * channelNumerator coeff index d
declarations.docstring: If all support indices lie in one quotient band for channel `d`, the factorial moment is `(d!)^k` times that channel numerator.

declarations.name: factorialMoment_eq_zero_of_channelNumerator_eq_zero_band
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_eq_zero_of_channelNumerator_eq_zero_band {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d k : ℕ) (hlo : ∀ j, k * d ≤ index j) (hhi : ∀ j, index j < (k + 1) * d) (hchannel : channelNumerator coeff index d = 0) : factorialMoment coeff index = 0
declarations.docstring: Channel cancellation inside one quotient band forces the corresponding factorial moment to vanish.

declarations.name: factorialMoment_eq_factorial_mul_channelNumerator_firstBand
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_eq_factorial_mul_channelNumerator_firstBand {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) (hlo : ∀ j, d ≤ index j) (hhi : ∀ j, index j < 2 * d) : factorialMoment coeff index = (d.factorial : ℤ) * channelNumerator coeff index d
declarations.docstring: In the first quotient band, the factorial moment is `d!` times the `d`-channel numerator.

declarations.name: factorialMoment_eq_zero_of_channelNumerator_eq_zero_firstBand
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_eq_zero_of_channelNumerator_eq_zero_firstBand {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) (hlo : ∀ j, d ≤ index j) (hhi : ∀ j, index j < 2 * d) (hchannel : channelNumerator coeff index d = 0) : factorialMoment coeff index = 0
declarations.docstring: First-band channel cancellation forces the factorial moment to vanish.

declarations.name: exists_index_ge_two_mul_of_factorialMoment_ne_zero_of_channel_eq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem exists_index_ge_two_mul_of_factorialMoment_ne_zero_of_channel_eq_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) (hlo : ∀ j, d ≤ index j) (hchannel : channelNumerator coeff index d = 0) (hmoment : factorialMoment coeff index ≠ 0) : ∃ j, 2 * d ≤ index j
declarations.docstring: If every support index is at least `d`, channel cancellation and a nonzero factorial moment force some support index to be at least `2d`.

declarations.name: channelLCM
declarations.docstring: The least common multiple of the channel moduli through `D`.

declarations.name: channelCoefficient_sub_factorial_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem channelCoefficient_sub_factorial_dvd {d i : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) : ((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1) ∣ ((i.factorial : ℤ) - (i.factorial / d.factorial ^ (i / d) : ℕ))
declarations.docstring: Every individual channel coefficient is congruent to its factorial coefficient modulo `d! - 1`. Unlike quotient-band rigidity, this statement has no restriction on the support index.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_mod_factorialMoment
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_mod_factorialMoment {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) : ((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1) ∣ factorialMoment coeff index - channelNumerator coeff index d
declarations.docstring: The factorial moment and every channel numerator have the same residue modulo `d! - 1`.

declarations.name: channelModulus_dvd_factorialMoment_of_channel_zero
declarations.signature: theorem channelModulus_dvd_factorialMoment_of_channel_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hzero : channelNumerator coeff index d = 0) : ((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1) ∣ factorialMoment coeff index
declarations.docstring: An annihilated `d`-channel forces its modulus `d! - 1` to divide the factorial moment.

declarations.name: channelLCM_dvd_factorialMoment_of_channels_zero
declarations.signature: theorem channelLCM_dvd_factorialMoment_of_channels_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (hzero : ∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 D, channelNumerator coeff index d = 0) : (channelLCM D : ℤ) ∣ factorialMoment coeff index
declarations.docstring: Simultaneous channel annihilation forces the full least-common-multiple obstruction, independently of the size or geometry of the support.

declarations.name: exists_channelCorrection
declarations.signature: theorem exists_channelCorrection {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) : ∃ k : ℤ, channelNumerator coeff index d = factorialMoment coeff index + ((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1) * k
declarations.docstring: Exact affine normal form for one channel: after subtracting the factorial moment, the remaining numerator is an integral multiple of `d! - 1`.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_eq_modulus_mul_of_moment_zero
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_eq_modulus_mul_of_moment_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hmoment : factorialMoment coeff index = 0) : ∃ k : ℤ, channelNumerator coeff index d = ((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1) * k
declarations.docstring: If the factorial moment is zero, the channel numerator is an integral multiple of `d! - 1`.

declarations.docstring: Recursive lcm of a list, normalized to `1` on the empty list.

declarations.signature: theorem listLCM_dvd_prod (values : List ℕ) : listLCM values ∣ values.prod

declarations.signature: theorem gcd_list_prod_dvd_prod_gcd (a : ℕ) (values : List ℕ) : Nat.gcd a values.prod ∣ (values.map (Nat.gcd a)).prod

declarations.name: list_prod_dvd_lcm_mul_pairwiseGCDProduct
declarations.signature: theorem list_prod_dvd_lcm_mul_pairwiseGCDProduct (values : List ℕ) : values.prod ∣ listLCM values * pairwiseGCDProduct values
declarations.docstring: The product of a finite list divides its lcm times the product of all pairwise gcds. This records precisely the gcd loss used in the factorial-gap estimate below.

declarations.name: dvd_descFactorial_of_pos
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_descFactorial_of_pos {n k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (hkn : k ≤ n) : n ∣ n.descFactorial k

declarations.name: gcd_factorial_sub_one_dvd_descFactorial_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem gcd_factorial_sub_one_dvd_descFactorial_sub_one {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m < n) : Nat.gcd (m.factorial - 1) (n.factorial - 1) ∣ n.descFactorial (n - m) - 1
declarations.docstring: Two factorial gaps can collide only through the intervening descending factorial: `gcd(m!-1,n!-1)` divides `n.descFactorial (n-m)-1`.

declarations.name: gcd_factorial_sub_one_le_pow_gap
declarations.signature: theorem gcd_factorial_sub_one_le_pow_gap {m n : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hmn : m < n) : Nat.gcd (m.factorial - 1) (n.factorial - 1) ≤ n ^ (n - m)

declarations.name: factorial_gap_gcd_exact
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_gap_gcd_exact {m n : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hmn : m < n) : let g

declarations.name: factorialGapFrom
declarations.signature: def factorialGapFrom : ℕ → ℕ → List ℕ | _, 0 => [] | m, k + 1 => (m.factorial - 1) :: factorialGapFrom (m + 1) k /-- Sum `r + (r+1) + ... + (r+k-1)`. This recursive form keeps the collision proof free of natural-number division. -/ def intervalExponent : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ | _, 0 => 0 | r, k + 1 => r + intervalExponent (r + 1) k /-- Triangular collision exponent `1+...+k`. -/ def triangularExponent (k : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: intervalExponent
declarations.signature: def intervalExponent : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ | _, 0 => 0 | r, k + 1 => r + intervalExponent (r + 1) k /-- Triangular collision exponent `1+...+k`. -/ def triangularExponent (k : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Sum `r + (r+1) + ... + (r+k-1)`. This recursive form keeps the collision proof free of natural-number division.

declarations.name: triangularExponent
declarations.docstring: Triangular collision exponent `1+...+k`.

declarations.name: pairDistanceExponent
declarations.signature: def pairDistanceExponent : ℕ → ℕ | 0 => 0 | k + 1 => triangularExponent k + pairDistanceExponent k /-- Collision of one factorial gap with a later consecutive block costs the sum of the intervening index distances. -/ theorem cross_factorialGap_prod_le_pow_intervalExponent {m r k D : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hmax : m + r + k ≤ D + 1) : ((factorialGapFrom (m + r) k).map (Nat.gcd (m.factorial - 1))).prod ≤ D ^ intervalExponent r k

declarations.name: cross_factorialGap_prod_le_pow_intervalExponent
declarations.signature: theorem cross_factorialGap_prod_le_pow_intervalExponent {m r k D : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (hmax : m + r + k ≤ D + 1) : ((factorialGapFrom (m + r) k).map (Nat.gcd (m.factorial - 1))).prod ≤ D ^ intervalExponent r k
declarations.docstring: Collision of one factorial gap with a later consecutive block costs the sum of the intervening index distances.

declarations.name: pairwiseGCDProduct_factorialGapFrom_le

declarations.name: intervalExponent_eq

declarations.name: factorialGapFrom_prod_le_channelLCM_mul_pow
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapFrom_prod_le_channelLCM_mul_pow {m k D : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hmax : m + k ≤ D + 1) : (factorialGapFrom m k).prod ≤ channelLCM D * D ^ pairDistanceExponent k

declarations.name: factorialGapSegment
declarations.signature: def factorialGapSegment (D k : ℕ) : List ℕ

declarations.name: factorialGapSegment_prod_le_channelLCM_mul_pow

declarations.name: factorialGapSegment_prod_le_channelLCM_mul_pow_choose
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapSegment_prod_le_channelLCM_mul_pow_choose {D k : ℕ} (hkD : k < D) : (factorialGapSegment D k).prod ≤ channelLCM D * D ^ ((k + 1).choose 3)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite segment inequality in binomial closed form: `choose (k+1) 3 = k(k^2-1)/6`.

declarations.name: factorialGapFrom_prod_eq_prod_range
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapFrom_prod_eq_prod_range (m k : ℕ) : (factorialGapFrom m k).prod = ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, ((m + i).factorial - 1)
declarations.docstring: Reindex the consecutive list as the finite interval used in the paper.

declarations.name: factorialGapSegment_log_sum_le_channelLCM_add_choose
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapSegment_log_sum_le_channelLCM_add_choose {D k : ℕ} (hkD : k < D) : (∑ n ∈ Finset.Ico (D + 1 - k) (D + 1), Real.log ((n.factorial - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) ≤ Real.log (channelLCM D : ℝ) + (((k + 1).choose 3 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log (D : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The exact logarithmic segment inequality, on the paper's index interval. The Ico endpoint D+1 includes D. No asymptotic estimate or Stirling loss is used to pass from the checked product inequality to this statement.

declarations.name: factorialGapSegment_base_pow_le_channelLCM_mul_pow_choose
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapSegment_base_pow_le_channelLCM_mul_pow_choose {D k : ℕ} (hkD : k < D) : ((D + 1 - k).factorial - 1) ^ k ≤ channelLCM D * D ^ ((k + 1).choose 3)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite lower constraint on the channel lcm. It combines the smallest gap in the final `k`-block with the pairwise-gcd upper bound.

declarations.name: channelLCM_lt_radiusFactorial_sub_one_of_dvd_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem channelLCM_lt_radiusFactorial_sub_one_of_dvd_of_lt {D M R : ℕ} (hMpos : 0 < M) (hdiv : channelLCM D ∣ M) (hsmall : M < (R + 1).factorial - 1) : channelLCM D < (R + 1).factorial - 1
declarations.docstring: If a positive integer is a multiple of the channel lcm and is smaller than the factorial gap at `R+1`, then the channel lcm is smaller than that gap as well.

declarations.name: factorialGapSegment_base_pow_lt_radiusFactorial_mul_pow
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapSegment_base_pow_lt_radiusFactorial_mul_pow {D k M R : ℕ} (hkD : k < D) (hMpos : 0 < M) (hdiv : channelLCM D ∣ M) (hsmall : M < (R + 1).factorial - 1) : ((D + 1 - k).factorial - 1) ^ k < ((R + 1).factorial - 1) * D ^ ((k + 1).choose 3)
declarations.docstring: Finite radius constraint obtained by combining divisibility by the channel lcm with the final-block estimate.

declarations.name: factorialGapSegment_log_radius_constraint
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapSegment_log_radius_constraint {D k M R : ℕ} (hkD : k < D) (hMpos : 0 < M) (hdiv : channelLCM D ∣ M) (hsmall : M < (R + 1).factorial - 1) : (k : ℝ) * Real.log (((D + 1 - k).factorial - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) < Real.log (((R + 1).factorial - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) + (((k + 1).choose 3 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log (D : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Logarithmic form of the exact pre-asymptotic radius constraint. This is the finite real inequality to which explicit Stirling estimates and the choice `k = Nat.sqrt (2 * D)` can be applied; it contains no asymptotic notation.

declarations.name: log_factorial_sub_one_lower_bound
declarations.signature: theorem log_factorial_sub_one_lower_bound {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ) - n - Real.log 2 ≤ Real.log ((n.factorial - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: An explicit lower bound for the logarithm of a factorial gap. It is the global lower Stirling estimate with only nonnegative secondary terms discarded, and the elementary loss `n! - 1 ≥ n! / 2`.

declarations.name: log_factorial_sub_one_upper_bound
declarations.signature: theorem log_factorial_sub_one_upper_bound {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : Real.log ((n.factorial - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) * Real.log (n : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Elementary upper bound for a factorial gap: `log(n! - 1) ≤ n log n`.

declarations.name: factorialGapSegment_stirling_radius_constraint
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapSegment_stirling_radius_constraint {D k M R : ℕ} (hkD : k < D) (hMpos : 0 < M) (hdiv : channelLCM D ∣ M) (hsmall : M < (R + 1).factorial - 1) : (k : ℝ) * (((D + 1 - k : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log ((D + 1 - k : ℕ) : ℝ) - (D + 1 - k : ℕ) - Real.log 2) < ((R + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log (R + 1 : ℝ) + (((k + 1).choose 3 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log (D : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Explicit finite radius constraint after applying the stated Stirling bounds. The conclusion contains no factorials or logarithms of factorial gaps.

declarations.name: radiusOptimizationWindow
declarations.docstring: Optimizing block length from the elementary lcm argument.

declarations.name: radiusOptimizationWindow_sq_le
declarations.signature: theorem radiusOptimizationWindow_sq_le (D : ℕ) : radiusOptimizationWindow D ^ 2 ≤ 2 * D

declarations.name: radiusOptimizationWindow_lt
declarations.signature: theorem radiusOptimizationWindow_lt {D : ℕ} (hD : 3 ≤ D) : radiusOptimizationWindow D < D

declarations.name: optimized_stirling_radius_constraint
declarations.signature: theorem optimized_stirling_radius_constraint {D M R : ℕ} (hD : 3 ≤ D) (hMpos : 0 < M) (hdiv : channelLCM D ∣ M) (hsmall : M < (R + 1).factorial - 1) : let k
declarations.docstring: The Stirling constraint at the final-block length `⌊√(2D)⌋`.

declarations.name: three_mul_choose_two_mul_add_one_le_four_mul_cube
declarations.docstring: Cubic upper bound for the collision exponent on the exact square subsequence `D = 2t²`, `k = 2t`.

declarations.name: square_subsequence_radius_cubic_of_log_constraint
declarations.signature: theorem square_subsequence_radius_cubic_of_log_constraint {t R : ℕ} (ht : 4096 ≤ t) (hconstraint : (2 * t : ℝ) * (((2 * t ^ 2 + 1 - 2 * t : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log ((2 * t ^ 2 + 1 - 2 * t : ℕ) : ℝ) - (2 * t ^ 2 + 1 - 2 * t : ℕ) - Real.log 2) < ((R + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log (R + 1 : ℝ) + (((2 * t + 1).choose 3 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log ((2 * t ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℝ)) : t ^ 3 < 8 * (R + 1)
declarations.docstring: On the exact square subsequence, the finite logarithmic constraint already forces a cubic radius. The deliberately coarse constant keeps this implication fully explicit; no asymptotic notation is used.

declarations.name: square_subsequence_radius_cubic_lower
declarations.signature: theorem square_subsequence_radius_cubic_lower {t M R : ℕ} (ht : 4096 ≤ t) (hMpos : 0 < M) (hdiv : channelLCM (2 * t ^ 2) ∣ M) (hsmall : M < (R + 1).factorial - 1) : t ^ 3 < 8 * (R + 1)
declarations.docstring: On `D = 2t²`, the divisibility and factorial-gap hypotheses force the explicit lower bound `t³ < 8(R+1)`.

declarations.name: no_eventual_square_subsequence_cubic_upper
declarations.signature: theorem no_eventual_square_subsequence_cubic_upper (M R : ℕ → ℕ) (hMpos : ∀ t, 4096 ≤ t → 0 < M t) (hdiv : ∀ t, 4096 ≤ t → channelLCM (2 * t ^ 2) ∣ M t) (hsmall : ∀ t, 4096 ≤ t → M t < (R t + 1).factorial - 1) : ¬ ∃ T, ∀ t, T ≤ t → 8 * (R t + 1) ≤ t ^ 3
declarations.docstring: Under the channel-lcm and factorial-gap hypotheses for every sufficiently large `t`, the reverse cubic bound `8(R(t)+1) ≤ t³` cannot hold eventually.

declarations.name: not_isLittleO_square_subsequence_radius
declarations.signature: theorem not_isLittleO_square_subsequence_radius (M R : ℕ → ℕ) (hMpos : ∀ t, 4096 ≤ t → 0 < M t) (hdiv : ∀ t, 4096 ≤ t → channelLCM (2 * t ^ 2) ∣ M t) (hsmall : ∀ t, 4096 ≤ t → M t < (R t + 1).factorial - 1) : ¬ (fun t : ℕ => ((R t + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) =o[Filter.atTop] (fun t : ℕ => (t : ℝ) ^ 3)
declarations.docstring: Mathlib little-o form of the square-subsequence obstruction. Thus the radius sequence cannot be `o(t³)`, equivalently cannot be `o(D^(3/2))` after the reparameterization `D = 2t²`, under the checked channel hypotheses.

declarations.name: square_subsequence_radius_three_halves_of_log_constraint
declarations.signature: theorem square_subsequence_radius_three_halves_of_log_constraint {t R : ℕ} (ht : 2 ^ 32 ≤ t) (hconstraint : (2 * t : ℝ) * (((2 * t ^ 2 + 1 - 2 * t : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log ((2 * t ^ 2 + 1 - 2 * t : ℕ) : ℝ) - (2 * t ^ 2 + 1 - 2 * t : ℕ) - Real.log 2) < ((R + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log (R + 1 : ℝ) + (((2 * t + 1).choose 3 : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log ((2 * t ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℝ)) : 3 * t ^ 3 < 2 * (R + 1)
declarations.docstring: Retaining most of the terminal factorial index sharpens the first coarse square-subsequence constant: for `t ≥ 2^32`, the same finite logarithmic constraint forces `R + 1 > (3/2)t³`.

declarations.name: square_subsequence_radius_three_halves_lower
declarations.signature: theorem square_subsequence_radius_three_halves_lower {t M R : ℕ} (ht : 2 ^ 32 ≤ t) (hMpos : 0 < M) (hdiv : channelLCM (2 * t ^ 2) ∣ M) (hsmall : M < (R + 1).factorial - 1) : 3 * t ^ 3 < 2 * (R + 1)
declarations.docstring: The channel hypotheses force the explicit bound `R + 1 > (3/2)t³` on `D = 2t²`.

declarations.name: no_eventual_square_subsequence_three_halves_upper
declarations.signature: theorem no_eventual_square_subsequence_three_halves_upper (M R : ℕ → ℕ) (hMpos : ∀ t, 2 ^ 32 ≤ t → 0 < M t) (hdiv : ∀ t, 2 ^ 32 ≤ t → channelLCM (2 * t ^ 2) ∣ M t) (hsmall : ∀ t, 2 ^ 32 ≤ t → M t < (R t + 1).factorial - 1) : ¬ ∃ T, ∀ t, T ≤ t → 2 * (R t + 1) ≤ 3 * t ^ 3
declarations.docstring: Sequence form of the improved constant: the competing upper bound `R(t)+1 ≤ (3/2)t³` cannot hold eventually.

declarations.name: compConstTerm
declarations.docstring: Companion-constant term, anchored at `n ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: invFactSubOneTerm
declarations.docstring: Unit-fractional term `1/(n!−1)`, anchored at `n ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: unitFactTerm
declarations.docstring: Unit-factorial term `1/n!`, anchored at `n ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: companion_tsum_add_unitFact_eq_series
declarations.signature: theorem companion_tsum_add_unitFact_eq_series : (∑' n : ℕ, compConstTerm n) + (∑' n : ℕ, unitFactTerm n) = _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: **Telescope identity.** The companion constant series plus the unit- factorial series reproduces the Erdős #68 series termwise.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_stream_domination_below
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_stream_domination_below (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) (k : ℕ) (hdom : (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc m (m + k), (((factorialGapStepCarry j : ℝ) + 1 / ((j.factorial : ℝ) - 1)) * (((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) / (j.factorial : ℝ)))) + (((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) / ((m + k).factorial : ℝ)) ≤ (1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1)) / (m : ℝ)) : factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1
declarations.docstring: **Lower-window certificate.** If the finite weighted carry stream from `m` through `m+k`, augmented by its explicit remainder weight, stays below `(1+ε_m)/m`, then index `m` sits in the lower cylinder and is again a frontier miss.

declarations.name: companionScaledTail
declarations.docstring: The scaled omitted companion tail `δ_m = m! ∑_{n>m} 1/(n!(n!−1))`.

declarations.name: summable_compConstTerm_tail
declarations.signature: theorem summable_compConstTerm_tail (m : ℕ) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => compConstTerm (m + 1 + k))

declarations.name: companionScaledTail_pos
declarations.signature: theorem companionScaledTail_pos (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) : 0 < companionScaledTail m

declarations.name: compConstTerm_tail_le
declarations.signature: private theorem compConstTerm_tail_le (m k : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) : compConstTerm (m + 1 + k) ≤ (1 / ((((m + 1).factorial : ℕ) : ℝ) - 1)) * (1 / (((m + 1 + k).factorial : ℕ) : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: Termwise domination of the companion tail by the exponential tail.

declarations.name: companionScaledTail_lt
declarations.signature: theorem companionScaledTail_lt (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : companionScaledTail m < 1 / ((((m + 1).factorial : ℕ) : ℝ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: `δ_m < 1/((m+1)!−1)`: the omitted tail is far below one factorial cell.

declarations.name: companionScaledTail_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem companionScaledTail_lt_one (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : companionScaledTail m < 1

declarations.name: compConstPartial_cast_eq_sum_range
declarations.signature: theorem compConstPartial_cast_eq_sum_range (m : ℕ) : ((compConstPartial m : ℚ) : ℝ) = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), compConstTerm n
declarations.docstring: The finite companion partial sum, cast to the reals, is the range-sum of the anchored companion terms.

declarations.name: companionConstant_eq_partial_add_tail
declarations.signature: theorem companionConstant_eq_partial_add_tail (m : ℕ) : companionConstant = ((compConstPartial m : ℚ) : ℝ) + ∑' k : ℕ, compConstTerm (m + 1 + k)
declarations.docstring: `C = C_m + (tail after m)`.

declarations.name: scaledPrefixFrac_cast_eq_companion_sub_tail
declarations.signature: theorem scaledPrefixFrac_cast_eq_companion_sub_tail (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : ((scaledPrefixFrac m : ℚ) : ℝ) = (m.factorial : ℝ) * companionConstant - companionScaledTail m
declarations.docstring: **Tail identity.** The finite fractional carrier is the fixed constant's factorial orbit minus the scaled omitted tail.

declarations.name: floor_sub_small_eq_floor_sub_indicator
declarations.signature: theorem floor_sub_small_eq_floor_sub_indicator (J δ : ℝ) (hδpos : 0 < δ) (hδlt : δ < 1) : ⌊J - δ⌋ = ⌊J⌋ - (if Int.fract J < δ then 1 else 0)
declarations.docstring: Subtracting `0 < δ < 1` lowers a floor exactly when the fractional part is below `δ`.

declarations.name: companionWrap
declarations.docstring: The near-integer wrap indicator `σ_m = [fract(m!·C) < δ_m]`.

declarations.name: companionWrap_eq_zero_or_one
declarations.signature: theorem companionWrap_eq_zero_or_one (m : ℕ) : companionWrap m = 0 ∨ companionWrap m = 1

declarations.name: floor_scaledPrefixFrac_eq_facFloor_sub_wrap
declarations.signature: theorem floor_scaledPrefixFrac_eq_facFloor_sub_wrap (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : ⌊scaledPrefixFrac m⌋ = facFloor companionConstant m - companionWrap m
declarations.docstring: **Wrap identity.** `⌊F_m⌋ = ⌊m!·C⌋ − σ_m`.

declarations.name: secondLayerPrefixFloor_eq_floor_scaledPrefixFrac
declarations.signature: theorem secondLayerPrefixFloor_eq_floor_scaledPrefixFrac (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : secondLayerPrefixFloor m = ⌊scaledPrefixFrac m⌋
declarations.docstring: The finite second-layer floor of `SecondLayerDigit` is the carrier floor.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_eq_companion_digit_law
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_eq_companion_digit_law (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) : factorialGapStepCarry m = ((m : ℤ) - 1 - canonicalDigit companionConstant m) + companionWrap m - (m : ℤ) * companionWrap (m - 1)
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional companion carry law.** For `m ≥ 3`, `b_m = (m − 1 − d_m(C)) + σ_m − m·σ_{m−1}`.

declarations.name: canonicalDigit_companion_of_unit_carry
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalDigit_companion_of_unit_carry {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hunit : factorialGapStepCarry m = 1) : canonicalDigit companionConstant m = (m : ℤ) - 2 ∨ canonicalDigit companionConstant m = (m : ℤ) - 1
declarations.docstring: A unit carry forces the companion digit into the two top classes.

declarations.name: canonicalDigit_companion_of_zero_carry
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalDigit_companion_of_zero_carry {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hzero : factorialGapStepCarry m = 0) : canonicalDigit companionConstant m = (m : ℤ) - 1 ∨ canonicalDigit companionConstant m = 0
declarations.docstring: A zero carry forces the companion digit into `{m−1, 0}`.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_companion_floor_residues
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_companion_floor_residues {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hfloor : ((facFloor companionConstant m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) ≠ 0) (hpred : ((facFloor companionConstant m + 1 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) ≠ 0) : factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional constant-only miss certificate.** If the floor of the fixed constant's factorial orbit avoids the residues `−2` and `−1` modulo `m`, the carry at `m` is non-unit. No tail hypothesis remains.

declarations.name: secondLayerFloorStableAt_companion_iff
declarations.signature: theorem secondLayerFloorStableAt_companion_iff (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : SecondLayerFloorStableAt companionConstant m ↔ companionScaledTail m ≤ Int.fract ((m.factorial : ℝ) * companionConstant)
declarations.docstring: The floor-stability hypothesis of `SecondLayerDigit` at the companion constant is exactly the absence of a wrap: `δ_m ≤ fract(m!·C)`.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_eq_complement_companion_digit_of_no_wrap
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_eq_complement_companion_digit_of_no_wrap {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hnow : companionScaledTail m ≤ Int.fract ((m.factorial : ℝ) * companionConstant)) (hprev : companionScaledTail (m - 1) ≤ Int.fract (((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) * companionConstant)) : factorialGapStepCarry m = (m : ℤ) - 1 - canonicalDigit companionConstant m
declarations.docstring: Away from wraps at `m` and `m−1`, the carry is exactly the complement digit of the companion constant.

declarations.name: canonicalDigitTerm
declarations.signature: noncomputable def canonicalDigitTerm (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The canonical factorial digit, normalized as the corresponding summand of the factorial expansion. The two initial indices are suppressed because the mixed-radix expansion starts at radix two.

declarations.name: summable_canonicalDigitTerm
declarations.docstring: Canonical factorial digit terms are summable. The pointwise majorant is `m / m!`, a shifted exponential series.

declarations.name: sum_range_succ_canonicalDigitTerm
declarations.signature: theorem sum_range_succ_canonicalDigitTerm (x : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : (∑ m ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), canonicalDigitTerm x m) = ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 2 N, (canonicalDigit x m : ℝ) / (m.factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The partial sum of normalized canonical digits is exactly the digit sum appearing in `factorial_expansion_partial`.

declarations.name: tendsto_canonicalRemainder_div_factorial_zero
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_canonicalRemainder_div_factorial_zero (x : ℝ) : Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => canonicalRemainder x N / (N.factorial : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
declarations.docstring: The explicit remainder in the finite factorial expansion tends to zero.

declarations.name: tsum_canonicalDigitTerm
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_canonicalDigitTerm (x : ℝ) : (∑' m : ℕ, canonicalDigitTerm x m) = x - (⌊x⌋ : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Every real number is the sum of its integer part and the convergent series of its canonical factorial digits.

declarations.name: hasSum_canonicalDigitTerm
declarations.signature: theorem hasSum_canonicalDigitTerm (x : ℝ) : HasSum (canonicalDigitTerm x) (x - (⌊x⌋ : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: The canonical factorial digits sum to the fractional part of `x`.

declarations.name: unitFactTail
declarations.docstring: The exponential tail beyond `m`.

declarations.name: unitFactScaledTail
declarations.docstring: The exponential tail scaled by `m!`.

declarations.name: summable_unitFactTail
declarations.signature: theorem summable_unitFactTail (m : ℕ) : Summable (fun k : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / ((m + 1 + k).factorial : ℝ))

declarations.name: unitFactTail_term_lt_telescope
declarations.signature: private theorem unitFactTail_term_lt_telescope {m k : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : (1 : ℝ) / ((m + 1 + k).factorial : ℝ) < 1 / ((m + k).factorial : ℝ) - 1 / ((m + k + 1).factorial : ℝ)

declarations.name: unitFactTail_lt_one_div_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem unitFactTail_lt_one_div_factorial {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : unitFactTail m < (1 : ℝ) / (m.factorial : ℝ)

declarations.name: unitFactScaledTail_pos_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem unitFactScaledTail_pos_lt_one {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : 0 < unitFactScaledTail m ∧ unitFactScaledTail m < 1

declarations.name: unitFact_tsum_eq_expPrefix_add_tail
declarations.signature: theorem unitFact_tsum_eq_expPrefix_add_tail (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : (∑' n : ℕ, unitFactTerm n) = (factorialExpPrefix m : ℝ) + unitFactTail m

declarations.name: unitFact_tsum_scaled_decomposition
declarations.signature: theorem unitFact_tsum_scaled_decomposition (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : (m.factorial : ℝ) * (∑' n : ℕ, unitFactTerm n) = (factorialExpScaled m : ℝ) + unitFactScaledTail m

declarations.name: eventually_facFloor_mod_neg_two_of_not_irrational_add_unitFact
declarations.signature: theorem eventually_facFloor_mod_neg_two_of_not_irrational_add_unitFact (x : ℝ) (hrat : ¬ Irrational (x + ∑' n, unitFactTerm n)) : ∃ M, ∀ m, M ≤ m → ((facFloor x m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0
declarations.docstring: Rationality of `x + (e - 2)` forces the exceptional residue `-2` eventually along the factorial orbit of `x`.

declarations.name: canonicalDigitTerm_add_unitFactTerm_eq_telescope_of_digit_sub_two
declarations.signature: private theorem canonicalDigitTerm_add_unitFactTerm_eq_telescope_of_digit_sub_two {x : ℝ} {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hdigit : canonicalDigit x m = (m : ℤ) - 2) : canonicalDigitTerm x m + unitFactTerm m = (1 : ℝ) / ((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) - 1 / (m.factorial : ℝ)

declarations.name: not_irrational_add_unitFact_of_eventually_canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_add_unitFact_of_eventually_canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two (x : ℝ) (hdigits : ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, M ≤ m → canonicalDigit x m = (m : ℤ) - 2) : ¬ Irrational (x + (∑' n : ℕ, unitFactTerm n))
declarations.docstring: Eventual exceptional digits make `x + (e - 2)` rational.

declarations.name: eventually_facFloor_mod_neg_two_iff_eventually_canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two
declarations.signature: theorem eventually_facFloor_mod_neg_two_iff_eventually_canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two (x : ℝ) : (∃ M, ∀ m, M ≤ m → ((facFloor x m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0) ↔ (∃ M, ∀ m, M ≤ m → canonicalDigit x m = (m : ℤ) - 2)
declarations.docstring: Eventual exceptional floor residues are exactly eventual exceptional canonical digits.

declarations.name: not_irrational_add_unitFact_iff_eventually_canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_add_unitFact_iff_eventually_canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two (x : ℝ) : ¬ Irrational (x + ∑' n, unitFactTerm n) ↔ ∃ M, ∀ m, M ≤ m → canonicalDigit x m = (m : ℤ) - 2
declarations.docstring: The generic fixed-orbit rationality boundary in canonical-digit form.

declarations.name: not_irrational_add_unitFact_iff_eventually_facFloor_mod_neg_two
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_add_unitFact_iff_eventually_facFloor_mod_neg_two (x : ℝ) : ¬ Irrational (x + ∑' n, unitFactTerm n) ↔ ∃ M, ∀ m, M ≤ m → ((facFloor x m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0
declarations.docstring: The generic fixed-orbit rationality boundary in floor-residue form.

declarations.name: not_irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_eventually_companion_floor_neg_two
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_eventually_companion_floor_neg_two : ¬ Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries ↔ ∃ M, ∀ m, M ≤ m → ((facFloor companionConstant m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0
declarations.docstring: The Erdős #68 series is rational exactly when the companion factorial orbit is eventually concentrated in the exceptional residue `-2`.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_companion_floor_misses
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_companion_floor_misses : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries ↔ ∀ B, ∃ m, B < m ∧ ((facFloor companionConstant m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The exact open boundary: irrationality of the Erdős #68 series is equivalent to cofinally many escapes from the exceptional residue.

declarations.name: tsum_unitFactTerm_eq_exp_one_sub_two
declarations.signature: theorem tsum_unitFactTerm_eq_exp_one_sub_two : (∑' n : ℕ, unitFactTerm n) = Real.exp 1 - 2
declarations.docstring: The anchored unit-factorial series is exactly `exp 1 - 2`.

declarations.name: companionConstant
declarations.docstring: The fixed companion constant whose factorial orbit controls the carry congruence.

declarations.name: companionConstant_add_unitFact_eq_series
declarations.signature: theorem companionConstant_add_unitFact_eq_series : companionConstant + (∑' n : ℕ, unitFactTerm n) = _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: The named companion constant differs from the original series by exactly the anchored unit-factorial series.

declarations.name: compConstTerm_pos
declarations.signature: theorem compConstTerm_pos {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 0 < compConstTerm n
declarations.docstring: A positive companion term on its actual support.

declarations.name: facFloor_add_two_emod_eq_canonicalDigit_add_two_emod
declarations.signature: theorem facFloor_add_two_emod_eq_canonicalDigit_add_two_emod (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ((facFloor x m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = ((canonicalDigit x m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ))
declarations.docstring: A factorial-scale floor and its canonical radix digit have the same residue modulo the current radix, even after the `+2` normalization used by the companion orbit.

declarations.name: facFloor_mod_eq_neg_two_of_canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two
declarations.signature: theorem facFloor_mod_eq_neg_two_of_canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) (hdigit : canonicalDigit x m = (m : ℤ) - 2) : ((facFloor x m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0
declarations.docstring: The eventual digit pattern `m-2` is the factorial-digit form of the companion orbit's distinguished residue `-2`.

declarations.name: canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two_of_facFloor_mod_eq_neg_two
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalDigit_eq_sub_two_of_facFloor_mod_eq_neg_two (x : ℝ) {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hmod : ((facFloor x m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0) : canonicalDigit x m = (m : ℤ) - 2
declarations.docstring: Conversely, at every radix at least three the distinguished floor residue forces the unique canonical digit `m-2`.

declarations.name: floor_sub_small_eq_or_eq_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem floor_sub_small_eq_or_eq_sub_one (J δ : ℝ) (hδpos : 0 < δ) (hδlt : δ < 1) : ⌊J - δ⌋ = ⌊J⌋ ∨ ⌊J - δ⌋ = ⌊J⌋ - 1
declarations.docstring: Subtracting a quantity strictly between zero and one changes a real floor by either zero or exactly one.

declarations.name: floor_sub_small_mod_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem floor_sub_small_mod_ne_zero (J δ : ℝ) (m : ℕ) (hδpos : 0 < δ) (hδlt : δ < 1) (hfloor : ((⌊J⌋ + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) ≠ 0) (hpred : ((⌊J⌋ + 1 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) ≠ 0) : ((⌊J - δ⌋ + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The two-residue form of the small-subtraction floor lemma.

declarations.name: floor_mod_eq_neg_two_of_mul_sub_int_sub_small
declarations.signature: theorem floor_mod_eq_neg_two_of_mul_sub_int_sub_small (m : ℕ) (K E : ℤ) (J r : ℝ) (hJ : J = (((m : ℤ) * K - E : ℤ) : ℝ) - r) (hrpos : 0 < r) (hrlt : r < 1) (hEmod : E % (m : ℤ) = 1) : ((⌊J⌋ + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0
declarations.docstring: Arithmetic core of the rationality-only one-residue normal form. If `J` is an integral multiple of `m`, minus an integer congruent to one, minus a strictly sub-unit positive remainder, then its floor is `-2` modulo `m`. For the companion orbit the intended data are `J = m! * companionConstant`, the multiple comes from a hypothetical rational value of the original series, the integer is the truncated exponential sum, and the remainder is the positive tail of `m! * exp 1`.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_constant_floor_residues
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_constant_floor_residues {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (J δ : ℝ) (hdecomp : (scaledPrefixFrac m : ℝ) = J - δ) (hδpos : 0 < δ) (hδlt : δ < 1) (hfloor : ((⌊J⌋ + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) ≠ 0) (hpred : ((⌊J⌋ + 1 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) ≠ 0) : factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1
declarations.docstring: **Corrected constant-only carry-miss interface.** If the rational carrier is a positive sub-unit tail below `J`, and the floor of `J` avoids the two adjacent residue classes `-2` and `-1`, then the carry at `m` is non-unit. The intended specialization is `J = m! * companionConstant`; the statement is kept in decomposition form so that any independently proved tail estimate can feed it directly.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_add

declarations.name: channelNumerator_smul
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_smul (z : ℤ) (f : ℕ →₀ ℤ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator (z • f) d = z * channelNumerator f d

declarations.name: channelNumerator_neg
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_neg (f : ℕ →₀ ℤ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator (-f) d = -channelNumerator f d

declarations.name: channelNumerator_sub
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_sub (f g : ℕ →₀ ℤ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator (f - g) d = channelNumerator f d - channelNumerator g d

declarations.name: channelNumerator_sum
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → ℕ →₀ ℤ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator (∑ i ∈ s, f i) d = ∑ i ∈ s, channelNumerator (f i) d

declarations.name: factorialMoment_add

declarations.name: factorialMoment_smul
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_smul (z : ℤ) (f : ℕ →₀ ℤ) : factorialMoment (z • f) = z * factorialMoment f

declarations.name: factorialMoment_neg
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_neg (f : ℕ →₀ ℤ) : factorialMoment (-f) = -factorialMoment f

declarations.name: factorialMoment_sub
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_sub (f g : ℕ →₀ ℤ) : factorialMoment (f - g) = factorialMoment f - factorialMoment g

declarations.name: factorialMoment_sum
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → ℕ →₀ ℤ) : factorialMoment (∑ i ∈ s, f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, factorialMoment (f i)

declarations.name: channelNumerator_single
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_single (i : ℕ) (z : ℤ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator (single i z) d = z * (channelWeight i d : ℤ)

declarations.name: factorialMoment_single
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_single (i : ℕ) (z : ℤ) : factorialMoment (single i z) = z * (i.factorial : ℤ)

declarations.name: adjacentDifference
declarations.signature: noncomputable def adjacentDifference (n : ℕ) : ℕ →₀ ℤ
declarations.docstring: Adjacent difference `T_n = n e_{n-1} - e_n`.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_adjacentDifference
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_adjacentDifference {n d : ℕ} (_hn : 1 ≤ n) : channelNumerator (adjacentDifference n) d = channelEvent d n

declarations.name: factorialMoment_adjacentDifference
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_adjacentDifference {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) : factorialMoment (adjacentDifference n) = 0

declarations.name: pred_div_eq_of_dvd
declarations.signature: lemma pred_div_eq_of_dvd {d n : ℕ} (hdpos : 0 < d) (hn : 0 < n) (hnd : d ∣ n) : (n - 1) / d = n / d - 1

declarations.name: channelEvent_eq_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem channelEvent_eq_of_dvd {d n : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hn : 0 < n) (hnd : d ∣ n) : channelEvent d n = ((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1) * (channelWeight n d : ℤ)

declarations.name: channelEvent_eq_indicator

declarations.name: channelNumerator_adjacentDifference_eq
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_adjacentDifference_eq {n d : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hd : 2 ≤ d) : channelNumerator (adjacentDifference n) d = (if d ∣ n then ((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1) * (channelWeight n d : ℤ) else 0)

declarations.name: channelWeight_self

declarations.name: channelWeight_two_mul_pow

declarations.name: channelWeight_two_even
declarations.signature: lemma channelWeight_two_even (k : ℕ) : channelWeight (2 * k) 2 = k.factorial * ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (2 * i + 1)

declarations.name: channelWeight_two_odd
declarations.signature: lemma channelWeight_two_odd (k : ℕ) : channelWeight (2 * k + 1) 2 = (2 * k + 1) * channelWeight (2 * k) 2

declarations.name: two_dvd_channelWeight_two_of_four_le
declarations.signature: lemma two_dvd_channelWeight_two_of_four_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 4 ≤ n) : 2 ∣ channelWeight n 2

declarations.name: three_dvd_channelWeight_two_of_three_le
declarations.signature: lemma three_dvd_channelWeight_two_of_three_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) : 3 ∣ channelWeight n 2

declarations.name: six_dvd_channelWeight_two_of_four_le
declarations.signature: lemma six_dvd_channelWeight_two_of_four_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 4 ≤ n) : 6 ∣ channelWeight n 2

declarations.name: twelve_dvd_factorial_sub_two_channelWeight

declarations.name: channelWeight_sub_factorial_dvd

declarations.name: channelLCM_dvd_factorialMoment_of_channels_zero

declarations.name: coprime_lcm_of_coprime
declarations.signature: lemma coprime_lcm_of_coprime {x a b : ℕ} (ha : Nat.Coprime x a) (hb : Nat.Coprime x b) : Nat.Coprime x (Nat.lcm a b)

declarations.name: coprime_twelve_finset_lcm
declarations.signature: lemma coprime_twelve_finset_lcm (s : Finset ℕ) (hs : ∀ d ∈ s, 2 ≤ d) : Nat.Coprime 12 (s.lcm fun d => d.factorial - 1)

declarations.name: isolatedChannelUnit
declarations.signature: noncomputable def isolatedChannelUnit (n : ℕ) : ℕ →₀ ℤ

declarations.name: isolatedChannelUnit_eq
declarations.signature: theorem isolatedChannelUnit_eq (n : ℕ) : isolatedChannelUnit n = if n ≤ 1 then 0 else adjacentDifference n - ∑ d ∈ (Finset.Ico 2 n).attach, if d.1 ∣ n then (channelWeight n d.1 : ℤ) • isolatedChannelUnit d.1 else 0

declarations.name: isolatedChannelUnit_of_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem isolatedChannelUnit_of_le_one {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 1) : isolatedChannelUnit n = 0

declarations.name: isolatedChannelUnit_of_two_le
declarations.signature: theorem isolatedChannelUnit_of_two_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : isolatedChannelUnit n = adjacentDifference n - ∑ d ∈ (Finset.Ico 2 n).attach, if d.1 ∣ n then (channelWeight n d.1 : ℤ) • isolatedChannelUnit d.1 else 0

declarations.name: factorialMoment_isolatedChannelUnit
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_isolatedChannelUnit {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialMoment (isolatedChannelUnit n) = 0

declarations.name: channelNumerator_isolatedChannelUnit
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_isolatedChannelUnit {n d : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hd : 2 ≤ d) : channelNumerator (isolatedChannelUnit n) d = if d = n then ((n.factorial : ℤ) - 1) else 0

declarations.name: isolatedChannelUnit_apply_one_of_odd
declarations.signature: theorem isolatedChannelUnit_apply_one_of_odd {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hodd : Odd n) : isolatedChannelUnit n 1 = 0
declarations.docstring: Odd isolated units have vanishing index-`1` coordinate.

declarations.name: lambda24
declarations.docstring: Sharp `D = 2` moment: `-6 e_2 + e_4` has vanishing channel `2` and moment `12`.

declarations.name: lambda234
declarations.docstring: Sharp `D = 3` moment: `-6 e_2 - 8 e_3 + 5 e_4` has vanishing channels `2,3` and moment `60 = 12 L_3`.

declarations.name: residualCentreTerm
declarations.docstring: One summand of the finite residual centre.

declarations.name: factorialCoeffTerm
declarations.docstring: One divisor-factorial coefficient summand.

declarations.name: residualCentre
declarations.docstring: The finite rational centre `m! * sum_{2 <= n <= m} 1 / ((n!)^(floor(m/n)) (n!-1))`.

declarations.name: factorialCoeffRat
declarations.docstring: Rational form of the divisor-factorial coefficient `sum_{n | m, n >= 2} m! / (n!)^(m/n)`.

declarations.name: factorialCoeffNat
declarations.docstring: Integer form of the divisor-factorial coefficient.

declarations.name: factorialCoeffTerm_eq_natCast_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem factorialCoeffTerm_eq_natCast_of_dvd (m n : ℕ) (hdvd : n ∣ m) : factorialCoeffTerm m n = (m.factorial / (n.factorial ^ (m / n)) : ℕ)
declarations.docstring: Each rational divisor-factorial summand is the cast of its exact natural quotient.

declarations.name: factorialCoeffRat_eq_natCast
declarations.signature: theorem factorialCoeffRat_eq_natCast (m : ℕ) : factorialCoeffRat m = (factorialCoeffNat m : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: The rational divisor-factorial coefficient is the cast of the integer coefficient with the same support.

declarations.name: factorial_eq_mul_pred_factorial
declarations.signature: private theorem factorial_eq_mul_pred_factorial (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) : m.factorial = m * (m - 1).factorial

declarations.name: pred_div_eq_of_not_dvd
declarations.signature: private theorem pred_div_eq_of_not_dvd {m n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hndvd : ¬n ∣ m) : (m - 1) / n = m / n

declarations.name: pred_div_add_one_eq_of_dvd
declarations.signature: private theorem pred_div_add_one_eq_of_dvd {m n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hnm : n ≤ m) (hdvd : n ∣ m) : (m - 1) / n + 1 = m / n

declarations.name: residualCentreTerm_of_not_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem residualCentreTerm_of_not_dvd (m n : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hndvd : ¬n ∣ m) : residualCentreTerm m n = (m : ℚ) * residualCentreTerm (m - 1) n
declarations.docstring: Away from a divisor of `m`, the centre term merely scales by `m`.

declarations.name: residualCentreTerm_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem residualCentreTerm_of_dvd (m n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hnm : n ≤ m) (hdvd : n ∣ m) : residualCentreTerm m n = (m : ℚ) * residualCentreTerm (m - 1) n - factorialCoeffTerm m n
declarations.docstring: At a divisor of `m`, increasing the exponent removes exactly the corresponding divisor-factorial coefficient term.

declarations.name: residualCentreTerm_self
declarations.signature: theorem residualCentreTerm_self (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : residualCentreTerm m m = factorialEpsilon m
declarations.docstring: The diagonal centre term is the factorial error `1 / (m! - 1)`.

declarations.name: factorialCoeffTerm_self
declarations.signature: theorem factorialCoeffTerm_self (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) : factorialCoeffTerm m m = 1
declarations.docstring: The diagonal divisor-factorial coefficient term is one.

declarations.name: residualCentre_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem residualCentre_recurrence (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) : residualCentre m = (m : ℚ) * residualCentre (m - 1) + 1 + factorialEpsilon m - factorialCoeffRat m
declarations.docstring: Exact finite-sum recurrence for the residual centre.

declarations.name: residualCentre_recurrence_int
declarations.signature: theorem residualCentre_recurrence_int (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) : residualCentre m = (m : ℚ) * residualCentre (m - 1) + 1 + factorialEpsilon m - ((factorialCoeffNat m : ℤ) : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: Integer-coefficient form of the concrete finite-centre recurrence.

declarations.name: residualCentre_defectCode_eq_factorial_floor
declarations.signature: theorem residualCentre_defectCode_eq_factorial_floor (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) : centreDefectCode residualCentre (fun k => (factorialCoeffNat k : ℤ)) m = ⌊(m : ℚ) * centreGap residualCentre (m - 1) - 1 / ((m.factorial : ℚ) - 1)⌋
declarations.docstring: The concrete residual centre instantiates the integer factorial defect code: its code is the floor of the preceding rescaled gap.

declarations.name: residualCentre_gap_factorial_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem residualCentre_gap_factorial_recurrence (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) : centreGap residualCentre m = (m : ℚ) * centreGap residualCentre (m - 1) - 1 / ((m.factorial : ℚ) - 1) - (centreDefectCode residualCentre (fun k => (factorialCoeffNat k : ℤ)) m : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: Exact fractional recurrence for the gap of the concrete finite residual centre.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorial_sub_one_gt
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorial_sub_one_gt {p n : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hdiv : p ∣ n.factorial - 1) : n < p
declarations.docstring: Every prime divisor of a factorial gap `n! - 1` is strictly larger than the source index `n`. This is the basic support separation behind the collision-core construction.

declarations.name: gcd_factorial_sub_one_eq_descFactorial_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem gcd_factorial_sub_one_eq_descFactorial_sub_one {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m < n) : Nat.gcd (m.factorial - 1) (n.factorial - 1) = Nat.gcd (m.factorial - 1) (n.descFactorial (n - m) - 1)
declarations.docstring: Exact shared-support identity for two factorial gaps. The previously checked divisibility bound is sharpened here to equality: every common factor is already visible in the intervening descending factorial minus one, and conversely.

declarations.name: privateQuotients_coprime_of_gcd_dvd_core
declarations.signature: theorem privateQuotients_coprime_of_gcd_dvd_core {a b C : ℕ} (hgPos : 0 < Nat.gcd a b) (hcollision : Nat.gcd a b ∣ C) : Nat.Coprime (a / Nat.gcd a C) (b / Nat.gcd b C)
declarations.docstring: If a collision core contains the full gcd of two denominators, then removing from each denominator the part visible in that core leaves coprime quotients. The proof factors both residual quotients through the standard coprime pair obtained by dividing by their common gcd.

declarations.name: factorialGap_privateQuotients_coprime_of_collision
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_privateQuotients_coprime_of_collision {m n C : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hcollision : Nat.gcd (m.factorial - 1) (n.factorial - 1) ∣ C) : Nat.Coprime ((m.factorial - 1) / Nat.gcd (m.factorial - 1) C) ((n.factorial - 1) / Nat.gcd (n.factorial - 1) C)
declarations.docstring: Factorial-gap specialization of the collision-core quotient theorem. Any core containing the pairwise gcd makes the two corresponding private quotients coprime.

declarations.name: pairwiseCollisionCore
declarations.signature: def pairwiseCollisionCore {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Lcm of all off-diagonal pairwise gcds in a finite denominator family. Each index is omitted from its own inner lcm, so diagonal terms do not erase the private support.

declarations.name: collisionCore
declarations.signature: def collisionCore {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: The collision core used by the endpoint decomposition also contains a distinguished base denominator.

declarations.name: endpointDenominatorLcm
declarations.signature: def endpointDenominatorLcm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Common denominator for the distinguished base and the finite denominator family.

declarations.name: endpointTailNumerator
declarations.signature: def endpointTailNumerator {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Numerator of the reciprocal tail after placing every denominator over the common endpoint lcm.

declarations.name: endpointBaseNumerator
declarations.signature: def endpointBaseNumerator {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (K base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Positive base contribution to the displayed endpoint numerator over the full common denominator.

declarations.name: endpointNumerator
declarations.signature: def endpointNumerator {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (K base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Displayed natural endpoint numerator. The intended endpoint application supplies the inequality making this truncated subtraction an ordinary positive difference.

declarations.name: endpointDenominatorLcm_pos
declarations.signature: theorem endpointDenominatorLcm_pos {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : 0 < endpointDenominatorLcm base s d
declarations.docstring: Positivity of every displayed denominator makes the full endpoint lcm strictly positive.

declarations.name: endpointDenominator_dvd_endpointDenominatorLcm
declarations.signature: theorem endpointDenominator_dvd_endpointDenominatorLcm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) : d i ∣ endpointDenominatorLcm base s d
declarations.docstring: Every displayed denominator divides the full endpoint lcm.

declarations.name: endpointTailNumerator_div_endpointDenominatorLcm
declarations.signature: theorem endpointTailNumerator_div_endpointDenominatorLcm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : (endpointTailNumerator base s d : ℚ) / endpointDenominatorLcm base s d = ∑ i ∈ s, 1 / (d i : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: Clearing the full endpoint lcm and then dividing back recovers the literal reciprocal sum.

declarations.name: endpointBaseNumerator_div_endpointDenominatorLcm
declarations.signature: theorem endpointBaseNumerator_div_endpointDenominatorLcm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : (endpointBaseNumerator K base s d : ℚ) / endpointDenominatorLcm base s d = (K : ℚ) / base
declarations.docstring: The distinguished contribution has the same exact common-denominator interpretation.

declarations.name: endpointTailNumerator_le_endpointBaseNumerator_of_gap_nonneg
declarations.signature: theorem endpointTailNumerator_le_endpointBaseNumerator_of_gap_nonneg {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (hgap : 0 ≤ (K : ℚ) / base - ∑ i ∈ s, 1 / (d i : ℚ)) : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d
declarations.docstring: Nonnegativity of the rational endpoint gap is exactly the side condition that makes the displayed natural subtraction ordinary.

declarations.name: endpointNumerator_div_endpointDenominatorLcm
declarations.signature: theorem endpointNumerator_div_endpointDenominatorLcm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) : (endpointNumerator K base s d : ℚ) / endpointDenominatorLcm base s d = (K : ℚ) / base - ∑ i ∈ s, 1 / (d i : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: Under the ordinary-subtraction side condition, the displayed natural endpoint numerator divided by its lcm is exactly the rational endpoint gap.

declarations.name: pairwiseCollisionCore_pos
declarations.signature: theorem pairwiseCollisionCore_pos {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : 0 < pairwiseCollisionCore s d
declarations.docstring: The pairwise collision core of a positive denominator family is positive, including for the empty family where the finite lcm is `1`.

declarations.name: finset_lcm_factorization_lt_of_all_lt
declarations.signature: theorem finset_lcm_factorization_lt_of_all_lt {α : Type*} {s : Finset α} {f : α → ℕ} {q e : ℕ} (he : 0 < e) (hpos : ∀ x ∈ s, 0 < f x) (hlt : ∀ x ∈ s, (f x).factorization q < e) : (s.lcm f).factorization q < e
declarations.docstring: If every member of a positive finite family has `q`-valuation below `e`, then so does their least common multiple.

declarations.name: collisionCore_pos
declarations.signature: theorem collisionCore_pos {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : 0 < collisionCore base s d
declarations.docstring: Adjoining a positive distinguished base keeps the full collision core positive.

declarations.name: pairwiseCollisionCore_dvd_denominatorLcm
declarations.signature: theorem pairwiseCollisionCore_dvd_denominatorLcm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} : pairwiseCollisionCore s d ∣ s.lcm d
declarations.docstring: Every pairwise collision factor already occurs in the lcm of the denominator family.

declarations.name: collisionCore_dvd_endpointDenominatorLcm
declarations.signature: theorem collisionCore_dvd_endpointDenominatorLcm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} : collisionCore base s d ∣ endpointDenominatorLcm base s d
declarations.docstring: The full collision core divides the common endpoint denominator.

declarations.name: gcd_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem gcd_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i j : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) (hj : j ∈ s) (hij : i ≠ j) : Nat.gcd (d i) (d j) ∣ pairwiseCollisionCore s d
declarations.docstring: Every off-diagonal pairwise gcd divides the finite pairwise collision core.

declarations.name: lcm_gcd_left_distrib
declarations.signature: theorem lcm_gcd_left_distrib {a b c : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hc : 0 < c) : Nat.lcm (Nat.gcd a b) (Nat.gcd a c) = Nat.gcd a (Nat.lcm b c)
declarations.docstring: Binary distributivity underlying the incremental collision recurrence: the lcm of the parts of two positive denominators shared with `a` is the part of their lcm shared with `a`.

declarations.name: finset_lcm_gcd_left
declarations.signature: theorem finset_lcm_gcd_left {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {a : ℕ} {d : ι → ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : s.lcm (fun i => Nat.gcd a (d i)) = Nat.gcd a (s.lcm d)
declarations.docstring: Finite-family form of `lcm_gcd_left_distrib`. All collisions of one positive denominator with a positive finite family collapse exactly to its gcd with the family lcm.

declarations.name: pairwiseCollisionCore_insert
declarations.signature: theorem pairwiseCollisionCore_insert {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ s) : pairwiseCollisionCore (insert a s) d = Nat.lcm (pairwiseCollisionCore s d) (s.lcm fun j => Nat.gcd (d a) (d j))
declarations.docstring: Adjoining one denominator updates the pairwise collision core by the lcm of the old core and the new denominator's collisions with the old family. The recurrence updates the collision core using one new lcm rather than recomputing all pairs.

declarations.name: pairwiseCollisionCore_insert_gcd_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem pairwiseCollisionCore_insert_gcd_lcm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ s) (hda : 0 < d a) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : pairwiseCollisionCore (insert a s) d = Nat.lcm (pairwiseCollisionCore s d) (Nat.gcd (d a) (s.lcm d))
declarations.docstring: Sharpened one-step collision recurrence. For positive denominators, the entire new collision contribution is the single repeated part `gcd (d a) (s.lcm d)`.

declarations.name: collisionCore_insert
declarations.signature: theorem collisionCore_insert {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ s) : collisionCore base (insert a s) d = Nat.lcm (collisionCore base s d) (s.lcm fun j => Nat.gcd (d a) (d j))
declarations.docstring: The same one-step recurrence after adjoining the distinguished base; the factorial-block collision core below is an instance of this identity.

declarations.name: collisionCore_insert_gcd_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem collisionCore_insert_gcd_lcm {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {a : ι} (ha : a ∉ s) (hda : 0 < d a) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : collisionCore base (insert a s) d = Nat.lcm (collisionCore base s d) (Nat.gcd (d a) (s.lcm d))
declarations.docstring: Positive-denominator sharpening of `collisionCore_insert`: the new full-core inflow is exactly the gcd of the added denominator with the previous denominator lcm.

declarations.name: pairwiseCollisionCore_mul_denominatorLcm_dvd_denominatorProd
declarations.signature: theorem pairwiseCollisionCore_mul_denominatorLcm_dvd_denominatorProd {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : pairwiseCollisionCore s d * s.lcm d ∣ s.prod d
declarations.docstring: The repeated-support core and the denominator lcm together divide the full denominator product. Primewise, their exponents are respectively the second-largest and largest displayed valuations, whose sum is bounded by the total valuation. The insertion proof exposes the same fact directly through the exact gcd-with-prior-lcm recurrence.

declarations.name: collisionCore_div_base_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem collisionCore_div_base_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) : collisionCore base s d / base ∣ pairwiseCollisionCore s d
declarations.docstring: Cancelling a positive distinguished base from the full collision core leaves a divisor of the pairwise collision core.

declarations.name: collisionCore_div_base_eq_pairwiseCollisionCore_div_gcd
declarations.signature: theorem collisionCore_div_base_eq_pairwiseCollisionCore_div_gcd {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) : collisionCore base s d / base = pairwiseCollisionCore s d / Nat.gcd base (pairwiseCollisionCore s d)
declarations.docstring: Exact form of base cancellation in the collision core. Normalization removes precisely the part of the pairwise repeated-support core already visible in the distinguished base, rather than merely producing an unspecified divisor of that core.

declarations.name: collisionCore_div_base_factorization
declarations.signature: theorem collisionCore_div_base_factorization {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q : ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : (collisionCore base s d / base).factorization q = (pairwiseCollisionCore s d).factorization q - base.factorization q
declarations.docstring: Primewise form of exact base cancellation. The normalized collision valuation is the repeated-support valuation in the denominator family minus the valuation already absorbed by the distinguished base.

declarations.name: primePower_dvd_collisionCore_div_base_iff
declarations.signature: theorem primePower_dvd_collisionCore_div_base_iff {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : q ^ e ∣ collisionCore base s d / base ↔ q ^ (e + base.factorization q) ∣ pairwiseCollisionCore s d
declarations.docstring: A prime power survives base normalization exactly when the pairwise collision core contains that power on top of the complete base valuation. This turns normalized collision mass into a higher-power repeated-hit condition.

declarations.name: collisionCore_div_base_mul_denominatorLcm_dvd_denominatorProd
declarations.signature: theorem collisionCore_div_base_mul_denominatorLcm_dvd_denominatorProd {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : (collisionCore base s d / base) * s.lcm d ∣ s.prod d
declarations.docstring: Product/lcm control in the normalized endpoint form: after cancelling the distinguished base, the remaining collision core times the denominator lcm divides the denominator product. Thus lcm estimates give corresponding upper bounds for the normalized collision core.

declarations.name: exists_pairwise_primePower_support_of_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem exists_pairwise_primePower_support_of_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (hpow : q ^ e ∣ pairwiseCollisionCore s d) : ∃ i ∈ s, ∃ j ∈ s, i ≠ j ∧ q ^ e ∣ d i ∧ q ^ e ∣ d j
declarations.docstring: Every positive prime power visible in the pairwise collision core is visible to full multiplicity in two distinct denominators. This is the valuation-sensitive converse to `gcd_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore`; later prime-power hit counts apply it one exponent at a time.

declarations.name: primePower_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore_iff
declarations.signature: theorem primePower_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore_iff {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : q ^ e ∣ pairwiseCollisionCore s d ↔ ∃ i ∈ s, ∃ j ∈ s, i ≠ j ∧ q ^ e ∣ d i ∧ q ^ e ∣ d j
declarations.docstring: Prime-power divisibility of the pairwise collision core is exactly repeated full-power support in the denominator family.

declarations.name: gcd_dvd_collisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem gcd_dvd_collisionCore {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i j : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) (hj : j ∈ s) (hij : i ≠ j) : Nat.gcd (d i) (d j) ∣ collisionCore base s d
declarations.docstring: Every off-diagonal pairwise gcd also divides the full collision core after adjoining the distinguished base denominator.

declarations.name: exists_pairwise_primePower_support_of_dvd_collisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem exists_pairwise_primePower_support_of_dvd_collisionCore {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (hpowBase : ¬q ^ e ∣ base) (hpow : q ^ e ∣ collisionCore base s d) : ∃ i ∈ s, ∃ j ∈ s, i ≠ j ∧ q ^ e ∣ d i ∧ q ^ e ∣ d j
declarations.docstring: Away from the distinguished base, every prime power in the full collision core comes from two full-multiplicity denominator hits.

declarations.name: primePower_dvd_collisionCore_iff
declarations.signature: theorem primePower_dvd_collisionCore_iff {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (hpowBase : ¬q ^ e ∣ base) : q ^ e ∣ collisionCore base s d ↔ ∃ i ∈ s, ∃ j ∈ s, i ≠ j ∧ q ^ e ∣ d i ∧ q ^ e ∣ d j
declarations.docstring: If the distinguished base omits `q^e`, full collision-core support is equivalent to two distinct full-power denominator hits.

declarations.name: prime_not_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore_of_unique_support
declarations.signature: theorem prime_not_dvd_pairwiseCollisionCore_of_unique_support {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q : ℕ} {i : ι} (hq : q.Prime) (hunique : ∀ j ∈ s, j ≠ i → ¬q ∣ d j) : ¬q ∣ pairwiseCollisionCore s d
declarations.docstring: A prime occurring in at most one displayed denominator cannot enter the pairwise collision core.

declarations.name: prime_not_dvd_collisionCore_of_unique_support
declarations.signature: theorem prime_not_dvd_collisionCore_of_unique_support {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q : ℕ} {i : ι} (hq : q.Prime) (hqbase : ¬q ∣ base) (hunique : ∀ j ∈ s, j ≠ i → ¬q ∣ d j) : ¬q ∣ collisionCore base s d
declarations.docstring: If that uniquely supported prime also misses the distinguished base, it misses the full collision core.

declarations.name: collisionCore_privateQuotients_pairwise_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem collisionCore_privateQuotients_pairwise_coprime {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : (s : Set ι).Pairwise fun i j => Nat.Coprime (d i / Nat.gcd (d i) (collisionCore base s d)) (d j / Nat.gcd (d j) (collisionCore base s d))
declarations.docstring: Removing from every positive denominator the portion visible in the finite collision core produces a pairwise-coprime family. This is the finite-family form of the private-support separation theorem.

declarations.name: privateQuotient
declarations.signature: def privateQuotient {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) (i : ι) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Private quotient owned by one denominator after deleting all support visible in the collision core.

declarations.name: privateQuotient_eq_one_of_dvd_base
declarations.signature: theorem privateQuotient_eq_one_of_dvd_base {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hpos : 0 < d i) (hdiv : d i ∣ base) : privateQuotient base s d i = 1
declarations.docstring: An owner already contained in the distinguished base has no surviving private quotient. This is the generic absorption mechanism behind the fact that a fixed owner cannot remain useful on factorial blocks whose base grows without bound.

declarations.name: privateModulus
declarations.signature: def privateModulus {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Product of all finite-family private quotients.

declarations.name: privateQuotient_lcm_eq_privateModulus
declarations.signature: theorem privateQuotient_lcm_eq_privateModulus {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : s.lcm (privateQuotient base s d) = privateModulus base s d
declarations.docstring: The private modulus is also the lcm of the private quotients. Pairwise coprimality is exactly what converts the lcm into the product.

declarations.name: privateModulus_pos
declarations.signature: theorem privateModulus_pos {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : 0 < privateModulus base s d
declarations.docstring: A positive denominator family has positive private modulus, even when all collision deletion quotients equal one.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_privateQuotient_of_unique_support
