declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_privateQuotient_of_unique_support {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q : ℕ} {i : ι} (hq : q.Prime) (hqdi : q ∣ d i) (hqbase : ¬q ∣ base) (hunique : ∀ j ∈ s, j ≠ i → ¬q ∣ d j) : q ∣ privateQuotient base s d i
declarations.docstring: A prime uniquely supported on one denominator survives in that denominator's private quotient.

declarations.name: primePow_dvd_privateQuotient_of_unique_support
declarations.signature: theorem primePow_dvd_privateQuotient_of_unique_support {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q e : ℕ} {i : ι} (hq : q.Prime) (hqPowDi : q ^ e ∣ d i) (hqbase : ¬q ∣ base) (hunique : ∀ j ∈ s, j ≠ i → ¬q ∣ d j) : q ^ e ∣ privateQuotient base s d i
declarations.docstring: Unique support preserves the complete displayed prime power, not only one copy of its prime. Hence a prefix-private power remains present in the corresponding private quotient with its full multiplicity.

declarations.name: privateModulus_one_lt_of_unique_prime_support
declarations.signature: theorem privateModulus_one_lt_of_unique_prime_support {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {q : ℕ} {i : ι} (hq : q.Prime) (hi : i ∈ s) (hqdi : q ∣ d i) (hqbase : ¬q ∣ base) (hunique : ∀ j ∈ s, j ≠ i → ¬q ∣ d j) (hpos : ∀ j ∈ s, 0 < d j) : 1 < privateModulus base s d
declarations.docstring: Consequently a uniquely supported prime makes the full private modulus nontrivial.

declarations.name: weightedPrivateNumerator
declarations.signature: def weightedPrivateNumerator {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (r a : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Weighted leave-one-out CRT numerator for a finite modulus family. The term owned by `i` omits exactly the modulus `r i`.

declarations.name: weightedPrivateNumerator_modEq_owner
declarations.signature: theorem weightedPrivateNumerator_modEq_owner {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {r a : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) : weightedPrivateNumerator s r a ≡ a i * (s.erase i).prod r [MOD r i]
declarations.docstring: Modulo one owned factor, every other leave-one-out term vanishes. Thus the full weighted numerator projects to the single owner term.

declarations.name: weightedPrivateNumerator_coprime_product
declarations.signature: theorem weightedPrivateNumerator_coprime_product {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {r a : ι → ℕ} (hpair : (s : Set ι).Pairwise fun i j => Nat.Coprime (r i) (r j)) (hweight : ∀ i ∈ s, Nat.Coprime (a i) (r i)) : Nat.Coprime (weightedPrivateNumerator s r a) (s.prod r)
declarations.docstring: Private-support CRT lemma. If the moduli are pairwise coprime and each weight is coprime to its own modulus, then the weighted leave-one-out numerator is coprime to the full modulus product. Thus none of the private prime-power support can disappear in primitive reduction.

declarations.name: privateWeight
declarations.signature: def privateWeight {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) (i : ι) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Canonical weight paired with one private quotient.

declarations.name: collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator
declarations.signature: def collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Canonical weighted numerator attached to the finite collision core.

declarations.name: collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator_modEq_owner
declarations.signature: theorem collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator_modEq_owner {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hi : i ∈ s) : collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator base s d ≡ privateWeight base s d i * (s.erase i).prod (privateQuotient base s d) [MOD privateQuotient base s d i]
declarations.docstring: The collision-weighted numerator has an exact one-owner projection modulo each private quotient.

declarations.name: privateWeight_coprime_privateQuotient
declarations.signature: theorem privateWeight_coprime_privateQuotient {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hpos : 0 < d i) : Nat.Coprime (privateWeight base s d i) (privateQuotient base s d i)
declarations.docstring: A canonical collision-core weight is coprime to its private quotient. Both are the standard gcd-reduced quotients of the core and the owned denominator.

declarations.name: privateOwnerTerm_mod_prime_pos
declarations.signature: theorem privateOwnerTerm_mod_prime_pos {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base q : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hq : q.Prime) (hi : i ∈ s) (hpos : ∀ j ∈ s, 0 < d j) (hqdvd : q ∣ privateQuotient base s d i) : 0 < (privateWeight base s d i * (s.erase i).prod (privateQuotient base s d)) % q
declarations.docstring: A prime owned by one canonical private quotient cannot divide that quotient's one-owner weighted term. Pairwise private support excludes the leave-one-out product, while the gcd-reduced canonical weight excludes the remaining factor.

declarations.name: collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator_coprime_privateModulus
declarations.signature: theorem collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator_coprime_privateModulus {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : Nat.Coprime (collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator base s d) (privateModulus base s d)
declarations.docstring: Complete abstract private-support survival theorem for the canonical collision core: its canonical weighted numerator is coprime to the entire private modulus.

declarations.name: lcm_div_gcd_right_distrib
declarations.signature: theorem lcm_div_gcd_right_distrib {a b C : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hC : 0 < C) : Nat.lcm (a / Nat.gcd a C) (b / Nat.gcd b C) = Nat.lcm a b / Nat.gcd (Nat.lcm a b) C
declarations.docstring: Pairwise lcm commutes with deleting the prime-power component shared with a fixed positive core. This is the reusable factorization identity behind the endpoint equation `R = L / C`.

declarations.name: finset_lcm_div_gcd_right_distrib
declarations.signature: theorem finset_lcm_div_gcd_right_distrib {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {C : ℕ} (hC : 0 < C) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : s.lcm (fun i => d i / Nat.gcd (d i) C) = s.lcm d / Nat.gcd (s.lcm d) C
declarations.docstring: Finite-family lift of `lcm_div_gcd_right_distrib`: removing the part shared with a fixed positive collision core commutes with taking the lcm of a finite family of positive denominators.

declarations.name: privateModulus_eq_lcm_div_gcd_collisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem privateModulus_eq_lcm_div_gcd_collisionCore {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : privateModulus base s d = s.lcm d / Nat.gcd (s.lcm d) (collisionCore base s d)
declarations.docstring: The canonical private modulus is exactly the denominator-family lcm after deleting the prime-power support visible in the collision core.

declarations.name: privateModulus_eq_endpointDenominatorLcm_div_collisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem privateModulus_eq_endpointDenominatorLcm_div_collisionCore {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : privateModulus base s d = endpointDenominatorLcm base s d / collisionCore base s d
declarations.docstring: With the distinguished base included, the canonical private modulus is the full endpoint common denominator divided by the collision core.

declarations.name: privateModulus_dvd_endpointDenominatorLcm_div_base
declarations.signature: theorem privateModulus_dvd_endpointDenominatorLcm_div_base {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : privateModulus base s d ∣ endpointDenominatorLcm base s d / base
declarations.docstring: The private modulus divides the common-denominator multiplier of the distinguished base.

declarations.name: privateModulus_dvd_endpointBaseNumerator
declarations.signature: theorem privateModulus_dvd_endpointBaseNumerator {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : privateModulus base s d ∣ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d
declarations.docstring: Hence the private modulus divides the entire positive base contribution, independently of the displayed coefficient `K`.

declarations.name: endpointDenominatorTerm_eq_privateWeight_mul_leaveOneOut
declarations.signature: theorem endpointDenominatorTerm_eq_privateWeight_mul_leaveOneOut {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ j ∈ s, 0 < d j) (hi : i ∈ s) : endpointDenominatorLcm base s d / d i = privateWeight base s d i * (s.erase i).prod (privateQuotient base s d)
declarations.docstring: Each common-denominator tail term is exactly its canonical collision weight times the product of every other private quotient.

declarations.name: endpointTailNumerator_eq_collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator
declarations.signature: theorem endpointTailNumerator_eq_collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) : endpointTailNumerator base s d = collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator base s d
declarations.docstring: The canonical collision-weighted numerator is literally the tail numerator over the full endpoint common denominator.

declarations.name: endpointNumerator_add_tail_eq_endpointBaseNumerator
declarations.signature: theorem endpointNumerator_add_tail_eq_endpointBaseNumerator {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) : endpointNumerator K base s d + endpointTailNumerator base s d = endpointBaseNumerator K base s d
declarations.docstring: Under the positive-endpoint ordering, the displayed numerator plus its tail numerator recovers the base contribution exactly.

declarations.name: endpointNumerator_add_tail_modEq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem endpointNumerator_add_tail_modEq_zero {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) : endpointNumerator K base s d + endpointTailNumerator base s d ≡ 0 [MOD privateModulus base s d]
declarations.docstring: Exact negative-residue transport for the displayed endpoint numerator: `Z + T` is zero modulo the private modulus.

declarations.name: endpointNumerator_add_collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator_modEq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem endpointNumerator_add_collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator_modEq_zero {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) : endpointNumerator K base s d + collisionWeightedPrivateNumerator base s d ≡ 0 [MOD privateModulus base s d]
declarations.docstring: The same negative-residue congruence stated with the canonical collision-weighted CRT numerator.

declarations.name: coprime_left_of_add_modEq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem coprime_left_of_add_modEq_zero {Z T R : ℕ} (hmod : Z + T ≡ 0 [MOD R]) (hcop : Nat.Coprime T R) : Nat.Coprime Z R
declarations.docstring: If `Z + T` vanishes modulo `R` and `T` is coprime to `R`, then `Z` is also coprime to `R`.

declarations.name: endpointNumerator_coprime_privateModulus
declarations.signature: theorem endpointNumerator_coprime_privateModulus {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) : Nat.Coprime (endpointNumerator K base s d) (privateModulus base s d)
declarations.docstring: Complete private-support survival statement for the displayed endpoint: under the positive-endpoint ordering, its numerator is coprime to the whole private modulus.

declarations.name: exists_large_prefix_private_factorialGap_hit
declarations.signature: theorem exists_large_prefix_private_factorialGap_hit {p n C : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hn2 : 2 ≤ n) (hpn : p ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hlarge : C * n < p) : ∃ m, 2 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ n ∧ C * m < p ∧ p ∣ m.factorial - 1 ∧ ∀ k, 2 ≤ k → k < m → Nat.Coprime p (k.factorial - 1)
declarations.docstring: A large prime divisor of a factorial gap becomes prefix-private at its first occurrence. The size bound transfers from the index `n` to the minimal hit `m`, producing a factorial gap where the prime is genuinely prefix-private.

declarations.name: prime_not_dvd_succ_factorial_sub_one_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem prime_not_dvd_succ_factorial_sub_one_of_dvd {q n : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hqdvd : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) : ¬q ∣ (n + 1).factorial - 1
declarations.docstring: A prime dividing `n! - 1` cannot also divide the immediately following factorial gap. Modulo that prime, `(n+1)! - 1` reduces to `n`, while every prime divisor of `n! - 1` is larger than `n`.

declarations.name: projectedResidue
declarations.docstring: Canonical projection of a weighted support numerator modulo `Q`.

declarations.name: complementaryProjectedResidue
declarations.docstring: Canonical projection of the additive inverse of a natural numerator. The outer remainder sends the zero residue to zero rather than to `Q`.

declarations.name: projectedResidue_eq_complementary_of_add_modEq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem projectedResidue_eq_complementary_of_add_modEq_zero {Z T Q : ℕ} (hQ : 0 < Q) (hmod : Z + T ≡ 0 [MOD Q]) : projectedResidue Z Q = complementaryProjectedResidue T Q
declarations.docstring: If `Z + T` vanishes modulo a positive modulus, the projection of `Z` is the complementary projection of `T`.

declarations.name: endpointPrivateResidue
declarations.signature: def endpointPrivateResidue {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (K base : ℕ) (s : Finset ι) (d : ι → ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Least nonnegative private-modulus residue of the displayed endpoint numerator. Under a nontrivial private modulus, coprimality makes it the least positive residue.

declarations.name: projectedResidue_endpointPrivateResidue_eq_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem projectedResidue_endpointPrivateResidue_eq_of_dvd {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {Q : ℕ} (hQ : Q ∣ privateModulus base s d) : projectedResidue (endpointPrivateResidue K base s d) Q = projectedResidue (endpointNumerator K base s d) Q
declarations.docstring: Reducing the least residue modulo a divisor of the full private modulus is the same as reducing the original endpoint numerator directly.

declarations.name: projectedResidue_bounds_of_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem projectedResidue_bounds_of_coprime {Z R : ℕ} (hR : 1 < R) (hcop : Nat.Coprime Z R) : 0 < projectedResidue Z R ∧ projectedResidue Z R ≤ Z ∧ projectedResidue Z R < R
declarations.docstring: A residue of a number coprime to a nontrivial modulus is positive, bounded above by the number, and strictly below the modulus.

declarations.name: complementaryProjectedResidue_eq_sub_of_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem complementaryProjectedResidue_eq_sub_of_coprime {T R : ℕ} (hR : 1 < R) (hcop : Nat.Coprime T R) : complementaryProjectedResidue T R = R - T % R
declarations.docstring: For a coprime numerator and a nontrivial modulus, the complementary projection is the literal positive complement of the ordinary remainder.

declarations.name: add_complementaryProjectedResidue_eq_succ_div_mul
declarations.signature: theorem add_complementaryProjectedResidue_eq_succ_div_mul {T R : ℕ} (hR : 1 < R) (hcop : Nat.Coprime T R) : T + complementaryProjectedResidue T R = (T / R + 1) * R
declarations.docstring: Adding that complementary projection advances the Euclidean quotient by exactly one. This is the natural-number form of the distance from `T / R` to its next integer.

declarations.name: endpointPrivateResidue_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem endpointPrivateResidue_bounds {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) (hR : 1 < privateModulus base s d) : 0 < endpointPrivateResidue K base s d ∧ endpointPrivateResidue K base s d ≤ endpointNumerator K base s d ∧ endpointPrivateResidue K base s d < privateModulus base s d
declarations.docstring: The actual displayed endpoint residue satisfies the same sharp natural bounds once the private modulus is nontrivial.

declarations.name: endpointPrivateResidue_add_tail_modEq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem endpointPrivateResidue_add_tail_modEq_zero {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) : endpointPrivateResidue K base s d + endpointTailNumerator base s d ≡ 0 [MOD privateModulus base s d]
declarations.docstring: The least positive endpoint residue carries the same negative-tail congruence as the displayed endpoint numerator.

declarations.name: endpointPrivateResidue_add_owner_modEq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem endpointPrivateResidue_add_owner_modEq_zero {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ j ∈ s, 0 < d j) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) (hi : i ∈ s) : endpointPrivateResidue K base s d + privateWeight base s d i * (s.erase i).prod (privateQuotient base s d) ≡ 0 [MOD privateQuotient base s d i]
declarations.docstring: Projecting further to one private quotient leaves a single explicit owner term in the negative-tail congruence.

declarations.name: endpointPrivateResidue_add_owner_modEq_zero_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem endpointPrivateResidue_add_owner_modEq_zero_of_dvd {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base q : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ j ∈ s, 0 < d j) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) (hi : i ∈ s) (hq : q ∣ privateQuotient base s d i) : endpointPrivateResidue K base s d + privateWeight base s d i *
declarations.docstring: The same owner congruence descends to every divisor of the owned private quotient.

declarations.name: complementary_residue_lower_bound
declarations.signature: theorem complementary_residue_lower_bound {ρ T q : ℕ} (hmod : ρ + T ≡ 0 [MOD q]) (hTpos : 0 < T % q) : q - T % q ≤ ρ
declarations.docstring: If `ρ` is the additive complement of a nonzero residue `T mod q`, then `ρ` is at least the explicit complementary residue `q - T mod q`.

declarations.name: endpointPrivateResidue_owner_lower_bound
declarations.signature: theorem endpointPrivateResidue_owner_lower_bound {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base q : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} {i : ι} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ j ∈ s, 0 < d j) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) (hi : i ∈ s) (hq : q ∣ privateQuotient base s d i) (howner : 0 <
declarations.docstring: A nonzero one-owner projection gives a concrete numerical lower bound for the full endpoint private residue.

declarations.name: scaled_endpoint_upper_bound_excluded_by_residue
declarations.signature: theorem scaled_endpoint_upper_bound_excluded_by_residue {ρ Z L scale budget : ℕ} (hρZ : ρ ≤ Z) (hupper : scale * Z ≤ budget * L) (hlarge : budget * L < scale * ρ) : False
declarations.docstring: An upper bound on a scaled endpoint numerator is incompatible with a strictly larger scaled least residue.

declarations.name: endpoint_scaled_upper_bound_false_of_privateResidue
declarations.signature: theorem endpoint_scaled_upper_bound_false_of_privateResidue {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {K base scale budget : ℕ} {s : Finset ι} {d : ι → ℕ} (hbase : 0 < base) (hpos : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 < d i) (htail : endpointTailNumerator base s d ≤ endpointBaseNumerator K base s d) (hR : 1 < privateModulus base s d) (hupper : scale * endpointNumerator K base s d ≤ budget * endpointDenominatorLcm base s d) (hlarge :
declarations.docstring: Collision-core specialization of the preceding incompatibility.

declarations.name: leaveOneOutModulus
declarations.docstring: Modulus obtained by omitting one private quotient.

declarations.name: min_leaveOneOutModulus_mul_max_eq
declarations.signature: theorem min_leaveOneOutModulus_mul_max_eq {R r₁ r₂ : ℕ} (hR : 0 < R) (hr₁ : r₁ ∣ R) (hr₂ : r₂ ∣ R) : min (leaveOneOutModulus R r₁) (leaveOneOutModulus R r₂) * max r₁ r₂ = R
declarations.docstring: Two divisors of a positive modulus satisfy the exact order-reversing deletion identity: the smaller leave-one-out modulus times the larger deleted factor recovers the full modulus.

declarations.name: leaveOneOut_lcm_eq_of_coprime_divisors
declarations.signature: theorem leaveOneOut_lcm_eq_of_coprime_divisors {R a b : ℕ} (ha : a ∣ R) (hb : b ∣ R) (hab : Nat.Coprime a b) : Nat.lcm (leaveOneOutModulus R a) (leaveOneOutModulus R b) = R
declarations.docstring: Deleting two coprime divisors of a modulus produces two projection moduli whose lcm recovers the full modulus. Unlike the owner-indexed specialization below, the deleted factors may come from the same private quotient.

declarations.name: projection_disagreement_forces_gt
declarations.signature: theorem projection_disagreement_forces_gt {ρ B Q₁ Q₂ : ℕ} (hQ₁ : B < Q₁) (hQ₂ : B < Q₂) (hneq : projectedResidue ρ Q₁ ≠ projectedResidue ρ Q₂) : B < ρ
declarations.docstring: Any residue below both projection moduli has identical projections. Thus disagreement forces it above the prescribed budget.

declarations.name: projection_disagreement_forces_min_modulus_le_residue
declarations.signature: theorem projection_disagreement_forces_min_modulus_le_residue {ρ Q₁ Q₂ : ℕ} (hneq : projectedResidue ρ Q₁ ≠ projectedResidue ρ Q₂) : min Q₁ Q₂ ≤ ρ
declarations.docstring: Quantitative form: unequal projections force the true residue to reach at least the smaller modulus.

declarations.name: leaveOneOut_disagreement_forces_min_modulus_le_residue
declarations.signature: theorem leaveOneOut_disagreement_forces_min_modulus_le_residue {R ρ r₁ r₂ : ℕ} (hneq : projectedResidue ρ (leaveOneOutModulus R r₁) ≠ projectedResidue ρ (leaveOneOutModulus R r₂)) : min (leaveOneOutModulus R r₁) (leaveOneOutModulus R r₂) ≤ ρ
declarations.docstring: Leave-one-out specialization of the quantitative projection theorem.

declarations.name: projectedResidue_complementaryProjectedResidue_eq_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem projectedResidue_complementaryProjectedResidue_eq_of_dvd {T Q R : ℕ} (hR : 0 < R) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hQR : Q ∣ R) : projectedResidue (complementaryProjectedResidue T R) Q = complementaryProjectedResidue T Q
declarations.docstring: Complementary projection commutes with passage from a full positive modulus to any positive divisor. This is the coefficient-free transport needed to compare the global private residue with leave-one-out views.

declarations.name: projectedResidue_eq_residue_of_eq_of_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem projectedResidue_eq_residue_of_eq_of_lcm {ρ Q₁ Q₂ R : ℕ} (hρR : ρ < R) (hlcm : Nat.lcm Q₁ Q₂ = R) (heq : projectedResidue ρ Q₁ = projectedResidue ρ Q₂) : projectedResidue ρ Q₁ = ρ
declarations.docstring: If two projection moduli jointly recover the full modulus, equal projections are not merely compatible: their common value is the full least residue. Thus a leave-one-out pair whose lcm is `R` has an exact dichotomy between disagreement and a genuinely small global residue.

declarations.name: projectionPairFloor
declarations.signature: def projectionPairFloor (ρ Q₁ Q₂ : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: A branch-free lower certificate extracted from two projections: use their common value when they agree, and otherwise use the smaller modulus.

declarations.name: projectionPairFloor_full_divisor_eq_min
declarations.signature: theorem projectionPairFloor_full_divisor_eq_min {ρ Q R : ℕ} (hρR : ρ < R) (hQ : 0 < Q) (hQR : Q ∣ R) : projectionPairFloor ρ R Q = min ρ Q
declarations.docstring: Pairing the full modulus with one positive divisor has no hidden CRT branch: the pair floor is exactly the smaller of the full least residue and that divisor.

declarations.name: lt_mul_min_iff
declarations.signature: theorem lt_mul_min_iff {A S x y : ℕ} : A < S * min x y ↔ A < S * x ∧ A < S * y
declarations.docstring: A product exceeds a scaled minimum exactly when it exceeds both scaled entries. This elementary split is useful for exposing the two independent arithmetic obligations hidden by a branch-free projection floor.

declarations.name: projectionPairFloor_le_residue_of_lt_of_lcm
declarations.signature: theorem projectionPairFloor_le_residue_of_lt_of_lcm {ρ Q₁ Q₂ R : ℕ} (hρR : ρ < R) (hlcm : Nat.lcm Q₁ Q₂ = R) : projectionPairFloor ρ Q₁ Q₂ ≤ ρ
declarations.docstring: When the two moduli recover `R`, the computable pair floor is always bounded by the full least residue. This packages the equality and disagreement branches into one unconditional CRT certificate.

declarations.name: projectedResidue_eq_of_congruent_bounded
declarations.signature: theorem projectedResidue_eq_of_congruent_bounded {Z T Q B : ℕ} (hmod : Z ≡ T [MOD Q]) (hZle : Z ≤ B) (hBQ : B < Q) : projectedResidue T Q = Z
declarations.docstring: A congruent endpoint numerator smaller than a projection modulus is exactly the corresponding projected residue.

declarations.name: large_projection_identifies_endpoint
declarations.signature: theorem large_projection_identifies_endpoint {Z T R Q B : ℕ} (hmod : Z ≡ T [MOD R]) (hQR : Q ∣ R) (hZle : Z ≤ B) (hBQ : B < Q) : projectedResidue T Q = Z
declarations.docstring: Congruence modulo `R` descends to every divisor `Q` of `R`, so a bounded endpoint identifies every sufficiently large projected residue.

declarations.name: large_projection_excludes_bounded_endpoint
declarations.signature: theorem large_projection_excludes_bounded_endpoint {Z T R Q B : ℕ} (hmod : Z ≡ T [MOD R]) (hQR : Q ∣ R) (hZle : Z ≤ B) (hBQ : B < Q) (hproj : B < projectedResidue T Q) : False
declarations.docstring: One projected residue above the endpoint budget excludes every positive endpoint numerator in that budget.

declarations.name: projection_disagreement_excludes_bounded_endpoint
declarations.signature: theorem projection_disagreement_excludes_bounded_endpoint {Z T R Q₁ Q₂ B : ℕ} (hmod : Z ≡ T [MOD R]) (hQ₁R : Q₁ ∣ R) (hQ₂R : Q₂ ∣ R) (hZle : Z ≤ B) (hBQ₁ : B < Q₁) (hBQ₂ : B < Q₂) (hneq : projectedResidue T Q₁ ≠ projectedResidue T Q₂) : False
declarations.docstring: Deterministic two-projection certificate: unequal sufficiently large projections rule out a bounded endpoint numerator congruent to the weighted support numerator modulo the full private modulus.

declarations.name: leaveOneOut_disagreement_excludes_bounded_endpoint
declarations.signature: theorem leaveOneOut_disagreement_excludes_bounded_endpoint {Z T R r₁ r₂ B : ℕ} (hmod : Z ≡ T [MOD R]) (hr₁ : r₁ ∣ R) (hr₂ : r₂ ∣ R) (hZle : Z ≤ B) (hB₁ : B < leaveOneOutModulus R r₁) (hB₂ : B < leaveOneOutModulus R r₂) (hneq : projectedResidue T (leaveOneOutModulus R r₁) ≠ projectedResidue T (leaveOneOutModulus R r₂)) : False
declarations.docstring: Leave-one-out specialization for the weighted endpoint numerator.

declarations.name: factorialGapTail_eq_next_add_tail
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapTail_eq_next_add_tail (D : ℕ) : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapTail D = (1 : ℝ) / (((((D + 1).factorial : ℤ) - 1 : ℤ)) : ℝ) + _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapTail (D + 1)
declarations.docstring: Splitting off the first omitted factorial-gap term advances the universal tail cutoff by one.

declarations.name: factorialBlockIndices
declarations.docstring: Reciprocal-denominator index block for the factorial endpoint: `2, …, 2p-1`.

declarations.name: factorialGapDenominator
declarations.docstring: Literal Erdős #68 reciprocal denominator.

declarations.name: prefixPrivate_factorialGap_unique_in_tailoredBlock
declarations.signature: theorem prefixPrivate_factorialGap_unique_in_tailoredBlock {q n : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hn2 : 2 ≤ n) (hqdvd : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hprefix : ∀ k, 2 ≤ k → k < n → Nat.Coprime q (k.factorial - 1)) : n / 2 + 1 ≤ n ∧ n ∈ factorialBlockIndices (n / 2 + 1) ∧ ∀ m ∈ factorialBlockIndices (n / 2 + 1), m ≠ n → ¬q ∣ factorialGapDenominator m
declarations.docstring: A prefix-private prime hit becomes genuinely unique on the tailored factorial block with parameter `n / 2 + 1`. The hit lies at the block's upper endpoint when `n` is odd and one below it when `n` is even; prefix privacy handles every earlier index and the successor lemma handles the only possible later index.

declarations.name: exists_large_unique_factorialBlock_hit
declarations.signature: theorem exists_large_unique_factorialBlock_hit {q n C : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hn2 : 2 ≤ n) (hqdvd : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hlarge : C * n < q) : ∃ m p, 2 ≤ m ∧ m ≤ n ∧ p = m / 2 + 1 ∧ C * m < q ∧ p ≤ m ∧ m ∈ factorialBlockIndices p ∧ q ∣ factorialGapDenominator m ∧ ∀ k ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, k ≠ m → ¬q ∣ factorialGapDenominator k
declarations.docstring: Passing to the least factorial-gap hit turns any prime satisfying the displayed size hypotheses into a uniquely supported upper-half prime on an explicit tailored endpoint block.

declarations.name: cofinal_unique_factorialBlock_hits_of_cofinal_large_primes
declarations.signature: theorem cofinal_unique_factorialBlock_hits_of_cofinal_large_primes (hsource : ∀ A : ℕ, ∃ q n : ℕ, q.Prime ∧ 2 ≤ n ∧ A < n ∧ q ∣ n.factorial - 1 ∧ n < q) : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ p m q : ℕ, B < p ∧ q.Prime ∧ p ≤ m ∧ m ∈ factorialBlockIndices p ∧ q ∣ factorialGapDenominator m ∧
declarations.docstring: A cofinal supply of prime divisors `q > n` of factorial gaps promotes to cofinally many tailored blocks with a uniquely supported upper-half prime. The factorial threshold in the hypothesis forces the least hit past `2B+1`, hence its tailored block parameter past `B`.

declarations.name: factorialBlockBase
declarations.docstring: Distinguished predecessor-factorial denominator in the prime block.

declarations.name: factorialBlockCoefficient
declarations.docstring: Actual strict-successor coefficient at the predecessor prefix, converted to a natural number for the displayed positive endpoint numerator.

declarations.name: factorialBlockEndpointLcm
declarations.docstring: Full literal common denominator `L_p`.

declarations.name: factorialBlockCollisionCore
declarations.docstring: Literal collision core `C_p`.

declarations.name: factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore
declarations.docstring: Collision core after cancelling the forced predecessor-factorial base.

declarations.name: factorialBlockUpperDescFactorial
declarations.docstring: Product of the upper factorial block `p⋯(2p-1)`, which remains after cancelling `(p-1)!` from `(2p-1)!`.

declarations.name: factorialBlockPrivateModulus
declarations.docstring: Literal private modulus `R_p = L_p / C_p`.

declarations.name: factorialBlockTailNumerator
declarations.docstring: Common-denominator reciprocal-tail numerator `T_p`.

declarations.name: factorialBlockBaseNumerator
declarations.docstring: Positive predecessor contribution to the displayed block numerator.

declarations.name: factorialBlockEndpointNumerator
declarations.docstring: Literal displayed endpoint numerator `Z_p`.

declarations.name: factorialBlockPrivateResidue
declarations.docstring: Literal least private-modulus residue `ρ_p`.

declarations.name: factorialBlockPrivateQuotient
declarations.docstring: Literal private quotient owned by the factorial-gap denominator at index `n`.

declarations.name: factorialGapDenominator_dvd_factorialBlockBase_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapDenominator_dvd_factorialBlockBase_of_lt {p n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hlt : factorialGapDenominator n < p) : factorialGapDenominator n ∣ factorialBlockBase p
declarations.docstring: Once the growing predecessor-factorial base passes a fixed factorial-gap denominator, that denominator divides the base.

declarations.name: factorialBlockPrivateQuotient_eq_one_of_gap_lt
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockPrivateQuotient_eq_one_of_gap_lt {p n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hlt : factorialGapDenominator n < p) : factorialBlockPrivateQuotient p n = 1
declarations.docstring: Every fixed factorial-gap owner is eventually absorbed by the growing base: for all `p > n! - 1`, its literal private quotient is exactly one. Thus a cofinal two-owner argument must use indices (or prime factors) escaping with the block parameter rather than remaining fixed.

declarations.name: factorialBlockParameter_le_gap_of_privateQuotient_ne_one
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockParameter_le_gap_of_privateQuotient_ne_one {p n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hne : factorialBlockPrivateQuotient p n ≠ 1) : p ≤ factorialGapDenominator n
declarations.docstring: Contrapositive form of fixed-owner absorption: a nontrivial private quotient can survive only while the block parameter has not passed its source denominator.

declarations.name: factorialBlockFixedPairPrivateQuotients_eq_one
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockFixedPairPrivateQuotients_eq_one {p i j : ℕ} (hi : 2 ≤ i) (hj : 2 ≤ j) (hlt : max (factorialGapDenominator i) (factorialGapDenominator j) < p) : factorialBlockPrivateQuotient p i = 1 ∧ factorialBlockPrivateQuotient p j = 1
declarations.docstring: Direct fixed-pair no-go form: after the block parameter passes the two source denominators, both private quotients are simultaneously absorbed.

declarations.name: factorialBlockLeaveOneOutModulus
declarations.docstring: Literal projection modulus obtained by deleting the private quotient owned by index `n` from the full private modulus.

declarations.name: factorialBlockFactorProjectionModulus
declarations.docstring: Literal projection modulus obtained by deleting any selected divisor of the full private modulus. This factor-level view can split one owner's private quotient into several CRT channels.

declarations.name: factorialBlockPrivateOwnerTerm
declarations.docstring: Literal one-owner term attached to index `n` in the private CRT projection of the factorial block.

declarations.name: factorialBlockScale
declarations.docstring: Exact scale `2p²(2p-1)!` in the endpoint comparison.

declarations.name: factorialBlockBudget
declarations.docstring: Exact budget numerator `2p+1` in the endpoint upper bound.

declarations.name: factorialBlockEndpointGap
declarations.docstring: Literal rational endpoint gap `K_{p-1}/(p-1)! - s_{2p-1}`.

declarations.name: factorialBlockEndpointUpperBound
declarations.docstring: Literal Archimedean endpoint allowance `(2p+1)/(2p²(2p-1)!)`.

declarations.name: factorialGapTail_lt_factorialBlockEndpointUpperBound
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapTail_lt_factorialBlockEndpointUpperBound {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapTail (2 * p - 1) < (factorialBlockEndpointUpperBound p : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The actual tail beyond `2p-1` lies below the literal prime-block allowance. Splitting off the first term gains the factor missing from the coarser bound `tail D < 1/D!`.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_addedTerm_add_gridCell_le_endpointUpperBound
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_addedTerm_add_gridCell_le_endpointUpperBound {p : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) : (1 : ℝ) / (((2 * p).factorial : ℝ) - 1) + 1 / ((2 * p).factorial : ℝ) ≤ (factorialBlockEndpointUpperBound p : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The newly added `2p`-th factorial-gap term plus one full `2p`-factorial grid cell still fits inside the prime-block endpoint allowance.

declarations.name: factorialBlockEndpointWindow
declarations.docstring: The exact positive endpoint window targeted by a full prime block.

declarations.name: strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_pos
declarations.signature: theorem strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_pos (n : ℕ) : (0 : ℤ) < strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix n : ℚ) : ℝ) n
declarations.docstring: The strict successor of every genuine factorial-gap prefix is a positive integer.

declarations.name: factorialBlockCoefficient_cast_eq_strictFacTop
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockCoefficient_cast_eq_strictFacTop {p : ℕ} : (factorialBlockCoefficient p : ℤ) = strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix (p - 1) : ℚ) : ℝ) (p - 1)
declarations.docstring: Conversion to a natural coefficient does not alter the positive strict successor at the predecessor prefix.

declarations.name: factorialBlockEndpointWindow_of_unitCarryBlock
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockEndpointWindow_of_unitCarryBlock {p : ℕ} (hp : 3 ≤ p) (hunit : ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc p (2 * p), factorialGapStepCarry m = 1) : factorialBlockEndpointWindow p
declarations.docstring: If every strict-successor carry from `p` through `2p` is the unit carry, the normalized strict successor stays fixed across the whole block. The final prefix is then trapped in the literal prime-block endpoint window.

declarations.name: factorialBlockEndpointWindow_of_series_eq_rat
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockEndpointWindow_of_series_eq_rat {p q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hp : 3 ≤ p) (hq : 0 < q) (hqp : q ≤ p - 1) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : factorialBlockEndpointWindow p
declarations.docstring: If a displayed rational denominator already clears at `(p-1)!`, then the literal strict-successor endpoint is the series itself. Consequently its gap above the prefix through `2p-1` is exactly the analytic tail and therefore lies in the endpoint window used below.

declarations.name: factorialGapDenominator_cast
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapDenominator_cast {n : ℕ} : (factorialGapDenominator n : ℚ) = (n.factorial : ℚ) - 1
declarations.docstring: Casting a factorial-gap denominator into the rationals recovers the denominator appearing in the Erdős #68 prefix.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_reciprocalSum_eq_factorialGapPrefix
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_reciprocalSum_eq_factorialGapPrefix {p : ℕ} : (∑ n ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, 1 / (factorialGapDenominator n : ℚ)) = factorialGapPrefix (2 * p - 1)
declarations.docstring: The reciprocal sum over the literal prime block is exactly the actual factorial-gap prefix through `2p-1`.

declarations.name: factorialGapDenominator_pos_of_mem
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapDenominator_pos_of_mem {p n : ℕ} (hn : n ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) : 0 < factorialGapDenominator n
declarations.docstring: Every literal block denominator is positive.

declarations.name: factorialBlockPrivateModulus_pos
declarations.docstring: The literal private modulus is always positive.

declarations.name: factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_mul_gapLcm_dvd_gapProd
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_mul_gapLcm_dvd_gapProd {p : ℕ} : factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p * (factorialBlockIndices p).lcm factorialGapDenominator ∣ (factorialBlockIndices p).prod factorialGapDenominator
declarations.docstring: Literal factorial-block specialization of the normalized collision product/lcm bound.

declarations.name: factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_le_gapProd_div_gapLcm
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_le_gapProd_div_gapLcm {p : ℕ} : factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p ≤ (factorialBlockIndices p).prod factorialGapDenominator / (factorialBlockIndices p).lcm factorialGapDenominator
declarations.docstring: Explicit upper-bound form of the factorial-block product/lcm divisibility. Any stronger lower estimate for the factorial-gap lcm gives a corresponding upper estimate for the normalized collision core.

declarations.name: factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_pos
declarations.docstring: The normalized factorial-block collision core is always positive.

declarations.name: factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_factorization
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_factorization {p q : ℕ} : (factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p).factorization q = (pairwiseCollisionCore (factorialBlockIndices p) factorialGapDenominator).factorization q - (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q
declarations.docstring: The factorial-block normalized collision valuation is exactly the pairwise repeated-support valuation above the amount already carried by the predecessor-factorial base; it is the valuation formula used by the prime-power incidence estimates below.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePower_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore_iff_two_hits
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_primePower_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore_iff_two_hits {p q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) : q ^ e ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p ↔ ∃ i ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, ∃ j ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, i ≠ j ∧ q ^ (e + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q) ∣ factorialGapDenominator i ∧ q ^ (e + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q) ∣ factorialGapDenominator j
declarations.docstring: A normalized factorial-block prime power is exactly a repeated factorial-gap hit at the exponent obtained by adding the full predecessor-factorial base valuation.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePower_le_gapPow_of_two_hits
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_primePower_le_gapPow_of_two_hits {p q e i j : ℕ} (hi : i ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hij : i < j) (hiPow : q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator i) (hjPow : q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator j) : q ^ e ≤ j ^ (j - i)
declarations.docstring: Any prime power shared by two displayed factorial gaps is at most the power of the later index whose exponent is their separation. This is the pairwise metric form of the factorial-gap gcd bound.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_prime_hitPair_distance_gt_exponent
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_prime_hitPair_distance_gt_exponent {p q e i j : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hi : i ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hij : i < j) (hiPow : q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator i) (hjPow : q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator j) : e < j - i
declarations.docstring: Prime-power hits are universally farther apart than their exponent. No block-endpoint hypothesis is needed: a prime dividing `j! - 1` is automatically larger than `j`, and the factorial-gap gcd bound then compares `q^e` with `j^(j-i)`.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_hitPair_distance_gt_exponent_of_endpoint_lt_base
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_hitPair_distance_gt_exponent_of_endpoint_lt_base {p q e i j : ℕ} (he : 0 < e) (hendpoint : 2 * p - 1 < q) (hi : i ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hj : j ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hij : i < j) (hiPow : q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator i) (hjPow : q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator j) : e < j - i
declarations.docstring: Above the displayed block endpoint, every pair of `q^e` factorial-gap hits—not merely one selected pair—is separated by more than `e` indices, which bounds how many such hits fit inside a factorial block.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePowerHitCount_mul_succ_le_of_endpoint_lt_base
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_primePowerHitCount_mul_succ_le_of_endpoint_lt_base {p q e : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (he : 0 < e) (hendpoint : 2 * p - 1 < q) : ((factorialBlockIndices p).filter fun i => q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator i).card * (e + 1) ≤ 2 * p + e - 2
declarations.docstring: Quantitative packing consequence of universal hit spacing. When the power base exceeds the block endpoint, thickening every `q^e`-hit by the interval of length `e+1` starting there produces disjoint intervals inside `[2, 2p-1+e]`. Hence the number of hits times `e+1` is bounded by the length `2p+e-2` of that enlarged block.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePowerHitCount_mul_succ_le
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_primePowerHitCount_mul_succ_le {p q e : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) : ((factorialBlockIndices p).filter fun i => q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator i).card * (e + 1) ≤ 2 * p + e - 2
declarations.docstring: Universal prime-power packing bound. For a prime base, the automatic inequality `j < q` at every factorial-gap hit removes the endpoint hypothesis from the preceding estimate.

declarations.name: exists_factorialBlock_hitPair_with_normalizedPrimePower_le_gapPow
declarations.signature: theorem exists_factorialBlock_hitPair_with_normalizedPrimePower_le_gapPow {p q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hpow : q ^ e ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) : ∃ i ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, ∃ j ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, i < j ∧ q ^ (e + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q) ∣ factorialGapDenominator i ∧ q ^ (e + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q) ∣ factorialGapDenominator j ∧ q ^ (e + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q) ≤
declarations.docstring: Distance-sensitive witness for a normalized collision prime power. The full surviving exponent together with the predecessor-factorial base valuation divides two displayed gaps, hence is bounded by the intervening descending-factorial collision cost.

declarations.name: exists_factorialBlock_hitPair_distance_gt_of_endpointPow_lt_normalizedPrimePower
declarations.signature: theorem exists_factorialBlock_hitPair_distance_gt_of_endpointPow_lt_normalizedPrimePower {p q e d : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hpow : q ^ e ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) (hlarge : (2 * p - 1) ^ d < q ^ (e + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q)) : ∃ i ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, ∃ j ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, i < j ∧ d < j - i ∧ q ^ (e + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q) ∣
declarations.docstring: A normalized collision prime power that exceeds the `d`-th power of the block endpoint can only be witnessed by hits more than `d` indices apart. Thus any independent spacing bound for prime-power factorial hits gives a corresponding exclusion from the private modulus.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_exponent_add_base_factorization_lt_prime
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_exponent_add_base_factorization_lt_prime {p q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hpow : q ^ e ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) : e + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q < q
declarations.docstring: Exact excess-exponent ceiling for a normalized collision prime power. The surviving exponent plus the full predecessor-factorial valuation stays strictly below `q`; otherwise `q^q` would divide a displayed gap `i! - 1`, while every such `q`-hit has `i < q` and hence `i! - 1 < q^q`.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_factorization_add_base_lt_prime
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_factorization_add_base_lt_prime {p q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hdiv : q ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) : (factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p).factorization q + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q < q
declarations.docstring: Primewise form of the exact excess-exponent ceiling: the complete normalized-core valuation plus the predecessor-factorial valuation is strictly smaller than the prime itself.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_exponent_add_base_factorization_lt_blockDiameter
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_exponent_add_base_factorization_lt_blockDiameter {p q e : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hpow : q ^ e ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) : e + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q < 2 * p - 3
declarations.docstring: Global block-diameter ceiling for every normalized collision prime. The complete surviving exponent and the predecessor-factorial base valuation occur together in two displayed gaps. Universal prime-hit spacing therefore bounds their sum by the diameter of `[2,2p-1]`, without any assumption that `q` lies above the endpoint.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_factorization_add_base_lt_blockDiameter
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_factorization_add_base_lt_blockDiameter {p q : ℕ} (hp : 2 ≤ p) (hq : q.Prime) (hdiv : q ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) : (factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p).factorization q + (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q < 2 * p - 3
declarations.docstring: Primewise form of the global diameter ceiling. For every prime in the normalized core, its complete normalized valuation plus its full base valuation is strictly smaller than `2p-3`.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_factorization_lt_blockDiameter_of_endpoint_lt_prime
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_normalizedCollision_factorization_lt_blockDiameter_of_endpoint_lt_prime {p q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hendpoint : 2 * p - 1 < q) (hdiv : q ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) : (factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p).factorization q < 2 * p - 3
declarations.docstring: For a collision prime above the entire displayed block, the complete normalized valuation is bounded by the block diameter, not merely by the prime. Indeed the full valuation survives as a prime power, while the predecessor-factorial base has zero `q`-valuation. The resulting repeated hits must be farther apart than that valuation, but both lie in `[2, 2p-1]`. This is the valuation cutoff naturally matched to least-prime-factor inputs with `2p-1 < q`.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_base_factorization_lt_pred_of_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_base_factorization_lt_pred_of_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore {p q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hdiv : q ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) : (factorialBlockBase p).factorization q < q - 1
declarations.docstring: Prime-support specialization of the exact excess-exponent ceiling.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_prime_mul_pred_gt_pred_of_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_prime_mul_pred_gt_pred_of_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore {p q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hdiv : q ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) : p - 1 < q * (q - 1)
declarations.docstring: Every prime surviving predecessor-factorial normalization lies above the sharp factorial-channel square-root threshold. If `q * (q - 1) ≤ p - 1`, then `q^(q-1)` already divides `(p - 1)!`, contradicting the exact local valuation ceiling.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_prime_sq_gt_pred_of_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_prime_sq_gt_pred_of_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore {p q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hdiv : q ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) : p - 1 < q ^ 2
declarations.docstring: Coarser square form of the sharp normalized-collision cutoff.

declarations.name: factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_coprime_factorial_of_mul_pred_le
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_coprime_factorial_of_mul_pred_le {p k : ℕ} (hcut : k * (k - 1) ≤ p - 1) : Nat.Coprime (factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p) k.factorial
declarations.docstring: The normalized collision core has no prime support in any complete factorial channel lying below the sharp cutoff.

declarations.name: factorialBlockBase_mul_normalizedCollisionCore
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockBase_mul_normalizedCollisionCore {p : ℕ} : factorialBlockBase p * factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p = factorialBlockCollisionCore p
declarations.docstring: The predecessor-factorial base is a literal factor of the collision core, so the normalized core reconstructs it without truncation.

declarations.name: factorialBlockBase_mul_upperDescFactorial
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockBase_mul_upperDescFactorial {p : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) : factorialBlockBase p * factorialBlockUpperDescFactorial p = (2 * p - 1).factorial
declarations.docstring: Exact factorial cancellation across the prime block.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_factorCollisionCap_of_normalizedCollisionCap
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_factorCollisionCap_of_normalizedCollisionCap {p a b : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) (hcap : factorialBlockBudget p * factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p * max a b < 2 * p ^ 2 * factorialBlockUpperDescFactorial p) : factorialBlockBudget p * factorialBlockCollisionCore p * max a b < factorialBlockScale p
declarations.docstring: Base cancellation for arbitrary selected factors of the private modulus. The deleted factors need not be complete owner quotients.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_collisionCap_of_normalizedCollisionCap
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_collisionCap_of_normalizedCollisionCap {p i j : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) (hcap : factorialBlockBudget p * factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p * max (factorialBlockPrivateQuotient p i) (factorialBlockPrivateQuotient p j) < 2 * p ^ 2 * factorialBlockUpperDescFactorial p) : factorialBlockBudget p * factorialBlockCollisionCore p * max (factorialBlockPrivateQuotient p i)

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePower_dvd_collisionCore_iff_two_hits
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_primePower_dvd_collisionCore_iff_two_hits {p n q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hpn : p ≤ n) (hqden : q ∣ factorialGapDenominator n) : q ^ e ∣ factorialBlockCollisionCore p ↔ ∃ i ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, ∃ j ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, i ≠ j ∧ q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator i ∧ q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator j

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePower_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore_iff_of_upper_hit

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePower_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore_iff_one_lt_hitCount

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePower_not_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore_of_hitCount_le_one

This aggregates prime-power incidence bounds into the precise local collision load used by the scale split.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePower_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore_iff_one_lt_hitCount_of_not_dvd_base

declarations.name: factorialBlock_normalizedCollisionCore_factorization_lt_of_not_dvd_base_of_hitCount_le_one

declarations.name: factorialBlock_primePower_dvd_normalizedCollisionCore_iff_one_lt_hitCount_of_endpoint_lt_base

Consequently a positive `q^e`-layer survives in the normalized collision core exactly when that layer hits two displayed factorial gaps. This applies to every endpoint prime in the collision core, without a chosen upper-half hit.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_normalizedCollisionCore_factorization_lt_of_endpoint_lt_base_of_hitCount_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_normalizedCollisionCore_factorization_lt_of_endpoint_lt_base_of_hitCount_le_one {p q e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 0 < e) (hendpoint : 2 * p - 1 < q) (hcount : ((factorialBlockIndices p).filter fun i => q ^ e ∣ factorialGapDenominator i).card ≤ 1) : (factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p).factorization q < e
declarations.docstring: Endpoint-prime valuation cutoff with no preselected upper-half hit. Any at-most-one incidence estimate for `q^e` on the full block forces the complete normalized `q`-valuation below `e`.

declarations.name: factorialBlock_normalizedCollisionCore_factorization_le_one_of_endpoint_lt_base_of_primeSqHitCount_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlock_normalizedCollisionCore_factorization_le_one_of_endpoint_lt_base_of_primeSqHitCount_le_one {p q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hendpoint : 2 * p - 1 < q) (hcount : ((factorialBlockIndices p).filter fun i => q ^ 2 ∣ factorialGapDenominator i).card ≤ 1) : (factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p).factorization q ≤ 1
declarations.docstring: Prime-square specialization of the endpoint incidence cutoff. Thus the endpoint-prime part of the normalized collision core is squarefree as soon as every `q^2` layer has at most one factorial-gap hit.

declarations.name: factorialBlockPrime_dvd_privateQuotient_of_unique_upper_prime
declarations.signature: theorem factorialBlockPrime_dvd_privateQuotient_of_unique_upper_prime {p n q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hpn : p ≤ n) (hqden : q ∣ factorialGapDenominator n) (hunique : ∀ m ∈ factorialBlockIndices p, m ≠ n → ¬q ∣ factorialGapDenominator m) : q ∣ privateQuotient (factorialBlockBase p) (factorialBlockIndices p) factorialGapDenominator n

declarations.name: factorialBlockPrivateModulus_one_lt_of_unique_upper_prime

declarations.name: factorialBlockPrivateOwnerTerm_mod_pos_of_unique_upper_prime

declarations.name: factorialBlock_tail_le_baseNumerator_of_endpointGap_pos
