declarations.name: tendsto_log_factorialGap_div_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_log_factorialGap_div_two_pow : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log ((n.factorial : ℝ) - 1) / (2 : ℝ) ^ n) atTop (𝓝 0)
declarations.docstring: The logarithm of a factorial-gap denominator is negligible at dyadic scale; the elementary bound `log(n! - 1) ≤ n²` suffices.

declarations.name: tendsto_factorialGap_rpow_one_div_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_factorialGap_rpow_one_div_two_pow : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((n.factorial : ℝ) - 1) ^ (1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ n)) atTop (𝓝 1)
declarations.docstring: Factorial-gap denominators fail the doubly exponential root-growth hypothesis: their `2^n`-th roots converge to one.

declarations.name: factorial_pow_dvd_factorial_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_pow_dvd_factorial_of_dvd {d m : ℕ} (hd : d ∣ m) : d.factorial ^ (m / d) ∣ m.factorial
declarations.docstring: Every summand in the factorial-divisor coefficient is integral.

declarations.name: factorialCoeff
declarations.docstring: Divisor-regrouped coefficient in the factorial expansion of Erdős #68.

declarations.name: factorialCoeff_summand_mul
declarations.signature: theorem factorialCoeff_summand_mul {d m : ℕ} (hd : d ∈ m.divisors.filter (fun d => 2 ≤ d)) : d.factorial ^ (m / d) * (m.factorial / (d.factorial ^ (m / d))) = m.factorial
declarations.docstring: Every selected quotient in `factorialCoeff` cancels exactly.

declarations.name: primeDilationResidue
declarations.docstring: The residue target at prime dilation `k * p`.

declarations.name: WindowHit
declarations.signature: def WindowHit (F U : ℚ) (p : ℕ) (a : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: A rational interval of length `U` meets one prescribed residue class modulo `p`. This is the exact finite predicate consumed by the #68 reduction.

declarations.name: windowHit_of_integral_carry
declarations.signature: theorem windowHit_of_integral_carry {F U : ℚ} {p : ℕ} {a z : ℤ} (hmod : Int.ModEq p z a) (hlower : F < z) (hupper : (z : ℚ) ≤ F + U) : WindowHit F U p a
declarations.docstring: An integral carry with the required congruence and real enclosure supplies the corresponding prime-window hit.

declarations.name: no_integral_carry_of_windowMiss
declarations.signature: theorem no_integral_carry_of_windowMiss {F U : ℚ} {p : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hmiss : ¬ WindowHit F U p a) : ¬ ∃ z : ℤ, Int.ModEq p z a ∧ F < z ∧ (z : ℚ) ≤ F + U
declarations.docstring: A single missed window excludes every integral carry satisfying both its residue law and its exact enclosure.

declarations.name: integer_unique_in_short_window
declarations.signature: theorem integer_unique_in_short_window {F U : ℚ} (hU : U < 1) {z w : ℤ} (hzLower : F < z) (hzUpper : (z : ℚ) ≤ F + U) (hwLower : F < w) (hwUpper : (w : ℚ) ≤ F + U) : z = w
declarations.docstring: If the interval radius is less than one, it contains at most one integer.

declarations.name: factorial_pow_floor_dvd_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_pow_floor_dvd_factorial (i d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) : d.factorial ^ (i / d) ∣ i.factorial
declarations.docstring: The floor-factorial channel denominator divides the ambient factorial.

declarations.name: channelWeight
declarations.docstring: Integral weight of index `i` in the divisor channel `d`.

declarations.name: channelWeight_mul_denominator
declarations.signature: theorem channelWeight_mul_denominator (i d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) : d.factorial ^ (i / d) * channelWeight i d = i.factorial
declarations.docstring: The floor-channel denominator cancels exactly.

declarations.name: channelNumerator
declarations.signature: def channelNumerator (lam : ℕ →₀ ℤ) (d : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Finite-support integer numerator in channel `d`.

declarations.name: factorialMoment
declarations.docstring: The factorial moment of a finite-support coefficient vector.

declarations.name: channelEvent
declarations.docstring: Sparse recurrence event between consecutive channel columns.

declarations.name: channelEvent_eq_zero_of_not_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem channelEvent_eq_zero_of_not_dvd {d n : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hnd : ¬ d ∣ n) : channelEvent d n = 0
declarations.docstring: Away from a divisor event, consecutive channel columns obey the exact factorial recurrence.

declarations.name: lambda34
declarations.docstring: The coefficient vector supported on indices `3,4` with coefficients `2,-1`.

declarations.name: lambda34_channel_ge_five
declarations.signature: theorem lambda34_channel_ge_five (d : ℕ) (hd : 5 ≤ d) : channelNumerator lambda34 d = -12

declarations.name: lambda34ResidualOfTail
declarations.docstring: The exact finite residual after isolating the infinite factorial tail.

declarations.name: lambda34_residual_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem lambda34_residual_bounds (theta : ℚ) (hlower : 1 / 119 < theta) (hupper : theta < 1 / 50) : (-93 / 575 : ℚ) < lambda34ResidualOfTail theta ∧ lambda34ResidualOfTail theta < (-309 / 13685 : ℚ) ∧ -1 < lambda34ResidualOfTail theta ∧ lambda34ResidualOfTail theta < 0
declarations.docstring: The stated elementary factorial-tail enclosure gives a strict nonzero subunit residual for the `(3,4)` certificate.

declarations.name: strictSuccessor
declarations.docstring: The least integer strictly greater than a rational number. Unlike the ordinary ceiling, this advances by one even at an integral input.

declarations.name: strictSuccessor_sub_int
declarations.signature: theorem strictSuccessor_sub_int (x : ℚ) (z : ℤ) : strictSuccessor (x - z) = strictSuccessor x - z
declarations.docstring: Integer translation does not change the fractional geometry of the strict-successor construction. This is the exact cancellation that removes the divisor-factorial prefix from the prime-block packets.

declarations.name: canonicalFactorialDigit
declarations.docstring: Canonical factorial digit at radix step `n + 1`, using the terminating floor convention.

declarations.name: factorial_scaled_rational_eq_intCast
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_scaled_rational_eq_intCast (a : ℤ) {q n : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (hqn : q ≤ n) : ((n.factorial : ℚ) * ((a : ℚ) / (q : ℚ))) = (((n.factorial / q : ℕ) : ℤ) * a : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Once an explicit rational denominator divides `n!`, the scaled rational is literally an integer.

declarations.name: canonicalFactorialDigit_eq_zero_of_rational
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalFactorialDigit_eq_zero_of_rational (a : ℤ) {q n : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) (hqn : q ≤ n) : canonicalFactorialDigit ((a : ℚ) / (q : ℚ)) n = 0
declarations.docstring: Every rational number has eventually zero canonical factorial digits. The explicit threshold is its displayed denominator.

declarations.name: prime_pow_dvd_factorial_dilation
declarations.signature: theorem prime_pow_dvd_factorial_dilation {p k : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : p ^ k ∣ (k * p).factorial
declarations.docstring: A prime contributes at least `k` copies to `(k p)!`. This is the exact valuation input behind the fixed-dilation prime-power criterion.

declarations.name: prime_pow_dvd_factorial_dilation_div
declarations.signature: theorem prime_pow_dvd_factorial_dilation_div {p k q : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hqfac : q ∣ (k * p).factorial) (hpq : ¬p ∣ q) : p ^ k ∣ (k * p).factorial / q
declarations.docstring: If a denominator is coprime to `p`, clearing it from `(k p)!` preserves all `k` forced copies of `p`.

declarations.name: prime_pow_dvd_cleared_rational_numerator
declarations.signature: theorem prime_pow_dvd_cleared_rational_numerator {p k q a : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hqfac : q ∣ (k * p).factorial) (hpq : ¬p ∣ q) : p ^ k ∣ ((k * p).factorial / q) * a
declarations.docstring: Multiplying by a numerator preserves the fixed-dilation prime power.

declarations.name: strictFacTop
declarations.signature: noncomputable def strictFacTop (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Strict successor of the factorially scaled prefix.

declarations.name: strictFacTopRat
declarations.docstring: Computable rational form of `strictFacTop`, used for exact finite certificates while retaining the real-valued statement needed for the series.

declarations.name: strictFacTop_ratCast
declarations.signature: theorem strictFacTop_ratCast (x : ℚ) (n : ℕ) : strictFacTop (x : ℝ) n = strictFacTopRat x n
declarations.docstring: The rational and real strict-successor implementations agree exactly.

declarations.name: strictFacTop_div_factorial_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem strictFacTop_div_factorial_bounds (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : x < (strictFacTop x n : ℝ) / (n.factorial : ℝ) ∧ (strictFacTop x n : ℝ) / (n.factorial : ℝ) ≤ x + 1 / (n.factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: After normalization by `n!`, the strict successor lies in the one-factorial-cell interval immediately above its input.

declarations.name: rationalGridPoint_le_iff_crosses
declarations.signature: theorem rationalGridPoint_le_iff_crosses {q : ℕ} {S H r u : ℚ} {k : ℤ} (hq : 0 < q) (hH : (q : ℚ) * H = (k : ℚ) + r) (htail : (q : ℚ) * (S - H) = u) : ((k + 1 : ℤ) : ℚ) / q ≤ S ↔ 1 ≤ r + u
declarations.docstring: Algebraic form of the grid crossing. If `q*S` is obtained from `q*H = k+r` by adding the scaled tail `u`, then the next `q⁻¹` grid point lies below `S` exactly when the fractional pieces cross one.

declarations.name: factorialGrid_plateau
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGrid_plateau {n : ℕ} {H G S : ℝ} {z : ℤ} (hHG : H < G) (hGS : G ≤ S) (htail : (n.factorial : ℝ) * (S - H) < 1) (hgrid : (n.factorial : ℝ) * G = (z : ℝ)) : strictFacTop H n = z ∧ facFloor S n = z
declarations.docstring: A factorial grid point between a prefix value `H` and a target `S` forces both the strict successor of `n!H` and the canonical floor of `n!S` to equal the same grid integer, provided the remaining factorial tail is strictly shorter than one grid unit.

declarations.name: prime_pow_dvd_strictFacTop_of_rational_target
declarations.signature: theorem prime_pow_dvd_strictFacTop_of_rational_target {p k q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : 0 < q) (hqn : q ≤ k * p) (hpq : ¬p ∣ q) {H : ℝ} (hH : H < (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) (htail : (((k * p).factorial : ℝ) * ((a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ) - H)) < 1) : (p : ℤ) ^ k ∣ strictFacTop H (k * p)
declarations.docstring: If a rational target with denominator `q` lies above a prefix by less than one factorial grid unit, then at every dilated prime index `k p` whose factorial clears `q`, the strict factorial successor is divisible by `p^k`. Thus a rational value of the series imposes a prime-power divisibility condition on the strict factorial successor.

declarations.name: canonicalDigit_eq_zero_of_plateau
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalDigit_eq_zero_of_plateau {x : ℝ} {m : ℕ} {z zPrev : ℤ} (hfloor : facFloor x m = z) (hfloorPrev : facFloor x (m - 1) = zPrev) (hscale : z = (m : ℤ) * zPrev) : canonicalDigit x m = 0
declarations.docstring: Consecutive plateau floors whose grid integers scale by the next radix force the corresponding canonical factorial digit to vanish.

declarations.name: firstExit_carry_rigid
declarations.signature: theorem firstExit_carry_rigid {δ : ℝ} {b : ℤ} (hδ0 : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ2 : δ < 2) (hb : b = -⌊δ⌋) : b = 0 ∨ b = -1
declarations.docstring: If the first-exit offset lies in `[0,2)`, the strict-successor carry `-floor δ` is rigidly either zero or minus one.

declarations.name: one_div_sub_one_geometric_split
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_sub_one_geometric_split {x : ℚ} (hx0 : x ≠ 0) (hx1 : x ≠ 1) (K : ℕ) : 1 / (x - 1) = (∑ j ∈ Finset.range K, 1 / x ^ (j + 1)) + 1 / (x ^ K * (x - 1))
declarations.docstring: Finite geometric peeling of a factorial-gap denominator. The first `K` terms are pure powers of `x`; all non-factorial denominator content is confined to the final residual.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefix
declarations.docstring: The exact rational prefix of the Erdős #68 series through index `n`.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefix_cast
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefix_cast (n : ℕ) : ((factorialGapPrefix n : ℚ) : ℝ) = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 n, (1 : ℝ) / ((((k.factorial : ℤ) - 1 : ℤ) : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: Casting the exact rational prefix to the reals gives the finite real prefix used in the analytic tail decomposition.

declarations.name: prime_pow_dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_of_series_eq_rat
declarations.signature: theorem prime_pow_dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_of_series_eq_rat {p k q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : 0 < q) (hqn : q ≤ k * p) (hpq : ¬p ∣ q) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : (p : ℤ) ^ k ∣ strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix (k * p) : ℚ) : ℝ) (k * p)
declarations.docstring: A rational value for the Erdős #68 series forces the expected `p^k` divisibility of the actual prefix strict successor at every factorial index `k p` clearing the denominator and coprime to it.

declarations.name: strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_eq_cleared_rational_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_eq_cleared_rational_of_dvd {n q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : 0 < q) (hqfac : q ∣ n.factorial) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix n : ℚ) : ℝ) n = (((n.factorial / q : ℕ) : ℤ) * a : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Once `n!` clears a displayed rational denominator, the strict successor of the Erdős #68 prefix is exactly the corresponding cleared rational grid integer. The hypothesis is divisibility `q ∣ n!`, not the cruder size bound `q ≤ n`. Only the divisibility is used, and it is strictly weaker: every `q ≤ n` divides `n!`, and some larger denominators do too (for example `12 ∣ 4!`).

declarations.name: strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_eq_cleared_rational
declarations.signature: theorem strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_eq_cleared_rational {n q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : 0 < q) (hqn : q ≤ n) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix n : ℚ) : ℝ) n = (((n.factorial / q : ℕ) : ℤ) * a : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: Size-bound corollary of the divisibility form, kept so the existing consumers are unchanged.

declarations.name: rational_denominator_ge_of_prime_miss
declarations.signature: theorem rational_denominator_ge_of_prime_miss {p q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hp : p.Prime) (hq : 0 < q) (hmiss : ¬(p : ℤ) ∣ strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix p : ℚ) : ℝ) p) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : p ≤ q
declarations.docstring: One exact missed prime already gives a quantitative obstruction: the denominator of any displayed rational value of the Erdős #68 series must be at least that prime.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_prime_power_misses
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_prime_power_misses {k : ℕ} (hmiss : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ B < p ∧ ¬(p : ℤ) ^ k ∣ strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix (k * p) : ℚ) : ℝ) (k * p)) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Any cofinal family of fixed-exponent prime-power misses for the actual prefix strict successors proves the irrationality of the Erdős #68 series.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefix_eq_prev_add
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefix_eq_prev_add {τ : ℕ} (hτ : 2 ≤ τ) : factorialGapPrefix τ = factorialGapPrefix (τ - 1) + 1 / ((τ.factorial : ℚ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: Adding the endpoint `τ` to the actual factorial-gap prefix contributes exactly `1 / (τ! - 1)`.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGap
declarations.docstring: Distance from the strict factorial successor of the preceding actual prefix to that scaled prefix. Unlike an ordinary fractional-part complement, this takes the value one when the scaled prefix is integral.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry
declarations.docstring: The exact rounding carry in the strict-successor recurrence for the Erdős #68 prefixes.

declarations.name: strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_step
declarations.signature: theorem strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_step {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix m : ℚ) : ℝ) m = (m : ℤ) * strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix (m - 1) : ℚ) : ℝ) (m - 1) + 1 - factorialGapStepCarry m
declarations.docstring: The strict factorial successors of consecutive prefixes satisfy an exact radix recurrence with `factorialGapStepCarry` as rounding digit.

declarations.name: strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_div_factorial_step
declarations.signature: theorem strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_div_factorial_step {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : (strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix m : ℚ) : ℝ) m : ℝ) / (m.factorial : ℝ) = (strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix (m - 1) : ℚ) : ℝ) (m - 1) : ℝ) / ((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) + ((1 - factorialGapStepCarry m : ℤ) : ℝ) / (m.factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Dividing the strict-successor recurrence by `m!` turns its carry defect into one ordinary factorial-series coefficient.

declarations.name: strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_carry_expansion
declarations.signature: theorem strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_carry_expansion (M : ℕ) (hM : 2 ≤ M) : (strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix M : ℚ) : ℝ) M : ℝ) / (M.factorial : ℝ) = (strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix 2 : ℚ) : ℝ) 2 : ℝ) / ((2 : ℕ).factorial : ℝ) + ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 3 M, ((1 - factorialGapStepCarry m : ℤ) : ℝ) / (m.factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Exact finite factorial-series expansion of the normalized strict successor. The coefficient at index `m` is `1 - factorialGapStepCarry m`; thus an eventual unit-carry tail is exactly an eventual zero-coefficient tail in this representation.

declarations.name: tendsto_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_div_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_div_factorial : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix n : ℚ) : ℝ) n : ℝ) / (n.factorial : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries)
declarations.docstring: The normalized strict successor of the prefix converges to the Erdős #68 series. Hence an eventually stationary normalized carry recurrence has the series itself as its rational stationary value.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_of_dvd_pred_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_of_dvd_pred_factorial {m q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hq : 0 < q) (hqfac : q ∣ (m - 1).factorial) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : factorialGapStepCarry m = 1
declarations.docstring: If the Erdős #68 series has a displayed rational value `a / q`, then every carry after the denominator threshold is exactly one.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_of_series_eq_rat
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_of_series_eq_rat {m q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hq : 0 < q) (hqm : q ≤ m - 1) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : factorialGapStepCarry m = 1
declarations.docstring: Size-bound corollary of the divisibility form, kept so the existing consumers are unchanged.

declarations.name: not_irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventually_unit_carries
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventually_unit_carries (hunit : ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, M ≤ m → factorialGapStepCarry m = 1) : ¬Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: If the carry sequence is eventually one, then the normalized strict-successor recurrence is eventually constant. Its independently proved limit is the original series, so the series is rational.

declarations.name: not_irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_eventually_unit_carries
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_eventually_unit_carries : ¬Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries ↔ ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, M ≤ m → factorialGapStepCarry m = 1
declarations.docstring: Exact carry characterization of rationality: the series is non-irrational exactly when its carry sequence is eventually one.

declarations.name: rational_denominator_ge_of_nonunit_carry
declarations.signature: theorem rational_denominator_ge_of_nonunit_carry {m q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hmiss : factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1) (hq : 0 < q) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : m ≤ q
declarations.docstring: A single exact non-unit carry at index `m` forces every displayed rational denominator of the series to be at least `m`.

declarations.name: rational_denominator_not_dvd_pred_factorial_of_nonunit_carry
declarations.signature: theorem rational_denominator_not_dvd_pred_factorial_of_nonunit_carry {m q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hmiss : factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1) (hq : 0 < q) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) : ¬ (q ∣ (m - 1).factorial)
declarations.docstring: A single exact non-unit carry at index `m` excludes every displayed rational denominator dividing `(m-1)!`. This is strictly stronger than `rational_denominator_ge_of_nonunit_carry`, which only excludes `q ≤ m - 1`. The size bound leaves every `q > m - 1` open, including the `(m-1)`-smooth ones such as `(m-1)!` itself and the primorial below `m`; the divisibility form excludes all of them at once. Equivalently, the Smarandache function (also called the Kempner function) `min {k : q ∣ k!}` of any displayed denominator is at least `m`, so `q` carries a prime power `p ^ e` with `e` exceeding the multiplicity of `p` in `(m-1)!`.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGap_pos_le_one
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGap_pos_le_one (m : ℕ) : 0 < factorialGapPredecessorGap m ∧ factorialGapPredecessorGap m ≤ 1

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_bounds {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : (-1 : ℤ) ≤ factorialGapStepCarry m ∧ factorialGapStepCarry m ≤ (m : ℤ) - 1
declarations.docstring: The actual rounding carry lies in the sharp range required by the strict-successor divisibility criterion.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_iff_dvd_strictFacTopRat
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_iff_dvd_strictFacTopRat {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 ↔ (m : ℤ) ∣ strictFacTopRat (factorialGapPrefix m) m
declarations.docstring: The unit-carry condition is exactly divisibility of the computable rational strict successor by its index. This eliminates the real predecessor gap and its floor: at every `m ≥ 3`, a unit carry occurs precisely when the exact integer `strictFacTopRat (factorialGapPrefix m) m` is a multiple of `m`.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_nonunit_carries
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_nonunit_carries (hmiss : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, B < m ∧ factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Arbitrarily late failures of the unit-carry condition prove the irrationality of the Erdős #68 series.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_nonunit_carries
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_nonunit_carries : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries ↔ ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, B < m ∧ factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1
declarations.docstring: The original irrationality problem is exactly the assertion that non-unit carries occur cofinally. No implication is lost in passing from the series to this integer recurrence.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_strictFacTopRat_misses
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_strictFacTopRat_misses : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries ↔ ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, B < m ∧ ¬(m : ℤ) ∣ strictFacTopRat (factorialGapPrefix m) m
declarations.docstring: The original irrationality problem is equivalently a cofinal failure of one purely integral divisibility test on the exact rational prefixes. No prime restriction, real approximation, or rounding-carry hypothesis remains in this formulation.

declarations.name: shiftGapTerm
declarations.signature: noncomputable def shiftGapTerm (t : ℤ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The shifted factorial-gap term `1/(n!+t)`, anchored at `n ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: shiftCompanionTerm
declarations.signature: noncomputable def shiftCompanionTerm (t : ℤ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The shifted companion term `1/(n!(n!+t))`, anchored at `n ≥ 2`.

declarations.name: shiftGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Erdős's shifted series `S_t = ∑_{n≥2} 1/(n!+t)`.

declarations.name: shiftCompanionConstant
declarations.docstring: The shifted companion constant `C_t = ∑_{n≥2} 1/(n!(n!+t))`.

declarations.name: factorial_sub_one_le_add_shift
declarations.signature: private theorem factorial_sub_one_le_add_shift {t : ℤ} (ht : -1 ≤ t) {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (n.factorial : ℝ) - 1 ∧ (n.factorial : ℝ) - 1 ≤ (n.factorial : ℝ) + (t : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: For `t ≥ −1` and `n ≥ 2` the shifted denominator dominates `n! − 1 ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: shiftGapTerm_eq_unitFact_sub_mul
declarations.signature: theorem shiftGapTerm_eq_unitFact_sub_mul {t : ℤ} (ht : -1 ≤ t) (n : ℕ) : shiftGapTerm t n = unitFactTerm n - (t : ℝ) * shiftCompanionTerm t n
declarations.docstring: Termwise decomposition `1/(n!+t) = 1/n! − t/(n!(n!+t))`.

declarations.name: summable_shiftGapTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_shiftGapTerm {t : ℤ} (ht : -1 ≤ t) : Summable (shiftGapTerm t)

declarations.name: summable_shiftCompanionTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_shiftCompanionTerm {t : ℤ} (ht : -1 ≤ t) : Summable (shiftCompanionTerm t)

declarations.name: shiftGapSeries_eq_neg_mul_companion_add_unitFact
declarations.signature: theorem shiftGapSeries_eq_neg_mul_companion_add_unitFact {t : ℤ} (ht : -1 ≤ t) : shiftGapSeries t = (-(t : ℝ) * shiftCompanionConstant t) + ∑' n : ℕ, unitFactTerm n
declarations.docstring: **Family decomposition.** `S_t = (−t·C_t) + (e − 2)` in the anchored form used by the generic companion-orbit boundary.

declarations.name: facFloor_neg_mul_add_two_emod_eq_zero_iff
declarations.signature: theorem facFloor_neg_mul_add_two_emod_eq_zero_iff (t : ℤ) (K : ℝ) (m : ℕ) : ((facFloor (-(t : ℝ) * K) m + 2 : ℤ) % (m : ℤ)) = 0 ↔ (m : ℤ) ∣ ⌈(t : ℝ) * (m.factorial : ℝ) * K⌉ - 2
declarations.docstring: Pointwise translation between the floor residue of the generic boundary and the ceiling residue of the shifted orbit.

declarations.name: not_irrational_shiftGapSeries_iff_eventually_ceil_residue_two
declarations.signature: theorem not_irrational_shiftGapSeries_iff_eventually_ceil_residue_two {t : ℤ} (ht : -1 ≤ t) : ¬ Irrational (shiftGapSeries t) ↔ ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, M ≤ m → (m : ℤ) ∣ ⌈(t : ℝ) * (m.factorial : ℝ) * shiftCompanionConstant t⌉ - 2
declarations.docstring: **Uniform family boundary.** For every integer `t ≥ −1`, the shifted series `S_t` is rational exactly when `⌈t·m!·C_t⌉ ≡ 2 (mod m)` for all sufficiently large `m`.

declarations.name: irrational_shiftGapSeries_iff_cofinal_ceil_residue_misses
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_shiftGapSeries_iff_cofinal_ceil_residue_misses {t : ℤ} (ht : -1 ≤ t) : Irrational (shiftGapSeries t) ↔ ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, B < m ∧ ¬ (m : ℤ) ∣ ⌈(t : ℝ) * (m.factorial : ℝ) * shiftCompanionConstant t⌉ - 2
declarations.docstring: **Uniform family boundary, escape form.** `S_t` is irrational exactly when the shifted ceiling orbit escapes the residue `2` cofinally.

declarations.name: shiftGapSeries_neg_one_eq_factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: The member `t = −1` is the Erdős #68 series.

declarations.name: shiftGapSeries_zero_eq_exp_one_sub_two
declarations.docstring: The member `t = 0` is `e − 2`.

declarations.name: irrational_shiftGapSeries_zero
declarations.docstring: The family boundary decides the member `t = 0`: the orbit `⌈0⌉ = 0` never lies in the residue class `2` once `m ≥ 3`, so `e − 2`, hence `e`, is irrational.

declarations.name: five_not_dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix

declarations.name: eleven_not_dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix

declarations.name: fifty_one_not_dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix
declarations.docstring: An exact composite-index certificate immediately before the first observed unit carry.

declarations.name: sixty_not_dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix
declarations.docstring: A larger exact composite-index certificate; the corresponding carry at index `60` is zero rather than one.

declarations.name: sixty_four_not_dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix
declarations.docstring: A larger direct certificate at index `64`; the exact carry there is `51`, again excluding the unit-carry pattern forced by rationality.

declarations.name: sixty_seven_not_dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix
declarations.docstring: Direct exact computation at the prime index `67` excludes the excluding the prime-divisibility pattern forced by rationality there.

declarations.name: eleven_le_rational_denominator

That leaves `59!` itself, and every other `59`-smooth denominator, unexcluded; this statement removes all of them.

declarations.name: abs_one_sub_factorialGapStepCarry_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_one_sub_factorialGapStepCarry_le {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : |(1 : ℤ) - factorialGapStepCarry m| ≤ (m : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The ordinary-factorial-series coefficient `1 - factorialGapStepCarry m` has at most linear growth. This is the pointwise estimate needed for the small-numerator hypothesis in the Erdős--Straus cumulative-product rationality criterion.

declarations.name: tendsto_abs_one_sub_factorialGapStepCarry_div
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_abs_one_sub_factorialGapStepCarry_div : Filter.Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => ((|(1 : ℤ) - factorialGapStepCarry m| : ℤ) : ℝ) / ((((m - 1) * m : ℕ) : ℝ))) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)
declarations.docstring: The carry-defect coefficients satisfy the exact asymptotic hypothesis from Erdős--Straus Theorem 2.1 after taking the cumulative radices `alpha_m = m`: `|1 - beta_m| / ((m-1)m)` tends to zero.

declarations.name: eventually_bounded_coboundary_state
declarations.signature: theorem eventually_bounded_coboundary_state {B N : ℕ} (hB : 0 < B) {d c : ℕ → ℤ} (hrec : ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m → (B : ℤ) * d m = (m : ℤ) * c m - c (m + 1)) (hcoeff : ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m → (2 : ℤ) - (m : ℤ) ≤ d m ∧ d m ≤ 2) (hhalf : ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m → 2 * |c (m + 1)| < (m : ℤ)) : ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, M ≤ m → -(B : ℤ) < c m ∧ c m ≤ 0
declarations.docstring: A state bound for the Erdős--Straus coboundary recurrence. If the coefficient lies in the factorial-gap window `2 - m ≤ d m ≤ 2` and the next state satisfies the assumed half-radix window, then every sufficiently late state lies in the canonical interval `(-B, 0]`. The lower endpoint first follows weakly from the coefficient and half-radix bounds. Equality `c m = -B` would force `c (m + 1) ≤ -2B`, contradicting that same weak bound at the next index.

declarations.name: eventually_zero_of_bounded_coboundary_core
declarations.signature: theorem eventually_zero_of_bounded_coboundary_core {B N : ℕ} (hB : 0 < B) {d c : ℕ → ℤ} (hrec : ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m → (B : ℤ) * d m = (m : ℤ) * c m - c (m + 1)) (hstate : ∀ m : ℕ, N ≤ m → -(B : ℤ) < c m ∧ c m ≤ 0) : ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, M ≤ m → d m = 0
declarations.docstring: Once an Erdős--Straus coboundary state lies in the canonical interval `(-B, 0]`, its recurrence has no nonzero infinite trajectory. At a large index divisible by `B`, the next state is a multiple of `B` in that interval and hence zero; zero then remains absorbing.

declarations.name: sq_dvd_double_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_iff
declarations.signature: theorem sq_dvd_double_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_iff {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpTwo : p ≠ 2) : (p : ℤ) ^ 2 ∣ strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix (2 * p) : ℚ) : ℝ) (2 * p) ↔ (factorialGapStepCarry (2 * p) = 1 ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix (2 * p - 1) : ℚ) : ℝ) (2 * p - 1)) ∨ (factorialGapStepCarry (2 * p) = 1 + (p : ℤ) ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ 2 * strictFacTop

This is the exact series specialization of the abstract two-stage strict-successor criterion: a proof of irrationality may now rule out either a unit carry together with a predecessor multiple, or the exceptional carry `1 + p` together with its shifted predecessor residue.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_double_prime_branch_failures
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_double_prime_branch_failures (hmiss : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ p ≠ 2 ∧ B < p ∧ ¬((factorialGapStepCarry (2 * p) = 1 ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix (2 * p - 1) : ℚ) : ℝ) (2 * p - 1)) ∨ (factorialGapStepCarry (2 * p) = 1 + (p : ℤ) ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ 2 * strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix (2 * p - 1) : ℚ) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A cofinal family of odd primes at which both doubled-index square-hit branches fail proves the original Erdős #68 series irrational. The hypothesis is stated entirely in terms of the actual carry and predecessor strict successor; no such cofinal family is constructed here.

declarations.name: dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_iff_predecessorGap_window
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_strictFacTop_factorialGapPrefix_iff_predecessorGap_window {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : (m : ℤ) ∣ strictFacTop ((factorialGapPrefix m : ℚ) : ℝ) m ↔ 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) < (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m ∧ (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m ≤ 2 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: Divisibility at an index `m` is equivalent to the predecessor gap lying in one explicit short interval. This removes the floor and carry from the single-power (`k = 1`) condition.

declarations.name: actualFirstCrossing_gap_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem actualFirstCrossing_gap_bounds {τ : ℕ} (hτ : 2 ≤ τ) {G : ℚ} (hbefore : factorialGapPrefix (τ - 1) < G) (hcross : G ≤ factorialGapPrefix τ) : 0 < G - factorialGapPrefix (τ - 1) ∧ G - factorialGapPrefix (τ - 1) ≤ 1 / ((τ.factorial : ℚ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: At any genuine first crossing of a rational grid level by the actual Erdős #68 prefixes, the exit gap is positive and at most the newly added factorial-gap term.

declarations.name: firstExitDelta
declarations.signature: noncomputable def firstExitDelta (τ : ℕ) (V : ℝ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The normalized offset at a first crossing of the factorial grid. For the actual Erdős #68 prefix this is `τ! * (H_τ - G) = 1 + 1 / (τ! - 1) - τ! * (G - H_{τ-1})`.

declarations.name: actualFirstCrossing_scaledOffset_eq
declarations.signature: theorem actualFirstCrossing_scaledOffset_eq {τ : ℕ} (hτ : 2 ≤ τ) (G : ℚ) : (τ.factorial : ℝ) * (((factorialGapPrefix τ - G : ℚ) : ℝ)) = firstExitDelta τ (((G - factorialGapPrefix (τ - 1) : ℚ) : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: The scaled distance from the crossing level to the new actual prefix is the normalized first-exit offset expressed in terms of the preceding gap.

declarations.name: actualFirstCrossing_delta_lt_two
declarations.signature: theorem actualFirstCrossing_delta_lt_two {τ : ℕ} (hτ : 2 ≤ τ) {G : ℚ} (hbefore : factorialGapPrefix (τ - 1) < G) : firstExitDelta τ (((G - factorialGapPrefix (τ - 1) : ℚ) : ℝ)) < 2

declarations.name: firstExitDelta_ge_one_iff
declarations.signature: theorem firstExitDelta_ge_one_iff {τ : ℕ} (hτ : 2 ≤ τ) (V : ℝ) : 1 ≤ firstExitDelta τ V ↔ V ≤ 1 / ((τ.factorial : ℝ) * ((τ.factorial : ℝ) - 1))
declarations.docstring: The `δ ≥ 1` exit branch is exactly the exceptionally small-gap branch. This is the algebraic threshold behind the stronger first-crossing denominator obstruction.

declarations.name: firstExit_carry_eq_neg_one_iff
declarations.signature: theorem firstExit_carry_eq_neg_one_iff {τ : ℕ} (hτ : 2 ≤ τ) {V : ℝ} {b : ℤ} (hδ2 : firstExitDelta τ V < 2) (hb : b = -⌊firstExitDelta τ V⌋) : b = -1 ↔ V ≤ 1 / ((τ.factorial : ℝ) * ((τ.factorial : ℝ) - 1))
declarations.docstring: If the normalized first-exit offset lies in `[0,2)`, then the negative unit carry occurs exactly when the exit gap is at most `1 / (τ! (τ! - 1))`.

declarations.name: positive_fraction_denominator_ge
declarations.signature: theorem positive_fraction_denominator_ge {a v N : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hv : 0 < v) (hN : 0 < N) (hbound : (a : ℚ) / (v : ℚ) ≤ 1 / (N : ℚ)) : N ≤ v
declarations.docstring: A positive rational fraction bounded above by `1 / N` must have denominator at least `N`. No coprimality hypothesis is needed, so this applies directly to any displayed first-crossing gap representation.

declarations.name: positive_real_fraction_denominator_ge
declarations.signature: theorem positive_real_fraction_denominator_ge {a v N : ℕ} (ha : 0 < a) (hv : 0 < v) (hN : 0 < N) (hbound : (a : ℝ) / (v : ℝ) ≤ 1 / (N : ℝ)) : N ≤ v
declarations.docstring: Real-cast version of the elementary positive-fraction denominator bound, convenient after applying the first-exit floor criterion.

declarations.name: actualFirstCrossing_denominator_ge
declarations.signature: theorem actualFirstCrossing_denominator_ge {τ a v : ℕ} (hτ : 2 ≤ τ) (ha : 0 < a) (hv : 0 < v) {G : ℚ} (hgap : G - factorialGapPrefix (τ - 1) = (a : ℚ) / (v : ℚ)) (hbefore : factorialGapPrefix (τ - 1) < G) (hcross : G ≤ factorialGapPrefix τ) : τ.factorial - 1 ≤ v

declarations.docstring: On the actual negative-unit exit branch, the first-crossing gap has the strong denominator lower bound `τ! (τ! - 1)`.

declarations.name: typeTwoOverlapCoefficient_lt_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem typeTwoOverlapCoefficient_lt_factorial {n : ℕ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) : 2 * n ^ 4 + 3 * n ^ 3 + 4 * n ^ 2 + 2 < n.factorial
declarations.docstring: For `n ≥ 8`, the factorial already dominates the exact polynomial coefficient that appears when one specializes the Kovač--Tao Type-2 interval overlap test to the factorial gaps `n! - 1` with width `n^2 + 1`.

declarations.name: factorialGap_typeTwo_nextInterval_overlap
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_typeTwo_nextInterval_overlap {n : ℕ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) : (((n + 1).factorial : ℤ) - ((n + 1 : ℤ) ^ 2 + 2)) * (((n + 1).factorial : ℤ) - 1) < (((n + 1 : ℤ) ^ 2 + 1)) * (((n.factorial : ℤ) - ((n : ℤ) ^ 2 + 2)) * ((n.factorial : ℤ) - ((n : ℤ) ^ 2 + 1)))
declarations.docstring: Exact next-interval overlap for the factorial-gap specialization of Kovač--Tao, Lemma 5.1. At stage `n`, take the positive-integer interval whose upper endpoint is `n! - 1` and whose width is `n^2 + 1`. For every `n ≥ 8`, the single interval at stage `n+1` already contributes more tail length than the largest reciprocal gap at stage `n`. Together with the analytic hypotheses of Kovač--Tao, Lemma 5.1, this is the elementary interval inequality used to construct a rational reciprocal series with denominators between `n! - n^2 - 2` and `n! - 1`. The theorem below is only that inequality: it proves neither the existence statement nor the rationality or irrationality of the unperturbed Erdős #68 series.

declarations.name: centreGap_factorial_recurrence

declarations.name: real_prefix_eq_prev_add

declarations.name: predGap_succ_eq
declarations.signature: theorem predGap_succ_eq (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : factorialGapPredecessorGap (m + 1) = (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m - (factorialGapStepCarry m : ℝ) - 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: Rearranged radix recurrence: consecutive predecessor gaps satisfy the exact affine recursion with the rounding carry as the subtracted digit.

declarations.name: predGap_split
declarations.signature: theorem predGap_split (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) : factorialGapPredecessorGap m = ((factorialGapStepCarry m : ℝ) + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1)) / (m : ℝ) + factorialGapPredecessorGap (m + 1) / (m : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: One unrolling step of the carry-stream expansion, in the direction used by induction: the gap at `m` splits into the current carry contribution plus the rescaled successor gap.

declarations.name: factorialReal_succ_div
declarations.signature: private theorem factorialReal_succ_div {n : ℕ} : ((n.factorial : ℝ) / ((n + 1).factorial : ℝ)) = 1 / ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Weight lemma: factorial ratio across one index.

declarations.name: mul_add_div
declarations.signature: private theorem mul_add_div (x y w z : ℝ) : x * ((y + w) / z) = x * (y / z) + x * (w / z)
declarations.docstring: Multiplicative distribution over a division: isolated so that no `Finset.sum` is ever exposed to `field_simp`.

declarations.name: mul_div_swap
declarations.signature: private theorem mul_div_swap (x y z : ℝ) : x * (y / z) = y * (x / z)

declarations.name: predGap_eq_carry_stream
declarations.signature: theorem predGap_eq_carry_stream (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (k : ℕ) : factorialGapPredecessorGap m = ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc m (m + k), (((factorialGapStepCarry j : ℝ) + 1 / ((j.factorial : ℝ) - 1)) * (((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) / (j.factorial : ℝ))) + (((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) / ((m + k).factorial : ℝ)) * factorialGapPredecessorGap (m + k + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Exact finite carry-stream expansion.** The predecessor gap at `m` equals the weighted carry stream from `m` through `m+k` plus the explicitly rescaled terminal gap at `m+k+1`.

declarations.name: carry_stream_remainder_bounds
declarations.signature: theorem carry_stream_remainder_bounds (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (k : ℕ) : (0 : ℝ) < ((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) / ((m + k).factorial : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap (m + k + 1) ∧ ((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) / ((m + k).factorial : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap (m + k + 1) ≤ ((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) / ((m + k).factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: The remainder of the finite expansion is positive and bounded by its weight, because every predecessor gap lies in `(0, 1]`.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_iff_scaled_gap
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_eq_one_iff_scaled_gap (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) : factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 ↔ 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) < (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m ∧ (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m ≤ 2 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: **Sharp three-window reading of the carry.** The unit carry occurs exactly when the scaled predecessor gap lands in `(1 + ε_m, 2 + ε_m]`.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_scaled_gap_gt
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_scaled_gap_gt (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hgt : 2 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) < (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m) : factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1
declarations.docstring: Frontier consumer: a strictly dominant scaled gap forces a non-unit carry, i.e. a strict-successor divisibility miss at index `m`.

declarations.name: factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_stream_domination
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapStepCarry_ne_one_of_stream_domination (m : ℕ) (hm : 3 ≤ m) (k : ℕ) (hdom : (2 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1)) / (m : ℝ) < ∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc m (m + k), (((factorialGapStepCarry j : ℝ) + 1 / ((j.factorial : ℝ) - 1)) * (((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) / (j.factorial : ℝ)))) : factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1
declarations.docstring: **Digit-stream certificate.** If the finite weighted carry stream from `m` through `m+k` dominates `(2 + ε_m)/m`, then index `m` is a frontier miss. All hypotheses are integer-checkable given certified digits `b_j`.

declarations.name: gapSuccessor
declarations.docstring: The exact integer strict successor of the rational prefix at index `m`.

declarations.name: gapSuccessor_def
declarations.signature: theorem gapSuccessor_def (m : ℕ) : gapSuccessor m = strictFacTopRat (factorialGapPrefix m) m

declarations.name: gapSuccessor_eq_mul_pred_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem gapSuccessor_eq_mul_pred_of_dvd {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (h : (m : ℤ) ∣ gapSuccessor m) : gapSuccessor m = (m : ℤ) * gapSuccessor (m - 1)
declarations.docstring: **Degenerate recurrence.** At an index carrying the unit rounding digit the additive term of the radix recurrence vanishes and the strict successor is exactly `m` times its predecessor.

declarations.name: gapSuccessor_dvd_of_eventually_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem gapSuccessor_dvd_of_eventually_dvd {M : ℕ} (hM : 3 ≤ M) (h : ∀ k, M ≤ k → (k : ℤ) ∣ gapSuccessor k) {j : ℕ} (hj : M ≤ j + 1) : ∀ m, j ≤ m → gapSuccessor j ∣ gapSuccessor m
declarations.docstring: **Divisibility chain.** Past the branch threshold every strict successor divides all later ones.

declarations.name: factorial_mul_gapSuccessor_eq_of_eventually_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_mul_gapSuccessor_eq_of_eventually_dvd {M : ℕ} (hM : 3 ≤ M) (h : ∀ k, M ≤ k → (k : ℤ) ∣ gapSuccessor k) {j : ℕ} (hj : M ≤ j + 1) : ∀ m, j ≤ m → (j.factorial : ℤ) * gapSuccessor m = (m.factorial : ℤ) * gapSuccessor j
declarations.docstring: **Multiplicative normal form.** Past the branch threshold `N m / m!` is constant: `j! · N m = m! · N j` for all `j ≤ m`.

declarations.name: eventually_dvd_gapSuccessor_of_not_irrational
declarations.signature: theorem eventually_dvd_gapSuccessor_of_not_irrational {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hrat : ¬ Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries) : ∃ B : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, B < m → (d : ℤ) ∣ gapSuccessor m
declarations.docstring: **Rigidity.** If the Erdős #68 series is not irrational then every fixed modulus eventually divides the strict successor. The modulus is chosen in advance and does not move with the index.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_not_dvd_gapSuccessor
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_not_dvd_gapSuccessor {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (h : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, B < m ∧ ¬ (d : ℤ) ∣ gapSuccessor m) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries

This is a sufficient condition, strictly stronger than the canonical equivalence `irrational ↔ cofinally many m with ¬ m ∣ N m`; it does not replace it.

declarations.name: not_eventually_odd_gapSuccessor_of_not_irrational

declarations.signature: theorem moving_factor_pair_criterion_literal (hcert : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m q : ℕ, 4 ≤ m ∧ B < m / 2 + 1 ∧ q.Prime ∧ q ∣ m.factorial - 1 ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k < m → Nat.Coprime q (k.factorial - 1)) ∧ factorialBlockBudget (m / 2 + 1) * factorialBlockEndpointLcm (m / 2 + 1) < factorialBlockScale (m / 2 + 1) * complementaryProjectedResidue (factorialBlockTailNumerator (m / 2 + 1)) (factorialBlockPrivateModulus (m / 2 + 1)) ∧ factorialBlockBudget (m / 2 + 1) * factorialBlockCollisionCore (m / 2 + 1) * q < factorialBlockScale (m / 2 + 1)) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Literal prime/prefix-private form of the moving-factor cofinal consumer; canonical set membership is derived, not left as a stronger extra hypothesis.

declarations.name: fixed_owner_absorption
declarations.signature: theorem fixed_owner_absorption {p n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hlt : factorialGapDenominator n < p) : factorialGapDenominator n ∣ (p - 1).factorial ∧ factorialBlockPrivateQuotient p n = 1
declarations.docstring: The statement actually located at long res:split-factor-normalized-collision is fixed-owner absorption, not a displayed arbitrary-factor theorem.

declarations.name: finite_decimal_comparison
declarations.docstring: The exact decimal comparison in the finite-evidence paragraph. The two small power certificates avoid asking norm_num to construct the whole large comparison at once. This does NOT prove that a rational denominator reaches 2^39990; that requires the missing interval/continued-fraction formalisation.

declarations.name: supported_integral_normal_form
declarations.signature: theorem supported_integral_normal_form (f : ℕ →₀ ℤ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) : ∃ k : ℤ, channelNumerator f d = factorialMoment f + ((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1) * k
declarations.docstring: Integral normal form on the literal finite coefficient support.

declarations.name: supported_quotient_band
declarations.signature: theorem supported_quotient_band (f : ℕ →₀ ℤ) (d k : ℕ) (hlo : ∀ n ∈ f.support, k * d ≤ n) (hhi : ∀ n ∈ f.support, n < (k + 1) * d) : factorialMoment f = (d.factorial : ℤ) ^ k * channelNumerator f d
declarations.docstring: The whole band identity with no restrictions on zero coefficients.

declarations.name: supported_first_band_cancellation
declarations.signature: theorem supported_first_band_cancellation (f : ℕ →₀ ℤ) (d : ℕ) (hlo : ∀ n ∈ f.support, d ≤ n) (hhi : ∀ n ∈ f.support, n < 2 * d) (hz : channelNumerator f d = 0) : factorialMoment f = 0

declarations.name: supported_breakpoint_escape
declarations.signature: theorem supported_breakpoint_escape (f : ℕ →₀ ℤ) (d : ℕ) (hlo : ∀ n ∈ f.support, d ≤ n) (hz : channelNumerator f d = 0) (hm : factorialMoment f ≠ 0) : ∃ n ∈ f.support, 2 * d ≤ n
declarations.docstring: The witness is an actually supported index, not an unused list entry.

declarations.name: factorial_mul_div_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_mul_div_of_le {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≤ j) : i.factorial * (j.factorial / i.factorial) = j.factorial

declarations.name: shifted_factorial_linear_combo
declarations.signature: private theorem shifted_factorial_linear_combo (P : ℕ → ℤ) {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≤ j) : (↑(j.factorial / i.factorial) : ℤ) * ((i.factorial : ℤ) + P i) - ((j.factorial : ℤ) + P j) = (↑(j.factorial / i.factorial) : ℤ) * P i - P j

declarations.name: int_gcd_eval_shifted_factorial_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem int_gcd_eval_shifted_factorial_dvd (P : ℕ → ℤ) {i j : ℕ} (hij : i < j) : (Int.gcd ((i.factorial : ℤ) + P i) ((j.factorial : ℤ) + P j) : ℤ) ∣ P j - (↑(j.factorial / i.factorial) : ℤ) * P i
declarations.docstring: Two shifted factorials collide only through the explicit integer `P j - (j!/i!) (P i)`.

declarations.name: int_gcd_shifted_factorial_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem int_gcd_shifted_factorial_dvd (t : ℤ) {i j : ℕ} (hij : i < j) : (Int.gcd ((i.factorial : ℤ) + t) ((j.factorial : ℤ) + t) : ℤ) ∣ t * ((↑(j.factorial / i.factorial) : ℤ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: Constant-shift specialisation: `gcd(i!+t, j!+t)` divides `t ((j!/i!) - 1)`. The factorial-gap case `t = -1` recovers a multiple of the already-checked identity `gcd(i!-1, j!-1) ∣ (j!/i!) - 1`.

declarations.name: int_gcd_unperturbed_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem int_gcd_unperturbed_factorial {i j : ℕ} (hij : i ≤ j) : Int.gcd (i.factorial : ℤ) (j.factorial : ℤ) = i.factorial
declarations.docstring: The unperturbed family makes the collision difference vanish, so the gcd identity supplies no lcm gain: `lcm_{n ≤ N} n! = N!`.

declarations.name: eval_shifted_collision_eq_zero_of_zero
declarations.signature: theorem eval_shifted_collision_eq_zero_of_zero {i j : ℕ} : (0 : ℤ) - (↑(j.factorial / i.factorial) : ℤ) * (0 : ℤ) = 0

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefixLCMNumerator
declarations.docstring: Common-denominator numerator of the factorial-gap prefix when the literal prefix LCM is used as denominator.

declarations.name: factorialGapMaxHits
declarations.signature: def factorialGapMaxHits (q M e : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.docstring: Indices at which the exact `q`-adic exponent of `n! - 1` is `e`.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrincipalResidue
declarations.signature: def factorialGapPrincipalResidue (q M e : ℕ) : ZMod q
declarations.docstring: Sum modulo `q` of the inverses of the maximal-hit cofactors.

declarations.name: factorialGap_dvd_prefixLCM
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_dvd_prefixLCM {M n : ℕ} (hn : n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M) : n.factorial - 1 ∣ factorialGapPrefixLCM M
declarations.docstring: Every displayed factorial gap divides the literal prefix LCM.

declarations.name: factorialGap_pos_of_mem_Icc
declarations.signature: private theorem factorialGap_pos_of_mem_Icc {M n : ℕ} (hn : n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M) : 0 < n.factorial - 1

declarations.name: prime_dvd_div_of_factorization_lt
declarations.signature: private theorem prime_dvd_div_of_factorization_lt {q e d L : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hdPos : 0 < d) (hLPos : 0 < L) (hdL : d ∣ L) (hqeL : q ^ e ∣ L) (hdLt : d.factorization q < e) : q ∣ L / d
declarations.docstring: If `q^e` divides a positive common multiple but a positive divisor has smaller `q`-valuation, the quotient by that divisor still contains `q`.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefixLCM_pos
declarations.docstring: The literal prefix lcm is positive, including the empty prefix.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefix_eq_lcm_ratio
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefix_eq_lcm_ratio (M : ℕ) : factorialGapPrefix M = (factorialGapPrefixLCMNumerator M : ℚ) / factorialGapPrefixLCM M
declarations.docstring: The exact rational prefix is represented by the literal lcm numerator.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefixLCM_cofactor_not_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefixLCM_cofactor_not_dvd {q M e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hmax : ∀ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M, ¬q ^ (e + 1) ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hattain : ∃ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M, q ^ e ∣ n.factorial - 1) : ¬q ∣ factorialGapPrefixLCM M / q ^ e
declarations.docstring: At the maximal displayed prime exponent, the lcm cofactor is a unit modulo the prime.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefixLCMNumerator_mod_prime
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefixLCMNumerator_mod_prime {q M e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 1 ≤ e) (hmax : ∀ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M, ¬q ^ (e + 1) ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hattain : ∃ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M, q ^ e ∣ n.factorial - 1) : (factorialGapPrefixLCMNumerator M : ZMod q) = ((factorialGapPrefixLCM M / q ^ e : ℕ) : ZMod q) * factorialGapPrincipalResidue q M e
declarations.docstring: **Prime-pole numerator formula.** If `e` is the positive maximum `q`-adic exponent among the displayed factorial gaps, the common-denominator numerator modulo `q` is the LCM cofactor times the reciprocal sum of the maximal-hit cofactors.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefix_den_full_prime_power_iff
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefix_den_full_prime_power_iff {q M e : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (he : 1 ≤ e) (hmax : ∀ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M, ¬q ^ (e + 1) ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hattain : ∃ n ∈ Finset.Icc 2 M, q ^ e ∣ n.factorial - 1) : (factorialGapPrefix M).den.factorization q = (factorialGapPrefixLCM M).factorization q ↔ factorialGapPrincipalResidue q M e ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The full prime power survives in the reduced denominator of the actual rational prefix exactly when the maximal-hit inverse sum is nonzero.

declarations.name: primePoleResidue_139_cancel
declarations.docstring: The three displayed cofactors cancel modulo 139.

declarations.name: primePoleResidue_2593_cancel
declarations.docstring: The three displayed cofactors cancel modulo 2593.

declarations.name: reducedDenominator_factorization_eq_iff
declarations.signature: theorem reducedDenominator_factorization_eq_iff {p B L : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hL : 0 < L) (hpL : p ∣ L) : (L / B.gcd L).factorization p = L.factorization p ↔ ¬p ∣ B
declarations.docstring: Reduction preserves the full exponent of a prime divisor of the common denominator precisely when the numerator is nonzero modulo that prime.

declarations.name: natRatio_den_eq
declarations.signature: theorem natRatio_den_eq (B : ℕ) {L : ℕ} (hL : 0 < L) : ((B : ℚ) / L).den = L / B.gcd L
declarations.docstring: The denominator of the actual rational quotient is the common denominator divided by the numerator's gcd with it.

declarations.name: natRatio_den_factorization_eq_iff
declarations.signature: theorem natRatio_den_factorization_eq_iff {p B L : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hL : 0 < L) (hpL : p ∣ L) : ((B : ℚ) / L).den.factorization p = L.factorization p ↔ ¬p ∣ B
declarations.docstring: Actual rational denominator form of the prime-power survival criterion.

declarations.name: predecessorGap_threshold_of_carry_ge_one_and_unit_successor_gap
declarations.signature: theorem predecessorGap_threshold_of_carry_ge_one_and_unit_successor_gap {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hcarry : (1 : ℤ) ≤ factorialGapStepCarry m) (hunit : factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 → 2 / (m : ℝ) ≤ factorialGapPredecessorGap (m + 1)) : 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) + 2 / (m : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m
declarations.docstring: A positive carry meets the tail-free threshold automatically unless it is exactly one; in that boundary case the displayed successor-gap estimate is the precise remaining input supplied by the affine gap recurrence.

declarations.name: predecessorGap_threshold_of_carry_ge_one_and_unit_next_carry_ge_three
declarations.signature: theorem predecessorGap_threshold_of_carry_ge_one_and_unit_next_carry_ge_three {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hcarry : (1 : ℤ) ≤ factorialGapStepCarry m) (hnext : factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 → (3 : ℤ) ≤ factorialGapStepCarry (m + 1)) : 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) + 2 / (m : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m
declarations.docstring: A purely discrete sufficient version of the preceding lemma. At a unit carry, a next carry of at least three forces the required successor-gap margin.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventual_odd_threshold
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventual_odd_threshold (hodd : ∀ m : ℕ, 25 ≤ m → Odd m → 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) + 2 / (m : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: The combined odd-index threshold conjecture is already a complete irrationality producer. No prime-number theorem or Euclid step is needed: odd indices themselves are cofinal.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventual_odd_carry_margin
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventual_odd_carry_margin (hcarry : ∀ m : ℕ, 25 ≤ m → Odd m → (1 : ℤ) ≤ factorialGapStepCarry m) (hunit : ∀ m : ℕ, 25 ≤ m → Odd m → factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 → 2 / (m : ℝ) ≤ factorialGapPredecessorGap (m + 1)) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Two-obligation form of the computationally suggested producer: an eventual positive carry at odd indices, plus control of every unit-carry successor gap there, proves Erdős #68.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventual_odd_two_carry_pattern
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventual_odd_two_carry_pattern (hcarry : ∀ m : ℕ, 25 ≤ m → Odd m → (1 : ℤ) ≤ factorialGapStepCarry m) (hnext : ∀ m : ℕ, 25 ≤ m → Odd m → factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 → (3 : ℤ) ≤ factorialGapStepCarry (m + 1)) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Fully integer-valued adjacent-carry producer suggested by the computation. It is stronger than necessary but removes the remaining real margin.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventual_odd_unit_carry_break
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_eventual_odd_unit_carry_break (hbreak : ∀ m : ℕ, 25 ≤ m → Odd m → factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 → factorialGapStepCarry (m + 1) ≠ 1) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: **Target-aligned adjacent-carry producer.** The positive-carry clause in the preceding threshold route is unnecessary for irrationality itself. At each sufficiently large odd index, a non-unit current carry is already a frontier miss; if the current carry is unit, it is enough that the successor carry is non-unit. Thus eventual exclusion of adjacent unit carries on odd starts directly proves Erdős #68.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_odd_unit_carry_break
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_odd_unit_carry_break : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries ↔ ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, B < m ∧ Odd m ∧ (factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1 ∨ factorialGapStepCarry (m + 1) ≠ 1)
declarations.docstring: **Exact sparse odd-pair characterization.** Uniform exclusion at every large odd start is stronger than necessary. Erdős #68 is equivalent to cofinally many odd-start pairs in which at least one of the two carries is non-unit. Thus a proof may select a sparse arithmetic subsequence of odd starts instead of controlling all odd indices.

declarations.name: consecutive_unit_carries_iff_mul_dvd_strictSuccessor
declarations.signature: theorem consecutive_unit_carries_iff_mul_dvd_strictSuccessor {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : (factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 ∧ factorialGapStepCarry (m + 1) = 1) ↔ ((m : ℤ) * (m + 1 : ℤ)) ∣ strictFacTopRat (factorialGapPrefix (m + 1)) (m + 1)
declarations.docstring: Two adjacent unit carries are a single product-divisibility event at the later strict successor. This is the arithmetic form of the no-repeat target: one must rule out divisibility by `m(m+1)`, rather than separately reason about two rounding windows.

declarations.name: consecutive_unit_carries_iff_ultra_endpoint_cylinders
declarations.signature: theorem consecutive_unit_carries_iff_ultra_endpoint_cylinders {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : (factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 ∧ factorialGapStepCarry (m + 1) = 1) ↔ ((m : ℝ) * (m + 1 : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries (m - 1) < factorialGapScaledTail (m + 1)) ∨ ((m : ℝ) * (m + 1 : ℝ) - 1 + factorialGapScaledTail (m + 1) ≤ (m : ℝ) * (m + 1 : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries (m - 1))
declarations.docstring: **Exact adjacent-unit ultra-cylinder classification.** Two consecutive unit carries force the single earlier canonical remainder into one of two endpoint cylinders of width on the order of `m⁻³`. The lower cylinder is pulled back from zero through two factorial digits, while the upper cylinder is its maximal-digit reflection.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_odd_ultra_endpoint_escape
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_odd_ultra_endpoint_escape : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries ↔ ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, B < m ∧ Odd m ∧ ¬(((m : ℝ) * (m + 1 : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries (m - 1) < factorialGapScaledTail (m + 1)) ∨ ((m : ℝ) * (m + 1 : ℝ) - 1 + factorialGapScaledTail (m + 1) ≤ (m : ℝ) * (m + 1 : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries (m - 1)))
declarations.docstring: **Exact shrinking-target characterization of Erdős #68.** Irrationality is equivalent to cofinal escape, along odd starting indices, from the two adjacent-unit ultra-cylinders. This is an exact replacement of the carry predicate by a two-sided shrinking target for one canonical remainder; it does not assert that the distinguished orbit escapes.

declarations.name: consecutive_unit_carries_iff_predecessorGap_width_one_window
declarations.signature: theorem consecutive_unit_carries_iff_predecessorGap_width_one_window {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : (factorialGapStepCarry m = 1 ∧ factorialGapStepCarry (m + 1) = 1) ↔ (m : ℝ) + 2 + (m + 1 : ℝ) / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) + 1 / (((m + 1).factorial : ℝ) - 1) < (m : ℝ) * (m + 1 : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m ∧ (m : ℝ) * (m + 1 : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m ≤ (m : ℝ) + 3 + (m + 1 : ℝ) / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) + 1 / (((m + 1).factorial : ℝ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: **Finite rational width-one criterion for an adjacent unit pair.** After the predecessor-gap recurrence is substituted, the two carry windows collapse to one interval of exact width one. Every displayed quantity is computed from the finite rational prefix through `m - 1`; the full series, canonical remainder, and infinite tail have disappeared.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_odd_mul_not_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_odd_mul_not_dvd : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries ↔ ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, B < m ∧ Odd m ∧ ¬((m : ℤ) * (m + 1 : ℤ)) ∣ strictFacTopRat (factorialGapPrefix (m + 1)) (m + 1)
declarations.docstring: **Exact sparse product-divisibility characterization.** Combining the odd-pair characterization with the adjacent-carry arithmetic packages the whole problem as cofinal failure of one explicit product divisibility along a freely chosen sparse sequence of odd indices.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_doublePrimeEndpoint_mul_not_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_doublePrimeEndpoint_mul_not_dvd (hmiss : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ B < p ∧ ¬(((2 * p - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) * ((2 * p : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∣ strictFacTopRat (factorialGapPrefix (2 * p)) (2 * p)) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Endpoint consumer aligned with the existing prime block `[p,2p]`: cofinally many product misses at the odd starts `2p-1` already prove the problem. This lets the private-prime/tailored-block machinery target only the final two carries of each selected block.

declarations.name: primeTranslatorCoeff

declarations.name: primeTranslatorIndex
declarations.docstring: Support indices `(p-1,p)` of the prime-pair translator.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_eq_factorialMoment_of_all_lt
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_eq_factorialMoment_of_all_lt {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hlt : ∀ j, index j < d) : channelNumerator coeff index d = factorialMoment coeff index

declarations.name: primeTranslator_moment_zero
declarations.signature: theorem primeTranslator_moment_zero {p : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p) : factorialMoment (primeTranslatorCoeff p) (primeTranslatorIndex p) = 0

declarations.name: primeTranslator_channel_zero_of_p_lt

declarations.name: prime_pred_div_eq
declarations.signature: theorem prime_pred_div_eq {p d : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hdp : d < p) : (p - 1) / d = p / d
declarations.docstring: A prime does not cross a `d`-quotient wall at its final predecessor when `2 ≤ d < p`.

declarations.name: channelCoefficient_prime_eq_mul_pred
declarations.signature: theorem channelCoefficient_prime_eq_mul_pred {p d : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hdp : d < p) : p.factorial / d.factorial ^ (p / d) = p * ((p - 1).factorial / d.factorial ^ ((p - 1) / d))
declarations.docstring: Below a prime, the channel coefficient at `p` is `p` times the coefficient at `p-1`.

declarations.name: primeTranslator_channel_zero_of_lt_p
declarations.signature: theorem primeTranslator_channel_zero_of_lt_p {p d : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hdp : d < p) : channelNumerator (primeTranslatorCoeff p) (primeTranslatorIndex p) d = 0
declarations.docstring: Every channel below `p` annihilates the prime translator.

declarations.name: primeTranslator_channels_zero
declarations.signature: theorem primeTranslator_channels_zero {D p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hDp : D < p) : ∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 D, channelNumerator (primeTranslatorCoeff p) (primeTranslatorIndex p) d = 0
declarations.docstring: A prime translator annihilates every requested channel below its prime.

declarations.name: primeTranslator_channel_at_prime
declarations.signature: theorem primeTranslator_channel_at_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : channelNumerator (primeTranslatorCoeff p) (primeTranslatorIndex p) p = (p.factorial : ℤ) - 1
declarations.docstring: At the prime itself, the sole surviving channel numerator is exactly its normalizing modulus `p! - 1`.

declarations.name: channelResidualTerm

declarations.docstring: The real contribution of one channel to the tail beyond `D`.

declarations.name: channelResidual
