declarations.name: summable_one_div_factorial_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem summable_one_div_factorial_sub_one : Summable (fun d : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / ((((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1 : ℤ)) : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: Reciprocal factorial gaps form a summable real series.

declarations.name: summable_channelResidualTerm
declarations.signature: theorem summable_channelResidualTerm {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) : Summable (fun d : ℕ => channelResidualTerm D coeff index d)
declarations.docstring: Every finite-support channel residual is summable. Beyond the largest support index, its numerator is the fixed factorial moment and the denominator grows factorially.

declarations.name: factorialGapTailTerm
declarations.signature: noncomputable def factorialGapTailTerm (D d : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: One summand of the universal factorial-gap tail beyond `D`.

declarations.name: factorialGapTail
declarations.docstring: The universal factorial-gap tail beyond `D`.

declarations.name: summable_factorialGapTailTerm
declarations.docstring: The factorial-gap tail is summable at every cutoff.

declarations.name: factorialGapTail_eq_shifted_tsum
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapTail_eq_shifted_tsum (D : ℕ) : factorialGapTail D = ∑' k : ℕ, (1 : ℝ) / ((((D + 1 + k).factorial : ℤ) - 1 : ℤ) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Reindex the tail by its distance beyond the cutoff.

declarations.name: hasSum_factorial_telescope
declarations.signature: theorem hasSum_factorial_telescope (D : ℕ) : HasSum (fun k : ℕ => (1 : ℝ) / ((D + k).factorial : ℝ) - 1 / ((D + k + 1).factorial : ℝ)) (1 / (D.factorial : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: The reciprocal-factorial difference beginning at `D` telescopes exactly to `1 / D!`.

declarations.name: one_div_factorial_sub_one_lt_telescope
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_factorial_sub_one_lt_telescope {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : (1 : ℝ) / (((m.factorial : ℤ) - 1 : ℤ) : ℝ) < 1 / ((m - 1).factorial : ℝ) - 1 / (m.factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Each factorial-gap reciprocal from index three onward is strictly smaller than the adjacent telescoping reciprocal-factorial difference.

declarations.name: factorialGapTail_lt_one_div_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapTail_lt_one_div_factorial {D : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D) : factorialGapTail D < (1 : ℝ) / (D.factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Beyond every cutoff `D ≥ 2`, the factorial-gap tail is strictly less than `1 / D!`.

declarations.name: factorialGapTail_pos
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapTail_pos {D : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D) : 0 < factorialGapTail D
declarations.docstring: Every actual factorial-gap tail beginning at a cutoff of at least two is strictly positive.

declarations.name: channelCorrectionQuotient
declarations.signature: noncomputable def channelCorrectionQuotient {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: Canonical integral quotient in the affine channel congruence.

declarations.name: channelCorrectionQuotient_spec
declarations.signature: theorem channelCorrectionQuotient_spec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) : channelNumerator coeff index d = factorialMoment coeff index + ((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1) * channelCorrectionQuotient coeff index d
declarations.docstring: The chosen correction quotient realizes the exact affine channel congruence.

declarations.name: finiteChannelCorrection
declarations.signature: noncomputable def finiteChannelCorrection {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: Only the channels between the cutoff and the largest support index can contribute a nonzero integral correction.

declarations.name: summable_finiteChannelCorrection
declarations.signature: theorem summable_finiteChannelCorrection {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) : Summable (finiteChannelCorrection D coeff index)
declarations.docstring: The correction series is finite.

declarations.name: channelResidualTerm_eq_moment_mul_tail_add_correction
declarations.signature: theorem channelResidualTerm_eq_moment_mul_tail_add_correction {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (hD : 1 ≤ D) (d : ℕ) : channelResidualTerm D coeff index d = (factorialMoment coeff index : ℝ) * factorialGapTailTerm D d + finiteChannelCorrection D coeff index d
declarations.docstring: Pointwise residual classification: each normalized channel is its factorial moment times the universal factorial-gap term plus a correction which is integral and supported on a finite interval.

declarations.name: exists_channelResidual_eq_moment_mul_factorialGapTail_add_int
declarations.signature: theorem exists_channelResidual_eq_moment_mul_factorialGapTail_add_int {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (hD : 1 ≤ D) : ∃ K : ℤ, channelResidual D coeff index = (factorialMoment coeff index : ℝ) * factorialGapTail D + (K : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: For a finite coefficient family, the residual differs from its factorial moment times the factorial-gap tail by an integer.

declarations.name: factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: The original Erdős #68 series, expressed through the universal factorial-gap tail beginning after `1`.

declarations.name: factorialGapSeries_eq_sum_add_tail
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapSeries_eq_sum_add_tail {D : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D) : factorialGapSeries = (∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 D, (1 : ℝ) / ((((d.factorial : ℤ) - 1 : ℤ) : ℝ))) + factorialGapTail D
declarations.docstring: Split the original series into its finite prefix through `D` and the remaining universal tail.

declarations.name: channelResidual_eq_cutoff_one_of_channels_zero
declarations.signature: theorem channelResidual_eq_cutoff_one_of_channels_zero {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (hD : 2 ≤ D) (hchannels : ∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 D, channelNumerator coeff index d = 0) : channelResidual D coeff index = channelResidual 1 coeff index
declarations.docstring: If every channel from `2` through `D` vanishes, changing the residual cutoff from `1` to `D` removes only zero summands.

declarations.name: exists_channelResidual_eq_moment_mul_factorialGapSeries_add_int
declarations.signature: theorem exists_channelResidual_eq_moment_mul_factorialGapSeries_add_int {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (hD : 2 ≤ D) (hchannels : ∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 D, channelNumerator coeff index d = 0) : ∃ K : ℤ, channelResidual D coeff index = (factorialMoment coeff index : ℝ) * factorialGapSeries + (K : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: For every finite-support channel-kernel vector, the residual modulo integers is exactly its factorial moment times the original Erdős #68 series.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_add_coeff
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_add_coeff {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (left right : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator (fun j => left j + right j) index d = channelNumerator left index d + channelNumerator right index d
declarations.docstring: Adding coefficient vectors adds every channel numerator.

declarations.name: channelResidualTerm_add_coeff
declarations.signature: theorem channelResidualTerm_add_coeff {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (left right : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : channelResidualTerm D (fun j => left j + right j) index d = channelResidualTerm D left index d + channelResidualTerm D right index d
declarations.docstring: Adding coefficient vectors adds each real residual summand.

declarations.name: channelResidual_add_coeff
declarations.signature: theorem channelResidual_add_coeff {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (D : ℕ) (left right : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) : channelResidual D (fun j => left j + right j) index = channelResidual D left index + channelResidual D right index
declarations.docstring: The full infinite residual is additive on every finite-support coefficient space.

declarations.name: primeTranslator_channelResidual_eq_one
declarations.signature: theorem primeTranslator_channelResidual_eq_one {D p : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D) (hp : p.Prime) (hDp : D < p) : channelResidual D (primeTranslatorCoeff p) (primeTranslatorIndex p) = 1
declarations.docstring: The prime-pair translator is an exact unit direction for the full infinite channel residual: every tail channel vanishes except `p`, where numerator and normalizing modulus coincide.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_mul_coeff
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_mul_coeff {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (z : ℤ) (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator (fun j => z * coeff j) index d = z * channelNumerator coeff index d
declarations.docstring: Scaling coefficients scales every channel numerator exactly.

declarations.name: factorialMoment_sum_type
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_sum_type {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (leftCoeff : ι → ℤ) (leftIndex : ι → ℕ) (rightCoeff : κ → ℤ) (rightIndex : κ → ℕ) : factorialMoment (Sum.elim leftCoeff rightCoeff) (Sum.elim leftIndex rightIndex) = factorialMoment leftCoeff leftIndex + factorialMoment rightCoeff rightIndex
declarations.docstring: Factorial moments split across a disjoint union of finite supports.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_sum_type
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_sum_type {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (leftCoeff : ι → ℤ) (leftIndex : ι → ℕ) (rightCoeff : κ → ℤ) (rightIndex : κ → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator (Sum.elim leftCoeff rightCoeff) (Sum.elim leftIndex rightIndex) d = channelNumerator leftCoeff leftIndex d + channelNumerator rightCoeff rightIndex d
declarations.docstring: Channel numerators split across a disjoint union of finite supports.

declarations.name: channelResidualTerm_sum_type
declarations.signature: theorem channelResidualTerm_sum_type {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (D : ℕ) (leftCoeff : ι → ℤ) (leftIndex : ι → ℕ) (rightCoeff : κ → ℤ) (rightIndex : κ → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : channelResidualTerm D (Sum.elim leftCoeff rightCoeff) (Sum.elim leftIndex rightIndex) d = channelResidualTerm D leftCoeff leftIndex d + channelResidualTerm D rightCoeff rightIndex d
declarations.docstring: Each residual summand splits across a disjoint union of finite supports.

declarations.name: channelResidual_sum_type
declarations.signature: theorem channelResidual_sum_type {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (D : ℕ) (leftCoeff : ι → ℤ) (leftIndex : ι → ℕ) (rightCoeff : κ → ℤ) (rightIndex : κ → ℕ) : channelResidual D (Sum.elim leftCoeff rightCoeff) (Sum.elim leftIndex rightIndex) = channelResidual D leftCoeff leftIndex + channelResidual D rightCoeff rightIndex
declarations.docstring: The full residual splits across a disjoint union of finite supports.

declarations.name: appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff
declarations.signature: def appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff {ι : Type*} (coeff : ι → ℤ) (p : ℕ) (z : ℤ) : Sum ι (Fin 2) → ℤ
declarations.docstring: Append an integer multiple of the prime translator on a disjoint support.

declarations.name: appendPrimeTranslatorIndex
declarations.signature: def appendPrimeTranslatorIndex {ι : Type*} (index : ι → ℕ) (p : ℕ) : Sum ι (Fin 2) → ℕ
declarations.docstring: Indices for a support enlarged by the prime translator.

declarations.name: factorialMoment_appendPrimeTranslator
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_appendPrimeTranslator {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {p : ℕ} (z : ℤ) (hp : 0 < p) : factorialMoment (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff coeff p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex index p) = factorialMoment coeff index
declarations.docstring: Appending a prime translator preserves the factorial moment.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_appendPrimeTranslator
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_appendPrimeTranslator {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {p d : ℕ} (z : ℤ) (hp : p.Prime) (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hdp : d < p) : channelNumerator (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff coeff p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex index p) d = channelNumerator coeff index d
declarations.docstring: Appending a prime translator does not change any requested channel below its prime.

declarations.name: primeTranslator_scaled_channelResidual_eq_int
declarations.signature: theorem primeTranslator_scaled_channelResidual_eq_int {D p : ℕ} (z : ℤ) (hD : 2 ≤ D) (hp : p.Prime) (hDp : D < p) : channelResidual D (fun j => z * primeTranslatorCoeff p j) (primeTranslatorIndex p) = (z : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Every integer multiple of the prime translator shifts the full residual by exactly that integer.

declarations.name: channelResidual_appendPrimeTranslator
declarations.signature: theorem channelResidual_appendPrimeTranslator {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {D p : ℕ} (z : ℤ) (hD : 2 ≤ D) (hp : p.Prime) (hDp : D < p) : channelResidual D (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff coeff p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex index p) = channelResidual D coeff index + (z : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Appending a scaled prime translator shifts the full residual by that integer and changes nothing else in the original support.

declarations.name: exists_primeTranslator_residual_abs_le_half
declarations.signature: theorem exists_primeTranslator_residual_abs_le_half {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {D p : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D) (hp : p.Prime) (hDp : D < p) : ∃ z : ℤ, |channelResidual D (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff coeff p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex index p)| ≤ (1 : ℝ) / 2
declarations.docstring: Nearest-integer rounding along the prime unit direction always places the residual in the closed interval of radius `1/2`.

declarations.name: exists_primeTranslator_reduced_kernel
declarations.signature: theorem exists_primeTranslator_reduced_kernel {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {D p : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D) (hp : p.Prime) (hDp : D < p) (hchannels : ∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 D, channelNumerator coeff index d = 0) (hmoment : factorialMoment coeff index ≠ 0) : ∃ z : ℤ, (∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 D, channelNumerator (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff coeff p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex index p) d = 0) ∧ factorialMoment (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff coeff p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex index p) ≠ 0 ∧ |channelResidual D (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff coeff p z)
declarations.docstring: A nonzero-moment vector in the finite channel kernel can be enlarged by a prime unit translator while preserving the requested zero channels and the nonzero moment; its residual can then be reduced to absolute value at most `1/2`.

declarations.name: exists_primeTranslator_strict_reduced_kernel
declarations.signature: theorem exists_primeTranslator_strict_reduced_kernel {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) {D p : ℕ} (hD : 2 ≤ D) (hp : p.Prime) (hDp : D < p) (hchannels : ∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 D, channelNumerator coeff index d = 0) (hmoment : factorialMoment coeff index ≠ 0) (hnonint : ∀ k : ℤ, channelResidual D coeff index ≠ (k : ℝ)) : ∃ z : ℤ, (∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 D, channelNumerator (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff coeff p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex index p) d = 0) ∧ factorialMoment (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff coeff p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex index p) ≠ 0 ∧
declarations.docstring: If the base residual is not an integer, nearest-integer translation gives a strictly nonzero residual of absolute value at most `1/2`, while preserving the finite channel kernel and factorial moment.

declarations.name: augmentedChannelMomentMatrix
declarations.signature: def augmentedChannelMomentMatrix {n : ℕ} (index : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℤ
declarations.docstring: Square augmented matrix whose first row is the factorial moment and whose remaining rows are the consecutive channels `2, ..., n + 1`.

declarations.name: cramerChannelKernelCoeff
declarations.signature: def cramerChannelKernelCoeff {n : ℕ} (index : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℤ
declarations.docstring: Cramer's-rule coefficient vector for unit factorial moment and zero consecutive channels.

declarations.name: dotProduct_cramer_single_eq_det_updateRow
declarations.signature: theorem dotProduct_cramer_single_eq_det_updateRow {n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℤ) (row : Fin (n + 1) → ℤ) : row ⬝ᵥ A.cramer (Pi.single 0 1) = (A.updateRow 0 row).det
declarations.docstring: Evaluating a Cramer vector against any row is the determinant obtained by replacing the distinguished row by that row. This converts every later tail-channel numerator into one exact determinant, rather than a signed sum of opaque Cramer coefficients.

declarations.name: channelCoefficientRow
declarations.signature: def channelCoefficientRow {ι : Type*} (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : ι → ℤ
declarations.docstring: The integral coefficient row of one channel on a fixed support.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_eq_dotProduct_channelCoefficientRow
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_eq_dotProduct_channelCoefficientRow {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (coeff : ι → ℤ) (index : ι → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator coeff index d = channelCoefficientRow index d ⬝ᵥ coeff
declarations.docstring: A channel numerator is the dot product of its coefficient row with the chosen integer coefficient vector.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_cramerChannelKernel_eq_det_updateRow
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_cramerChannelKernel_eq_det_updateRow {n : ℕ} (index : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) (d : ℕ) : channelNumerator (cramerChannelKernelCoeff index) index d = ((augmentedChannelMomentMatrix index).updateRow 0 (channelCoefficientRow index d)).det
declarations.docstring: Every channel numerator of the distinguished Cramer kernel is exactly the determinant formed by replacing the moment row with that channel row. This identity remains valid beyond the Vandermonde range, including at the floor-discontinuous tail channels where termwise sign control fails.

declarations.name: cramerChannelKernel_mulVec
declarations.signature: theorem cramerChannelKernel_mulVec {n : ℕ} (index : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) : Matrix.mulVec (augmentedChannelMomentMatrix index) (cramerChannelKernelCoeff index) = (augmentedChannelMomentMatrix index).det • (Pi.single 0 1)
declarations.docstring: Cramer's rule packages the determinant as the moment row and zero in every channel row.

declarations.name: factorialMoment_cramerChannelKernel
declarations.signature: theorem factorialMoment_cramerChannelKernel {n : ℕ} (index : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) : factorialMoment (cramerChannelKernelCoeff index) index = (augmentedChannelMomentMatrix index).det
declarations.docstring: The Cramer coefficient vector has factorial moment equal to the augmented determinant.

declarations.name: channelNumerator_cramerChannelKernel_zero
declarations.signature: theorem channelNumerator_cramerChannelKernel_zero {n : ℕ} (index : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) (d : Fin n) : channelNumerator (cramerChannelKernelCoeff index) index (d.val + 2) = 0
declarations.docstring: Every channel row of the Cramer coefficient vector vanishes.

declarations.name: exists_nonzeroMoment_channelKernel_of_augmented_det_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem exists_nonzeroMoment_channelKernel_of_augmented_det_ne_zero {n : ℕ} (index : Fin (n + 1) → ℕ) (hdet : (augmentedChannelMomentMatrix index).det ≠ 0) : ∃ coeff : Fin (n + 1) → ℤ, (∀ d : Fin n, channelNumerator coeff index (d.val + 2) = 0) ∧ factorialMoment coeff index ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: One explicit nonzero determinant produces a finite channel-kernel vector with nonzero factorial moment.

declarations.name: factorialGridScale
declarations.docstring: A square factorial scale divisible by every product of two consecutive positive integers below `D`. The square is chosen to make the exact grid arithmetic elementary.

declarations.name: factorialGridBase
declarations.docstring: Integer reciprocal of the normalized Vandermonde node associated with channel `d` at the common factorial grid scale.

declarations.name: factorial_lt_succ_pow
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_lt_succ_pow {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) : d.factorial < (d + 1) ^ d
declarations.docstring: The elementary inequality underlying strict monotonicity of factorial roots.

declarations.name: factorialGridBase_lt_succ
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGridBase_lt_succ {D d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hdD : d + 1 ≤ D) : factorialGridBase D d < factorialGridBase D (d + 1)
declarations.docstring: Consecutive factorial-grid bases are strictly increasing. This is the exact integer form of strict monotonicity of `(d!)^(1/d)` needed by the Vandermonde construction.

declarations.name: factorialGridVandermondeNode
declarations.docstring: Vandermonde nodes for a cutoff with `n + 1` channel rows: the moment node is `1`, followed by the exact integer reciprocal nodes for channels `2, ..., n + 2`.

declarations.name: one_lt_factorialGridBase_two
declarations.docstring: The first factorial-grid channel node is strictly larger than the moment node.

declarations.name: factorialGridVandermondeNode_strictMono
declarations.docstring: All exact factorial-grid Vandermonde nodes are strictly increasing and hence pairwise distinct.

declarations.name: factorialGridReciprocalNode
declarations.docstring: Rational normalized Vandermonde nodes: reciprocals of the exact integer grid bases, including the moment node `1`.

declarations.name: factorialGridReciprocalNode_injective
declarations.docstring: The normalized reciprocal nodes remain pairwise distinct.

declarations.name: factorialGrid_vandermonde_det_ne_zero
declarations.docstring: The exact normalized factorial-grid Vandermonde determinant is nonzero.

declarations.name: factorialGridShiftedVandermonde
declarations.signature: def factorialGridShiftedVandermonde (n t : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin (n + 2)) (Fin (n + 2)) ℚ
declarations.docstring: Consecutive factorial-grid columns beginning at exponent `t`, written as a row-scaled Vandermonde matrix.

declarations.name: factorialGridShiftedVandermonde_apply
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGridShiftedVandermonde_apply (n t : ℕ) (i j : Fin (n + 2)) : factorialGridShiftedVandermonde n t i j = factorialGridReciprocalNode n i ^ (t + j.val)
declarations.docstring: Entrywise, the shifted matrix consists of consecutive powers `alpha_i^(t+j)`.

declarations.name: factorialGridReciprocalNode_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGridReciprocalNode_ne_zero (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)) : factorialGridReciprocalNode n i ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Every reciprocal factorial-grid node is nonzero.

declarations.name: factorialGridShiftedVandermonde_det_ne_zero
declarations.docstring: Any consecutive block of normalized factorial-grid columns has nonzero determinant.

declarations.name: factorialGridIndex
declarations.signature: def factorialGridIndex (n t : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2)) : ℕ
declarations.docstring: Exact support indices for consecutive factorial-grid columns beginning at exponent `t`.

declarations.name: channelCoefficient_div_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem channelCoefficient_div_factorial {i d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) : (((i.factorial / d.factorial ^ (i / d) : ℕ) : ℚ) / (i.factorial : ℚ)) = ((d.factorial ^ (i / d) : ℕ) : ℚ)⁻¹
declarations.docstring: Normalizing an integral channel coefficient by its ambient factorial recovers the reciprocal channel denominator exactly.

declarations.name: channel_dvd_factorialGridScale
declarations.signature: theorem channel_dvd_factorialGridScale {n d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hdn : d ≤ n + 2) : d ∣ factorialGridScale (n + 2)
declarations.docstring: Every requested channel divides the common factorial-grid scale.

declarations.name: factorialGridIndex_div
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGridIndex_div {n t : ℕ} (j : Fin (n + 2)) {d : ℕ} (hd : 0 < d) (hdn : d ≤ n + 2) : factorialGridIndex n t j / d = (t + j.val) * (factorialGridScale (n + 2) / d)
declarations.docstring: Quotients of factorial-grid indices by requested channels have the exact linear exponent expected by the Vandermonde parameterization.

declarations.name: normalizedFactorialGridMatrix
declarations.signature: def normalizedFactorialGridMatrix (n t : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin (n + 2)) (Fin (n + 2)) ℚ
declarations.docstring: The augmented integer channel/moment matrix on the factorial grid, column-normalized over the rationals by the ambient factorials.

declarations.name: normalizedFactorialGridMatrix_eq_shiftedVandermonde
declarations.signature: theorem normalizedFactorialGridMatrix_eq_shiftedVandermonde (n t : ℕ) : normalizedFactorialGridMatrix n t = factorialGridShiftedVandermonde n t
declarations.docstring: The normalized augmented channel/moment matrix is exactly the shifted Vandermonde matrix on the reciprocal factorial-grid nodes.

declarations.name: normalizedFactorialGridMatrix_det_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem normalizedFactorialGridMatrix_det_ne_zero (n t : ℕ) : (normalizedFactorialGridMatrix n t).det ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The normalized augmented matrix on every consecutive factorial-grid block has nonzero determinant.

declarations.name: augmentedFactorialGridMatrix_det_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem augmentedFactorialGridMatrix_det_ne_zero (n t : ℕ) : (augmentedChannelMomentMatrix (factorialGridIndex n t)).det ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The original integer augmented channel/moment matrix on the factorial grid also has nonzero determinant.

declarations.name: exists_factorialGrid_nonzeroMoment_channelKernel
declarations.signature: theorem exists_factorialGrid_nonzeroMoment_channelKernel (n t : ℕ) : ∃ coeff : Fin (n + 2) → ℤ, (∀ d : Fin (n + 1), channelNumerator coeff (factorialGridIndex n t) (d.val + 2) = 0) ∧ factorialMoment coeff (factorialGridIndex n t) ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Every factorial-grid block explicitly produces an integer coefficient vector with zero consecutive channels and nonzero factorial moment.

declarations.name: cramerFactorialGrid_channels_zero
declarations.signature: theorem cramerFactorialGrid_channels_zero (n t : ℕ) : ∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + 2), channelNumerator (cramerChannelKernelCoeff (factorialGridIndex n t)) (factorialGridIndex n t) d = 0
declarations.docstring: The explicit factorial-grid Cramer vector annihilates every channel from `2` through `n + 2`.

declarations.name: cramerFactorialGrid_moment_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem cramerFactorialGrid_moment_ne_zero (n t : ℕ) : factorialMoment (cramerChannelKernelCoeff (factorialGridIndex n t)) (factorialGridIndex n t) ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The explicit factorial-grid Cramer vector has nonzero factorial moment.

declarations.name: exists_cramerFactorialGridResidual_eq_det_mul_factorialGapSeries_add_int
declarations.signature: theorem exists_cramerFactorialGridResidual_eq_det_mul_factorialGapSeries_add_int (n t : ℕ) : ∃ K : ℤ, channelResidual (n + 2) (cramerChannelKernelCoeff (factorialGridIndex n t)) (factorialGridIndex n t) = ((augmentedChannelMomentMatrix (factorialGridIndex n t)).det : ℝ) * factorialGapSeries + (K : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: For the factorial-grid Cramer vector, the residual differs from the nonzero augmented determinant times the Erdős problem 68 series by an integer.

declarations.name: cramerFactorialGrid_channelNumerator_eq_moment_of_max_lt
declarations.signature: theorem cramerFactorialGrid_channelNumerator_eq_moment_of_max_lt (n t d : ℕ) (hmax : (t + (n + 1)) * factorialGridScale (n + 2) < d) : channelNumerator (cramerChannelKernelCoeff (factorialGridIndex n t)) (factorialGridIndex n t) d = factorialMoment (cramerChannelKernelCoeff (factorialGridIndex n t)) (factorialGridIndex n t)
declarations.docstring: Beyond the largest factorial-grid support index, every tail numerator is exactly the fixed factorial moment. Thus the floor-discontinuous finite region is the only place where channel signs can change.

declarations.name: cramerFactorialGrid_channelNumerator_ne_zero_of_max_lt
declarations.signature: theorem cramerFactorialGrid_channelNumerator_ne_zero_of_max_lt (n t d : ℕ) (hmax : (t + (n + 1)) * factorialGridScale (n + 2) < d) : channelNumerator (cramerChannelKernelCoeff (factorialGridIndex n t)) (factorialGridIndex n t) d ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: In particular, no factorial-grid Cramer tail numerator can vanish once the channel lies beyond the largest support index.

declarations.name: exists_factorialGrid_primeTranslator_reduced_kernel
declarations.signature: theorem exists_factorialGrid_primeTranslator_reduced_kernel (n t : ℕ) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hDp : n + 2 < p) : ∃ z : ℤ, (∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + 2), channelNumerator (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff (cramerChannelKernelCoeff (factorialGridIndex n t)) p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex (factorialGridIndex n t) p) d = 0) ∧ factorialMoment (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff (cramerChannelKernelCoeff (factorialGridIndex n t)) p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex (factorialGridIndex n t) p) ≠ 0 ∧ |channelResidual (n + 2)
declarations.docstring: Every factorial-grid Cramer vector can be enlarged by a prime translator above the cutoff, preserving its zero channels and nonzero moment while reducing the residual to absolute value at most `1/2`.

declarations.name: factorialGridIndex_gt
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGridIndex_gt (n B : ℕ) (j : Fin (n + 2)) : B < factorialGridIndex n (B + 1) j
declarations.docstring: Choosing the grid start as `B+1` places every factorial-grid index above the prescribed support threshold.

declarations.name: exists_remote_factorialGrid_primeTranslator_reduction
declarations.signature: theorem exists_remote_factorialGrid_primeTranslator_reduction (n B : ℕ) : ∃ p : ℕ, ∃ z : ℤ, p.Prime ∧ (∀ j : Sum (Fin (n + 2)) (Fin 2), B < appendPrimeTranslatorIndex (factorialGridIndex n (B + 1)) p j) ∧ (∀ d ∈ Finset.Icc 2 (n + 2), channelNumerator (appendPrimeTranslatorCoeff (cramerChannelKernelCoeff (factorialGridIndex n (B + 1))) p z) (appendPrimeTranslatorIndex (factorialGridIndex n (B + 1)) p) d = 0) ∧
declarations.docstring: For every cutoff and support threshold, a factorial-grid block and a prime translator pair can be chosen entirely above the threshold, with the stated zero-channel, nonzero-moment, and residual bounds.

declarations.name: factorialGapScaledTail
declarations.docstring: The exact tail after `m`, scaled by `m!`.

declarations.name: factorialGapScaledTail_pos
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapScaledTail_pos {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : 0 < factorialGapScaledTail m
declarations.docstring: The scaled factorial-gap tail is positive.

declarations.name: factorialGapScaledTail_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapScaledTail_lt_one {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : factorialGapScaledTail m < 1
declarations.docstring: The scaled factorial-gap tail is strictly smaller than one.

declarations.name: factorialGapScaledTail_lt_two_div
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapScaledTail_lt_two_div {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : factorialGapScaledTail m < 2 / (m : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: A sharper elementary tail width: after scaling by `m!`, the entire future tail is less than `2 / m`.

declarations.name: factorialGapEndpointFlag
declarations.docstring: The endpoint flag records whether the canonical remainder of the full series lies above the exact scaled tail.

declarations.name: factorialGapEndpointFlag_eq_zero_or_one
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapEndpointFlag_eq_zero_or_one (m : ℕ) : factorialGapEndpointFlag m = 0 ∨ factorialGapEndpointFlag m = 1
declarations.docstring: Every endpoint flag is zero or one.

declarations.name: factorialGapEndpointFlag_eq_zero_iff
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapEndpointFlag_eq_zero_iff (m : ℕ) : factorialGapEndpointFlag m = 0 ↔ canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries m < factorialGapScaledTail m
declarations.docstring: A zero endpoint flag is exactly strict containment below the scaled tail.

declarations.name: factorialGapEndpointFlag_eq_one_iff
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapEndpointFlag_eq_one_iff (m : ℕ) : factorialGapEndpointFlag m = 1 ↔ factorialGapScaledTail m ≤ canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries m
declarations.docstring: A one endpoint flag is exactly containment at or above the scaled tail.

declarations.name: factorialGapScaledTail_pred_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapScaledTail_pred_recurrence {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : (m : ℝ) * factorialGapScaledTail (m - 1) = 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) + factorialGapScaledTail m
declarations.docstring: Exact scaled-tail recurrence after adjoining the `m`-th summand.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapRat
declarations.docstring: Exact rational version of the predecessor gap. This is executable: it uses only the finite prefix through `m - 1` and rational floor.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapRat_cast
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapRat_cast (m : ℕ) : ((factorialGapPredecessorGapRat m : ℚ) : ℝ) = factorialGapPredecessorGap m
declarations.docstring: The executable rational predecessor gap agrees with the real-valued quantity used by the analytic carry reduction.

declarations.name: factorialBlockCoefficient_cast_eq_strictFacTopRat
declarations.docstring: The natural coefficient used by the factorial-block CRT package is exactly the executable rational strict successor.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat
declarations.docstring: The reduced scaled prefix whose strict upper-grid residue is the predecessor gap.

declarations.name: rat_finset_sum_den_dvd_prod_den
declarations.signature: theorem rat_finset_sum_den_dvd_prod_den {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (f : α → ℚ) : (∑ x ∈ s, f x).den ∣ (∏ x ∈ s, (f x).den)
declarations.docstring: The reduced denominator of a finite rational sum divides the product of the reduced denominators of its summands.

declarations.name: rat_finset_sum_den_dvd_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem rat_finset_sum_den_dvd_of_dvd {α : Type*} (s : Finset α) (f : α → ℚ) {M : ℕ} (hdiv : ∀ x ∈ s, (f x).den ∣ M) : (∑ x ∈ s, f x).den ∣ M
declarations.docstring: A common multiple of all summand denominators is already a common denominator for the reduced finite sum. This retains least-common-multiple rather than product-level valuation information.

declarations.name: factorialGapReciprocal_den
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapReciprocal_den {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) : (1 / ((k.factorial : ℚ) - 1)).den = k.factorial - 1
declarations.docstring: Each literal factorial-gap reciprocal has its displayed positive denominator already in lowest terms.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefix_den_dvd_gapProduct
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefix_den_dvd_gapProduct (n : ℕ) : (factorialGapPrefix n).den ∣ (∏ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 n, (k.factorial - 1))
declarations.docstring: The denominator of the actual prefix divides the product of its literal factorial-gap denominators.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefixLCM
declarations.docstring: The least common multiple of the literal factorial-gap denominators through one prefix endpoint.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefix_den_dvd_prefixLCM
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefix_den_dvd_prefixLCM (n : ℕ) : (factorialGapPrefix n).den ∣ factorialGapPrefixLCM n
declarations.docstring: The reduced denominator of the exact prefix divides the factorial-gap least common multiple through the same endpoint.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den_dvd_prefixLCM
declarations.docstring: Integer factorial scaling cannot add denominator valuation, so the actual reduced predecessor denominator is bounded by the same prefix LCM.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapRat_den
declarations.docstring: Taking a strict upper-grid complement changes the numerator but not the reduced denominator.

declarations.name: not_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den_of_prefixPrivate
declarations.signature: theorem not_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den_of_prefixPrivate {m q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hprefix : ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k < m → Nat.Coprime q (k.factorial - 1)) : ¬q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den
declarations.docstring: A prime coprime to every earlier factorial gap is absent from the reduced denominator of the scaled earlier prefix.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator
declarations.docstring: Integral numerator of the predecessor gap over the reduced denominator of the scaled finite prefix. The numerator lies in `1, ..., den`, with the terminal value `den` representing an integral scaled prefix.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat
declarations.docstring: Natural-number representative of the positive reduced predecessor-gap numerator, for modular projection onto denominator primes.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_pos
declarations.docstring: The strict upper-grid residue numerator is always positive.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat_cast
declarations.signature: @[simp] theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat_cast (m : ℕ) : (factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat m : ℤ) = factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator m
declarations.docstring: The natural representative casts back to the integral numerator.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_le_den
declarations.docstring: The strict upper-grid residue numerator is at most its reduced denominator. Equality is exactly the integral scaled-prefix convention.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_isCoprime_den
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_isCoprime_den (m : ℕ) : IsCoprime (factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator m) ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The reduced upper-grid residue numerator is coprime to its denominator, which is the coprimality needed for the later finite CRT arguments.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_ne_zero_of_one_lt_dvd_den
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_ne_zero_of_one_lt_dvd_den {m d : ℕ} (hd : 1 < d) (hdDen : d ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) : factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat m % d ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Every nontrivial divisor of the reduced denominator sees a nonzero projection of the reduced predecessor-gap numerator.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_ne_zero_of_prime_dvd_den
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_ne_zero_of_prime_dvd_den {m q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hqDen : q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) : factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat m % q ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Every prime factor of the reduced denominator sees a nonzero projection of the reduced predecessor-gap numerator.

declarations.name: primeFinset_prod_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den
declarations.signature: theorem primeFinset_prod_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den {m : ℕ} {s : Finset ℕ} (hprime : ∀ q ∈ s, q.Prime) (hdiv : ∀ q ∈ s, q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) : (∏ q ∈ s, q) ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den
declarations.docstring: A finite set of distinct prime factors of the actual reduced denominator multiplies to an actual CRT divisor of that denominator.

declarations.name: one_lt_primeFinset_prod
declarations.signature: theorem one_lt_primeFinset_prod {s : Finset ℕ} (hs : s.Nonempty) (hprime : ∀ q ∈ s, q.Prime) : 1 < ∏ q ∈ s, q
declarations.docstring: A nonempty finite product of primes is a nontrivial modulus.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_primeFinset_prod_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_primeFinset_prod_ne_zero {m : ℕ} {s : Finset ℕ} (hs : s.Nonempty) (hprime : ∀ q ∈ s, q.Prime) (hdiv : ∀ q ∈ s, q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) : factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat m % (∏ q ∈ s, q) ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: A finite nonempty set of surviving denominator primes therefore gives a nonzero numerator projection modulo their full CRT product.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapRat_eq_numerator_div_den
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapRat_eq_numerator_div_den (m : ℕ) : factorialGapPredecessorGapRat m = (factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator m : ℚ) / (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den
declarations.docstring: Exact numerator/denominator normal form of the finite predecessor gap.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapRat_succ_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapRat_succ_recurrence {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : factorialGapPredecessorGapRat (m + 1) = (m : ℚ) * factorialGapPredecessorGapRat m - 1 / ((m.factorial : ℚ) - 1) - (factorialGapStepCarry m : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: Exact rational recurrence for consecutive reduced predecessor gaps. This is the finite arithmetic orbit underlying the interval checker: the next gap is obtained by multiplying by the new radix, subtracting the factorial error, and subtracting the integer carry.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_succ_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_succ_recurrence {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : (factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator (m + 1) : ℚ) / (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den = (m : ℚ) * ((factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator m : ℚ) / (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) - 1 / ((m.factorial : ℚ) - 1) - (factorialGapStepCarry m : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: Consecutive coprime numerator/denominator pairs satisfy the same exact rational recurrence.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_dvd_den_mul_gap
declarations.docstring: Conversely, the next reduced denominator always divides the old denominator times the newly adjoined factorial gap.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer
declarations.docstring: The exact reduction factor removed when the raw denominator `v_m * (m! - 1)` is normalized at the next endpoint.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_mul_transitionNormalizer
declarations.docstring: The next reduced denominator times the transition normalizer is the unreduced denominator produced by adjoining `1/(m!-1)`.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer_pos
declarations.docstring: The exact transition normalizer is positive at every nontrivial factorial-gap step.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_succ_recurrence_cleared
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_succ_recurrence_cleared {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator (m + 1) * ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den : ℤ) * ((m.factorial : ℤ) - 1) = (m : ℤ) * factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator m * ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den : ℤ) * ((m.factorial : ℤ) - 1) - ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den : ℤ) * ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den : ℤ) - factorialGapStepCarry m * ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den : ℤ) * ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den : ℤ) * ((m.factorial : ℤ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: Clearing all positive denominators gives a pure integer recurrence for the consecutive reduced pairs.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_mul_transitionNormalizer
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator_mul_transitionNormalizer {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator (m + 1) * factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer m = (m : ℤ) * factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator m * ((m.factorial : ℤ) - 1) - (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den - factorialGapStepCarry m * (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den * ((m.factorial : ℤ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: After exposing the exact transition normalizer, the reduced numerator obeys an integral recurrence with no next-denominator factor.

declarations.name: transitionNormalizer_mul_predecessorGapNumerator_modEq_neg_den
declarations.signature: theorem transitionNormalizer_mul_predecessorGapNumerator_modEq_neg_den {m d : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hdA : d ∣ m.factorial - 1) : Int.ModEq (d : ℤ) (factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer m * factorialGapPredecessorGapNumerator (m + 1)) (-(factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: At a newly adjoined divisor `d | m!-1`, the normalized next numerator has a completely explicit congruence: multiplying it by the transition normalizer gives `-v_m` modulo `d`. The identity retains the reduction factor omitted by the earlier qualitative nonvanishing statement.

declarations.name: prime_coprime_factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer_of_dvd_gap
declarations.signature: theorem prime_coprime_factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer_of_dvd_gap {m q : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hq : q.Prime) (hqA : q ∣ m.factorial - 1) (hqV : ¬q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) : Nat.Coprime q (factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer m)
declarations.docstring: A genuinely new prime is also absent from the transition normalizer. Thus the exact entry congruence can be inverted modulo every entering private prime; cancellation cannot hide in the normalizer.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer_of_collision
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer_of_collision {m q : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hq : q.Prime) (hqV : q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) (hcollision : q ∣ m ∨ q ∣ m.factorial - 1) : q ∣ factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer m
declarations.docstring: Every old denominator prime that collides with the new radix or factorial gap is absorbed by the transition normalizer. This is the prime-level converse to persistence away from both collision factors.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den_dvd_radix_gap_succ_den
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den_dvd_radix_gap_succ_den {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den : ℤ) ∣ (m : ℤ) * ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den : ℤ) * ((m.factorial : ℤ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: Reduced denominators can lose factors at one step only through the new radix `m` or the newly adjoined factorial gap `m! - 1`. Equivalently, every other factor of `v_m` persists into `v_(m+1)`.

declarations.name: dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_of_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_of_coprime {m d : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hdV : d ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) (hdm : Nat.Coprime d m) (hdA : Nat.Coprime d (m.factorial - 1)) : d ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den
declarations.docstring: Composite-divisor form of denominator persistence. Any full divisor of `v_m` survives into `v_(m+1)` when it is coprime to both possible absorption factors, the radix `m` and the new factorial gap `m! - 1`. Unlike the prime-only form below, this retains prime-power valuations.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den {m q : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hq : q.Prime) (hqV : q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) (hqm : ¬q ∣ m) (hqA : ¬q ∣ m.factorial - 1) : q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den
declarations.docstring: Prime-factor form of denominator persistence. A prime already present in `v_m` survives in `v_(m+1)` unless it is absorbed by `m` or by the new denominator `m! - 1`.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_of_dvd_gap
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_of_dvd_gap {m q : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hq : q.Prime) (hqA : q ∣ m.factorial - 1) (hqV : ¬q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) : q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den
declarations.docstring: A genuinely new prime factor of the adjoined factorial gap enters the next reduced denominator. Cancellation is impossible because reducing the old gap did not expose that prime: modulo `q`, the cleared recurrence leaves only `v_m * v_(m+1)`.

declarations.name: dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_of_dvd_gap_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_of_dvd_gap_coprime {m d : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hdA : d ∣ m.factorial - 1) (hdV : Nat.Coprime d (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) : d ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den
declarations.docstring: Composite entry form. Every divisor of the new factorial gap that is coprime to the old reduced denominator enters the next reduced denominator in full.

declarations.name: prime_pow_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_of_dvd_gap
declarations.signature: theorem prime_pow_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_succ_den_of_dvd_gap {m q e : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hq : q.Prime) (hqPowA : q ^ e ∣ m.factorial - 1) (hqV : ¬q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den) : q ^ e ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (m + 1)).den
declarations.docstring: Every full prime power dividing a new factorial gap enters the next reduced denominator when the underlying prime is absent from the old denominator.
