declarations.docstring: An already-born individual component survives one more endpoint exactly when its prime avoids the new radix and the new factorial gap.

declarations.name: mk_mem_factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources_succ_iff
declarations.signature: theorem mk_mem_factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources_succ_iff {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (⟨n, q⟩ : FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource) ∈ factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources (n + 1) ↔ q ∈ factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePrimes n
declarations.docstring: The components born at the new source gap are precisely the canonical prefix-private primes of that gap. Their avoidance interval at the entry endpoint is empty.

declarations.name: factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources
declarations.docstring: The already-active components that survive the transition from endpoint `n` to endpoint `n + 1`.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeSources
declarations.docstring: The already-active components killed at the transition from endpoint `n` to endpoint `n + 1` by a collision with the new radix or factorial gap.

declarations.name: factorialGapBornPrivatePrimeSources
declarations.docstring: The components born from the new source gap `n! - 1`.

declarations.name: mem_factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources
declarations.signature: theorem mem_factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources {a : FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource} {n : ℕ} : a ∈ factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources n ↔ a ∈ factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources n ∧ Nat.Coprime a.2 n ∧ Nat.Coprime a.2 (n.factorial - 1)

declarations.name: mem_factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeSources
declarations.signature: theorem mem_factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeSources {a : FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource} {n : ℕ} : a ∈ factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeSources n ↔ a ∈ factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources n ∧ ¬(Nat.Coprime a.2 n ∧ Nat.Coprime a.2 (n.factorial - 1))

declarations.name: mem_factorialGapBornPrivatePrimeSources
declarations.signature: theorem mem_factorialGapBornPrivatePrimeSources {a : FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource} {n : ℕ} : a ∈ factorialGapBornPrivatePrimeSources n ↔ a.1 = n ∧ a.2 ∈ factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePrimes n

declarations.name: factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources_union_killed
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources_union_killed (n : ℕ) : factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources n ∪ factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeSources n = factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources n
declarations.docstring: The old active set is partitioned exactly into survivors and killed components.

declarations.name: factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources_disjoint_killed
declarations.docstring: The survivor and killed portions of the active set are disjoint.

declarations.name: factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources_succ_eq_surviving_union_born
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources_succ_eq_surviving_union_born {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources (n + 1) = factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources n ∪ factorialGapBornPrivatePrimeSources n
declarations.docstring: The successor active set consists exactly of the surviving old components and the components born at the new source gap.

declarations.name: factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePrimeSources_disjoint_born
declarations.docstring: No component born at source `n` can already be an old survivor: survivors have strictly smaller source index.

declarations.name: factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources_prime_ne
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources_prime_ne {n : ℕ} {a b : FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource} (ha : a ∈ factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources n) (hb : b ∈ factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources n) (hab : a ≠ b) : a.2 ≠ b.2
declarations.docstring: Distinct active source pairs carry distinct primes, even if they were born at different gaps. Prefix privacy at the later gap rules out reuse of every earlier gap prime.

declarations.name: factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSourcePowers_pairwise_coprime
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSourcePowers_pairwise_coprime {n : ℕ} : (factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources n : Set FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource).Pairwise (fun a b => Nat.Coprime (factorialGapPrivatePrimeSourcePower a) (factorialGapPrivatePrimeSourcePower b))
declarations.docstring: Active individual prime-power components are pairwise coprime.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrivatePrimeSourcePower_dvd_entry_den
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrivatePrimeSourcePower_dvd_entry_den {n : ℕ} {a : FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource} (ha : a ∈ factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources n) : factorialGapPrivatePrimeSourcePower a ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (a.1 + 1)).den
declarations.docstring: Every active individual component enters at the successor of its source gap with its complete factorial-gap valuation.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus
declarations.docstring: The complete canonical componentwise accumulator at endpoint `n`.

declarations.name: factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePowerModulus
declarations.docstring: The product of the old components that survive the transition from endpoint `n` to endpoint `n + 1`.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledPrivatePowerModulus
declarations.docstring: The product of the old components killed at the transition from endpoint `n` to endpoint `n + 1`.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus
declarations.docstring: The squarefree prime-label product of the components killed at one transition.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledTransitionGcd
declarations.docstring: The complete killed prime-power mass actually visible in the exact transition normalizer.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect
declarations.docstring: The excess killed prime-power multiplicity left after cancelling everything visible in the transition normalizer.

declarations.name: factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer
declarations.docstring: The transition normalizer after removing the complete common factor with the killed prime-power product.

declarations.name: factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor
declarations.docstring: The part of the new factorial gap not selected into the canonical prefix-private prime-power birth modulus.

declarations.name: factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePowerModulus_mul_unselectedBirthCofactor
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePowerModulus_mul_unselectedBirthCofactor {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePowerModulus n * factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n = n.factorial - 1
declarations.docstring: The selected birth modulus and its complementary cofactor recover the entire new factorial gap.

declarations.name: factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePowerModulus_pos
declarations.docstring: The selected birth modulus is positive at every nontrivial factorial-gap step.

declarations.name: factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_pos
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_pos {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 0 < factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n
declarations.docstring: The complementary unselected part of a nontrivial factorial gap is positive.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_boundary_or_repeat
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_boundary_or_repeat {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) : q = n + 1 ∨ ∃ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k ∧ k < n ∧ q ∣ k.factorial - 1
declarations.docstring: A prime appearing in the unselected part of `n! - 1` is either the boundary prime `n + 1` or already appeared in an earlier factorial gap. Thus the birth cofactor contains only boundary/repeat support, while every genuinely new prime larger than the boundary is selected into `P_n` with its complete valuation.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorial_two_before_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorial_two_before_sub_one {q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hq5 : 5 ≤ q) : q ∣ (q - 2).factorial - 1
declarations.docstring: Every prime `q ≥ 5` is an automatic linear-size divisor of the factorial gap two indices earlier: `q ∣ (q - 2)! - 1`. This Wilson boundary family explains why an upper bound of shape `p(n! - 1) < (1 + ε)n` on an infinite subsequence does not by itself produce private support or irrationality.

declarations.name: factorialGapDenominatorProduct
declarations.docstring: Product of the literal factorial gaps through `B`. This is the finite counting scale for first-hit arguments: every prime already seen by time `B` divides this one integer.

declarations.name: factorialGapDenominatorProduct_pos
declarations.docstring: The finite factorial-gap product is positive.

declarations.name: exists_prime_avoiding_factorialGapProduct_of_lt
declarations.signature: theorem exists_prime_avoiding_factorialGapProduct_of_lt {B : ℕ} {s : Finset ℕ} (hprime : ∀ q ∈ s, q.Prime) (hlt : factorialGapDenominatorProduct B < ∏ q ∈ s, q) : ∃ q ∈ s, ¬q ∣ factorialGapDenominatorProduct B
declarations.docstring: Prime-product pigeonhole for factorial gaps. If a finite set of distinct primes has product larger than all gaps through `B`, at least one of those primes has not occurred in any factorial gap through `B`. This finite pigeonhole statement compares prime-product growth with the elementary size of `factorialGapDenominatorProduct B`, without assuming a large prime factor at a preselected index.

declarations.name: exists_late_prefixPrivate_factorialGap_hit_of_primeProduct_lt
declarations.signature: theorem exists_late_prefixPrivate_factorialGap_hit_of_primeProduct_lt {B : ℕ} {s : Finset ℕ} (hprime : ∀ q ∈ s, q.Prime) (hfive : ∀ q ∈ s, 5 ≤ q) (hlt : factorialGapDenominatorProduct B < ∏ q ∈ s, q) : ∃ q ∈ s, ∃ m, B < m ∧ m ≤ q - 2 ∧ q.Prime ∧ q ∣ m.factorial - 1 ∧ ∀ k, 2 ≤ k → k < m → Nat.Coprime q (k.factorial - 1)
declarations.docstring: Wilson's automatic hit at `q - 2`, combined with the prime-product pigeonhole, produces a genuinely prefix-private hit after `B` while retaining the explicit upper bound `m ≤ q - 2`. Thus an asymptotic comparison between a prime product and the elementary gap product yields cofinal private anchors whose supporting prime is controlled from above by the chosen prime window. This complements large-prime-factor theorems, which control the prime from below but may lose all upper control when passing to the least hit.

declarations.name: cofinal_prefixPrivate_factorialGap_hits
declarations.signature: theorem cofinal_prefixPrivate_factorialGap_hits : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ q m : ℕ, B < m ∧ q.Prime ∧ m < q ∧ q ∣ m.factorial - 1 ∧ ∀ k, 2 ≤ k → k < m → Nat.Coprime q (k.factorial - 1)
declarations.docstring: Cofinal prefix-private factorial-gap primes are unconditional. Given a cutoff `B`, choose a prime `q ≥ B! + 5`; Wilson supplies the hit at `q - 2`. The least hit for `q` cannot occur at or below `B`, since then the prime would be at most `B! - 1`. Thus cofinal private support needs no external large-prime-factor theorem. Quantitative applications still need a sharper estimate, such as the prime-product pigeonhole above, to control `q` relative to its least hit.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_reflected_factorialGap_of_odd
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_reflected_factorialGap_of_odd {q n : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hn : Odd n) (hnq : n < q) (hqdvd : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) : q ∣ (q - n - 1).factorial - 1
declarations.docstring: Wilson reflection for an odd factorial-gap index. If a prime `q > n` divides `n! - 1`, then the complementary factorial at `q - n - 1` is also `1` modulo `q`. This is the exact collision mechanism behind the `n! - 1` extension of Stewart's small-prime-factor subsequence: such a factor is not automatically prefix-private.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorialBlockCollisionCore_of_odd_reflection
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorialBlockCollisionCore_of_odd_reflection {p q n : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hn : Odd n) (hpn : p ≤ n) (hnmem : n ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hrefmem : q - n - 1 ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hqUpper : q < 2 * n + 1) (hqdvd : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) : q ∣ factorialBlockCollisionCore p
declarations.docstring: If the reflected index lies in the same factorial block and `q < 2n + 1`, the two distinct full `q`-hits force `q` into the block's collision core. In particular, a Stewart-scale divisor `q < 1.381n` cannot be counted as private support merely from its size.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_of_odd_reflection
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore_of_odd_reflection {p q n : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hn : Odd n) (hpn : p ≤ n) (hnmem : n ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hrefmem : q - n - 1 ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hqUpper : q < 2 * n + 1) (hqdvd : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) : q ∣ factorialBlockNormalizedCollisionCore p
declarations.docstring: A reflected upper-half collision survives predecessor-factorial normalization: the same prime `q` lies in the normalized collision core, not only in the unnormalised core.

declarations.name: one_lt_factorialBlockPrimeHitCount_of_odd_reflection
declarations.signature: theorem one_lt_factorialBlockPrimeHitCount_of_odd_reflection {p q n : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hn : Odd n) (hpn : p ≤ n) (hnmem : n ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hrefmem : q - n - 1 ∈ factorialBlockIndices p) (hqUpper : q < 2 * n + 1) (hqdvd : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) : 1 < ((factorialBlockIndices p).filter fun i => q ∣ factorialGapDenominator i).card
declarations.docstring: Incidence-count form of the reflected collision: the prime `q` hits at least two displayed factorial gaps in the block.

declarations.name: prime_succ_not_dvd_factorial_sub_one
declarations.docstring: Wilson's theorem excludes the apparent boundary exception: for `n ≥ 2`, the prime `n + 1` cannot divide `n! - 1`.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_repeat
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_repeat {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) : ∃ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k ∧ k < n ∧ q ∣ k.factorial - 1
declarations.docstring: Consequently every prime in the unselected birth cofactor is repeat support from a strictly earlier factorial gap.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_of_repeat
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_of_repeat {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqGap : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hrepeat : ∃ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k ∧ k < n ∧ q ∣ k.factorial - 1) : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n
declarations.docstring: Conversely, a prime dividing both the current factorial gap and one strictly earlier gap cannot be selected as prefix-private, so its complete current support remains in the unselected birth cofactor.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_interval_collision
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_interval_collision {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) : ∃ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k ∧ k + 1 < n ∧ q ∣ n.descFactorial (n - k) - 1 ∧ q ≤ n ^ (n - k)
declarations.docstring: Repeat support in the unselected birth cofactor is separated from the current endpoint by at least one whole factorial gap. Moreover it is visible in the exact intervening descending-factorial collision and obeys the corresponding power bound.

declarations.name: square_dvd_mul_sub_one_iff_quotient_balance
declarations.signature: theorem square_dvd_mul_sub_one_iff_quotient_balance {q a b A B : ℕ} (hqPos : 0 < q) (ha : a = 1 + q * A) (hb : b = 1 + q * B) : q ^ 2 ∣ a * b - 1 ↔ q ∣ A + B
declarations.docstring: Once two factors are individually `1` modulo `q`, their product is `1` modulo `q²` exactly when their first-order quotient residues cancel. This is the elementary linearization behind nonterminal factorial square hits.

declarations.name: factorialGap_square_dvd_later_iff_blockQuotient_balance
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_square_dvd_later_iff_blockQuotient_balance {k n q : ℕ} (hkn : k < n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqEarlier : q ∣ k.factorial - 1) (hqLater : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) : q ^ 2 ∣ n.factorial - 1 ↔ q ∣ (k.factorial - 1) / q + (n.descFactorial (n - k) - 1) / q
declarations.docstring: Nonterminal square-lift criterion. If a prime `q` already divides both factorial gaps at `k<n`, then the intervening descending factorial is also `1` modulo `q`. The later hit lifts from `q` to `q²` exactly when the two first-order quotient residues—one from `k!` and one from the intervening factorial block—sum to zero modulo `q`.

declarations.name: prime_not_mem_largePrefixPrivatePrimes_of_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor
declarations.signature: theorem prime_not_mem_largePrefixPrivatePrimes_of_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) : q ∉ factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePrimes n
declarations.docstring: A prime supported by the unselected cofactor cannot simultaneously be one of the selected prefix-private birth primes.

declarations.name: primePower_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_of_prime_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem primePower_dvd_unselectedBirthCofactor_of_prime_dvd {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) : q ^ (n.factorial - 1).factorization q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n
declarations.docstring: The unselected cofactor retains the complete current-gap valuation of each prime in its support: no part of a repeated prime power is removed by the selected birth product.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorialGapPrivatePrimeSourcePower_of_mem_killed
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorialGapPrivatePrimeSourcePower_of_mem_killed {n : ℕ} {a : FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource} (ha : a ∈ factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeSources n) : a.2 ∣ factorialGapPrivatePrimeSourcePower a
declarations.docstring: Every killed source prime divides its complete source power.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus_dvd_killedPrivatePowerModulus
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus_dvd_killedPrivatePowerModulus (n : ℕ) : factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus n ∣ factorialGapKilledPrivatePowerModulus n
declarations.docstring: The squarefree killed-prime modulus divides the complete killed prime-power product.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledTransitionGcd_mul_reducedTransitionNormalizer
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapKilledTransitionGcd_mul_reducedTransitionNormalizer (n : ℕ) : factorialGapKilledTransitionGcd n * factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n = factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer n
declarations.docstring: The killed transition gcd times the reduced normalizer recovers the original transition normalizer exactly.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledTransitionGcd_mul_killedMultiplicityDefect
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapKilledTransitionGcd_mul_killedMultiplicityDefect (n : ℕ) : factorialGapKilledTransitionGcd n * factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n = factorialGapKilledPrivatePowerModulus n
declarations.docstring: The killed transition gcd times the multiplicity defect recovers the full killed prime-power product exactly.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledPrivatePowerModulus_pos
declarations.docstring: The complete killed prime-power product is positive, including when the killed set is empty.

declarations.name: factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePowerModulus_pos
declarations.docstring: The surviving prime-power product is positive, including when no old component survives the transition.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect_pos
declarations.docstring: Dividing the killed prime-power product by its transition gcd leaves a positive multiplicity defect.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_killedMultiplicityDefect_source_collision
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_killedMultiplicityDefect_source_collision {n q : ℕ} (hq : q.Prime) (hqDefect : q ∣ factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n) : ∃ a : FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource, a ∈ factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeSources n ∧ a.2 = q ∧ (q ∣ n ∨ q ∣ n.factorial - 1)
declarations.docstring: Every prime in the excess-kill defect comes from one exact old active source component killed at the current transition. Its label therefore collides with either the current radix `n` or the current factorial gap `n! - 1`; the defect introduces no third support mechanism.

declarations.name: factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer_pos
declarations.docstring: Dividing the positive transition normalizer by the killed transition gcd leaves a positive reduced outflow.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect_coprime_reducedTransitionNormalizer
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect_coprime_reducedTransitionNormalizer {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : Nat.Coprime (factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n) (factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n)
declarations.docstring: After cancelling the full killed/transition gcd, the remaining killed multiplicity defect and reduced transition normalizer are coprime.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_eq_surviving_mul_killed
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_eq_surviving_mul_killed (n : ℕ) : factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus n = factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePowerModulus n * factorialGapKilledPrivatePowerModulus n
declarations.docstring: The active accumulator factors into the components that survive the next transition and those killed there.

declarations.name: factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePowerModulus_coprime_of_prime_dvd_birth
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePowerModulus_coprime_of_prime_dvd_birth {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) : Nat.Coprime q (factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePowerModulus n)
declarations.docstring: A prime occurring in the current unselected birth mass is coprime to the product of all old components that survive this same transition. Indeed, every survivor is coprime to the complete current factorial gap.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_factorization_eq_killed_of_prime_dvd_birth
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_factorization_eq_killed_of_prime_dvd_birth {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) : (factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus n).factorization q = (factorialGapKilledPrivatePowerModulus n).factorization q
declarations.docstring: At a repeated-birth prime, every active old component with that label is killed, so the complete old accumulator valuation is exactly the killed valuation. This separates the old residual multiplicity from the multiplicity removed by the transition.

declarations.name: factorialGapBornPrivatePrimeSourcePowers_prod
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapBornPrivatePrimeSourcePowers_prod (n : ℕ) : (∏ a ∈ factorialGapBornPrivatePrimeSources n, factorialGapPrivatePrimeSourcePower a) = factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePowerModulus n
declarations.docstring: The product of the source-pair powers born at `n` is exactly the canonical multiplicity-sensitive modulus `P_n`.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_succ
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_succ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus (n + 1) = factorialGapSurvivingPrivatePowerModulus n * factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePowerModulus n
declarations.docstring: The next accumulator is exactly the product of surviving old components and the new source-gap modulus.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_succ_mul_killed
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_succ_mul_killed {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus (n + 1) * factorialGapKilledPrivatePowerModulus n = factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus n * factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePowerModulus n
declarations.docstring: Exact balance law for the canonical accumulator: multiplying the next accumulator by the killed product equals multiplying the old accumulator by the newly born product.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_dvd_den
declarations.docstring: The componentwise canonical accumulator divides the actual reduced denominator at its endpoint.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer_of_mem_killed
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer_of_mem_killed {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) {a : FactorialGapPrivatePrimeSource} (ha : a ∈ factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeSources n) : a.2 ∣ factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer n
declarations.docstring: Every killed source prime divides the exact transition normalizer.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus_dvd_transitionNormalizer
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus_dvd_transitionNormalizer {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus n ∣ factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer n
declarations.docstring: The product of all distinct killed prime labels divides the exact transition normalizer. Prime-power multiplicity may be only partly absorbed, but every killed support prime is witnessed in the reduction factor.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus_dvd_killedTransitionGcd
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus_dvd_killedTransitionGcd {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapKilledPrivatePrimeModulus n ∣ factorialGapKilledTransitionGcd n
declarations.docstring: All distinct killed prime labels lie in the common killed/transition factor. Any nontrivial defect therefore records excess multiplicity, not an entirely missed killed support prime.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor
declarations.docstring: The part of the reduced denominator not accounted for by the canonical componentwise accumulator. The successor recurrence above turns this quotient into the exact collision/re-entry remainder.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_mul_residualCofactor
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_mul_residualCofactor (n : ℕ) : factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus n * factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n = (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den
declarations.docstring: The reduced denominator factors exactly into the componentwise accumulator and its residual cofactor.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_pos
declarations.docstring: The residual cofactor is always positive.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_recurrence {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1) * factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer n * factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePowerModulus n = factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n * (n.factorial - 1) * factorialGapKilledPrivatePowerModulus n
declarations.docstring: Exact recurrence for the residual cofactor. The next residual, transition cancellation, and newly born product balance the old residual, new factorial gap, and killed product.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_reduced_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_reduced_recurrence {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1) * factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n * factorialGapLargePrefixPrivatePowerModulus n = factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n * (n.factorial - 1) * factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n
declarations.docstring: Cancelling the full gcd between the killed prime-power mass and the transition normalizer leaves an exact recurrence whose right-hand collision factor is only the genuinely unabsorbed multiplicity defect.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_intrinsic_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_intrinsic_recurrence {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1) * factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n = factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n * factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n * factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n
declarations.docstring: Cancelling the complete selected birth modulus leaves the intrinsic residual-cofactor dynamics. New residual mass can enter only through the unselected part of the new factorial gap or through excess killed prime-power multiplicity; the reduced transition normalizer is the exact outflow factor.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_factorization_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_factorization_recurrence {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)).factorization q + (factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n).factorization q = (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n).factorization q + (factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n).factorization q + (factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n).factorization q
declarations.docstring: Primewise form of the intrinsic residual-cofactor recurrence. For every prime candidate `q`, its next residual valuation plus its reduced outflow valuation is exactly its old residual valuation plus its repeated-birth and excess-kill inflow valuations.

declarations.name: factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer_factorization_eq_zero_of_prime_dvd_defect
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer_factorization_eq_zero_of_prime_dvd_defect {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqDefect : q ∣ factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n) : (factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n).factorization q = 0
declarations.docstring: A prime carried by the excess-kill defect cannot simultaneously occur in the reduced transition outflow. This is the primewise content of the gcd cancellation defining `D_n` and `R_n`.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_factorization_eq_of_prime_dvd_defect
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_factorization_eq_of_prime_dvd_defect {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqDefect : q ∣ factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n) : (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)).factorization q = (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n).factorization q + (factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n).factorization q + (factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n).factorization q
declarations.docstring: At every prime in the excess-kill defect, the intrinsic recurrence has no outflow term: its next residual valuation is exactly its old valuation plus both inflow valuations.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_factorization_lt_succ_of_prime_dvd_defect
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_factorization_lt_succ_of_prime_dvd_defect {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqDefect : q ∣ factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n) : (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n).factorization q < (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)).factorization q
declarations.docstring: Every prime in the excess-kill defect gains strictly more residual valuation at the next endpoint. Excess killed multiplicity is therefore a genuine one-step growth event, never hidden by simultaneous outflow.

declarations.name: factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect_dvd_residualCofactor_succ
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect_dvd_residualCofactor_succ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: The complete excess-kill defect, with all of its prime multiplicities, is absorbed into the next residual cofactor. Coprimality with the reduced outflow prevents any part of `D_n` from being cancelled on the left.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_factorization_eq_of_not_dvd_outflow
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_succ_factorization_eq_of_not_dvd_outflow {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hqNotOutflow : ¬q ∣ factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n) : (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)).factorization q = (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n).factorization q + (factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n).factorization q + (factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n).factorization q
declarations.docstring: At a prime absent from the reduced transition outflow, the next residual valuation is exactly the sum of the old residual and both inflow valuations.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_factorization_lt_succ_of_prime_dvd_birth_not_outflow
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_factorization_lt_succ_of_prime_dvd_birth_not_outflow {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) (hqNotOutflow : ¬q ∣ factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n) : (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n).factorization q < (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)).factorization q
declarations.docstring: A repeated-birth prime absent from the reduced outflow forces strict growth of its residual valuation.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_reducedTransitionNormalizer_of_prime_dvd_birth_of_not_residual_growth
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_reducedTransitionNormalizer_of_prime_dvd_birth_of_not_residual_growth {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) (hnotGrowth : ¬(factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n).factorization q < (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)).factorization q) : q ∣ factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n
declarations.docstring: Every repeated-birth prime either grows in the residual cofactor or is present in the reduced outflow. Hence failure of residual growth forces divisibility of the reduced transition normalizer.

declarations.name: factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_div_gcd_reducedTransitionNormalizer_dvd_residualCofactor_succ
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_div_gcd_reducedTransitionNormalizer_dvd_residualCofactor_succ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n / Nat.gcd (factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) (factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n) ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Remove from the repeated-birth cofactor exactly its gcd with the reduced outflow. Every remaining prime power divides the next residual cofactor in full. This is the multiplicity-sensitive global form of the birth-versus-outflow dichotomy.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den_of_prime_dvd_birth_and_reduced_outflow
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den_of_prime_dvd_birth_and_reduced_outflow {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) (hqOutflow : q ∣ factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n) : q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den
declarations.docstring: A repeated-birth prime can occur in the reduced outflow only if it was already present in the old reduced denominator. Purely new denominator mass from the current gap cannot be cancelled by normalization.

declarations.name: gcd_factorialGap_transitionNormalizer_dvd_predecessorScaledRat_den
declarations.signature: theorem gcd_factorialGap_transitionNormalizer_dvd_predecessorScaledRat_den {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : Nat.gcd (n.factorial - 1) (factorialGapPredecessorTransitionNormalizer n) ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den
declarations.docstring: The complete common factor of the current factorial gap and transition normalizer already divides the old reduced denominator. This retains full prime-power multiplicity, not merely prime support.

declarations.name: gcd_unselectedBirthCofactor_reducedTransitionNormalizer_dvd_predecessorScaledRat_den
declarations.signature: theorem gcd_unselectedBirthCofactor_reducedTransitionNormalizer_dvd_predecessorScaledRat_den {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : Nat.gcd (factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) (factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n) ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den
declarations.docstring: Hence the full multiplicity-sensitive overlap between repeated birth mass and reduced outflow already divides the old denominator.

declarations.name: factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_factorization_eq_gap_of_prime_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_factorization_eq_gap_of_prime_dvd {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) : (factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n).factorization q = (n.factorial - 1).factorization q
declarations.docstring: At every prime in the unselected cofactor, that cofactor retains exactly the complete current factorial-gap valuation.

declarations.name: factorialGap_factorization_le_den_of_reducedOutflow_exceeds_residual
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_factorization_le_den_of_reducedOutflow_exceeds_residual {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) (hexcess : (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n).factorization q < (factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n).factorization q) : (n.factorial - 1).factorization q ≤ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den.factorization q
declarations.docstring: If reduced outflow at a repeated-birth prime exceeds all old residual mass at that prime, then the current factorial-gap valuation was no larger than the complete old denominator valuation. Thus cancellation beyond the old residual is possible only without a genuine multiplicity amplification at the current gap.

declarations.name: factorialGap_primePower_dvd_residualCofactor_succ_of_den_factorization_lt_gap
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_primePower_dvd_residualCofactor_succ_of_den_factorization_lt_gap {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) (hamplifies : (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den.factorization q < (n.factorial - 1).factorization q) : q ^ (n.factorial - 1).factorization q ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Genuine repeated-prime multiplicity amplification cannot disappear into transition normalization. If the current factorial gap contains strictly more `q`-adic mass than the whole old reduced denominator, then that complete current prime power divides the next residual cofactor.

declarations.name: factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den_factorization_lt_gap_of_record
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat_den_factorization_lt_gap_of_record {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqGap : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hrecord : ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k < n → (k.factorial - 1).factorization q < (n.factorial - 1).factorization q) : (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den.factorization q < (n.factorial - 1).factorization q
declarations.docstring: A strict `q`-adic record for the current factorial gap is already larger than the actual old reduced-denominator valuation. This replaces the opaque denominator comparison by a pure factorial-gap history condition.

declarations.name: factorialGap_repeatedRecordPrimePower_dvd_residualCofactor_succ
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_repeatedRecordPrimePower_dvd_residualCofactor_succ {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqGap : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hrepeat : ∃ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k ∧ k < n ∧ q ∣ k.factorial - 1) (hrecord : ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k < n → (k.factorial - 1).factorization q < (n.factorial - 1).factorization q) : q ^ (n.factorial - 1).factorization q ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Every repeated strict valuation record enters the next residual cofactor with its complete current factorial-gap multiplicity.

declarations.name: factorialGap_repeatedRecordPrimePower_dvd_succ_den
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_repeatedRecordPrimePower_dvd_succ_den {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqGap : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hrepeat : ∃ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k ∧ k < n ∧ q ∣ k.factorial - 1) (hrecord : ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k < n → (k.factorial - 1).factorization q < (n.factorial - 1).factorization q) : q ^ (n.factorial - 1).factorization q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (n + 1)).den
declarations.docstring: The same record power divides the complete next reduced denominator.

declarations.name: predecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_repeatedRecordPrimePower_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem predecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_repeatedRecordPrimePower_ne_zero {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqGap : q ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hrepeat : ∃ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k ∧ k < n ∧ q ∣ k.factorial - 1) (hrecord : ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k < n → (k.factorial - 1).factorization q < (n.factorial - 1).factorization q) : factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat (n + 1) % q ^ (n.factorial - 1).factorization q ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Reduced coprimality turns every repeated strict valuation record into a nonzero next-numerator projection modulo its complete prime power.

declarations.name: factorialGap_firstRepeatedPrimeSquare_entry
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_firstRepeatedPrimeSquare_entry {n k p : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hp : p.Prime) (hk2 : 2 ≤ k) (hkn : k < n) (hpEarlier : p ∣ k.factorial - 1) (hpSq : p ^ 2 ∣ n.factorial - 1) (hfirstSq : ∀ j : ℕ, 2 ≤ j → j < n → ¬p ^ 2 ∣ j.factorial - 1) : p ^ 2 ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1) ∧ p ^ 2 ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (n + 1)).den ∧ factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat (n + 1) % (p ^ 2) ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: A square criterion with no reduced-denominator hypothesis. If `p²` first appears in a factorial gap at `n`, while `p` already appeared at one earlier gap, then `p²` enters the next residual cofactor and actual denominator and has a nonzero reduced-numerator projection.

declarations.name: factorialWilsonQuotient
declarations.docstring: The natural Wilson quotient. Wilson's theorem makes the displayed division exact whenever `p` is prime.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_factorial_pred_factorial_add_one
declarations.docstring: Wilson's theorem in the divisibility form used below.

declarations.name: factorialWilsonQuotient_mul_prime
declarations.signature: theorem factorialWilsonQuotient_mul_prime {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : factorialWilsonQuotient p * p = (p - 1).factorial + 1
declarations.docstring: Exact reconstruction of the numerator from the natural Wilson quotient.

declarations.name: one_le_factorialWilsonQuotient
declarations.signature: theorem one_le_factorialWilsonQuotient {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : 1 ≤ factorialWilsonQuotient p
declarations.docstring: For a prime, the Wilson quotient is positive.

declarations.name: factorialWilsonQuotient_balance
declarations.signature: theorem factorialWilsonQuotient_balance {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : p * (factorialWilsonQuotient p - 1) = (p - 1) * ((p - 2).factorial - 1)
declarations.docstring: The exact balance behind the Wilson-quotient square criterion.

declarations.name: factorialWilsonQuotient_modEq_one_iff_square_dvd_gap
declarations.signature: theorem factorialWilsonQuotient_modEq_one_iff_square_dvd_gap {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : factorialWilsonQuotient p ≡ 1 [MOD p] ↔ p ^ 2 ∣ (p - 2).factorial - 1
declarations.docstring: Wilson criterion. For every prime `p`, the congruence `W_p ≡ 1 (mod p)` is equivalent to a square hit in the factorial gap at `p - 2`. Thus the higher-order Wilson condition is exactly the valuation-amplification trigger used below, rather than merely a numerical coincidence at `p = 107`.

declarations.name: factorialGap_halfFactorial_Wilson_record_entry
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_halfFactorial_Wilson_record_entry {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpFive : 5 ≤ p) (hhalf : p ∣ ((p - 1) / 2).factorial - 1) (hWilson : factorialWilsonQuotient p ≡ 1 [MOD p]) (hfirstSq : ∀ j : ℕ, 2 ≤ j → j < p - 2 → ¬p ^ 2 ∣ j.factorial - 1) : p ^ 2 ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (p - 1) ∧ p ^ 2 ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat (p - 1)).den ∧ factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat (p - 1) % (p ^ 2) ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The joint source pattern now has a direct denominator-growth conclusion. A half-factorial `+1` hit supplies the earlier occurrence; `W_p ≡ 1 (mod p)` supplies the square occurrence at `p - 2`; and the first-square condition promotes their conjunction to a strict valuation record. The full square then survives in the next residual cofactor and actual reduced denominator.

declarations.name: oneHundredSeven_sq_not_dvd_factorialGap_before_105
declarations.docstring: Before endpoint `105`, no factorial gap carries two factors of `107`. This is a finite residue calculation, not a cofinal claim.

declarations.name: oneHundredSeven_repeatedRecord_at_105
declarations.signature: theorem oneHundredSeven_repeatedRecord_at_105 : (107 : ℕ).Prime ∧ 107 ∣ (105 : ℕ).factorial - 1 ∧ (∃ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k ∧ k < 105 ∧ 107 ∣ k.factorial - 1) ∧ (∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k < 105 → (k.factorial - 1).factorization 107 < ((105 : ℕ).factorial - 1).factorization 107)
declarations.docstring: An exact repeated-valuation record: `107` occurs at exponent one in `53! - 1` and at exponent at least two in `105! - 1`, exceeding every prior valuation.

declarations.name: oneHundredSeven_factorialWilsonQuotient_modEq_one
declarations.docstring: The concrete square hit is equivalently the Wilson-quotient congruence `W_107 ≡ 1 (mod 107)`.

declarations.name: oneHundredSeven_halfFactorial_Wilson_record_entry
declarations.docstring: At `p = 107`, the half-factorial hit, Wilson-quotient congruence, and finite first-square record force a square in the reduced denominator at `106`.

declarations.name: oneHundredSeven_sq_dvd_residualCofactor_106
declarations.docstring: The concrete record at `105` forces the full square `107^2` into the next residual cofactor.

declarations.name: predecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_oneHundredSeven_sq_at_106_ne_zero
declarations.docstring: The same concrete square is an actual next-denominator divisor and therefore sees a nonzero reduced-numerator projection.

declarations.name: nineHundredSeventyOne_sq_not_dvd_factorialGap_before_609
declarations.docstring: Before the nonterminal record index `609`, no factorial gap carries two factors of `971`. This is a finite residue calculation, not a cofinal claim.

declarations.name: nineHundredSeventyOne_firstRepeatedPrimeSquare_entry
declarations.docstring: The exact scan's first genuinely non-Wilson record: `971` occurs in `361! - 1`, its square first occurs in `609! - 1`, and `609 < 971 - 2`. The complete square therefore enters the actual denominator at endpoint `610` and has a nonzero reduced-numerator projection.

declarations.name: factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationPrimes
declarations.docstring: Repeated-birth primes whose current factorial-gap multiplicity strictly exceeds their complete multiplicity in the old reduced denominator.

declarations.name: mem_factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationPrimes_iff
declarations.signature: theorem mem_factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationPrimes_iff {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : q ∈ factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationPrimes n ↔ q.Prime ∧ q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n ∧ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den.factorization q < (n.factorial - 1).factorization q
declarations.docstring: Membership in the canonical repeated-birth amplification set.

declarations.name: factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus
declarations.docstring: The complete current-gap prime powers at every amplified repeated prime, assembled into one canonical pairwise-coprime product.

declarations.name: factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus_dvd_birth
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus_dvd_birth {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus n ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n
declarations.docstring: The amplification modulus is genuinely a subproduct of the unselected birth cofactor, with every selected prime retained to full multiplicity.

declarations.name: factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus_dvd_residualCofactor_succ
declarations.docstring: Every amplified repeated-birth component survives normalization in full, so their complete canonical product divides the next residual cofactor.

declarations.name: factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus_dvd_birth_gcd_residual_succ
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus_dvd_birth_gcd_residual_succ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus n ∣ Nat.gcd (factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) (factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1))
declarations.docstring: The amplified repeated-birth mass is therefore a common divisor of the current birth cofactor and the next residual cofactor, not merely a support-level witness.

declarations.name: factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus_pos
declarations.docstring: The canonical amplification product is always positive.

declarations.name: one_lt_factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus
declarations.docstring: A nonempty amplification-prime set gives a genuinely nontrivial full-multiplicity modulus.

declarations.name: factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus_dvd_succ_den
declarations.docstring: Amplified repeated-birth mass is not merely present in the residual quotient: it divides the complete next reduced denominator.

declarations.name: predecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_repeatedBirthAmplificationModulus_ne_zero
declarations.signature: theorem predecessorGapNumeratorNat_mod_repeatedBirthAmplificationModulus_ne_zero {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hnonempty : (factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationPrimes n).Nonempty) : factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat (n + 1) % factorialGapRepeatedBirthAmplificationModulus n ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: Whenever amplification occurs, reduced coprimality turns the whole full-multiplicity product into a nonzero next-numerator CRT projection.

declarations.name: factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_dvd_predecessorScaledRat_den_mul_residualCofactor_succ
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_dvd_predecessorScaledRat_den_mul_residualCofactor_succ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den * factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: The repeated-birth cofactor splits across two adjacent times: its birth/outflow overlap was already present in the old denominator, while the complementary prime-power mass divides the next residual cofactor. Consequently the entire `B_n` divides their product.

declarations.name: factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_le_predecessorScaledRat_den_mul_residualCofactor_succ
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor_le_predecessorScaledRat_den_mul_residualCofactor_succ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n ≤ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den * factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)
declarations.docstring: Numerical form of the two-time conservation law: repeated birth mass cannot exceed the old denominator times the next residual cofactor.

declarations.name: prime_dvd_accumulator_or_residualCofactor_of_prime_dvd_birth_and_reduced_outflow
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_accumulator_or_residualCofactor_of_prime_dvd_birth_and_reduced_outflow {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqBirth : q ∣ factorialGapUnselectedBirthCofactor n) (hqOutflow : q ∣ factorialGapReducedTransitionNormalizer n) : q ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus n ∨ q ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n
declarations.docstring: The old denominator mass required by a birth/outflow collision is already visible either in the canonical active accumulator or in the old residual cofactor.

declarations.name: factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor_factorization_lt_succ_of_prime_dvd_birth_not_old_den

declarations.name: prime_dvd_new_residualCofactor_interval_collision
declarations.signature: theorem prime_dvd_new_residualCofactor_interval_collision {n q : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (hq : q.Prime) (hqNext : q ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor (n + 1)) (hqNotOld : ¬q ∣ factorialGapComponentwiseResidualCofactor n) (hqNotDefect : ¬q ∣ factorialGapKilledMultiplicityDefect n) : ∃ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k ∧ k + 1 < n ∧ q ∣ n.descFactorial (n - k) - 1 ∧ q ≤ n ^ (n - k)

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_componentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_threshold
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_componentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus_threshold (hthreshold : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, 3 ≤ n ∧ B < n ∧ (factorialGapActivePrivatePrimeSources n).Nonempty ∧ (((n : ℤ) + 2) * (n.factorial : ℤ) - 2) * ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat n).den : ℤ) ≤ ((n : ℤ) ^ 2 * ((n.factorial : ℤ) - 1)) * ((factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat n % factorialGapComponentwiseAccumulatedPrivatePowerModulus n : ℕ) : ℤ)) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Componentwise accumulated-modulus criterion. This retains each private prime power independently, so a later collision at one prime does not erase the surviving contributions born at the same source gap.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_predecessorGapNumerator_mod_threshold
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_predecessorGapNumerator_mod_threshold (hthreshold : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m q : ℕ, 3 ≤ m ∧ B < m ∧ q.Prime ∧ q ∣ (factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den ∧ (((m : ℤ) + 2) * (m.factorial : ℤ) - 2) * ((factorialGapPredecessorScaledRat m).den : ℤ) ≤ ((m : ℤ) ^ 2 * ((m.factorial : ℤ) - 1)) * ((factorialGapPredecessorGapNumeratorNat m % q : ℕ) : ℤ)) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Prime-modulus form of the same criterion. It is useful only when a single prime captures enough of the reduced denominator; in general a larger composite divisor is needed.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_prime_lower_endpoint_escape
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_prime_lower_endpoint_escape (hescape : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ B < p ∧ factorialGapScaledTail p ≤ (p : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries (p - 1)) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: Cofinal escape from the tiny lower cylinder at prime indices proves Erdős #68. A prime need not miss the full unit-carry target: landing in the maximal-digit upper cylinder also suffices.

declarations.name: factorialExpPrefix
declarations.docstring: Finite factorial-expansion prefix `sum_{2 <= n <= m} 1 / n!`.

declarations.name: factorialGapSecondLayerPrefix
declarations.docstring: Finite second layer `sum_{2 <= n <= m} 1 / (n! (n! - 1))`.

declarations.name: factorialExpScaled
declarations.docstring: The factorial prefix scaled to an integer at level `m!`.

declarations.name: secondLayerPrefixFloor
declarations.docstring: The floor of the finite second layer at factorial scale `m!`.

declarations.name: secondLayerPrefixDigit
declarations.docstring: The mixed-radix digit made from two consecutive finite-prefix floors.

declarations.name: one_div_factorial_sub_one_eq_exp_add_second
declarations.signature: theorem one_div_factorial_sub_one_eq_exp_add_second {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : 1 / ((n.factorial : ℚ) - 1) = 1 / (n.factorial : ℚ) + 1 / ((n.factorial : ℚ) * ((n.factorial : ℚ) - 1))
declarations.docstring: Termwise elementary decomposition of a factorial-gap reciprocal.

declarations.name: factorialGapPrefix_eq_exp_add_second
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGapPrefix_eq_exp_add_second (m : ℕ) : factorialGapPrefix m = factorialExpPrefix m + factorialGapSecondLayerPrefix m
declarations.docstring: Exact decomposition of every finite factorial-gap prefix.

declarations.name: factorial_mul_expPrefix_eq_scaled
declarations.signature: theorem factorial_mul_expPrefix_eq_scaled (m : ℕ) : (m.factorial : ℚ) * factorialExpPrefix m = factorialExpScaled m
declarations.docstring: Scaling the finite factorial-expansion prefix by `m!` gives the displayed natural-number sum of exact quotients.

declarations.name: factorialExpPrefix_eq_prev_add
declarations.signature: theorem factorialExpPrefix_eq_prev_add {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : factorialExpPrefix m = factorialExpPrefix (m - 1) + 1 / (m.factorial : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: Adding the endpoint to the finite factorial-expansion prefix contributes exactly `1 / m!`.

declarations.name: factorialExpScaled_step
declarations.signature: theorem factorialExpScaled_step {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : factorialExpScaled m = m * factorialExpScaled (m - 1) + 1
declarations.docstring: The integral factorial-expansion head satisfies its exact radix recurrence.

declarations.name: secondLayerPrefixFloor_eq_strictFacTop_sub_exp
declarations.signature: theorem secondLayerPrefixFloor_eq_strictFacTop_sub_exp (m : ℕ) : secondLayerPrefixFloor m = strictFacTopRat (factorialGapPrefix m) m - (factorialExpScaled m : ℤ) - 1
declarations.docstring: The finite second-layer floor is the factorial-gap strict successor with the integral `e - 2` head removed.

declarations.name: secondLayerPrefixDigit_eq_carry
declarations.signature: theorem secondLayerPrefixDigit_eq_carry {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : secondLayerPrefixDigit m = (m : ℤ) - 1 - factorialGapStepCarry m
declarations.docstring: Exact finite second-layer digit law. No infinite-tail stabilization is used here.

declarations.name: SecondLayerFloorStableAt
declarations.docstring: The explicit condition needed to replace a finite second-layer prefix floor by the floor of an infinite target `x`.

declarations.name: canonicalDigit_eq_carry_of_secondLayerFloorStable
declarations.signature: theorem canonicalDigit_eq_carry_of_secondLayerFloorStable {x : ℝ} {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hmStable : SecondLayerFloorStableAt x m) (hprevStable : SecondLayerFloorStableAt x (m - 1)) : canonicalDigit x m = (m : ℤ) - 1 - factorialGapStepCarry m
declarations.docstring: Under floor stability at two consecutive scales, the canonical digit of the infinite target is the finite digit `m - 1 - carry`.

declarations.name: rational_not_eventually_canonicalDigit_eq_maximal
declarations.signature: theorem rational_not_eventually_canonicalDigit_eq_maximal (a : ℤ) {q : ℕ} (hq : 0 < q) : ¬ ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ m : ℕ, M ≤ m → 2 ≤ m → canonicalDigit (((a : ℚ) / (q : ℚ)) : ℝ) m = (m : ℤ) - 1
declarations.docstring: A rational number cannot have an eventually maximal canonical factorial-digit tail: rational tails are eventually zero.

declarations.name: factorialGap_lower_endpoint_escape_iff_nonunit_or_maximal_digit
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_lower_endpoint_escape_iff_nonunit_or_maximal_digit {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) : factorialGapScaledTail m ≤ (m : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries (m - 1) ↔ factorialGapStepCarry m ≠ 1 ∨ canonicalDigit _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries m = (m : ℤ) - 1
declarations.docstring: **The escape criterion is exactly the harmless-carry criterion.** The forward implication is the existing consumer; the converse is new and is what turns the one-way test into a normal form.

declarations.name: factorialGap_rational_denominator_ge_of_lower_endpoint_escape
declarations.signature: theorem factorialGap_rational_denominator_ge_of_lower_endpoint_escape {m q : ℕ} {a : ℤ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) (hq : 0 < q) (hseries : _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries = (a : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)) (hescape : factorialGapScaledTail m ≤ (m : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries (m - 1)) : m ≤ q
declarations.docstring: One escape at index `m` excludes every displayed rational denominator below `m`. Unlike the existing prime-indexed consumer, no primality assumption is needed.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_lower_endpoint_escape
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_iff_cofinal_lower_endpoint_escape : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries ↔ ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, B < m ∧ factorialGapScaledTail m ≤ (m : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries (m - 1)
declarations.docstring: **Third exact normal form for Erdős #68.** The series is irrational exactly when its canonical factorial orbit escapes the lower endpoint cylinder cofinally. Because `0 < factorialGapScaledTail m < 2/m`, this is a shrinking-target statement with target radius `O(m⁻²)`.

declarations.name: lower_endpoint_escape_of_predecessorGap_outside_window
declarations.signature: theorem lower_endpoint_escape_of_predecessorGap_outside_window {m : ℕ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hout : (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m ≤ 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) ∨ 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) + 2 / (m : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m) : factorialGapScaledTail m ≤ (m : ℝ) * canonicalRemainder _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries (m - 1)
declarations.docstring: **Tail-free two-sided window.** Escaping the lower endpoint cylinder is implied by the finite predecessor gap avoiding a rational window of width `2/m` — on *either* side. The corpus previously exposed only the upper half.

declarations.name: irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_predecessorGap_outside_window
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_factorialGapSeries_of_cofinal_predecessorGap_outside_window (hout : ∀ B : ℕ, ∃ m : ℕ, 3 ≤ m ∧ B < m ∧ ((m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m ≤ 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) ∨ 1 + 1 / ((m.factorial : ℝ) - 1) + 2 / (m : ℝ) ≤ (m : ℝ) * factorialGapPredecessorGap m)) : Irrational _root_.Erdos68.factorialGapSeries
declarations.docstring: **Two-sided finite consumer.** Cofinal avoidance of the explicit rational window of width `2/m` proves irrationality. No infinite sum, real floor, or tail occurs in the hypothesis.

declarations.name: lower_endpoint_target_radius_lt_two_div_sq
declarations.signature: theorem lower_endpoint_target_radius_lt_two_div_sq {m : ℕ} (hm : 2 ≤ m) : 0 < factorialGapScaledTail m / (m : ℝ) ∧ factorialGapScaledTail m / (m : ℝ) < 2 / (m : ℝ) ^ 2
declarations.docstring: The trapping radius is quadratically small: the exact target has width `factorialGapScaledTail m / m ∈ (0, 2/m²)`.

declarations.name: dvd_strictSuccessor_iff_roundingDigit_eq_one
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_strictSuccessor_iff_roundingDigit_eq_one {m N Nprev b : ℤ} (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hrec : N = m * Nprev + 1 - b) (hbLower : -1 ≤ b) (hbUpper : b ≤ m - 1) : m ∣ N ↔ b = 1
declarations.docstring: Arithmetic core of the strict-successor recurrence. If `N = m * Nprev + 1 - b` with the sharp digit bounds `-1 ≤ b ≤ m - 1` and `m ≥ 3`, then `m ∣ N` holds exactly when `b = 1`. The result is stated over `ℤ` because the rounding digit can attain `-1` at the lower endpoint.

declarations.name: pow_dvd_dilation_strictSuccessor_iff
declarations.signature: theorem pow_dvd_dilation_strictSuccessor_iff {p N Nprev b : ℤ} {k : ℕ} (hp : 3 ≤ p) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hrec : N = ((k : ℤ) * p) * Nprev + 1 - b) (hbLower : -1 ≤ b) (hbUpper : b ≤ (k : ℤ) * p - 1) : p ^ k ∣ N ↔ ∃ r : ℤ, 0 ≤ r ∧ r < (k : ℤ) ∧ b = 1 + p * r ∧ p ^ (k - 1) ∣ (k : ℤ) * Nprev - r
declarations.docstring: Exact two-stage criterion for a prime-power hit at a dilated strict-successor index. The first stage forces the rounding digit into one of the `k` residue slots `1 + p r`; the second stage is the surviving predecessor congruence modulo `p^(k-1)`.

declarations.name: sq_dvd_double_strictSuccessor_iff
declarations.signature: theorem sq_dvd_double_strictSuccessor_iff {p N Nprev b : ℤ} (hp : 3 ≤ p) (hrec : N = (2 * p) * Nprev + 1 - b) (hbLower : -1 ≤ b) (hbUpper : b ≤ 2 * p - 1) : p ^ 2 ∣ N ↔ (b = 1 ∧ p ∣ 2 * Nprev) ∨ (b = 1 + p ∧ p ∣ 2 * Nprev - 1)
declarations.docstring: At dilation `k = 2`, a square hit has exactly two possible digit and predecessor-residue branches.

declarations.name: sq_dvd_double_strictSuccessor_prime_iff
declarations.signature: theorem sq_dvd_double_strictSuccessor_prime_iff {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hpTwo : p ≠ 2) {N Nprev b : ℤ} (hrec : N = (2 * (p : ℤ)) * Nprev + 1 - b) (hbLower : -1 ≤ b) (hbUpper : b ≤ 2 * (p : ℤ) - 1) : (p : ℤ) ^ 2 ∣ N ↔ (b = 1 ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ Nprev) ∨ (b = 1 + (p : ℤ) ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ 2 * Nprev - 1)
declarations.docstring: For an odd prime, the factor `2` cancels in the first square-hit branch, leaving the exact predecessor divisibility stated in the #68 prime-power reduction.

declarations.name: envelope_of_triangular_recurrence
declarations.signature: theorem envelope_of_triangular_recurrence (u A source : ℕ → ℤ) (w : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ) (hrec : ∀ n, u n = source n + ∑ d ∈ Finset.range n, w n d * u d) (hsource : ∀ n, A n ∣ source n) (htransport : ∀ n d, d < n → A n ∣ w n d * A d) : ∀ n, A n ∣ u n
declarations.docstring: Divisibility is preserved under a triangular integral recurrence when every edge transports the proposed envelope.

declarations.name: tail_divisor_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem tail_divisor_certificate (u A : ℕ → ℤ) (g : ℤ) (D N : ℕ) (hchain : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → A i ∣ A j) (henvelope : ∀ n, D < n → A n ∣ u n) (hfinite : ∀ n, D < n → n ≤ N → g ∣ u n) (hstop : g ∣ A (N + 1)) : ∀ n, D < n → g ∣ u n
declarations.docstring: The finite prefix and one envelope divisibility certify all later terms.

declarations.name: tail_common_divisors_iff
declarations.signature: theorem tail_common_divisors_iff (u A : ℕ → ℤ) (g : ℤ) (D N : ℕ) (hchain : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → A i ∣ A j) (henvelope : ∀ n, D < n → A n ∣ u n) (hfinite : ∀ n, D < n → n ≤ N → g ∣ u n) (hstop : g ∣ A (N + 1)) (hgreatest : ∀ b : ℤ, (∀ n, D < n → n ≤ N → b ∣ u n) → b ∣ g) : ∀ b : ℤ, (∀ n, D < n → b ∣ u n) ↔ b ∣ g
declarations.docstring: A finite gcd's universal property extends to the entire infinite tail when the stopping certificate applies. No positivity convention is needed for this common-divisor equivalence.

declarations.name: walkStep
declarations.signature: def walkStep (h N L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The single new totient pair entering the window when the base point advances: `δ_N = φ(N+h+1+L) − φ(N+1+L)`.

declarations.name: walkRes
declarations.signature: def walkRes (h N L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The residue the certificate reads: `ρ_N = A_{h,N,L} mod 2^L`, in `[0, 2^L)`.

declarations.name: walkCo
declarations.signature: def walkCo (h N L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The distance from the residue up to `2^L`: `σ_N = 2^L − ρ_N`. This is the signed distance to `0` on the lower side of the arc.

declarations.name: walkRes_nonneg
declarations.signature: lemma walkRes_nonneg (h N L : ℕ) : 0 ≤ walkRes h N L

declarations.name: walkRes_lt
declarations.signature: lemma walkRes_lt (h N L : ℕ) : walkRes h N L < 2 ^ L

declarations.name: walkRes_eq
declarations.signature: lemma walkRes_eq (h N L : ℕ) : walkRes h N L = 2 ^ L - walkCo h N L

declarations.name: walkRes_succ
declarations.signature: theorem walkRes_succ (h N L : ℕ) : walkRes h (N + 1) L = (2 * walkRes h N L + walkStep h N L) % 2 ^ L
declarations.docstring: **The walk step, exactly.** Immediate from `Recon249.windowDiscrepancy_shift_emod`: the residue evolves by the doubling map plus the one incoming totient pair.

declarations.name: two_le_totient
declarations.signature: lemma two_le_totient {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) : 2 ≤ Nat.totient n
declarations.docstring: `2 ≤ φ(n)` for `n ≥ 3`: the totient is positive and (above `2`) even.

declarations.name: walkStep_le
declarations.signature: lemma walkStep_le {h N L : ℕ} (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) : walkStep h N L ≤ (N : ℤ) + h + L - 2
declarations.docstring: **Upper budget.** `δ_N ≤ (N+h+L) − 2`.

declarations.name: walkStep_ge
declarations.signature: lemma walkStep_ge {h N L : ℕ} (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) : (2 : ℤ) - ((N : ℤ) + L) ≤ walkStep h N L
declarations.docstring: **Lower budget.** `2 − (N+L) ≤ δ_N`.

declarations.name: real_step_budget
declarations.signature: theorem real_step_budget {h N L : ℕ} (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) (j : ℕ) : 2 - ((N : ℤ) + j + L) ≤ walkStep h (N + j) L ∧ walkStep h (N + j) L ≤ (N : ℤ) + j + h + L - 2
declarations.docstring: **The budget along a run.** At every point of the orbit based at `N` the real step obeys both bounds. This is the complete list of constraints the size data imposes; `AdmissibleRun` below abstracts exactly this list.

declarations.name: not_certifiedKill_iff
declarations.signature: lemma not_certifiedKill_iff (h N L : ℕ) : ¬ certifiedKill h N L ↔ (walkRes h N L ≤ (N : ℤ) + h + L + 2 ∨ (2 : ℤ) ^ L - ((N : ℤ) + h + L + 2) ≤ walkRes h N L)
declarations.docstring: A certificate fails exactly when the residue lies in the arc of radius `N+h+L+2` about `0`, i.e. near `0` from above or near `2^L` from below.

declarations.name: upperBand_run
declarations.signature: theorem upperBand_run {h N L K : ℕ} (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) (hroom : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + K + h + L) + 8 ≤ 2 ^ L) (hfail : ∀ j, 0 < j → j < K → ¬ certifiedKill h (N + j) L) (hlo : (N : ℤ) + L ≤ walkRes h N L) (hhi : walkRes h N L ≤ (N : ℤ) + h + L + 2) : ∀ j, j < K → ((N : ℤ) + j + L + 2 ^ j - 1 ≤ walkRes h (N + j) L ∧ walkRes h (N + j) L ≤ (N : ℤ) + j + h + L + 2)
declarations.docstring: **The upper-band induction.** While the run keeps failing, the residue's excess over the trapping radius `N+j+L−1` at least doubles, and the residue stays on the upper side of the arc.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_upperBand
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_upperBand {h N L K : ℕ} (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) (hK : (h : ℤ) + 3 < 2 ^ (K - 1)) (hroom : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + K + h + L) + 8 ≤ 2 ^ L) (hlo : (N : ℤ) + L ≤ walkRes h N L) (hhi : walkRes h N L ≤ (N : ℤ) + h + L + 2) : ∃ j < K, certifiedKill h (N + j) L
declarations.docstring: **Upper-band escape.** If the residue at `N` fails but lies in the top `h+3` values of the failure arc, a certificate appears within `K` steps for any `K` with `2^(K-1) > h+3` — a bound depending on `h` alone, not on `N` or `L`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_upperBand_log
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_upperBand_log {h N L : ℕ} (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) (hroom : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + (Nat.log 2 (h + 3) + 2) + h + L) + 8 ≤ 2 ^ L) (hlo : (N : ℤ) + L ≤ walkRes h N L) (hhi : walkRes h N L ≤ (N : ℤ) + h + L + 2) : ∃ j ≤ Nat.log 2 (h + 3) + 1, certifiedKill h (N + j) L
declarations.docstring: **Upper-band escape, logarithmic form.** A certificate appears within `log₂(h+3) + 1` steps.

declarations.name: lowerBand_run
declarations.signature: theorem lowerBand_run {h N L K : ℕ} (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) (hroom : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + K + h + L) + 8 ≤ 2 ^ L) (hfail : ∀ j, 0 < j → j < K → ¬ certifiedKill h (N + j) L) (hlo : (N : ℤ) + h + L ≤ walkCo h N L) (hhi : walkCo h N L ≤ (N : ℤ) + h + L + 2) : ∀ j, j < K → ((N : ℤ) + j + h + L + 2 ^ j - 1 ≤ walkCo h (N + j) L ∧ walkCo h (N + j) L ≤ (N : ℤ) + j + h + L + 2)
declarations.docstring: **The lower-band induction.** Mirror image of `upperBand_run`: the excess of `σ_j = 2^L − ρ_j` over its trapping radius `N+j+h+L−1` at least doubles.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_lowerBand
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_lowerBand {h N L : ℕ} (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) (hroom : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + 3 + h + L) + 8 ≤ 2 ^ L) (hlo : (N : ℤ) + h + L ≤ walkCo h N L) (hhi : walkCo h N L ≤ (N : ℤ) + h + L + 2) : certifiedKill h (N + 1) L ∨ certifiedKill h (N + 2) L
declarations.docstring: **Lower-band escape: an absolute constant.** If the residue at `N` fails on the lower side of the arc and sits in the bottom `3` values, then a certificate holds at `N+1` or at `N+2`. There is no dependence on `h`, `N` or `L` whatsoever: at most two consecutive failures.

declarations.name: AdmissibleRun
declarations.signature: structure AdmissibleRun (h N L : ℕ) (a d : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: **Exactly the data the size argument has.** A run of the walk based at `N` for which the affine recurrence holds and the step obeys the two-sided totient budget of `real_step_budget`, and which never leaves the failure arc. Any argument that bounds the number of consecutive failures using only the recurrence and `φ(n) < n`, `2 ≤ φ(n)` must rule this out.

declarations.name: trap_upper
declarations.signature: theorem trap_upper (h N L : ℕ) (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) : AdmissibleRun h N L (fun j => (N : ℤ) + j + L - 1) (fun j => 2 - ((N : ℤ) + j + L))
declarations.docstring: **Upper-side trapped walk.** `a_j = (N+j+L) − 1` with `d_j = 2 − (N+j+L)` is admissible and fails forever. Its start is one below the threshold `N+L` of `certifiedKill_of_upperBand`.

declarations.name: trap_lower
declarations.signature: theorem trap_lower (h N L : ℕ) (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) : AdmissibleRun h N L (fun j => -((N : ℤ) + j + h + L - 1)) (fun j => (N : ℤ) + j + h + L - 2)
declarations.docstring: **Lower-side trapped walk.** `a_j = −((N+j+h+L) − 1)` with `d_j = (N+j+h+L) − 2` is admissible and fails forever. Its start is one below (in absolute value) the threshold `N+h+L` of `certifiedKill_of_lowerBand`.

declarations.name: trap_interior
declarations.signature: theorem trap_interior (h N L : ℕ) (c : ℤ) (hc1 : -((N : ℤ) + h + L - 2) ≤ c) (hc2 : c ≤ (N : ℤ) + L - 2) : AdmissibleRun h N L (fun _ => c) (fun _ => -c)
declarations.docstring: **The trapping is not a knife-edge: the whole interior is fixed.** For every `c` in the interior arc `−(N+h+L−2) ≤ c ≤ N+L−2` the *constant* walk `a_j = c`, `d_j = −c` is admissible and fails forever. So it is not merely some extremal trajectory that survives: every residue strictly inside the trapping radii is a fixed point of an admissible walk, and the step it uses is `|d_j| = |c|`, which can be as small as `0` — nowhere near the edge of the budget.

declarations.name: no_absolute_bound_on_consecutive_failures
declarations.signature: theorem no_absolute_bound_on_consecutive_failures (h N L : ℕ) (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) : ∃ a d : ℕ → ℤ, AdmissibleRun h N L a d ∧ ∀ K : ℕ, ∀ j < K, |a j| ≤ (N : ℤ) + j + h + L + 2
declarations.docstring: For every `h`, `N`, `L` there is a coarse `AdmissibleRun` that remains trapped. The second conjunct is already the `trapped` field of that structure. This does not construct a sequence of actual totient differences.

declarations.name: thresholds_are_sharp
declarations.signature: theorem thresholds_are_sharp (h N L : ℕ) (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) : ((fun j => (N : ℤ) + j + L - 1) 0 = ((N : ℤ) + L) - 1 ∧ AdmissibleRun h N L (fun j => (N : ℤ) + j + L - 1) (fun j => 2 - ((N : ℤ) + j + L))) ∧ ((fun j => -((N : ℤ) + j + h + L - 1)) 0 = -(((N : ℤ) + h + L) - 1) ∧ AdmissibleRun h N L (fun j => -((N : ℤ) + j + h + L - 1)) (fun j => (N : ℤ) + j + h + L - 2))
declarations.docstring: **Both escape thresholds are sharp to the unit inside `AdmissibleRun`.** The upper-band theorem fires at `N+L`; the walk of `trap_upper` starts at `N+L−1` and never escapes. The lower-band theorem fires at codistance `N+h+L`; the walk of `trap_lower` starts at codistance `N+h+L−1` and never escapes. These model walks have odd steps and therefore are not genuine totient walks in the range where totients are even.

declarations.name: upperBand_card
declarations.signature: theorem upperBand_card (h N L : ℕ) : (Finset.Icc ((N : ℤ) + L) ((N : ℤ) + h + L + 2)).card = h + 3
declarations.docstring: The upper band has `h+3` residues.

declarations.name: lowerBand_card
declarations.signature: theorem lowerBand_card (h N L : ℕ) : (Finset.Icc ((N : ℤ) + h + L) ((N : ℤ) + h + L + 2)).card = 3
declarations.docstring: The lower band has `3` residues.

declarations.name: coverage_fraction_tends_to_zero
declarations.signature: theorem coverage_fraction_tends_to_zero (h L M : ℕ) : ∃ N, M * (h + 6) < 2 * (N + h + L) + 5
declarations.docstring: **An arbitrarily small-ratio witness.** The failure arc holds `2·(N+h+L)+5` residues; the two escape theorems cover `h+6` of them, a count independent of `N`. The statement supplies, for each ratio `M`, one base point where the arc is more than `M` times the covered band. It does not itself state a limit or quantify over all larger base points.

declarations.name: lowerBand_instance
declarations.docstring: The lower-band hypothesis is satisfiable: at `h = 9`, `N = 9`, `L = 10` the codistance is `30` and `N+h+L = 28 ≤ 30 ≤ 30`. So `certifiedKill_of_lowerBand` fires, and predicts a kill at `N+1` or `N+2`.

declarations.name: lowerBand_instance_realised
declarations.docstring: And the prediction is correct: the kill is at `N+1`, while `N` itself fails. (Both facts are kernel evaluations, independent of the theorem.)

declarations.name: upperBand_instance
declarations.docstring: The upper-band hypothesis is satisfiable: at `h = 30`, `N = 1`, `L = 10` the residue is `14`, and `N+L = 11 ≤ 14 ≤ 43 = N+h+L+2`. With `K = 7` the escape theorem applies, since `h+3 = 33 < 64 = 2^6`.

declarations.name: upperBand_instance_realised
declarations.docstring: The escape here genuinely takes two steps, so the theorem is not silently predicting an immediate kill: `certifiedKill 30 1 10` and `certifiedKill 30 2 10` are both false, and `certifiedKill 30 3 10` is true.

declarations.name: split_arith
declarations.signature: private lemma split_arith {P r a d u v : ℤ} (hP : 4 * r < P) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (ha0 : 0 ≤ a) (haP : a < P) (hdlo : -(r - 1) ≤ d) (hdhi : d ≤ r - 1) (hu : u = (2 * a + d) % (2 * P)) (hv : v = (2 * a + d) % P) (hc1 : r + 1 < u) (hc2 : u < 2 * P - (r + 1)) (hfail1 : a ≤ r ∨ P - r ≤ a) (hfail2 : v ≤ r + 1 ∨ P - (r + 1) ≤ v) : False
declarations.docstring: The purely arithmetic core of the depth split. `a` is the depth-`L` residue, `d` the fresh totient letter, `u` the depth-`(L+1)` residue and `v` the residue of the same integer modulo `2^L` — which by `windowDiscrepancy_emod_truncate` is the base-`(N+1)`, depth-`L` residue. If the depth-`(L+1)` cell certifies while both depth-`L` cells fail, the size constraints are contradictory once `4r < P`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_depth_split
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_depth_split {h N L : ℕ} (hdeep : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + (h : ℤ) + (L : ℤ) + 2) < 2 ^ L) (hcert : certifiedKill h N (L + 1)) : certifiedKill h N L ∨ certifiedKill h (N + 1) L
declarations.docstring: **Depth split.** Below the doubling threshold `4·(N+h+L+2) < 2^L`, a certificate at depth `L+1` based at `N` is *nothing but* a certificate at depth `L` based at `N` or at `N+1`. This is the exact converse of the two corpus monotonicities `certifiedKill_add` (depth) and `AngleA2.certifiedKill_base_descent` (base): together they say the depth ladder and the free-`N` walk are one and the same ladder.

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_shift
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_shift {h N L K : ℕ} (hdeep : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + (K : ℤ) + (h : ℤ) + (L : ℤ) + 2) < 2 ^ L) (hcert : certifiedKill h N (L + K)) : ∃ j ≤ K, certifiedKill h (N + j) L
declarations.docstring: **The deep cell is the disjunction of the shallow walk.** Iterated depth split: a certificate at depth `L+K` based at `N` forces a certificate at depth `L` at one of the `K+1` bases `N, N+1, …, N+K`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_window_iff
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_window_iff {h N L K : ℕ} (hdeep : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + (K : ℤ) + (h : ℤ) + (L : ℤ) + 2) < 2 ^ L) : certifiedKill h N (L + K) ↔ ∃ j ≤ K, certifiedKill h (N + j) L
