declarations.docstring: **The window law, both directions.** Below the doubling threshold, a depth-`L+K` certificate at base `N` is exactly a depth-`L` certificate somewhere on the free-`N` walk `N, …, N+K`. The `←` direction is `AngleA2.certifiedKill_of_window_subset` and needs no hypothesis; the `→` direction is `exists_certifiedKill_shift`.

declarations.name: ConsecutiveFail
declarations.signature: def ConsecutiveFail (h N L K : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: `ConsecutiveFail h N L K`: the `K+1` cells `(N, L), (N+1, L), …, (N+K, L)` all fail to certify — a run of `K+1` consecutive failures along the free base point.

declarations.name: consecutiveFail_of_deep_fail
declarations.signature: theorem consecutiveFail_of_deep_fail {h N L K : ℕ} (hfail : ¬ certifiedKill h N (L + K)) : ConsecutiveFail h N L K
declarations.docstring: **Long runs come from one deep failure.** Hypothesis-free direction: a single failure at `(N, L+K)` produces `K+1` consecutive failures along `N` at depth `L`.

declarations.name: deep_fail_of_consecutiveFail
declarations.signature: theorem deep_fail_of_consecutiveFail {h N L K : ℕ} (hdeep : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + (K : ℤ) + (h : ℤ) + (L : ℤ) + 2) < 2 ^ L) (hrun : ConsecutiveFail h N L K) : ¬ certifiedKill h N (L + K)
declarations.docstring: **Runs are no longer than that.** Below the doubling threshold, `K+1` consecutive failures force the single deep failure back.

declarations.name: consecutiveFail_iff
declarations.signature: theorem consecutiveFail_iff {h N L K : ℕ} (hdeep : 4 * ((N : ℤ) + (K : ℤ) + (h : ℤ) + (L : ℤ) + 2) < 2 ^ L) : ConsecutiveFail h N L K ↔ ¬ certifiedKill h N (L + K)
declarations.docstring: **The run law.** `K+1` consecutive failures along the free `N` at depth `L` *is* a single failure at depth `L+K`. Consequently the run of failures starting at `N` has length exactly `Lmin(h,N) − L`, where `Lmin(h,N)` is the least certifying depth at base `N`: the free-`N` walk is the depth ladder in disguise.

declarations.name: forall_consecutiveFail_iff
declarations.signature: theorem forall_consecutiveFail_iff {h N L : ℕ} : (∀ K, ConsecutiveFail h N L K) ↔ ∀ j, ¬ certifiedKill h (N + j) L
declarations.docstring: An unending run at depth `L` from base `N` is exactly the failure of the whole free-`N` walk at that depth. Note the depth hypothesis of `consecutiveFail_iff` degrades as `K` grows at fixed `L`, so this equivalence is the honest unconditional one: it does *not* upgrade to `∀ K, ¬ certifiedKill h N (L+K)`.

declarations.name: fail_26_3_19
declarations.docstring: The deep failure behind the `h = 26` run.

declarations.name: depth_seven_nondegenerate
declarations.docstring: Depth `7` is live at `(h, N) = (26, 3)`: the floor of `certifiedKill_depth_floor` is cleared with room to spare.

declarations.name: freeWalk_run_13
declarations.docstring: **Thirteen consecutive failures** along the free `N`, at period `h = 26` and depth `L = 7`: bases `N = 3, 4, …, 15`.

declarations.name: freeWalk_run_13_sharp
declarations.docstring: The run ends: base `16` certifies at the same depth `7`.

declarations.name: fail_22_4518_32
declarations.docstring: The deep failure behind the `h = 22` runs; `Lmin(22, 4518) = 33`.

declarations.name: depth_fourteen_nondegenerate
declarations.docstring: Depth `14` is live at `(h, N) = (22, 4518)`.

declarations.name: freeWalk_run_19
declarations.docstring: **Nineteen consecutive failures** along the free `N`, at period `h = 22` and depth `L = 14`: bases `N = 4518, …, 4536`. Depth `14` is the certificate's own floor at this scale, and it is live — `freeWalk_run_19_sharp` certifies at `4537`.

declarations.name: freeWalk_run_19_sharp
declarations.docstring: The run ends: base `4537` certifies at depth `14`.

declarations.name: freeWalk_run_19_exact
declarations.docstring: The `h = 22`, `L = 14` run is exactly `19` long.

declarations.name: freeWalk_run_17
declarations.docstring: **Seventeen consecutive failures**, same period, at depth `L = 16` — where the doubling threshold `4·(N+K+h+L+2) < 2^L` *does* hold, so `consecutiveFail_iff` applies and the run length `17` is exactly `Lmin(22,4518) − 16 = 33 − 16`.

declarations.name: freeWalk_run_17_threshold
declarations.docstring: The doubling threshold holds for `freeWalk_run_17`, so that run is governed by the two-sided law `consecutiveFail_iff`.

declarations.name: freeWalk_run_17_sharp
declarations.docstring: …and it is exactly `17` long: base `4535` certifies at depth `16`.

declarations.name: freeWalk_run_17_exact
declarations.docstring: The exact form of the previous three: at `(h, L) = (22, 16)` and base `4518` the run of consecutive failures has length exactly `17`, established through the two-sided law rather than by enumeration.

declarations.name: no_small_absolute_run_bound
declarations.signature: theorem no_small_absolute_run_bound : (2 * ((3 : ℤ) + 26 + 7 + 2) < 2 ^ 7 ∧ ConsecutiveFail 26 3 7 12) ∧ (4 * ((4518 : ℤ) + 16 + 22 + 16 + 2) < 2 ^ 16 ∧ ConsecutiveFail 22 4518 16 16) ∧ (2 * ((4518 : ℤ) + 22 + 14 + 2) < 2 ^ 14 ∧ ConsecutiveFail 22 4518 14 18)
declarations.docstring: **The negative, as a statement.** For each `K ∈ {12, 16, 18}` there is a period `h`, a base `N` and a depth `L` clearing the depth floor `2(N+h+L+2) < 2^L` at which `K+1` consecutive bases all fail. No absolute bound on run length is proved here, and by `consecutiveFail_iff` any such bound `K` would be the assertion that the least certifying depth never exceeds the floor by more than `K` — a quantitative statement about `∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ` strictly stronger than Erdős #249.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_split
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_split (h N k L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy h N (k + L) = 2 ^ L * windowDiscrepancy h N k + windowDiscrepancy h (N + k) L
declarations.docstring: **Split identity.** A depth-`(k+L)` window at base `N` is exactly `2^L` times the depth-`k` window at base `N` plus the depth-`L` window at base `N + k`. `AngleA3.windowDiscrepancy_emod_pow` records only that `2^L` divides the head. Here the head is identified: it is itself a window discrepancy. So deepening and sliding are the same operation seen at two place values, and the `N`-walk carries no information beyond the single deep window at the fixed base.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_slide_emod
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_slide_emod (h N k L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy h N (k + L) % 2 ^ L = windowDiscrepancy h (N + k) L % 2 ^ L
declarations.docstring: The `N`-walk at depth `L` reads exactly the low `L` bits of the deepening at the fixed base `N`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_walk_iff
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_walk_iff (h N k L : ℕ) : certifiedKill h (N + k) L ↔ ((N : ℤ) + k + h + L + 2 < windowDiscrepancy h N (k + L) % 2 ^ L ∧ windowDiscrepancy h N (k + L) % 2 ^ L < 2 ^ L - ((N : ℤ) + k + h + L + 2))
declarations.docstring: **The walk in closed form.** Every cell the free-`N` walk visits is a window on the single integer `windowDiscrepancy h N (k+L)`; only the exclusion radius moves.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_descend
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_descend {h M N L : ℕ} (hMN : M ≤ N) (hcert : certifiedKill h N L) : certifiedKill h M (L + (N - M))
declarations.docstring: **Descent with an explicit depth price.** A certificate at base `N` and depth `L` gives a certificate at every smaller base `M`, at depth `L + (N − M)`: one extra unit of depth per unit of base descended. This is `Lift.AngleA3.certifiedKill_of_endpoint'` written in walk coordinates; `AngleA4.exists_certifiedKill_antitone` is the same statement with the depth left unquantified.

declarations.name: base_descent_not_free
declarations.docstring: **The depth price of §2 is sharp.** Base descent is not free: `certifiedKill 1 2 5` holds and `certifiedKill 1 1 5` fails. So the `+1` depth per unit of base in `certifiedKill_descend` cannot be removed.

declarations.name: base_descent_repaired
declarations.docstring: What the transfer does deliver at the same cell: one more unit of depth repairs it.

declarations.name: walk_run_transfers
declarations.signature: theorem walk_run_transfers {h N L K : ℕ} (hKL : K ≤ L) (hrun : ∀ k ≤ K, ¬ certifiedKill h (N + k) L) : ∀ k ≤ K, ¬ certifiedKill h (N + L) k
declarations.docstring: **A last-cell transfer, stated for a run.** If the free-`N` walk at depth `L` fails at the `K+1` base points `N, …, N+K` (with `K ≤ L`), then the *depth* walk at the fixed base point `N + L` fails at every depth up to `K`. The proof uses only the failure at `N+K`; the other `K` failures are decorative. The relevant cells share the right endpoint `N + K + L`, and the conclusion is the contrapositive of the existing anti-diagonal transfer. It is not a two-sided description of a run. **Vacuity, stated plainly.** The conclusion `¬ certifiedKill h (N+L) k` is automatic from `certifiedKill_depth_floor` whenever `2(N+L+h+k+2) ≥ 2^k`, i.e. whenever `k ≲ log₂ N`. So this transfer has content only for runs *longer* than `log₂` of their own base point. Applied to `failure_run_seven` (`h = 3`, `N = 64`, `L = 12`, `K = 6`) it is **vacuous**: `k ≤ 6` and `2^6 = 64 < 2·(64+12+3+6+2)`. **MEASURED, NOT PROVED HERE.** A search reported the following non-vacuous instance; this file neither verifies it no

declarations.name: ascent_witness
declarations.docstring: A genuine certificate at base `63`, depth `8`, shift `3`.

declarations.name: ascent_blocked
declarations.docstring: The very next base point has no certificate at depth `18`.

declarations.name: no_bounded_ascent_law
declarations.signature: theorem no_bounded_ascent_law (b : ℕ) (hb : b ≤ 10) : certifiedKill 3 63 8 ∧ ¬ certifiedKill 3 64 (8 + b)
declarations.docstring: **No bounded-budget ascent law.** There is no `b ≤ 10` for which `certifiedKill h N L → certifiedKill h (N+1) (L+b)`: the cell `(h,N,L) = (3,63,8)` carries a certificate and its successor base point carries none at any depth up to `18`. Since `certifiedKill` is upward closed in depth (`certifiedKill_add`), a single failure at depth `18` kills every smaller depth at once. Walking one step *up* in the base point therefore costs at least `11` extra depth at this cell — and nothing in the corpus bounds that cost anywhere.

declarations.name: failure_run_seven
declarations.signature: theorem failure_run_seven : ∀ k ∈ Finset.range 7, ¬ certifiedKill 3 (64 + k) 12
declarations.docstring: **A run of seven.** At shift `3` and depth `12` the walk fails at seven consecutive base points. The exclusion radius there is at most `87` inside the modulus `2^12 = 4096`, so the failure zone occupies about `4.2%` of the circle: this is not a boundary artefact of a saturated radius, it is the walk genuinely sitting in a thin zone seven steps running.

declarations.name: failure_run_seven_bracketed
declarations.docstring: The run of `failure_run_seven` is exactly seven: certificates on both sides.

declarations.name: not_certifiedKill_of_pow_le
declarations.signature: theorem not_certifiedKill_of_pow_le {h N L : ℕ} (hN : 2 ^ L ≤ N) : ¬ certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: Beyond `2^L` the exclusion radius swallows the whole circle: no certificate at depth `L` can exist at a base point that large.

declarations.name: free_walk_run_unbounded
declarations.signature: theorem free_walk_run_unbounded (h L K : ℕ) : ∀ k ≤ K, ¬ certifiedKill h (2 ^ L + k) L
declarations.docstring: **No absolute run bound.** For every shift `h`, every depth `L` and every length `K`, the `K+1` consecutive base points `2^L, …, 2^L + K` are all failures. So the brief's "absolute bound `K` on consecutive failures" is false as stated; any true bound must be conditioned on `N` being small relative to `2^L`.

declarations.name: not_certifiedKill_zero_shift
declarations.signature: theorem not_certifiedKill_zero_shift (N L : ℕ) : ¬ certifiedKill 0 N L
declarations.docstring: **A run bound must use `h ≥ 1`.** At `h = 0` the window vanishes identically (`Lift.AngleA3.windowDiscrepancy_zero_shift`), so every certificate fails at every base point and every depth: the failure run is infinite. Nothing about the doubling map alone can therefore bound a run.

declarations.name: failure_zone_step_invariant
declarations.signature: theorem failure_zone_step_invariant (r β : ℤ) (hβ : |β| ≤ r) : ∃ δ : ℤ, |δ| ≤ r ∧ |2 * β + δ| ≤ r
declarations.docstring: **A pure integer cancellation allowed by the crude size bound.** For any `β` in an interval of radius `r`, the choice `δ = −β` obeys `|δ| ≤ r` and leaves `2β + δ` in the same interval. This statement has no arithmetic content: it mentions neither `Nat.totient` nor `windowDiscrepancy` nor `certifiedKill`. In particular, it does not prove that the actual totient step can make this choice. It shows only that a model which retains the size bound and otherwise treats `δ` as free cannot exclude one-step persistence by interval expansion alone.

declarations.name: evenFloor
declarations.docstring: `evenFloor n = 2⌊n/2⌋`: a comparison function. It is even, monotone, unbounded, and satisfies the crude bound `0 ≤ f n ≤ n`. It does not satisfy all totient properties used elsewhere in the free-walk analysis.

declarations.name: evenFloor_le
declarations.signature: theorem evenFloor_le (n : ℕ) : evenFloor n ≤ n
declarations.docstring: The surrogate obeys `φ`'s size bound.

declarations.name: le_evenFloor_succ
declarations.signature: theorem le_evenFloor_succ (n : ℕ) : n ≤ evenFloor n + 1
declarations.docstring: The comparison function is within one of the identity.

declarations.name: evenFloor_even
declarations.docstring: The surrogate is even, as `φ n` is for `n ≥ 3`.

declarations.name: abs_evenDelta_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_evenDelta_le (h n : ℕ) : |((evenFloor (n + h) : ℤ) - (evenFloor n : ℤ))| ≤ ((n + h : ℕ) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The comparison function satisfies the analogue of the crude bound `abs_deltaTotient_le`.

declarations.name: evenFloor_shift
declarations.signature: theorem evenFloor_shift {h : ℕ} (hh : 2 ∣ h) (n : ℕ) : evenFloor (n + h) = evenFloor n + h
declarations.docstring: An even shift translates the surrogate exactly.

declarations.name: evenWindow
declarations.signature: def evenWindow (h N L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The surrogate window discrepancy, verbatim the definition of `windowDiscrepancy` with `φ` replaced by `evenFloor`.

declarations.name: evenKill
declarations.signature: def evenKill (h N L : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The surrogate certificate, verbatim the definition of `certifiedKill`.

declarations.name: sum_two_pow_reflect
declarations.signature: private lemma sum_two_pow_reflect (n : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, (2 : ℤ) ^ (n - 1 - j) = 2 ^ n - 1

declarations.name: evenWindow_eq
declarations.signature: theorem evenWindow_eq {h : ℕ} (hh : 2 ∣ h) (N L : ℕ) : evenWindow h N L = (h : ℤ) * (2 ^ L - 1)
declarations.docstring: **The surrogate window in closed form.** For an even shift, every coefficient is `h`, so the window is `h·(2^L − 1)`.

declarations.name: not_evenKill
declarations.signature: theorem not_evenKill {h : ℕ} (hh : 2 ∣ h) (hpos : 0 < h) (N L : ℕ) : ¬ evenKill h N L
declarations.docstring: **The no-go.** For every even `h > 0` the surrogate certificate fails at *every* base point and *every* depth. `evenFloor` satisfies the crude size bound `abs_evenDelta_le` and is even, monotone and unbounded. Thus a proof of a bound on consecutive failures that uses only the recurrence `A_{N+1} ≡ 2A_N + δ_N` and this size bound cannot be valid for every function in that model. This countermodel says nothing about arguments using sharper totient properties: for example, `evenFloor 4 = 4` violates `φ(n) < n` for `n > 1`, and `evenFloor 1 = 0` does not model the lower bound used by `FreeWalk1`.

declarations.name: InHalfZone
declarations.docstring: The half zone at seam length `s`: rank `d` is above `s / 2` but not above `2 * s / 3`. Exactly the ranks the two-thirds identities miss.

declarations.name: InHalfZone.two_le
declarations.signature: theorem InHalfZone.two_le {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : 2 ≤ d

declarations.name: InHalfZone.half
declarations.signature: theorem InHalfZone.half {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : s < 2 * d

declarations.name: InHalfZone.third
declarations.signature: theorem InHalfZone.third {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : 3 * d ≤ 2 * s

declarations.name: InHalfZone.three_le_s
declarations.signature: theorem InHalfZone.three_le_s {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : 3 ≤ s

declarations.name: InHalfZone.lt
declarations.signature: theorem InHalfZone.lt {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : d < s

declarations.name: inHalfZone_or_late_of_half
declarations.signature: theorem inHalfZone_or_late_of_half {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hhalf : s < 2 * d) : InHalfZone s d ∨ 2 * s < 3 * d
declarations.docstring: The half zone and the two-thirds zone together are the `s < 2 * d` region: this is why they are the only two cases of `LargestSkipHalfAt`.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_eq_threeTerm_of_halfRank
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_eq_threeTerm_of_halfRank {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : truncatedMersenneWeight s d = 2 ^ (2 * s - d) + 4 ^ (s - d) + 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d)
declarations.docstring: **Quotient-three weight identity.** In the half zone `s/2 < d ≤ 2s/3` Euclidean division of `2 * s` by `d` has quotient exactly three, so the truncated Mersenne weight has exactly three power terms. This is the three-term analogue of `truncatedMersenneWeight_eq_twoPower_add_fourPower_of_lateRank`.

declarations.name: seven_mul_cubeSuffixSum_add_boundary
declarations.signature: theorem seven_mul_cubeSuffixSum_add_boundary (s d T : ℕ) (hdT : d ≤ T) (hT : 3 * T ≤ 2 * s) : 7 * (∑ e ∈ Finset.Ico (d + 1) (T + 1), 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * e)) + 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * T) = 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d)
declarations.docstring: Division-free base-eight telescope: the descending cube powers over the half-zone part of the strict suffix.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_sum_halfZone
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_sum_halfZone {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum = ((∑ e ∈ Finset.Ico (d + 1) s, 2 ^ (2 * s - e)) + ∑ e ∈ Finset.Ico (d + 1) s, 4 ^ (s - e)) + ∑ e ∈ Finset.Ico (d + 1) ((2 * s) / 3 + 1), 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * e)
declarations.docstring: The strict suffix above a half-zone rank splits at `⌊2s/3⌋`: below that cut the ranks are still half-zone (three power terms), above it they are two-thirds-zone (two power terms). The result is the late two-column sum plus one extra base-eight column carried only by the half-zone part.

declarations.name: halfGapCorrection
declarations.docstring: The correction term of the exact half-zone adjacent gap: the analogue of the late correction `2 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 4`, scaled by seven. Dividing the whole gap by `21` gives `2 ^ (s+1) + (2 * 4 ^ (s-d) + 4)/3 + (6 * 2 ^ (2s-3d) + 2 ^ (2s mod 3))/7`.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_tailWeight_add_exactHalfGap
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_mul_tailWeight_add_exactHalfGap {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : 21 * (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum + (21 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + halfGapCorrection s d) = 21 * truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: **Exact half-zone adjacent-gap identity**, stated without division. This is the analogue of `three_mul_tailWeight_add_exactLateGap_eq_three_mul_headWeight`, with the scale `3` replaced by `21 = 3 * 7`.

declarations.name: halfGapCorrection_lt_twentyOne_mul_gap
declarations.signature: theorem halfGapCorrection_lt_twentyOne_mul_gap {s d : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (h : InHalfZone s d) : halfGapCorrection s d < 21 * 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: The half-zone correction is strictly smaller than one further scaled dyadic gap. This is the analogue of `exactLateGap_correction_lt_three_mul_gap`.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_largestSkipLowerWeight_add_exactHalfGap_eq_upperWeight
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_mul_largestSkipLowerWeight_add_exactHalfGap_eq_upperWeight {s d : ℕ} {u : Finset ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) (hu : ∀ e ∈ u, 2 ≤ e ∧ e < d) : 21 * wordWeightSum s (largestSkipLowerWord s d u).toNatWord + (21 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + halfGapCorrection s d) = 21 * wordWeightSum s (largestSkipUpperWord s d u).toNatWord
declarations.docstring: Exact half-zone adjacent word gap, including an arbitrary common lower prefix. Analogue of `three_mul_largestSkipLowerWeight_add_exactLateGap_eq_upperWeight`.

declarations.name: seamAdjacentCut_above_eq_largestSkipUpperWord_of_halfZone
declarations.signature: theorem seamAdjacentCut_above_eq_largestSkipUpperWord_of_halfZone {s d : ℕ} {u : Finset ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (h : InHalfZone s d) (hu : ∀ e ∈ u, 2 ≤ e ∧ e < d) (hsupp : seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s) = u ∪ Finset.Ico (d + 1) s) : (seamAdjacentCut s hs).above = largestSkipUpperWord s d u
declarations.docstring: At a half-zone largest false rank, the actual upper adjacent word is the explicit largest-skip upper word. Analogue of `seamAdjacentCut_above_eq_largestSkipUpperWord_of_support`.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_remainder_add_overshoot_eq_exactHalfGap
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_mul_remainder_add_overshoot_eq_exactHalfGap {s d : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hd : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d) (h : InHalfZone s d) : 21 * ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder + (seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot) = 21 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + halfGapCorrection s d
declarations.docstring: **The exact half-zone adjacent gap of the actual seam cut.** This is the half-zone analogue of `three_mul_remainder_add_overshoot_eq_exactLateGap`. Dividing by `21`, the gap is `2 ^ (s+1) + (2 * 4 ^ (s-d) + 4)/3 + (6 * 2 ^ (2s-3d) + 2 ^ (2s mod 3))/7`.

declarations.name: twentyOne_dvd_halfGapCorrection
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_dvd_halfGapCorrection {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : 21 ∣ halfGapCorrection s d
declarations.docstring: The half-zone correction is a multiple of `21`, so the gap identity does divide exactly. Consequently **no contradiction can be extracted from divisibility by `21`** (or by `3`, or by `7`): the correction is congruent to zero for every half-zone rank, unconditionally.

declarations.name: skipHalfGapCorrection
declarations.docstring: The exact adjacent-gap correction, at scale `21`, on the whole `s < 2 * d` region. The two-thirds branch is the corpus's late correction `2 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 4` scaled by seven; the half branch is `halfGapCorrection`.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_remainder_add_overshoot_eq_skipHalfGap
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_mul_remainder_add_overshoot_eq_skipHalfGap {s d : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hd : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d) (hhalf : s < 2 * d) : 21 * ((seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder + (seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot) = 21 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + skipHalfGapCorrection s d
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional exact adjacent gap for every half-late largest false rank.** This is the union of the corpus's two-thirds identity with the half-zone identity proved above; together they cover all of `SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt`.

declarations.name: skipHalfGapCorrection_pos_and_lt
declarations.signature: theorem skipHalfGapCorrection_pos_and_lt {s d : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hhalf : s < 2 * d) : 0 < skipHalfGapCorrection s d ∧ skipHalfGapCorrection s d < 21 * 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: The combined correction is positive and below one further scaled gap.

declarations.name: gap_strictly_between_of_largestSkipHalf
declarations.signature: theorem gap_strictly_between_of_largestSkipHalf {s d : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hd : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d) (hhalf : s < 2 * d) : 2 ^ (s + 1) < (seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder + (seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot ∧ (seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder + (seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot < 2 ^ (s + 2)
declarations.docstring: **The adjacent gap of a half-late row sits strictly between one and two dyadic gaps.** A sharp, correction-free consequence of the two identities.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_overshoot_add_fortyTwo_eq_skipHalfGap
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_mul_overshoot_add_fortyTwo_eq_skipHalfGap {s d : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hd : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d) (hhalf : s < 2 * d) (hland : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2) : 21 * (seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot + 42 = skipHalfGapCorrection s d
declarations.docstring: Under the `seamExcess = 2` landing constraint the whole gap identity collapses onto the overshoot alone. This is the exact form the surviving `SkipD1` branch has to contradict.

declarations.name: landing_forces_correction_window
declarations.signature: theorem landing_forces_correction_window {s d : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hd : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d) (hhalf : s < 2 * d) (hland : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2) : 42 ≤ skipHalfGapCorrection s d ∧ skipHalfGapCorrection s d < 21 * 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: The landing constraint forces the correction into the window `[42, 21 * 2 ^ (s+1))`.

declarations.name: le_halfGapCorrection
declarations.signature: theorem le_halfGapCorrection {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : 105 ≤ halfGapCorrection s d
declarations.docstring: **The size route is dead.** The lower end of the landing window is met automatically: every half-zone correction already exceeds `105 > 42`, with no hypothesis on the row at all. Combined with `halfGapCorrection_lt_twentyOne_mul_gap` for the upper end, this says `landing_forces_correction_window` is vacuously satisfied — the landing constraint extracts no size contradiction from a half-zone rank.

declarations.name: landing_congruence_is_trivial
declarations.signature: theorem landing_congruence_is_trivial {s d : ℕ} (h : InHalfZone s d) : halfGapCorrection s d % 21 = 0
declarations.docstring: Likewise the `21`-divisibility route is dead: the correction is a multiple of `21` for every half-zone rank, so reducing the landing identity `21 * overshoot + 42 = halfGapCorrection s d` modulo `21`, `7` or `3` produces `0 = 0`.

declarations.name: isLargestFalseRank_eleven_seven
declarations.docstring: `7` is the largest false rank of the greedy seam word at `s = 11`.

declarations.name: inHalfZone_eleven_seven
declarations.docstring: And that rank is in the half zone, not the two-thirds zone.

declarations.name: seamAdjacentCut_gap_eleven
declarations.docstring: The hypotheses of the half-zone gap identity are satisfiable, and the identity pins the adjacent gap at `s = 11` to the exact value `4270`.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_eq_threeTerm_of_halfRank
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_eq_threeTerm_of_halfRank {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hhalf : 2 * s < 4 * d) (hnotlate : 3 * d ≤ 2 * s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s d = 2 ^ (2 * s - d) + 4 ^ (s - d) + 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d)
declarations.docstring: In the half zone `s/2 < d ≤ 2s/3` Euclidean division of `2 * s` by `d` has quotient exactly three, so the truncated Mersenne weight has three power terms.

declarations.name: seven_mul_threePowerSuffixSum_add_boundary
declarations.signature: theorem seven_mul_threePowerSuffixSum_add_boundary (s m d : ℕ) (hm : 3 * m ≤ 2 * s) (hdm : d ≤ m) : 7 * (∑ e ∈ Finset.Ico (d + 1) (m + 1), 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * e)) + 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * m) = 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d)
declarations.docstring: The third-order correction powers telescope with ratio eight. This is the half-zone analogue of `three_mul_fourPowerSuffixSum_add_four`.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_sum_eq_threeTerm_of_halfRank
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_sum_eq_threeTerm_of_halfRank {s d m : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hhalf : 2 * s < 4 * d) (hnotlate : 3 * d ≤ 2 * s) (hm3 : 3 * m ≤ 2 * s) (hmtop : 2 * s < 3 * (m + 1)) : (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum = (∑ e ∈ Finset.Ico (d + 1) s, 2 ^ (2 * s - e)) + (∑ e ∈ Finset.Ico (d + 1) s, 4 ^ (s - e)) + ∑ e ∈ Finset.Ico (d + 1) (m + 1), 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * e)
declarations.docstring: In the half zone the whole strict suffix splits into the two late-zone telescopes plus a third-order correction supported on `(d, 2s/3]`.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_tailWeight_add_exactHalfGap_eq_twentyOne_mul_headWeight
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_mul_tailWeight_add_exactHalfGap_eq_twentyOne_mul_headWeight {s d m : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hhalf : 2 * s < 4 * d) (hnotlate : 3 * d ≤ 2 * s) (hm3 : 3 * m ≤ 2 * s) (hmtop : 2 * s < 3 * (m + 1)) : 21 * (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum + (21 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 14 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 18 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d) + 3 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * m) + 28) = 21 * truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: **The half-zone adjacent-gap identity.** The corpus records the exact gap only in the late zone `2s < 3d`, where the weight has two power terms. In the half zone `s/2 < d ≤ 2s/3` the weight has three terms, and the gap acquires a third telescope with ratio eight. Dividing by `21` this reads `gap = 2^(s+1) + (2*4^(s-d) + 4)/3 + (6*2^(2s-3d) + 2^(2s mod 3))/7`. The statement is division-free.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_tailWeight_add_exactHalfGap_eq_twentyOne_mul_headWeight_floor
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_mul_tailWeight_add_exactHalfGap_eq_twentyOne_mul_headWeight_floor {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hhalf : 2 * s < 4 * d) (hnotlate : 3 * d ≤ 2 * s) : 21 * (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum + (21 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 14 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 18 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d) + 3 * 2 ^ (2 * s % 3) + 28) = 21 * truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: The same identity with the third-order boundary written out: `m` is `⌊2s/3⌋`, so `2 * s - 3 * m` is `2 * s % 3`, a value in `{0, 1, 2}`.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_largestSkipLowerWeight_add_exactHalfGap_eq_upperWeight
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_mul_largestSkipLowerWeight_add_exactHalfGap_eq_upperWeight {s d m : ℕ} {u : Finset ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hu : ∀ e ∈ u, 2 ≤ e ∧ e < d) (hhalf : 2 * s < 4 * d) (hnotlate : 3 * d ≤ 2 * s) (hm3 : 3 * m ≤ 2 * s) (hmtop : 2 * s < 3 * (m + 1)) : 21 * wordWeightSum s (largestSkipLowerWord s d u).toNatWord + (21 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 14 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 18 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d) + 3 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * m) + 28) = 21 * wordWeightSum s (largestSkipUpperWord s d u).toNatWord
declarations.docstring: Exact half-rank adjacent word gap, including an arbitrary common lower prefix. This is the half-zone counterpart of `three_mul_largestSkipLowerWeight_add_exactLateGap_eq_upperWeight`.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_remainder_lt_exactHalfGap
declarations.signature: theorem twentyOne_mul_remainder_lt_exactHalfGap {s d m : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hd : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d) (hhalf : 2 * s < 4 * d) (hnotlate : 3 * d ≤ 2 * s) (hm3 : 3 * m ≤ 2 * s) (hmtop : 2 * s < 3 * (m + 1)) : 21 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 21 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 14 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 18 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d) + 3 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * m) + 28
declarations.docstring: **The half-zone strip invariant.** At a largest false rank lying in the half zone `s/2 < d ≤ 2s/3` the greedy remainder is strictly below the exact adjacent gap. This is the half-zone counterpart of `three_mul_remainder_lt_exactLateGap`, and it is the sharpest magnitude constraint the hypothesis `LargestSkipHalfAt s` can produce.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_pred_eq_two_mul_landing
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_pred_eq_two_mul_landing {s : ℕ} (hs : 4 ≤ s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s (s - 1) = 2 * (2 ^ s + 2)
declarations.docstring: The smallest weight in row `s` is **exactly twice** the landing remainder `2^s + 2` of a `-2` final middle cell.

declarations.name: landing_add_tailWeight_lt_truncatedWeight
declarations.signature: theorem landing_add_tailWeight_lt_truncatedWeight {s d : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) : (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum + (2 ^ s + 2) < truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: **The core no-go.** For every rank `d` of every row `s ≥ 2`, the landing remainder `2^s + 2` lies strictly below the exact adjacent gap at `d`. The slack is `2^s - 2`, so the inequality is never tight. Consequently the magnitude constraint carried by *any* largest false rank — `remainder + tail < weight`, the sharp form proved above — is implied by the landing value alone. It separates no rank from any other, and in particular cannot refute `(s/2 < d)`.

declarations.name: landing_lt_truncatedWeight
declarations.signature: theorem landing_lt_truncatedWeight {s d : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) : 2 ^ s + 2 < truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: The same statement without the tail: the landing remainder is below *every* weight of its row.

declarations.name: landing_satisfies_exactLateGap_strip
declarations.signature: theorem landing_satisfies_exactLateGap_strip {s d : ℕ} (hR : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = 2 ^ s + 2) : 3 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + (3 * 2 ^ s + 2 * 4 ^ (s - d)) = 3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 4 + 2
declarations.docstring: **Late zone.** At the landing value the corpus's late strip invariant `three_mul_remainder_lt_exactLateGap` holds identically, with exact slack `3 * 2^s + 2 * 4^(s-d) - 2`. No late rank is excluded.

declarations.name: landing_satisfies_exactHalfGap_strip
declarations.signature: theorem landing_satisfies_exactHalfGap_strip {s d m : ℕ} (hR : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = 2 ^ s + 2) : 21 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + (21 * 2 ^ s + 14 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 18 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d) + 3 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * m)) = 21 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 14 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 18 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * d) + 3 * 2 ^ (2 * s - 3 * m) + 28 + 14
declarations.docstring: **Half zone.** At the landing value the half strip invariant proved above holds identically, with exact slack `21 * 2^s + 14 * 4^(s-d) + 18 * 2^(2s-3d) + 3 * 2^(2s-3m) - 14`. No half-zone rank is excluded either.

declarations.name: isLargestFalseRank_thirteen_seven
declarations.docstring: Row `13` skips rank `7`, and nothing above it.

declarations.name: thirteen_seven_halfZone
declarations.docstring: Rank `7` of row `13` sits in the **half but not late** zone `13/2 < 7 ≤ 26/3`, where the weight has three power terms. So the three-term regime is genuinely occupied by the concrete greedy: the identities above are not about an empty case.

declarations.name: twentyOne_mul_remainder_thirteen_lt_exactHalfGap
declarations.docstring: The half-zone strip invariant, instantiated at a row where its hypotheses actually hold.

declarations.name: isLargestFalseRank_sixtyOne_sixty
declarations.docstring: Row `61` — the first row of `SkipD1`'s dichotomy — skips rank `60`.

declarations.name: largestSkipHalfAt_sixtyOne
declarations.docstring: **`LargestSkipHalfAt` is not refutable.** It holds at row `61`, the first row of `SkipD1.cofRanks_subset_or_largestSkipHalfAt`, and at row `13`. Direct computation of the integer seam greedy finds the largest false rank strictly above `s / 2` at *every* row `5 ≤ s ≤ 400`, so the inequality this angle was asked to refute is, as far as computation reaches, simply true.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_eq_of_seamExcess_eq_two
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_eq_of_seamExcess_eq_two {s : ℕ} (h : Recon257.seamExcess s = 2) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = 2 ^ s + 2
declarations.docstring: The landing constraint in remainder form.

declarations.name: landingRow_magnitude_consistent
declarations.signature: theorem landingRow_magnitude_consistent (D : ℕ) (hD : 1 ≤ D) (hlanding : Recon257.seamExcess (D + 1) = 2) {d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hds : d < D + 1) : (seamWeightsFrom (D + 1) (d + 1)).sum + seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (D + 1) < truncatedMersenneWeight (D + 1) d
declarations.docstring: **The H2 verdict.** Assume the landing constraint `Recon257.seamExcess (D+1) = 2`. Then the sharp magnitude constraint that a largest false rank imposes — greedy remainder plus the whole strict suffix weight stays under the skipped weight — holds at **every** rank `d` of the landing row, with no hypothesis on `d` beyond `1 ≤ d < D + 1`. So magnitudes cannot single out any rank at all, and in particular cannot refute `(D+1)/2 < d₀`. The reason is structural: the seam weight word is `2^(s+1)`-gap-dominating (`truncatedMersenneWeight_dominanceGap`), and the landing remainder `2^s + 2` is exactly **half** the smallest weight of the row (`truncatedMersenneWeight_pred_eq_two_mul_landing`), hence below every adjacent gap by a margin of at least `2^s - 2`. This closes angle H2 negatively.

declarations.name: landingRow_satisfies_exactLateGap_strip
declarations.signature: theorem landingRow_satisfies_exactLateGap_strip (D : ℕ) (hlanding : Recon257.seamExcess (D + 1) = 2) (d : ℕ) : 3 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (D + 1) < 3 * 2 ^ (D + 1 + 1) + 2 * 4 ^ (D + 1 - d) + 4
declarations.docstring: The late strip invariant is a consequence of the landing constraint alone: it holds for every `d`, so it excludes nothing.

declarations.name: landingRow_satisfies_exactHalfGap_strip
declarations.signature: theorem landingRow_satisfies_exactHalfGap_strip (D : ℕ) (hlanding : Recon257.seamExcess (D + 1) = 2) (d m : ℕ) : 21 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (D + 1) < 21 * 2 ^ (D + 1 + 1) + 14 * 4 ^ (D + 1 - d) + 18 * 2 ^ (2 * (D + 1) - 3 * d) + 3 * 2 ^ (2 * (D + 1) - 3 * m) + 28
declarations.docstring: The half strip invariant proved in this file is likewise a consequence of the landing constraint alone, for every `d` and every `m`.

declarations.name: two_dvd_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem two_dvd_two_pow {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) : ∃ k : ℕ, (2 : ℕ) ^ n = 2 * k
declarations.docstring: A positive power of two is twice something.

declarations.name: four_dvd_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem four_dvd_two_pow {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : ∃ k : ℕ, (2 : ℕ) ^ n = 4 * k
declarations.docstring: A power of two with exponent at least two is four times something.

declarations.name: geometricCore_eq_twoPow_mul_add_one
declarations.signature: theorem geometricCore_eq_twoPow_mul_add_one (d : ℕ) {q : ℕ} (hq : 1 ≤ q) : ∃ H : ℕ, (∑ i ∈ Finset.range q, (2 ^ d) ^ i) = 2 ^ d * H + 1
declarations.docstring: The geometric core `∑ i < q, (2^d)^i` is `2^d * H + 1`.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_eq_twoPow_mul_geom
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_eq_twoPow_mul_geom {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d ≤ 2 * s) : ∃ H : ℕ, truncatedMersenneWeight s d = 2 ^ ((2 * s) % d) * (2 ^ d * H + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The valuation law.** The truncated Mersenne weight factors as `2 ^ ((2*s) % d)` times an odd number of the shape `2^d * H + 1`. Its two-adic valuation is therefore exactly `(2 * s) % d`.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_mod_two
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_mod_two {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d ≤ 2 * s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s d % 2 = if d ∣ 2 * s then 1 else 0
declarations.docstring: The weight of rank `d` at row `s` is **odd exactly when `d ∣ 2 * s`**.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_mod_four
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_mod_four {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d ≤ 2 * s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s d % 4 = (if (2 * s) % d = 0 then 1 else if (2 * s) % d = 1 then 2 else 0)
declarations.docstring: The mod-`4` refinement. The weight is `≡ 1` when `d ∣ 2*s`, `≡ 2` when `d ∣ 2*s - 1`, and `≡ 0` otherwise.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_two_mod_two
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_two_mod_two {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 % 2 = 1
declarations.docstring: Rank `2` always carries an odd weight: `2 ∣ 2 * s` for every `s`.

declarations.name: wordWeightSum_add_seamIntegerGreedyRemainder
declarations.signature: theorem wordWeightSum_add_seamIntegerGreedyRemainder {s : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) : wordWeightSum s (seamGreedyWord s).toNatWord + seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: The selected weight sum and the greedy remainder add up to the target.

declarations.name: seamSubsetTarget_mod_two
declarations.signature: theorem seamSubsetTarget_mod_two {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) : seamSubsetTarget s % 2 = 0
declarations.docstring: The seam subset target is even.

declarations.name: sum_seamWordSupport_mod_two
declarations.signature: theorem sum_seamWordSupport_mod_two {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) (b : SeamRowWord s) : (∑ d ∈ seamWordSupport b, truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 2 = ((seamWordSupport b).filter (fun d => d ∣ 2 * s)).card % 2
declarations.docstring: **The support parity law.** Modulo two, the selected weight sum counts the selected ranks that divide `2 * s`.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_mod_two
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_mod_two {s : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s % 2 = ((seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s)).filter (fun d => d ∣ 2 * s)).card % 2
declarations.docstring: **The remainder parity law.** The concrete integer seam greedy remainder is congruent modulo two to the number of selected ranks dividing `2 * s`.

declarations.name: eq_two_of_dvd_two_mul_of_prime
declarations.signature: theorem eq_two_of_dvd_two_mul_of_prime {s d : ℕ} (hp : Nat.Prime s) (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hdvd : d ∣ 2 * s) : d = 2
declarations.docstring: A rank strictly below a **prime** row that divides `2 * s` is `2`.

declarations.name: divisorSelected_prime
declarations.signature: theorem divisorSelected_prime {s : ℕ} (hs : 13 ≤ s) (hp : Nat.Prime s) : (seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s)).filter (fun d => d ∣ 2 * s) = {2}
declarations.docstring: On a prime row the selected ranks dividing `2 * s` are exactly `{2}`.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_odd_of_prime
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_odd_of_prime {s : ℕ} (hs : 13 ≤ s) (hp : Nat.Prime s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s % 2 = 1
declarations.docstring: **Prime rows have an odd greedy remainder.** Unconditional.

declarations.name: seamExcess_ne_two_of_prime
declarations.signature: theorem seamExcess_ne_two_of_prime {s : ℕ} (hs : 13 ≤ s) (hp : Nat.Prime s) : Recon257.seamExcess s ≠ 2
declarations.docstring: On a prime row the greedy remainder is not `2 ^ s + 2`, so the landing excess of a hypothetical `-2` final middle cell cannot occur there.

declarations.name: seamExcess_ne_zero_of_prime
declarations.signature: theorem seamExcess_ne_zero_of_prime {s : ℕ} (hs : 13 ≤ s) (hp : Nat.Prime s) : Recon257.seamExcess s ≠ 0
declarations.docstring: The same for the dyadic half point itself: on a prime row the remainder is never `2 ^ s`, i.e. the excess never vanishes.

declarations.name: finalMiddleCell_neg_two_impossible_of_prime_succ
declarations.signature: theorem finalMiddleCell_neg_two_impossible_of_prime_succ (D : ℕ) (hD : 12 ≤ D) (hp : Nat.Prime (D + 1)) (hncarry : ¬ (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega : 5 ≤ D)).successorCarries) (hmiddle : 4 * (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega : 5 ≤ D)).remainder + (seamPerturbedFamily D (by omega : 3 ≤ D)).gap - (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega : 5 ≤ D)).belowPulse < (seamAdjacentCut D (by omega : 5 ≤ D)).terminalWeight) (hcell : 4 * ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega : 5 ≤ D)).remainder : ℤ) - ((seamAdjacentCut D (by omega : 5 ≤ D)).belowPulse : ℤ) - 4 = -2) : False
declarations.docstring: **The unconditional exclusion.** A hypothetical final middle cell of charge `-2` at rank `D` is impossible whenever `D + 1` is prime. There is no tail hypothesis: neither `hright` nor `hcof` nor any bound `S` appears. Compare `SkipD1.exists_bound_allRight_landingExcess_two_impossible`, which needs both an all-right tail and an ineffective bound.

declarations.name: dvd_two_mul_not_late
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_two_mul_not_late {s d : ℕ} (_hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hdvd : d ∣ 2 * s) : 3 * d ≤ 2 * s
declarations.docstring: Every rank strictly below the row that divides `2 * s` sits at or below two thirds of the row. So no divisor of `2 * s` is ever *late*.

declarations.name: dvd_two_mul_half_eq_cofThree
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_two_mul_half_eq_cofThree {s d : ℕ} (_hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hhalf : s < 2 * d) (hdvd : d ∣ 2 * s) : 3 * d = 2 * s
declarations.docstring: The only divisor of `2 * s` that reaches the half zone at all is the cofactor-`3` rank, which sits exactly on the two-thirds boundary.

declarations.name: dvd_two_mul_sub_one_not_late
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_two_mul_sub_one_not_late {s d : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) (_hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hdvd : d ∣ 2 * s - 1) : 3 * d ≤ 2 * s
declarations.docstring: The same for `2 * s - 1`, the ranks the mod-`4` shadow can see.

declarations.name: four_dvd_truncatedMersenneWeight_of_late
declarations.signature: theorem four_dvd_truncatedMersenneWeight_of_late {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) : 4 ∣ truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: **Late weights are divisible by four.** In the late zone the weight has two power terms `2 ^ (2s-d) + 4 ^ (s-d)`, both of which are multiples of `4`.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_mod_twoPow_of_late
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_mod_twoPow_of_late {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) : truncatedMersenneWeight s d % 2 ^ (s + 1) = 4 ^ (s - d)
declarations.docstring: Sharper: in the late zone the entire low half of the weight is the single power `4 ^ (s - d)`.

declarations.name: four_dvd_lateBlock
declarations.signature: theorem four_dvd_lateBlock {s d₀ : ℕ} (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d₀) : 4 ∣ ∑ d ∈ Finset.Ico (d₀ + 1) s, truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: The block of ranks above a late largest false rank contributes nothing modulo four.

declarations.name: lateBlock_mod_four_indep
declarations.signature: theorem lateBlock_mod_four_indep {s d₀ d₁ : ℕ} (h0 : 2 * s < 3 * d₀) (h1 : 2 * s < 3 * d₁) : (∑ d ∈ Finset.Ico (d₀ + 1) s, truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 4 = (∑ d ∈ Finset.Ico (d₁ + 1) s, truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 4
declarations.docstring: **The blindness statement.** Two different late largest false ranks give exactly the same mod-`4` block contribution, namely `0`.

declarations.name: sum_seamWordSupport_mod_four_of_late
declarations.signature: theorem sum_seamWordSupport_mod_four_of_late {s d₀ : ℕ} {u : Finset ℕ} (_hd2 : 2 ≤ d₀) (_hds : d₀ < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d₀) (hu : ∀ e ∈ u, 2 ≤ e ∧ e < d₀) (hsupp : seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s) = u ∪ Finset.Ico (d₀ + 1) s) : (∑ d ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s), truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 4 = (∑ d ∈ u, truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 4
declarations.docstring: **The mod-`4` shadow of the landing equation lives below two thirds.** If the row has a late largest false rank then the mod-`4` residue of the selected weight sum equals that of the lower prefix alone.

declarations.name: exists_lowerPrefix_sum_mod_four_of_largestSkipLate
declarations.signature: theorem exists_lowerPrefix_sum_mod_four_of_largestSkipLate {s d₀ : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d₀) (hds : d₀ < s) (hmax : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d₀) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d₀) : ∃ u : Finset ℕ, (∀ e ∈ u, 2 ≤ e ∧ e < d₀) ∧ (∑ d ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s), truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 4 = (∑ d ∈ u, truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 4
declarations.docstring: Packaged for the D1 target. Under `IsLargestFalseRank … d₀` with `d₀` late, the mod-`4` content of `seamExcess (D+1) = 2` is a statement about ranks below `d₀` only, so it cannot refute the lateness of `d₀`.

declarations.name: d0Table
declarations.docstring: The measured largest false rank of row `61 + k`, for `k < 440`. Each entry is certified below by `SkipD3.rowChk`, which checks that the rank's greedy bit is off and every greedy bit above it, up to the terminal rank `s-1`, is on.

declarations.name: d0At
declarations.docstring: Lookup into `d0Table`.

declarations.name: rowOk
declarations.docstring: The row certificate: the tabulated rank is a genuine rank, lies within `8` of the row index, is in the two-thirds late zone, and really is the largest false rank of the concrete greedy row.

declarations.name: blockAll
declarations.signature: theorem blockAll : ∀ k ∈ List.range 440, rowOk (61 + k) = true
declarations.docstring: **The kernel check.** All `440` rows `61,…,500` pass.

declarations.name: rowOk_of_block
declarations.signature: theorem rowOk_of_block {s : ℕ} (h1 : 61 ≤ s) (h2 : s ≤ 500) : rowOk s = true

declarations.name: exists_largestFalseRank_of_rowOk
declarations.signature: theorem exists_largestFalseRank_of_rowOk {s : ℕ} (h : rowOk s = true) : ∃ d : ℕ, IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d ∧ s ≤ d + 8 ∧ 2 * s < 3 * d
declarations.docstring: Unpacking a row certificate.

declarations.name: largestFalseRank_near_terminal
declarations.signature: theorem largestFalseRank_near_terminal {s : ℕ} (h1 : 61 ≤ s) (h2 : s ≤ 500) : ∃ d : ℕ, IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d ∧ s ≤ d + 8 ∧ 2 * s < 3 * d
declarations.docstring: **The measurement, kernel-certified.** On every row from `61` to `500` the concrete integer seam greedy has a largest false rank lying within `8` of the row index — and in particular deep inside the two-thirds late zone, hence far above the half boundary `s / 2`.

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_block
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_block {s : ℕ} (h1 : 61 ≤ s) (h2 : s ≤ 500) : LargestSkipLateAt s
declarations.docstring: The two-thirds form.

declarations.name: largestSkipHalfAt_block
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipHalfAt_block {s : ℕ} (h1 : 61 ≤ s) (h2 : s ≤ 500) : SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt s
declarations.docstring: The half form — the exact proposition `SkipD1` leaves as the residue.

declarations.name: highTable
declarations.docstring: Sample rows well beyond the block, with their measured largest false ranks. The rows `546,547,548`, `630,631,632` and `1113,1114,1115` are the three-row `AngleB2` landing windows of the surviving classes `D = 545, 629, 1112`; the rest are spot checks up to `s = 3001`.

declarations.name: highAll
declarations.signature: theorem highAll : ∀ p ∈ highTable, pairOk p = true
declarations.docstring: **The kernel check at scale.** Every sampled high row passes, up to `s = 3001`.

declarations.name: largestFalseRank_near_terminal_high
declarations.signature: theorem largestFalseRank_near_terminal_high {s d : ℕ} (h : (s, d) ∈ highTable) : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d ∧ s ≤ d + 8 ∧ 2 * s < 3 * d

declarations.name: largestSkipLateAt_high
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipLateAt_high {s d : ℕ} (h : (s, d) ∈ highTable) : LargestSkipLateAt s

declarations.name: largestSkipHalfAt_high
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipHalfAt_high {s d : ℕ} (h : (s, d) ∈ highTable) : SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt s

declarations.name: largestSkipHalfAt_3001
declarations.docstring: Explicitly: the largest false rank of row `3001` is `3000`, one below the terminal rank, nowhere near `1500`.

declarations.name: largestSkipHalfAt_survivorWindow
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipHalfAt_survivorWindow {D s : ℕ} (hD : D = 101 ∨ D = 122 ∨ D = 164 ∨ D = 314 ∨ D = 545 ∨ D = 629 ∨ D = 1112) (h1 : D + 1 ≤ s) (h2 : s < D + 4) : SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt s
declarations.docstring: **All twenty-one rows of the seven surviving classes.** `SkipD3` isolates `D = 101, 122, 164, 314, 545, 629, 1112` as the classes below `1370` on which the true below-pulse orbit stays positive to depth `25`. At every row of every one of their three-row `AngleB2` landing windows, the largest false rank sits in the half band. So the half-band residue is live on all seven — it excludes none of them.

declarations.name: largestSkipHalfAt_landingRow
declarations.signature: theorem largestSkipHalfAt_landingRow (D : ℕ) (hD : 60 ≤ D) (hD' : D ≤ 499) : SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt (D + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The residue holds unconditionally on the whole checked block.** For every `D` from `60` to `499`, `SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt (D+1)` is a theorem — with no all-right-tail hypothesis and no landing hypothesis.

declarations.name: no_refutation_on_block
declarations.signature: theorem no_refutation_on_block : ¬ ∃ D : ℕ, 60 ≤ D ∧ D ≤ 499 ∧ ¬ SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt (D + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The target inequality is not refutable.** There is no `D` in the checked range at which `LargestSkipHalfAt (D+1)` fails, so no size or divisibility argument refuting it can be sound on that range.

declarations.name: not_forall_not_largestSkipHalfAt_landingRow
declarations.docstring: The global form: the refutation programme, as a universally quantified statement over all `D ≥ 60`, is false.

declarations.name: allRight_landingRow_conclusion_is_unconditional
declarations.signature: theorem allRight_landingRow_conclusion_is_unconditional (D : ℕ) (hD : 60 ≤ D) (hD' : D ≤ 499) : (∀ _h : (∀ s : ℕ, D + 1 ≤ s → seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true), ∀ _h' : Recon257.seamExcess (D + 1) = 2, SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt (D + 1)) ∧ SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt (D + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The vacuity statement, made formal.** The conclusion of `SkipD1.allRight_landingExcess_two_forces_halfSkip_landingRow` follows from its hypotheses *and also* from nothing at all, on the entire checked range. So on `60 ≤ D ≤ 499` that theorem is exclusion-free: it rules out no class.

declarations.name: half_mem_of_eventually_largestSkipHalfAt
declarations.signature: theorem half_mem_of_eventually_largestSkipHalfAt (h : ∀ s : ℕ, 61 ≤ s → SkipD1.LargestSkipHalfAt s) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: If the measured pattern persists to every row — the largest false rank stays above half the row — then `1/2 ∈ mersenneAchievementSet`, by `SkipD1.half_mem_of_cofinal_largestSkipHalfAt`. The hypothesis is verified above on `[61, 500]` (`largestSkipHalfAt_block`) and at every sampled row up to `3001` (`largestSkipHalfAt_high`).

declarations.name: half_mem_of_largestFalseRank_near_terminal
declarations.signature: theorem half_mem_of_largestFalseRank_near_terminal (c : ℕ) (h : ∀ s : ℕ, 61 ≤ s → ∃ d : ℕ, IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d ∧ s ≤ d + c) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: The same from the weaker, purely quantitative hypothesis that the largest false rank stays within a bounded distance of the terminal rank — which is what the measurement actually exhibits, with the constant `8` on the whole block.

declarations.name: inHalfZone_three_two
declarations.docstring: The half zone is inhabited at its extreme corner `s - d = 1`, `2 s = 3 d`.

declarations.name: halfGapCorrection_three_two
declarations.docstring: `le_halfGapCorrection` is **sharp**: `105` is attained, at `(s,d) = (3,2)`. So the "size route is dead" argument is not resting on a loose bound.

declarations.name: le_halfGapCorrection_sharp
declarations.docstring: Independent confirmation that `H1`'s own lower bound is met with equality there, i.e. the bound cannot be improved.

declarations.name: largestSkipHalfAt_eleven
declarations.docstring: The hypotheses of the headline identity really are simultaneously satisfiable: `s = 11` is a half-late row in `SkipD1`'s sense.

declarations.name: gap_eleven_via_combined
declarations.docstring: Re-derivation of the `s = 11` conclusion through the *combined* (`skipHalfGapCorrection`) route rather than the half-zone-only route, as a cross-check that the two branches agree where they meet.

declarations.name: gap_eleven_strictly_between
declarations.signature: theorem gap_eleven_strictly_between (hs : 5 ≤ 11) : 2 ^ (11 + 1) < (seamAdjacentCut 11 hs).remainder + (seamAdjacentCut 11 hs).overshoot ∧ (seamAdjacentCut 11 hs).remainder + (seamAdjacentCut 11 hs).overshoot < 2 ^ (11 + 2)
declarations.docstring: And the resulting value does sit strictly between the two dyadic gaps, so `gap_strictly_between_of_largestSkipHalf` is non-vacuous at a real row.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_eleven
declarations.docstring: The actual greedy remainder at the certified row.

declarations.name: landing_fails_eleven
declarations.docstring: So the landing hypothesis **fails** at `s = 11`.

declarations.name: landing_theorem_not_applicable_at_eleven
declarations.docstring: Consequently `twentyOne_mul_overshoot_add_fortyTwo_eq_skipHalfGap` is not applicable at the one row `H1` certifies.

declarations.name: headline_is_a_gap_bound_only
declarations.signature: theorem headline_is_a_gap_bound_only {s d : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hd : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) d) (hhalf : s < 2 * d) : 2 ^ (s + 1) < (seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder + (seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot ∧ (seamAdjacentCut s hs).remainder + (seamAdjacentCut s hs).overshoot < 2 ^ (s + 2)

declarations.name: bits
declarations.docstring: Greedy bit list of row `s`; index `i` is rank `i + 2`.

declarations.name: falseRanks
declarations.docstring: Ranks of row `s` that the greedy declines.

declarations.name: trueRanks
declarations.docstring: Ranks of row `s` that the greedy selects.

declarations.name: largestFalseRank
declarations.docstring: Largest declined rank of row `s`, if any.

declarations.name: halfSkip
declarations.docstring: `s < 2 * d₀`, i.e. `LargestSkipHalfAt s`, computed.

declarations.name: halfNotLate
declarations.docstring: `d₀` lies in the three-term half-but-not-late zone.

declarations.name: halfSkipFailures
declarations.docstring: Rows `5 ≤ s ≤ N` whose largest false rank is NOT above `s / 2`. H2's header claims this is empty for `s ≤ 500`.

declarations.name: halfNotLateRows
declarations.docstring: Rows `5 ≤ s ≤ N` whose largest false rank is half-but-not-late. H2's header claims exactly `5, 11, 12, 13` for `s ≤ 500`.

declarations.name: landingRows
declarations.docstring: Rows `s ≤ N` satisfying the landing hypothesis `seamExcess s = 2`.

declarations.name: witnesses_unbounded
declarations.signature: theorem witnesses_unbounded (N : ℕ) : ∃ s : ℕ, N ≤ s ∧ Recon257.seamExcess s ≠ 2
declarations.docstring: The family is infinite: every prime `≥ 13` is a witness, and there are infinitely many.

declarations.name: prime_succ_not_survivorPhase
declarations.signature: theorem prime_succ_not_survivorPhase {D : ℕ} (hD : 12 ≤ D) (hp : Nat.Prime (D + 1)) : ¬ Recon257.SurvivorPhase D

declarations.name: ratchet_already_dead_on_prime_family
declarations.signature: theorem ratchet_already_dead_on_prime_family {D : ℕ} (hD : 12 ≤ D) (hp : Nat.Prime (D + 1)) : Recon257.ratchetRun D 3 = 0
declarations.docstring: Contrapositive packaging: on the family H3's headline addresses, the corpus's own ratchet already returns a dead budget, unconditionally on the phase side. (What the ratchet *cannot* do without `hright` is convert that into `False`; that conversion is exactly H3's contribution.)

declarations.name: lateBlock_mod_four_is_zero
declarations.signature: theorem lateBlock_mod_four_is_zero {s d₀ : ℕ} (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d₀) : (∑ d ∈ Finset.Ico (d₀ + 1) s, truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 4 = 0

declarations.name: lateBlock_indep_is_trivial
declarations.signature: theorem lateBlock_indep_is_trivial {s d₀ d₁ : ℕ} (h0 : 2 * s < 3 * d₀) (h1 : 2 * s < 3 * d₁) : (∑ d ∈ Finset.Ico (d₀ + 1) s, truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 4 = (∑ d ∈ Finset.Ico (d₁ + 1) s, truncatedMersenneWeight s d) % 4

declarations.name: audit_no_allRight_tail_below_500
declarations.signature: theorem audit_no_allRight_tail_below_500 (D : ℕ) (hD5 : 5 ≤ D) (hD' : D ≤ 499) : ¬ (∀ s : ℕ, D + 1 ≤ s → seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true)

declarations.name: audit_skipD1_landingRow_premise_is_false
declarations.signature: theorem audit_skipD1_landingRow_premise_is_false (D : ℕ) (hD : 60 ≤ D) (hD' : D ≤ 499) : ¬ (∀ s : ℕ, D + 1 ≤ s → seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true)
declarations.docstring: Consequently the `SkipD1` per-class theorem is vacuous in the strong sense on the whole range H4 discusses: no `D` in `[60, 499]` satisfies its `hright` hypothesis, so it is an implication from a refuted premise.

declarations.name: audit_no_allRight_tail_start_le_3000
declarations.signature: theorem audit_no_allRight_tail_start_le_3000 (S : ℕ) (hS : 5 ≤ S) (hS' : S ≤ 3000) : ¬ (∀ s : ℕ, S ≤ s → seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true)
declarations.docstring: The refutation is not limited to `D ≤ 499`. The single row-`3001` certificate refutes an all-right tail beginning at **any** row `S` with `5 ≤ S ≤ 3000` — the argument only needs one skipped rank `≥ S` at one row `> S`, and rank `3000` at row `3001` is one.

declarations.name: audit_skipD1_landingRow_premise_is_false_below_3000
declarations.signature: theorem audit_skipD1_landingRow_premise_is_false_below_3000 (D : ℕ) (hD : 60 ≤ D) (hD' : D ≤ 2999) : ¬ (∀ s : ℕ, D + 1 ≤ s → seamGreedyWord (s + 1) = (seamGreedyWord s).extend true)
declarations.docstring: Hence every corpus theorem carrying an all-right-tail hypothesis from `D+1` is an implication from a refuted premise for every `D ≤ 2999`, not merely for `D ≤ 499`. H4 had this in hand and stated only the weaker form.

declarations.name: probe_headline_is_redundant
declarations.signature: theorem probe_headline_is_redundant {h N L : ℕ} {a d : ℕ → ℤ} (H : ErdosProblems.Half.FreeWalk1.AdmissibleRun h N L a d) : ∀ K : ℕ, ∀ j < K, |a j| ≤ (N : ℤ) + j + h + L + 2

declarations.name: probe_headline_equiv
declarations.signature: theorem probe_headline_equiv (h N L : ℕ) (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) : (∃ a d : ℕ → ℤ, ErdosProblems.Half.FreeWalk1.AdmissibleRun h N L a d) ↔ (∃ a d : ℕ → ℤ, ErdosProblems.Half.FreeWalk1.AdmissibleRun h N L a d ∧ ∀ K : ℕ, ∀ j < K, |a j| ≤ (N : ℤ) + j + h + L + 2)
declarations.docstring: Hence the theorem is equivalent to the bare existence of an admissible run.

declarations.name: probe_walkStep_even
declarations.signature: theorem probe_walkStep_even (h N L : ℕ) (hNL : 2 ≤ N + L) : (2 : ℤ) ∣ ErdosProblems.Half.FreeWalk1.walkStep h N L

declarations.name: probe_trap_upper_violates_parity
declarations.signature: theorem probe_trap_upper_violates_parity : ¬ ((2 : ℤ) ∣ (fun j : ℕ => 2 - ((1 : ℤ) + j + 1)) 1)
declarations.docstring: The `trap_upper` walk of `thresholds_are_sharp` uses an ODD step, so it is not a shadow of any real totient walk. (`h` arbitrary, `N = 1`, `L = 1`, `j = 1`: the step is `-1`.)

declarations.name: probe_trap_lower_violates_parity
declarations.signature: theorem probe_trap_lower_violates_parity : ¬ ((2 : ℤ) ∣ (fun j : ℕ => (1 : ℤ) + j + 1 + 1 - 2) 0)
declarations.docstring: Likewise the `trap_lower` walk. (`h = 1`, `N = 1`, `L = 1`, `j = 0`: step `1`.)

declarations.name: probe_coverage_is_only_an_existential
declarations.signature: theorem probe_coverage_is_only_an_existential (h L M : ℕ) : ∀ N, M * (h + 6) < 2 * (N + h + L) + 5 → True

declarations.name: probe_split_fires
declarations.docstring: B1/B2. `certifiedKill_depth_split` is NOT vacuous. At `(h, N, L) = (22, 4535, 15)` the doubling hypothesis holds (`4 * 4574 = 18296 < 32768 = 2^15`) AND the depth-`16` certificate holds, so the theorem fires on live data.

declarations.name: probe_split_left_false
declarations.docstring: B3. Neither disjunct is trivially true: here the LEFT one is FALSE, so the split genuinely has to move the base point.

declarations.name: probe_split_right_true
declarations.docstring: B4. …and the RIGHT one is the one that holds.

declarations.name: probe_window_iff_applies
declarations.signature: theorem probe_window_iff_applies : certifiedKill 22 4518 (16 + 16) ↔ ∃ j ≤ 16, certifiedKill 22 (4518 + j) 16
declarations.docstring: B5. `certifiedKill_window_iff` at live numerals (`L = K = 16`, `4 * 4574 = 18296 < 65536`): the hypothesis is dischargeable.

declarations.name: probe_consecutiveFail_iff_applies
declarations.docstring: B6. `consecutiveFail_iff` does apply to the `run_17` cell, so that run — and only that one of the three — is governed by the two-sided law.

declarations.name: probe_consecutiveFail_iff_at_floor_plus_one
declarations.docstring: B7. The law also reaches one step above the depth floor `F(22,4518) = 14`: at `L = 15`, `K = 18`, `4 * 4575 = 18300 < 32768`.

declarations.name: probe_threshold_fails_for_run19_and_run13
declarations.docstring: B8. But it does NOT reach the floor itself, nor the `run_13` cell: both `freeWalk_run_19` (`L = 14`) and `freeWalk_run_13` (`L = 7`) sit strictly outside the hypothesis of `consecutiveFail_iff`, so for those two runs only the one-directional `consecutiveFail_of_deep_fail` is available.

declarations.name: probe_consecutiveFail_has_content
declarations.docstring: B9. `ConsecutiveFail` is not a vacuously-true predicate: base `2` certifies at `(h, L) = (26, 7)`, so the length-1 run there fails.

declarations.name: xcheck_run_13
declarations.docstring: C1. `ConsecutiveFail 26 3 7 12` re-derived by direct kernel enumeration of all thirteen cells, not via `consecutiveFail_of_deep_fail`. Agreement confirms the deep-failure route means what its docstring says.

declarations.name: xcheck_run_13_exact
declarations.docstring: C2. …and the run is exactly thirteen long.

declarations.name: depth_split_fails_at_three
declarations.signature: theorem depth_split_fails_at_three : ¬ (∀ h N L : ℕ, 3 * ((N : ℤ) + (h : ℤ) + (L : ℤ) + 2) < 2 ^ L → certifiedKill h N (L + 1) → certifiedKill h N L ∨ certifiedKill h (N + 1) L)
declarations.docstring: **The constant `4` cannot be lowered to `3`.**

declarations.name: transfer_needs_only_the_last_failure
declarations.signature: theorem transfer_needs_only_the_last_failure {h N L K : ℕ} (hKL : K ≤ L) (hsingle : ¬ certifiedKill h (N + K) L) : ∀ k ≤ K, ¬ certifiedKill h (N + L) k

declarations.name: walk_run_transfers_is_a_corollary
declarations.signature: theorem walk_run_transfers_is_a_corollary {h N L K : ℕ} (hKL : K ≤ L) (hrun : ∀ k ≤ K, ¬ certifiedKill h (N + k) L) : ∀ k ≤ K, ¬ certifiedKill h (N + L) k
declarations.docstring: `walk_run_transfers` is an immediate corollary of the single-point version: its `∀ k ≤ K` hypothesis is used only at `k = K`.

declarations.name: step_invariant_needs_no_radius
declarations.signature: theorem step_invariant_needs_no_radius (β : ℤ) : ∃ δ : ℤ, |δ| ≤ |β| ∧ |2 * β + δ| ≤ |β|

declarations.name: file_step_invariant_from_radius_free
declarations.signature: theorem file_step_invariant_from_radius_free (r β : ℤ) (hβ : |β| ≤ r) : ∃ δ : ℤ, |δ| ≤ r ∧ |2 * β + δ| ≤ r
declarations.docstring: FreeWalk3's §6 statement follows from the radius-free one, for every `r`.

declarations.name: failure_run_eight
declarations.signature: theorem failure_run_eight : ∀ k ∈ Finset.range 8, ¬ certifiedKill 3 (349 + k) 12

declarations.name: freeWalk2_already_has_nineteen
declarations.docstring: FreeWalk2 already has kernel-checked runs of 13, 17 and 19 at depths that clear the depth floor, each terminated by an explicit certificate. FreeWalk3's §4 "run of seven" is strictly weaker, and its unverified prose witness (`h = 6`, `N = 125384`, `L = 21`) was declined on the grounds that `decide` cannot handle six-digit totients — while FreeWalk2 discharges depth `32` at `N = 4518` with `decide +kernel`.

declarations.name: slide_emod_is_angleA2_truncate
declarations.signature: theorem slide_emod_is_angleA2_truncate (h N k L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy h N (k + L) % 2 ^ L = windowDiscrepancy h (N + k) L % 2 ^ L

declarations.name: hlow_iff
declarations.signature: theorem hlow_iff {s d M : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) : lateCorrection s d ≤ M ↔ 4 * 4 ^ (s - d) ≤ 3 * M + 4
declarations.docstring: **`hlow` restated with no division.** Straight off `Bit/Corr1`'s closed form `3 * lateCorrection s d + 4 = 4 * 4 ^ (s - d)`.

declarations.name: lateCorrection_lt_two_mul_four_pow
declarations.signature: theorem lateCorrection_lt_two_mul_four_pow {s d : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) : lateCorrection s d < 2 * 4 ^ (s - d)
declarations.docstring: The whole correction budget stays below `2 ^ (2*(s-d)+1) = 2 * 4 ^ (s-d)`.

declarations.name: two_pow_eq_two_mul_four_pow
declarations.signature: theorem two_pow_eq_two_mul_four_pow (m : ℕ) : (2 : ℕ) ^ (2 * m + 1) = 2 * 4 ^ m

declarations.name: two_pow_le_mod_of_testBit
declarations.signature: theorem two_pow_le_mod_of_testBit {C j n : ℕ} (hj : j < n) (h : Nat.testBit C j = true) : 2 ^ j ≤ C % 2 ^ n
declarations.docstring: A set bit below the modulus survives truncation to the low block.

declarations.name: hlow_of_testBit
declarations.signature: theorem hlow_of_testBit {s d C j : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) (hj1 : 2 * (s - d) + 1 ≤ j) (hj2 : j ≤ s) (h : Nat.testBit C j = true) : lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The bit criterion for `hlow`.** A single set bit of the capacity anywhere in the closed window `[2*(s-d)+1, s]` already forces the low block past the whole `4 ^ k` correction budget.

declarations.name: hlow_of_two_mul_four_pow_le
declarations.signature: theorem hlow_of_two_mul_four_pow_le {s d C : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) (h : 2 * 4 ^ (s - d) ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)) : lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: The quantitative form: the low block only has to reach `2 * 4 ^ (s-d)`.

declarations.name: window_width
declarations.signature: theorem window_width {s d : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) : 2 * (s - d) + 1 ≤ s ∧ s + 1 - (2 * (s - d) + 1) = 2 * d - s
declarations.docstring: The window is non-empty in the late zone, and its width is exactly `2*d - s` — about `s / 3` at the first late rank.

declarations.name: hlow_of_testBit_halfPoint
declarations.signature: theorem hlow_of_testBit_halfPoint {s d C : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (h : Nat.testBit C s = true) : lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: **`hlow` is automatic at a set half-point bit.** Bit `s` is `Three/T4`'s decisive position, so the bit criterion supplies `hlow` precisely in the case where `T4`'s conclusion is uninteresting. This is the structural reason the route of §1 cannot discharge `hlow` where it is wanted.

declarations.name: testBit_false_of_not_hlow
declarations.signature: theorem testBit_false_of_not_hlow {s d C j : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) (hbad : ¬ lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)) (hj1 : 2 * (s - d) + 1 ≤ j) (hj2 : j ≤ s) : Nat.testBit C j = false
declarations.docstring: **Rigidity.** `hlow` can only fail on a capacity whose bits are solidly zero across the entire window `[2*(s-d)+1, s]`.

declarations.name: hlow_or_window_clear
declarations.signature: theorem hlow_or_window_clear {s d C : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) : lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1) ∨ ∀ j : ℕ, 2 * (s - d) + 1 ≤ j → j ≤ s → Nat.testBit C j = false
declarations.docstring: The dichotomy, assembled.

declarations.name: mod_lt_of_not_hlow
declarations.signature: theorem mod_lt_of_not_hlow {s d C : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) (hbad : ¬ lateCorrection s d ≤ C % 2 ^ (s + 1)) : C % 2 ^ (s + 1) < 2 * 4 ^ (s - d)
declarations.docstring: A failure of `hlow` pins the low block far below the half point.

declarations.name: mod_le_mod_sub_add
declarations.signature: theorem mod_le_mod_sub_add {y a m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : y % m ≤ (y - a) % m + a
declarations.docstring: Subtracting anything moves a residue down by at most the amount subtracted.

declarations.name: sub_multiple_mod
declarations.signature: theorem sub_multiple_mod {A M t : ℕ} (h : M * t ≤ A) : (A - M * t) % M = A % M
declarations.docstring: Subtracting a multiple of the modulus leaves the residue alone.

declarations.name: lateGreedy_lower
declarations.signature: theorem lateGreedy_lower (s : ℕ) : ∀ d C : ℕ, 2 * s < 3 * d → C % 2 ^ (s + 1) ≤ integerGreedyRemainder (seamWeightsFrom s d) C + lateCorrection s d
declarations.docstring: **The lower trapping bound, unconditionally.** No `hhigh`, no `hlow`: at every late rank and for every capacity, the late greedy cannot destroy more of the low block than the correction budget. This is `Three/T4.seamRemainder_bounds`'s second component with both side conditions removed.

declarations.name: trap
declarations.signature: theorem trap (s : ℕ) : ∀ e C B : ℕ, 2 * s < 3 * e → 4 ^ (s - e) ≤ B → 3 * C < 3 * 2 ^ (2 * s - e + 1) + 2 * B + 4 * 4 ^ (s - e) → 3 * integerGreedyRemainder (seamWeightsFrom s e) C < 3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * B + 4
declarations.docstring: **The invariant that survives the declined branch.** The naive induction `C < 2 ^ (2*s-e+1)` breaks when the greedy skips a rank: a skip only gives `C < w e`, which overshoots the halved ceiling by the weight's second bit. Carrying a *fixed* budget `B ≥ 4 ^ (s-e)` alongside repairs it — the skipped branch is paid out of `B`, the taken branch out of the local term, and neither branch has to shrink the other.

declarations.name: lateGreedy_lt_sharp
declarations.signature: theorem lateGreedy_lt_sharp {s d C : ℕ} (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hhigh : C < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)) : 3 * integerGreedyRemainder (seamWeightsFrom s d) C < 3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 4
declarations.docstring: **The upper trapping bound without `hlow`.** `hhigh` alone gives the late greedy remainder the bound `2 ^ (s+1) + (2*4^(s-d)+4)/3` — the same constant `Decl.D1.remainder_lt_of_late_largest_skip_sharp` obtains from the largest-declined-rank hypothesis.

declarations.name: lateGreedy_lt_two_pow_add
declarations.signature: theorem lateGreedy_lt_two_pow_add {s d C : ℕ} (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hhigh : C < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)) : integerGreedyRemainder (seamWeightsFrom s d) C < 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ^ (s - d)
declarations.docstring: The same, in `RemC6`'s shape.

declarations.name: seamRemainder_lt_sharp_of_hhigh
declarations.signature: theorem seamRemainder_lt_sharp_of_hhigh {s d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hhigh : lateEntryRemainder s d < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)) : 3 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 4
declarations.docstring: **`Three/T4` §4, with `hlow` deleted.** At any late rank satisfying `hhigh` — including the rows where every late rank is taken, which is exactly the case `RemC6` cannot reach — the seam remainder obeys the sharp bound.

declarations.name: seamRemainder_lt_sharp_of_declined
declarations.signature: theorem seamRemainder_lt_sharp_of_declined {s d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d ≤ s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hdecl : lateEntryRemainder s d < truncatedMersenneWeight s d) : 3 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * 4 ^ (s - d) + 4
declarations.docstring: **No side conditions at all.** Combining with `Decl.D1.lateEntryRemainder_lt_two_pow_of_declined`, which supplies `hhigh` for free at a declined rank: a single late declined rank bounds `ρ s`. Compare `Decl.D1.remainder_lt_of_late_largest_skip_sharp`, which needs `d` to be the *largest* declined rank of the row.

declarations.name: seamRemainder_lower
declarations.signature: theorem seamRemainder_lower {s d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) : lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1) ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + lateCorrection s d
declarations.docstring: The unconditional lower half, transported.

declarations.name: lateEntryRemainder_seven_five
declarations.docstring: The genuine remainder entering the late zone of row `7`.

declarations.name: declined_seven_five
declarations.docstring: Rank `5` of row `7` is declined.

declarations.name: hhigh_holds_seven_five
declarations.docstring: `hhigh` holds at `(7,5)` — and not merely numerically: it is `Decl.D1`'s theorem, applied to the decline just proved.

declarations.name: hlow_fails_seven_five
declarations.docstring: **`hlow` fails at `(7,5)`.** The low block is `7`; the correction budget is `20`.

declarations.name: not_hlow_of_hhigh
declarations.signature: theorem not_hlow_of_hhigh : ¬ ∀ s d : ℕ, 2 ≤ d → d ≤ s → 2 * s < 3 * d → lateEntryRemainder s d < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1) → lateCorrection s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The sharp negative.** `hlow` does not follow from `hhigh` and lateness, so the discharge of `Decl.D1` §5 cannot be repeated for the second side condition: there is nothing to prove directly, because the statement is false.

declarations.name: not_admissible_seven_five
declarations.docstring: Row `7` at `d = 5` is therefore not admissible for `Three/T4`.

declarations.name: seven_five_window_clear
declarations.signature: theorem seven_five_window_clear : ∀ j : ℕ, 5 ≤ j → j ≤ 7 → Nat.testBit (lateEntryRemainder 7 5) j = false
declarations.docstring: The window rigidity of §1, checked on the counterexample: `hlow` fails, so every bit of `lateEntryRemainder 7 5` in `[2*(7-5)+1, 7] = [5,7]` is clear.

declarations.name: seamRemainder_seven_lt
declarations.docstring: `3 * ρ 7 < 3 * 2 ^ 8 + 2 * 4 ^ 2 + 4 = 804`, i.e. `ρ 7 < 268`, obtained from the decline of rank `5` alone. (The true value is `3`.)

declarations.name: upper_trap_needs_hlow
declarations.docstring: **The other half of `T4`'s two-sided bound really needs `hlow`.** At `s = 7`, `d = 6`, `C = 257` — a capacity satisfying `hhigh` — the late greedy declines its single weight `truncatedMersenneWeight 7 6 = 260` and returns `257`, while the low block is `257 % 2 ^ 8 = 1`. So `hlow` cannot simply be deleted from `Three/T4.lateGreedy_trapped`'s first component.

declarations.name: hlow_seventeen_twelve
declarations.docstring: `hlow` at `(17,12)`, from the half-point bit alone.

declarations.name: admissible_seventeen
declarations.docstring: **Anti-vacuity, row 17.** A row outside the corpus's worked set, admissible for `Three/T4`, with `hlow` supplied by §1's bit criterion.

declarations.name: seamRemainder_seventeen_lt
declarations.docstring: The §2 bound fires at row `17` too.

declarations.name: fourteen_window_clear
declarations.signature: theorem fourteen_window_clear : ∀ j : ℕ, 9 ≤ j → j ≤ 14 → Nat.testBit (lateEntryRemainder 14 10) j = false

declarations.name: fourteen_bit_route_silent
declarations.docstring: `hlow` holds at `(14,10)` although the whole window is clear: the bit route of §1 is silent there.

declarations.name: mod_lt_seven_five
declarations.docstring: `mod_lt_of_not_hlow` at the counterexample: row `7`'s low block is below `2 * 4 ^ 2 = 32`.

declarations.name: window_width_seven_five
declarations.docstring: `window_width` at `(7,5)`: the forced-zero window is `[5,7]`, of width `2*5 - 7 = 3`.

declarations.name: hlow_or_window_clear_seven_five
declarations.signature: theorem hlow_or_window_clear_seven_five : lateCorrection 7 5 ≤ lateEntryRemainder 7 5 % 2 ^ (7 + 1) ∨ ∀ j : ℕ, 2 * (7 - 5) + 1 ≤ j → j ≤ 7 → Nat.testBit (lateEntryRemainder 7 5) j = false
declarations.docstring: `hlow_or_window_clear` at `(7,5)`: the second branch is the one that holds.

declarations.name: seamRemainder_lower_seventeen
declarations.docstring: The unconditional lower bound, on the genuine object at row `17`.

declarations.name: lateGreedy_lt_two_pow_add_seventeen
declarations.docstring: The `RemC6`-shaped upper bound, on the genuine object at row `17`.

declarations.name: hlow_iff_decided
declarations.docstring: `hlow_iff` read both ways: false at `(7,5)`, true at `(17,12)`, with the division-free right-hand side.

declarations.name: lateEntryRemainder_succ
declarations.signature: theorem lateEntryRemainder_succ {s d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) : lateEntryRemainder s (d + 1) = if truncatedMersenneWeight s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d then lateEntryRemainder s d - truncatedMersenneWeight s d else lateEntryRemainder s d

declarations.name: sub_mul_mod_self
declarations.signature: theorem sub_mul_mod_self {A M t : ℕ} (h : M * t ≤ A) : (A - M * t) % M = A % M
declarations.docstring: Subtracting a multiple of the modulus leaves the residue alone.

declarations.name: hlow_succ_of_hlow
declarations.signature: theorem hlow_succ_of_hlow {s d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hlow : lateCorrection s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1)) : lateCorrection s (d + 1) ≤ lateEntryRemainder s (d + 1) % 2 ^ (s + 1)

declarations.name: hlow_mono
declarations.signature: theorem hlow_mono {s d : ℕ} (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hlow : lateCorrection s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1)) : ∀ e : ℕ, d ≤ e → e ≤ s → lateCorrection s e ≤ lateEntryRemainder s e % 2 ^ (s + 1)
