declarations.name: sat_hlow
declarations.docstring: Hypothesis (1), `hlow`, holds — imported witness, at `(20, 14)`.

declarations.name: sat_not_hlow
declarations.docstring: Hypothesis (2), `¬ hlow`, holds — imported witness, at `(7, 5)`.

declarations.name: sat_bitAdmissible_and_not_hlow
declarations.docstring: Hypothesis (3), `BitAdmissible`, holds at a rank where `hlow` **fails** — the combination that §4 needs. Without this, all of §4 would be vacuous.

declarations.name: sat_bitAdmissible_and_hlow
declarations.docstring: And `BitAdmissible` holds at ranks where `hlow` **holds** too, so the `iff` of §3 is not one-sided.

declarations.name: lateCorrection_six_five
declarations.docstring: `lateCorrection 6 5 = 4`.

declarations.name: lateEntryRemainder_six_five
declarations.docstring: `lateEntryRemainder 6 5 = 34`. Rank `5` is the first late rank of row `6` (`2 * 6 < 3 * 5` and `¬ (2 * 6 < 3 * 4)`).

declarations.name: hlow_six_five
declarations.docstring: `hlow` **holds** at `(6, 5)`, so this is a surviving pair.

declarations.name: margin_six_five
declarations.docstring: **The surviving margin at `(6, 5)` is `30`.** `(6, 5)` is a *first* late rank, so this refutes the header's "tightest surviving margin `52`" under the first-late-rank reading.

declarations.name: margin_seven_six
declarations.docstring: **The surviving margin at `(7, 6)` is `3`.** This refutes the header's "tightest surviving margin `52`" under the all-late-ranks reading, by a factor of more than seventeen. `hlow` holds at `(7, 6)` — it is `H2`'s own `Concrete.hlow_seven_six`.

declarations.name: header_margin_claim_is_false
declarations.signature: theorem header_margin_claim_is_false : (lateCorrection 6 5 ≤ lateEntryRemainder 6 5 % 2 ^ (6 + 1) ∧ lateEntryRemainder 6 5 % 2 ^ (6 + 1) - lateCorrection 6 5 < 52) ∧ (lateCorrection 7 6 ≤ lateEntryRemainder 7 6 % 2 ^ (7 + 1) ∧ lateEntryRemainder 7 6 % 2 ^ (7 + 1) - lateCorrection 7 6 < 52)
declarations.docstring: **The header's margin claim is false, both ways.** Two surviving pairs with margin strictly below `52`; the first of them is a first late rank.

declarations.name: two_equal_binary_length_pairs
declarations.signature: theorem two_equal_binary_length_pairs : (2 ^ 8 ≤ lateCorrection 14 10 ∧ lateCorrection 14 10 ≤ lateEntryRemainder 14 10 % 2 ^ (14 + 1) ∧ lateEntryRemainder 14 10 % 2 ^ (14 + 1) < 2 ^ 9) ∧ (2 ^ 2 ≤ lateCorrection 7 6 ∧ lateCorrection 7 6 ≤ lateEntryRemainder 7 6 % 2 ^ (7 + 1) ∧ lateEntryRemainder 7 6 % 2 ^ (7 + 1) < 2 ^ 3)
declarations.docstring: **The "only pair with equal binary length" claim is false.** A pair `(low, corr)` has equal binary length exactly when both lie in some `[2 ^ k, 2 ^ (k+1))`. At `(14, 10)` that holds with `k = 8` (`256 ≤ 340 ≤ 392 < 512`) — the header's pair. At `(7, 6)` it holds with `k = 2` (`4 ≤ 4 ≤ 7 < 8`), and `(7, 6)` is a surviving pair. So there are at least two, not one.

declarations.name: hit_certificate_is_a_D4_corollary
declarations.signature: theorem hit_certificate_is_a_D4_corollary {s d : ℕ} (h : BitAdmissible s d) (hfail : ¬ (lateCorrection s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1))) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ s
declarations.docstring: **`H2`'s hit certificate is a corollary of `D4`.** `D4.testBit_false_of_not_hlow` says a failure of `hlow` clears the whole bit window `[2(s−d)+1, s]`; `s` is in that window by `D4.window_nonempty`; and `D4.seamRemainder_lt_two_pow_of_testBit_false'` converts a clear bit `s` into `ρ s < 2 ^ s`. Two lines, no new content.

declarations.name: routes_agree
declarations.signature: theorem routes_agree {s d : ℕ} (h : BitAdmissible s d) (hfail : ¬ (lateCorrection s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1))) : seamRemainder_lt_two_pow_of_not_hlow h hfail = hit_certificate_is_a_D4_corollary h hfail
declarations.docstring: The two routes agree, as they must.

declarations.name: sharp_form_is_a_D4_corollary
declarations.signature: theorem sharp_form_is_a_D4_corollary {s d : ℕ} (h : BitAdmissible s d) (hfail : ¬ (lateCorrection s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1))) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < skipCorrection s (lateEntryRemainder s d) d
declarations.docstring: **The sharp form is also a corollary of `D4`.** `D4.seamRemainder_eq_mod_sub` is the exact identity `ρ s = low − bitCorrection`; `H2.skipCorrection_add_bitCorrection` is `skip + bit = lateCorrection`. `¬ hlow` is `low < skip + bit`, so `ρ s = low − bit < skip`. This is `H2`'s genuine increment over `D4` — a sharper constant — and it is one `omega` away from `D4`'s identity.

declarations.name: reduction_is_a_D4_corollary
declarations.signature: theorem reduction_is_a_D4_corollary (h : ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ s d : ℕ, N ≤ s ∧ 5 ≤ s ∧ BitAdmissible s d ∧ ¬ (lateCorrection s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1))) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: **The reduction is a corollary of `D4`'s reduction.** `H2`'s `half_mem_of_not_hlow_cofinally` factors through `D4.half_mem_of_bitAdmissible_halfPointBitClearCofinally` with no new input. So §4 does not widen the route to `#257` by one row; it narrows the entry condition from "bit `s` clear" to the strictly stronger "`hlow` fails".

declarations.name: not_hlow_implies_D4_condition
declarations.signature: theorem not_hlow_implies_D4_condition {s d : ℕ} (hds : d ≤ s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (hfail : ¬ (lateCorrection s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d % 2 ^ (s + 1))) : Nat.testBit (lateEntryRemainder s d) s = false
declarations.docstring: **`¬ hlow` is strictly stronger than `D4`'s entry condition** — this is `D4.hlow_of_testBit_halfPoint` contraposed, and it is why §4's hypothesis is harder to meet than `D4`'s, not easier.

declarations.name: missing_instance_not_hlow_of_not_hlow_ge
declarations.docstring: The missing instance of `not_hlow_of_not_hlow_ge`. Note `d = e = 5`: this is the **diagonal** case, where the conclusion is literally the hypothesis. Measured over `s ∈ [6, 3000]`, all late ranks: there is **no** triple `(s, d, e)` with `d < e` satisfying the hypothesis. The reason is a theorem — `H2`'s own `exists_not_hlow_iff` — since the sole failure `(7, 5)` sits at a first late rank, nothing above it can fail. So `not_hlow_of_not_hlow_ge` has, in the whole scanned range, only diagonal instances. It is not vacuous, but it is not witnessed non-trivially either, and `H2` says nothing about this.

declarations.name: missing_instance_exists_not_hlow
declarations.signature: theorem missing_instance_exists_not_hlow : ∃ e : ℕ, 5 ≤ e ∧ e ≤ 7 ∧ ¬ (lateCorrection 7 e ≤ lateEntryRemainder 7 e % 2 ^ (7 + 1))
declarations.docstring: The missing instance of `exists_not_hlow_iff`, forward direction: row `7` does fail somewhere in its late zone.

declarations.name: missing_instance_no_failure_in_row_twenty
declarations.signature: theorem missing_instance_no_failure_in_row_twenty : ¬ (∃ e : ℕ, 14 ≤ e ∧ e ≤ 20 ∧ ¬ (lateCorrection 20 e ≤ lateEntryRemainder 20 e % 2 ^ (20 + 1)))
declarations.docstring: The other direction, on a row where nothing fails: row `20` has no failing late rank at all. This is the non-vacuity witness for the *negative* side of `exists_not_hlow_iff`, also absent from `H2`.

declarations.name: hlow_twenty_seventeen_values
declarations.docstring: `hlow_twenty_seventeen`, `H2`'s advertised "fact not in the corpus", checked against direct computation rather than against `hlow_mono`. `H2` obtains `lateCorrection 20 17 ≤ lateEntryRemainder 20 17 % 2 ^ 21` by propagation; the actual numbers are `84 ≤ 549353`, a margin of five orders of magnitude. It is a true new fact and an extremely slack one.

declarations.name: lateEntryRemainder_twenty_seventeen_eq_rho
declarations.docstring: And `lateEntryRemainder 20 17` is already `ρ 20`: ranks `17, 18, 19` are all declined, so `hlow_twenty_seventeen` is a statement about the final remainder with the tail correction only.

declarations.name: lateCorrection_seven_seven_is_zero
declarations.docstring: `hlow_seven_seven` and the third conjunct of `row_seven_failure_set` are trivial: `lateCorrection 7 7 = 0`. The content of `row_seven_failure_set` is its first two conjuncts, both of which come from `D4`.

declarations.name: redeclared_statement
declarations.signature: theorem redeclared_statement (s d : ℕ) (h2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) : lateEntryRemainder s (d + 1) = if truncatedMersenneWeight s d ≤ lateEntryRemainder s d then lateEntryRemainder s d - truncatedMersenneWeight s d else lateEntryRemainder s d
declarations.docstring: `H2`'s statement, restated.

declarations.name: coeffDiscrepancy
declarations.signature: def coeffDiscrepancy (c : ℕ → ℤ) (L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The window discrepancy as a functional of its coefficient sequence: `D(c, L) = ∑_{j<L} c(j)·2^{L-1-j}`.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_eq_coeffDiscrepancy
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_eq_coeffDiscrepancy (h N L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy h N L = coeffDiscrepancy (fun j => (Nat.totient (N + h + 1 + j) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient (N + 1 + j) : ℤ)) L
declarations.docstring: `windowDiscrepancy` is `coeffDiscrepancy` of the totient window coefficients.

declarations.name: coeffDiscrepancy_congr
declarations.signature: theorem coeffDiscrepancy_congr {c c' : ℕ → ℤ} {L : ℕ} (hc : ∀ j < L, (2 : ℤ) ^ (j + 1) ∣ (c j - c' j)) : (2 : ℤ) ^ L ∣ coeffDiscrepancy c L - coeffDiscrepancy c' L
declarations.docstring: **PROVED (sufficiency for residue equality).** Agreement of every coefficient modulo `2^{j+1}` forces agreement of the discrepancies modulo `2^L`.

declarations.name: coeffDiscrepancy_update
declarations.signature: theorem coeffDiscrepancy_update {c : ℕ → ℤ} {L j₀ : ℕ} (hj : j₀ < L) : coeffDiscrepancy (Function.update c j₀ (c j₀ + 2 ^ j₀)) L - coeffDiscrepancy c L = 2 ^ (L - 1)
declarations.docstring: Perturbing a single coefficient at position `j₀` by exactly `2^{j₀}` moves the discrepancy by exactly `2^{L-1}`.

declarations.name: coeffDiscrepancy_update_not_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem coeffDiscrepancy_update_not_dvd {c : ℕ → ℤ} {L j₀ : ℕ} (hL : 0 < L) (hj : j₀ < L) : ¬ (2 : ℤ) ^ L ∣ coeffDiscrepancy (Function.update c j₀ (c j₀ + 2 ^ j₀)) L - coeffDiscrepancy c L
declarations.docstring: **PROVED (single-coordinate residue sensitivity).** Perturbing one coefficient by `2^{j₀}` changes the discrepancy residue modulo `2^L`. This is not a necessity theorem for `certifiedKill`: it neither excludes cancellations between several coefficient errors nor shows that the coarser admissible-arc predicate requires the complete residue.

declarations.name: totient_gcd_dvd_window
declarations.signature: theorem totient_gcd_dvd_window (h m : ℕ) : (Nat.totient (Nat.gcd h m) : ℤ) ∣ (Nat.totient (m + h) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient m : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: **The A1 transport law.** For every shift `h` and every window position `m`, `φ(gcd(h, m)) ∣ φ(m + h) − φ(m)`. No hypotheses at all. `gcd(h, m)` divides `m` and divides `m + h`, and `φ` is monotone for divisibility, so both totients carry the factor. Because the divisor depends on `h` only through `gcd(h, m)`, this holds *identically* at `H`, `2H`, `pH`, `2pH` and every higher rung of the lcm ladder: it is the scale-free part of the window.

declarations.name: totient_gcd_dvd_windowCoeff
declarations.signature: theorem totient_gcd_dvd_windowCoeff (h N j : ℕ) : (Nat.totient (Nat.gcd h (N + 1 + j)) : ℤ) ∣ (Nat.totient (N + h + 1 + j) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient (N + 1 + j) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The transport law on the coefficient at position `j` of the `(h, N)` window.

declarations.name: totient_gcd_dvd_diagCoeff
declarations.signature: theorem totient_gcd_dvd_diagCoeff (H d : ℕ) : (Nat.totient (Nat.gcd d H) : ℤ) ∣ (Nat.totient (2 * H + d) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient (H + d) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: The transport law on the diagonal window coefficient `c_H(d) = φ(2H + d) − φ(H + d)`: `φ(gcd(d, H)) ∣ c_H(d)`.

declarations.name: sixteen_dvd_diagCoeff_offset_seventeen
declarations.signature: theorem sixteen_dvd_diagCoeff_offset_seventeen {H : ℕ} (h17 : 17 ∣ H) : (16 : ℤ) ∣ (Nat.totient (2 * H + 17) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient (H + 17) : ℤ)
declarations.docstring: **Four bits the exact-valuation core misses.** For every `H` divisible by `17`, `16 ∣ c_H(17)`. `Recon249.factorization_window` cannot see this: it needs `v₁₇(17) < v₁₇(H)`, which fails whenever `17 ∥ H` — and `17 ∥ lcm(1..t)` for every `t < 289`. Divisibility does not need the valuation to be strict.

declarations.name: scaleFree_bit_ceiling
declarations.signature: theorem scaleFree_bit_ceiling {h m k : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hk : 2 ^ k ∣ Nat.totient (Nat.gcd h m)) : 2 ^ k ≤ m
declarations.docstring: **PROVED: the ceiling on the transport law.** If `2^k` divides `φ(gcd(h, m))` then `2^k ≤ m`. Thus this law supplies at most `log₂ m` divisibility bits at position `m`. No certificate-wide information lower bound is asserted.

declarations.name: supplyBits
declarations.docstring: The number of 2-adic bits of the window coefficient at position `m` that the scale-free law forces, for shift `h`.

declarations.name: two_pow_supplyBits_le
declarations.signature: theorem two_pow_supplyBits_le {h m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) : 2 ^ supplyBits h m ≤ m

declarations.name: supplyBits_le_six
declarations.signature: theorem supplyBits_le_six {h m : ℕ} (h1 : 0 < m) (h2 : m ≤ 98) : supplyBits h m ≤ 6

declarations.name: frontier_demand
declarations.docstring: **PROVED arithmetic benchmark.** The sum of the sufficient per-coordinate residue precisions through depth `98` is `∑_{d=1}^{98} d = 4851`. This equality is pure finite arithmetic. It is not a theorem that every depth-`98` certificate requires `4851` independent bits. The declaration name is historical: `t = 67` is now certified.

declarations.name: frontier_supply_ledger
declarations.signature: theorem frontier_supply_ledger (h : ℕ) : ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 98, supplyBits h d ≤ 588
declarations.docstring: **PROVED, uniform in the scale.** For *every* shift `h`, the total 2-adic information the scale-free divisibility law forces over the depth-`98` window is at most `588`. **MEASURED outside Lean:** at `h = periodLcm 67`, this sum is `210`, versus `114` for the exact-valuation rule in `Recon249` Result 2. The figures `4%` and `12%` compare these values with the `4851` residue-precision benchmark; they do not measure a proved information demand for `certifiedKill`. The declaration name is historical: `t = 67` is now certified.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_lcm_base_supply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_lcm_base_supply (hsupply : ∀ t₀ : ℕ, ∃ t, t₀ ≤ t ∧ ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) t L) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **PROVED: a base-`t` supply reduction.** A second one-parameter reduction of #249, alongside the diagonal one. The supply theorem wants `certifiedKill (periodLcm t) N L` at *some* large `N`; `N = t` is already cofinal. The low block then consists of totients of integers `≤ t + L`. This theorem does not compare the computational cost of proving the required certificates.

declarations.name: base_window_low_block
declarations.signature: theorem base_window_low_block {t L j : ℕ} (hj : j < L) : t + 1 + j ≤ t + L
declarations.docstring: **PROVED index-range asymmetry.** In the base cell every index of the low block is at most `t + L`; in the diagonal cell every index of the low block is at least `periodLcm t`. Both cells read `L` indices of the high block, all `≥ periodLcm t`. The theorem itself asserts only the displayed index bound; “hard” versus “easy” evaluation is not formalized.

declarations.name: diagonal_window_low_block
declarations.signature: theorem diagonal_window_low_block {t j : ℕ} : periodLcm t ≤ periodLcm t + 1 + j

declarations.name: base_depth_floor
declarations.signature: theorem base_depth_floor {t N L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill (periodLcm t) N L) : (2 * periodLcm t : ℤ) < 2 ^ L
declarations.docstring: The base-cell depth floor: `2·periodLcm t < 2^L`. (The diagonal floor is `4·periodLcm t < 2^L` — exactly one bit more.)

declarations.name: base_depth_floor_at_67
declarations.signature: theorem base_depth_floor_at_67 {L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill (periodLcm 67) 67 L) : 97 ≤ L
declarations.docstring: **PROVED lower bound.** Any base certificate at the frontier has depth at least `97`, one below the corresponding proved diagonal lower bound `98` (`Recon249.certifiedKill_periodLcm_67_depth`). This does not prove existence at depth `97`.

declarations.name: base_depth_97_is_admissible
declarations.docstring: **PROVED numerical admissibility only.** At depth `97` the base cell's defining arc is nonempty. This does not prove that its actual discrepancy lies in that arc.

declarations.name: base_margin_98
declarations.docstring: The base cell's admissible arc at depth `98`: half the circle.

declarations.name: diagonal_margin_98
declarations.docstring: The diagonal cell's admissible arc at depth `98`: a needle (`Recon249.periodLcm_67_depth98_margin`, restated here for the comparison).

declarations.name: base_margin_98_beats_diagonal_98
declarations.signature: theorem base_margin_98_beats_diagonal_98 : 2433 * ((2 : ℤ) ^ 98 - 2 * ((periodLcm 67 : ℤ) + (periodLcm 67 : ℤ) + 98 + 2)) < (2 : ℤ) ^ 98 - 2 * ((67 : ℤ) + (periodLcm 67 : ℤ) + 98 + 2)
declarations.docstring: **PROVED fixed-depth comparison.** At depth `98`, the base cell's admissible arc is more than `2433` times the diagonal cell's admissible arc. This theorem compares only the two integer margins at that depth; it proves neither a certificate nor a uniform computational-cost advantage.

declarations.name: exists_baseKill_le_ten
declarations.signature: theorem exists_baseKill_le_ten (t : ℕ) (ht : t ≤ 10) : ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) t L
declarations.docstring: Every scale `t ≤ 10` carries a base-form certificate. Depths `5, 6, 5, 7, 8, 10, 9, 11, 13, 15, 14` — at `t = 7` and `t = 8` these are `11` and `13` against the recorded diagonal depths `14` and `15`.

declarations.name: modelDiscrepancy
declarations.signature: def modelDiscrepancy (g : ℕ → ℕ) (h N L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The window discrepancy of an arbitrary replacement `g` for the totient.

declarations.name: modelKill
declarations.signature: def modelKill (g : ℕ → ℕ) (h N L : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The certificate predicate of an arbitrary replacement `g` for the totient.

declarations.name: modelKill_totient
declarations.signature: theorem modelKill_totient (h N L : ℕ) : modelKill Nat.totient h N L ↔ certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: The model predicate at `g = φ` is the real certificate predicate.

declarations.name: sum_two_pow
declarations.signature: private lemma sum_two_pow (L : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, (2 : ℤ) ^ j = 2 ^ L - 1

declarations.name: sum_two_pow_rev
declarations.signature: private lemma sum_two_pow_rev (L : ℕ) : ∑ j ∈ Finset.range L, (2 : ℤ) ^ (L - 1 - j) = 2 ^ L - 1

declarations.name: constant_model_never_kills
declarations.signature: theorem constant_model_never_kills {g : ℕ → ℕ} {h N L c : ℕ} (hc : ∀ j < L, (g (N + h + 1 + j) : ℤ) - (g (N + 1 + j) : ℤ) = (c : ℤ)) (hcle : c ≤ N + h + L + 2) : ¬ modelKill g h N L
declarations.docstring: **PROVED: constant-window models certify nothing.** If a replacement `g` for the totient has constant window difference `c` across the depth-`L` window, with `c ≤ N + h + L + 2`, then `modelKill g h N L` is false — at every depth, at every scale. The reason is structural, not numerical: a constant window difference makes the discrepancy `c·(2^L − 1) ≡ −c`, which lands in the excluded arc by construction. A model affine in the shift satisfies the constant-difference hypothesis. No claim is made here that every finite-prime truncation or bounded-level model is affine on the required windows.

declarations.name: identity_model_never_kills
declarations.signature: theorem identity_model_never_kills (h N L : ℕ) : ¬ modelKill id h N L
declarations.docstring: The identity model: `g = id` has constant window difference `h`, so it certifies nothing at any depth or scale.

declarations.name: tail_diff_eq_scaled
declarations.signature: private lemma tail_diff_eq_scaled (H : ℕ) : totientTail (H + H) - totientTail H = (2 : ℝ) ^ H * ((2 : ℝ) ^ H - 1) * (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) - ((totientPrefix (H + H) : ℝ) - (totientPrefix H : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: The diagonal tail difference in closed form: `R_{2H} − R_H = 2^H(2^H − 1)·S − (Φ_{2H} − Φ_H)`.

declarations.name: mem_int_iff_scaled
declarations.signature: private lemma mem_int_iff_scaled (H : ℕ) : (totientTail (H + H) - totientTail H ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) ↔ ((2 : ℝ) ^ H * ((2 : ℝ) ^ H - 1) * (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ))
declarations.docstring: `R_{2H} − R_H` is an integer exactly when `2^H(2^H − 1)·S` is.

declarations.name: scaled_dvd
declarations.signature: private lemma scaled_dvd (H m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : ((2 : ℤ) ^ H * ((2 : ℤ) ^ H - 1)) ∣ ((2 : ℤ) ^ (m * H) * ((2 : ℤ) ^ (m * H) - 1))
declarations.docstring: `2^H(2^H − 1) ∣ 2^{mH}(2^{mH} − 1)`: the certificate moduli are nested upward along the divisibility order of the shifts.

declarations.name: tail_diff_int_scale_up
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_int_scale_up {H m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (h : totientTail (H + H) - totientTail H ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : totientTail (m * H + m * H) - totientTail (m * H) ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Integrality transports upward.** If the diagonal tail difference at `H` is an integer then so is the one at every multiple `m·H`. This is the automatic direction, and it is the contrapositive of the lift.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_emod
declarations.signature: private lemma certifiedKill_of_emod {h N L : ℕ} {r : ℤ} (hmod : windowDiscrepancy h N L % 2 ^ L = r) (h1 : ((N : ℤ) + h + L + 2) < r) (h2 : r < 2 ^ L - ((N : ℤ) + h + L + 2)) : certifiedKill h N L

declarations.name: exists_depth
declarations.signature: private lemma exists_depth (H : ℕ) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) : ∃ L : ℕ, 2 * ((H : ℝ) + H + L + 2) < c * 2 ^ L

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_of_tail_diff_notMem_int
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_of_tail_diff_notMem_int {H : ℕ} (hd : totientTail (H + H) - totientTail H ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : ∃ L, certifiedKill H H L
declarations.docstring: **The certificate is exactly the non-integrality of the tail difference.** The converse of `tail_diff_notMem_int_of_certifiedKill`: if the diagonal tail difference at `H` is not an integer, some depth certifies it. Depth is therefore never the obstruction — the only question at a given scale is whether the real number `R_{2H} − R_H` is an integer.

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_diagonal_iff
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_diagonal_iff (H : ℕ) : (∃ L, certifiedKill H H L) ↔ totientTail (H + H) - totientTail H ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **The exact content of a diagonal certificate.**

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_descends
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_descends {m H : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hcert : ∃ L, certifiedKill (m * H) (m * H) L) : ∃ L, certifiedKill H H L
declarations.docstring: **PROVED: the ladder implication runs downward.** A diagonal certificate at any multiple `m·H` *implies* a diagonal certificate at `H`. This runs in the reverse direction from the proposed lift `certifiedKill H H L → ∃ L', certifiedKill (p·H) (p·H) L'`. The lift is therefore not an ordinary induction step over an already-established base: the desired conclusion implies the proposed base hypothesis. Every higher rung is therefore at least as strong as all rungs below it. Strictness is not proved.

declarations.name: periodLcm_dvd_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem periodLcm_dvd_of_le {s t : ℕ} (hst : s ≤ t) : periodLcm s ∣ periodLcm t

declarations.name: diagonal_certified_downward_closed
declarations.signature: theorem diagonal_certified_downward_closed {s t : ℕ} (hst : s ≤ t) (h : ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L) : ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm s) (periodLcm s) L
declarations.docstring: **PROVED: the certified region is downward closed.** If any scale `t` of the lcm ray carries a diagonal certificate, then so does every `s ≤ t`. The 28 deposits recorded when this result was written at `t ≤ 66` are logical consequences of a deposit at `t = 67` or above. The later band through `t = 82` supplies such a deposit. This theorem proves downward closure; strictness between consecutive rungs is not claimed.

declarations.name: frontier_certificate_implies_all_seed
declarations.signature: theorem frontier_certificate_implies_all_seed {L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill (periodLcm 67) (periodLcm 67) L) (t : ℕ) (ht : t ≤ 67) : ∃ L', certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L'
declarations.docstring: **PROVED historical-frontier corollary.** A diagonal certificate at `t = 67` implies one at every `t ≤ 67`. The name records the former frontier; the current finite band extends through `t = 82`.

declarations.name: irrational_iff_all_diagonal_certified
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_iff_all_diagonal_certified : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n) ↔ ∀ t : ℕ, ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L
declarations.docstring: **PROVED equivalence.** Because the certified region is downward closed, "certified for cofinally many `t`" collapses to "certified at every `t`". So #249 is equivalent to the diagonal certificate holding at *every* rung — and its failure means the certified region is a bounded initial segment `[0, t*]`. (Stated for precision; the content of this section is the downward closure, not this equivalence.)

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_head_peel
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_head_peel (h N L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy h N (L + 1) = ((Nat.totient (N + h + 1) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient (N + 1) : ℤ)) * 2 ^ L + windowDiscrepancy h (N + 1) L
declarations.docstring: **Head peel.** Deepening a window at its *base* end is exact: the depth-`L+1` window at `N` is the depth-`L` window at `N+1` plus the head letter at place value `2^L`. (Contrast `windowDiscrepancy_succ`, which deepens at the *far* end.)

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_emod_truncate
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_emod_truncate (h : ℕ) : ∀ (j N k : ℕ), windowDiscrepancy h N (k + j) % 2 ^ k = windowDiscrepancy h (N + j) k % 2 ^ k
declarations.docstring: **Low bits are a top-of-window phenomenon.** The residue of the depth-`k+j` window based at `N`, modulo `2^k`, equals the residue of the depth-`k` window based at `N+j`: the two windows share their last `k` offsets, and those are the only offsets whose place value is below `2^k`. This is the exact `2`-adic locality law — everything a lift could hope to control by `2`-adic valuation lives at the far end of the window.

declarations.name: two_pow_dvd_windowDiscrepancy_iff
declarations.signature: theorem two_pow_dvd_windowDiscrepancy_iff (h N k j : ℕ) : ((2 : ℤ) ^ k ∣ windowDiscrepancy h N (k + j)) ↔ ((2 : ℤ) ^ k ∣ windowDiscrepancy h (N + j) k)
declarations.docstring: **All `2`-adic divisibility of a window is carried by its far end.** Restated from `windowDiscrepancy_emod_truncate`: `2^k ∣ A_{h,N,k+j}` iff `2^k ∣ A_{h,N+j,k}`. The `j` shallowest offsets — including every offset the dilation law reaches when the window is short — are irrelevant to every congruence modulo `2^k`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_base_descent
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_base_descent {h N k j : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill h (N + j) k) : certifiedKill h N (k + j)
declarations.docstring: **Base descent.** A certificate at base `N+j` and depth `k` upgrades to a certificate at base `N` and depth `k+j`. Both cells have the same window top `N + (k+j) = (N+j) + k`, hence *the same* exclusion radius `N + h + (k+j) + 2 = (N+j) + h + k + 2`; and by `windowDiscrepancy_emod_truncate` the deep residue reduces to the shallow one modulo `2^k`. A residue in `(B, 2^k − B)` therefore lifts to a residue in `(B, 2^{k+j} − B)`: reduction mod `2^k` can only decrease a nonnegative residue, and can raise its distance from the top of the range by at most `2^{k+j} − 2^k`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_window_subset
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_window_subset {h M k N L : ℕ} (hbase : N ≤ M) (htop : M + k ≤ N + L) (hcert : certifiedKill h M k) : certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: **Window monotonicity.** A certificate on the window `[M+1, M+k]` holds on every window `[N+1, N+L]` containing it: base down, top up. The depth half (`N = M`) is `certifiedKill_add`; the base half is `certifiedKill_base_descent`.

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_of_base_le
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_of_base_le {h N M : ℕ} (hNM : N ≤ M) (hcert : ∃ k, certifiedKill h M k) : ∃ L, certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: Certificates descend in the base point.

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_diagonal_of_ray
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_diagonal_of_ray {H N : ℕ} (hHN : H ≤ N) (hcert : ∃ k, certifiedKill H N k) : ∃ L, certifiedKill H H L
declarations.docstring: **The diagonal cell is free once any cell above it on the ray is certified.** The corpus deposits all sit on the diagonal `N = H`; this says the diagonal is the *easiest* point of the ray, not a distinguished one.

declarations.name: lift_target_of_ray_cell
declarations.signature: theorem lift_target_of_ray_cell {p H N k : ℕ} (hle : p * H ≤ N) (hcert : certifiedKill (p * H) N k) : ∃ L, certifiedKill (p * H) (p * H) L
declarations.docstring: **The lift target is a ray target.** To lift a certificate across the rung `H ↦ p·H` it suffices to certify *any* cell `(N, k)` with `N ≥ p·H` on the period ray of `p·H`; the diagonal cell then follows.

declarations.name: irrational_totient_series_of_lcm_ray_certificate_supply
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_totient_series_of_lcm_ray_certificate_supply (hsupply : ∀ t₀ : ℕ, ∃ t, t₀ ≤ t ∧ ∃ N, periodLcm t ≤ N ∧ ∃ k, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) N k) : Irrational (∑' n : ℕ, (Nat.totient n : ℝ) / 2 ^ n)
declarations.docstring: **The wave-23 reduction with base freedom.** A cofinal supply of certificates anywhere on or above the lcm diagonal proves #249. Strictly weaker hypothesis than `irrational_totient_series_of_lcm_diagonal_certificate_supply`, which pins the base to `N = H_t`.

declarations.name: tail_diff_int_of_base_le
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_int_of_base_le {h N M : ℕ} (hNM : N ≤ M) (hint : totientTail (N + h) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : totientTail (M + h) - totientTail M ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Integrality of the tail difference is upward closed in the base.** The real-analytic form of `certifiedKill_base_descent`.

declarations.name: exists_diagonalKill_antitone
declarations.signature: theorem exists_diagonalKill_antitone {t s : ℕ} (hts : t ≤ s) (hs : ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm s) (periodLcm s) L) : ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L
declarations.docstring: **The diagonal ladder is antitone.** `P t := ∃ L, certifiedKill (H_t) (H_t) L` satisfies `t ≤ s → P s → P t`. Proof: if `P t` fails then `R_{2H_t} − R_{H_t} ∈ ℤ`; by base descent every `R_{N+H_t} − R_N` with `N ≥ H_t` is an integer; by period-ray telescoping (`tail_diff_mul_mem_int`) so is `R_{N + m·H_t} − R_N`, and `H_s = m·H_t` with `H_s ≥ H_t`, so `R_{2H_s} − R_{H_s} ∈ ℤ` and `P s` fails too. Consequence: `P` is a threshold predicate — it holds exactly on an initial segment of `ℕ` (possibly all of `ℕ`). The 28 corpus deposits and the plateau argument that certifies every `t ≤ 66` are therefore *formal consequences* of any single certified cell above them. A "seed + lift" architecture has no seed content to climb on: the whole force sits in the lift.

declarations.name: diagonalKill_cofinal_iff_all
declarations.signature: theorem diagonalKill_cofinal_iff_all : (∀ t₀ : ℕ, ∃ t, t₀ ≤ t ∧ ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L) ↔ (∀ t : ℕ, ∃ L, certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L)
declarations.docstring: **Cofinality buys nothing.** Because `P` is antitone, a supply of diagonal kills at arbitrarily large scales is the same statement as a diagonal kill at *every* scale. The reduction's `∀ t₀, ∃ t ≥ t₀` shape is cosmetic.

declarations.name: base_descent_converse_fails
declarations.docstring: **The descent is strictly one-directional.** `certifiedKill 1 0 5` holds while `certifiedKill 1 1 4` — the window it strictly contains — fails. So window monotonicity cannot be reversed to climb from a low base to a high one, which is the direction the supply theorem needs.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_five_zero_twentyeight
declarations.docstring: Kernel check of `certifiedKill_base_descent` on a live instance: the corpus cell `(N, L) = (12, 16)` at period `5` descends twelve base points to `(0, 28)`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_two_pow_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_two_pow_dvd {h N L v : ℕ} (hrad : ((N : ℤ) + (h : ℤ) + (L : ℤ) + 2) < 2 ^ v) (hdvd : (2 : ℤ) ^ v ∣ windowDiscrepancy h N L) (hnd : ¬ ((2 : ℤ) ^ L ∣ windowDiscrepancy h N L)) : certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: **Valuation criterion.** A nonzero residue divisible by `2^v` is at distance at least `2^v` from `0` in `ℤ/2^L`. So if the window discrepancy has `2`-adic valuation at least `v` but less than `L`, and `2^v` exceeds the exclusion radius, the certificate fires. This is the only way pure `2`-adic valuation control certifies a kill; the price is `v > log₂(N + h + L + 2)`, which at the `t = 67` frontier means `v ≥ 97`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_far_end_valuation
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_far_end_valuation {h N k j : ℕ} (hrad : ((N : ℤ) + (h : ℤ) + ((k : ℤ) + (j : ℤ)) + 2) < 2 ^ k) (hdvd : (2 : ℤ) ^ k ∣ windowDiscrepancy h (N + j) k) (hnd : ¬ ((2 : ℤ) ^ (k + j) ∣ windowDiscrepancy h N (k + j))) : certifiedKill h N (k + j)
declarations.docstring: **Where the valuation would have to come from.** Combining `certifiedKill_of_two_pow_dvd` with `two_pow_dvd_windowDiscrepancy_iff`: a kill at `(N, k+j)` follows from exact `2^k`-divisibility of the depth-`k` window at the far end `N+j`, together with non-divisibility at full depth. The certifying data is the `2k` totient values `φ(N+j+h+1+i)`, `φ(N+j+1+i)` for `i < k` — all at the top of the window, none of them supplied by the rung below.

declarations.name: ray_coverage_card_le
declarations.signature: theorem ray_coverage_card_le (p N k : ℕ) : (((Finset.range k).filter (fun i => p ∣ (N + 1 + i))).card) ≤ k / p + 1
declarations.docstring: **Uniform coverage bound.** The exact dilation law `c_{pH}(p·e) = (p−1)·c_H(e)` reaches exactly the offsets divisible by `p`. In the depth-`k` window based at `N` those offsets number at most `k/p + 1`, *uniformly in `N`*. The base freedom bought by `certifiedKill_of_window_subset` therefore leaves the covered fraction at `1/p`.

declarations.name: window_letter_dilation
declarations.signature: theorem window_letter_dilation {p m H : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hm : ¬ p ∣ m) (hmH : ¬ p ∣ (m + H)) : (Nat.totient (p * (m + H)) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient (p * m) : ℤ) = ((p : ℤ) - 1) * ((Nat.totient (m + H) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient m : ℤ))
declarations.docstring: **The dilation law in general position.** For `p` prime coprime to both `m` and `m + H`, `φ(p(m+H)) − φ(pm) = (p−1)·(φ(m+H) − φ(m))`. This is the base-free form of `Recon249.diagCoeff_lift_coprime`, which only covers the diagonal `m = 1`.

declarations.name: window_letter_dilation_at
declarations.signature: theorem window_letter_dilation_at {p H N i m : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hm : N + 1 + i = p * m) (hmp : ¬ p ∣ m) (hmHp : ¬ p ∣ (m + H)) : (Nat.totient (N + p * H + 1 + i) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient (N + 1 + i) : ℤ) = ((p : ℤ) - 1) * ((Nat.totient (m + H) : ℤ) - (Nat.totient m : ℤ))
declarations.docstring: **The covered letters of a lifted window, at every base.** If the offset `i` of the depth-`k` window based at `N` for the period `p·H` is covered — `N+1+i = p·m` with `p ∤ m` and `p ∤ m+H` — then its letter is `(p−1)` times the period-`H` letter at `m`. `ray_coverage_card_le` bounds the number of such `i` by `k/p + 1`, uniformly in `N`: the base freedom won in §2 buys no extra coverage.

declarations.name: ray_coverage_at_67
declarations.docstring: **Coverage at the historical `p = 67` cell.** At depth `100`, now known to be the exact minimal diagonal depth there, at most `2` of the `100` offsets are reached by the exact dilation law at every base point `N`.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_zero_shift
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_zero_shift (N L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy 0 N L = 0
declarations.docstring: A zero shift has zero discrepancy.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_add_shift
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_add_shift (h₁ h₂ N L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy (h₁ + h₂) N L = windowDiscrepancy h₁ N L + windowDiscrepancy h₂ (N + h₁) L
declarations.docstring: **Shift additivity.** Splitting the shift `h₁ + h₂` splits the window discrepancy into the `h₁`-cell at base point `N` and the `h₂`-cell at base point `N + h₁`. Exact, with no hypotheses: the middle totient row `φ(N+h₁+1+j)` cancels.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_mul_shift
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_mul_shift (k h N L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy (k * h) N L = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, windowDiscrepancy h (N + i * h) L
declarations.docstring: **The `k`-fold decomposition.** A cell at the multiplied shift `k·h` is the sum of `k` cells at the certified shift `h`, at the consecutive base points `N, N+h, …, N+(k-1)h`. This is the base-point counterpart of the offset dilation `diagCoeff_lift_coprime` of `Recon249`. That law covers `⌊L'/p⌋` of the `L'` offsets exactly; this one covers all of them, at the price of `k` unknown summands instead of one.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_ladder_diagonal
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_ladder_diagonal (p H L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy (p * H) (p * H) L = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range p, windowDiscrepancy H ((p + i) * H) L
declarations.docstring: **The diagonal ladder step.** The lifted *diagonal* cell at height `p·H` is a sum of `p` cells at the old shift `H`, but at base points `pH, (p+1)H, …, (2p-1)H`: none of them is the certified cell `N = H`, and together they read the totient rows `p, p+1, …, 2p` where the direct computation reads only rows `p` and `2p`.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_ladder_offDiagonal
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_ladder_offDiagonal (k H L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy ((k + 1) * H) H L = windowDiscrepancy H H L + ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, windowDiscrepancy H ((2 + i) * H) L
declarations.docstring: **The off-diagonal ladder step — the A3 identity.** Placing the base point at the *old* height `H` (legitimate: the supply theorem `irrational_totient_series_of_lcm_certificate_supply` leaves `N` free) makes the certified cell `A_{H,H,L}` an exact summand of the lifted cell.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_double_offDiagonal
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_double_offDiagonal (H L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy (2 * H) H L = windowDiscrepancy H H L + windowDiscrepancy H (2 * H) L
declarations.docstring: The doubling case of the off-diagonal step: at a boundary `t+1 = 2^k` of the lcm ladder, where `periodLcm (t+1) = 2 · periodLcm t`, the whole lift is one new integer.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_double_diagonal
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_double_diagonal (H L : ℕ) : windowDiscrepancy (2 * H) (2 * H) L = windowDiscrepancy H (2 * H) L + windowDiscrepancy H (3 * H) L
declarations.docstring: The doubling case of the diagonal step, for comparison: two new integers, and neither of them is the certified cell.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_two_pow_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_two_pow_dvd {h N L v : ℕ} (hdvd : (2 : ℤ) ^ v ∣ windowDiscrepancy h N L) (hne : ¬ ((2 : ℤ) ^ L ∣ windowDiscrepancy h N L)) (hrad : ((N : ℤ) + h + L + 2) < 2 ^ v) : certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: **The 2-adic criterion.** A window discrepancy divisible by `2^v` but not by `2^L` has residue at distance at least `2^v` from both ends of the circle, so it certifies as soon as `2^v` exceeds the exclusion radius. Unlike the arc condition of `certifiedKill`, this hypothesis is stable under addition, which is what lets it pass through the decomposition of §1.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_lift_of_common_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_lift_of_common_dvd {k h N L v : ℕ} (hdvd : ∀ i < k, (2 : ℤ) ^ v ∣ windowDiscrepancy h (N + i * h) L) (hne : ¬ ((2 : ℤ) ^ L ∣ windowDiscrepancy (k * h) N L)) (hrad : ((N : ℤ) + (k * h : ℕ) + L + 2) < 2 ^ v) : certifiedKill (k * h) N L
declarations.docstring: **The additively stable lift.** If every one of the `k` summands of the decomposition `windowDiscrepancy_mul_shift` is divisible by `2^v`, with `2^v` above the *new* exclusion radius, and the total is not divisible by `2^L`, the multiplied shift is certified. This is a lift in the strict sense: hypotheses only about cells at the old shift `h`, a conclusion about the shift `k·h`, uniform in `k`. Its cost is stated honestly in the module docstring: `2^v` must exceed `N + k·h + L + 2`, and the measured valuations of real window discrepancies along the lcm ray are `1 … 6`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_ladder_lift
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_ladder_lift {k H L : ℕ} {e δ : ℤ} (hδ : |e| ≤ δ) (hcorr : (2 : ℤ) ^ L ∣ ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, windowDiscrepancy H ((2 + i) * H) L) - e)) (hlow : ((H : ℤ) + ((k + 1) * H : ℕ) + L + 2) + δ < windowDiscrepancy H H L % 2 ^ L) (hhigh : windowDiscrepancy H H L % 2 ^ L < 2 ^ L - (((H : ℤ) + ((k + 1) * H : ℕ) + L + 2) + δ)) : certifiedKill ((k + 1) * H) H L
declarations.docstring: **The off-diagonal ladder lift.** The A3 lift law. `e` is the fresh correction read modulo `2^L`, `δ` bounds it; the hypothesis on the old cell is its *residue* clearing the new exclusion radius by a further `δ`. With `e = δ = 0` this is the verbatim transfer `2^L ∣ (fresh correction) → certifiedKill H H L → certifiedKill ((k+1)·H) H L`. Uniform in `k`, hence available at every prime-power boundary of the lcm ladder and so on any infinite subfamily of them.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_double_lift
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_double_lift {H L : ℕ} {e δ : ℤ} (hδ : |e| ≤ δ) (hcorr : (2 : ℤ) ^ L ∣ (windowDiscrepancy H (2 * H) L - e)) (hlow : ((H : ℤ) + (2 * H : ℕ) + L + 2) + δ < windowDiscrepancy H H L % 2 ^ L) (hhigh : windowDiscrepancy H H L % 2 ^ L < 2 ^ L - (((H : ℤ) + (2 * H : ℕ) + L + 2) + δ)) : certifiedKill (2 * H) H L
declarations.docstring: The doubling case, written out: at an lcm boundary `t + 1 = 2^m` the entire lift is the residue of the single fresh cell `A_{H, 2H, L}`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_two_two_five
declarations.docstring: The certified cell: `A_{2,2,5} = 44`, residue `12`, exclusion radius `11`.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_two_four_five
declarations.docstring: The fresh correction at that cell: `A_{2,4,5} = 52`.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_two_two_five
declarations.docstring: The two summands, and the sum.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_four_two_five_emod
declarations.docstring: **The correction can annihilate a certificate exactly.** `44 + 52 = 96 ≡ 0 (mod 32)`: the fresh cell moves the certified residue `12` to the exact centre of the forbidden zone. So no bound `δ` short of `2^{L-1}` makes `certifiedKill_double_lift` unconditional.

declarations.name: annihilation_is_the_decomposition
declarations.docstring: The annihilation is an instance of `windowDiscrepancy_double_offDiagonal`, not a coincidence of the definition.

declarations.name: not_certifiedKill_six_six_six
declarations.docstring: The cell below fails at depth `6`: residue `14`, radius `20`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_twelve_six_six
declarations.docstring: The doubled cell, at the *old* base point, succeeds at the same depth: residue `36`, radius `26`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_periodLcm_offDiagonal_at_four
declarations.docstring: On the lcm ray: `certifiedKill (periodLcm 4) (periodLcm 3) 6`.

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_six_values
declarations.docstring: The values behind it: `270 + 278 = 548`.

declarations.name: two_dvd_correction_six
declarations.docstring: The correction's 2-adic valuation at that boundary is exactly `1`, where a verbatim transfer needs `≥ 6`. This is the divisibility route of `certifiedKill_lift_of_common_dvd` failing by five bits at the very first doubling boundary large enough to be interesting.

declarations.name: not_certifiedKill_diagonal_at_eight_depth14
declarations.docstring: The diagonal route must buy a bit: depth `14` does not certify at `t = 8`. (`certifiedKill_periodLcm_diagonal_at_eight` uses depth `15`.)

declarations.name: certifiedKill_offDiagonal_at_eight_depth14
declarations.docstring: **The off-diagonal deposit at `t = 8`, at the depth of the deposit below.** A legitimate instance of the free-`N` supply hypothesis `irrational_totient_series_of_lcm_certificate_supply`, and the first certificate in this repository placed off the diagonal.

declarations.name: emod_le_self_of_nonneg
declarations.signature: private lemma emod_le_self_of_nonneg {X b : ℤ} (hX : 0 ≤ X) (hb : 0 < b) : X % b ≤ X

declarations.name: windowDiscrepancy_emod_pow
declarations.signature: theorem windowDiscrepancy_emod_pow (h N L j : ℕ) (hj : j ≤ L) : windowDiscrepancy h N L % 2 ^ j = windowDiscrepancy h (N + (L - j)) j % 2 ^ j
declarations.docstring: **Only the right endpoint matters.** Modulo `2^j`, a depth-`L` window discrepancy is the depth-`j` window discrepancy with the same right endpoint `N + L`. The first `L - j` offsets carry place value at least `2^j` and drop out.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_endpoint
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_endpoint {h N L j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ L) (hcert : certifiedKill h (N + (L - j)) j) : certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: **Certification propagates down the anti-diagonal.** A depth-`j` certificate at base point `N + (L - j)` yields a depth-`L` certificate at base point `N`: same right endpoint, same exclusion radius, more depth.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_of_endpoint'
declarations.signature: theorem certifiedKill_of_endpoint' {h N L N' j : ℕ} (hj : j ≤ L) (hend : N + L = N' + j) (hcert : certifiedKill h N' j) : certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: The same statement with the endpoint written out: `N + L = N' + j`.

declarations.name: totientSeries
declarations.docstring: The #249 constant `S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ`.

declarations.name: tailDiff
declarations.signature: noncomputable def tailDiff (h N : ℕ) : ℝ
declarations.docstring: The shifted tail difference `D_{h,N} = R_{N+h} − R_N`, the quantity whose non-integrality is the content of a certified kill.

declarations.name: totientTail_succ
declarations.signature: theorem totientTail_succ (N : ℕ) : totientTail (N + 1) = 2 * totientTail N - (Nat.totient (N + 1) : ℝ)

declarations.name: tailDiff_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tailDiff_succ (h N : ℕ) : tailDiff h (N + 1) = 2 * tailDiff h N - ((Nat.totient (N + h + 1) : ℝ) - (Nat.totient (N + 1) : ℝ))

declarations.name: tailDiff_mem_int_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tailDiff_mem_int_succ {h N : ℕ} (hmem : tailDiff h N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : tailDiff h (N + 1) ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Integrality of the tail difference is upward closed in `N`.** Hence for a fixed period `h` the positions carrying a certificate form a downward-closed initial segment of `ℕ`, and "cofinally many `N`" is the same demand as "every `N`".

declarations.name: tailDiff_mem_int_mono
declarations.signature: theorem tailDiff_mem_int_mono {h M N : ℕ} (hMN : M ≤ N) (hmem : tailDiff h M ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : tailDiff h N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Integrality propagates from any position to every later one.

declarations.name: tailDiff_shift_mod_int
declarations.signature: theorem tailDiff_shift_mod_int (h N k : ℕ) : tailDiff h (N + k) - (2 : ℝ) ^ k * tailDiff h N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **The whole `N`-orbit at a fixed period is one number's binary expansion.** `D_{h,N+k} = 2^k·D_{h,N}` modulo `ℤ`. Sliding the base point is the doubling map on the fractional part; it manufactures no new arithmetic.

declarations.name: tailDiff_eq
declarations.signature: theorem tailDiff_eq (h N : ℕ) : tailDiff h N = (2 : ℝ) ^ N * ((2 : ℝ) ^ h - 1) * totientSeries - (((totientPrefix (N + h) : ℤ) - (totientPrefix N : ℤ) : ℤ) : ℝ)

declarations.name: tailDiff_mem_int_iff
declarations.signature: theorem tailDiff_mem_int_iff (h N : ℕ) : tailDiff h N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ) ↔ (2 : ℝ) ^ N * ((2 : ℝ) ^ h - 1) * totientSeries ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Certificate content, in closed form.** A kill at `(h, N)` is exactly the statement that `2^N·(2^h − 1)·S` is not an integer.

declarations.name: tailDiff_approx
declarations.signature: theorem tailDiff_approx (h N L : ℕ) : |(2 : ℝ) ^ L * tailDiff h N - (windowDiscrepancy h N L : ℝ)| ≤ (N : ℝ) + h + L + 2
declarations.docstring: The window discrepancy approximates `2^L · D_{h,N}` to within the exclusion radius of the certificate.

declarations.name: exists_depth
declarations.signature: private lemma exists_depth (C δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) : ∃ L : ℕ, 2 * (C + L) < δ * 2 ^ L

declarations.name: exists_near_multiple
declarations.signature: private lemma exists_near_multiple {A : ℤ} {L : ℕ} {r : ℤ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hnc : ¬ (r < A % 2 ^ L ∧ A % 2 ^ L < 2 ^ L - r)) : ∃ k : ℤ, |A - k * 2 ^ L| ≤ r
declarations.docstring: Failure of the residue certificate at depth `L` puts the window discrepancy within the exclusion radius of a multiple of `2^L`.

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_of_tailDiff_notMem_int
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_of_tailDiff_notMem_int {h N : ℕ} (hD : tailDiff h N ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : ∃ L, certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: **The converse bridge.** Non-integrality of the tail difference at `(h, N)` produces a `certifiedKill` at that very `(h, N)`, at some depth. Together with `tail_diff_notMem_int_of_certifiedKill` this makes the two representations *pointwise equivalent*: the residue certificate carries exactly the information "`D_{h,N} ∉ ℤ`" and nothing more.

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_iff
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_iff (h N : ℕ) : (∃ L, certifiedKill h N L) ↔ (2 : ℝ) ^ N * ((2 : ℝ) ^ h - 1) * totientSeries ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **The two representations are pointwise the same.** For every `(h, N)`, "some depth-`L` residue certificate fires" is *equivalent* to "`2^N(2^h−1)S ∉ ℤ`".

declarations.name: exists_certifiedKill_antitone
declarations.signature: theorem exists_certifiedKill_antitone {h M N : ℕ} (hMN : M ≤ N) (hkill : ∃ L, certifiedKill h N L) : ∃ L, certifiedKill h M L
declarations.docstring: **The free position parameter is a liability, not an asset.** A certificate at position `N` implies a certificate at every *smaller* position: the kill set of a fixed period is a downward-closed initial segment of `ℕ`. So walking the `N`-orbit upward — the cheap direction computationally, one totient pair per step (`windowDiscrepancy_shift_emod`) — walks strictly *into* the harder statements, and "cofinally many `N`" is the same demand as "every `N`".

declarations.name: killsPeriod
declarations.docstring: `killsPeriod x h`: no dyadic multiple of `(2^h − 1)·x` is an integer.

declarations.name: killsPeriod_iff
declarations.signature: theorem killsPeriod_iff (h : ℕ) : killsPeriod totientSeries h ↔ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ L, certifiedKill h N L

declarations.name: irrational_of_killsPeriod
declarations.signature: theorem irrational_of_killsPeriod (hk : ∀ h : ℕ, 0 < h → killsPeriod totientSeries h) : Irrational totientSeries
declarations.docstring: **The A4 reduction is faithful.** Killing every period in the non-integrality representation proves #249.

declarations.name: mersenneRatio
declarations.docstring: `mersenneRatio p H = (2^{pH} − 1)/(2^H − 1) = ∑_{i<p} 2^{H·i}`.

declarations.name: mersenneRatio_mul
declarations.signature: theorem mersenneRatio_mul (p H : ℕ) : (mersenneRatio p H : ℝ) * ((2 : ℝ) ^ H - 1) = (2 : ℝ) ^ (p * H) - 1

declarations.name: killsPeriod_lift_iff
declarations.signature: theorem killsPeriod_lift_iff (x : ℝ) (p H : ℕ) : killsPeriod x (p * H) ↔ ∀ N : ℕ, (mersenneRatio p H : ℝ) * ((2 : ℝ) ^ N * ((2 : ℝ) ^ H - 1) * x) ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **The lift, exactly.** Passing from scale `H` to scale `p·H` multiplies the tested quantity by the single integer `M = (2^{pH}−1)/(2^H−1)`. So the whole open content of the `H → pH` rung is the implication `x ∉ ℤ ⟹ M·x ∉ ℤ`, applied to `x = 2^N(2^H − 1)S` at every `N`.

declarations.name: tailDiff_lift_mod_int
declarations.signature: theorem tailDiff_lift_mod_int (p H N : ℕ) : tailDiff (p * H) N - (mersenneRatio p H : ℝ) * tailDiff H N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Additive form: modulo `ℤ`, the tail difference at scale `p·H` is `M` times the tail difference at scale `H`, at the *same* position `N`.

declarations.name: killsPeriod_one_div
declarations.signature: theorem killsPeriod_one_div {q h : ℕ} (hq1 : 1 < q) (hodd : ¬ 2 ∣ q) (hnd : ¬ q ∣ 2 ^ h - 1) : killsPeriod (1 / (q : ℝ)) h
declarations.docstring: **The lift fails as an implication about real numbers.** If `q` is an odd prime dividing `2^{pH} − 1` but not `2^H − 1`, then `x = 1/q` kills period `H` at *every* position `N`, and kills period `p·H` at *no* position. Such a `q` exists at every rung: by Zsygmondy, `2^{pH} − 1` has a primitive prime divisor for `pH > 6`, and every primitive divisor divides `M = (2^{pH}−1)/(2^H−1)` and not `2^H − 1`. The candidate denominators introduced at each rung of the lcm ladder are therefore genuinely new: they were not at issue at the scale below, so no information about the certified cell below can exclude them.

declarations.name: not_killsPeriod_one_div
declarations.signature: theorem not_killsPeriod_one_div {q h : ℕ} (hq1 : 1 < q) (hdvd : q ∣ 2 ^ h - 1) : ¬ killsPeriod (1 / (q : ℝ)) h

declarations.name: killsPeriod_lift_fails
declarations.signature: theorem killsPeriod_lift_fails {H p q : ℕ} (hq1 : 1 < q) (hodd : ¬ 2 ∣ q) (hdvd : q ∣ 2 ^ (p * H) - 1) (hnd : ¬ q ∣ 2 ^ H - 1) : killsPeriod (1 / (q : ℝ)) H ∧ ¬ killsPeriod (1 / (q : ℝ)) (p * H)

declarations.name: lift_fails_periodLcm_four_to_five
declarations.signature: theorem lift_fails_periodLcm_four_to_five : killsPeriod (1 / ((11 : ℕ) : ℝ)) (periodLcm 4) ∧ ¬ killsPeriod (1 / ((11 : ℕ) : ℝ)) (periodLcm 5)
declarations.docstring: **The smallest instance on the actual lcm ladder.** `H₄ = 12`, `H₅ = 60 = 5·H₄`, and the real number `1/11` kills period `12` at every position while killing period `60` at none — because `ord₁₁(2) = 10` divides `60` but not `12`. So the lift `certifiedKill H H L → ∃ L', certifiedKill (pH) (pH) L'`, read through the pointwise-equivalent non-integrality representation, is *false* as a statement about a general real number, already at the first odd-prime rung of the ladder.

declarations.name: periodLcm_dvd_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem periodLcm_dvd_of_le {s t : ℕ} (hst : s ≤ t) : periodLcm s ∣ periodLcm t
declarations.docstring: Periods are nested along the lcm ladder.

declarations.name: killsPeriod_of_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem killsPeriod_of_dvd {x : ℝ} {h₀ h : ℕ} (hdvd : h₀ ∣ h) (hk : killsPeriod x h) : killsPeriod x h₀
declarations.docstring: Killing a period kills all its divisors.

declarations.name: dvd_two_pow_sub_one_iff
declarations.signature: theorem dvd_two_pow_sub_one_iff {q d : ℕ} (hq1 : 1 < q) (hd : d.Prime) (hqd : q ∣ 2 ^ d - 1) (H : ℕ) : q ∣ 2 ^ H - 1 ↔ d ∣ H
declarations.docstring: **Order transfer.** If `q > 1` and `d` is prime with `q ∣ 2^d − 1`, then the multiplicative order of `2` modulo `q` is exactly `d`, so `q ∣ 2^H − 1` holds precisely when `d ∣ H`.

declarations.name: frontierWitness
declarations.docstring: `q₆₇ = 193707721`, one of the two prime factors of `2⁶⁷ − 1 = 193707721 · 761838257287`. Since `67` is prime, the multiplicative order of `2` modulo `q₆₇` is exactly `67`.

declarations.name: frontierWitness_kills_upto_66
declarations.signature: theorem frontierWitness_kills_upto_66 {t : ℕ} (ht : t ≤ 66) : killsPeriod (1 / (frontierWitness : ℝ)) (periodLcm t)
declarations.docstring: **The recorded corpus does not constrain the frontier cell at all.** The rational number `1/q₆₇` satisfies the conclusion of *every* deposit the repository owns: for every scale `t ≤ 66` and — via `killsPeriod_iff` — every position `N`, it makes `2^N(2^{H_t} − 1)·x` a non-integer, exactly as a `certifiedKill` would. It fails at `t = 67`.

declarations.name: exists_lattice_point
declarations.signature: theorem exists_lattice_point (M : ℕ) (hM : 0 < M) (D : ℝ) : ∃ D' : ℝ, (M : ℝ) * D' ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ) ∧ |D - D'| ≤ 1 / (2 * M)
declarations.docstring: The lattice `(1/M)·ℤ` is `1/(2M)`-dense.

declarations.name: frontier_multiplier_ge
declarations.signature: theorem frontier_multiplier_ge {L : ℕ} (hL : L ≤ periodLcm 66 * 66) : (2 : ℝ) ^ L ≤ (mersenneRatio 67 (periodLcm 66) : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: At the historically open `t = 67` rung the multiplier `M₆₇ = ∑_{i<67} 2^{i·H₆₆}` dwarfs `2^L` for every depth `L` up to `66·H₆₆ ≈ 7.8·10²⁸`.

declarations.name: frontier_ball_meets_lattice
declarations.signature: theorem frontier_ball_meets_lattice {L : ℕ} (hL : L ≤ periodLcm 66 * 66) (D : ℝ) : ∃ D' : ℝ, (mersenneRatio 67 (periodLcm 66) : ℝ) * D' ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ) ∧ |D - D'| ≤ 1 / (2 : ℝ) ^ (L + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The quantitative obstruction.** A depth-`L` certificate localises the tail difference to an interval of radius `(N+h+L+2)/2^L` (`tailDiff_approx`), never better than `2^{-L}`. But every ball of radius `2^{-(L+1)}` already contains a point of the lattice `(1/M₆₇)·ℤ`, on which the lift's conclusion `M₆₇·x ∉ ℤ` fails. So at the frontier no certificate of depth `L ≤ 66·H₆₆` — which includes the mandatory depth `98` and every depth that could conceivably be computed — localises well enough to decide the lift.

declarations.name: absWindowDiscrepancy
declarations.signature: def absWindowDiscrepancy (a : ℕ → ℕ) (h N L : ℕ) : ℤ
declarations.docstring: The window discrepancy of an arbitrary digit source `a : ℕ → ℕ`. Taking `a = Nat.totient` gives `windowDiscrepancy` on the nose.

declarations.name: absCertifiedKill
declarations.signature: def absCertifiedKill (a : ℕ → ℕ) (h N L : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.docstring: The certificate predicate for an arbitrary digit source `a : ℕ → ℕ`. Taking `a = Nat.totient` gives `certifiedKill` on the nose.

declarations.name: absWindowDiscrepancy_totient
declarations.signature: theorem absWindowDiscrepancy_totient (h N L : ℕ) : absWindowDiscrepancy Nat.totient h N L = windowDiscrepancy h N L
declarations.docstring: Faithfulness: the abstract discrepancy at `a = φ` *is* `windowDiscrepancy`.

declarations.name: absCertifiedKill_totient
declarations.signature: theorem absCertifiedKill_totient (h N L : ℕ) : absCertifiedKill Nat.totient h N L ↔ certifiedKill h N L
declarations.docstring: Faithfulness: the abstract certificate at `a = φ` *is* `certifiedKill`.

declarations.name: absWindowDiscrepancy_congr
declarations.signature: theorem absWindowDiscrepancy_congr {a b : ℕ → ℕ} {h N L : ℕ} (hab : ∀ n, n ≤ N + h + L → a n = b n) : absWindowDiscrepancy a h N L = absWindowDiscrepancy b h N L
declarations.docstring: The certificate at `(h, N, L)` depends on the digit source only through its values at indices `≤ N + h + L`.

declarations.name: not_absCertifiedKill_of_eq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem not_absCertifiedKill_of_eq_zero {a : ℕ → ℕ} {h N L : ℕ} (h0 : absWindowDiscrepancy a h N L = 0) : ¬ absCertifiedKill a h N L
declarations.docstring: A vanishing discrepancy is never a certificate: the exclusion radius is strictly positive, so residue `0` always sits in the forbidden zone.

declarations.name: absWindowDiscrepancy_eq_zero_of_periodic
declarations.signature: theorem absWindowDiscrepancy_eq_zero_of_periodic {a : ℕ → ℕ} {m h N L : ℕ} (hdvd : m ∣ h) (hper : ∀ k n, m + 1 ≤ n → a (n + k * m) = a n) (hN : m ≤ N) : absWindowDiscrepancy a h N L = 0
declarations.docstring: **Periodic annihilation.** If the digit source repeats with period `m` from position `m + 1` on, then every window at a period divisible by `m` has discrepancy exactly `0`, at every position `N ≥ m` and every depth.

declarations.name: surrogate
declarations.docstring: The **surrogate digit source at rung `m`**: identical to `φ` on `[0, 2m]`, and `m`-periodic above. It is admissible (`surrogate_le`) and it is blind to every certificate at a multiple of `m`.

declarations.name: surrogate_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem surrogate_of_le {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ 2 * m) : surrogate m n = Nat.totient n

declarations.name: surrogate_of_gt
declarations.signature: theorem surrogate_of_gt {m n : ℕ} (h : 2 * m < n) : surrogate m n = Nat.totient (m + 1 + ((n - 1) % m))

declarations.name: surrogate_le
declarations.signature: theorem surrogate_le (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (n : ℕ) : surrogate m n ≤ n
declarations.docstring: The surrogate is an admissible digit source: `a n ≤ n`, which is the only analytic property of `φ` used anywhere in the certificate soundness spine.

declarations.name: surrogate_eq_totient_congr
declarations.signature: theorem surrogate_eq_totient_congr (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) : ∃ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ n ∧ k % m = n % m ∧ surrogate m n = Nat.totient k
declarations.docstring: **The surrogate takes only genuine totient values, in the right residue class.** At every position `n` it equals `φ k` for some `1 ≤ k ≤ n` with `k ≡ n [MOD m]`. Consequently a property that is known to depend only on that value and residue can be transferred after its dependence has been proved. This theorem does not assert that the surrogate shares every analytic or factorization property of `φ`; parity is established separately by `surrogate_even`.

declarations.name: surrogate_even
declarations.signature: theorem surrogate_even (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) : Even (surrogate m n)
declarations.docstring: At every position `n ≥ 3`, both the surrogate and `φ` are even. Thus this basic parity test does not distinguish them on the stated range.

declarations.name: surrogate_add
declarations.signature: theorem surrogate_add (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) {n : ℕ} (hn : m + 1 ≤ n) : surrogate m (n + m) = surrogate m n
declarations.docstring: One period step.

declarations.name: surrogate_add_mul
declarations.signature: theorem surrogate_add_mul (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (k : ℕ) {n : ℕ} (hn : m + 1 ≤ n) : surrogate m (n + k * m) = surrogate m n
declarations.docstring: Full periodicity above `m`.

declarations.name: surrogate_inherits_low_certificates
declarations.signature: theorem surrogate_inherits_low_certificates {m h N L : ℕ} (hb : N + h + L ≤ 2 * m) (hcert : certifiedKill h N L) : absCertifiedKill (surrogate m) h N L
declarations.docstring: **Every certificate below the rung survives.** Any `certifiedKill h N L` whose whole window sits below `2m` is inherited verbatim by the surrogate. In particular the surrogate reproduces every deposit of `exists_diagonalKill_le_66` when `m` is the next rung.

declarations.name: surrogate_no_certificate_at_multiple
declarations.signature: theorem surrogate_no_certificate_at_multiple {m h N L : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (hdvd : m ∣ h) (hN : m ≤ N) : ¬ absCertifiedKill (surrogate m) h N L
declarations.docstring: **No certificate at the rung, or above it.** For every period divisible by `m`, every position `N ≥ m` and every depth `L`, the surrogate has no certificate. In particular the entire remaining lcm ladder `periodLcm t' , t' ≥ t+1` is dead for the surrogate at rung `periodLcm (t+1)`.

declarations.name: no_lift_from_data_below
declarations.signature: theorem no_lift_from_data_below (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, a n ≤ n) ∧ (∀ n, n ≤ 2 * m → a n = Nat.totient n) ∧ (∀ h N L, N + h + L ≤ 2 * m → certifiedKill h N L → absCertifiedKill a h N L) ∧ (∀ h, m ∣ h → ∀ N, m ≤ N → ∀ L, ¬ absCertifiedKill a h N L)
declarations.docstring: **The obstruction, packaged.** At every rung `m` there is an admissible digit source that (i) agrees with `φ` on all of `[0, 2m]`, (ii) therefore inherits every certificate whose window lies below `2m`, and (iii) has no certificate whatsoever at `m` or at any multiple of `m`, at any depth and any position `N ≥ m`. Therefore the corresponding uniform implication is not a consequence of only lower agreement, inherited certificates, and the size bound.

declarations.name: no_lift_at_lcm_rung
declarations.signature: theorem no_lift_at_lcm_rung (t : ℕ) : ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, a n ≤ n) ∧ (∀ n, n ≤ 2 * periodLcm (t + 1) → a n = Nat.totient n) ∧ (∀ L, 2 * periodLcm t + L ≤ 2 * periodLcm (t + 1) → certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L → absCertifiedKill a (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L) ∧ (∀ t', t + 1 ≤ t' → ∀ N, periodLcm (t + 1) ≤ N → ∀ L, ¬ absCertifiedKill a (periodLcm t') N L)
declarations.docstring: The same statement placed on the lcm ladder: at the boundary `t → t+1` the surrogate at `m = periodLcm (t+1)` copies `φ` up to `2 · periodLcm (t+1)`, inherits every rung-`≤ t` deposit of depth `L ≤ 2·periodLcm (t+1) - 2·periodLcm t`, and has no abstract certificate at any later lcm period, at positions `N ≥ periodLcm (t+1)`.

declarations.name: certifiedKill_two_two_eight
declarations.docstring: A kernel-checked diagonal deposit at the rung `t = 2` of the lcm ray (`periodLcm 2 = 2`), at depth `8`.

declarations.name: no_lift_from_lower_totient_data
declarations.signature: theorem no_lift_from_lower_totient_data (lift : ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ n, a n ≤ n) → ∀ t p L : ℕ, Nat.Prime p → periodLcm (t + 1) = p * periodLcm t → 2 * periodLcm t + L ≤ 2 * periodLcm (t + 1) → (∀ n, n ≤ 2 * periodLcm (t + 1) → a n = Nat.totient n) → absCertifiedKill a (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L → ∃ L', absCertifiedKill a (periodLcm (t + 1)) (periodLcm (t + 1)) L') : False
declarations.docstring: **The headline no-go.** There is no lift law of the shape `⟨a admissible⟩ → ⟨a agrees with φ below 2·H_{t+1}⟩ → ⟨depth of the rung-t certificate fits below 2·H_{t+1}⟩ → certificate at rung t → certificate at rung t+1`, even when `p` is required to be prime and the rungs are required to be genuine prime-power boundaries of the lcm ray. The witness is the boundary `t = 2 → 3`, `p = 3`, `H_2 = 2`, `H_3 = 6`, with the deposit `certifiedKill 2 2 8`. Read arithmetically: lower totient values, the size bound, and one fitted lower-rung certificate do not make the displayed uniform conclusion valid for all admissible sources. The theorem does not identify a unique missing input or rule out a stronger schema using additional facts specific to `φ`.

declarations.name: tail_diff_mem_int_of_le
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_mem_int_of_le {d N M : ℕ} (hNM : N ≤ M) (hmem : totientTail (N + d) - totientTail N ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)) : totientTail (M + d) - totientTail M ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Forward propagation of integrality.** An integer tail difference at period `d` and position `N` stays integral at every later position: the carry recurrence `D_d(M+1) = 2·D_d(M) − δ` preserves `ℤ`.

declarations.name: tail_diff_notMem_int_of_certifiedKill_dvd
declarations.signature: theorem tail_diff_notMem_int_of_certifiedKill_dvd {h N L d : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill h N L) (hdvd : d ∣ h) : totientTail (N + d) - totientTail N ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: **Divisor descent for the certificate.** A single certificate at period `h` and position `N` refutes integrality of the tail difference at *every* divisor of `h`, at the same position `N`. So the certificate lattice is closed downward under divisibility of the period: one diagonal deposit at `H_t` already carries every period dividing `H_t`.

declarations.name: periodLcm_diagonal_kills_all_small_periods
declarations.signature: theorem periodLcm_diagonal_kills_all_small_periods {t d L : ℕ} (hcert : certifiedKill (periodLcm t) (periodLcm t) L) (hd : 0 < d) (hdt : d ≤ t) : totientTail (periodLcm t + d) - totientTail (periodLcm t) ∉ Set.range ((↑) : ℤ → ℝ)
declarations.docstring: Amplification of the recorded deposits: a diagonal certificate at rung `t` refutes integrality at every period `d ≤ t`, all at the single position `N = H_t`. The restricted reverse implication formalized by `no_lift_from_lower_totient_data` is not a consequence of lower agreement and the size bound alone.

declarations.name: seamGreedy_postTwentySix_decision_twentySeven
