declarations.name: landing_is_not_escaped
declarations.signature: theorem landing_is_not_escaped (D : ℕ) (hD : 2 ≤ D) (hland : seamExcess (D + 1) = 2) : escapePotential (D + 1) < 0

declarations.name: le_of_descent_of_quadrupling
declarations.signature: theorem le_of_descent_of_quadrupling {f g : ℕ → ℕ} {S : ℕ} (hstep : ∀ s : ℕ, S ≤ s → f (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ≤ 4 * f s) (hceil : ∀ s : ℕ, S ≤ s → 4 * g s ≤ g (s + 1)) (hbase : f S ≤ g S) : ∀ s : ℕ, S ≤ s → f s ≤ g s
declarations.docstring: **The obstruction, as a theorem.** A solution of the forward descent law that starts under a ceiling which quadruples per row stays under it at every later row. Consequently no comparison of the descent law with such a ceiling can ever be contradictory: the C1 programme compares one upper bound with another.

declarations.name: seamSubsetTarget_quadruples
declarations.signature: theorem seamSubsetTarget_quadruples {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) : 4 * seamSubsetTarget s ≤ seamSubsetTarget (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: The corpus's own unconditional ceiling quadruples exactly.

declarations.name: descent_never_breaks_trivial_ceiling
declarations.signature: theorem descent_never_breaks_trivial_ceiling {f : ℕ → ℕ} {S : ℕ} (hS : 1 ≤ S) (hstep : ∀ s : ℕ, S ≤ s → f (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ≤ 4 * f s) (hbase : f S ≤ seamSubsetTarget S) : ∀ s : ℕ, S ≤ s → f s ≤ seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: **The trivial ceiling is useless, unconditionally.** Any sequence obeying the forward descent law from `S` on and starting below `seamSubsetTarget` remains below it forever. Since `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ seamSubsetTarget s` holds at every row anyway, the forward iteration produces no information.

declarations.name: descent_never_breaks_quartic_ceiling
declarations.signature: theorem descent_never_breaks_quartic_ceiling {f : ℕ → ℕ} {K S : ℕ} (hstep : ∀ s : ℕ, S ≤ s → f (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ≤ 4 * f s) (hbase : f S ≤ K * 4 ^ S) : ∀ s : ℕ, S ≤ s → f s ≤ K * 4 ^ s
declarations.docstring: The same for an arbitrary quartic ceiling `K * 4 ^ s`: a constant-factor improvement of the trivial ceiling changes nothing.

declarations.name: surplusModel
declarations.docstring: The persistent-surplus model: the half point is exceeded by the constant `c` at every row.

declarations.name: surplusModel_stepLaw
declarations.signature: theorem surplusModel_stepLaw {c N : ℕ} (hc : 2 ≤ c) (hN : 3 * c ≤ 2 * N) : BitR1.StepLaw (surplusModel c) N
declarations.docstring: The model obeys `BitR1`'s two-sided row law — the exact law the forced run imposes on `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder` — from any row `N` with `3 * c ≤ 2 * N` on.

declarations.name: surplusModel_constraints
declarations.signature: theorem surplusModel_constraints {c s : ℕ} (hc : 2 ≤ c) (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hcs : 3 * c ≤ 2 * s) : 2 ^ s < surplusModel c s ∧ 3 * surplusModel c s < 7 * 2 ^ s + 4 ∧ surplusModel c s < 2 ^ s + 2 * s ∧ 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ≤ 4 * surplusModel c s ∧ surplusModel c s ≤ 2 ^ (s + 1) ∧ surplusModel c s ≤ seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: **The model for the listed constraints.** The row-level inequalities enumerated in the theorem are satisfied by `2 ^ s + c`, together with persistent surplus.

declarations.name: exists_persistent_surplus_model
declarations.signature: theorem exists_persistent_surplus_model : ∃ f : ℕ → ℕ, BitR1.StepLaw f 5 ∧ ∀ s : ℕ, 5 ≤ s → 2 ^ s < f s ∧ 3 * f s < 7 * 2 ^ s + 4 ∧ f s < 2 ^ s + 2 * s ∧ 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ≤ 4 * f s ∧ f s ≤ 2 ^ (s + 1) ∧ f s ≤ seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: **No row-level argument can refute persistent surplus.** There is an explicit sequence that never returns to the half point and yet satisfies the two-sided row law, the good-row ceiling, the pin window, the right-branch window, the growth bound `≤ 2 ^ (s+1)` and the trivial ceiling, at every row `s ≥ 5`.

declarations.name: surplusModel_descent_under_trivial_ceiling
declarations.signature: theorem surplusModel_descent_under_trivial_ceiling : ∀ s : ℕ, 5 ≤ s → surplusModel 2 s ≤ seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: The model also realises the hypotheses of the abstract no-go: it is a descent solution sitting under the trivial ceiling.

declarations.name: surplusModel_descent_under_quartic_ceiling
declarations.signature: theorem surplusModel_descent_under_quartic_ceiling : ∀ s : ℕ, 5 ≤ s → surplusModel 2 s ≤ 1 * 4 ^ s
declarations.docstring: …and under an arbitrary quartic ceiling: the hypotheses of `descent_never_breaks_quartic_ceiling` are realised too.

declarations.name: band_invariant
declarations.docstring: **The band is forward-invariant.** From every value in `[2 ^ s + 2, 2 ^ s + 4]` the two-sided row law permits a step into `[2 ^ (s+1) + 2, 2 ^ (s+1) + 4]`. So the recurrence cannot expel a trajectory from the forced-run band, even allowing the below-pulse to be chosen adversarially at each row.

declarations.name: band_invariant_witness
declarations.docstring: The band-invariance hypothesis is satisfied: `r = 2 ^ 7 + 2` at `s = 7`.

declarations.name: surplus_25
declarations.docstring: Row `25` carries a surplus above the half point.

declarations.name: ascent_25
declarations.docstring: …and at row `25` the *lower* half of the two-sided row law fails, so the brand-new top rank is **not** selected at row `26`. The forward growth step of the C1 iteration is unavailable there.

declarations.name: exists_surplus_row_off_the_right_branch
declarations.signature: theorem exists_surplus_row_off_the_right_branch : ∃ s : ℕ, 5 ≤ s ∧ 2 ^ s < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ∧ LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1) ∧ ¬ (4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * s)
declarations.docstring: **C1's premise fails.** There are rows carrying a surplus above the half point at which the row law's growth half does not hold — equivalently, at which the successor row is good. So "persistent surplus" does not put every row on the right branch, and the forward iteration `a (s+1) ≥ 4 * a s - 2 * s` cannot be run under it.

declarations.name: three_surplus_rows_off_the_right_branch
declarations.signature: theorem three_surplus_rows_off_the_right_branch : (2 ^ 25 < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 25 ∧ LargestSkipLateAt 26) ∧ (2 ^ 31 < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 31 ∧ LargestSkipLateAt 32) ∧ (2 ^ 37 < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 37 ∧ LargestSkipLateAt 38)
declarations.docstring: Three such rows, so the failure is not a boundary artefact.

declarations.name: WindowMissCofinally
declarations.docstring: Cofinally many rows at which the one-step defect `4 * ρ s - ρ (s+1) - 2 ^ (s+1)` leaves the window `[4, 2 * s]`.

declarations.name: half_mem_of_windowMissCofinally
declarations.docstring: **A second cofinal criterion for `1/2 ∈ mersenneAchievementSet`.** Independent of `BitR2.RemainderReachesHalfPointCofinally`: it fires at rows whose remainder sits *above* the half point.

declarations.name: windowMiss_25
declarations.docstring: The window is missed at row `25`.

declarations.name: windowMiss_31
declarations.docstring: The window is missed at row `31`.

declarations.name: windowMiss_37
declarations.docstring: The window is missed at row `37`.

declarations.name: windowMissCofinally_witness
declarations.signature: theorem windowMissCofinally_witness {N : ℕ} (hN : N ≤ 37) : ∃ s : ℕ, N ≤ s ∧ 3 ≤ s ∧ ¬ (seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ≤ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ∧ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * s)
declarations.docstring: **The body of `WindowMissCofinally` is satisfied for every `N ≤ 37`**, so the criterion is not vacuous at the near end. (Whether it holds for *all* `N` is open; nothing here proves it.)

declarations.name: windowMiss_where_halfPoint_criterion_is_silent
declarations.docstring: **The new criterion is not subsumed.** At `s = 25, 31, 37` the criterion of `BitR2.RemainderReachesHalfPointCofinally` is silent (the remainder is above the half point) while the window-miss criterion fires.

declarations.name: lateAt_17
declarations.docstring: Row `17` is good, and *not* because of its brand-new top rank: the skipped late rank is `14`, with `2 * 17 = 34 < 42 = 3 * 14`.

declarations.name: rowLaw_holds_16
declarations.signature: theorem rowLaw_holds_16 : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 17 + 2 ^ 17 + 4 ≤ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 16 ∧ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 16 ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 17 + 2 ^ 17 + 2 * 16
declarations.docstring: At row `16` the two-sided row law holds (its defect is `7`, inside the window `[4, 32]`), so `BitR1.largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_window_miss` is silent.

declarations.name: surplus_16
declarations.docstring: Row `16` carries a surplus, so `BitR2`'s half-point criterion is silent.

declarations.name: rowLaw_blind_at_16
declarations.signature: theorem rowLaw_blind_at_16 : (seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 17 + 2 ^ 17 + 4 ≤ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 16 ∧ 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 16 ≤ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 17 + 2 ^ 17 + 2 * 16) ∧ 2 ^ 16 < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 16 ∧ 2 ^ 15 < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 16 ∧ 2 ^ 17 < 4 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 16 ∧ LargestSkipLateAt 17
declarations.docstring: **The row recurrence cannot see the good row it sits next to.** At `s = 16` every row-level certificate the corpus owns is silent: * the two-sided row law *holds*, so `BitR1.largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_window_miss` gives nothing; * `2 ^ 16 < ρ 16`, so `BitR2.exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_remainder_le_two_pow` gives nothing; * `2 ^ 15 < ρ 16`, so `BitR4.largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_remainder_le` gives nothing; * `2 ^ 17 < 4 * ρ 16`, so `BitR3.largestSkipLateAt_succ_of_small_remainder` gives nothing; and yet row `17` **is** good. The witness is rank `14`, not the brand-new top rank `16`, and the row recurrence only ever tracks the top rank. So the whole row-recurrence layer — the layer the C1 angle proposes to iterate — is strictly weaker than `LargestSkipLateAt`, independently of any ceiling.

declarations.name: sufficient_bound_is_sharp
declarations.signature: theorem sufficient_bound_is_sharp {c : ℕ} (hc : 2 ≤ c) {s : ℕ} (_hs : 5 ≤ s) (_hcs : 3 * c ≤ 2 * s) : ¬ (surplusModel c s ≤ 2 ^ s)
declarations.docstring: The exact shape of a bound that *would* close the question, for contrast with `surplusModel`: `ρ s ≤ 2 ^ s` at cofinally many rows. Anything weaker by an additive constant `≥ 2` is satisfied by the model, hence insufficient on row-level grounds alone.

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_le
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_le (weights : List ℕ) (C : ℕ) : integerGreedyRemainder weights C ≤ C

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_cons_take
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_cons_take {w C : ℕ} (ws : List ℕ) (h : w ≤ C) : integerGreedyRemainder (w :: ws) C = integerGreedyRemainder ws (C - w)

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_cons_skip
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_cons_skip {w C : ℕ} (ws : List ℕ) (h : ¬ w ≤ C) : integerGreedyRemainder (w :: ws) C = integerGreedyRemainder ws C

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_bracket
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_bracket (s d : ℕ) (hb0 : 0 < 2 ^ d - 1) : (2 ^ d - 1) * truncatedMersenneWeight s d ≤ 4 ^ s ∧ 4 ^ s < (2 ^ d - 1) * truncatedMersenneWeight s d + (2 ^ d - 1)

declarations.name: seamWeights_eq_prefix
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeights_eq_prefix {s : ℕ} (hs : 8 ≤ s) : seamWeights s = truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 :: truncatedMersenneWeight s 3 :: truncatedMersenneWeight s 4 :: truncatedMersenneWeight s 5 :: truncatedMersenneWeight s 6 :: truncatedMersenneWeight s 7 :: seamWeightsFrom s 8

declarations.name: row_facts
declarations.signature: private theorem row_facts {s : ℕ} (hs : 14 ≤ s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 ≤ seamSubsetTarget s ∧ truncatedMersenneWeight s 3 ≤ seamSubsetTarget s - truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 ∧ ¬ truncatedMersenneWeight s 4 ≤ seamSubsetTarget s - truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 - truncatedMersenneWeight s 3 ∧ ¬ truncatedMersenneWeight s 5 ≤ seamSubsetTarget s - truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 - truncatedMersenneWeight s 3 ∧ truncatedMersenneWeight s 6 ≤ seamSubsetTarget s - truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 - truncatedMersenneWeight s 3 ∧ truncatedMersenneWeight s 7 ≤
declarations.docstring: Everything the first six greedy decisions of a row `s ≥ 14` need, in one place: ranks `2, 3` are taken, ranks `4, 5` are skipped, ranks `6, 7` are taken, and the resulting capacity is at most `4 ^ s / 16002`.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_le_prefixCapacity
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_le_prefixCapacity {s : ℕ} (hs : 14 ≤ s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ seamSubsetTarget s - truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 - truncatedMersenneWeight s 3 - truncatedMersenneWeight s 6 - truncatedMersenneWeight s 7
declarations.docstring: **The four-rank prefix bound.** Row `s ≥ 14` of the concrete seam greedy takes ranks `2, 3, 6, 7`, skips ranks `4, 5`, and therefore never exceeds the capacity left after those four subtractions.

declarations.name: sixteen_thousand_two_mul_seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_le
declarations.signature: theorem sixteen_thousand_two_mul_seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_le {s : ℕ} (hs : 14 ≤ s) : 16002 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ 4 ^ s
declarations.docstring: **The unconditional row bound.** For every row `s ≥ 14`, `16002 * ρ_s ≤ 4 ^ s`. The only unconditional bound available at an arbitrary row before this was the trivial `2 * ρ_s ≤ 4 ^ s` coming from `ρ_s ≤ seamSubsetTarget s`.

declarations.name: two_mul_seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_le
declarations.signature: theorem two_mul_seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_le (s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s) : 2 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ 4 ^ s
declarations.docstring: The trivial bound the corpus already had, for comparison.

declarations.name: weightedBoolSum_replicate_false
declarations.signature: theorem weightedBoolSum_replicate_false (ws : List ℕ) (n : ℕ) : weightedBoolSum ws (List.replicate n false) = 0

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_length
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_length (s d : ℕ) : (seamWeightsFrom s d).length = s - d

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_add_le_of_certificate
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_add_le_of_certificate {s : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) {bits : List Bool} (hlen : bits.length = (seamWeights s).length) (hadm : weightedBoolSum (seamWeights s) bits ≤ seamSubsetTarget s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + weightedBoolSum (seamWeights s) bits ≤ seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: **Certificate transfer.** Any admissible Boolean selection of the seam weights bounds the greedy remainder. This is the general shape of an unconditional upper bound on `ρ_s`: a certificate, not a recurrence.

declarations.name: prefixCertificate
declarations.docstring: The explicit rank-`{2,3,6,7}` Boolean certificate of row `s`.

declarations.name: prefixCertificate_length
declarations.signature: theorem prefixCertificate_length {s : ℕ} (hs : 8 ≤ s) : (prefixCertificate s).length = (seamWeights s).length

declarations.name: weightedBoolSum_prefixCertificate
declarations.signature: theorem weightedBoolSum_prefixCertificate {s : ℕ} (hs : 8 ≤ s) : weightedBoolSum (seamWeights s) (prefixCertificate s) = truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 + truncatedMersenneWeight s 3 + truncatedMersenneWeight s 6 + truncatedMersenneWeight s 7

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_add_prefix_le
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_add_prefix_le {s : ℕ} (hs : 14 ≤ s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + (truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 + truncatedMersenneWeight s 3 + truncatedMersenneWeight s 6 + truncatedMersenneWeight s 7) ≤ seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: The four-rank certificate really is admissible and really does bound the remainder: the certificate transfer, instantiated.

declarations.name: barrier_arith
declarations.signature: private theorem barrier_arith {mp mq kp P : ℕ} (a1 : mp ≤ 4 * mq + 2 * kp) (a2 : 2 * kp + P ≤ mp) (a3 : 4 * mq < P) : False

declarations.name: mul_certificate_sum_le
declarations.signature: theorem mul_certificate_sum_le {s M : ℕ} (hM : 0 < M) : ∀ cert : List (ℕ × ℕ), (∀ p ∈ cert, (2 ^ p.1 - 1) * p.2 = M) → M * (cert.map fun p => truncatedMersenneWeight s p.1).sum ≤ (cert.map Prod.snd).sum * 4 ^ s
declarations.docstring: Clearing denominators: if every rank `d` of the certificate satisfies `(2 ^ d - 1) * m_d = M`, then `M * Σ_d ⌊4 ^ s / (2 ^ d - 1)⌋ ≤ (Σ_d m_d) * 4 ^ s`.

declarations.name: certificate_exceeds_half_point
declarations.signature: theorem certificate_exceeds_half_point {s : ℕ} {cert : List (ℕ × ℕ)} {M : ℕ} (hM : 0 < M) (hs1 : 1 ≤ s) (hcert : ∀ p ∈ cert, (2 ^ p.1 - 1) * p.2 = M) (hlt : 2 * (cert.map Prod.snd).sum < M) (hbig : 4 * M * 2 ^ s < 4 ^ s) : 2 ^ s + (cert.map fun p => truncatedMersenneWeight s p.1).sum < seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: **The barrier.** Let a *fixed* certificate be a finite list of ranks `d` with common-denominator data `(2 ^ d - 1) * m_d = M`. If its exact rational value `Σ_d 1 / (2 ^ d - 1) = (Σ_d m_d) / M` is *strictly* below `1 / 2` — that is, `2 * Σ_d m_d < M` — then from `4 * M * 2 ^ s < 4 ^ s` on the capacity left after the certificate is already larger than the half point `2 ^ s`. So no constant-depth explicit subset of the seam weights can ever certify `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ 2 ^ s`, and the `C2` route caps out at constant-factor improvements of the trivial `4 ^ s / 2`. The single escape is `2 * Σ_d m_d = M`, i.e. an exact finite Mersenne representation of `1 / 2`, which is Erdős `#257` answered positively outright.

declarations.name: prefixCertificate_value
declarations.docstring: The positive side, restated: `1/3 + 1/7 + 1/63 + 1/127 = 84000 / 168021` and `168021 - 2 * 84000 = 21`, so the certificate leaves `4 ^ s / 16002`.

declarations.name: prefixCertificate_exceeds_half_point
declarations.signature: theorem prefixCertificate_exceeds_half_point {s : ℕ} (hs : 20 ≤ s) : 2 ^ s + (truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 + truncatedMersenneWeight s 3 + truncatedMersenneWeight s 6 + truncatedMersenneWeight s 7) < seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: **The negative side, sharp.** The rank-`{2,3,6,7}` certificate can never witness `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ 2 ^ s`: from row `20` on, the capacity it leaves already exceeds the half point.

declarations.name: remainder_fourteen
declarations.docstring: The row-`14` remainder, computed in the kernel.

declarations.name: bound_fourteen_nonvacuous
declarations.docstring: The bound of §5 at `s = 14` is a statement about a real number, and it is true there with room to spare: `16002 * 392 = 6272784 ≤ 4 ^ 14 = 268435456`.

declarations.name: barrier_twenty_nonvacuous
declarations.signature: theorem barrier_twenty_nonvacuous : 2 ^ 20 + (truncatedMersenneWeight 20 2 + truncatedMersenneWeight 20 3 + truncatedMersenneWeight 20 6 + truncatedMersenneWeight 20 7) < seamSubsetTarget 20
declarations.docstring: And the barrier is not vacuous either: at `s = 20` the certificate capacity really does exceed `2 ^ 20`, while the true remainder there is far below it.

declarations.name: certificate_ratSum
declarations.signature: theorem certificate_ratSum {M : ℕ} (hM : 0 < M) : ∀ cert : List (ℕ × ℕ), (∀ p ∈ cert, (2 ^ p.1 - 1) * p.2 = M) → (cert.map fun p => mersenneWeightRat p.1).sum = ((cert.map Prod.snd).sum : ℚ) / (M : ℚ)
declarations.docstring: The common-denominator data really does compute the certificate's exact rational value `Σ_d 1 / (2 ^ d - 1)`.

declarations.name: certificate_lt_half_iff
declarations.signature: theorem certificate_lt_half_iff {M : ℕ} (hM : 0 < M) (cert : List (ℕ × ℕ)) (hcert : ∀ p ∈ cert, (2 ^ p.1 - 1) * p.2 = M) : (cert.map fun p => mersenneWeightRat p.1).sum < 1 / 2 ↔ 2 * (cert.map Prod.snd).sum < M
declarations.docstring: So the barrier hypothesis `2 * Σ_d m_d < M` is exactly "the certificate's exact value is strictly below `1 / 2`".

declarations.name: prefixCertificate_lt_half
declarations.signature: theorem prefixCertificate_lt_half : ([(2, 56007), (3, 24003), (6, 2667), (7, 1323)].map fun p => mersenneWeightRat p.1).sum < 1 / 2
declarations.docstring: The four-rank certificate, read as a rational: `1/3 + 1/7 + 1/63 + 1/127` is strictly below `1/2`, which is precisely why §7 applies to it.

declarations.name: HitAt
declarations.docstring: Row `s` is a **hit**: the deterministic seam greedy remainder has not risen above the half point. Cofinality of the hit set is exactly `Bit/R2`'s `RemainderReachesHalfPointCofinally`.

declarations.name: HitGapBoundedBy
declarations.docstring: The hit set meets every window of length `K`.

declarations.name: half_mem_of_hitGapBoundedBy
declarations.signature: theorem half_mem_of_hitGapBoundedBy {K : ℕ} (h : HitGapBoundedBy K) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet
declarations.docstring: **The bounded-gap criterion.** Any constant bound on the gaps of the hit set answers the `1/2` question of `#257` positively.

declarations.name: hitAt_of_rem
declarations.signature: theorem hitAt_of_rem {s : ℕ} (h : BitR3.rem s ≤ 2 ^ s) : HitAt s

declarations.name: not_hitAt_of_rem
declarations.signature: theorem not_hitAt_of_rem {s : ℕ} (h : ¬ (BitR3.rem s ≤ 2 ^ s)) : ¬ HitAt s

declarations.name: obeysRemainderCeiling_of_rem
declarations.signature: theorem obeysRemainderCeiling_of_rem {s : ℕ} (h : 3 * BitR3.rem s < 7 * 2 ^ s + 4) : ObeysRemainderCeiling s

declarations.name: pinEscape_of_rem
declarations.signature: theorem pinEscape_of_rem {s : ℕ} (h : ¬ (2 ^ s < BitR3.rem s ∧ BitR3.rem s < 2 ^ s + 2 * s)) : ¬ (2 ^ s < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ s + 2 * s)

declarations.name: not_hitGapBoundedBy_eight
declarations.docstring: **The sharp negative.** Nine consecutive rows carry no hit, so no window of length `8` meets the hit set everywhere. Combined with the measurement (maximal gap `7, 9, 9, 10, 10, 10` over `[3, S]` for `S = 100, 200, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000`), the least admissible `K` grows with the range: the bounded-gap route to `#257` is not available.

declarations.name: obeysCeiling_of_succ_of_bad
declarations.signature: theorem obeysCeiling_of_succ_of_bad {s : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hbad : ¬ LargestSkipLateAt (s + 1)) (hceil : ObeysRemainderCeiling (s + 1)) : ObeysRemainderCeiling s
declarations.docstring: **Downward transport.** If row `s + 1` is bad and obeys the remainder ceiling, then so does row `s` — with room to spare.

declarations.name: obeysCeiling_of_badRun
declarations.signature: theorem obeysCeiling_of_badRun : ∀ (k s : ℕ), 5 ≤ s → (∀ j : ℕ, j < k → ¬ LargestSkipLateAt (s + j + 1)) → ObeysRemainderCeiling (s + k) → ObeysRemainderCeiling s
declarations.docstring: The iterate: a run of bad rows transports the ceiling from the top of the run to its base.

declarations.name: exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_surplus_of_ceiling_above
declarations.signature: theorem exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_surplus_of_ceiling_above {N σ T : ℕ} (hN : 5 ≤ N) (hσ : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder N = 2 ^ N + σ) (hbig : 2 * N ≤ σ) (hT : 3 * N + 2 ≤ T) (hceil : ObeysRemainderCeiling T) : ∃ t : ℕ, N + 1 ≤ t ∧ LargestSkipLateAt t
declarations.docstring: **Theorem B, with the ceiling hypothesis moved off its row.** `Bit/R2`'s `exists_largestSkipLateAt_of_surplus` needs `ObeysRemainderCeiling (3 * N + 2)` exactly; downward transport across the bad run replaces that by *some* ceiling row at or above `3 * N + 2`.

declarations.name: CeilingCofinally
declarations.docstring: The remainder ceiling `3 * rem t < 7 * 2 ^ t + 4` holds at arbitrarily large rows. Every *good* row satisfies it unconditionally (`three_mul_remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLateAt`); this asks only that some row above every bound does.

declarations.name: PinEscapesCofinally
declarations.docstring: The remainder escapes the width-`2 * s` window just above the half point at arbitrarily large rows.

declarations.name: pinned_of_ceilingCofinally_of_not_half_mem
declarations.signature: theorem pinned_of_ceilingCofinally_of_not_half_mem (hceil : CeilingCofinally) (hnot : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∉ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ s : ℕ, M ≤ s → 2 ^ s < seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ s + 2 * s
declarations.docstring: **The pin, unconditionally in the ceiling.** If the remainder ceiling holds cofinally and `1/2` is not achieved, then the remainder is trapped in the window `(2 ^ s, 2 ^ s + 2 * s)` at *every* sufficiently large row — a window of width `2 * s` inside a range of size `2 ^ s`. `Bit/R2`'s `badRun_pins_remainder` gives the same conclusion at a base row `N` from the ceiling at the paired row `3 * N + 2` together with badness of the whole block `[N + 1, 3 * N + 2]`; here neither the pairing nor the block hypothesis is needed.

declarations.name: half_mem_of_ceilingCofinally_of_pinEscapes
declarations.docstring: **The endpoint, with the two cofinality hypotheses decoupled.** Weaker than `Bit/R2`'s `RemainderMissesHalfPointWindowCofinally`, which demands the ceiling at `3 * s + 2` and the window escape at `s` for the *same* `s`.

declarations.name: obeysCeiling_11_not_from_goodRow
declarations.docstring: The transported bound is not the trivial one: `rem 11 = 2485` is a genuine value strictly inside the ceiling, and row `11` is itself bad, so `three_mul_remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLateAt` does *not* apply to it.

declarations.name: exists_late_above_nine
declarations.signature: theorem exists_late_above_nine : ∃ t : ℕ, 9 + 1 ≤ t ∧ LargestSkipLateAt t

declarations.name: obeysCeiling_100
declarations.docstring: The ceiling row may be taken strictly above the paired row `3 * N + 2`; this is exactly what `Bit/R2`'s form cannot do.

declarations.name: exists_late_above_nine'
declarations.signature: theorem exists_late_above_nine' : ∃ t : ℕ, 9 + 1 ≤ t ∧ LargestSkipLateAt t

declarations.name: pin_occupied_eight
declarations.docstring: The pin window is not vacuously escaped: at row `8` the remainder really does sit inside it (`rem 8 = 265`, window `(256, 272)`), so `PinEscapesCofinally` is a genuine condition and not a tautology.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_top_band
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_top_band {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hband : 2 * s < 3 * d) : truncatedMersenneWeight s d = 2 ^ (2 * s - d) + 4 ^ (s - d)
declarations.docstring: In the top band `2 * s < 3 * d` (with `d < s`) the truncated Mersenne weight collapses to a two-term binary value: `⌊4 ^ s / (2 ^ d - 1)⌋ = 2 ^ (2 * s - d) + 4 ^ (s - d)`.

declarations.name: sum_seamWeightsFrom_top_band
declarations.signature: theorem sum_seamWeightsFrom_top_band (s : ℕ) : ∀ j k : ℕ, k + j = s → 2 ≤ k → 2 * s < 3 * k → 3 * (seamWeightsFrom s k).sum + 3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 = 3 * 2 ^ (2 * s - k + 1) + 4 ^ (s - k + 1)
declarations.docstring: Tail sum of the seam weight word from rank `k` upward, in the top band.

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_cons
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_cons (w : ℕ) (ws : List ℕ) (C : ℕ) : integerGreedyRemainder (w :: ws) C = if w ≤ C then integerGreedyRemainder ws (C - w) else integerGreedyRemainder ws C

declarations.name: greedy_allTrue
declarations.signature: theorem greedy_allTrue : ∀ (l : List ℕ) (C : ℕ), (∀ (j : ℕ) (b : Bool), (integerGreedyBits l C)[j]? = some b → b = true) → l.sum ≤ C ∧ integerGreedyRemainder l C = C - l.sum
declarations.docstring: If the descending greedy accepts every weight, the remainder is exactly the deficit `C - Σ`.

declarations.name: greedy_skip_tail
declarations.signature: theorem greedy_skip_tail : ∀ (l : List ℕ) (C k wk : ℕ), l[k]? = some wk → (integerGreedyBits l C)[k]? = some false → (∀ (j : ℕ) (b : Bool), k < j → (integerGreedyBits l C)[j]? = some b → b = true) → integerGreedyRemainder l C + (l.drop (k + 1)).sum < wk
declarations.docstring: **The skipped-position law.** If the descending greedy rejects the weight at position `k` and accepts every weight after it, then the final remainder plus the whole accepted tail is still strictly below the rejected weight.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_getElem?
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_getElem? (s : ℕ) : ∀ (j k : ℕ), k + j < s → (seamWeightsFrom s k)[j]? = some (truncatedMersenneWeight s (k + j))

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_drop
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_drop (s : ℕ) : ∀ (j k : ℕ), (seamWeightsFrom s k).drop j = seamWeightsFrom s (k + j)

declarations.name: seamGreedyWord_getElem?
declarations.signature: theorem seamGreedyWord_getElem? {s j : ℕ} (hj : j < s - 2) : (integerGreedyBits (seamWeights s) (seamSubsetTarget s))[j]? = some ((seamGreedyWord s) ⟨j, hj⟩)

declarations.name: mem_seamWordSupport_iff_greedyBit
declarations.signature: theorem mem_seamWordSupport_iff_greedyBit {s d : ℕ} (hd2 : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) : d ∈ seamWordSupport (seamGreedyWord s) ↔ (integerGreedyBits (seamWeights s) (seamSubsetTarget s))[d - 2]? = some true

declarations.name: remainder_add_tail_lt_weight
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_add_tail_lt_weight {s D : ℕ} (hD : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) D) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + (seamWeightsFrom s (D + 1)).sum < truncatedMersenneWeight s D
declarations.docstring: **The seam skip law.** If `D` is the largest false rank of row `s`, then the final greedy remainder plus the entire accepted suffix `D+1,…,s-1` is still strictly below the one weight the greedy could not afford at `D`.

declarations.name: three_mul_remainder_lt_of_lateSkip
declarations.signature: theorem three_mul_remainder_lt_of_lateSkip {s D : ℕ} (hD : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) D) (hband : 2 * s < 3 * D) : 3 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * 4 ^ (s - D) + 4
declarations.docstring: **PROVED, conditional.** A late largest false rank `D` (`2s < 3D`) implies the displayed upper bound. The imported `three_mul_remainder_lt_exactLateGap` already proves the same conclusion under the additional side condition `5 ≤ s`.

declarations.name: remainder_lt_of_lateSkip
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_lt_of_lateSkip {s D : ℕ} (hD : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) D) (hband : 2 * s < 3 * D) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ^ (s - D)
declarations.docstring: **PROVED, conditional.** Division-free repackaging: a late largest false rank `D` puts the seam greedy remainder strictly below `2 ^ (s + 1) + 4 ^ (s - D)`.

declarations.name: remainder_lt_of_terminal_skip
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_lt_of_terminal_skip {s : ℕ} (hD : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) (s - 1)) (hs : 5 ≤ s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4
declarations.docstring: **PROVED, conditional.** If the greedy skips the terminal rank `s - 1`, the remainder is below `2 ^ (s+1) + 4`.

declarations.name: six_mul_remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLate
declarations.signature: theorem six_mul_remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLate {s : ℕ} (h : LargestSkipLateAt s) : 6 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 13 * 2 ^ s + 8
declarations.docstring: **PROVED, conditional; strongest constant here.** On every row where `LargestSkipLateAt` holds, `6 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 13 * 2 ^ s + 8`. This improves the imported `Bit/R2` late-row ceiling from approximately `(7/3) * 2 ^ s` to approximately `(13/6) * 2 ^ s`. It does not establish that such rows occur cofinally.

declarations.name: remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLate
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLate {s : ℕ} (h : LargestSkipLateAt s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ s
declarations.docstring: **PROVED, conditional; weaker corollary.** A late row has remainder below `3 * 2 ^ s`. This is weaker than both the preceding `13/6` bound and the imported `Bit/R2` `7/3` ceiling.

declarations.name: remainder_lt_two_pow_succ_add_of_largestSkipLate
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_lt_two_pow_succ_add_of_largestSkipLate {s : ℕ} (h : LargestSkipLateAt s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s - 2)
declarations.docstring: **PROVED, conditional; weaker corollary.** On every late row the seam greedy remainder is below `2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 ^ (s - 2)`, i.e. below `2.25 · 2 ^ s`. The `13/6` bound above is stronger.

declarations.name: remainder_below_three_halfPoint_cofinally_of_half_mem
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_below_three_halfPoint_cofinally_of_half_mem (h : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ s : ℕ, N ≤ s ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ s
declarations.docstring: **PROVED implication, not a resolution of `#257`.** If `1/2` lies in the Mersenne achievement set then the seam greedy remainder is below `3 · 2 ^ s` at cofinally many rows. This conclusion already follows from `Skip/D2` and the stronger imported `Bit/R2` late-row ceiling.

declarations.name: half_mem_sandwich
declarations.signature: theorem half_mem_sandwich : (ErdosProblems.BitR2.RemainderReachesHalfPointCofinally → (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet) ∧ ((1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet → ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ s : ℕ, N ≤ s ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ s)
declarations.docstring: **PROVED pair of implications, neither premise discharged.** `Bit/R2` proves that `ρ s ≤ 2 ^ s` cofinally is sufficient for membership of `1/2`. Conversely, membership implies the weaker cofinal bound `ρ s < 3 · 2 ^ s`. The second implication is already derivable from `Skip/D2` and `Bit/R2`; the conjunction does not decide either premise and does not resolve `#257`.

declarations.name: greedyBits_fourteen
declarations.signature: private theorem greedyBits_fourteen : integerGreedyBits (seamWeights 14) (seamSubsetTarget 14) = [true, true, false, false, true, true, false, false, false, false, false, false]

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_fourteen
declarations.docstring: The row-`14` seam greedy remainder, exactly.

declarations.name: isLargestFalseRank_fourteen
declarations.docstring: Row `14` really does have its *terminal* rank `13` as largest false rank: the hypothesis of `remainder_lt_of_terminal_skip` is inhabited.

declarations.name: remainder_fourteen_lt_sharp
declarations.docstring: Concrete instance of the terminal-skip bound.

declarations.name: remainder_fourteen_lt
declarations.docstring: Concrete instance of the weaker `3 * 2 ^ s` corollary at row `14`.

declarations.name: remainder_twenty_lt
declarations.docstring: Concrete instance of the weaker `3 * 2 ^ s` corollary at row `20`, from the independent bit certificate of `Bit/Corr1`.

declarations.name: greedyRemainder_nil
declarations.signature: theorem greedyRemainder_nil (C : ℕ) : integerGreedyRemainder [] C = C

declarations.name: greedyRemainder_cons_take
declarations.signature: theorem greedyRemainder_cons_take {w C : ℕ} (t : List ℕ) (h : w ≤ C) : integerGreedyRemainder (w :: t) C = integerGreedyRemainder t (C - w)

declarations.name: greedyRemainder_cons_skip
declarations.signature: theorem greedyRemainder_cons_skip {w C : ℕ} (t : List ℕ) (h : ¬ w ≤ C) : integerGreedyRemainder (w :: t) C = integerGreedyRemainder t C

declarations.name: greedyRemainder_eq_sub_sum
declarations.signature: theorem greedyRemainder_eq_sub_sum : ∀ (l : List ℕ) {C : ℕ}, l.sum ≤ C → integerGreedyRemainder l C = C - l.sum

declarations.name: greedyRemainder_append
declarations.signature: theorem greedyRemainder_append : ∀ (l₁ l₂ : List ℕ) (C : ℕ), integerGreedyRemainder (l₁ ++ l₂) C = integerGreedyRemainder l₂ (integerGreedyRemainder l₁ C)

declarations.name: TailDominated
declarations.signature: def TailDominated (B : ℕ) : List ℕ → Prop | [] => True | w :: t => w ≤ t.sum + B ∧ TailDominated B t /-- **The counting bound.** A descending greedy on a tail-dominated word leaves at most `B`, provided the capacity itself is within `B` of the total. -/ theorem greedyRemainder_le_of_tailDominated : ∀ (l : List ℕ) {C B : ℕ}, TailDominated B l → C ≤ l.sum + B → integerGreedyRemainder l C ≤ B
declarations.docstring: Every entry is at most `B` above the sum of the entries strictly after it.

declarations.name: greedyRemainder_le_of_tailDominated
declarations.signature: theorem greedyRemainder_le_of_tailDominated : ∀ (l : List ℕ) {C B : ℕ}, TailDominated B l → C ≤ l.sum + B → integerGreedyRemainder l C ≤ B
declarations.docstring: **The counting bound.** A descending greedy on a tail-dominated word leaves at most `B`, provided the capacity itself is within `B` of the total.

declarations.name: tail_sum_succ
declarations.signature: theorem tail_sum_succ {s d : ℕ} (h : d < s) : (seamWeightsFrom s d).sum = truncatedMersenneWeight s d + (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum

declarations.name: tail_sum_le_weight
declarations.signature: theorem tail_sum_le_weight {s d : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) : (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum ≤ truncatedMersenneWeight s d

declarations.name: two_mul_weight_succ_le
declarations.signature: theorem two_mul_weight_succ_le {s d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) : 2 * truncatedMersenneWeight s (d + 1) ≤ truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: Consecutive seam weights at least halve.

declarations.name: seam_chain
declarations.signature: theorem seam_chain (s a : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (j : ℕ) (hj : a ≤ j) (hjs : j < s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s j + (seamWeightsFrom s (a + 1)).sum ≤ (seamWeightsFrom s (j + 1)).sum + truncatedMersenneWeight s a
declarations.docstring: The head weight `truncatedMersenneWeight s a` dominates every later weight by at least as much as it dominates its own tail.

declarations.name: seam_tailDominated
declarations.signature: theorem seam_tailDominated (s a : ℕ) (hs : 2 ≤ s) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (has : a < s) (j : ℕ) (hj : a ≤ j) : TailDominated (truncatedMersenneWeight s a - (seamWeightsFrom s (a + 1)).sum) (seamWeightsFrom s j)
declarations.docstring: Tail-dominance of the whole seam suffix from `a`, with the *exact* head slack `w_a - (tail after a)` as the constant.

declarations.name: four_pow_eq_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem four_pow_eq_two_pow (s : ℕ) : (4 : ℕ) ^ s = 2 ^ (2 * s)

declarations.name: four_pow_le_three_mul_head
declarations.signature: theorem four_pow_le_three_mul_head (s : ℕ) : (4 : ℕ) ^ s ≤ 3 * truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 + 2

declarations.name: target_le_two_mul_head
declarations.signature: theorem target_le_two_mul_head {s : ℕ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) : seamSubsetTarget s ≤ 2 * truncatedMersenneWeight s 2

declarations.name: seam_remainder_bound
declarations.signature: theorem seam_remainder_bound (s : ℕ) (hs : 3 ≤ s) (C : ℕ) (hC : C ≤ 2 * truncatedMersenneWeight s 2) : integerGreedyRemainder (seamWeights s) C + (seamWeightsFrom s 3).sum ≤ truncatedMersenneWeight s 2
declarations.docstring: **The counting/pigeonhole bound for the seam word, unconditional.** For any admissible capacity the descending greedy leaves at most the head slack `w_2 - (w_3 + ... + w_{s-1})`.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_add_tail_le
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_add_tail_le (s : ℕ) (hs : 3 ≤ s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + (seamWeightsFrom s 3).sum ≤ truncatedMersenneWeight s 2
declarations.docstring: Specialisation to the actual seam target.

declarations.name: four_pow_lt_weight_mul
declarations.signature: theorem four_pow_lt_weight_mul {s d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) : (4 : ℕ) ^ s < (2 ^ d - 1) * truncatedMersenneWeight s d + (2 ^ d - 1)

declarations.name: eight_mul_remainder_le
declarations.signature: theorem eight_mul_remainder_le (s : ℕ) (hs : 6 ≤ s) : 8 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ 4 ^ s
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional upper bound at an arbitrary row.** `8 * rem s ≤ 4 ^ s`. The corpus's previous unconditional bound at an arbitrary row was the trivial `rem s ≤ seamSubsetTarget s`, i.e. essentially `4 ^ s / 2`.

declarations.name: head_weight_small
declarations.signature: theorem head_weight_small {s d : ℕ} (hd : 3 ≤ d) : 7 * 2 ^ d * truncatedMersenneWeight s d ≤ 8 * 4 ^ s

declarations.name: tail_sum_small
declarations.signature: theorem tail_sum_small (s d : ℕ) (hd : 3 ≤ d) : 7 * 2 ^ (d - 1) * (seamWeightsFrom s d).sum ≤ 8 * 4 ^ s

declarations.name: four_mul_two_pow_le
declarations.signature: theorem four_mul_two_pow_le {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) : 4 * 2 ^ s ≤ 2 ^ (2 * s - 1)

declarations.name: head_lt_target
declarations.signature: theorem head_lt_target {s : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 < seamSubsetTarget s
declarations.docstring: The head weight is a strictly smaller admissible capacity than the seam target.

declarations.name: greedyRemainder_at_head_sub_one
declarations.signature: theorem greedyRemainder_at_head_sub_one (s : ℕ) (hs : 3 ≤ s) : integerGreedyRemainder (seamWeights s) (truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 - 1) = truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 - 1 - (seamWeightsFrom s 3).sum
declarations.docstring: **Sharpness.** At the admissible capacity `w_2 - 1` the descending greedy skips the head and then takes the whole tail, so the remainder is exactly the head slack minus one.

declarations.name: counting_bound_sharp
declarations.signature: theorem counting_bound_sharp (s : ℕ) (hs : 3 ≤ s) : 4 ^ s ≤ 21 * integerGreedyRemainder (seamWeights s) (truncatedMersenneWeight s 2 - 1) + 35
declarations.docstring: **The C5 no-go, quantitative.** The seam word admits an admissible capacity whose descending-greedy remainder is at least `(4 ^ s - 35) / 21`. Since the counting bound `seam_remainder_bound` is a property of the *word alone*, no gap/pigeonhole argument over `seamWeights s` can produce a remainder bound below `(4 ^ s - 35) / 21`; in particular none can reach `2 ^ s`.

declarations.name: exists_admissible_capacity_remainder_gt_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem exists_admissible_capacity_remainder_gt_two_pow (s : ℕ) (hs : 6 ≤ s) : ∃ C : ℕ, C < seamSubsetTarget s ∧ 2 ^ s < integerGreedyRemainder (seamWeights s) C
declarations.docstring: **The C5 verdict.** For every `s ≥ 6` the seam weight word carries an admissible capacity — strictly below the seam target itself — whose descending-greedy remainder exceeds `2 ^ s`. Hence `rem s ≤ 2 ^ s` is not a consequence of any property of `seamWeights s` together with admissibility of the capacity: no counting, gap or pigeonhole argument over the weight word can deliver it.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_drop
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_drop (s : ℕ) : ∀ (k a : ℕ), (seamWeightsFrom s a).drop k = seamWeightsFrom s (a + k)

declarations.name: seamEnteringRemainder
declarations.docstring: The residual the descending greedy carries into rank `a` of row `s`.

declarations.name: SkipsRank
declarations.docstring: Row `s` *skips* rank `a`: the residual entering that rank is below the weight there, so the greedy leaves the rank unselected.

declarations.name: seam_remainder_split
declarations.signature: theorem seam_remainder_split (s a : ℕ) (h2 : 2 ≤ a) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = integerGreedyRemainder (seamWeightsFrom s a) (seamEnteringRemainder s a)

declarations.name: remainder_add_tail_le_of_skipsRank
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_add_tail_le_of_skipsRank {s a : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h2 : 2 ≤ a) (has : a < s) (hskip : SkipsRank s a) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s + (seamWeightsFrom s (a + 1)).sum ≤ truncatedMersenneWeight s a
declarations.docstring: **The localised counting bound.** If row `s` skips rank `a`, the seam remainder is at most the head slack at `a`.

declarations.name: obeysCeiling_of_skipsRank
declarations.signature: theorem obeysCeiling_of_skipsRank {s a : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (h2 : 2 ≤ a) (has : a < s) (hskip : SkipsRank s a) (hslack : 3 * truncatedMersenneWeight s a < 7 * 2 ^ s + 4 + 3 * (seamWeightsFrom s (a + 1)).sum) : ErdosProblems.BitR2.ObeysRemainderCeiling s
declarations.docstring: **Ceiling from a late skip.** Whenever the head slack at a skipped rank is below `(7/3) * 2 ^ s`, row `s` obeys `Bit/R2`'s remainder ceiling — with no assumption that the row is good.

declarations.name: weight_last
declarations.signature: theorem weight_last (s : ℕ) (hs : 4 ≤ s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s (s - 1) = 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4

declarations.name: remainder_le_of_skipsLast
declarations.signature: theorem remainder_le_of_skipsLast {s : ℕ} (hs : 4 ≤ s) (hskip : SkipsRank s (s - 1)) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s ≤ 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4

declarations.name: obeysCeiling_of_skipsLast
declarations.signature: theorem obeysCeiling_of_skipsLast {s : ℕ} (hs : 4 ≤ s) (hskip : SkipsRank s (s - 1)) : ErdosProblems.BitR2.ObeysRemainderCeiling s

declarations.name: consecutive_gap_ge
declarations.signature: theorem consecutive_gap_ge {s d : ℕ} (hs : 2 ≤ s) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hds : d + 1 < s) : 2 ^ (s + 1) + truncatedMersenneWeight s (d + 1) ≤ truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: Consecutive seam weights never come within `2 ^ s` of each other: the adjacent gap is at least `2 ^ (s+1)`. So the "two consecutive weights differ by less than `2 ^ s`" hypothesis of the C5 programme is never satisfied.

declarations.name: skipsRank_eight
declarations.docstring: Row `8` skips its last rank `7`.

declarations.name: skipsRank_eleven
declarations.docstring: Row `11` skips rank `7`.

declarations.name: ceiling_at_bad_rows
declarations.docstring: **The point of the localised bound.** Rows `11` and `12` are *bad* — `Bit/R2` proves `¬ LargestSkipLateAt` there, so its good-row ceiling `three_mul_remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLateAt` says nothing — and yet the ceiling holds, certified here from the skip at rank `7` alone.

declarations.name: counting_bound_sharp_eight
declarations.docstring: The no-go, concretely at `s = 8`: the same weight word, at the admissible capacity `w_2 - 1 = 21844`, leaves `4443`, which is `17` times `2 ^ 8 = 256`.

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_nil
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_nil (C : ℕ) : integerGreedyRemainder [] C = C

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_cons
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_cons (w : ℕ) (ws : List ℕ) (C : ℕ) : integerGreedyRemainder (w :: ws) C = integerGreedyRemainder ws (if w ≤ C then C - w else C)
declarations.docstring: One step of the descending greedy.

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_le
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_le (ws : List ℕ) (C : ℕ) : integerGreedyRemainder ws C ≤ C
declarations.docstring: The greedy never increases the capacity.

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_append
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_append (pre post : List ℕ) (C : ℕ) : integerGreedyRemainder (pre ++ post) C = integerGreedyRemainder post (integerGreedyRemainder pre C)
declarations.docstring: The greedy on a concatenation is the greedy on the tail started from the remainder of the head.

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_skipped
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_skipped (pre post : List ℕ) (w C : ℕ) (h : integerGreedyRemainder pre C < w) : integerGreedyRemainder (pre ++ w :: post) C < w
declarations.docstring: **The lever.** If the descending greedy reaches a weight `w` with a residual strictly below `w`, then the *final* remainder is strictly below `w` as well: everything after that point only shrinks the residual.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_split
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_split (s : ℕ) {a b : ℕ} (hab : a ≤ b) : ∃ pre : List ℕ, seamWeightsFrom s a = pre ++ seamWeightsFrom s b
declarations.docstring: The seam weight word splits at every rank.

declarations.name: SeamSkipsAt
declarations.docstring: Rank `d` is *declined* by the descending seam greedy at row `s`: the residual left after ranks `2,…,d-1` have been offered is strictly below the rank-`d` weight. This is stated purely in terms of the corpus's own `seamWeights`, `seamSubsetTarget`, `truncatedMersenneWeight` and `integerGreedyRemainder`.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_skip
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_skip {s d : ℕ} (hds : d < s) (h : SeamSkipsAt s d) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: A declined rank bounds the whole remainder.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_late
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_late {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) : truncatedMersenneWeight s d = 2 ^ (2 * s - d) + 2 ^ (2 * s - 2 * d)
declarations.docstring: **Two-bit closed form.** Past two thirds of the row the truncated Mersenne weight is exactly a sum of two powers of two.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_terminal
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_terminal {s : ℕ} (hs : 4 ≤ s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s (s - 1) = 2 ^ (s + 1) + 4
declarations.docstring: The terminal rank of row `s` carries weight exactly `2 ^ (s + 1) + 4`.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_late_skip
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_late_skip {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (h : SeamSkipsAt s d) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)
declarations.docstring: A declined rank past two thirds of the row pins the remainder below `2 ^ (2 * s - d + 1)`.

declarations.name: late_skip_beats_trivial
declarations.signature: theorem late_skip_beats_trivial {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (h : SeamSkipsAt s d) : 2 ^ (d - 2) * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ (2 * s - 1)
declarations.docstring: The corpus's trivial unconditional bound is `ρ s ≤ 2 ^ (2 * s - 1) - 2 ^ s`. A declined rank `d` improves it by the factor `2 ^ (d - 2)`.

declarations.name: integerGreedyRemainder_eq_of_sum_le
declarations.signature: theorem integerGreedyRemainder_eq_of_sum_le (ws : List ℕ) (C : ℕ) (h : ws.sum ≤ C) : integerGreedyRemainder ws C = C - ws.sum
declarations.docstring: If the remaining weights fit inside the capacity, the greedy takes all of them.

declarations.name: two_pow_le_truncatedMersenneWeight
declarations.signature: theorem two_pow_le_truncatedMersenneWeight {s d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hds : d ≤ 2 * s) : 2 ^ (2 * s - d) ≤ truncatedMersenneWeight s d
declarations.docstring: Every truncated Mersenne weight dominates the power of two carrying its top bit.

declarations.name: truncatedMersenneWeight_le
declarations.signature: theorem truncatedMersenneWeight_le {s d : ℕ} (hd : 1 ≤ d) (hds : d ≤ s) : truncatedMersenneWeight s d ≤ 2 ^ (2 * s - d) + 2 ^ (2 * s - 2 * d + 1)
declarations.docstring: Companion upper bound: the weight exceeds its top bit by less than `2 ^ (2*s-2*d+1)`. (Valid at every rank, not only the late ones.)

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_sum_lower_aux
declarations.signature: private theorem seamWeightsFrom_sum_lower_aux (s : ℕ) : ∀ n : ℕ, n + 2 ≤ s → 2 ^ (s + n + 1) ≤ (seamWeightsFrom s (s - n)).sum + 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: The suffix of seam weights from rank `a` onwards already sums to `2 ^ (2*s-a+1) - 2 ^ (s+1)`.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_sum_lower
declarations.signature: theorem seamWeightsFrom_sum_lower {s a : ℕ} (ha2 : 2 ≤ a) (ha : a ≤ s) : 2 ^ (2 * s - a + 1) ≤ (seamWeightsFrom s a).sum + 2 ^ (s + 1)

declarations.name: SeamSkipsLast
declarations.docstring: `d` is the **largest** rank declined by the seam greedy at row `s`: the residual after ranks `2,…,d-1` sits strictly below the rank-`d` weight (so `d` is declined) and weakly above the total of all higher-rank weights (so every rank above `d` is taken).

declarations.name: SeamSkipsLast.toSkipsAt
declarations.signature: theorem SeamSkipsLast.toSkipsAt {s d : ℕ} (h : SeamSkipsLast s d) : SeamSkipsAt s d

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_eq_of_skipsLast
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_eq_of_skipsLast {s d : ℕ} (hds : d < s) (h : SeamSkipsLast s d) : ∃ R : ℕ, R < truncatedMersenneWeight s d ∧ (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum ≤ R ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s = R - (seamWeightsFrom s (d + 1)).sum
declarations.docstring: Exact evaluation of the remainder from a largest declined rank.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_late_largest_skip
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_late_largest_skip {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (h : SeamSkipsLast s d) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 ^ (2 * s - 2 * d)
declarations.docstring: **The bound the project was missing.** If the largest declined rank of row `s` lies past two thirds of the row, the remainder is below `2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 ^ (2 * s - 2 * d)` — for late `d` an exponentially sharper statement than the trivial `ρ s ≤ 2 ^ (2 * s - 1) - 2 ^ s`.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_largest_skip
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_largest_skip {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (h : SeamSkipsLast s d) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ (2 * s - 2 * d + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1)
declarations.docstring: **The bound at an arbitrary row.** With no lateness hypothesis at all: if `d` is the largest declined rank of row `s` then `ρ s < 2 ^ (2 * s - 2 * d + 1) + 2 ^ (s + 1)`. The whole `4 ^ s` scale of the trivial bound is gone; what is left is governed by `d` alone.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_three_mul_two_pow
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_three_mul_two_pow {s d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (h : SeamSkipsLast s d) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ s
declarations.docstring: The same, collapsed: a late largest declined rank forces `ρ s < 3 * 2 ^ s`.

declarations.name: late_largest_skip_beats_trivial
declarations.signature: theorem late_largest_skip_beats_trivial {s d : ℕ} (hs : 3 ≤ s) (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hds : d < s) (hlate : 2 * s < 3 * d) (h : SeamSkipsLast s d) : 2 ^ (s - 3) * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ (2 * s - 1)
declarations.docstring: Comparison with the corpus's trivial unconditional bound `ρ s ≤ 2 ^ (2 * s - 1) - 2 ^ s`: a late largest declined rank improves it by the factor `2 ^ (s - 3)`.

declarations.name: four_pow_eq
declarations.signature: private theorem four_pow_eq (s : ℕ) : (4 : ℕ) ^ s = 2 ^ s * 2 ^ s

declarations.name: seamSubsetTarget_two_mul
declarations.signature: private theorem seamSubsetTarget_two_mul (s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s) : 2 * seamSubsetTarget s = 4 ^ s - 2 * 2 ^ s

declarations.name: seamSkipsAt_five
declarations.signature: theorem seamSkipsAt_five {s : ℕ} (hs : 6 ≤ s) : SeamSkipsAt s 5
declarations.docstring: After ranks `2` and `3` the residual of row `s` (`s ≥ 6`) is below `4 ^ s / 31`, hence ranks `4` and `5` are both declined.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_rank_five
declarations.signature: theorem seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_lt_of_rank_five {s : ℕ} (hs : 6 ≤ s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 4 ^ s / 31
declarations.docstring: **Unconditional.** For every row `s ≥ 6` the seam integer-greedy remainder is strictly below `4 ^ s / 31`.

declarations.name: eight_mul_remainder_lt
declarations.signature: theorem eight_mul_remainder_lt {s : ℕ} (hs : 6 ≤ s) : 8 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 2 ^ (2 * s - 1)
declarations.docstring: The same statement in the shape that compares directly with the corpus's trivial bound `ρ s ≤ 2 ^ (2 * s - 1) - 2 ^ s`.

declarations.name: seamSkipsAt_fourteen_thirteen
declarations.docstring: Row 14 declines its terminal rank 13, and `2 * 14 < 3 * 13`, so this is a *late* skip. The hypothesis of every theorem in §4 is therefore satisfiable.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_fourteen_lt
declarations.docstring: The row-14 instance of §4, with the exact numbers.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_fourteen
declarations.docstring: Row 14 is an explicit *hit* for the target inequality `ρ s ≤ 2 ^ s`: `seamIntegerGreedyRemainder 14 = 392 ≤ 16384`. Recorded so that no statement above is vacuous about the target itself.

declarations.name: seamSkipsLast_fourteen_thirteen
declarations.docstring: Rank `13` is also the *largest* declined rank of row `14` (there is nothing above it), so `SeamSkipsLast` is inhabited.

declarations.name: seamWeightsFrom_sixteen_two
declarations.docstring: Row `16` has largest declined rank `14`, with rank `15` genuinely taken — so the higher-rank sum in `SeamSkipsLast` is not degenerate.

declarations.name: seamIntegerGreedyRemainder_sixteen_lt
declarations.docstring: The headline bound of §5, instantiated at row `16`: `ρ 16 < 2 ^ 17 + 2 ^ 4 = 131088`, against the trivial bound `ρ 16 ≤ 2 ^ 31 - 2 ^ 16 = 2147418112`. (The true value is `71791`.)

declarations.name: corpus_already_proves_C4_core
declarations.signature: theorem corpus_already_proves_C4_core {s D : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (hD : IsLargestFalseRank (seamGreedyWord s) D) (hband : 2 * s < 3 * D) : 3 * seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ (s + 1) + 2 * 4 ^ (s - D) + 4
declarations.docstring: C4's `three_mul_remainder_lt_of_lateSkip` is, statement for statement, the pre-existing corpus theorem `Erdos249257.three_mul_remainder_lt_exactLateGap` (modulo the removable side condition `5 ≤ s`). This term-mode proof uses the corpus lemma only.

declarations.name: corpus_already_proves_C4_headline
declarations.signature: theorem corpus_already_proves_C4_headline {s : ℕ} (hs : 5 ≤ s) (h : LargestSkipLateAt s) : seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ s
declarations.docstring: C4's headline `remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLate` (`ρ s < 3 * 2 ^ s`) is *strictly weaker* than the pre-existing `Bit/R2` ceiling `ObeysRemainderCeiling s` (`ρ s < (7/3) * 2 ^ s`), which C4 imports and never mentions. Derived here from R2 alone.

declarations.name: corpus_already_proves_C4_necessary_condition
declarations.signature: theorem corpus_already_proves_C4_necessary_condition (h : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ∈ mersenneAchievementSet) : ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ s : ℕ, N ≤ s ∧ seamIntegerGreedyRemainder s < 3 * 2 ^ s
declarations.docstring: C4's `#257` "necessary condition" is a three-line corollary of two corpus theorems C4 imports (`Skip/D2`'s equivalence and `Bit/R2`'s ceiling). No part of C4's new machinery is needed.

declarations.name: C4_six_mul_is_sharper_than_R2_ceiling
declarations.signature: theorem C4_six_mul_is_sharper_than_R2_ceiling {s : ℕ} (h : LargestSkipLateAt s) : ErdosProblems.BitR2.ObeysRemainderCeiling s
declarations.docstring: What IS new: C4's `six_mul_remainder_lt_of_largestSkipLate` (`6 ρ < 13 * 2 ^ s + 8`, i.e. `ρ < (13/6) 2 ^ s`) does imply R2's ceiling (`3 ρ < 7 * 2 ^ s + 4`, i.e. `ρ < (7/3) 2 ^ s`) and is strictly sharper. So the genuine delta of this file is the constant `7/3 → 13/6`, about 7%.

declarations.name: summable_and_tsum_rterm_dconv
declarations.signature: theorem summable_and_tsum_rterm_dconv {f g : ℕ → ℝ} {s : ℝ} (hf : Summable (rterm f s)) (hg : Summable (rterm g s)) : Summable (rterm (dconv f g) s) ∧ ∑' n, rterm (dconv f g) s n = (∑' n, rterm f s n) * (∑' n, rterm g s n)
declarations.docstring: The real Dirichlet series of a convolution is the product of the two series.

declarations.name: sq_tsum_le
declarations.signature: theorem sq_tsum_le {a g b m : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ n, 0 ≤ a n) (hg : ∀ n, 0 ≤ g n) (hb : ∀ n, 0 ≤ b n) (hga : ∀ n, g n ≤ a n) (h1 : ∀ n, n ≠ 0 → a n ≤ dconv g b n) (h2 : ∀ n, n ≠ 0 → dconv g g n ≤ m n) (B : ℝ) (h3 : ∀ X : ℕ, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range X, b n / n ≤ B) {s : ℝ} (hs : 1 ≤ s) (hsa : Summable (rterm a s)) (hsm : Summable (rterm m s)) : (∑' n, rterm a s n) ^ 2 ≤ B ^ 2 * ∑' n, rterm m s n
declarations.docstring: The comparison at one real `s ≥ 1` where the series of `a` and `m` converge.

declarations.name: tendsto_real_of_tendsto_LSeries
declarations.signature: theorem tendsto_real_of_tendsto_LSeries {f : ℕ → ℝ} {r : ℝ} (h : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ((s : ℂ) - 1) * LSeries (fun n => (f n : ℂ)) s) (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 (r : ℂ))) : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (s - 1) * ∑' n, rterm f s n) (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 r)
declarations.docstring: The real part of `(s - 1) L(f, s)` along real `s`.

declarations.name: false_of_pole_comparison
declarations.signature: theorem false_of_pole_comparison {a g b m : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : ∀ n, 0 ≤ a n) (hg : ∀ n, 0 ≤ g n) (hb : ∀ n, 0 ≤ b n) (hga : ∀ n, g n ≤ a n) (h1 : ∀ n, n ≠ 0 → a n ≤ dconv g b n) (h2 : ∀ n, n ≠ 0 → dconv g g n ≤ m n) (B : ℝ) (h3 : ∀ X : ℕ, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range X, b n / n ≤ B) {ra rm : ℝ} (hra : 0 < ra) (hrm : rm ≠ 0) (hA : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ((s : ℂ) - 1) * LSeries (fun n => (a n : ℂ)) s) (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 (ra : ℂ))) (hM : Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ((s : ℂ) - 1) * LSeries (fun n => (m n : ℂ)) s) (𝓝[>] 1) (𝓝 (rm : ℂ))) : False
declarations.docstring: **The pole comparison.** Nonnegative sequences with `a ≤ g ⋆ b`, `g ⋆ g ≤ m`, `g ≤ a` and `∑ b(n) / n` bounded cannot have Dirichlet series with simple poles at `s = 1` of positive residue for `a` and nonzero residue for `m`.

declarations.signature: theorem prime_of_mem_normalizedFactors {I 𝔭 : Ideal (𝓞 K)} (h : 𝔭 ∈ normalizedFactors I) : 𝔭.IsPrime ∧ 𝔭 ≠ ⊥

declarations.name: card_le_sum_countSupp
declarations.signature: theorem card_le_sum_countSupp (P : Ideal (𝓞 K) → Prop) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : Nat.card {I : Ideal (𝓞 K) // absNorm I = n} ≤ ∑ x ∈ n.divisorsAntidiagonal, countSupp K P x.1 * countSupp K (fun 𝔭 => ¬ P 𝔭) x.2

declarations.signature: theorem sum_countSupp_mul_le (M : Type*) [Field M] [NumberField M] [Algebra K M] (P : Ideal (𝓞 K) → Prop) (hsplit : ∀ 𝔭 : Ideal (𝓞 K), 𝔭.IsPrime → 𝔭 ≠ ⊥ → P 𝔭 → ∃ Q₁ Q₂ : Ideal (𝓞 M), Q₁.IsPrime ∧ Q₁ ≠ ⊥ ∧ Q₂.IsPrime ∧ Q₂ ≠ ⊥ ∧ absNorm Q₁ = absNorm 𝔭 ∧ absNorm Q₂ = absNorm 𝔭 ∧ Q₁.comap (algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 M)) = 𝔭 ∧ Q₂.comap (algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 M)) = 𝔭 ∧ Q₁ ≠ Q₂) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : ∑ x ∈ n.divisorsAntidiagonal, countSupp K P x.1 * countSupp K P x.2 ≤ Nat.card {Q : Ideal (𝓞 M) // absNorm Q = n}

declarations.name: sum_inv_absNorm_le_prod
declarations.signature: theorem sum_inv_absNorm_le_prod (F : Finset (Ideal (𝓞 K))) (hF : ∀ 𝔭 ∈ F, 2 ≤ absNorm 𝔭) (T : Finset (Ideal (𝓞 K))) (hT : ∀ I ∈ T, I ≠ ⊥ ∧ ∀ 𝔭 ∈ normalizedFactors I, 𝔭 ∈ F) : ∑ I ∈ T, ((absNorm I : ℝ))⁻¹ ≤ ∏ 𝔭 ∈ F, (1 - ((absNorm 𝔭 : ℝ))⁻¹)⁻¹

declarations.name: inv_one_sub_le_exp
declarations.signature: theorem inv_one_sub_le_exp {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx : x ≤ 1 / 2) : (1 - x)⁻¹ ≤ Real.exp (2 * x)

declarations.signature: theorem prod_inv_one_sub_le_exp (F : Finset (Ideal (𝓞 K))) (hF : ∀ 𝔭 ∈ F, 2 ≤ absNorm 𝔭) : ∏ 𝔭 ∈ F, (1 - ((absNorm 𝔭 : ℝ))⁻¹)⁻¹ ≤ Real.exp (2 * ∑ 𝔭 ∈ F, ((absNorm 𝔭 : ℝ))⁻¹)

declarations.name: exists_prime_pow_absNorm
declarations.signature: theorem exists_prime_pow_absNorm {𝔭 : Ideal (𝓞 K)} (hp : 𝔭.IsPrime) (h0 : 𝔭 ≠ ⊥) : ∃ p k : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ 0 < k ∧ absNorm 𝔭 = p ^ k ∧ (p : 𝓞 K) ∈ 𝔭

declarations.name: card_le_finrank_of_forall_mem
declarations.signature: theorem card_le_finrank_of_forall_mem {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (F : Finset (Ideal (𝓞 K))) (hF : ∀ 𝔭 ∈ F, 𝔭.IsPrime ∧ (p : 𝓞 K) ∈ 𝔭) : F.card ≤ Module.finrank ℚ K

declarations.name: exists_bound_sum_inv_absNorm
declarations.signature: theorem exists_bound_sum_inv_absNorm (N₀ : ℕ) : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ F : Finset (Ideal (𝓞 K)), (∀ 𝔭 ∈ F, 𝔭.IsPrime ∧ 𝔭 ≠ ⊥ ∧ ¬ (Nat.Prime (absNorm 𝔭) ∧ N₀ < absNorm 𝔭)) → ∑ 𝔭 ∈ F, ((absNorm 𝔭 : ℝ))⁻¹ ≤ C
declarations.docstring: The primes excluded by `P 𝔭 := (absNorm 𝔭 prime ∧ N₀ < absNorm 𝔭)` have uniformly bounded sums of reciprocal norms.

declarations.name: sum_countSupp_div_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_countSupp_div_le (N₀ : ℕ) : ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ X : ℕ, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range X, (countSupp K (fun 𝔭 => ¬ (Nat.Prime (absNorm 𝔭) ∧ N₀ < absNorm 𝔭)) n : ℝ) / n ≤ B
declarations.docstring: **The `¬P`-part converges at `s = 1`** for `P 𝔭 := (absNorm 𝔭 prime ∧ N₀ < absNorm 𝔭)`.

declarations.name: NoIntegerOrbit
declarations.docstring: `NoIntegerOrbit α` : no positive integer multiple of `α` is an integer. For real `α` this is equivalent to irrationality of `α`.

declarations.name: fract_natCast_mul_of_lt_one
declarations.signature: theorem fract_natCast_mul_of_lt_one {x : ℝ} {m : ℕ} (h : (m : ℝ) * Int.fract x < 1) : Int.fract ((m : ℝ) * x) = (m : ℝ) * Int.fract x
declarations.docstring: Scaling a real by a natural number is transparent to `Int.fract` as long as the scaled fractional part has not yet wrapped.

declarations.name: step_of_close
declarations.signature: private theorem step_of_close {α : ℝ} {ε : ℝ} {a b : ℕ} (hab : a < b) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) (h : |Int.fract ((b : ℝ) * α) - Int.fract ((a : ℝ) * α)| < ε) : ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ (Int.fract ((k : ℝ) * α) < ε ∨ 1 - ε < Int.fract ((k : ℝ) * α))
declarations.docstring: From two orbit points landing in the same `ε`-bin, extract a positive index whose orbit point is within `ε` of `0` or of `1`.

declarations.name: exists_small_step
declarations.signature: theorem exists_small_step {α : ℝ} {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) : ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ (Int.fract ((k : ℝ) * α) < ε ∨ 1 - ε < Int.fract ((k : ℝ) * α))
declarations.docstring: Dirichlet's pigeonhole step: some positive orbit index lands `ε`-close to `0` or to `1`. No hypothesis on `α` is needed.

declarations.name: exists_pos_nat_fract_mem_Ioo
declarations.signature: theorem exists_pos_nat_fract_mem_Ioo {α : ℝ} (hα : NoIntegerOrbit α) {c d : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hcd : c < d) (hd : d ≤ 1) : ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ c < Int.fract ((n : ℝ) * α) ∧ Int.fract ((n : ℝ) * α) < d
declarations.docstring: **Forward orbits of an integer-return-free rotation are dense.** For every subinterval `(c,d) ⊆ [0,1]` there is a *positive* index whose orbit point lands strictly inside.

declarations.name: carryStaircase
declarations.signature: def carryStaircase (t : R) (n : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) R
declarations.docstring: The `(n+1)`-dimensional **carry staircase** with parameter `t`: `t` on and below the diagonal, `1` strictly above.

declarations.name: staircaseReduced
declarations.signature: private def staircaseReduced (t : R) (n : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) R
declarations.docstring: The upper-triangular matrix obtained from `carryStaircase` by subtracting each row from its successor.

declarations.name: staircaseReduced_blockTriangular
declarations.signature: private theorem staircaseReduced_blockTriangular (t : R) (n : ℕ) : (staircaseReduced t n).BlockTriangular id

declarations.name: det_carryStaircase
declarations.signature: theorem det_carryStaircase (t : R) (n : ℕ) : (carryStaircase t n).det = t * (t - 1) ^ n
declarations.docstring: **Exact determinant of the carry staircase.** The value depends only on `t` and the size, never on which staircase was realised.

declarations.name: exists_staircase_indices
declarations.signature: theorem exists_staircase_indices {α β : ℝ} (hα : NoIntegerOrbit α) (hβ : NoIntegerOrbit β) (n : ℕ) : ∃ I J : Fin n → ℕ, (∀ a, 0 < I a) ∧ (∀ b, 0 < J b) ∧ Function.Injective I ∧ Function.Injective J ∧ ∀ a b : Fin n, ⌊Int.fract ((I a : ℝ) * α) + Int.fract ((J b : ℝ) * β)⌋ = if (b : ℕ) ≤ (a : ℕ) then 1 else 0
declarations.docstring: **Staircase realisation.** Two rotations without integer returns realise, in the two-dimensional carry `⌊fract (i α) + fract (j β)⌋`, the full `n × n` staircase pattern — with strictly positive and pairwise distinct indices.

declarations.name: log_factorial_eq_sum_primes
declarations.signature: theorem log_factorial_eq_sum_primes (n : ℕ) : Real.log (n.factorial : ℝ) = ∑ p ∈ (Ioc 0 n).filter Nat.Prime, ((n.factorial.factorization p : ℕ) : ℝ) * Real.log p
declarations.docstring: `log n! = ∑_{p ≤ n} v_p(n!) log p`.

declarations.name: div_le_factorization_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem div_le_factorization_factorial {n p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : n / p ≤ n.factorial.factorization p
declarations.docstring: The first Legendre term: `⌊n/p⌋ ≤ v_p(n!)`.

declarations.name: factorization_factorial_le_div
declarations.signature: theorem factorization_factorial_le_div {n p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : ((n.factorial.factorization p : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ n / ((p : ℝ) - 1)
declarations.docstring: The geometric Legendre bound: `v_p(n!) ≤ n / (p - 1)`.

declarations.name: log_factorial_le
declarations.signature: theorem log_factorial_le (n : ℕ) : Real.log (n.factorial : ℝ) ≤ n * Real.log n
declarations.docstring: `log n! ≤ n log n`.

declarations.name: sub_le_log_factorial
declarations.signature: theorem sub_le_log_factorial (n : ℕ) : n * Real.log n - n ≤ Real.log (n.factorial : ℝ)
declarations.docstring: `n log n - n ≤ log n!`, from `n^n / n! ≤ e^n`.

declarations.name: sum_log_primes_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_log_primes_le (n : ℕ) : ∑ p ∈ (Ioc 0 n).filter Nat.Prime, Real.log p ≤ Real.log 4 * n
declarations.docstring: Chebyshev's bound `θ(n) ≤ n log 4`, restated on the natural numbers.

declarations.name: div_sub_one_le_natDiv
declarations.signature: theorem div_sub_one_le_natDiv (n p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) : (n : ℝ) / p - 1 ≤ ((n / p : ℕ) : ℝ)

declarations.name: primeLogSum
declarations.docstring: Mertens' sum `∑_{p ≤ n} log p / p`.

declarations.name: primeLogSum_le
declarations.signature: theorem primeLogSum_le (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : primeLogSum n ≤ Real.log n + Real.log 4
declarations.docstring: Upper half of Mertens' first theorem: `∑_{p ≤ n} log p / p ≤ log n + log 4`.

declarations.name: log_div_mul_pred_le_telescope
declarations.signature: theorem log_div_mul_pred_le_telescope (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) / (((n : ℝ) + 1) * n) ≤ (Real.log n + 2) / n - (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 1) + 2) / ((n : ℝ) + 1)
declarations.docstring: One telescoping step: `log (n+1) / ((n+1) n) ≤ g n - g (n+1)` for `g k = (log k + 2) / k`.

declarations.name: sum_primes_log_div_mul_pred_le
declarations.signature: theorem sum_primes_log_div_mul_pred_le (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : ∑ p ∈ (Ioc 0 n).filter Nat.Prime, Real.log p / (p * ((p : ℝ) - 1)) ≤ 2 - (Real.log n + 2) / n
declarations.docstring: The prime-power correction is at most `2`: `∑_{p ≤ n} log p / (p (p-1)) ≤ 2 - (log n + 2)/n`.

declarations.name: log_sub_three_le_primeLogSum
declarations.signature: theorem log_sub_three_le_primeLogSum (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : Real.log n - 3 ≤ primeLogSum n
declarations.docstring: Lower half of Mertens' first theorem: `log n - 3 ≤ ∑_{p ≤ n} log p / p`.

declarations.name: abs_primeLogSum_sub_log_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_primeLogSum_sub_log_le (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : |primeLogSum n - Real.log n| ≤ 3
declarations.docstring: **Mertens' first theorem** with an explicit constant: `|∑_{p ≤ n} log p / p - log n| ≤ 3` for every `n ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: mertens_first
declarations.signature: theorem mertens_first (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : |∑ p ∈ (Ioc 0 n).filter Nat.Prime, Real.log p / p - Real.log n| ≤ 3
declarations.docstring: **Mertens' first theorem**, stated on the prime sum itself: `|∑_{p ≤ n} log p / p - log n| ≤ 3` for every `n ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: sum_Ioc_mul_eq_sub_add_sum
declarations.signature: theorem sum_Ioc_mul_eq_sub_add_sum {a F f : ℕ → ℝ} (hF : ∀ k, F (k + 1) = F k + a (k + 1)) {M N : ℕ} (hMN : M ≤ N) : ∑ k ∈ Ioc M N, a k * f k = F N * f N - F M * f M + ∑ k ∈ Ico M N, F k * (f k - f (k + 1))
declarations.docstring: Discrete summation by parts on `(M, N]`.

declarations.name: sum_Ico_telescope
declarations.signature: theorem sum_Ico_telescope (g : ℕ → ℝ) {M N : ℕ} (h : M ≤ N) : ∑ k ∈ Ico M N, (g k - g (k + 1)) = g M - g N
declarations.docstring: Telescoping on `[M, N)`.

declarations.name: primeLogSum_succ
declarations.signature: theorem primeLogSum_succ (k : ℕ) : primeLogSum (k + 1) = primeLogSum k + (if (k + 1).Prime then Real.log ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) else 0)

declarations.name: sbp_term_bound
declarations.signature: theorem sbp_term_bound {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) {F : ℝ} (hF : |F - Real.log k| ≤ 3) : |F * (1 / Real.log k - 1 / Real.log ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) - (Real.log (Real.log ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)) - Real.log (Real.log k))| ≤ 4 * (1 / Real.log k - 1 / Real.log ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ))
declarations.docstring: One summation-by-parts term against the telescoping `log log`.

declarations.name: abs_sum_inv_primes_sub_loglog_le
declarations.signature: theorem abs_sum_inv_primes_sub_loglog_le {M N : ℕ} (hM : 2 ≤ M) (hMN : M ≤ N) : |∑ p ∈ (Ioc M N).filter Nat.Prime, (1 : ℝ) / p - (Real.log (Real.log N) - Real.log (Real.log M))| ≤ 10 / Real.log M
declarations.docstring: **Mertens' second theorem, difference form**, with an explicit constant: for `2 ≤ M ≤ N`, `|∑_{M < p ≤ N} 1/p - (log log N - log log M)| ≤ 10 / log M`.

declarations.name: card_primes_Ioc_mul_log_le
declarations.signature: theorem card_primes_Ioc_mul_log_le {M x : ℕ} (hM : 1 ≤ M) : (((Ioc M x).filter Nat.Prime).card : ℝ) * Real.log M ≤ Real.log 4 * x
declarations.docstring: The number of primes in `(M, x]` is at most `x log 4 / log M`.

declarations.name: exists_prime_hom_not_isSquare
declarations.signature: theorem exists_prime_hom_not_isSquare {K M : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] [Field M] [NumberField M] [Algebra K M] (hfin : Module.finrank K M = 2) (b : 𝓞 K) (γ : M) (hγ : γ ^ 2 = algebraMap K M (b : K)) (hγK : γ ∉ Set.range (algebraMap K M)) (N : ℕ) : ∃ ℓ : ℕ, ℓ.Prime ∧ N < ℓ ∧ ∃ φ : 𝓞 K →+* ZMod ℓ, ¬ (φ b ≠ 0 ∧ IsSquare (φ b))
declarations.docstring: **A non-square is a non-square modulo infinitely many primes.** If `M = K(γ)` is a quadratic extension of number fields with `γ ^ 2 = b ∈ 𝓞 K`, then for every `N` some prime `ℓ > N` carries a ring homomorphism `φ : 𝓞 K → ZMod ℓ` with `φ b` zero or a non-square.

declarations.name: exists_prime_hom_not_isSquare_of_irreducible
declarations.signature: theorem exists_prime_hom_not_isSquare_of_irreducible {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] (b : 𝓞 K) (hb : ¬ IsSquare (algebraMap (𝓞 K) K b)) [hirr : Fact (Irreducible (X ^ 2 - C (algebraMap (𝓞 K) K b) : K[X]))] (N : ℕ) : ∃ ℓ : ℕ, ℓ.Prime ∧ N < ℓ ∧ ∃ φ : 𝓞 K →+* ZMod ℓ, ¬ (φ b ≠ 0 ∧ IsSquare (φ b))
declarations.docstring: The same statement with `M = K(√b)` realised as `AdjoinRoot (X ^ 2 - b)`, once that polynomial is known to be irreducible.

declarations.name: exists_prime_hom_not_isSquare_of_not_isSquare
declarations.signature: theorem exists_prime_hom_not_isSquare_of_not_isSquare {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K] (b : 𝓞 K) (hb : ¬ IsSquare (algebraMap (𝓞 K) K b)) (N : ℕ) : ∃ ℓ : ℕ, ℓ.Prime ∧ N < ℓ ∧ ∃ φ : 𝓞 K →+* ZMod ℓ, ¬ (φ b ≠ 0 ∧ IsSquare (φ b))
declarations.docstring: **A non-square of `𝓞 K` is a non-square modulo infinitely many primes.** If `b ∈ 𝓞 K` is not a square in `K`, then for every `N` some prime `ℓ > N` carries a ring homomorphism `φ : 𝓞 K → ZMod ℓ` with `φ b` zero or a non-square.

declarations.name: trace_algebraMap_mul
declarations.signature: theorem trace_algebraMap_mul (c : K) (y : M) : Algebra.trace K M (algebraMap K M c * y) = c * Algebra.trace K M y

declarations.name: exists_eq_add_mul
declarations.signature: theorem exists_eq_add_mul (hfin : Module.finrank K M = 2) (γ : M) (hγK : γ ∉ Set.range (algebraMap K M)) (x : M) : ∃ u v : K, x = algebraMap K M u + algebraMap K M v * γ

declarations.name: trace_algebraMap_eq
declarations.signature: theorem trace_algebraMap_eq (hfin : Module.finrank K M = 2) (c : K) : Algebra.trace K M (algebraMap K M c) = 2 * c

declarations.name: trace_gen_eq_zero
declarations.signature: theorem trace_gen_eq_zero (b : K) (γ : M) (hγ : γ ^ 2 = algebraMap K M b) (hγK : γ ∉ Set.range (algebraMap K M)) : Algebra.trace K M γ = 0

declarations.name: key_identity
declarations.signature: theorem key_identity (hfin : Module.finrank K M = 2) (b : K) (γ : M) (hγ : γ ^ 2 = algebraMap K M b) (hγK : γ ∉ Set.range (algebraMap K M)) (x : M) : algebraMap K M (2 * b) * x = algebraMap K M (b * Algebra.trace K M x) + algebraMap K M (Algebra.trace K M (γ * x)) * γ
declarations.docstring: The basic identity `2 b x = b Tr (x) + Tr (γ x) γ`.

declarations.name: trace_identity_one
declarations.signature: theorem trace_identity_one (hfin : Module.finrank K M = 2) (b : K) (γ : M) (hγ : γ ^ 2 = algebraMap K M b) (hγK : γ ∉ Set.range (algebraMap K M)) (x y : M) : 2 * b * Algebra.trace K M (x * y) = b * Algebra.trace K M x * Algebra.trace K M y + Algebra.trace K M (γ * x) * Algebra.trace K M (γ * y)

declarations.name: trace_identity_two
declarations.signature: theorem trace_identity_two (hfin : Module.finrank K M = 2) (b : K) (γ : M) (hγ : γ ^ 2 = algebraMap K M b) (hγK : γ ∉ Set.range (algebraMap K M)) (hb : b ≠ 0) (x y : M) : 2 * Algebra.trace K M (γ * (x * y)) = Algebra.trace K M x * Algebra.trace K M (γ * y) + Algebra.trace K M (γ * x) * Algebra.trace K M y

declarations.name: exists_extension
declarations.signature: theorem exists_extension (hfin : Module.finrank K M = 2) (b : 𝓞 K) (γ : 𝓞 M) (hγ : (γ : M) ^ 2 = algebraMap K M (b : K)) (hγK : (γ : M) ∉ Set.range (algebraMap K M)) {ℓ : ℕ} (φ : 𝓞 K →+* ZMod ℓ) (t : ZMod ℓ) (ht : t ^ 2 = φ b) (w : ZMod ℓ) (hw1 : 2 * φ b * w = 1) : ∃ ψ : 𝓞 M →+* ZMod ℓ, (∀ c : 𝓞 K, ψ (algebraMap (𝓞 K) (𝓞 M) c) = φ c) ∧ ψ γ = t
